Atomic Energy Commission — village industries programme
9.x: The Second Plan left the Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela steel plants. It also saw the development of Chittaranjan locomotives, Perambur coaches and the Atomic Energy Commission.
9.tq: Match the named locations with the industrial outcome they represent.

9.s: The goal of a ‘socialistic pattern of society’ was adopted in connection with which of the following?
9.x: The goal of a socialistic pattern of society was adopted through the Industrial Policy of 1956 in the context of the Second Plan.
9.tq: Distinguish the policy instrument from the earlier planning precursors and later legislation.

9.s: The Bombay Plan was published under the title
o: An Economic Programme for Self-contained Villages
A Plan of Economic Development for India
9.x: The Bombay Plan was titled “A Plan of Economic Development for India.”
9.tq: Use the exact title as the distinguishing factual clue.

9.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Bombay Plan?
o: It advocated complete withdrawal of the state from economic activity.
It proposed massive state intervention, public-sector dominance and licensing to protect infant industries.
It gave agriculture and industry equal weight under Marxist socialism.
It proposed only decentralised village production.
9.x: The Bombay Plan proposed substantial state intervention, a dominant public sector and licensing to protect infant industries.
9.tq: Identify the precise policy package and reject descriptions belonging to other plans.

9.s: The Bombay Plan aimed at trebling national income within
9.x: One of the Bombay Plan’s objectives was to treble national income in 15 years.
9.tq: Test the plan’s distinctive time-bound quantitative objective.

9.s: Which of the following persons was associated with the Bombay Plan?
9.x: J.R.D. Tata was among the eight Bombay industrialists associated with the Bombay Plan. G.D. Birla and Kasturbhai Lalbhai were also associated with it.
9.tq: Separate the industrialist authors of the Bombay Plan from authors of non-official ideological plans.

9.s: The People’s Plan was formulated by
9.x: The People’s Plan was formulated by M.N. Roy in 1945.
9.tq: Use author-plan matching to discriminate among non-official plans.

9.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the People’s Plan?
o: Marxist socialism and equal weight to agriculture and industry
Public-sector licensing to protect infant industries
A decentralised economy of self-contained villages alone
9.x: The People’s Plan advocated Marxist socialism, stressed basic necessities and gave agriculture and industry equal weight.
9.tq: Match the ideological description with the correct non-official plan.

9.s: The slogan ‘reforms with a human face’ was associated with ideas echoed in the
9.x: The People’s Plan’s emphasis on basic necessities was echoed in the 1990s slogan ‘reforms with a human face’.
9.tq: Use the distinctive slogan as a clue to the relevant plan.

9.s: Which of the following statements about the Sarvodaya Plan is correct?
o: It was prepared by P.R. Brahmananda in 1956.
It was prepared by M.N. Roy in 1945.
It was prepared by eight Bombay industrialists in 1944–45.
It was prepared by Jayaprakash Narayan in 1950.
9.x: The Sarvodaya Plan was prepared by Jayaprakash Narayan in 1950 and drew on Gandhian constructive work and Vinoba Bhave’s Sarvodaya ideas.
9.tq: Combine author and year to distinguish closely related non-official plans.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gandhian Plan — agriculture, cottage and village industries
People’s Plan — self-contained villages and Trusteeship
Bombay Plan — Marxist socialism and basic necessities
Sarvodaya Plan — licensing to protect infant industries
9.x: The Gandhian Plan emphasised agriculture, cottage and village industries, decentralisation, Swadeshi, Sarvodaya and Trusteeship.
9.tq: Match each plan with its characteristic core proposal.

9.s: Which of the following pairs of planning precursors is correctly matched with its year?
9.x: The Karachi Resolution was adopted in 1931, while the National Planning Committee was set up in 1938.
9.tq: Arrange the two early planning milestones by their years.

9.s: Who is known as the ‘Father of Indian Planning’?
9.x: M. Visvesvaraya is known as the Father of Indian Planning.
9.tq: Test the exact title attached to the planning pioneer.

9.s: The Indian Statistical Institute was made an Institution of National Importance by the
9.x: The Indian Statistical Institute was made an Institution of National Importance through the ISI Act of 1959.
9.tq: Identify the correct legislation by separating it from related institutional dates.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding P.C. Mahalanobis:
1. He chaired the National Income Committee in 1949.
2. The National Income Committee recommended the National Sample Survey.
3. The first round of the National Sample Survey was held in 1950–51.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Mahalanobis chaired the National Income Committee, whose recommendation led to the National Sample Survey; its first round was held in 1950–51.
9.tq: Link the committee, recommendation and first-round dates in sequence.

9.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the institutional or intellectual work of P.C. Mahalanobis?
o: Creation of the NSSO and CSO
Formulation of the Solow-Swan production function
9.x: Mahalanobis helped create the NSSO and CSO, founded the journal Sankhya and devised the Mahalanobis distance. The Solow-Swan production function was not his contribution.
9.tq: Find the unrelated theoretical contribution among Mahalanobis’s known associations.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly lists honours received by P.C. Mahalanobis?
o: Padma Vibhushan in 1968, FRS in 1945 and Weldon Medal in 1944
Padma Vibhushan in 1945, FRS in 1968 and Weldon Medal in 1959
Bharat Ratna in 1968, FRS in 1944 and Nobel Prize in 1945
Padma Bhushan in 1959, FRS in 1944 and Weldon Medal in 1968
9.x: P.C. Mahalanobis received the Weldon Medal in 1944, became an FRS in 1945 and received the Padma Vibhushan in 1968.
9.tq: Match each honour with its correct year rather than accepting a reversed sequence.

9.s: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June because it is the birth anniversary of
9.x: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, the birth anniversary of P.C. Mahalanobis, since 2007.
9.tq: Link the observance date with the personality and the start year.

9.s: The Harrod-Domar model was developed independently by
9.x: The Harrod-Domar model was developed independently by Roy Harrod and Evsey Domar.
9.tq: Use author-model association to separate growth theories.

9.s: In the Harrod-Domar growth equation g = s/k, the symbol k represents
o: the extra capital required to produce one extra unit of output
9.x: In the equation g = s/k, k is the capital-output ratio, representing the additional capital needed to produce one additional unit of output.
9.tq: Decode the formula by identifying the economic meaning of each variable.

9.s: If the savings rate remains unchanged, an increase in the capital-output ratio in the Harrod-Domar model will generally
o: leave the growth rate permanently unchanged
convert the model into the Mahalanobis model
9.x: Since g = s/k, a higher capital-output ratio reduces growth when the savings rate remains unchanged.
9.tq: Apply the inverse relationship shown in the growth equation.

9.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between savings and growth in the Harrod-Domar model?
o: Growth rises only when the capital-output ratio rises.
Growth falls when the savings rate rises.
Growth rises when the savings rate rises, other factors remaining constant.
9.x: The model states that growth depends positively on the savings rate and negatively on the capital-output ratio.
9.tq: Use the direction of change in the equation to eliminate reversed relationships.

9.s: According to the Harrod-Domar approach, increased investment raises output and employment primarily through the
9.x: The model links increased investment with higher output and employment through the multiplier effect.
9.tq: Identify the mechanism that connects investment with output and employment.

9.s: The wage-goods model was put forward by
9.x: The wage-goods model was put forward by C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda in 1956.
9.tq: Distinguish the authors of the wage-goods model from those of other growth models.

9.s: The book associated with the wage-goods model is
o: A Plan of Economic Development for India
9.x: Vakil and Brahmananda put forward the wage-goods model in their 1956 work, Planning for an Expanding Economy.
9.tq: Use the exact work-title association to distinguish the model from plan documents.

9.s: According to the wage-goods model, the principal constraint on economic expansion is the supply of
o: wage goods such as food and essential consumer goods
9.x: The wage-goods model identifies the supply of food and essential consumer goods as the real constraint on expansion, rather than the supply of capital goods.
9.tq: Test the central contrast between wage goods and capital goods.

9.s: How would an increase in the supply of wage goods help the economy according to the wage-goods model?
o: It would allow disguised unemployed workers to be put to productive work.
It would eliminate the need for agricultural production.
It would reduce the labour force available for production.
It would make capital goods unnecessary in every sector.
9.x: A larger supply of wage goods makes it possible to support and employ disguised unemployed labour in productive activities.
9.tq: Trace the model’s causal link from wage-goods supply to labour utilisation.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the wage-goods model from the Mahalanobis model?
o: The wage-goods model prioritised heavy industry, whereas the Mahalanobis model prioritised wage goods.
The wage-goods model prioritised agriculture and wage goods, whereas the Mahalanobis model prioritised heavy industry.
Both models gave identical priority to agriculture and heavy industry.
Neither model considered the availability of goods relevant to growth.
9.x: The wage-goods model favoured agriculture and wage goods, while the Mahalanobis strategy gave priority to heavy industry and capital goods.
9.tq: Compare the contrasting sectoral priorities directly.

9.s: The Janata Party came to power at the Union level in 1977 during which Five Year Plan?
9.x: The Janata Party came to power in 1977 while the Fifth Five Year Plan was in operation.
9.tq: Use the year-plan association to identify the correct option.

9.s:
With reference to the planning strategy of the Janata Government, consider the following statements:
1. The Fifth Five Year Plan was ended one year ahead of schedule.
2. A Rolling Plan was adopted for the period 1978–80.
3. The concept of the Rolling Plan was advocated by Gunnar Myrdal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Janata Government ended the Fifth Plan in 1978, adopted a Rolling Plan for 1978–80, and followed a concept advocated by Gunnar Myrdal.
9.tq: Check the year, duration and associated thinker together before selecting the coded combination.

9.s: Which one of the following was NOT an emphasis of the alternative strategy adopted by the Janata Government?
9.x: The Janata strategy emphasised agriculture, rural development, employment, small and cottage industries, and minimum needs rather than heavy industry.
9.tq: Find the alternative priority that conflicts with the stated emphasis on rural and employment-oriented development.

9.s:
The Janata Government’s alternative strategy gave priority to which of the following combination of areas?
1. Agriculture and rural development
2. Employment
3. Small and cottage industries
4. Minimum needs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
9.x: All four areas formed the principal emphasis of the Janata Government’s alternative strategy.
9.tq: When all listed items represent a coherent policy package, test whether the inclusive combination is supported.

9.s: Which of the following correctly represents the broad significance of the three major plan models in India’s planning experience?
o: Harrod–Domar—employment; Mahalanobis—minimum needs; wage-goods model—heavy industry
9.x: The Harrod–Domar model focused on savings, the Mahalanobis model on capital goods, and the wage-goods model on food. Together they shaped and also attracted criticism of India’s industry-first development path.
9.tq: Start from the sure conceptual pair and eliminate options that reverse the model–focus relationship.

9.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 is correct?
o: It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 1 September 2026 to amend the 1959 Act without replacing it.
It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2026 to replace the 1949 Act.
It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 2 September 2026 to replace the 1931 Act.
It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 2 August 2026 to replace the 1959 Act.
9.x: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 2 August 2026 and seeks to replace the 1959 Act.
9.tq: Distinguish the correct date, House and legislation being replaced from closely changed alternatives.

9.s:
Under the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, which of the following institutional arrangements is proposed?
1. The Indian Statistical Institute would become a statutory body corporate.
2. Its Board of Governors would consist of 11 members.
3. The President of India would be the Visitor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The Bill proposes to make the Institute a statutory body corporate, provide for an 11-member Board of Governors, and designate the President as Visitor.
9.tq: Verify the proposed legal status, composition and constitutional office together.

9.s: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 was referred to which parliamentary body and on what date?
o: Standing Committee on Finance on 1 September 2026
Standing Committee on Finance on 4 August 2026
Standing Committee on Education on 2 September 2026
9.x: The Bill was referred to the Standing Committee on Finance on 1 September 2026.
9.tq: Use the committee–date pair and reject options that alter either the committee or the date.

9.s: What was the theme of the National Statistics Day in 2026?
o: Unlocking the Potential of Administrative Data
9.x: The 2026 National Statistics Day theme was “Unlocking the Potential of Administrative Data.”
9.tq: Test the exact official theme rather than a broader phrase with a similar meaning.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding planning traditions:
1. Stalin’s USSR began five-year plans in 1928.
2. The planning system initiated in Stalin’s USSR was described as imperative planning.
3. India follows indicative planning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Soviet Union under Stalin began five-year plans in 1928 and followed imperative planning, whereas India follows indicative planning.
9.tq: Separate the first-use date from the contrasting types of planning followed by the USSR and India.

9.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Stalin’s USSR began five-year plans.
B. The Janata Party came to power in India.
C. The Fifth Five Year Plan was ended one year early.
D. The Rolling Plan for 1978–80 was adopted.
9.x: Stalin’s USSR began five-year plans in 1928, the Janata Party came to power in 1977, the Fifth Plan ended early in 1978, and the Rolling Plan followed for 1978–80.
9.tq: Fix the early anchor year first, then place the closely related 1977–80 Indian developments.

10.s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Fifth Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Fifth Five Year Plan emphasised removal of poverty, self-reliance and control of inflation.
10.tq: Direct recall of the plan’s distinctive objective.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan gave primary emphasis to Human Resource Development?
10.x: Human resource development was the main objective of the Eighth Five Year Plan.
10.tq: Direct plan-and-objective matching.

10.s: The objective ‘Growth with Social Justice and Equity’ is associated with the:
10.x: The Ninth Five Year Plan focused on growth with social justice and equity.
10.tq: Identify the plan from its characteristic tagline.

10.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the objectives of the Five Year Plans:
1. The Fifth Plan emphasised removal of poverty and self-reliance.
2. The Seventh Plan focused on food, work and productivity.
3. The Eighth Plan focused on human resource development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: All three statements correctly state the principal objectives of the Fifth, Seventh and Eighth Plans respectively.
10.tq: Combine three closely related plan-objective pairs and verify each statement.

10.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ninth Plan — Growth with social justice and equity
Seventh Plan — Food, work and productivity
Fifth Plan — Removal of poverty and self-reliance
10.x: Human resource development was the principal objective of the Eighth Plan, whereas the Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and doubling of per capita income in ten years.
10.tq: Find the wrong plan-objective pair by eliminating the familiar correct matches.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the objective of the Tenth Five Year Plan?
o: Faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth
Growth with stability and progressive self-reliance
8 per cent GDP growth and doubling of per capita income in ten years
Removal of poverty and technological self-reliance
10.x: The Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and sought to double per capita income within ten years.
10.tq: Direct recall of a numerical target linked with a plan.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan was described as the last Five Year Plan of India?
10.x: The Twelfth Five Year Plan, covering 2012–17, was the last Five Year Plan.
10.tq: Direct recall of a terminating institutional phase.

10.s:
Arrange the following plans in chronological order of their periods:
A. Eighth Five Year Plan
B. Fifth Five Year Plan
C. Tenth Five Year Plan
D. Seventh Five Year Plan
10.x: The Fifth, Seventh, Eighth and Tenth Plans covered 1974–79, 1985–90, 1992–97 and 2002–07 respectively.
10.tq: Arrange plans by their stated periods, using the earliest and latest items first.

10.s: The First Five Year Plan was formally launched on:
10.x: The First Five Year Plan was launched on 1 April 1951.
10.tq: Numerical date recall with closely placed alternatives.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the period of the Fifth Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Fifth Five Year Plan was scheduled for 1974–79, although it ended in 1978.
10.tq: Distinguish the scheduled plan period from the year of early termination.

10.s: The Fifth Five Year Plan ended before its scheduled completion in:
10.x: Although the Fifth Plan was scheduled for 1974–79, it ended in 1978.
10.tq: Test the exceptional end year rather than the normal five-year span.

10.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Annual Plans associated with the transition to the Eighth Five Year Plan?
o: They covered 1990–92, after which the Eighth Plan began in 1992.
They covered 1985–90 and preceded the Seventh Plan.
They covered 1966–69 and immediately preceded the Fourth Plan.
They covered 1978–80 and were revised every year.
10.x: Annual Plans were implemented in 1990–91 and 1991–92, and the Eighth Plan began in 1992.
10.tq: Separate Annual Plans from the similarly named Plan Holiday and Rolling Plan.

10.s: The Twelfth Five Year Plan was launched on:
10.x: The Twelfth Five Year Plan was launched on 1 April 2012 and covered 2012–17.
10.tq: Direct recall of a plan launch date.

10.s: The plan system in India, as represented by the First to Twelfth Five Year Plans, extended from:
10.x: The Five Year Plan system ran from 1951 to 2017, ending with the Twelfth Plan.
10.tq: Test the complete chronological span of the planning era.

10.s: The Eleventh Five Year Plan had a GDP growth target of:
10.x: The original GDP growth target of the Eleventh Plan was 9 per cent, later revised to 8.1 per cent.
10.tq: Recall the original target while distinguishing it from the revised target and achievement.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan recorded the highest GDP growth among the plans listed?
10.x: The Eleventh Five Year Plan recorded the highest GDP growth, with actual growth of about 8 per cent.
10.tq: Compare actual growth figures across successive plans.

10.s: Which one of the following plans recorded the lowest actual GDP growth?
10.x: The Third Plan recorded actual growth of about 2.2 per cent, the lowest among the listed plans.
10.tq: Identify the extreme value from the plan-wise achievement figures.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about plan-wise GDP growth:
1. The First Plan exceeded its target growth rate.
2. The Third Plan exceeded its target growth rate.
3. The Seventh Plan exceeded its target growth rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: The First Plan achieved 3.6 per cent against a target of 2.1 per cent, and the Seventh achieved 6 per cent against 5 per cent. The Third achieved only 2.2 per cent against its 5.6 per cent target.
10.tq: Compare target and achievement rather than relying on the plan’s objective.

10.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to target and actual GDP growth?
1. First Plan — 2.1 per cent target and 3.6 per cent actual
2. Third Plan — 5.6 per cent target and 2.2 per cent actual
3. Tenth Plan — 8 per cent target and 7.7 per cent actual
10.x: All three pairs are correct: the First, Third and Tenth Plans recorded the stated target and actual growth rates.
10.tq: Verify target-achievement pairs individually before selecting the coded combination.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan recorded actual GDP growth of approximately 6.0 per cent against a target of 5.0 per cent?
10.x: The Seventh Plan achieved about 6.0 per cent growth against its target of 5.0 per cent.
10.tq: Match a paired target-and-achievement figure to the correct plan.

10.s: The Eighth Five Year Plan achieved actual GDP growth of approximately:
10.x: The Eighth Plan recorded actual GDP growth of approximately 6.68 per cent, against a target of 5.6 per cent.
10.tq: Use the distinctive decimal achievement to distinguish adjacent plans.

10.s: Which one of the following plans had a target growth rate of 7 per cent and achieved approximately 5.4 per cent growth?
10.x: The Ninth Plan initially had a 7 per cent target and achieved about 5.4 per cent growth; the later target was stated as 6.5 per cent.
10.tq: Distinguish the original target from the later revised target.

10.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Eighth Five Year Plan is correct?
1. Per capita national output grew by about 3.9 per cent annually.
2. Agricultural growth was about 3.6 per cent against a target of 3.5 per cent.
3. Industrial growth was about 8.5 per cent against a target of 8.1 per cent.
10.x: All three statements correctly describe the Eighth Plan’s per capita output, agricultural growth and industrial growth performance.
10.tq: Read sectoral target-achievement data together rather than separately.

10.s: Which group contains only those Five Year Plans that exceeded their GDP growth targets?
o: First, Second, Fifth, Seventh and Eighth
Second, Fifth, Sixth, Eighth and Ninth
First, Third, Sixth, Seventh and Tenth
First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth
10.x: The First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth Plans achieved growth above their respective targets.
10.tq: Identify the complete set by comparing each target with its achievement.

10.s: The largest shortfall between targeted and actual GDP growth occurred during the:
10.x: The Third Plan targeted 5.6 per cent growth but achieved only about 2.2 per cent, mainly reflecting the plan’s failure during wars and droughts.
10.tq: Compare the gap between target and achievement, not merely the actual growth rate.

10.s: The Twelfth Five Year Plan had which of the following growth targets in its final formulation?
10.x: The Twelfth Plan had a 9 per cent target in the Approach Paper, but the final target was fixed at 8 per cent.
10.tq: Distinguish an approach-paper proposal from the final approved target.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the actual GDP growth achieved during the Tenth Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent growth and achieved approximately 7.7 per cent.
10.tq: Separate a plan’s target from its actual achievement.

10.s: The Community Development Programme was introduced during which Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Community Development Programme was introduced in 1952 during the First Five Year Plan.
10.tq: Directly link the programme with its introducing plan.

10.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bank nationalisation of 14 banks — Fourth Plan
Drought Prone Area Programme — Fifth Plan
10.x: Bank nationalisation involving 14 banks was undertaken during the Fourth Plan. The Drought Prone Area Programme, Minimum Needs Programme and Twenty-Point Programme belong to the Fourth, Fifth and Fifth Plans respectively.
10.tq: Start from the sure programme–plan pair and eliminate swapped plans.

10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Drought Prone Area Programme was introduced during the Fourth Plan.
2. The Minimum Needs Programme was introduced during the Fifth Plan.
3. The Twenty-Point Programme was introduced during the Sixth Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Twenty-Point Programme was introduced during the Fifth Plan, making statement 3 false.
10.tq: Find the statement containing the plan swap.

10.s: The first population policy and the Tribal Sub-Plan are associated with which Five Year Plan?
10.x: The first population policy was introduced in 1976 and the Tribal Sub-Plan was associated with the Fifth Plan.
10.tq: Use the common plan association for two linked policy initiatives.

10.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
10.x: NREP was introduced in 1980 during the Sixth Plan, but the pair is not correctly matched as stated because NREP belongs to the Sixth Plan; the other three pairs are also correctly matched. Therefore, this question as framed has no unique incorrect pair.
10.tq: Check every programme against its plan before selecting the exception.

10.s: The Women's Component Plan and the seven Basic Minimum Services were associated with the:
10.x: The Women's Component Plan and seven Basic Minimum Services were associated with the Ninth Plan.
10.tq: Discriminate between closely succeeding plan periods.

10.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
10.x: Command Area Development was introduced in 1974–75 during the Fifth Plan. IRDP and NABARD belong to the Sixth Plan, while the Women's Component Plan belongs to the Ninth Plan.
10.tq: Use the year–plan relationship to identify the correct pair.

10.s: The Integrated Rural Development Programme, after the merger of TRYSEM, NREP and other schemes, is associated with which plan?
10.x: IRDP, including the merger of TRYSEM, NREP and other schemes, was associated with the Sixth Plan during 1978–80.
10.tq: Identify the plan from the programme’s restructuring period.

10.s: Which Five Year Plan was the first to focus on gender issues and inter-State as well as intra-State inequalities?
10.x: The Sixth Plan was the first plan to focus on gender issues and inter-State and intra-State inequalities.
10.tq: Directly test the distinctive feature of a plan.

10.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. First Plan — Agriculture and irrigation
b. Second Plan — Heavy industry
c. Sixth Plan — Power
 d. Seventh Plan — Employment
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
10.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Agriculture and irrigation dominated the First Plan, heavy industry the Second, power became significant in the Sixth, and employment was the thrust of the Seventh Plan.
10.tq: Match each plan with its distinctive focus sector.

10.s: Human development was the core of which Five Year Plan, which also shifted emphasis from heavy industry towards infrastructure?
10.x: The Eighth Plan placed human development at the core and shifted emphasis from heavy industry to infrastructure.
10.tq: Use the combined focus and structural shift as identifying clues.

10.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Eighth Plan is correct?
o: It assigned the highest priority to bank nationalisation.
Its main focus was exclusively heavy industry.
Its public outlay was financed mainly by deficit financing.
It made power the sole focus of public expenditure.
10.x: The Eighth Plan’s public outlay was financed mainly by deficit financing, while its developmental emphasis moved towards human development and infrastructure.
10.tq: Choose the precise positive statement and reject absolute distractors.

10.s: In the Tenth Plan, agriculture was described as the:
10.x: The Tenth Plan made agriculture the prime moving force of the economy.
10.tq: Test the exact wording used for the plan’s sectoral priority.

10.s: Which sector was placed first in the Eleventh Plan, with education receiving the highest emphasis?
10.x: The Eleventh Plan placed the social sector first, with education at the top of its priorities.
10.tq: Distinguish the plan’s social-sector priority from industrial priorities.

10.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Eleventh Plan’s inclusive-growth strategy?
o: Complete withdrawal of the private sector
Access to health, education and skills
10.x: The Eleventh Plan envisaged continued reform and a competitive private sector; it did not propose its complete withdrawal. The other three were components of inclusive growth.
10.tq: Reject the extreme statement that reverses the stated strategy.

10.s:
The Eleventh Plan’s inclusive-growth strategy included which of the following?
1. Infrastructure thrust
2. Good governance
3. Continued reform and a competitive private sector
4. Attention to disadvantaged groups
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: All four were components of the Eleventh Plan’s inclusive-growth strategy. The strategy combined infrastructure, governance, private-sector reform and support for disadvantaged groups.
10.tq: Recognise the comprehensive strategy option when all listed components are valid.

10.s: The investment requirement under the Eleventh Plan was estimated at 37 per cent of GDP, rising to what level by the end of the Plan?
10.x: The Eleventh Plan required investment equivalent to 37 per cent of GDP, rising to 39 per cent by the end of the Plan.
10.tq: Distinguish the initial requirement from the end-of-plan figure.

10.s: How many national monitorable targets and State-level targets were set under the Eleventh Plan?
10.x: The Eleventh Plan set 27 national monitorable targets, including 13 targets at the State level.
10.tq: Separate the national count from the State-level subset.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Eleventh Plan’s monitorable targets?
o: GDP growth 9%, agricultural growth 4%, IMR 28 and TFR 2.1
GDP growth 9%, agricultural growth 6%, IMR 30 and TFR 2.1
GDP growth 10%, agricultural growth 4%, IMR 20 and TFR 1.9
GDP growth 8%, agricultural growth 5%, IMR 25 and TFR 2.5
10.x: The Eleventh Plan targeted 9 per cent GDP growth, 4 per cent agricultural growth, an IMR of 28 and a TFR of 2.1. Its MMR target was 1 per 1,000 live births.
10.tq: Split the option into several figures and verify each one.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the Eleventh and Twelfth Plans?
o: Eleventh: balanced regional growth; Twelfth: complete self-reliance
Eleventh: inclusive growth only; Twelfth: poverty elimination only
Eleventh: faster and more inclusive growth; Twelfth: faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth
Eleventh: sustainable growth only; Twelfth: industrial growth only
10.x: The Eleventh Plan was titled “Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth”, while the Twelfth Plan emphasised “Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth”.
10.tq: Compare the exact themes rather than relying on broad similarities.

10.s:
Which of the following was a broad objective of the Twelfth Plan?
1. Reduction of poverty
2. Reduction of regional inequality across and within States
3. Welfare of SCs, STs, OBCs and minorities
4. Creation of employment for youth
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: All four were broad objectives of the Twelfth Plan. It also sought to promote sustainable and inclusive growth.
10.tq: Identify the option containing the complete set of social objectives.

10.s: Under the Twelfth Plan, spending on health, education and skills was increased by how many percentage points of GDP?
10.x: The Twelfth Plan raised spending on health, education and skills by 1.2 percentage points of GDP.
10.tq: Distinguish the social-sector increase from the infrastructure increase.

10.s:
Which of the following measures was associated with the Twelfth Plan?
1. Reduction in the number of Centrally Sponsored Schemes
2. Provision of a flexi-fund
3. Promotion of public-private partnerships in the social sector
4. Review of the plan/non-plan distinction by the Rangarajan Committee
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: All four measures were associated with the Twelfth Plan. The Plan also increased allocations for health, education and skills and for infrastructure.
10.tq: Check whether each administrative reform belongs to the same plan package.

10.s: The planned public outlay for the Second Plan was Rs 4,800 crore. What was the actual outlay?
10.x: The planned public outlay was Rs 4,800 crore, while actual public outlay was Rs 4,600 crore.
10.tq: Distinguish planned outlay from actual outlay.

10.s: The actual public outlay of Rs 4,600 crore during the Second Plan consisted of investment expenditure and current expenditure of:
o: Rs 3,800 crore and Rs 800 crore respectively
Rs 3,650 crore and Rs 950 crore respectively
Rs 4,000 crore and Rs 600 crore respectively
Rs 3,100 crore and Rs 1,500 crore respectively
10.x: Actual outlay comprised Rs 3,650 crore of investment expenditure and Rs 950 crore of current spending.
10.tq: Use the component figures and verify that they add to the total.

10.s: Which of the following was NOT a reason for pruning the Second Plan’s outlay?
o: A sustained fall in inflation caused by excess food production
10.x: The outlay was pruned because of food and capital shortages, inflation, unrealistic closed-economy assumptions and the 1957–58 foreign-exchange crisis. A sustained fall in inflation was not a reason.
10.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated economic conditions.

10.s: Which one of the following was a major criticism of the Nehru–Mahalanobis strategy?
o: It neglected agriculture and contributed to food shortages and inflation.
It relied excessively on labour-intensive small industries and created too many jobs.
It gave no importance to heavy industry.
10.x: The strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture, generating food shortages and inflation, and relying on capital-intensive heavy industry that created few jobs.
10.tq: Identify the criticism that combines the sectoral and macroeconomic effects.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahalanobis model:
1. It assumed a relatively closed economy.
2. It gave priority to capital-intensive heavy industry.
3. It generated substantial employment in the short run.
4. It was associated with food shortages and inflation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Capital-intensive heavy industry was criticised for creating relatively few jobs, so statement 3 is false.
10.tq: Locate the employment statement that contradicts the capital-intensive strategy.

10.s: The Tenth Plan model projected growth of 8.1 per cent, whereas the actual growth during the Plan years lay in the range of:
10.x: The Tenth Plan model projection was 8.1 per cent, while actual growth during the Plan years ranged from 6.2 to 8.6 per cent.
10.tq: Compare the projected figure with the actual range.

10.s: Which of the following is an example of duplication during plan implementation?
o: Separate population policies for every district
Parallel Five Year Plans for each ministry
10.x: Duplication in implementation was illustrated by overlapping rural electrification schemes.
10.tq: Apply the concept of duplication to the concrete example.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Eighth Plan’s performance against its targets?
o: Public-sector outlay share was 39% against a target of 37%, and employment growth was 4% against 2.6%.
Public-sector outlay share was 45.2% against a target of 34.3%, and employment growth was 2.6% against 2%.
Public-sector outlay share was 25% against a target of 34.3%, and employment growth was 1% against 2%.
Public-sector outlay share was 34.3% against a target of 45.2%, and employment growth was 2% against 2.6%.
10.x: The Eighth Plan achieved a public-sector share of 34.3 per cent against a target of 45.2 per cent, while employment growth was 2 per cent against the target of 2.6 per cent.
10.tq: Read actual and target figures in the correct direction.

10.s: The Prakasam Barrage and Nagarjuna Sagar projects are associated respectively with which plan periods?
o: First to Second and First to Second
10.x: Prakasam Barrage, completed in 1957, and Nagarjuna Sagar are both associated with the First-to-Second Plan period.
10.tq: Match project chronology with the plan period rather than the completion year alone.

10.s: Which project was sanctioned during the Third Plan?
10.x: Srisailam was sanctioned in 1963 during the Third Plan.
10.tq: Use the project’s sanction year to identify the plan.

10.s: The foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar was laid by Jawaharlal Nehru on:
10.x: Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar on 10 December 1955.
10.tq: Test the exact date and associated national leader.

10.s: Telugu Ganga is associated with which Five Year Plan?
10.x: The Telugu Ganga project, associated with 1983, was launched during the Sixth Plan.
10.tq: Link the project year with the corresponding plan period.

10.s: The Third Five Year Plan was adversely affected primarily by which combination of events?
o: The 1966 devaluation and the abolition of the Planning Commission
The 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis and political instability
The 1971 war and the oil shock of 1973
The 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965–66 drought
10.x: The Third Plan was derailed by the wars of 1962 and 1965 and the severe drought of 1965–66. This led to the Plan Holiday during 1966–69.
10.tq: Use the cause-effect link and distinguish the events responsible for the Plan Holiday.

10.s: The postponement of the Eighth Five Year Plan was mainly associated with
o: political instability and the balance-of-payments crisis of 1990–91
the termination of the Fifth Plan by the Janata government
10.x: Political instability and the 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis postponed the Eighth Plan. Annual Plans were implemented during 1990–92.
10.tq: Match the plan with its specific interruption rather than with a nearby plan crisis.

10.s: During the Eleventh Five Year Plan period in Andhra Pradesh, which sector received the first priority?
10.x: The social sector received the first priority in Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan. Education received the highest priority within the social sector.
10.tq: Identify the broad priority before narrowing it to the highest-priority component.

10.s: Which one of the following was the highest-priority component within the social sector of Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan?
10.x: Education was given the highest priority within the social sector in Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan.
10.tq: Test the inner ranking within a broad sector priority.

10.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Five Year Plan:
1. The State targeted a GSDP growth rate of 9.5 percent.
2. The State achieved a GSDP growth rate of 5.28 percent.
3. The State achieved an industrial growth rate of 10 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The industrial growth target was 10 percent, but the achievement was 7.26 percent, making statement 3 false.
10.tq: Separate targets from achievements and reject the statement that converts a target into an achievement.

10.s: The industrial growth target and achievement of Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan were, respectively,
10.x: Andhra Pradesh targeted 10 percent industrial growth during the Eleventh Plan and achieved 7.26 percent.
10.tq: Read the pair in the stated order—target first and achievement second.

10.s: At the end of the Eleventh Five Year Plan, the per capita income of Andhra Pradesh was approximately
10.x: The per capita income of Andhra Pradesh at the end of the Eleventh Plan was ₹68,970, which was above the national figure.
10.tq: Use the exact numerical figure and distinguish it from nearby income values.

10.s: What was the share of agriculture and allied activities in the GSDP of Andhra Pradesh at the end of the Eleventh Plan?
10.x: Agriculture and allied activities accounted for 21.27 percent of Andhra Pradesh’s GSDP at the end of the Eleventh Plan.
10.tq: Test the exact percentage from a comparison of closely spaced numerical options.

10.s: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) was launched by the Centre in
10.x: RKVY was launched by the Centre in 2007. An allocation of ₹1,862 crore was associated with the programme in the stated account.
10.tq: Use the year-based direct recall pattern for a centrally launched programme.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Jalayagnam in Andhra Pradesh?
o: An irrigation mission launched in 2004 to complete major and medium projects
A financial inclusion scheme launched in 2015
A rural employment programme launched in 1990
An industrial corridor launched in 2007 to promote exports
10.x: Jalayagnam was an irrigation mission launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2004 for completing major and medium irrigation projects.
10.tq: Use the programme-purpose-year combination and reject swapped programme identities.

10.s: Plan finance of a State consists principally of
o: State’s own resources and Normal Central Assistance
Finance Commission grants and private foreign investment
Only tax revenue collected by the Union Government
Only market borrowings and external assistance
10.x: Plan finance comprises the State’s own resources—such as balance from current revenue, public-sector surpluses and borrowings—along with Normal Central Assistance.
10.tq: Combine the two components instead of selecting one source alone.

10.s:
Which of the following are included in the State’s own resources for plan finance?
1. Balance from current revenue
2. Public-sector surpluses
3. Borrowings
4. Normal Central Assistance
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: Balance from current revenue, public-sector surpluses and borrowings are State’s own resources. Normal Central Assistance is a separate component of plan finance.
10.tq: Separate State-generated resources from central assistance.

10.s: The Gadgil formula for allocation of Central assistance was introduced in
10.x: The Gadgil formula was introduced in 1969. It was later modified into the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula in 1991.
10.tq: Distinguish the original formula year from the later modified formula year.

10.s: Under the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula, which component carried the largest weight in allocating Central assistance?
10.x: Population carried the largest weight of 60 percent. Per capita income had 25 percent, while fiscal performance and special problems had 7.5 percent each.
10.tq: Find the largest weight in a multi-part formula before considering the smaller components.

10.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula:

List-I (Component)
a. Population
b. Per capita income
c. Fiscal performance
d. Special problems

List-II (Weight)
i. 7.5 percent
 ii. 25 percent
 iii. 60 percent
 iv. 7.5 percent

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: Population received 60 percent, per capita income 25 percent, and fiscal performance and special problems received 7.5 percent each.
10.tq: Start from the sure pair with the largest numerical weight and eliminate codes.

10.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the pattern of assistance to States?
o: Special Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
General Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
Special Category States — 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan
10.x: Special Category States received assistance in the ratio of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan. General Category States received 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan.
10.tq: Compare the two categories through their grant-loan ratios.

10.s: Andhra Pradesh was classified under which category for the pattern of Central plan assistance?
10.x: Andhra Pradesh was classified as a General Category State. The General Category pattern consisted of 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan.
10.tq: Apply the category classification to the specific State named in the question.

10.s: Which one of the following statements regarding planning institutions is correct?
o: Planning Commission plan grants continued unchanged after 2015.
NITI Aayog retained the Planning Commission’s power to allocate plan funds.
Planning Commission plan grants ended after its abolition in 2015, and NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation role.
NITI Aayog was established to approve State Five Year Plans.
10.x: The abolition of the Planning Commission in 2015 ended its plan-grant role. NITI Aayog does not perform the function of allocating plan funds.
10.tq: Reject the familiar but incorrect transfer of the Planning Commission’s fund-allocation power to NITI Aayog.

10.s: The average growth during the First to Eleventh Five Year Plans was approximately
o: 1 percent, compared with 4.5 percent before Independence
2.5 percent, compared with 3 percent before Independence
4.5 percent, compared with 1 percent before Independence
8 percent, compared with 4.5 percent before Independence
10.x: Average growth during the First to Eleventh Plans was approximately 4.5 percent, compared with about 1 percent in the pre-Independence period.
10.tq: Read the comparison in the stated order and avoid reversing the planning and pre-Independence figures.

10.s: Which range correctly represents the approximate average growth rates of agriculture and industry during the planning period?
10.x: Agriculture grew at approximately 2–3 percent, while industry grew at approximately 6–8 percent during the planning period.
10.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap between agricultural and industrial growth ranges.

10.s: Which of the following groups contains only industrial and scientific institutions associated with the expansion of India’s industrial base during planning?
o: FCI, NABARD, SBI and the Green Revolution
Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and the IITs
NITI Aayog, Gadgil formula, SBI and FCI
10.x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela steel plants, along with Chittaranjan, Perambur and the IITs, formed part of the industrial and scientific base created during planning.
10.tq: Identify the group belonging to the same institutional-industrial category.

10.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with India’s achievement of food self-sufficiency during the planning period?
o: Food Corporation of India established in 1965
10.x: The Atomic Energy Commission contributed to scientific and technological capacity, not directly to food self-sufficiency. The Green Revolution, FCI and National Seeds Corporation were associated with food security.
10.tq: Find the institution that belongs to the industrial-scientific group rather than the food-security group.

10.s: The State Bank of India originated from which institution during the First Plan period?
10.x: The State Bank of India was created from the Imperial Bank during the First Plan period.
10.tq: Test the institutional predecessor rather than the later development role.

10.s: NABARD was established in
10.x: NABARD was established in 1982 as one of the important institutions associated with planned development.
10.tq: Use direct year recall with nearby institutional dates as distractors.

10.s: The poverty ratio declined from 48.3 percent in 1977–78 to which level in 1983–84?
10.x: The poverty ratio declined from 48.3 percent in 1977–78 to 37.4 percent in 1983–84.
10.tq: Track the direction and exact end value of a numerical trend.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about the failures of planning:
1. Poverty and inequality persisted.
2. Employment growth lagged behind targets.
3. Regional imbalance existed both across and within States.
4. Industrial growth exceeded targets in every Plan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because industrial growth remained below target in several Plans, including the Sixth Plan.
10.tq: Find the single absolute statement that overstates a generally uneven planning outcome.

10.s: The expression “the poor became poorer” was used in relation to which Five Year Plan context?
o: The Eighth Plan’s poverty and safety-net outcomes
The Twelfth Plan’s regional planning strategy
10.x: The expression was used to describe persistent poverty and inequality under the Eighth Plan despite the existence of a safety net.
10.tq: Link the quoted evaluative phrase with the correct Plan context.

10.s: Which of the following was identified as a continuing regional problem requiring attention under the Twelfth Plan?
o: Excessive industrial concentration only in Union Territories
Regional imbalance across and within States
10.x: Correcting regional imbalance across States and within States was identified as an objective under the Twelfth Plan.
10.tq: Apply the stated planning objective to the regional-development problem.

10.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 and Viksit Bharat 2047?
o: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047.
Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 replaced the National Development Council.
Viksit Bharat 2047 is a district-level programme under Swarna Andhra.
Both are annual plans prepared by the Planning Commission.
10.x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is aligned with the national Viksit Bharat 2047 vision and represents a long-horizon development framework for Andhra Pradesh.
10.tq: Test the relationship between two similarly structured development visions.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current status of Five Year Plans and plan-style planning?
o: Five Year Plans ended in 2017, but plan-style credit and regional planning continue.
Five Year Plans ended in 2015 and all forms of regional planning also ended.
Five Year Plans continued beyond 2017 under NITI Aayog with unchanged fund allocation powers.
Five Year Plans were replaced by Annual Plans administered by the Planning Commission.
10.x: The Five Year Plan system ended in 2017, but plan-style credit planning and regional planning continue through other institutions and frameworks.
10.tq: Separate the end of a formal planning system from the continuation of planning-like activities.

10.s: According to the NABARD Andhra Pradesh State Focus Paper 2026–27, the proposed credit plan was approximately
10.x: The NABARD Andhra Pradesh State Focus Paper 2026–27 proposed a credit plan of ₹5.11 lakh crore, up from ₹4.24 lakh crore.
10.tq: Distinguish the total credit plan from its sectoral components and previous value.

10.s: Under the NABARD Andhra Pradesh State Focus Paper 2026–27, which sector received a proposed allocation of ₹2.55 lakh crore?
10.x: ₹2.55 lakh crore was proposed for agriculture and allied activities, while ₹1.64 lakh crore was proposed for MSMEs.
10.tq: Match the precise allocation with the correct sector rather than the total plan size.

10.s: Under Swarna Andhra @2047, which of the following is NOT one of the three economic regions identified for Andhra Pradesh?
10.x: The three identified economic regions are Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Kurnool is not included in this three-region grouping.
10.tq: Find the outsider in a closed list of three named regions.

10.s: With the help of NITI Aayog, the Visakhapatnam economic region under Swarna Andhra @2047 is associated with an envisaged economy of approximately
10.x: The Visakhapatnam economic region is associated with an envisaged economy of USD 750–800 billion by 2047, with NITI Aayog’s assistance.
10.tq: Use the exact range and avoid confusing it with a single-point estimate.

10.s: Which one of the following statements about Kerala’s current planning practice is correct?
o: Kerala’s Gender Budget is less than one-tenth of plan outlay.
Kerala continues Annual Plans, and its Gender Budget exceeds one-fifth of plan outlay.
Kerala has completely discontinued Annual Plans.
Kerala uses only Five Year Plans administered by NITI Aayog.
10.x: Kerala continues to prepare Annual Plans, and its Gender Budget accounts for more than one-fifth of plan outlay. Extreme poverty in Kerala was reported to have ended in November 2025.
10.tq: Combine two linked current facts and reject the absolute discontinuation claim.

10.s: Kerala was reported to have ended extreme poverty in
10.x: Kerala was reported to have ended extreme poverty in November 2025.
10.tq: Test the precise month and year of a current development milestone.

11.s: The First Five-Year Plan achieved an actual growth rate of approximately:
11.x: The First Plan achieved 3.6 per cent growth against its target of 2.1 per cent.
11.tq: Match the actual outcome with the plan target, not with figures from another plan.

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Plan Holiday:
1. Only Annual Plans were implemented during this period.
2. The Green Revolution began during 1966–67.
3. The Third Plan recorded growth of 5.6 per cent against a target of 2.2 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the figures: Third Plan growth was 2.2 per cent against a target of 5.6 per cent.
11.tq: Split the actual-growth and target figures before selecting the coded option.

11.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Planning and the Poor — Padma Desai
India: Planning for Industrialization — B.S. Minhas alone
Planning and the Poor — B.S. Minhas
India: Planning for Industrialization — Gulzarilal Nanda
11.x: B.S. Minhas authored Planning and the Poor in 1974. India: Planning for Industrialization was co-authored by Padma Desai and Jagdish Bhagwati.
11.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authors.

11.s:
Padma Desai is associated with which of the following descriptions?
1. She was a well-known critic of India’s planned economy.
2. She was the first Asian woman to earn a PhD in Economics from Harvard.
3. She co-authored India: Planning for Industrialization with Jagdish Bhagwati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All three statements are correct. Padma Desai earned her Harvard Economics PhD in 1960 and co-authored the 1970 work with Jagdish Bhagwati.
11.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each biographical and authorship detail is supported.

11.s: The chief drawback of Indian planning identified in the context of its implementation was:
11.x: The chief drawback was implementation failure, even though planning produced several measurable achievements.
11.tq: Distinguish a structural implementation problem from an exaggerated claim of complete failure.

11.s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement associated with planning in India?
11.x: Regional disparities persisted and therefore were a failure rather than an achievement. Planning did contribute to savings, investment, food security and scientific manpower.
11.tq: Find the item that belongs to the failures column rather than the achievements column.

11.s: Which one of the following was a failure of planning in India?
o: Expansion of transport and irrigation infrastructure
Growth of information technology and space capabilities
11.x: Rising unemployment was identified as a failure and as a root cause of poverty. The other options represent achievements.
11.tq: Separate positive structural outcomes from persistent social failures.

11.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Land reforms were poorly implemented.
2. Income inequality was reduced substantially after the reforms.
3. Unequal land ownership persisted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because income inequality was not reduced and became wider after the reforms.
11.tq: Use the reversed-trend trap in the statement on inequality.

11.s: Average economic growth over Plans I to XI was approximately:
11.x: Average growth over Plans I to XI was about 4.5 per cent, compared with roughly 1 per cent before Independence.
11.tq: Compare the long-period planning average with the pre-Independence benchmark.

11.s: Which of the following correctly represents the broad sectoral growth pattern during the plan period?
o: Industry grew by 6–8 per cent and agriculture by 2–3 per cent annually.
Industry grew by 2–3 per cent and agriculture by 6–8 per cent annually.
Both industry and agriculture grew by 6–8 per cent annually.
Both industry and agriculture grew by 0.3 per cent annually.
11.x: Industry grew by about 6–8 per cent, whereas agriculture grew by about 2–3 per cent. Agricultural growth before Independence had been only about 0.3 per cent.
11.tq: Check the reversed comparison between industry and agriculture.

11.s: The Fourth Five-Year Plan followed which strategy in relation to growth and self-reliance?
o: Bombay Plan strategy of abandoning public investment
Mahalanobis strategy of complete import dependence
Green Revolution strategy of zero industrial growth
Gadgil strategy of growth with stability
11.x: The Fourth Plan followed the Gadgil strategy, which emphasised growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.
11.tq: Match the plan with its named strategy and reject unrelated policy labels.

11.s:
Consider the following targets of the Fourth Plan:
1. Agriculture growth of 5 per cent a year
2. Industry growth of 8–10 per cent
3. Exports growth of about 7 per cent a year
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: The Fourth Plan targeted 5 per cent annual agricultural growth, 8–10 per cent industrial growth and about 7 per cent annual export growth.
11.tq: Retain the separate numerical targets before testing the combined option.

11.s: The Fourth Plan envisaged ending concessional PL-480 food imports by:
11.x: The Fourth Plan target was to end concessional PL-480 food imports by 1971.
11.tq: Use the specific deadline rather than the beginning or end year of the plan.

11.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Fourth Plan is correct?
o: It achieved 5.7 per cent growth against a target of 3.3 per cent.
It achieved 2.1 per cent growth against a target of 3.6 per cent.
It achieved 8 per cent growth against a target of 10 per cent.
It achieved 3.3 per cent growth against a target of 5.7 per cent.
11.x: The Fourth Plan achieved only 3.3 per cent growth against a target of 5.7 per cent. Droughts and the 1971 war adversely affected its performance.
11.tq: Check whether the actual growth and target have been reversed.

11.s: Which major banking-related measure was taken during the Fourth Plan period?
o: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in 1969.
All private banks were abolished in 1971.
11.x: A positive development during the Fourth Plan period was the nationalisation of 14 banks in 1969.
11.tq: Use the action-and-number combination to avoid the nationalisation–privatisation trap.

11.s:
Under the Gadgil formula, Special Category States initially included:
1. Assam
2. Jammu and Kashmir
3. Nagaland
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: The initial Special Category States under the Gadgil formula were Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, and Nagaland.
11.tq: Test list completeness through the all-inclusive option.

11.s: Under the Gadgil formula, assistance to Special Category States was provided in which proportion?
o: 30 per cent grant and 70 per cent loan
70 per cent grant and 30 per cent loan
50 per cent grant and 50 per cent loan
90 per cent grant and 10 per cent loan
11.x: Special Category States received 90 per cent of assistance as grant and 10 per cent as loan. General-category states received 30 per cent grant and 70 per cent loan.
11.tq: Distinguish the special-state ratio from the general-state ratio.

11.s: Which criterion received the same weight under both the Gadgil and Gadgil-Mukherjee formulas?
11.x: Population carried a weight of 60 per cent under both formulas. The weights for per capita income, tax effort and special problems changed.
11.tq: Compare corresponding rows before considering the changed weights.

11.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Criterion)
(a) Population
(b) Per capita income
(c) Tax effort or fiscal management
(d) Special problems

List-II (Weight under Gadgil-Mukherjee formula)
(i) 60 per cent
(ii) 25 per cent
(iii) 7.5 per cent
(iv) 7.5 per cent

Options:
11.x: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, population received 60 per cent, per capita income 25 per cent, tax effort 7.5 per cent and special problems 7.5 per cent.
11.tq: Start from the population pair and then distinguish the two equal 7.5 per cent entries.

11.s: Which of the following was included as a criterion under the Gadgil formula but omitted from the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula?
11.x: Ongoing irrigation and power projects carried 10 per cent under the Gadgil formula but had no separate weight under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula.
11.tq: Find the row marked absent rather than merely identifying changed percentages.

11.s: Which statement best describes planning after 1991?
o: It ended immediately after the Seventh Plan.
It shifted from directed planning to indicative planning, signalling priority sectors while leaving investment largely to the private sector.
It was made a constitutional requirement for all state governments.
It shifted from indicative planning to complete state direction of private investment.
11.x: After 1991, planning became indicative: it signalled priority sectors while private investment played a larger role. Planning was not a constitutional requirement.
11.tq: Apply the directed-versus-indicative distinction to the role of private investment.

11.s: Why did Five-Year Plans continue to provide value in a market economy after 1991?
o: They legally compelled every private firm to follow state targets.
They provided a long-term perspective for economic development.
They replaced Finance Commission transfers to the states.
11.x: Five-Year Plans continued to provide a long-term perspective even in a market economy. Planning itself was not constitutionally mandatory.
11.tq: Choose the purpose-based explanation rather than an exaggerated legal power.

11.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Planning Commission
B. Establishment of the National Development Council
C. Dissolution of the Planning Commission
D. Establishment of NITI Aayog
11.x: The Planning Commission was established in 1950, the National Development Council in 1952, the Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014, and NITI Aayog was established in 2015.
11.tq: Fix the earliest institutional dates first and then place the two successor events.

11.s: Which combination correctly describes the institutional shift associated with NITI Aayog?
o: Judicial planning, competitive federalism and abolition of state planning
Top-down planning, fund allocation and reduced state participation
Bottom-up approach, cooperative federalism and a think-tank role
Centralised planning, statutory authority and compulsory private investment
11.x: NITI Aayog marked a shift towards bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism. It functions primarily as a think tank rather than as a fund allocator.
11.tq: Separate the institutional role of a think tank from the former fund-allocation role.

11.s: Which statement regarding the National Development Council is correct?
o: It was established in 1952 and its functions have passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council, although a formal abolition resolution remains pending.
It was a constitutional body established under the Constitution.
It was formally abolished before the establishment of NITI Aayog.
It replaced NITI Aayog as the principal fund allocator in 2015.
11.x: The National Development Council was established in 1952 and is now inactive. Its functions have passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council, but formal abolition is still pending.
11.tq: Watch for the distinction between functional inactivity and formal abolition.

11.s: Which sequence correctly represents the replacement documents associated with NITI Aayog?
11.x: The replacement framework consisted of a Fifteen-Year Vision, Seven-Year Strategy and Three-Year Action Agenda.
11.tq: Arrange the documents by their stated time horizons, not by publication order.

11.s: The first Three-Year Action Agenda of NITI Aayog covered which period?
11.x: The first Three-Year Action Agenda covered the period from 2017–18 to 2019–20.
11.tq: Identify the exact coverage period rather than the year in which the framework was requested.

11.s: Under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission, States are preparing which documents?
11.x: States are preparing State Vision@2047 documents under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission.
11.tq: Match the official label with its stated target year.

11.s: Which institutional development ended the system of discretionary plan grants in India?
o: Establishment of the National Development Council
Introduction of the Goods and Services Tax
11.x: The abolition of the Planning Commission ended the system of discretionary plan grants. NITI Aayog was not created as a body with comparable financial powers.
11.tq: Identify the institutional change directly linked with the power that was withdrawn.

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog:
1. NITI Aayog possesses financial powers to redistribute plan grants among States.
2. Its Governing Council primarily coordinates policy among the Centre and the States.
3. The absence of financial powers limits it from functioning as a direct substitute for the Planning Commission in grant allocation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is false: NITI Aayog has no financial powers to redistribute plan grants. Statements 2 and 3 are correct because its Governing Council coordinates policy rather than distributing money.
11.tq: Split the options by checking the reversed financial-power claim.

11.s:
Assertion (A): The Governing Council of NITI Aayog coordinates policy rather than redistributing plan grants.
Reason (R): NITI Aayog does not possess financial powers for the distribution of such grants.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
11.x: Both statements are true, and the absence of financial powers explains why the Governing Council performs a coordinating role rather than redistributing plan grants.
11.tq: Test whether the institutional limitation directly explains the stated function.

11.s: At the 11th meeting of the NITI Aayog Governing Council, which measure was urged by the Prime Minister to promote grassroots planning?
o: Transfer of all plan grants to the Planning Commission
Replacement of regional planning by a single national plan
Abolition of all State-level planning bodies
11.x: The Prime Minister urged States to estimate GDP at the district level so that planning could move from a top-down approach towards grassroots planning.
11.tq: Match the policy suggestion with its intended shift in planning approach.

11.s:
With reference to Kerala's decentralised planning initiative, consider the following statements:
1. The People's Plan Campaign was launched on 17 August 1996.
2. It devolved 35–40% of plan outlay to local bodies.
3. The initiative now being discussed is known as “People's Plan 2.0”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All three statements are correct. Kerala's People's Plan Campaign began on 17 August 1996, devolved 35–40% of plan outlay to local bodies, and “People's Plan 2.0” is under discussion.
11.tq: Check the date, percentage and successor label separately before selecting the combined option.

11.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Discussion of “People's Plan 2.0” in Kerala
B. Launch of Kerala's People's Plan Campaign
C. Abolition of the Planning Commission and emergence of NITI Aayog
D. The 11th NITI Aayog Governing Council's emphasis on district-level GDP estimates
11.x: The People's Plan Campaign began in 1996, followed by the change from the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog, the 11th Governing Council's district-GDP emphasis, and the later discussion of “People's Plan 2.0”.
11.tq: Fix the earliest dated event first and then place the later planning developments.

11.s: Andhra Pradesh currently follows regional planning through which of the following set of economic regions?
11.x: Andhra Pradesh uses regional planning across three economic regions: Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati.
11.tq: Discriminate the exact three-member regional grouping from near-looking alternatives.

11.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Planning feature)
A. Kerala's People's Plan Campaign
B. Amaravati Economic Region
C. NITI Aayog Governing Council
D. Andhra Pradesh regional planning

List-II (Associated detail)
i. Coordination of policy without redistribution of plan grants
ii. Three economic regions
iii. Nine districts and about 44,962 sq km
iv. Devolution of 35–40% of plan outlay to local bodies

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
11.x: The People's Plan Campaign devolved 35–40% of plan outlay; the Amaravati region covers nine districts and about 44,962 sq km; the NITI Governing Council coordinates policy; and AP has three economic regions.
11.tq: Start from the sure percentage and area pairs, then complete the remaining matches.

12.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the four principal areas of the mandate of NITI Aayog?
o: Agricultural marketing; customs administration; currency printing; census operations
Knowledge and innovation; NITI for States; driving transformational change; monitoring and evaluation
Fiscal federalism; monetary policy; public debt management; industrial licensing
Defence production; foreign policy; judicial reforms; election management
12.x: The mandate of NITI Aayog covers knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation.
12.tq: Match the institution’s mandate with its actual functional areas and reject unrelated governmental functions.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Vice-Chairperson from the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
o: The CEO is the ex-officio Chairperson, whereas the Vice-Chairperson is nominated by the Finance Commission.
The Vice-Chairperson and the CEO are separate posts; both are appointed by the Prime Minister, but the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
The Vice-Chairperson is a constitutional authority, whereas the CEO is a statutory authority.
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the President, whereas the CEO is appointed by Parliament.
12.x: The Vice-Chairperson and CEO are distinct offices. The Prime Minister appoints both; the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
12.tq: Separate two closely associated offices by comparing their appointing authority and service status.

12.s: Who was the first Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
12.x: Sindhushree Khullar was the first CEO of NITI Aayog. Amitabh Kant and B.V.R. Subrahmanyam served later as CEOs.
12.tq: Identify the inaugural office-holder rather than the better-known subsequent incumbent.

12.s: Ashok Kumar Lahiri became Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog after replacing:
12.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice-Chairperson on 25 April 2026, succeeding Suman K. Bery, who had held the post from May 2022.
12.tq: Use the immediate predecessor trap in questions involving successive office-holders.

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog:
1. The CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister.
2. The CEO holds the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
3. The tenure of the CEO is fixed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three statements are correct. The CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister, has a fixed tenure and enjoys the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
12.tq: Check each statement against the appointment, tenure and rank provisions before selecting the combination.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of NITI Aayog:
1. The number of full-time members is not fixed.
2. Part-time members may be drawn from universities and research institutions.
3. Part-time members are ex-officio and rotational.
4. The maximum number of part-time members is two.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All four statements are correct. NITI Aayog has no fixed ceiling for full-time members, while it can have at most two rotational, ex-officio part-time members from universities and research bodies.
12.tq: Combine the general composition rule with the numerical ceiling for part-time members.

12.s: The maximum number of ex-officio members in NITI Aayog is:
o: Four Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Two Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Five Union Ministers nominated by the Governing Council
Three Union Ministers nominated by the President
12.x: NITI Aayog may have a maximum of four ex-officio members, who are Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister.
12.tq: Split the option into number and nominating authority before choosing the correct composition rule.

12.s: Special invitees to NITI Aayog are best described as:
o: Domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister
Chief Ministers elected by the Governing Council
Members of Parliament selected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Officials of the Finance Commission nominated by the President
12.x: Special invitees are domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister.
12.tq: Identify the correct category and nominating authority instead of confusing special invitees with ex-officio members.

12.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Full-time member)
a. K.V. Raju
b. M. Srinivas
c. Abhay Karandikar
d. Gobardhan Das

List-II (Professional association)
i. Director, IISER Bhopal
ii. Economist
iii. Secretary, Department of Science and Technology
iv. Former Director, AIIMS Delhi

option_a: a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i
option_b: a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
option_c: a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
option_d: a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
12.x: K.V. Raju is an economist, M. Srinivas was Director of AIIMS Delhi, Abhay Karandikar was Secretary of the Department of Science and Technology, and Gobardhan Das is Director of IISER Bhopal.
12.tq: Start from the sure professional association and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.

12.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the outgoing full-time members of the NITI Aayog panel?
12.x: V.K. Saraswat, Ramesh Chand and Arvind Virmani were among the outgoing full-time members. Abhay Karandikar belongs to the reconstituted panel.
12.tq: Find the one name belonging to the new panel rather than the outgoing group.

12.s:
Arrange the following Vice-Chairpersons of NITI Aayog in chronological order of assumption of office:
A. Suman K. Bery
B. Arvind Panagariya
C. Ashok Kumar Lahiri
D. Rajiv Kumar
12.x: The sequence is Arvind Panagariya, Rajiv Kumar, Suman K. Bery and Ashok Kumar Lahiri. Their respective periods began in 2015, 2017, May 2022 and April 2026.
12.tq: Fix the first and last office-holders, then place the intervening incumbents by year.

12.s: Which one of the following best describes the approach adopted by NITI Aayog for fostering cooperative federalism?
o: Allocating centrally sponsored grants to States
Imposing uniform plans on all States
Restricting State participation to annual plan discussions
Bringing States together on a single platform through a bottom-up approach
12.x: NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism by bringing States together on a common platform through a bottom-up approach.
12.tq: Identify the institutional approach rather than confusing it with the former top-down planning model.

12.s: State rankings in the SDG Index, Health Index and Fiscal Health Index primarily reflect which function of NITI Aayog?
12.x: State rankings in areas such as SDG, health and fiscal health foster competitive federalism while also encouraging intergovernmental cooperation.
12.tq: Link an institutional activity with the federal principle it promotes.

12.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four mandate areas listed for NITI Aayog in the India Year Book 2026?
12.x: The four mandate areas are knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation. Direct allocation of plan grants is not a mandate area of NITI Aayog.
12.tq: Find the option that belongs to the former Planning Commission rather than NITI Aayog.

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog:
1. It aims to build credible village-level plans and aggregate them upwards.
2. It functions as the government's think tank.
3. It is described as a directional and policy dynamo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three statements correctly describe the planning and policy role of NITI Aayog.
12.tq: Use the broad institutional description to identify the combination containing all correct statements.

12.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) is best described as:
o: A constitutional body supervising State finances
A fund-allocation division of the Union Finance Ministry
An autonomous institute conducting population census operations
An attached office of NITI Aayog monitoring and evaluating schemes
12.x: DMEO is an attached office of NITI Aayog concerned with monitoring and evaluation of schemes and policies.
12.tq: Match the body with its institutional status and principal function.

12.s: DMEO was established in 2015 by merging which two organisations?
12.x: DMEO was set up in 2015 through the merger of the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) and the Independent Evaluation Office (IEO).
12.tq: Test the merger pair directly, a common organisational-identity trap.

12.s: The major shift associated with the work of DMEO is from monitoring expenditure to:
