Consider the following statements regarding India's position in the Global MPI 2022:
1. The headcount ratio of multidimensional poverty was 16.4% in 2019–21.
2. Approximately 234 million people were multidimensionally poor.
3. The headcount ratio had declined from 55.1% in 2005–06.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
17.x: All three statements are correct. The headcount ratio fell from 55.1% in 2005–06 to 16.4% in 2019–21, representing about 234 million people in poverty in the latter period.
17.tq: Statement combination testing a percentage, an approximate population and a trend.

17.s: As reported in the Global MPI 2022, how many people moved out of multidimensional poverty in India between 2005–06 and 2019–21?
17.x: The Global MPI 2022 reported that 414 million people moved out of multidimensional poverty in India between 2005–06 and 2019–21.
17.tq: Number recall with close numerical distractors.

17.s:
Arrange the following Global MPI editions in chronological order of the India findings mentioned below:
A. Global MPI 2025
B. Global MPI 2018
C. Global MPI 2022
Which is the correct chronological sequence?
17.x: The correct sequence is Global MPI 2018, Global MPI 2022 and Global MPI 2025.
17.tq: Arrange the editions by their publication years.

17.s: India's MPI value in the Global MPI 2025 data was
17.x: The Global MPI 2025 data recorded India's MPI value as 0.061, compared with 0.064 in 2024.
17.tq: Direct numerical recall with adjacent-year values as distractors.

17.s: Which of the following is the correct descending order of the MPI values of the specified Indian States in 2019–21?
17.x: The values were Bihar 0.160, Meghalaya 0.133, Jharkhand 0.131 and Uttar Pradesh 0.103, giving the stated descending order.
17.tq: Compare closely spaced state-wise numerical values.

17.s: The Human Poverty Index introduced in the Human Development Report 1997 primarily measured deprivation in
o: longevity, knowledge and a decent standard of living
gender parity, inflation and literacy alone
17.x: The HPI measured deprivation in longevity, knowledge and a decent standard of living. It was developed to complement the HDI.
17.tq: Direct concept recall using the three component areas.

17.s: The Human Poverty Index was intended to indicate which of the following?
17.x: The Human Poverty Index indicated the standard of living by measuring selected forms of deprivation.
17.tq: Meaning-based discrimination between poverty and macroeconomic measures.

17.s: Which pair of indices was introduced as an earlier companion to the Human Poverty Index in the Human Development Report 1995?

17.s:
Consider the following statements about India's National MPI:

2. It uses 12 SDG-aligned indicators.
3. The standard-of-living dimension contains seven indicators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

17.tq: Combine structural features and indicator counts.

17.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the dimensions of India's National MPI with the number of indicators?
17.x: The health dimension has three indicators, education has two, and standard of living has seven indicators.

17.s: Which one of the following is NOT included under the health dimension of India's National MPI?
17.x: School attendance belongs to the education dimension. Nutrition, child and adolescent mortality, and maternal health are health indicators.
17.tq: Find the indicator belonging to a neighbouring dimension.

17.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the education dimension of India's National MPI?
o: Years of schooling and school attendance
17.x: Years of schooling and school attendance are the two education indicators in India's National MPI.
17.tq: Dimension-indicator matching.

17.s: Which of the following is NOT an indicator under the standard-of-living dimension of India's National MPI?
17.x: Adolescent birth rate is not an indicator of India's National MPI standard-of-living dimension. The listed living-standard indicators include cooking fuel, housing and bank accounts.
17.tq: Use a health-related look-alike indicator as the exception.

17.s: A person is considered MPI-poor under the National MPI when the person is deprived in at least what proportion of the weighted indicators?
17.x: A person is classified as MPI-poor when deprived in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.
17.tq: Threshold-value recall with fraction-based distractors.

17.s: The baseline report of India's National MPI, based on NFHS-4 data for 2015–16, was released in
17.x: The baseline report was released in November 2021 and used NFHS-4 data from 2015–16.

17.s: According to the National MPI Progress Review 2023, India's multidimensional poverty ratio declined from 24.85% in 2015–16 to
17.x: The Progress Review 2023 recorded a decline from 24.85% to 14.96% between 2015–16 and 2019–21.
17.tq: Pair the correct baseline and end-period percentages.

17.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National MPI Progress Review 2023:

2. The MPI value declined from 0.117 to 0.066.
3. Poverty intensity declined from 47% to 44%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
17.x: All three statements correctly describe the Progress Review 2023: about 13.5 crore people escaped poverty, MPI declined from 0.117 to 0.066, and intensity fell from 47% to 44%.
17.tq: Test several linked numerical changes in one coded question.

17.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the rural and urban multidimensional poverty ratios reported in the National MPI Progress Review 2023?
17.x: The Progress Review 2023 reported multidimensional poverty of 19.28% in rural areas and 5.27% in urban areas.
17.tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban figures.

17.s: According to the NITI Aayog discussion paper of January 2024, approximately how many people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2013–14 and 2022–23?
17.x: The discussion paper estimated that 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty during this period.
17.tq: Distinguish total people escaping poverty from the Uttar Pradesh contribution.

17.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the least-poor States according to the latest National MPI values mentioned?
17.x: The least-poor States were Kerala with an MPI of 0.002, Goa with 0.003 and Tamil Nadu with 0.009.
17.tq: Identify the grouped state-wise low values rather than the poorest state.

17.x: Bihar was identified as the poorest State, with an MPI value of 0.16.

17.s: The Multidimensional Poverty Index proposed by Alkire and Santos in 2010 is based on
o: only consumption expenditure data of urban households
household-survey micro-data and multiple individual-level deprivations
only national income data collected from industries
17.x: The MPI proposed by Alkire and Santos uses household-survey micro-data to identify multiple deprivations at the individual level.

o: Sabina Alkire and Maria Emma Santos
Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen
17.x: The MPI was proposed by Sabina Alkire and Maria Emma Santos in 2010.

17.s: In the MPI design proposed by Alkire and Santos, each education and health indicator carries a weight of
17.x: Each of the four education and health indicators carries a weight of 1/6. The six standard-of-living indicators carry 1/18 each.

17.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its MPI weight in the Alkire–Santos design?
17.x: Years of schooling carries a weight of 1/6. Nutrition and child school attendance also carry 1/6, whereas each standard-of-living indicator carries 1/18.
17.tq: Match a specific indicator with its weight while avoiding dimension swaps.

17.s: Which one of the following statements about the 2010 MPI design is NOT correct?
o: It measures only extreme poverty below one dollar a day.
It considers multiple deprivations at the individual level.
It uses dimensions such as education, health and standard of living.
17.x: The MPI is not a measure restricted to extreme poverty below one dollar a day. It captures multiple deprivations across several dimensions.
17.tq: Reject an over-specific income-poverty description in favour of the multidimensional method.

17.s: Which dimension-indicator pair is correctly matched under the Gender Inequality Index?
o: Reproductive health—maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Empowerment—consumer price index and unemployment rate
Reproductive health—parliamentary representation and school attendance
17.x: The reproductive-health dimension includes the maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate.

17.s: Which of the following indicators belongs to the empowerment dimension of the Gender Inequality Index?

17.s: The labour-market dimension of the Gender Inequality Index uses female and male labour-force participation rates for which age group?
17.x: The labour-market dimension uses female and male labour-force participation among persons aged 15 years and above.
17.tq: Age-range precision test.

17.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gender Inequality Index:

3. India's GII performance is affected by gaps in female labour-force participation and political representation.

17.x: All three statements are correct. The GII rises with greater inequality, uses the IHDI framework, and India's relative performance is affected by labour-force and political-representation gaps.
17.tq: Combine direction, framework and country-application statements.

17.s: The Capability Poverty Measure was introduced by the UNDP in which Human Development Report?
17.x: The Capability Poverty Measure was introduced by the UNDP in the Human Development Report 1996.

17.s: Which one of the following is NOT an indicator of the Capability Poverty Measure?
o: Births unattended by trained health personnel
Children under five who are underweight

17.x: Underweight children below five indicate deprivation in health and nutrition.
17.tq: Interpret the purpose of a specific indicator rather than merely recalling its name.

17.s: The Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index differs from the HDI because it
o: adjusts each HDI dimension for inequality

17.s: When inequality exists, the relationship between HDI and IHDI is correctly expressed as
o: IHDI is always higher than HDI
IHDI is equal to HDI in every country
HDI is calculated by subtracting IHDI from zero
17.x: When inequality exists, the IHDI is lower than the HDI because it discounts achievement for unequal distribution.
17.tq: Test the direction of the inequality adjustment.

17.s: A Gender Development Index value of 1 indicates
17.x: A GDI value of 1 represents gender parity in the measured dimensions of health, education and earned income.
17.tq: Distinguish the parity value of GDI from the direction of GII.

17.s:
The Gender Development Index compares female and male achievement across which of the following dimensions?

2. Education
3. Earned income

17.x: The GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in health, education and earned income.

17.x: Countries are placed into five groups according to their distance from gender parity.
17.tq: Direct count recall with nearby classification numbers as distractors.

17.s: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) of Andhra Pradesh declined from 0.053 in 2015–16 to which value in 2019–21?

Which of the statements given above are correct?
18.x: GDP per capita, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption are all among the six World Happiness Report variables.
18.tq: Use an all-correct combination when each item belongs to the stated index framework.

18.s: In the Environmental Performance Index 2026, the largest weight was assigned to
18.x: Ecosystem Vitality carried the largest weight at 45 percent, compared with 30 percent for Climate Change Mitigation and 25 percent for Environmental Health.
18.tq: Compare the three percentage weights rather than treating the index as equally weighted.

18.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Environmental Performance Index 2026:
1. It covered 47 indicators.
2. It covered 177 countries.
3. Environmental Health carried a weight of 25 percent.
4. Climate Change Mitigation carried a weight of 45 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
18.x: The EPI 2026 covered 47 indicators and 177 countries, and Environmental Health had a 25 percent weight. Climate Change Mitigation had 30 percent, not 45 percent; Ecosystem Vitality had 45 percent.
18.tq: Catch the swapped percentage between the two major environmental components.

18.s: The Corruption Perceptions Index uses a scale in which
o: 0 means very clean and 100 means highly corrupt
0 means moderate corruption and 100 means no data
0 means highly corrupt and 100 means very clean
both 0 and 100 indicate highly corrupt conditions
18.x: The Corruption Perceptions Index ranges from 0, meaning highly corrupt, to 100, meaning very clean.
18.tq: Check the direction of the corruption score before interpreting a country's performance.

18.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the Corruption Perceptions Index?
1. It covers 182 countries.
2. It uses 13 data sources.
3. A higher score indicates a cleaner public sector.
4. A score of zero indicates a very clean public sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
18.x: The CPI covers 182 countries, uses 13 data sources and interprets higher scores as cleaner conditions. A score of zero indicates highly corrupt conditions, making statement 4 false.
18.tq: Combine coverage, methodology and scale direction while rejecting the reversed endpoint.

18.s: The Agriculture Orientation Index is calculated as
o: agricultural employment divided by total employment
agriculture's share of government spending divided by its share of GDP
agricultural exports divided by agricultural imports
agriculture's share of GDP divided by its share of government spending
18.x: The Agriculture Orientation Index equals agriculture's share of government spending divided by agriculture's share of GDP.
18.tq: Preserve the numerator-denominator order in the ratio.

18.s: The Agriculture Orientation Index tracks which Sustainable Development Goal target indicator?
18.x: The Agriculture Orientation Index tracks SDG 2, specifically indicator 2.a.1.
18.tq: Match the agriculture-focused index with the agriculture-related SDG indicator.

18.s: The Government of India criticised the Global Hunger Index methodology primarily because
o: three of its four indicators cover only children and undernourishment relies on a small opinion-poll survey
all its indicators measure only agricultural exports
it uses only official census data from India
18.x: The Government of India argued that three of the four indicators concern only children and that the undernourishment measure rests on an opinion poll of about 3,000 respondents.
18.tq: Identify the specific methodological objections instead of accepting an absolute statement about all indicators.

18.s: Approximately how many respondents were involved in the opinion-poll survey cited in India's objection to the Global Hunger Index methodology?
18.x: The objection refers to an opinion-poll survey involving approximately 3,000 respondents for the undernourishment measure.
18.tq: Distinguish the order of magnitude in the survey-size figure.

18.s: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change rejected the Environmental Performance Index methodology in
18.x: MoEFCC rejected the Environmental Performance Index methodology in 2022.
18.tq: Use the stated year to distinguish the methodological objection from later counter-evidence.

18.s: Which of the following was NOT an objection raised by India to the Environmental Performance Index methodology?
o: Preference for absolute emissions over per-capita emissions
Exclusive reliance on agricultural output indicators
18.x: India objected to the preference for absolute emissions, the neglect of the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities, and the use of contested indicators. Agricultural output indicators were not identified as the objection.
18.tq: Find the unrelated sectoral claim among the stated methodological objections.

18.s: India's criticism that the Environmental Performance Index favours absolute emissions over per-capita emissions is described as
18.x: The criticism is described as a per-capita bias because the methodology is viewed as favouring absolute emissions over per-capita emissions.
18.tq: Match the criticism with its precise methodological label.

18.s: The principle which India stated was ignored by the Environmental Performance Index methodology is
18.x: India stated that the EPI methodology ignored CBDR-RC, the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities.
18.tq: Discriminate between environmental and trade-related international principles.

18.s:
Which of the following was cited as counter-evidence in response to concerns about India's environmental performance?
1. India ranked 23rd in CCPI 2026.
2. Fifty percent of India's installed power capacity was non-fossil in 2025.
3. India achieved this five years before the 2030 NDC target.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
18.x: The counter-evidence includes India's 23rd position in CCPI 2026, 50 percent non-fossil installed power capacity in 2025 and achievement five years before the 2030 NDC target.
18.tq: Check whether all three quantitative and time-related counter-evidence statements belong together.

18.s: According to the Global Gender Gap Index 2026, what was India's rank among the countries covered?
18.x: India was ranked 131st in the Global Gender Gap Index 2026.
18.tq: Use direct recall of the reported country rank while distinguishing nearby numerical options.

18.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's performance in the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2026:
1. India ranked 176th out of 177 countries overall.
2. India ranked 175th in the Air Quality sub-index.
3. India ranked 130th in Climate Mitigation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
18.x: All three statements are correct: India ranked 176th of 177 overall, 175th in Air Quality and 130th in Climate Mitigation in the EPI 2026.
18.tq: Check the overall rank and each sub-rank separately before selecting the complete combination.

18.s: India was placed at which position in the Responsible Nations Index 2026?
18.x: India ranked 16th among 154 countries in the Responsible Nations Index 2026.
18.tq: Read both the country rank and the total number of countries together to avoid confusing the denominator.

18.s: With reference to StartupBlink's Innovators Business Environment Index 2026, India was ranked:
18.x: India occupied the 54th position in StartupBlink's Innovators Business Environment Index 2026.
18.tq: Distinguish the index name and publisher context before recalling the numerical rank.

18.s: Which of the following is a criticism concerning the use of perception surveys and absolute-emission metrics in international indices?
o: They exclude all environmental indicators from the assessment.
They systematically favour populous developing countries.
They may disadvantage populous developing countries.
They measure only the formal employment sector of an economy.
18.x: Perception surveys and absolute-emission metrics may disadvantage populous developing countries, particularly because absolute emissions can be high due to population size.
18.tq: Apply the stated criticism to identify the consequence of the measurement approach rather than recalling a rank.

19.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding resource depletion:

List-I (Resource)
a. Groundwater
b. Topsoil
c. Biodiversity habitats
d. Sustainable forest managed for timber while retaining biodiversity

List-II (Associated condition)
i. Expansion of agriculture
ii. Deep bore tubewells for irrigation
iii. Brick production
iv. Not an instance of resource depletion

Select the correct answer using the code below.
19.x: Deep bore tubewells are associated with groundwater depletion, brick production with topsoil loss, and agricultural expansion with habitat loss. A sustainably managed forest retaining biodiversity is not an instance of resource depletion.
19.tq: Start from the sure resource–cause pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.

19.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Green Revolution:
1. HYV monoculture and chemical fertilisers contributed to a decline in soil fertility.
2. Irrigation requirements of HYV crops contributed to depletion of the water table.
3. Fertilisers, pesticides and herbicides polluted land, water and air and reduced biodiversity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: All three statements correctly describe the environmental consequences associated with HYV-based Green Revolution agriculture.
19.tq: Test the complete chain of effects rather than relying on a single familiar consequence.

19.s: Approximately what proportion of the world’s global land has been transformed by human activities?
19.x: About one-third of the world’s global land has been transformed by human activities.
19.tq: Distinguish the approximate global proportion from nearby but unsupported size claims.

19.s: More than what proportion of the world’s rivers have been dammed or diverted?
19.x: More than 60 percent of the world’s rivers have been dammed or diverted.
19.tq: Use the scale qualifier ‘more than’ and identify the correct approximate threshold.

19.s: Approximately what proportion of the Earth’s land is degraded?
19.x: About 40 percent of the Earth’s land is degraded.
19.tq: Separate the land-degradation figure from the distinct figures for transformed land and diverted rivers.

19.s: Which one of the following statements about urea use is correct?
o: Urea is not used in Indian agriculture because it is a non-nitrogenous fertiliser.
Urea accounts for approximately 56 percent of fertiliser use, and its overuse degrades soil and water.
Urea accounts for approximately 80 percent of fertiliser use and prevents water pollution.
Urea accounts for approximately 25 percent of fertiliser use and primarily improves biodiversity.
19.x: Urea constitutes approximately 56 percent of fertiliser use, while its overuse contributes to degradation of soil and water.
19.tq: Reject exaggerated numerical claims and pair the correct figure with its stated environmental effect.

19.s: Green urea is described as a low-carbon alternative produced using:
o: Crude oil and captured sulphur dioxide
Solar salt and atmospheric nitrogen alone
Green hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide
19.x: Green urea uses green hydrogen and captured carbon dioxide and is regarded as a low-carbon alternative.
19.tq: Test the exact input combination rather than the broad label ‘green’.

19.s: Which combination is identified as the main reason for India’s low Environmental Performance Index score?
o: Urban particulate pollution and coal-based power
Rural noise pollution and tidal energy
19.x: Urban particulate pollution and coal-based power are identified as the main reasons for India’s low Environmental Performance Index score.
19.tq: Apply the ‘main reasons’ wording and avoid substituting unrelated environmental indicators.

19.s: Resource depletion occurs when:
o: The rate of resource use is equal to its regeneration in every season
A forest is managed sustainably while biodiversity is retained
Resources are used faster than they can regenerate
The rate of resource use is slower than its regeneration
19.x: Resource depletion occurs when resources are used faster than their rate of regeneration. Sustainable forest management with retained biodiversity does not represent depletion.
19.tq: Translate the scenario into the rate comparison between extraction and regeneration.

19.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the functions of the environment:

List-I (Function)
a. Supplies resources
b. Assimilates waste
c. Sustains life
d. Aesthetic services

List-II (Meaning)
i. Scenery and amenity
ii. Absorbs and neutralises wastes
iii. Genetic and biodiversity
iv. Renewable and non-renewable resources

Select the correct answer using the code below.
19.x: The environment supplies renewable and non-renewable resources, assimilates wastes, sustains genetic and biological diversity, and provides scenery and amenity.
19.tq: Start with the distinctive meanings of aesthetic services and waste assimilation, then complete the code.

19.s: The first function of the environment is the:
o: Assimilation of all pollutants without limits
Supply or production of raw materials
19.x: The first function of the environment is the supply or production of raw materials.
19.tq: Test the ordered classification directly by identifying the first function.

19.s: The absorptive capacity of the environment refers to its ability to:
o: Convert all non-renewable resources into renewable resources
Prevent all human extraction of resources
Absorb degradation and process and neutralise pollutants without harm
19.x: Absorptive capacity is the ability of the environment to absorb degradation, or the maximum pollutant load an ecosystem can process and neutralise without harm.
19.tq: Use the operational definition and distinguish pollutant-processing capacity from resource production.

19.s: An environmental crisis is likely to arise when:
o: Extraction exceeds regeneration and waste exceeds absorptive capacity
Extraction remains below regeneration and waste remains below absorptive capacity
Aesthetic services increase in urban areas
19.x: An environmental crisis arises when resource extraction exceeds regeneration and waste generation exceeds the environment’s absorptive capacity.
19.tq: Pair the two threshold conditions instead of selecting only one of them.

19.s: Which of the following is NOT a human-driven cause of environmental degradation?
o: Expansion of roads and urban areas
19.x: Wildlife conservation is a conservation practice, not a human-driven cause of environmental degradation. Groundwater over-extraction, industrial emissions and urban expansion are causes.
19.tq: Find the conservation measure hidden among the listed degradation causes.

19.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deforestation is a human-driven cause of environmental degradation.
2. Chemical-intensive farming can contribute to environmental degradation.
3. Overfishing is a human-driven cause of environmental degradation.
4. Renewable energy production is classified as a cause of environmental degradation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: Deforestation, chemical-intensive farming and overfishing are human-driven causes. Renewable energy production is treated as a conservation-oriented practice rather than a cause in this classification.
19.tq: Identify the one classification reversal and select the code containing only genuine causes.

19.s: Which pair correctly represents the two environmental threats faced by India?
o: Poverty-induced degradation and pollution from affluence and rapid industrial growth
Rural literacy and excessive renewable energy production
Only natural disasters and seasonal rainfall variation
19.x: India faces poverty-induced degradation as well as pollution associated with affluence and rapid industrial growth.
19.tq: Distinguish the dual-source formulation from single-cause and unrelated alternatives.

19.s: With reference to the Environmental Kuznets Curve, which one of the following is correct?
o: Per-capita income is on the Y-axis and environmental degradation is on the X-axis; the curve is U-shaped.
Tax rate is on the X-axis and revenue is on the Y-axis; the curve is inverted-U shaped.
Per-capita income is on the X-axis and environmental degradation or pollution is on the Y-axis; the curve is inverted-U shaped.
Inflation is on the X-axis and unemployment is on the Y-axis; the curve is downward sloping.
19.x: The Environmental Kuznets Curve places per-capita income on the X-axis and environmental degradation or pollution on the Y-axis. Degradation initially rises, reaches a peak and then falls, producing an inverted-U shape.
19.tq: Check both axes before identifying the curve’s shape.

19.s: According to the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, environmental degradation generally:
o: Rises initially, reaches a peak and then falls as income increases
Rises only after the highest income level is reached
Remains constant at every income level
19.x: The hypothesis suggests that degradation increases during early growth, peaks at an intermediate income level and subsequently declines as income rises.
19.tq: Remember the three-stage movement: rise, peak and fall.

19.s: The Environmental Kuznets Curve is derived from the Kuznets Curve associated with Simon Kuznets, which describes the relationship between:
19.x: Simon Kuznets’ original curve describes inequality as initially rising and later falling with economic growth, also producing an inverted-U shape.
19.tq: Separate the original Kuznets relationship from the environmental adaptation of the curve.

19.s: A green economy primarily seeks to:
o: Reduce environmental risks and ecological scarcities while decoupling development from resource use and pollution
Increase resource use without considering ecological scarcity
Replace all economic activity with conservation activity
19.x: A green economy reduces environmental risks and ecological scarcities and seeks development decoupled from resource use and pollution.
19.tq: Select the option containing both the risk-reduction and decoupling dimensions.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about the Expert Group on Green National Accounts:
1. It was chaired by Sir Partha Dasgupta.
2. It was set up in 2011.
3. It submitted its report in 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: The Expert Group was chaired by Sir Partha Dasgupta, set up in 2011 and reported in 2013.
19.tq: Link the chairperson with the two chronological milestones.

19.s: Which Indian State was the first to adopt green GDP in the form of Gross Environment Product (GEP)?
19.x: Uttarakhand was the first Indian State to adopt green GDP in the form of Gross Environment Product.
19.tq: Test the state-level first-mover fact against plausible state alternatives.

19.s: Which of the following pairs relating to older welfare-adjusted measures is correctly matched?
o: NEW — Paul Samuelson; MEW — Nordhaus and Tobin
NEW — Nordhaus and Tobin; MEW — Paul Samuelson
NEW — Simon Kuznets; MEW — Sir Partha Dasgupta
NEW — World Bank; MEW — United Nations Statistical Commission
19.x: NEW is associated with Paul Samuelson, while MEW is associated with Nordhaus and Tobin.
19.tq: Start with the author–measure association and reject swapped names.

19.s: The trade-off view regarding growth and environmental protection is represented by the argument that:
o: Environmental protection is always costless in the short term
Economic growth and environmental protection can never conflict under any circumstances
Environmental rules may slow growth and countries should grow first and clean up later
19.x: The trade-off view argues that environmental rules can slow growth and reflects the ‘grow first, clean up later’ approach associated with Environmental Kuznets Curve logic.
19.tq: Recognise the characteristic slogan of the trade-off position.

19.s: Why is environmental protection regarded as an investment in long-term prosperity?
o: Environmental degradation eliminates all public expenditure
Environmental degradation raises health costs and lowers labour efficiency
Environmental protection prevents all economic growth
19.x: Environmental degradation raises health costs and lowers labour efficiency; therefore, protection can support long-term prosperity rather than merely impose a short-term cost.
19.tq: Trace the cause-and-effect link from degradation to health and labour outcomes.

19.s: Which groups are stated to bear most of the costs of environmental degradation?
o: Only large corporations and high-income households
People living in slums and flood-prone areas
19.x: The poor, particularly people living in slums and flood-prone areas, bear most of the costs of environmental degradation.
19.tq: Identify the distributional dimension rather than the aggregate economic argument.

19.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Environmental Impact Assessment in India:
1. It was first used in 1978 for river valley projects.
2. The EIA Notification was issued in 1994 and revised in 2006.
3. Environmental clearance is compulsory for 39 project categories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: EIA was first used in 1978 for river valley projects; the notification dates are 1994 and 2006, and clearance is compulsory for 39 project categories.
19.tq: Check the dates and the numerical category count together.

19.s: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 were framed under which legislation?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
19.x: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 were framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
19.tq: Use the ‘under the Act’ relationship and avoid confusing neighbouring environmental statutes.

19.s: Sovereign Green Bonds are principally associated with:
o: Financing environmentally beneficial or green activities through sovereign borrowing
Measuring income inequality through the Lorenz curve
19.x: Sovereign Green Bonds are instruments for sovereign borrowing associated with financing green or environmentally beneficial activities.
19.tq: Identify the purpose of the instrument rather than confusing it with an assessment or clearance mechanism.

19.s: Which organisation compiles India’s environment accounts in accordance with the UN System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
19.x: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation compiles environment accounts based on SEEA and has released ecosystem and natural-asset accounts since 2018.
19.tq: Ask ‘which body performs this function?’ to avoid swapping ministries and institutions.

19.s: The SEEA Central Framework was adopted by the UN Statistical Commission in:
19.x: The SEEA Central Framework was adopted by the UN Statistical Commission in 2012.
19.tq: Separate the international adoption year from India’s later release of accounts.

19.s: EnviStats India is an annual publication of MoSPI based on which framework?
o: World Bank’s Human Capital Index framework
IMF’s Balance of Payments Manual alone
19.x: EnviStats India is an annual MoSPI publication based on the United Nations Statistics Division’s FDES 2013.
19.tq: Match the publication with its issuing body and statistical framework.

19.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six components of EnviStats India?
19.x: The six components are conditions and quality; resources and use; residuals; extreme events; human settlements and health; and protection and management. Military expenditure and defence procurement is not one of them.
19.tq: Find the unrelated administrative category among the environmental-statistics components.

19.s: Which one of the following lists all six components of EnviStats India correctly?
o: Climate; agriculture; industry; tourism; finance; communications
Income and wealth; taxation; trade; inflation; banking; public debt
Conditions and quality; resources and use; residuals; extreme events; human settlements and health; protection and management
Forests; minerals; exports; defence; education; transport
19.x: EnviStats India covers conditions and quality, resources and use, residuals, extreme events, human settlements and health, and protection and management.
19.tq: Verify the complete named list and reject options containing non-environmental statistical categories.

19.s: According to the World Bank assessment published in 2013, India's annual cost of environmental degradation was approximately what proportion of its GDP?
19.x: The World Bank estimated India's annual cost of environmental degradation at about 5.7% of GDP in 2013.
19.tq: Use the precise institution-year-figure combination rather than a nearby percentage.

19.s: The World Bank estimated India's annual cost of environmental degradation at Rs 3.75 lakh crore for which year?
19.x: The estimated annual cost was Rs 3.75 lakh crore for 2009.
19.tq: Match the monetary estimate with its reference year.

19.s: Which one of the following best explains the mechanism through which environmental degradation imposes an economic cost on India?
o: Higher healthcare spending and lower labour productivity
Higher exports and lower public expenditure
Lower healthcare spending and higher labour productivity
Lower agricultural output and higher foreign exchange reserves
19.x: Environmental degradation raises healthcare expenditure and reduces labour productivity, creating a combined economic cost.
19.tq: Identify the cause-effect chain rather than selecting unrelated economic indicators.

19.s: The ISRO-SAC Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas, 2021, estimated the degraded area of India during 2018–19 at:
o: 97.85 million hectares, or 29.77% of the area
97.85 million hectares, or 28.8% of the area
94.53 million hectares, or 29.77% of the area
94.53 million hectares, or 28.8% of the area
19.x: The Atlas estimated 97.85 million hectares, equivalent to 29.77% of India's area, as degraded during 2018–19.
19.tq: Keep the area figure and percentage paired; APPSC often separates correct pairs from swapped pairs.

19.s:
Consider the following statements regarding land degradation in India:
1. The degraded area increased from 94.53 million hectares during 2003–05 to 97.85 million hectares during 2018–19.
2. The share of degraded area increased from 28.8% to 29.77% over the corresponding period.
3. The increase was approximately 2.2 lakh hectares per year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: All three statements are correct: the area rose from 94.53 to 97.85 million hectares, the share from 28.8% to 29.77%, and the increase was about 2.2 lakh hectares annually.
19.tq: Check the numerical progression and the rate together before selecting the coded combination.

19.s: Which two processes account for the leading shares of India's degraded area identified in the ISRO-SAC Atlas?
19.x: Water erosion accounted for 10.98% and vegetation degradation for 8.91%, making them the leading processes mentioned.
19.tq: Pair the processes with the largest stated shares rather than with regional examples.

19.s: The shares of India's degraded area attributed to water erosion and vegetation degradation are, respectively:
19.x: Water erosion accounts for 10.98% of the area and vegetation degradation for 8.91%.
19.tq: Watch for the reversed-comparison trap in paired percentages.

19.s: Which of the following correctly describes the major land-degradation problems associated with Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts?
o: Glacial erosion, landslides and permafrost degradation
Riverbank erosion caused exclusively by floods
Drought-induced soil degradation, desertification, wind erosion of topsoil and groundwater depletion
Coastal erosion, salinity and tidal inundation alone
19.x: Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai are associated with drought-induced soil degradation, desertification, topsoil loss through wind erosion and groundwater depletion.
19.tq: Use the district-specific cluster of causes instead of substituting coastal or fluvial processes.

19.s: Uppada in Kakinada is particularly associated with which form of environmental degradation?
19.x: Uppada in Kakinada is identified with coastal erosion.
19.tq: Discriminate the named coastal location from inland Rayalaseema examples.

19.s: In the delta regions of Andhra Pradesh, which combination is identified as a major land and water-related problem?
o: Coastal erosion and deep borewell failure
19.x: Salinity and waterlogging are the major problems identified for the delta regions.
19.tq: Match the regional setting with its characteristic pair of degradation processes.

19.s: The severe depletion of groundwater in Rayalaseema has been particularly associated with:
19.x: Deep borewells in Rayalaseema have caused severe groundwater depletion.
19.tq: Identify the specific human activity linked to the stated environmental effect.

19.s: During 2011–2020, the area restored globally through the reported land-restoration effort was approximately:
19.x: A total of 21.76 million hectares was restored during 2011–2020.
19.tq: Separate the area actually restored from the larger 2030 target.

19.s: The restoration of 21.76 million hectares during 2011–2020 was associated with carbon restoration of approximately:
19.x: The restoration was associated with 461.14 million tonnes of carbon.
19.tq: Match the restoration area with its corresponding carbon figure.

19.s: Which one of the following statements about the States contributing to land restoration is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh restored the largest area, while Telangana ranked among the top five.
Telangana and Andhra Pradesh both ranked first.
Telangana was the first State, and Andhra Pradesh was among the top five.
Andhra Pradesh was the first State, while Telangana was outside the top five.
19.x: Telangana was the first State in the reported restoration effort, while Andhra Pradesh was among the top five.
19.tq: Compare the distinct ranks of the two States without reversing their positions.

19.s: The restoration of 21.76 million hectares represented approximately what share of the 26 million hectare restoration target for 2030?
19.x: The restored area amounted to 84% of the 26 million hectare target for 2030.
19.tq: Relate the achievement percentage to the stated target rather than to the annual restoration rate.

19.s: The target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030 is associated with which international framework?
19.x: The 26 million hectare target by 2030 is associated with UNCCD COP17.
19.tq: Identify the responsible international framework from the institution-name trap.

19.s: India's second land-restoration progress report was associated with which event?
o: The publication of the ISRO-SAC Atlas 2021
The adoption of AP Common Zoning Regulations 2026
19.x: India's second land-restoration progress report was presented in the context of UNCCD COP17.
19.tq: Match the current report with the correct international forum, not with the earlier assessment or atlas.

19.s: The AP Common Zoning Regulations 2026 provide for how many land-use categories?
19.x: The AP Common Zoning Regulations 2026 provide for nine land-use categories.
19.tq: Recall the exact count in a regulatory classification.

19.s: Under the AP Common Zoning Regulations 2026, which of the following groups is identified as development-restricted?
o: Forests, hills, water bodies, eco-sensitive areas and CRZ
Agricultural fields, industrial zones, towns and highways
Only coastal settlements and irrigation canals
19.x: Forests, hills, water bodies, eco-sensitive areas and Coastal Regulation Zone areas are development-restricted under the regulations.
19.tq: Find the complete restricted-category list and reject options that omit or replace categories.

19.s: How many green building projects were reported in Andhra Pradesh?
19.x: Andhra Pradesh had 638 reported green building projects.
19.tq: Distinguish the green-building count from the restoration and carbon figures.

19.s: Why can conventional GDP growth conceal environmental degradation?
o: GDP directly deducts the depletion of natural capital from output
GDP excludes all healthcare and productivity-related expenditure
GDP ignores depletion of natural resources, allowing growth to hide the loss of natural capital
GDP measures only biodiversity and ecosystem services
19.x: Conventional GDP does not account for the depletion of natural resources; consequently, recorded growth can coexist with a loss of natural capital.
19.tq: Apply the distinction between aggregate output and natural-capital accounting.

20.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Adoption of Agenda 2030
B. Rio Earth Summit
C. Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment
D. Johannesburg World Summit on Sustainable Development
20.x: The Stockholm Conference was held in 1972, the Rio Earth Summit in 1992, the Johannesburg Summit in 2002 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
20.tq: Use the first and last milestones, then place the intermediate events by year.

20.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
20.x: The Johannesburg World Summit on Sustainable Development was held in 2002, also known as Rio+10. Stockholm was held in 1972, Rio+20 in 2012 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
20.tq: Check the year-event pairing and reject swapped milestone years.

20.s: The decision to develop the Sustainable Development Goals was taken at which event?
20.x: The 2012 Rio+20 Conference, formally the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, took the decision to develop the SDGs.
20.tq: Distinguish the closely related Rio, Rio+10 and Rio+20 milestones.

20.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 1992 Rio Earth Summit?
o: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
20.x: The SDGs were developed after the 2012 Rio+20 Conference and adopted in 2015. Agenda 21, the CBD and the UNFCCC are associated with the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.
20.tq: Find the later milestone among outcomes of the 1992 summit.

20.s: The Brundtland Commission was chaired by:
20.x: The World Commission on Environment and Development was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, who was the Prime Minister of Norway.
20.tq: Use the person-title and country association to identify the chairperson.

20.s: The Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by the United Nations General Assembly during its:
20.x: The SDGs were adopted at the 70th session of the UN General Assembly as part of the 2030 Agenda.
20.tq: Apply the numerical-session distinction instead of confusing it with the adoption year.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sustainable Development Goals:
1. There are 17 goals.
2. They contain 169 targets.
3. Their implementation period is 2015–2030.
4. They came into force from 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: The SDG framework consists of 17 goals and 169 targets, covers 2015–2030, and came into force from 2016.
20.tq: Verify each numerical and temporal statement independently before selecting the coded combination.

20.s: How many global indicators are associated with the Sustainable Development Goals?
20.x: The global SDG framework has 232 indicators. The figures 169, 277 and 113 relate respectively to targets, India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 and the SDG India Index 2023–24.
20.tq: Separate goals, targets and indicators before choosing the figure.

20.s: India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 contains how many indicators?
20.x: India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 contains 277 indicators and is associated with the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
20.tq: Distinguish the national indicator framework from the global indicator framework and the SDG India Index.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Millennium Development Goals?
20.x: The MDGs consisted of 8 goals for the period 2000–2015. They preceded and provided roots for the SDGs.
20.tq: Discriminate between the MDG and SDG goal counts and time periods.

20.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer:
List-I (SDG number)
A. 4
B. 7
C. 12
D. 16

List-II (Theme)
i. Responsible Consumption and Production
ii. Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
iii. Quality Education and lifelong learning
iv. Affordable and Clean Energy
20.x: SDG 4 concerns quality education, SDG 7 affordable and clean energy, SDG 12 responsible consumption and production, and SDG 16 peace, justice and strong institutions.
20.tq: Start with the sure goal-theme pair and eliminate codes that disturb it.

20.s: Which of the following statements about the grouping of the Sustainable Development Goals is correct?
o: Goals 8–10 deal exclusively with environmental protection.
Goals 1–7 extend the Millennium Development Goals.
The last seven goals deal only with poverty eradication.
20.x: Goals 1–7 extend the MDG concerns. Goals 8–10 cover jobs, infrastructure and distribution, while the last seven focus on sustainability.
20.tq: Use the broad grouping of consecutive goal numbers to reject overexclusive descriptions.

20.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of sustainability?
20.x: The three pillars are economic growth, social inclusion or equity, and environmental protection. Military strength is not a pillar of sustainability.
20.tq: Identify the outsider against the standard three-pillar framework.

20.s: Sustainable development requires the three pillars of sustainability to be:
o: Balanced without maximising any one pillar in isolation
Ranked with economic growth above all other considerations
20.x: Sustainable development seeks a balance among economic growth, social inclusion and environmental protection rather than maximising one pillar alone.
20.tq: Apply the balancing principle to a policy situation instead of selecting a single-pillar approach.

20.s: Which of the following represents a socio-environmental overlap?
o: A policy concerning only political representation
A policy combining military strength and economic growth
A policy combining only industrial output and profits
A policy combining social inclusion and environmental protection
20.x: The socio-environmental overlap combines social concerns with environmental protection. The three recognised overlaps include socio-economic, socio-environmental and eco-environmental dimensions.
20.tq: Break the compound term into its two component sustainability pillars.

20.s: The basic goal of sustainable development is to:
o: Maximise present profits regardless of future effects
Exploit all available resources before they become scarce
Meet present needs while preserving choices for future generations
Suspend economic development until environmental degradation ends
20.x: The core goal is to meet present needs without reducing the options available to future generations, within the Earth’s carrying capacity.
20.tq: Reject extreme present-only and growth-denial options and apply the intergenerational principle.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Agenda 2030:
1. It is universal in application.
2. Its goals are interconnected.
3. It follows the principle of leaving no one behind.
4. It is based on inclusive participation and partnerships.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: Agenda 2030 is universal, interconnected, inclusive and participatory, and is guided by the principle of leaving no one behind.
20.tq: Treat the comprehensive option as correct when each listed principle belongs to the agenda.

20.s: The principle that Agenda 2030 applies to developed, developing and least developed countries alike is known as its:
20.x: Universality means that Agenda 2030 applies to all countries, irrespective of their level of development.
20.tq: Match the exact principle with its defining scope rather than a related development term.

20.s: The Agenda 2030 framework is guided by which of the following human-rights instruments?
o: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species alone
20.x: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, along with international human-rights treaties, guides the Agenda 2030 framework.
20.tq: Identify the human-rights foundation rather than an environmental treaty.

20.s: Agenda 2030 places particular emphasis on ending all discrimination and violence against:
20.x: A specific focus of Agenda 2030 is ending all discrimination and violence against women and girls.
20.tq: Read the scope of the focus group precisely and avoid narrowing or broadening it without basis.

20.s: The two principal roots of Agenda 2030 are:
o: The World Trade Organization and the International Monetary Fund
The Kyoto Protocol and the Montreal Protocol
The Millennium Development Goals and the Rio+20 outcome
The Stockholm Convention and the Paris Agreement
20.x: Agenda 2030 grew from the Millennium Development Goals and the outcome of the Rio+20 Conference.
20.tq: Link the agenda to its stated development and conference antecedents.

20.s: Carrying capacity refers to:
o: The total quantity of minerals in the Earth’s crust
The maximum population an environment can support indefinitely without degradation
The annual rate of economic growth of a country
The maximum number of industries a city can legally establish
20.x: Carrying capacity is the maximum population that an environment can support indefinitely without degradation.
20.tq: Distinguish an ecological population concept from resource stocks and economic measures.

20.s:
The concern regarding the Earth’s finite carrying capacity is associated with which of the following works or events?
1. Limits to Growth
2. Our Common Future
3. United Nations Conference on Environment and Development, 1992
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: The finite carrying capacity of the Earth is a concern reflected in Limits to Growth, Our Common Future and the 1992 UNCED process.
20.tq: Use the comprehensive option when all three listed references address the same ecological limit.

20.s: Earth Overshoot Day is the date on which:
o: The global temperature first exceeds a fixed legal limit
Humanity’s annual demand on nature exceeds the Earth’s regeneration capacity for that year
The Earth completes one full cycle around the Sun
All countries formally adopt their annual environmental budgets
20.x: Earth Overshoot Day marks the point when humanity’s demand on nature in a year exceeds what the Earth can regenerate during that year.
20.tq: Identify the precise demand-versus-regeneration relationship in the definition.

20.s: Earth Overshoot Day is computed by the:
20.x: The Global Footprint Network computes Earth Overshoot Day. Plastic Overshoot Day is an analogous concept relating specifically to plastic use.
20.tq: Use the institutional-ownership trap and distinguish the ecological organisation from economic bodies.

20.s: Which of the following principles was NOT endorsed at the 1992 Rio process?
20.x: The precautionary principle, polluter pays principle and common but differentiated responsibilities were endorsed at Rio 1992. Unrestricted resource exploitation is contrary to sustainable development.
20.tq: Find the policy principle that contradicts the Rio sustainability framework.

20.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a 2015 Agenda 2030 milestone?
o: Adopted on 5 June 1992 at Rio de Janeiro
Adopted on 25 September 2015 at New York
20.x: Agenda 2030 was adopted on 25 September 2015 in New York. The other dates and places do not correspond to its adoption.
20.tq: Combine the exact date and venue to defeat swapped conference details.

20.s: According to the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026, India secured which position, representing its highest-ever rank?
20.x: India was ranked 94th in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026, its highest-ever position.
20.tq: Use the precise current-affairs figure and distinguish it from the preceding year's rank.

20.s: India's rank in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report improved from 99th in 2025 to 94th in 2026. This represents an improvement of:
20.x: India improved by five places, from 99th in 2025 to 94th in 2026.
20.tq: Subtract adjacent-year ranks rather than confusing the rank improvement with the longer-term gain.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's position in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026:
1. India ranked behind Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
2. India was found to be lagging on 13 of the 17 SDGs.
3. SDG 2 was identified as India's main area of concern.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: All three statements are correct. India ranked 94th, behind the four mentioned South Asian countries, lagged on 13 goals, and had SDG 2 as its principal concern.
20.tq: Check the complete set of country comparison, goal coverage and principal concern before selecting the coded combination.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's performance in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2025?
o: India ranked 94th of 167 with a score of about 67 and entered the top 100 for the first time.
India ranked 71st of 167 with a score of about 99 and entered the top 75 for the first time.
India ranked 99th of 167 with a score of about 67 and entered the top 100 for the first time.
India ranked 99th of 166 with a score of about 71 and remained outside the top 100.
20.x: In the 2025 SDSN report, India ranked 99th out of 167, scored approximately 67, and entered the top 100 for the first time.
20.tq: Separate the report year, rank, denominator and score instead of carrying figures over from another index.

20.s: Which of the following countries occupied the top position in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2025?
20.x: Finland was the highest-ranked country in the 2025 SDSN Sustainable Development Report, followed by Sweden and Denmark.
20.tq: Identify the first item in a short ranked list before considering the other leading countries.

20.s: India's first Voluntary National Review (VNR) on the Sustainable Development Goals was presented to the United Nations in:
20.x: India presented its first VNR to the United Nations in 2017.
20.tq: Distinguish the first reporting year from later VNR preparation and reporting years.

20.s: Which set of Sustainable Development Goals was covered in India's first Voluntary National Review presented in 2017?
20.x: India's first VNR covered seven goals: SDGs 1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 14 and 17.
20.tq: Start from the sure list membership and reject combinations containing substituted goal numbers.

20.s: The Voluntary National Review for 2025 was prepared by:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
20.x: India's 2025 VNR was prepared by NITI Aayog.
20.tq: Apply the 'who prepared or implemented it?' authority check to avoid institutional swaps.

20.s:
Which of the following was identified as a success contributing to India's SDG performance in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026?
1. DBT-led reduction in multidimensional poverty
2. Rural electrification
3. Digital connectivity
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: All three were identified as areas of progress: DBT contributed to reducing multidimensional poverty, rural electrification supported SDG 7, and digital connectivity supported SDG 9.
20.tq: Match each achievement with the reported progress areas before choosing the complete combination.

20.s: According to the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh was placed at which position among Indian States, with a score of 74?
20.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 and ranked ninth among Indian States in the SDG India Index 2023-24.
20.tq: Link the state score with its corresponding rank rather than confusing it with India's national score.

20.s: A State scoring 74 in the SDG India Index 2023-24 would be placed in which category?
20.x: The Frontrunner category covers scores from 65 to 99; Andhra Pradesh's score of 74 therefore places it in that category.
20.tq: Apply the score band to the hypothetical state instead of relying on the label alone.

20.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding SDG Index performance categories and scores:
List-I (Category)
A. Achiever
B. Frontrunner
C. Performer
D. Aspirant

List-II (Score)
1. 0–49
2. 50–65
3. 65–99
4. 100

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
20.x: Achiever corresponds to 100, Frontrunner to 65–99, Performer to 50–65, and Aspirant to 0–49.
20.tq: Start with the distinctive end categories, 100 and 0–49, then complete the middle pairings.

20.s: Which of the following correctly represents Andhra Pradesh's relative performance across selected SDGs in the SDG India Index 2023-24?
20.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first on SDG 7, second on SDG 14, third on SDG 1 and fourth on SDG 12.
20.tq: Preserve the order of the ranked goals; reversed comparisons are the principal trap.

20.s: Which Sustainable Development Goal saw Andhra Pradesh slip from 19th to 20th position and was identified as a concern?
20.x: SDG 4 was the area of concern, with Andhra Pradesh slipping from 19th to 20th position.
20.tq: Distinguish the concern indicator from the goals in which the State performed near the top.

20.s: The SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026 was presented at which event?
o: World Sustainable Development Summit at New Delhi
United Nations Climate Change Conference at Dubai
20.x: The 2026 SDSN Sustainable Development Report was presented at the 3rd Hamburg Sustainability Conference.
20.tq: Use the event-location association and reject famous but unrelated international forums.

20.s: Andhra Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Understanding with UN-Habitat for establishing a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in:
20.x: The proposed Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs is to be established in Amaravati under the MoU with UN-Habitat.
20.tq: Apply the location trap by distinguishing the named capital-region city from other prominent Andhra Pradesh cities.

20.s: The Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs proposed in Amaravati under the MoU with UN-Habitat is aligned primarily with:
20.x: The Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs is aligned with SDG 11, which concerns sustainable cities and communities.
20.tq: Infer the relevant goal from the precise subject of the initiative—urban affairs.

20.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the current regional comparison of India's SDG performance?
o: India leads all smaller South Asian neighbours and is on track for every goal.
India trails smaller South Asian neighbours but is off track on only 3 goals.
India leads Bhutan and Nepal but trails only Sri Lanka on all 17 goals.
India trails smaller South Asian neighbours and is off track on 13 of the 17 goals.
20.x: India continues to trail smaller South Asian neighbours and is off track on 13 of the 17 SDGs.
20.tq: Find the option that preserves both parts of the comparison: regional standing and number of goals off track.

20.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Brundtland Report — first definition of sustainable development; SDGs — target year 2040
Brundtland Report — first definition of sustainable development; SDGs — target year 2030
Brundtland Report — first definition of sustainable development in 1992; SDGs — target year 2030
Brundtland Report — first definition of sustainable development in 2015; SDGs — target year 2025
20.x: The Brundtland Report of 1987 is associated with the first definition of sustainable development, while the SDGs are intended to culminate in 2030.
20.tq: Separate the earlier conceptual milestone from the later SDG deadline and reject altered years.

21.s: The burden of proving that an activity is benign, in the context of the precautionary principle, rests upon:
o: The person or entity undertaking the activity
21.x: Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof shifts to the actor undertaking the potentially harmful activity to demonstrate that it is benign.
21.tq: Apply the principle by identifying who must establish that the risky activity is harmless.

21.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the scope of the Polluter Pays Principle?
o: Payment of a fixed penalty without restoration of the affected environment
Transfer of all environmental liabilities to the State
Bearing the costs of remediation as well as compensation for the damage caused
Payment only for the private compensation claimed by victims
21.x: The Polluter Pays Principle includes both remediation of the environmental damage and compensation for the affected persons or resources.
21.tq: Distinguish the complete legal consequence from the narrower idea of merely paying a fine.

21.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
a. Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
b. Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
c. M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
 d. M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath

List-II (Subject or principle)
i. Public trust doctrine
 ii. Oleum gas leak and absolute liability
 iii. Tanneries polluting the Palar River
 iv. Chemical units in Bichhri required to pay for clean-up

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
21.x: Vellore concerned Palar River pollution by tanneries and applied precautionary and polluter pays principles; Bichhri concerned chemical-unit clean-up; Oleum gas leak established absolute liability; Kamal Nath applied public trust doctrine.
21.tq: Start from the sure case-fact pair and eliminate codes with swapped cases.

21.s:
With reference to the Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case, consider the following statements:
1. It concerned pollution of the Palar River by tanneries.
2. It applied both the precautionary principle and the Polluter Pays Principle.
3. It concerned the diversion of forest land without Central approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: The Vellore case concerned tannery pollution of the Palar River and applied both principles. Diversion of forest land is associated with the Forest (Conservation) Act, not this case.
21.tq: Find the unrelated case-fact statement among closely connected environmental principles.

21.s: The principle of absolute liability, under which a hazardous industry is liable without exceptions, was laid down in connection with:
o: Pollution of the Palar River by tanneries
21.x: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987), arising from the Oleum gas leak, established absolute liability for hazardous industries without exceptions.
21.tq: Match the distinctive industrial accident with the legal principle it produced.

21.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: T.N. Godavarman case — any area recorded as forest
Taj Trapezium case — chemical units in Rajasthan required to pay for clean-up
Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar — pollution-free water and air under Article 21
M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath — State holds natural resources in trust for the public
21.x: The Bichhri case of Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action concerned chemical units in Rajasthan and clean-up costs. The Taj Trapezium case mandated the use of CNG.
21.tq: Check the case-specific subject rather than matching merely by environmental theme.

21.s: The decision that recognised pollution-free water and air as part of the right under Article 21 was given in:
o: T.N. Godavarman v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
21.x: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991) recognised the right to pollution-free water and air under Article 21.
21.tq: Use the Article 21 association to distinguish the case from other environmental precedents.

21.s: Which environmental case is associated with the mandating of CNG?
21.x: The Taj Trapezium case (1997) mandated the use of CNG as an environmental protection measure.
21.tq: Identify the unusual remedy associated with the correct case.

21.s: The T.N. Godavarman case is significant because its forest-related protection covers:
o: Only forests located within protected areas
Only reserved forests notified under the Wildlife Act
21.x: The T.N. Godavarman case (1995) covers any area recorded as forest, rather than only formally notified reserved forests.
21.tq: Test the scope of the category by focusing on the word ‘any’.

21.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 — protection of wildlife and habitats and regulation of hunting
Water Act, 1974 — control of air pollution only
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the Pollution Control Boards
21.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 protects wildlife and habitats and regulates hunting. The other purposes are associated with different laws.
21.tq: Match each Act with its core purpose and reject neighbouring environmental subjects.

21.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in:
21.x: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1974 and created the pollution control boards.
21.tq: Separate the closely spaced years of the principal environmental Acts.

21.s: The Central Pollution Control Board is best described as:
o: A constitutional body created under the Environment Protection Act
A judicial body constituted under Article 21
A statutory body under the Water Act, also functioning under the Air Act, 1981
A temporary body established under the EIA Notification, 2006
21.x: The CPCB was established in 1974 as a statutory body under the Water Act and also operates under the Air Act, 1981. It sets standards and monitors air and water.
21.tq: Identify the correct parent statute and distinguish a statutory body from constitutional and temporary bodies.

21.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior Central approval for diversion of forest land.
2. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1981.
3. The Air Act was amended in 1987 to introduce stricter penalties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All three statements are correct. The Forest Act requires prior Central approval for diversion, while the Air Act dates from 1981 and was amended in 1987 with stricter penalties.
21.tq: Verify each year and the associated legal consequence before selecting the coded combination.

21.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — legal basis for EIA and CRZ notifications
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the pollution control boards
21.x: The pollution control boards were created under the Water Act, 1974. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law whose Section 3 supports EIA and CRZ notifications.
21.tq: Reject the option that assigns a body’s origin to the wrong statute.

21.s: The Ganga Action Plan began in:
21.x: The Ganga Action Plan began in 1986; 1982 is the incorrect year associated with it.
21.tq: Discriminate between the stated year and the close but incorrect alternative.

21.s: Under the Water Act and the Air Act, the respective provisions under which State Pollution Control Boards can levy compensation are:
21.x: SPCBs can levy compensation under Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act.
21.tq: Keep the two similar statutory section numbers in their correct Act-wise order.

21.s: Under the Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026, the Fund is constituted under which provision, and how is it divided between the States/Union Territories and the Centre?
o: Section 33A of the Water Act; 75% and 25%
Section 31A of the Air Act; 25% and 75%
21.x: The Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026 place the Fund under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act. Seventy-five per cent goes to States/UTs and 25 per cent to the Centre.
21.tq: Combine the enabling provision with the percentage split instead of treating them as separate figures.

21.s: The Eco-Mark scheme was launched in:
21.x: The Eco-Mark scheme was launched in 1991 to label environment-friendly consumer products.
21.tq: Use the chronology of environmental initiatives to distinguish the scheme’s launch year.

21.s: Which symbol is used as the logo of the Eco-Mark scheme?
21.x: The Eco-Mark logo is an earthen pot, used for labelling environment-friendly consumer products.
21.tq: Test the distinctive logo rather than the general environmental purpose of the scheme.

21.s: Which institution certifies products under the Eco-Mark scheme?
21.x: The Bureau of Indian Standards certifies products under the Eco-Mark scheme.
21.tq: Identify the administering certification institution and avoid confusing it with an environmental regulator.

21.s: Which one of the following is NOT covered among the products notified under the Eco-Mark scheme?
21.x: The notified product groups include soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics, aerosols and food items. Drugs and antibiotics are not covered.
21.tq: Find the excluded product from a list containing several covered categories.

21.s: The National Environment Policy was adopted in:
21.x: The National Environment Policy was adopted in 2006 and serves as India’s overarching environment policy.
21.tq: Distinguish the policy year from the years of the umbrella Act and Eco-Mark scheme.

21.s: The central idea of the National Environment Policy, 2006 is that:
o: Economic growth must always be stopped to protect natural resources
Conservation and livelihood security are mutually exclusive
Environmental protection should be separated from development planning
Conservation and livelihood security can proceed together
21.x: The NEP 2006 rests on the idea that conservation and livelihood security go together rather than being opposed to each other.
21.tq: Apply the policy’s balancing approach instead of choosing an extreme conservation-versus-development position.

21.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the National Environment Policy, 2006?
o: Elimination of all development activity in ecologically sensitive areas
Integration of environmental concerns into development plans
21.x: The NEP objectives include conservation of critical resources, inter-generational equity and integration of environment into development plans. It does not prescribe elimination of all development activity.
21.tq: Reject the extreme statement that goes beyond the policy’s balanced objectives.

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Environment Policy, 2006:
1. It seeks efficient use of environmental resources.
2. It includes good environmental governance as an objective.
3. It recognises livelihood security for poor tribal communities.
4. It includes the precautionary approach, Polluter Pays Principle and public trust doctrine among its principles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All four statements correctly describe the objectives and principles of the National Environment Policy, 2006.
21.tq: Check whether each listed objective or principle belongs to the same policy framework before choosing the complete combination.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of EIA in India:
1. The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
2. Before the 1994 notification, environmental clearance was only an administrative decision.
3. The EIA Notification, 2006 replaced the 1994 notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: The 1994 notification was issued on 27 January under the EPA, clearance had earlier been only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.
21.tq: Arrange the legal transition in sequence and verify both the date and the status of clearance before 1994.

21.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
21.x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
21.tq: Focus on the reversed comparison between the old and new bases of appraisal.

21.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, environmental clearance became compulsory for how many project categories?
21.x: The EIA Notification, 2006 made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
21.tq: Test the precise statutory count rather than the broader idea of compulsory clearance.

21.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Category)
a. Category A
b. Category B
c. Category A clearance
 d. Category B clearance

List-II (Authority)
i. State Environment Impact Assessment Authority
 ii. State Expert Appraisal Committee
 iii. Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre
 iv. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
21.x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC. Category B projects are appraised by the State EAC and cleared by SEIAA.
21.tq: Separate the appraisal authority from the clearance authority before matching the categories.

21.s: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of stages in the EIA process?
21.x: The stages are Screening, Scoping, Public consultation and Appraisal. Screening applies only to Category B projects.
21.tq: Use the process sequence and place the decision-oriented appraisal stage last.

21.s:
With reference to EIA stages, consider the following statements:
1. Screening is applicable only to Category B projects.
2. Defence and strategic projects are exempt from public consultation.
3. Scoping precedes public consultation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All three statements are correct. Screening is limited to Category B projects, the specified defence and strategic projects are exempt from public consultation, and scoping comes before public consultation.
21.tq: Check the exception and the process order together rather than treating every EIA stage as universal.

21.s: Which of the following was proposed by the Draft EIA 2020 notification?
o: Abolition of environmental clearance for Category A projects
Post-facto clearance on payment of penalties and a shorter public consultation period
Removal of all public consultation requirements
Replacement of impact potential by investment size
21.x: The Draft EIA 2020 proposed post-facto clearance upon payment of penalties and a shorter public consultation period. It attracted widespread protest and was not finalised.
21.tq: Identify the exact controversial proposals without extending them into absolute claims.

21.s: Which one of the following statements regarding post-facto environmental clearance is correct?
o: Vanashakti v. Union of India struck down the 2021 Office Memorandum allowing ex post facto clearances.
The S.P. Muthuraman case held retrospective environmental clearances legal.
Vanashakti v. Union of India upheld the 2021 Office Memorandum allowing ex post facto clearances.
Both cases made post-facto clearance compulsory for Category B projects.
21.x: In Vanashakti v. Union of India, the Supreme Court struck down the 2021 Office Memorandum permitting ex post facto clearances. The S.P. Muthuraman case also held retrospective environmental clearances illegal.
21.tq: Use the legal outcome trap by distinguishing ‘struck down’ and ‘upheld’ and checking the case names.

21.s: The ruling in Vanashakti v. Union of India regarding ex post facto clearances applies:
o: Only to projects in forest areas
Retrospectively to every project approved since 1994
21.x: The Supreme Court’s ruling striking down the 2021 Office Memorandum applies prospectively.
21.tq: Discriminate between the legal effects of prospective and retrospective operation.

21.s: In the event of the lapse of a State’s SEIAA or SEAC, which bodies step in as backup bodies under the July 2026 arrangement?
21.x: The backup bodies are SAEIA and SCEIA, which step in when a State’s SEIAA or SEAC lapses.
21.tq: Distinguish the specially named backup bodies from the regular central and State authorities.

21.s: What change was made in July 2026 concerning the tenure of members of the relevant EIA bodies?
o: It was increased from two years to five years
It was reduced from four years to two years
It was increased from three years to four years
