37.s: Antyodaya was first launched in:
37.x: The Antyodaya programme was first launched in Rajasthan in 1977.
37.tq: Recall the launch-place and year combination.

37.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Twenty Point Programme is correct?
37.x: The Twenty Point Programme was launched in 1975 and restructured in 1982, 1986 and 2006.
37.tq: Separate the original launch year from the successive restructuring years.

37.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Community Development Programme
B. Launch of the Twenty Point Programme
C. First launch of Antyodaya
D. Establishment of RUDSETI
37.x: The Community Development Programme began in 1952, the Twenty Point Programme was launched in 1975, Antyodaya began in 1977, and RUDSETI was established in 1982.
37.tq: Use the first and last dates to anchor the sequence, then place the middle events.

37.s: RUDSETI stands for:
o: Regional Union for Development and Self Employment Training Institution
Rural Development and Social Education Training Initiative
Rural Development and Self Employment Training Institute
Rural Employment and Development Support Training Institute
37.x: RUDSETI stands for Rural Development and Self Employment Training Institute.
37.tq: Test exact expansion of an institutional acronym.

37.s: Which of the following statements about RUDSETI is correct?
o: It was established at Ujire in Karnataka in 1982 and trains rural youth for self-employment.
It was established in Rajasthan in 1977 to provide micro-credit to women.
It was established in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 to refinance banks.
It was established in Delhi in 1975 to restructure the Twenty Point Programme.
37.x: RUDSETI was established at Ujire in Karnataka in 1982 and trains rural youth for self-employment. It became a model for the present RSETIs.
37.tq: Combine location, year and function while rejecting swapped institutional roles.

37.s: The Community Development Programme, described as the ‘mother of social development programmes’, was launched on:
37.x: The Community Development Programme was launched on 2 October 1952 and is described as the mother of social development programmes.
37.tq: Use the exact commemorative date associated with the programme.

37.s: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD as a pilot in:
37.x: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme as a pilot in 1992.
37.tq: Distinguish the pilot year from the earlier period of SHG-bank linkage pioneering.

37.s: Which one of the following is NOT a role associated with NABARD in the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme?
o: Replacing all commercial banks as direct lenders to SHGs
37.x: NABARD refinances banks and trains and promotes SHGs; it does not replace all commercial banks as direct lenders to SHGs.
37.tq: Find the institutional role that goes beyond the stated functions of the organisation.

37.s: A major lending feature of self-help groups under the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme is that they:
o: Can borrow only from foreign development agencies
Borrow only against immovable property as collateral
Borrow without collateral and generally at lower interest rates
Receive grants that cannot be repaid
37.x: SHGs can borrow collateral-free and generally obtain loans at lower interest rates under the linkage programme.
37.tq: Apply the defining lending condition to a practical borrowing situation.

37.s: Which State is reported as first in the country in SHG-bank linkage under APSES 2024–25?
37.x: Andhra Pradesh is reported as first in the country in SHG-bank linkage under APSES 2024–25.
37.tq: Use the State-specific performance distinction rather than a generic SHG association.

37.s: Which of the following countries are reported to be studying the NRLM SHG model?
o: Botswana, Namibia, Tunisia, Libya and Somalia
Ethiopia, Tanzania, Malawi, Kenya and Rwanda
Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Egypt and Morocco
Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Sudan and Algeria
37.x: Ethiopia, Tanzania, Malawi, Kenya and Rwanda are reported to be studying the NRLM SHG model.
37.tq: Recall the complete country list without substituting other African countries.

37.s: As reported in February 2026, the number of Lakhpati Didis had crossed:
37.x: Lakhpati Didis had crossed 2 crore as reported on 3 February 2026.
37.tq: Identify the correct scale of a current livelihood indicator.

37.s: Multidimensional poverty in India declined from 29.17 per cent in 2013–14 to what level in 2022–23?
37.x: The multidimensional poverty ratio declined from 29.17 per cent in 2013–14 to 11.28 per cent in 2022–23.
37.tq: Distinguish a precise percentage from nearby altered figures.

37.s: The decline in multidimensional poverty from 2013–14 to 2022–23 is associated with approximately how many people?
37.x: The decline in multidimensional poverty is associated with approximately 25 crore people.
37.tq: Match the percentage trend with its associated absolute number.

37.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or challenge relating to the SHG movement?
o: Debt stress caused by poor financial literacy
37.x: Uneven SHG quality, weak market links, debt stress due to poor financial literacy and political interference are identified challenges. The material does not identify an absence of political interference as a criticism.
37.tq: Select the option that reverses a stated challenge.

37.s: A self-help group has poor financial literacy and faces repayment pressure from multiple borrowings. This situation most directly illustrates:
o: The formalisation of SHGs during the Seventh Plan
Debt stress associated with the SHG movement
The collateral-free nature of SHG lending
37.x: Debt stress arising from poor financial literacy is one of the criticisms and challenges associated with the SHG movement.
37.tq: Apply a stated criticism to a short practical case.

37.s: Which of the following best explains the significance of the Andhra Pradesh model in the national livelihood mission context?
o: The SERP/Velugu model of Andhra Pradesh became a template for NRLM.
The model restricted SHGs to urban areas only.
The model replaced NABARD as the national refinancing agency.
The model was created exclusively for training government employees.
37.x: Andhra Pradesh’s SERP/Velugu model became a template for the National Rural Livelihoods Mission.
37.tq: Identify the State model that influenced a national programme.

37.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh and self-help groups:
1. Andhra Pradesh’s SERP/Velugu model became a template for NRLM.
2. Andhra Pradesh leads the country in SHG-bank linkage.
3. Andhra Pradesh was the place where the Grameen Bank was founded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Grameen Bank model originated in Bangladesh, not Andhra Pradesh.
37.tq: Separate Andhra Pradesh-specific achievements from the foreign origin of the Grameen model.

37.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its broad focus?
o: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh — Micro-credit to poor women in the unorganised sector
Swayamsiddha — Rural youth self-employment training at Ujire
RUDSETI — Integrated empowerment of women through SHGs
Community Development Programme — SHG-bank linkage pilot of 1992
37.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh focused on micro-credit to poor women in the unorganised sector. The other options interchange the functions of Swayamsiddha, RUDSETI and NABARD’s 1992 pilot.
37.tq: Start from the sure objective-function pair and reject cross-linked distractors.

38.s: Atal Pension Yojana, launched on 9 May 2015, primarily targets which category of persons?
o: Small and marginal farmers between 40 and 60 years
Unorganised-sector workers in the age group of 18–40 years
38.x: Atal Pension Yojana targets workers in the unorganised sector who enter the scheme between 18 and 40 years of age.
38.tq: Directly identify the target group and entry age of the scheme.

38.s: Under Atal Pension Yojana, the Government's co-contribution for eligible early subscribers was—
o: The entire subscriber contribution for three years
A fixed ₹5,000 per year for five years
50% of the subscriber's contribution or ₹1,000 per year, whichever was lower, for five years
50% of the subscriber's contribution without any monetary ceiling for ten years
38.x: For eligible persons joining before 31 December 2015, the Government contributed 50% of the subscriber's contribution or ₹1,000 per year, whichever was lower, for five years.
38.tq: Split the option by checking both the percentage and the monetary ceiling.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly states the pension benefit under Atal Pension Yojana?
o: ₹3,000 per month from the age of 55 years
₹1,000 per year after the age of 60 years
₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month from the age of 60 years
₹5,000 per month from the age of 58 years
38.x: Atal Pension Yojana provides a guaranteed pension ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month at the age of 60, depending on the contribution.
38.tq: Use the benefit range and commencement age to eliminate altered figures.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM):
1. It covers unorganised workers aged 18–40 years.
2. The monthly income limit is ₹15,000.
3. The subscriber must already be covered under NPS, ESIC or EPFO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: PM-SYM covers unorganised workers aged 18–40 years with monthly income up to ₹15,000. It excludes persons covered under NPS, ESIC or EPFO, making statement 3 false.
38.tq: Find the exclusion hidden in statement 3 by reversing the eligibility condition.

38.s: The contribution structure of PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan is based on—
o: Equal matching contributions by the worker and the Central Government
Voluntary contributions without any Government matching
Contribution only by the State Government
A fixed contribution made entirely by the employer
38.x: PM-SYM follows a matching contribution structure in which the worker and the Central Government contribute equal amounts.
38.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the matching contribution.

38.s: PM Kisan Maan-dhan is intended primarily for—
o: Small and marginal farmers entering between 18 and 40 years
38.x: PM Kisan Maan-dhan targets small and marginal farmers who join between 18 and 40 years of age.
38.tq: Match the scheme with its specific occupational beneficiary group.

38.s: Which statement correctly describes the contribution under PM Kisan Maan-dhan?
o: Every farmer contributes exactly ₹500 per month without Government support.
The contribution is determined by entry age, is below ₹100 per month, and is matched by the Centre.
The contribution is determined only by landholding size and is paid by the State Government.
The Centre contributes, but the farmer does not make any contribution.
38.x: Under PM Kisan Maan-dhan, the farmer's contribution depends on entry age, is below ₹100 per month, and is matched by the Central Government.
38.tq: Check the combined conditions of age-linked contribution, amount and matching support.

38.s: The pension payable under PM Kisan Maan-dhan at the age of 60 years is—
38.x: PM Kisan Maan-dhan provides a pension of ₹3,000 per month from the age of 60 years.
38.tq: Test the scheme-specific benefit against nearby pension amounts.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Unified Pension Scheme?
o: It is compulsory for all private-sector employees and is market-linked.
It is restricted to small and marginal farmers.
It provides only an insurance cover without pension benefits.
It is an option for Central Government employees covered under NPS and is Government-backed.
38.x: The Unified Pension Scheme is a Government-backed option for Central Government employees under NPS.
38.tq: Identify the beneficiary category and institutional linkage.

38.s: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, an assured pension equal to what proportion of average basic pay is available after 25 years of service?
o: 40% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
60% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
25% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
38.x: The Unified Pension Scheme assures 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years of service.
38.tq: Use the service-period and percentage figures together to identify the precise provision.

38.s:
Which of the following statements about the National Pension System is correct?
1. It is based on defined contribution and is market-linked.
2. It covers Government, private and unorganised-sector participants.
3. Minors may participate through NPS Vatsalya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: NPS is a defined-contribution, market-linked system open to Government, private and unorganised-sector participants; minors can participate through NPS Vatsalya.
38.tq: Accept the option containing all three independently supported features.

38.s: The regulator of the National Pension System and the authority administering Atal Pension Yojana under the NPS architecture is—
38.x: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) regulates NPS and administers APY under the NPS architecture.
38.tq: Apply the ‘who regulates this financial product?’ method.

38.s: The National Pension System became compulsory for Central Government civilian employees joining on or after—
38.x: NPS is compulsory for Central Government civilian employees who joined service on or after 1 January 2004.
38.tq: Distinguish the exact commencement date from nearby policy dates.

38.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an NPS account?
o: An account can be opened by one person for any third person.
It is based on defined contribution and market-linked returns.
Minors may participate through NPS Vatsalya.
It may cover Government, private and unorganised-sector participants.
38.x: An NPS account cannot be opened for a third person. The other statements describe features of NPS.
38.tq: Find the statement that reverses the specific account-opening restriction.

38.s: Atal Pension Yojana completed ten years in—
38.x: Atal Pension Yojana was launched in 2015 and completed ten years in 2025.
38.tq: Calculate the anniversary from the stated launch year.

38.s: Which of the following correctly represents the age band, annual premium and life cover under PMJJBY?
38.x: PMJJBY is a life insurance scheme for persons aged 18–50 years, with an annual premium of ₹436 and cover of ₹2 lakh.
38.tq: Separate PMJJBY from PMSBY by comparing type, age, premium and cover.

38.s: Which of the following correctly represents the age band, current annual premium and cover under PMSBY?
o: 18–70 years; ₹20; ₹2 lakh for death or full disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability
18–59 years; ₹20; ₹1 lakh for all forms of disability
38.x: PMSBY is available from 18 to 70 years at ₹20 per year, providing ₹2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.
38.tq: Check all four dimensions of the insurance table before selecting an option.

38.s: The annual premium of PMSBY was ₹12 up to—
38.x: The PMSBY premium remained ₹12 up to 31 May 2022; it was raised from 1 June 2022.
38.tq: Use the ‘true start, false end’ date distinction in a premium revision question.

38.s: Why was the PMSBY premium revised from 1 June 2022?
o: Claims had exceeded premiums, and this was the first revision since 2015.
The scheme changed from accident insurance to life insurance.
The age eligibility was reduced from 70 to 50 years.
The scheme was merged with PMJJBY.
38.x: PMSBY's premium was revised from 1 June 2022 because claims exceeded premiums; it was the first revision since the scheme began in 2015.
38.tq: Link the policy change to its stated financial cause and timing.

38.s: Which statement correctly compares the reported enrolments under PMJJBY and PMSBY?
o: PMJJBY had 27.33 crore and PMSBY had 57.92 crore enrolments.
PMJJBY had 57.92 crore and PMSBY had 27.33 crore enrolments.
38.x: The reported enrolments were 27.33 crore under PMJJBY and 57.92 crore under PMSBY.
38.tq: Compare the paired figures rather than recalling either figure in isolation.

38.s: Both PMJJBY and PMSBY are linked to PMJDY accounts primarily through—
o: Manual cash collection at post offices
Automatic debit of the premium from the account
38.x: Both insurance schemes are linked to PMJDY accounts through auto-debit of the applicable premium.
38.tq: Identify the operational mechanism connecting the schemes to bank accounts.

38.s: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana provides life and disability cover to—
o: Only small and marginal farmers below 18 years
Rural landless households, generally in the age group of 18–59 years
38.x: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana is an LIC-run life and disability insurance scheme for rural landless households aged 18–59 years.
38.tq: Match the insurance scheme with its occupational and age-based target group.

38.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Health Insurance Scheme for weavers is correct?
1. It covers a weaver's family of four consisting of the self, spouse and two children.
2. At least 50% of the weaver's income must come from handloom work.
3. Both male and female weavers are eligible.
4. A prescribed age cap is a criterion for eligibility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The scheme covers a family of four, requires at least 50% income from handloom work, and admits both male and female weavers. An age cap is not an eligibility criterion, so statement 4 is false.
38.tq: Locate the exception: the apparently plausible age condition is not required.

38.s: Direct Benefit Transfer was piloted on—
38.x: DBT was piloted on 1 January 2013 with seven schemes in 20 districts.
38.tq: Distinguish the pilot date from the later national launch of PAHAL.

38.s: At the pilot stage, Direct Benefit Transfer covered—
38.x: The initial DBT pilot covered seven schemes in 20 districts under UPA-II.
38.tq: Check the order of the two quantities: schemes first and districts second.

38.s: DBT was scaled up in 2015 primarily through the use of—
o: The National Food Security framework alone
The Goods and Services Tax network
38.x: After its pilot, DBT was scaled up in 2015 using the JAM trinity of Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile.
38.tq: Identify the institutional platform associated with the scale-up phase.

38.s: During FY 2024–25, DBT transferred approximately—
38.x: In FY 2024–25, ₹6.9 lakh crore was transferred directly through 327 schemes.
38.tq: Keep the amount and scheme count paired; distractors reverse or alter one figure.

38.s: The estimated savings from DBT during FY 2024–25, owing to removal of ghost and duplicate beneficiaries, were—
38.x: Removal of ghost and duplicate beneficiaries was estimated to generate savings of ₹2–3 lakh crore.
38.tq: Distinguish the lakh-crore scale from smaller monetary units.

38.s: Which mechanism routes Aadhaar-linked DBT payments, while AePS is used for cash withdrawal at micro-ATMs?
38.x: The Aadhaar Payment Bridge System routes Aadhaar-linked payments, whereas the Aadhaar-enabled Payment System facilitates cash withdrawal at micro-ATMs.
38.tq: Separate the payment-routing system from the cash-withdrawal service.

38.s: PAHAL, the DBT scheme for LPG, was launched nationally on—
38.x: PAHAL was launched nationally on 1 January 2015 and became the first application of JAM for LPG subsidy transfer.
38.tq: Discriminate between the DBT pilot date, PAHAL date and Ujjwala date.

38.s: Under PAHAL, the LPG subsidy is—
o: Paid directly into the beneficiary's bank account
Paid only in cash through LPG distributors
Transferred to the State Government treasury without beneficiary linkage
Credited to the mobile operator's account
38.x: PAHAL transfers the LPG subsidy directly into the beneficiary's bank account.
38.tq: Apply the core meaning of DBT to the LPG subsidy process.

38.s: The principal objective of Ujjwala is to provide—
o: Free LPG connections to women from BPL households and reduce indoor air pollution
LPG cylinders exclusively to Government employees
Free mobile phones to all rural women
Subsidised electricity connections to all urban households
38.x: Ujjwala provides free LPG connections to women belonging to BPL households, with the objective of reducing indoor air pollution.
38.tq: Connect the beneficiary group with the stated environmental and health objective.

38.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the JAM trinity.
List-I (Component)
a. Jan Dhan
b. Aadhaar
c. Mobile
List-II (Role)
i. Communication and intimation channel
ii. Biometric identity for beneficiary verification
iii. Bank account serving as destination for funds
Choose the correct answer:
38.x: Jan Dhan provides the bank account, Aadhaar verifies identity biometrically, and Mobile serves as the communication or intimation channel.
38.tq: Start from the sure pair: Jan Dhan is the bank-account component.

38.s: The JAM trinity was first proposed in—
38.x: The JAM trinity was first proposed in the Economic Survey 2014–15.
38.tq: Distinguish the proposal year from the later DBT scale-up year.

38.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the India Stack layer with its examples?
1. Presence-less layer — Aadhaar authentication
2. Paperless layer — e-KYC, e-Sign and DigiLocker
3. Cashless layer — UPI and AePS
4. Consent layer — DEPA
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All four matches are correct: Aadhaar authentication is presence-less; e-KYC, e-Sign and DigiLocker are paperless; UPI and AePS are cashless; and DEPA forms the consent layer.
38.tq: Verify each layer-example pair before accepting the comprehensive option.

38.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the four India Stack layers as listed with their functions?
38.x: The layers are presence-less, paperless, cashless and consent, represented respectively by Aadhaar authentication; e-KYC/e-Sign/DigiLocker; UPI/AePS; and DEPA.
38.tq: Use the sequence of layers and check the first and last positions.

38.s: Which statement about Jeevan Pramaan is correct?
o: It enables pensioners to create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics and was launched in 2014.
It is an LPG subsidy platform launched in 2015 without Aadhaar authentication.
It is a pension contribution platform available only to minors.
It is an accident insurance scheme launched in 2014 for workers aged 18–70 years.
38.x: Jeevan Pramaan was launched in 2014 and enables pensioners to create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics.
38.tq: Identify the service from its distinctive function rather than its general pension association.

38.s: Which applications are associated with the National Social Assistance Programme in the context of digital life certification?
o: Digital Life Certificate App and SAMBAL app
38.x: NSAP uses the Digital Life Certificate App and the SAMBAL app.
38.tq: Match the welfare programme with its named digital applications.

38.s: Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be made a condition for receiving—
o: Subsidies from the Consolidated Fund of India
38.x: Section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be required for subsidies charged to the Consolidated Fund.
38.tq: Use the exact statutory section and its limited welfare-related scope.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Puttaswamy judgements:
1. In 2017, a nine-judge Bench held privacy to be a fundamental right under Article 21.
2. In 2018, a five-judge Bench upheld Aadhaar for welfare and subsidies under Section 7.
3. The 2018 judgement struck down private use of Aadhaar under Section 57.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All three statements are correct. The 2017 nine-judge Bench recognised privacy under Article 21; the 2018 five-judge Bench upheld Aadhaar for welfare under Section 7 and struck down private use under Section 57.
38.tq: Track the two judgements separately by year, Bench strength and outcome.

38.s: The 2018 Aadhaar judgement was delivered by a five-judge Bench with what majority on the relevant issues?
38.x: The 2018 Aadhaar judgement was delivered by a five-judge Bench with a 4:1 majority.
38.tq: Distinguish the Bench strength from the majority ratio.

38.s:
Which of the following is a recognised challenge associated with Aadhaar-enabled service delivery?
1. Exclusion caused by biometric authentication failure, especially for elderly persons and labourers with worn fingerprints.
2. Privacy concerns arising from centralised data.
3. Complete elimination of all identity-verification risks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Biometric failure can exclude elderly persons and labourers with worn fingerprints, while centralised data raises privacy concerns. Aadhaar does not eliminate all identity-verification risks, so statement 3 is false.
38.tq: Reject the extreme claim in statement 3 and retain the two stated challenges.

38.s: Which Department is responsible for implementing the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana?
o: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment
38.x: The Department of Financial Services implements the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana.
38.tq: Identify the ministry or department that performs the implementation function.

38.s: Which one of the following is a basic feature of an account opened under the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana?
38.x: PMJDY provides basic bank accounts that can be maintained without a minimum balance.
38.tq: Distinguish an inclusion-oriented feature from restrictive banking conditions.

38.s:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. The RuPay debit card carries accident insurance cover of ₹2 lakh.
2. The overdraft facility has been raised to ₹10,000.
3. The accident insurance cover was originally ₹5 lakh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The RuPay card accident cover was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh, and the overdraft limit was raised from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000. Statement 3 is false because the original cover was ₹1 lakh.
38.tq: Split the statements by checking the revised figures against the original figures.

38.s: After 14 August 2018, the focus of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana shifted from:
o: Rural households to urban households only
Every unbanked adult to every household
Every household to every unbanked adult
38.x: The focus changed from covering every household to covering every unbanked adult.
38.tq: Test the direction of change in a policy target rather than merely recalling both terms.

38.s:
Which of the following was included in Phase II of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana during 2015–2018?
1. Overdraft facility
2. Credit Guarantee Fund for overdraft defaults
3. Unorganised-sector pensions under Swavalamban
4. Replacement of RuPay cards by credit cards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: Phase II included the overdraft facility, a Credit Guarantee Fund for overdraft defaults and unorganised-sector pensions under Swavalamban. Replacement of RuPay cards by credit cards was not a stated feature.
38.tq: Find the one unrelated policy measure among closely connected programme features.

38.s: As on 19 August 2026, which one of the following correctly represents the number of PMJDY accounts and the number of rural and semi-urban accounts respectively?
38.x: PMJDY had 59.09 crore accounts, of which 45.95 crore were in rural and semi-urban areas as on 19 August 2026.
38.tq: Match the total with its corresponding geographical sub-total.

38.s: Which pair correctly represents the PMJDY figures reported as on 19 August 2026?
o: Women account holders—32.92 crore; deposits—₹3,16,514 crore
Women account holders—45.95 crore; deposits—₹2,30,226 crore
Women account holders—32.92 crore; deposits—₹15,670 crore
Women account holders—59.09 crore; deposits—₹3,16,514 crore
38.x: The number of women account holders was 32.92 crore and deposits amounted to ₹3,16,514 crore.
38.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and reject combinations using the total or sub-total figures.

38.s: The deposits under PMJDY increased approximately how many times between March 2015 and 19 August 2026?
38.x: Deposits increased from ₹15,670 crore in March 2015 to ₹3,16,514 crore, approximately a twenty-fold increase.
38.tq: Estimate the order of magnitude from the initial and final figures.

38.s: The National Social Assistance Programme was launched in 1995 under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
38.x: NSAP was launched in 1995 under the Ministry of Rural Development.
38.tq: Use the implementing ministry as the identifying feature of the programme.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Social Assistance Programme:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
2. It fulfils the directive contained in Article 41 of the Constitution.
3. It is intended for Below Poverty Line households.
4. It became a Core of Core scheme from 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: NSAP is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for BPL households, fulfils Article 41 and has been a Core of Core scheme since 2016.
38.tq: When all statements describe separate institutional features, test whether the complete combination is valid.

38.s: Under the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, the monthly central assistance is:
o: ₹200 for 60–79 years and ₹300 for 80 years and above
₹500 for 60–79 years and ₹1,000 for 80 years and above
₹200 for 60–79 years and ₹500 for 80 years and above
₹300 for 60–79 years and ₹500 for 80 years and above
38.x: IGNOAPS provides ₹200 per month to persons aged 60–79 years and ₹500 per month to those aged 80 years and above.
38.tq: Compare the age bands before selecting the corresponding benefit.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly states the assistance under the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme?
o: ₹300 per month to widows aged 40–79 years and ₹500 to those aged 80 years and above
₹500 per month to widows aged 40–79 years and ₹300 to those aged 80 years and above
₹300 per month to all widows irrespective of age
₹200 per month to widows aged 40–79 years and ₹500 to those aged 80 years and above
38.x: IGNWPS provides ₹300 per month to widows aged 40–79 years and ₹500 per month to widows aged 80 years and above.
38.tq: Distinguish the widow-pension amount from the old-age-pension amount for the same age group.

A lump-sum payment on the death of the primary breadwinner
₹500 per month to all disabled persons irrespective of economic status
₹200 per month to all persons with disabilities

38.tq: Separate a regular pension benefit from a death-related lump-sum benefit.

38.s: The National Family Benefit Scheme under NSAP provides:
o: An overdraft facility to BPL households
A monthly pension to widows aged 40–79 years
A lump-sum benefit on the death of the primary breadwinner
38.x: NFBS provides a lump-sum benefit when the primary breadwinner of the household dies.
38.tq: Identify the event triggering the benefit rather than the beneficiary category alone.

38.s: Under the Annapurna scheme, free foodgrains are provided to:
o: Needy elderly persons who are not receiving IGNOAPS
All households affected by the death of a breadwinner
All rural households without bank accounts

38.s: The quantity of foodgrains provided monthly under the Annapurna scheme is:

38.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent National Social Assistance Programme figures?
o: About 2.09 crore beneficiaries and ₹6,952 crore for 2025–26
About 3.09 crore beneficiaries and ₹3,16,514 crore for 2025–26
About 3.09 crore beneficiaries and ₹9,652 crore for 2025–26
About 9.65 crore beneficiaries and ₹3,09,000 crore for 2025–26
38.x: The programme had about 3.09 crore beneficiaries and an allocation or expenditure figure of ₹9,652 crore for FY 2025–26.
38.tq: Match the beneficiary count with the associated financial figure.

38.s: States provide top-ups under NSAP in the range of approximately:
38.x: State governments provide additional assistance ranging from ₹50 to ₹3,200 per month.

38.s: The Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act was enacted in:
38.x: The Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act was enacted in 2008 and has subsequently been subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.
38.tq: Distinguish the original enactment year from the later consolidating code.

38.s: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is significant because it:
o: Subsumed the Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008
Transferred all social-security functions to State governments
Replaced two labour laws with one social-security scheme
38.x: The Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008 was subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.
38.tq: Identify the precise legal relationship between an earlier Act and a later code.

38.s: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is one of the four labour codes that replaced:
38.x: The four labour codes collectively replaced 29 earlier labour laws.
38.tq: Use the distinctive aggregate figure associated with a legislative consolidation.

38.s: The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 generally applies to establishments employing:
38.x: The EPF and MP Act, 1952 applies to establishments with 20 or more employees.
38.tq: Distinguish the statutory coverage threshold from nearby employment cut-offs.

38.s: Which of the following correctly represents the coverage of the Employees’ State Insurance system as on 31 March 2025?
o: 695 districts, 4.09 crore employees and 15.87 crore people
695 districts, 15.87 crore employees and 4.09 crore people
409 districts, 6.95 crore employees and 15.87 crore people
695 districts, 4.09 lakh employees and 1.587 crore people
38.x: ESI covered 695 districts, 4.09 crore employees and 15.87 crore people as on 31 March 2025.
38.tq: Keep the geographical, employee and population figures in their correct order.

38.s: India’s social protection coverage rose from 22 per cent in 2016 to what level in 2025?
38.x: Social protection coverage increased to 64.3 per cent in 2025 from 22 per cent in 2016.
38.tq: Test the trend and the final value together rather than either percentage alone.

38.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the beneficiaries of NTR Bharosa Pension in Andhra Pradesh?
38.x: NTR Bharosa Pension covers elderly persons, widows, single women, weavers, fishermen and artisans; it is not a universal pension for all formal-sector employees above 18 years.
38.tq: Find the category that falls outside the stated beneficiary groups.

38.s: NTR Bharosa Pension was earlier known as:
o: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
38.x: NTR Bharosa Pension was earlier known as YSR Pension Kanuka.
38.tq: Discriminate between similarly named Andhra Pradesh welfare programmes.

38.s: The monthly pension under NTR Bharosa Pension ranges approximately from:
38.x: NTR Bharosa Pension provides monthly pensions ranging from ₹4,000 to ₹15,000 to eligible beneficiaries.
38.tq: Select the correct lower and upper limits of the benefit range.

38.s: Which of the following correctly represents the December 2024 NTR Bharosa Pension disbursement in Andhra Pradesh?
38.x: In December 2024, 63,77,943 pensioners received ₹2,717.32 crore under the reported disbursement.
38.tq: Match the beneficiary count with its corresponding disbursement amount.

38.s: Which statement regarding Andhra Pradesh’s role in NSAP financing is correct?
o: The State tops up NSAP assistance from its own funds.
The State does not contribute any funds beyond the central assistance.
The State has transferred NSAP financing entirely to local bodies.
The State provides top-ups only for urban beneficiaries.
38.x: Andhra Pradesh supplements the central NSAP assistance through top-ups from its own funds.
38.tq: Identify the additional fiscal role played by the State government.

38.s: From January 2026, pension distribution under the Andhra Pradesh system was automated using:
38.x: From January 2026, real-time Aadhaar biometric verification was introduced to automate distribution and remove ghost beneficiaries.
38.tq: Match the administrative objective of eliminating ghosts with the appropriate verification technology.

38.s: The PMJDY completed 12 years in:
38.x: PMJDY completed 12 years in August 2026, when it had 59.09 crore accounts.
38.tq: Calculate the programme milestone from its stated anniversary year.

38.s: Which of the following is a major criticism concerning the old-age pension under NSAP?
o: Its real value has remained unchanged despite inflation.
Its real value has nearly doubled because of inflation.
Its real value has been reduced by nearly half because of inflation.
It has been converted entirely into a foodgrain benefit.
38.x: Inflation has eroded nearly half of the real value of the NSAP old-age pension.
38.tq: Distinguish nominal assistance from its inflation-adjusted real value.

38.s: The controversy in Kerala regarding pension delivery primarily concerned the choice between:
o: Bank accounts and postal savings certificates
DBT and doorstep delivery for elderly beneficiaries
38.x: Kerala’s decision to end doorstep pension delivery for DBT led to protests, highlighting the tension between digital transfers and doorstep delivery for the elderly.
38.tq: Identify the two alternative delivery mechanisms at the centre of the policy debate.

38.s: Approximately how many people escaped multidimensional poverty in India over the decade referred to in recent assessments?
38.x: An estimated 24.8 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty over the decade.
38.tq: Pay attention to the crore scale and the placement of the decimal.

38.s: India’s elderly population share is projected to rise from 10.1 per cent in 2021 to what level by 2036?
38.x: The elderly population share is projected to increase from 10.1 per cent in 2021 to 14.9 per cent in 2036, increasing the need for pensions.
38.tq: Compare the base-year share with the projected demographic share.

39.s: The National Food Security Act, 2013, provides which of the following to eligible persons?
o: A statutory right to minimum agricultural wages
A constitutional right to free electricity
A legal and justiciable right to subsidised foodgrains
A legal right to universal employment
39.x: The NFSA provides a legal and justiciable right to subsidised foodgrains and food and nutritional security.
39.tq: Identify the exact legal character of the Act rather than confusing it with a constitutional entitlement.

39.s: The National Food Security Act, 2013, commenced in which month and year?
39.x: The NFSA commenced in July 2013.
39.tq: Discriminate between the enactment period and the commencement date.

39.s: Which Ministry is primarily responsible for administering the National Food Security Act, 2013?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
39.x: The NFSA is administered by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
39.tq: Use the ministry-identification trap by distinguishing the food-distribution ministry from neighbouring ministries.

39.s: Under the National Food Security Act, the maximum coverage prescribed for the urban population is:
39.x: The NFSA provides for coverage of up to 50 per cent of the urban population and up to 75 per cent of the rural population.
39.tq: Split the rural and urban coverage figures before selecting the precise percentage.

39.s: The combined NFSA coverage of up to 75 per cent of the rural population and 50 per cent of the urban population is approximately equal to:
39.x: The prescribed rural and urban coverage together amount to approximately two-thirds, or about 67 per cent, of India’s population.
39.tq: Translate separate coverage percentages into the broad national proportion.

39.s: Under the NFSA, the entitlement of a Priority Household is:
o: 35 kg of foodgrains per person per month
5 kg of foodgrains per household per month
5 kg of foodgrains per person per month
7 kg of foodgrains per household per month
39.x: A Priority Household is entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month.
39.tq: Distinguish the per-person entitlement of a Priority Household from the per-household entitlement of AAY.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the entitlement of an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household under the NFSA?
o: 7 kg per person without any household ceiling
39.x: An AAY household is entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month under the NFSA framework.
39.tq: Watch the distinction between person-based and household-based quantities.

39.s: The issue prices prescribed in the NFSA for rice, wheat and coarse grains, respectively, are:
o: Rs 2, Rs 3 and Rs 1 per kg
Rs 3, Rs 2 and Rs 1 per kg
Rs 3, Rs 1 and Rs 2 per kg
Rs 1, Rs 2 and Rs 3 per kg
39.x: The Act prescribes issue prices of Rs 3 per kg for rice, Rs 2 for wheat and Rs 1 for coarse grains.
39.tq: Start from the sure rice pair and retain the exact order of the three commodities.

39.s: From 1 January 2023, NFSA foodgrains have been distributed free of cost under PMGKAY. This arrangement has been extended up to:
39.x: The free distribution of NFSA foodgrains under PMGKAY, beginning on 1 January 2023, has been extended up to 31 December 2028.
39.tq: Separate the commencement date from the extension end date.

39.s: Under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to:
o: A cash benefit of Rs 3,000 without meals
Only subsidised foodgrains for six months
Free meals and maternity benefit of not less than Rs 6,000
39.x: Section 4 provides pregnant women and lactating mothers with free meals and a maternity benefit of not less than Rs 6,000.
39.tq: Combine the two components of the entitlement instead of selecting the cash or meal component alone.

39.s:
With reference to grievance redress under the NFSA, consider the following statements:
1. An internal grievance-redress mechanism is provided.
2. A District Grievance Redressal Officer is provided under Section 15.
3. A State Food Commission is constituted in every State to monitor implementation and hear appeals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. The NFSA provides an internal mechanism and District Grievance Redressal Officers, while State Food Commissions monitor implementation and hear appeals.
39.tq: Check the institutional chain from the internal mechanism to district and State-level bodies.

39.s: For the purpose of issuing a ration card under the NFSA, the head of the household should ordinarily be:
o: The eldest male member irrespective of age
The person holding the Aadhaar card with the highest income
The eldest woman who is at least 18 years old
39.x: The eldest woman of the household, provided she is 18 years or older, is treated as the head for issuing the ration card.
39.tq: Apply the women-empowerment provision precisely, including the minimum age condition.

39.s: The draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposes to replace the AAY household entitlement with:
o: 7 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 35 kg per household
35 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 70 kg per household
10 kg per household, subject to a ceiling of 50 kg
5 kg per person, without a household ceiling
39.x: The draft Bill proposes 7 kg per person for AAY households, while retaining an overall cap of 35 kg per household.
39.tq: Read both parts of the proposed formula: the per-person figure and the household cap.

39.s: The proposed amendment to the AAY entitlement is intended principally to address which issue?
o: The inequity whereby smaller households receive more foodgrains per head
The shortage of Aadhaar-seeded ration cards
The lack of portability between States
The rising economic cost of foodgrain procurement
39.x: The stated aim is to remove the inequity under which smaller AAY households receive a greater quantity per person when the entitlement is fixed per household.
39.tq: Identify the policy rationale rather than confusing it with digitisation, portability or procurement issues.

39.s: Which of the following groups opposed the draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026?
o: Tamil Nadu, Kerala and the CPI(M)
Odisha, Assam and the Election Commission
39.x: Tamil Nadu, Kerala and the CPI(M) opposed the proposed amendment.
39.tq: Test the exact combination of political and State actors rather than a single-name association.

39.s: One Nation One Ration Card primarily enables:
o: Universal issue of new ration cards to urban residents
Inter-State portability of NFSA ration-card entitlements
Direct transfer of MSP to migrant workers
Replacement of all ration cards by voter identity cards
39.x: ONORC enables nationwide portability of NFSA ration-card entitlements, particularly benefiting migrant beneficiaries.
39.tq: Identify the central reform function and distinguish portability from replacement or cash transfer.

39.s: A migrant NFSA beneficiary using ONORC may draw foodgrains at an ePoS-enabled fair price shop after:
o: Obtaining a new ration card in the destination State only
Receiving prior approval from the District Collector of both States
Surrendering the ration card to the destination fair price shop
Biometric or Aadhaar authentication, with the family able to draw the balance at home
39.x: ONORC permits a migrant to lift the full or partial entitlement at an ePoS-enabled fair price shop after biometric or Aadhaar authentication; the family can draw the balance at the original location.
39.tq: Trace the portability process from authentication to division of the household entitlement.

39.s: One Nation One Ration Card was started in:
39.x: The ONORC initiative was started in August 2019; its nationwide coverage target was 1 June 2020.
39.tq: Separate the scheme’s starting date from its later nationwide rollout target.

o: Only the States having inter-State migrant workers
39.x: ONORC has been rolled out in all 36 States and Union Territories, covering approximately 80 crore NFSA beneficiaries.
39.tq: Use the complete administrative coverage figure rather than a partial State-only description.

39.s: During August 2019 to September 2025, ONORC recorded more than 187 crore portability transactions and approximately how much grain movement?
39.x: The period recorded more than 187 crore transactions and approximately 443 LMT of grain movement, including PMGKAY transactions.
39.tq: Keep the transaction count and grain quantity separate while identifying the correct scale of the figure.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly describes IM-PDS?
o: The national portability backbone of the Public Distribution System, operational from April 2018
A State-level foodgrain procurement portal launched in 2023
An urban housing programme approved for 2026-2031
A maternity-benefit platform operational from July 2013

c. SMART-PDS — April 2023 to March 2026
d. SARTHAK-PDS — approved for 2026-2031

Monitoring using AI, ML, blockchain and NLP

39.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the digitisation status of the Targeted Public Distribution System?
o: All ration cards are paper-based but all fair price shops use ePoS
About 50 per cent of ration cards are digitised and Aadhaar seeding is unavailable
Digitisation is confined to the Union Territories
Nearly 100 per cent of ration cards are digitised and about 99.9 per cent are Aadhaar-seeded
39.x: Approximately 100 per cent of ration cards have been digitised and about 99.9 per cent have been Aadhaar-seeded.

39.tq: Compare the numerator and denominator carefully in a near-complete implementation figure.

39.s: According to the World Food Summit, 1996, food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to which of the following?
o: Food of their choice irrespective of dietary needs
Adequate food supplied exclusively by the government
Sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Food grains available only during periods of shortage
39.x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life.
39.tq: Use the precise official definition and reject the look-alike phrase ‘food of their choice’.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognized dimension of food security?
39.x: Availability, accessibility, affordability or access, utilisation/absorption and stability are associated with food security. Accountability is not a dimension.
39.tq: Find the odd term among the established dimensions.

39.s: Which of the following best distinguishes national food security from household food security?
o: National food security concerns only imports, whereas household food security concerns only domestic production.
National food security concerns aggregate availability, whereas household food security concerns actual access and affordability for each household.
National food security applies to urban areas, whereas household food security applies only to rural areas.
National food security is based on nutrition, whereas household food security is based only on buffer stocks.
39.x: National food security refers to adequate aggregate production and stocks. Household food security requires that each household can actually obtain and afford food.
39.tq: Split the comparison into aggregate availability versus household-level access.

39.s:
Assertion (A): Food security remains necessary even in years of food surplus.
Reason (R): Starvation may result from unequal distribution even when aggregate food availability is adequate.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
39.x: Both statements are true, and unequal distribution explains why aggregate surplus does not automatically ensure household food security.
39.tq: Test whether the reason explains the distinction between national and household security.

39.s:
With reference to buffer stocks in India, consider the following statements:
1. Wheat and rice are procured by the Food Corporation of India from surplus states.
2. Procurement is made at a pre-announced Minimum Support Price on the advice of the CACP.
3. The procured grains may be sold at a lower issue price in deficit areas and during calamities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: FCI procures wheat and rice at the pre-announced MSP advised by CACP, and the stocks are released at lower issue prices in deficit areas or during calamities.
39.tq: Verify the agency, procurement price and purpose separately.

39.s: The strategic reserve of food grains is maintained at approximately what level above operational stocks?
39.x: The strategic reserve is maintained at 5 million tonnes above operational stocks.
39.tq: Recall the specific quantitative figure; the options are arranged in ascending order.

39.s: The principal purpose of OMSS (Domestic) sales of food grains is to:
o: Increase the procurement price paid to farmers
39.x: Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) sales are used to release food grains and help cool prices.
39.tq: Link the policy instrument with its stated market-stabilisation purpose.

39.x: The Bengal Famine of 1943 is stated to have caused approximately 30 lakh deaths.
39.tq: Distinguish the historically significant figure from nearby numerical distractors.

39.s:
Which of the following groups are identified among the most food-insecure sections of the population?

2. Scheduled Tribes
3. Landless and poor OBC sections
4. Large landowning households
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and landless or poor OBC sections are identified as among the most food-insecure groups. Large landowning households are not included in this description.

39.s:
Arrange the following developments in the Public Distribution System in chronological order:

B. Revamped Public Distribution System
C. National Food Security Act
D. Initial Public Distribution System

39.s: The Public Distribution System in India originated primarily as:
o: A World War II rationing measure
A replacement for the Integrated Child Development Services
39.x: The PDS began as a rationing measure during the Second World War, against the background of the Bengal famine.

39.s: The Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS) was introduced in June 1992 and covered approximately:
39.x: RPDS was introduced in June 1992 and covered 1,775 blocks.
39.tq: Match the reform year with its distinctive coverage figure.

39.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Targeted Public Distribution System introduced in June 1997?
o: It classified beneficiaries into BPL and APL categories.
It provided only cooked meals through schools.
It replaced all nutrition services at anganwadis.
It supplied grain exclusively to export-oriented farmers.

39.tq: Use the programme's beneficiary classification as the identifying feature.

39.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Programme)
a. PDS
b. ICDS
c. Mid-Day Meal/PM POSHAN
d. Food-for-Work

List-II (Food support)
i. Grain as wages
ii. Supplementary nutrition at anganwadis

iv. Hot cooked meal to eligible school-age children

39.s: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) was initiated in 1975 on an:
39.x: ICDS began in 1975 as an experimental programme.

39.s: Supplementary nutrition under ICDS is primarily provided through anganwadis to:
o: Only children aged 6–14 years enrolled in secondary schools
Children aged 0–6 years and pregnant and lactating women
39.x: ICDS provides supplementary nutrition through anganwadis to children aged 0–6 years and pregnant and lactating women.

39.s: Food-for-Work was introduced in India during:
39.x: The Food-for-Work programme was introduced in 1977–78 and provided grain as wages.
39.tq: Recall the programme year from the closely spaced historical alternatives.

39.s: The Mid-Day Meal/PM POSHAN programme is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
39.x: Mid-Day Meal, now PM POSHAN, is associated with the Ministry of Education.
39.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry performs this function?’ authority test.

39.s: Under the present description of PM POSHAN, hot cooked meals are provided to:
o: Pregnant women and lactating mothers only
Bal Vatika/pre-school, primary and upper primary students
Only children in upper primary classes
Children below six months through anganwadis
39.x: PM POSHAN provides hot cooked meals to Bal Vatika or pre-school children and students at the primary and upper primary levels.

39.s: Under the NFSA, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to:
o: Only subsidised wheat through Fair Price Shops
A monthly cash transfer of exactly ₹10,000 without food support
A take-home ration only after the child reaches six years
A free meal and a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000
39.x: NFSA provides pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal along with a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.

o: A take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS/anganwadi services
Only a school meal under PM POSHAN
39.x: Children aged 6 months to 6 years receive a take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS and anganwadi services.

39.s: Children between 6 and 14 years are covered under the NFSA food entitlement primarily through:

39.tq: Match the age bracket with the appropriate institutional delivery mechanism.

39.s: Who is most closely associated with the entitlement approach to understanding famine?
39.x: Amartya Sen developed the entitlement approach, especially in his work Poverty and Famines (1981).
39.tq: Identify the scholar associated with the named analytical approach.

o: A fall in aggregate food production in every case
An increase in the nutritional content of food
Excessive buffer stocks maintained by the government
A collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers

39.s: Poverty and Famines, which set out the entitlement approach to famine, was published in:
39.x: Amartya Sen's Poverty and Famines was published in 1981.
39.tq: Recall the associated publication year from the standard chronological options.

39.s: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) was launched in 2020 primarily in the context of the:

39.x: PMGKAY was launched in 2020 as part of the COVID-19 response and the Atmanirbhar package.
39.tq: Link the scheme with its crisis context rather than with the later NFSA merger.

39.s: At its launch, PMGKAY provided what additional food-grain entitlement?
o: 10 kg of free grain per family irrespective of family size
5 kg of subsidised grain per household instead of NFSA benefits
One hot cooked meal per person per day through schools
5 kg of free grain per person over and above the NFSA entitlement

39.tq: Distinguish an additional per-person entitlement from a household entitlement.

39.s: From 1 January 2023, PMGKAY was subsumed with the NFSA entitlement. What was the principal effect of this decision?
o: The entitlement was converted into a cash transfer
NFSA allocations were discontinued for all beneficiaries
The entire NFSA allocation became free of cost
Only the APL category received free grain
39.x: From 1 January 2023, the entire NFSA allocation became free under the merged arrangement described as ‘One Nation–One Price–One Ration’.
39.tq: Test the policy change after merger rather than the original launch feature.

39.s: For which period was the free food-grain arrangement under the extended PMGKAY continued?
39.x: The arrangement was extended for five years from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028.
39.tq: Use both boundary dates to distinguish the five-year extension.

39.s: The approximate cost of the five-year extension of the free food-grain arrangement under PMGKAY is:
39.x: The cost of the five-year extension is approximately ₹11.80 lakh crore, borne by the Union Government.
39.tq: Recall the distinctive budgetary magnitude and reject nearby figures.

39.s: The food subsidy provided in the Union Budget 2026–27 was:
39.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 provided ₹2,27,629 crore as food subsidy.
39.tq: Read the crore figure carefully and distinguish the transposed digits.

39.s: According to AP PDS data for 2024–25, which one of the following figures represents the number of Fair Price Shops in Andhra Pradesh?
39.x: Andhra Pradesh had 29,796 Fair Price Shops under the PDS during 2024–25.
39.tq: Use the exact numerical figure and eliminate nearby altered values.

39.s: The number of beneficiaries covered through PDS cards in Andhra Pradesh during 2024–25 was approximately:
39.x: The AP PDS covered approximately 1.48 crore beneficiaries through cards in 2024–25.
39.tq: Distinguish the precise coverage figure from similar-looking numerical distractors.

39.s: What was the approximate monthly quantity of rice distributed through the Andhra Pradesh PDS during 2024–25?
39.x: The monthly rice distribution under the AP PDS was approximately 2.35 lakh metric tonnes.
39.tq: Test the reported monthly quantity using close numerical alternatives.

39.s: Approximately what percentage of ration cards in Andhra Pradesh were Aadhaar-linked during 2024–25?
39.x: Around 98% of the ration cards were Aadhaar-linked in AP PDS data for 2024–25.
39.tq: Recall the percentage rather than confusing it with complete Aadhaar seeding under e-PDS.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding food entitlements under the Andhra Pradesh PDS:
1. A Priority Household receives 5 kg of rice per unit free of cost.
2. An Antyodaya Anna Yojana household receives 35 kg of rice per card free of cost.
3. Wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. PHH entitlement is 5 kg per unit, AAY entitlement is 35 kg per card, and wheat is supplied at 1 kg per card at Rs 16 per kg.
39.tq: Check each entitlement separately before selecting the combined code.

39.s: Which of the following correctly describes the millet entitlement under the Andhra Pradesh PDS?
o: 35 kg of ragi per card for AAY households only
Up to 3 kg per card of ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema, free of cost, in lieu of rice
5 kg of jowar per unit for PHH households at the market price
3 kg per unit of wheat throughout Andhra Pradesh at Rs 16 per kg
39.x: Ragi for all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema may be supplied up to 3 kg per card free of cost in lieu of rice.
39.tq: Discriminate between commodity, region, quantity and mode of substitution.

39.s: Which of the following is associated with the AP e-PDS system?
o: Manual allocation of rice cards without Aadhaar linkage
100% Aadhaar seeding, biometric transactions and intra-state portability
39.x: The AP e-PDS system includes 100% Aadhaar seeding of rice cards, biometric transactions and intra-state portability.
39.tq: Select the option containing the complete combination of system features.

39.s: Mobile Dispensing Units for doorstep delivery of PDS commodities in Andhra Pradesh were launched in:
39.x: The Mobile Dispensing Units, or doorstep delivery vans, were launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2021.
39.tq: Use the year-based recall pattern with nearby chronological distractors.

39.s:
With reference to Mee Mart in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Andhra Pradesh Civil Supplies Department and NCCF.
2. The first outlet was established at Lalupuram near Guntur.
3. The proposal envisages 1,000 outlets, of which 553 were ready.
4. The outlets were planned to sell items at Rs 3–5 below market prices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All four statements correctly describe the Mee Mart initiative: its partners, first location, proposed scale and price advantage.
39.tq: Verify the institution, location, scale and price details individually.

39.s: Mee Mart in Andhra Pradesh is proposed to be linked with which of the following for subsidy delivery?
o: Digital Rupee or Central Bank Digital Currency
39.x: Mee Mart is proposed to be linked with the Digital Rupee, or CBDC, for a digital food-subsidy model.
39.tq: Identify the exact digital-payment instrument rather than a related digital platform.

39.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Law or body)
 a. National Food Security Act, 2013
 b. Essential Commodities Act, 1955
 c. Food Corporations Act, 1964
 d. Article 47

List-II (Purpose)
 i. Duty to raise nutrition and the standard of living
 ii. Creation of the Food Corporation of India
 iii. Legal right to subsidised grain and food security with dignity
 iv. Control of production, supply, price and stocks of essential goods

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: NFSA provides the legal right to subsidised grain; the Essential Commodities Act regulates essential goods; the Food Corporations Act created FCI; and Article 47 concerns nutrition and living standards.
39.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate codes containing mismatches.

39.s: The Essential Commodities Act, 1955 primarily provides the basis for:
o: Constitutional recognition of the right to education
Control of production, supply, price and stocks of essential goods
39.x: The Essential Commodities Act enables control over the production, supply, prices and stocks of essential goods and supports PDS control orders.
39.tq: Match the law with its operational regulatory function.

39.s: The Food Corporations Act, 1964 is associated with the creation of:
39.x: The Food Corporations Act, 1964 created the Food Corporation of India for procurement, storage and distribution.
39.tq: Use the institution-founder or institution-enabling-law association.

39.s: Article 47 of the Constitution, in the context of food and nutrition, directs the State to:
o: Raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living
Create a separate food commission in every district
Regulate stock exchanges and securities markets
39.x: Article 47, a Directive Principle of State Policy, concerns raising the level of nutrition and the standard of living.
39.tq: Distinguish the constitutional directive from statutory and administrative mechanisms.

39.s: The TPDS (Control) Order, 2015 primarily lays down operational rules relating to:
o: Procurement of securities by stock exchanges
Ration cards and Fair Price Shops under NFSA
Appointment of members of the Finance Commission
39.x: The TPDS (Control) Order, 2015 provides operational rules for ration cards and Fair Price Shops under the NFSA framework.
39.tq: Identify the administrative instrument by the field it operationalises.

39.s: Which authority is designated as the grievance redressal officer at the district level under the NFSA grievance machinery?
39.x: A District Grievance Redressal Officer, or DGRO, is provided in each district for grievance redressal under the NFSA framework.
39.tq: Ask who performs the specific administrative function at the district level.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NFSA grievance machinery:
1. A State Food Commission is provided in each State.
2. An existing commission may be designated as the State Food Commission.
3. Public servants failing to comply with relief recommended by the DGRO may be penalised.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. Each State has a State Food Commission, an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs, and non-compliance with DGRO recommendations can attract penalties.
39.tq: Test the composition, cost-saving provision and enforcement consequence together.

39.s: At which levels are vigilance committees under the NFSA framework constituted?
o: State, district, block and Fair Price Shop levels
Only at the State and district levels
Only at the block and village levels
Only at the Central and State levels
39.x: NFSA vigilance committees function at the State, district, block and Fair Price Shop levels.
39.tq: Recall the complete multi-level institutional arrangement.

39.s:
Which of the following measures strengthens transparency and social accountability in the Public Distribution System under the NFSA framework?
1. Social audits
2. Mandatory disclosure of PDS records
3. Vigilance committees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA framework.
39.tq: Recognise the combination of transparency and community-monitoring mechanisms.

39.s: Buffer stocks in India were formally introduced during the:
39.x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, covering 1969–74.
39.tq: Link the policy innovation with its Five-Year Plan period.

39.s: Which body fixes the minimum buffer stock levels for each quarter?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
39.x: The minimum buffer stock levels are fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs and specified for each quarter.
39.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the authority.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly lists the dates used for fixing quarterly minimum buffer stock norms?
39.x: Quarterly buffer stock norms are fixed for 1 April, 1 July, 1 October and 1 January; the same dates are correctly listed in chronological cycle form in option a.
39.tq: Arrange recurring quarterly reference dates without confusing them with financial-year closing dates.

39.s: The strategic reserve component of buffer stocks consists of:
o: Only pulses held for export emergencies
Wheat and rice held for emergencies
Only imported cereals held by private traders
Sugar and edible oil held for urban consumers
39.x: The strategic reserve comprises wheat and rice maintained for emergency requirements.
39.tq: Distinguish the commodities and purpose of the strategic reserve.

39.s: According to the cited 2026 estimate, India’s foodgrain stocks were approximately:
o: 702 lakh metric tonnes, about four times the buffer norms
502 lakh metric tonnes, about three times the buffer norms
402 lakh metric tonnes, about twice the buffer norms
602 lakh metric tonnes, about three times the buffer norms
39.x: The estimate placed stocks at about 602 lakh metric tonnes, roughly three times the prescribed buffer norms.
39.tq: Separate the current approximate stock estimate from the earlier dated stock figure.

39.s: On 1 September 2025, the reported stock of rice and wheat was approximately:
o: Rice 369.06 lakh tonnes and wheat 332.97 lakh tonnes
Rice 332.97 lakh tonnes and wheat 369.06 lakh tonnes
Rice 369.06 lakh tonnes and wheat 302.97 lakh tonnes
Rice 339.06 lakh tonnes and wheat 332.97 lakh tonnes
39.x: The reported total was 702.03 lakh tonnes, comprising 369.06 lakh tonnes of rice and 332.97 lakh tonnes of wheat.
39.tq: Check both components and their order rather than relying only on the total.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective or effect of the Open Market Sale Scheme?
o: Replacing the Food Corporation of India’s procurement function with private procurement
Offloading excess central-pool stocks and reducing carrying costs
Raising grain supply during lean seasons and in deficit regions
39.x: OMSS involves FCI selling surplus central-pool grain at predetermined prices. It raises supply, moderates prices, offloads excess stocks and reduces carrying costs, but it does not replace FCI procurement with private procurement.
39.tq: Find the option that introduces a function not belonging to the scheme.

39.s: The proportion of households unable to afford the ICMR-NIN recommended diet declined from approximately 52% in 2011–12 to approximately what proportion in 2023–24?
39.x: The proportion declined from about 52% to about 25% by 2023–24. The corresponding figures were about 25% in rural areas and 21% in urban areas.
39.tq: Recall the direction and magnitude of change using the two benchmark years.

39.s: Which statement correctly represents the rural–urban figures for households unable to afford the ICMR-NIN recommended diet in 2023–24?
39.x: The reported proportions were approximately 25% for rural households and 21% for urban households.
39.tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban columns in a comparison-based figure.

39.s: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold through which combination of channels as a consumer price intervention?
o: Only State Food Commissions and Fair Price Shops
Only private supermarkets licensed by NITI Aayog
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets and mobile vans
FCI warehouses and commercial banks בלבד
39.x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.
39.tq: Match the intervention with its complete distribution-channel combination.

39.s: The National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India (NCCF) was set up in:
39.x: NCCF was established in 1965.
39.tq: Recall the establishment year using close decade-based distractors.

39.s: NCCF functions under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
39.x: NCCF functions under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
39.tq: Use the ministry-association trap by distinguishing neighbouring economic ministries.

39.s: Which of the following correctly describes the functions of NCCF?
o: It fixes constitutional food entitlements and hears NFSA appeals.
It procures essential goods and conducts price-stabilisation operations.
It exclusively manages strategic reserves of wheat and rice.
It regulates stock exchanges and issues currency notes.
39.x: NCCF procures essential goods and undertakes price-stabilisation operations. It is not the constitutional authority for food entitlements, the exclusive manager of strategic reserves, or a financial regulator.
39.tq: Identify the correct body-function pair and reject authority swaps.

39.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the proposed Draft NFS (Amendment) Bill, 2026?
o: It proposes 7 kg per person for AAY, subject to a cap of 35 kg.
It abolishes the AAY entitlement and provides only wheat.
It proposes 35 kg per person for every AAY household without any cap.
It fixes the AAY entitlement at 5 kg per unit without a household ceiling.
39.x: The draft proposal provides 7 kg per person for AAY, with the total entitlement capped at 35 kg.
39.tq: Distinguish a per-person proposal from the overall household cap.

39.s: Which of the following is identified as a proposed reform programme for the period 2026–31?
39.x: SARTHAK-PDS 2026–31 is identified as a proposed reform programme in the food distribution sector.
39.tq: Match the named programme with its stated period.

39.s: Which of the following is a stated criticism of the present food subsidy framework?
o: Issue prices have remained frozen since 2013 while subsidy costs have risen.
The NFSA excludes all rural households from food support.
The PDS supplies only imported foodgrains and no domestic cereals.
Issue prices have increased every year while subsidies have been abolished.
39.x: A criticism is that issue prices have been frozen since 2013 even as the subsidy burden has increased.
39.tq: Identify the precise trend and avoid reversed or extreme statements.

39.s: Which combination reflects the suggested expansion of the food-security basket and related convergence in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Imported wheat alone, with convergence with commercial banks
Sugar and petroleum, with convergence with the GST Council
Pulses, oil and fortified foods, with convergence with Anganwadi and MDM
Only cereals, with convergence limited to stock exchanges
39.x: Andhra Pradesh is exploring a wider PDS basket including pulses, oil and fortified foods, along with convergence with Anganwadi and the Mid-Day Meal programme.
39.tq: Apply the policy proposal to the correct commodities and linked programmes.

39.s: Which statement best captures the contemporary understanding of food security in the context of climate risk?
o: It concerns only urban households unable to purchase food.
It includes an affordable and nutritious food supply for about 1.4 billion people, not merely sufficient grain.
It concerns only producing enough cereals and excludes nutrition.
It is limited to maintaining strategic wheat reserves for emergencies.
39.x: Climate-related food-security concerns now include an affordable, nutritious supply for about 1.4 billion people, rather than only the availability of sufficient grain.
39.tq: Choose the comprehensive interpretation instead of the narrow cereal-only definition.

39.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet?
o: They are unrelated and cannot occur together.
Only hunger has any connection with food affordability.
They are identical concepts and always affect exactly the same households.
They overlap but are not identical concepts.
39.x: Poverty, hunger and unaffordability of a healthy diet overlap in many cases, but they are not identical concepts.
39.tq: Discriminate between related concepts without treating them as synonyms.

39.s: Which of the following combinations represents the major concerns raised about diversification of food support under the PDS?
o: Removing nutrition objectives and focusing only on storage
Replacing all cereals with imported pulses
Restricting food support to urban consumers
Adding eggs, milk and dietary diversity without reducing cereal support
39.x: The debate supports adding eggs, milk and dietary diversity while retaining cereal support rather than cutting it.
39.tq: Select the balanced policy position rather than an extreme replacement strategy.

40.s: Who co-authored the book *Target 3 Billion*, in which the PURA concept was elaborated?
40.x: Srijan Pal Singh co-authored *Target 3 Billion* with Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, in which the PURA concept was elaborated.
40.tq: Identify the exact person associated with a book rather than the originator of the concept.

40.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is best described as:
o: A successor and expansion of the PURA approach
A special programme for urban slum redevelopment
A scheme exclusively for tribal hostels
A replacement for the National Extension Service
40.x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is the successor and expansion of the PURA approach.
40.tq: Use the successor–predecessor relationship to distinguish closely related rural development initiatives.

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission:
1. It seeks to develop more than 300 Rurban clusters.
2. It aims to preserve the rural soul while providing urban amenities.
3. One of its objectives is to curb distress migration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: The mission envisages more than 300 Rurban clusters, combines the rural soul with urban amenities, and seeks to reduce distress migration.
40.tq: Test a mission through its scale, distinctive approach and intended social effect.

40.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: Replacing all Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies
40.x: The mission aims to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services and create well-planned clusters. It does not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies.
40.tq: Find the option that exceeds the institutional scope of the mission.

40.s: A Rurban cluster in a plain or coastal area normally comprises contiguous villages having a population of:
40.x: For plain and coastal areas, a Rurban cluster comprises contiguous villages with a population of 25,000 to 50,000.
40.tq: Separate population norms by geographical category before selecting the range.

40.s: For desert, hilly and tribal areas, a Rurban cluster is defined as contiguous villages having a population of:
40.x: In desert, hilly and tribal areas, the prescribed population range for a Rurban cluster is 5,000 to 25,000.
40.tq: Apply the geographical exception to the general cluster population norm.

40.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission was launched on 21 February 2016 at:
40.x: The mission was launched on 21 February 2016 at Kurubhat in Rajnandgaon district of Chhattisgarh.
40.tq: Combine the date with the precise launch location to avoid district–state swaps.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the funding pattern of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: It is funded mainly through convergence of existing schemes, with Critical Gap Funding up to 30% of project cost.
It is funded only by the concerned State Government through a 90:10 formula.
It is financed through foreign assistance without any scheme convergence.
It is financed entirely through a dedicated Central grant.
40.x: The mission mainly uses convergence of existing schemes and provides Critical Gap Funding of up to 30% of project cost.
40.tq: Distinguish convergence-based financing from a wholly dedicated grant mechanism.

40.s: Under the general funding pattern of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, the Centre–State sharing ratio is:
40.x: The normal Centre–State funding ratio is 60:40. A 90:10 ratio applies to North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
40.tq: Remember the general ratio separately from the special-region ratio.
