Consider the following statements regarding NMSA:
1. It is one of the eight missions under NAPCC.
2. It was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022–23.
3. Its components include Soil Health Management and the agroforestry sub-mission ‘Har Medh Par Ped’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All three statements are correct. NMSA is one of the eight NAPCC missions, was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022–23, and includes the listed components.
48.tq: Combine institutional status, transition year and component details in a coded statement question.

48.s: The National Mission on Natural Farming was approved as a stand-alone mission in:
48.x: The National Mission on Natural Farming was approved as a stand-alone mission in November 2024.
48.tq: Distinguish the approval year of the mission from the launch year of related farming schemes.

48.s: What was Andhra Pradesh’s fertiliser consumption in 2024–25?
48.x: Andhra Pradesh’s fertiliser consumption was 39.39 LMT in 2024–25.
48.tq: Distinguish actual consumption from the earlier product figure and the future requirement.

48.s: The fertiliser requirement projected for Andhra Pradesh for 2026–27 is:
48.x: The fertiliser requirement for Andhra Pradesh in 2026–27 is projected at 41.70 LMT.
48.tq: Read the time reference carefully and separate projected requirement from past consumption.

48.s: The earlier Andhra Pradesh fertiliser figure was reported as:
o: 41.70 LMT of product or 39.39 LMT of NPK nutrients
39.39 LMT of product or 41.70 LMT of NPK nutrients
17.22 LMT of product or 36.28 LMT of NPK nutrients
36.28 LMT of product or 17.22 LMT of NPK nutrients
48.x: The earlier value was 36.28 LMT of fertiliser product, equivalent to 17.22 LMT of NPK nutrients as stated.
48.tq: Keep product quantity and nutrient quantity in their correct order and units.

48.s: What change occurred in Andhra Pradesh’s pesticide use between 2014–15 and 2024–25?
o: It fell from 39.39 LMT to 17.22 LMT of active ingredient.
It fell from 2,650 MT to 1,716 MT of active ingredient.
It remained unchanged at 2,650 MT of active ingredient.
It increased from 1,716 MT to 2,650 MT of active ingredient.
48.x: Pesticide use declined from 2,650 MT in 2014–15 to 1,716 MT in 2024–25, measured as active ingredient.
48.tq: Track the direction of change and retain the correct measurement unit.

48.s: Rythu Seva Kendras, formerly known as Rythu Bharosa Kendras, function primarily as:
o: Village-level one-stop centres for agricultural services
48.x: Rythu Seva Kendras are village one-stop centres providing a range of agricultural inputs and services.
48.tq: Infer the institutional role from the range of services delivered at the centre.

48.s: Which of the following services is NOT associated with Rythu Seva Kendras?
48.x: RSKs handle inputs, soil testing, e-Panta, CCRCs, insurance and procurement. Approval of GM crops is associated with GEAC, not RSKs.
48.tq: Find the unrelated authority by asking which body would perform the regulatory function.

48.s: Which sequence correctly represents the rationalisation of soil-sampling centres in Andhra Pradesh?
48.x: Soil sampling initially ran through 10,778 RSKs; these were rationalised to 8,489 functional centres.
48.tq: Arrange the before-and-after institutional figures in the correct direction.

48.s: Permanent buildings for the rationalised Rythu Seva Kendras are being taken up under:
48.x: Permanent buildings for RSKs are coming up under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS).
48.tq: Match the infrastructure activity with the implementing programme.

48.s: For 2026–27, AP Seeds is supplying subsidised seed through Rythu Seva Kendras in which combination?
o: 4.89 lakh quintals at a cost of ₹294 crore
7.46 lakh quintals at a cost of ₹41.70 crore
7.46 lakh quintals at a cost of ₹294 crore
91,918 quintals at a cost of ₹62.20 crore
48.x: AP Seeds is supplying 7.46 lakh quintals of subsidised seed through RSKs, involving ₹294 crore in 2026–27.
48.tq: Pair the quantity with the corresponding financial allocation rather than mixing nearby figures.

48.s:
The Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971 provide for the establishment of which of the following bodies?
1. Central Insecticides Board
2. Registration Committee
3. National Pesticides Tribunal
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: The Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971 set up the Central Insecticides Board and the Registration Committee. A National Pesticides Tribunal is not mentioned as a body created by these provisions.
48.tq: Identify the correctly stated statutory bodies and reject the invented institutional name.

48.s: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 is intended to replace which of the following?
o: The Fertilisers Act, 1952 and Fertiliser Control Order, 1985
The Seeds Act, 1966 and Seeds Rules, 1968
The Insecticides Act, 1968 and Insecticides Rules, 1971
The Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and its agricultural orders
48.x: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 proposes to replace the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
48.tq: Use the replace-the-existing-law pattern and distinguish neighbouring agricultural laws.

48.s: Which one of the following is a stated feature of the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025?
o: Reduction of penalties for pesticide violations
Transfer of pesticide registration exclusively to State governments
Higher penalties and promotion of biological pesticides
48.x: The draft Bill proposes higher penalties and promotes biological pesticides.
48.tq: Match the policy proposal with its specific reform objectives.

48.s: The deadline for submitting comments on the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 was:
48.x: Comments on the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 were due by 4 February 2026.
48.tq: Separate the consultation deadline from the date of the report carrying the information.

48.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India continues to use at least 66 pesticides that are banned elsewhere.
2. Aldrin was associated with the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota.
3. Endosulfan was banned by the Supreme Court in 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All three statements are correct: at least 66 pesticides used in India are banned elsewhere, Aldrin killed mugger crocodiles in Kota, and the Supreme Court banned Endosulfan in 2011.
48.tq: Combine three related pesticide facts and select the complete set of correct statements.

48.s: Neem-based pesticides are classified as:
48.x: Neem-based pesticides are bio-pesticides.
48.tq: Discriminate between biological and chemical pesticide categories.

48.s: Integrated Pest Management primarily combines:
o: Biological, cultural and need-based chemical control
48.x: IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.
48.tq: Identify the management approach from the combination of control methods rather than from one component alone.

48.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
48.x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh in Rajasthan.
48.tq: Combine the date and location to distinguish the launch event from similar agricultural initiatives.

48.s: Since 2022-23, the Soil Health Card scheme has been part of Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana under the name:
48.x: Since 2022-23, the scheme has been included in RKVY as “Soil Health and Fertility”.
48.tq: Apply the ministry-scheme sub-component distinction and identify the exact official title.

48.s: Soil Health Cards are issued once in every:
48.x: Soil Health Cards are issued every two years and provide crop-wise nutrient dosages.
48.tq: Test the scheme cycle through closely spaced numerical alternatives.

48.s: Which one of the following sets contains only parameters tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
o: Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur and pH
Calcium, magnesium, sodium, chlorine and salinity only
Nitrogen, rainfall, temperature, humidity and pH
Phosphorus, potassium, crop yield, irrigation and rainfall
48.x: The Soil Health Card tests nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron, pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon. The other alternatives include non-Soil Health Card parameters or omit the specified nutrient set.
48.tq: Separate soil-nutrient parameters from climatic, crop and irrigation indicators.

48.s: How many parameters are tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
48.x: The scheme tests 12 parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.
48.tq: Use the exact quantitative value after identifying the complete parameter list.

48.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Soil Health Card figures stated for Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26?
o: 25.55 crore samples collected and 6 lakh tested
6 lakh samples collected and 5.52 lakh tested
6 lakh cards issued and 5.52 crore samples tested
5.52 lakh samples collected and 6 lakh tested
48.x: Andhra Pradesh collected 6 lakh soil samples and tested 5.52 lakh samples in 2025-26.
48.tq: Keep collection and testing figures in their correct order and units.

48.s: The number of Soil Health Cards issued nationally is reported to be over:
48.x: More than 25.55 crore Soil Health Cards have been issued nationally.
48.tq: Distinguish crore-scale quantities by place value and decimal position.

48.s:
With reference to agricultural technology projects, consider the following statements:
1. NATP was launched in 1998.
2. NATP was World Bank-aided.
3. NAIP was implemented during 2006-2014.
4. NAIP was World Bank-funded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid, while NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 and was also World Bank-funded.
48.tq: Check each project against its year, duration and funding source before selecting the coded combination.

48.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the National Agricultural Innovation Project?
o: ICAR as a catalyst for change
48.x: NAIP components included ICAR as a catalyst for change, production-to-consumption research, sustainable rural livelihood security, and basic and strategic research. Universal crop-price stabilisation was not listed as a component.
48.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated project-component group.

48.s: The Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM) covered the period from:
48.x: The period stated for SMAM is 2014-15 to 2025-26.
48.tq: Distinguish the exact start and end years from nearby scheme periods.

48.s: During 2014-15 to 2025-26, SMAM subsidised approximately how many machines?
48.x: SMAM subsidised 20.93 lakh machines during 2014-15 to 2025-26.
48.tq: Read the lakh–crore scale carefully when interpreting a large programme figure.

48.s: Which of the following correctly states the SMAM custom hiring centre figures?
o: 25,689 nationally and 2,395 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26
27,563 nationally and 239 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26
48.x: The stated SMAM figures are 27,563 custom hiring centres nationally and 239 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26. A separate Economic Survey count gives 25,689 national CHCs.
48.tq: Compare national and State figures without interchanging the geographical level.

48.s: Namo Drone Didi provides drones primarily to:
48.x: Namo Drone Didi provides drones to women’s Self-Help Groups.
48.tq: Identify the intended beneficiary group rather than the implementing or regulating institution.

48.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the reported distribution of Namo Drone Didi drones?
48.x: Five hundred drones had been distributed nationally, while Andhra Pradesh had given 529 drones according to the cited State figures.
48.tq: Separate national and State totals instead of assuming that the State figure must be lower.

48.s: The Standard Operating Procedure for drone spraying was issued on:
48.x: The SOP for drone spraying, including crop-specific SOPs, was issued on 20 April 2023.
48.tq: Distinguish the operational guideline date from scheme-launch and current-report dates.

48.s: Which of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh’s SMAM position for 2025-26?
48.x: In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh reported 38,610 machines, 239 custom hiring centres and expenditure of ₹169.32 crore under SMAM.
48.tq: Match a State-year data bundle without substituting figures from another year or programme.

48.s: India’s farm mechanisation level is estimated at approximately:
48.x: India’s farm mechanisation level is reported as 40-45 percent.
48.tq: Select the precise range rather than a rounded but unsupported estimate.

48.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the major SMAM figures for 2014-15 to 2025-26?
1. ₹9,639.96 crore allocated for mechanisation
2. 20.93 lakh machines subsidised
3. 646 hi-tech hubs
4. 25,260 farm machinery banks
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All four figures are stated for the period 2014-15 to 2025-26: ₹9,639.96 crore, 20.93 lakh machines, 646 hi-tech hubs and 25,260 farm machinery banks.
48.tq: Verify a multi-figure programme profile rather than relying on one familiar statistic.

48.s: Under SMAM, the amount stated for Kisan drones is:
48.x: ₹141.41 crore was provided for Kisan drones under SMAM.
48.tq: Distinguish the drone-specific allocation from total or State-level mechanisation expenditure.

48.s: Under Andhra Pradesh SMAM in 2024-25, the expenditure and number of farmers covered were respectively:
48.x: Andhra Pradesh spent ₹75.80 crore and covered 42,864 farmers under SMAM in 2024-25.
48.tq: Pair the correct year with the corresponding expenditure and beneficiary count.

48.s: Which of the following is the scientific core of the Green Revolution package?
48.x: Although the package included HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, assured irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation, the scientific core was the use of HYV seeds.
48.tq: Distinguish the central technological element from the other complementary inputs.

48.s: The HYV wheat varieties associated with Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats include:
48.x: Kalyan Sona and Sonalika were associated with HYV wheat derived from Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats.
48.tq: Link the person, crop and specific varieties in a name-based agricultural question.

48.s: IR-8 rice was developed at:
48.x: IR-8 rice originated from the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in the Philippines.
48.tq: Use institution–country association to distinguish rice research from wheat research.

48.s: M.S. Swaminathan is widely associated with being the:
48.x: M.S. Swaminathan is identified as the father of India’s Green Revolution.
48.tq: Match the prominent personality with the specific agricultural transformation.

48.s: Which sequence correctly describes the adoption and expansion of hybrid and HYV seeds in India?
o: Hybrid seeds from 1960; widespread adoption by 1963; full-fledged HYV programme from 1966
Hybrid seeds from 1966; widespread adoption by 1971; full-fledged programme from 1980
Hybrid seeds from 1951; widespread adoption by 1955; full-fledged programme from 1960
Hybrid seeds from 1963; widespread adoption by 1966; full-fledged programme from 1968
48.x: Hybrid seeds appeared from 1960, were widely adopted by 1963, and the HYV programme became full-fledged from 1966.
48.tq: Arrange closely spaced agricultural milestones in their correct sequence.

48.s: The HYV programme became full-fledged from 1966 following which combination of circumstances?
o: Introduction of the WTO and the launch of PMKSY
Two successive drought years, decline in foodgrain output and dependence on PL-480
A sharp rise in foodgrain output and complete food self-sufficiency
Abolition of irrigation projects and withdrawal of fertiliser subsidies
48.x: The programme became full-fledged from 1966 after the 1965-66 and 1966-67 droughts, foodgrain production fell to 72.3 and 74.2 MT, and India depended on PL-480 supplies.
48.tq: Connect the policy response with the crisis conditions that necessitated it.

48.s: The foodgrain production figures associated with the drought years 1965-66 and 1966-67 were respectively:
48.x: Foodgrain production fell to 72.3 million tonnes in 1965-66 and 74.2 million tonnes in 1966-67.
48.tq: Test the order of year-wise figures rather than only recognising the two numbers.

48.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the phases of the Green Revolution with their periods?
A. Pre-Green Revolution
B. Early Green Revolution
C. Later Green Revolution

1. 1951-68
2. 1968-81
3. 1987-92
48.x: The Pre-Green Revolution phase was 1951-68, the Early Green Revolution was 1968-81, and the Later Green Revolution was 1987-92.
48.tq: Start with the phase-year pair that is most certain and eliminate inconsistent codes.

48.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Intensive Agriculture District Programme
B. First Green Revolution period ended
C. Establishment of M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation
48.x: The order is IADP in 1960-61, the end of the first Green Revolution period, and establishment of the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation in 1988.
48.tq: Use the dated anchor at the beginning and the 1988 institution as the final anchor.

48.s: The call for a Second Green Revolution in India was made by:
48.x: Prime Minister Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution.
48.tq: Match the policy call with the person associated with it, avoiding confusion with agricultural scientists.

48.s:
The focus of the proposed Second Green Revolution included which of the following?
1. Pulses and oilseeds
2. Millets
3. Precision farming and micro-irrigation
4. Exclusive expansion of chemical pesticide use
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: The Second Green Revolution focus included pulses, oilseeds, millets, precision farming and micro-irrigation. Exclusive expansion of chemical pesticide use was not part of the stated focus.
48.tq: Reject an extreme exclusive claim while retaining the listed diversification and efficiency measures.

48.s: The concept of the Evergreen Revolution, associated with M.S. Swaminathan, refers to:
o: Replacement of all traditional crops by HYV crops
Permanent increase in productivity without ecological harm
Expansion of agriculture only through irrigation-intensive farming
Continuous use of chemical inputs irrespective of environmental effects
48.x: The Evergreen Revolution means productivity improvement in perpetuity without ecological harm.
48.tq: Identify the definition by combining productivity growth with ecological sustainability.

48.s: Which PMKSY component is primarily concerned with the faster completion of major and medium irrigation projects?
48.x: The Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) is intended for faster completion of major and medium projects.
48.tq: Match the irrigation component with its precise functional objective.

48.s:
Har Khet Ko Pani under PMKSY includes which of the following?
1. Command Area Development and Water Management
2. Surface minor irrigation
3. Repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies
4. Groundwater development
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Har Khet Ko Pani includes CAD&WM, surface minor irrigation, repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies, and groundwater-related measures.
48.tq: Treat the component as a bundle of irrigation-delivery measures and test every listed element.

48.s: Per Drop More Crop under PMKSY is primarily associated with:
48.x: Per Drop More Crop focuses on micro-irrigation. It was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now under RKVY.
48.tq: Distinguish the component’s functional focus from its administrative placement.

48.s: Which of the following correctly describes the present administrative position of Per Drop More Crop?
o: It remained under PMKSY after December 2021 without change
It was under RKVY from 2015 to 2021 and is now under PMKSY
It was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now under RKVY
48.x: Per Drop More Crop was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now administered under RKVY.
48.tq: Track the scheme’s transfer between programmes by using the time boundary as the discriminator.

48.s: Micro-irrigation, including drip and sprinkler systems, conserves water primarily by:
o: Delivering water more efficiently to the crop zone
Increasing evaporation from the soil surface
Replacing all groundwater with surface water
Eliminating the need for crop selection
48.x: Drip and sprinkler systems improve the efficiency of water application and thereby conserve water.
48.tq: Apply the underlying resource-efficiency principle to a farm-level situation.

48.s: The PDMC programme has brought approximately how much area under micro-irrigation?
48.x: PDMC has brought 109 lakh hectares under micro-irrigation.
48.tq: Distinguish lakh and crore expressions for the same scale of land coverage.

48.s: The subsidy under the micro-irrigation programme may be provided up to what proportion, subject to a cap of 5 hectares?
48.x: The subsidy may extend up to 55 percent, with a cap of 5 hectares.
48.tq: Combine the percentage ceiling with the area cap to identify the precise provision.

48.s: PM-KUSUM, launched in 2019, is associated with:
o: Construction of major irrigation dams only
Distribution of chemical fertilisers through cooperatives
Replacement of all farm pumps by diesel pumps
Solar pumps and solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps
48.x: PM-KUSUM promotes solar pumps and the solarisation of grid-connected farm pumps.
48.tq: Match the scheme with its energy technology and avoid confusing it with irrigation-construction programmes.

48.s: The effect of solar irrigation on groundwater extraction depends particularly on:
o: The number of Soil Health Cards issued
The size of the fertiliser subsidy alone
Only the number of tractors in the district
48.x: Solar irrigation may lead to over-extraction of groundwater depending on hydrogeology and the crops being grown.
48.tq: Apply the conditional environmental effect instead of treating a technology as universally beneficial or harmful.

48.s: Tubewells accounted for what share of India’s net irrigated area in 2021-22?
48.x: Tubewells accounted for 47.3 percent of the net irrigated area in 2021-22.
48.tq: Select the exact percentage from closely spaced alternatives and retain the reference year.

48.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding agricultural research institutes and their locations:

List-I (Institute)

a. Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI)
b. Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI)
c. Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI)
d. International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT)

List-II (Location)

i. Patancheru, Hyderabad
ii. New Delhi (Pusa)
iii. Cuttack
iv. Rajahmundry

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
48.x: CRRI is located at Cuttack, IARI at New Delhi (Pusa), CTRI at Rajahmundry and ICRISAT at Patancheru, Hyderabad.
48.tq: Start from the sure institute–location pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.

48.s: The National Rice Research Institute, formerly known as the Central Rice Research Institute, is located at
48.x: The Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI) is now called the National Rice Research Institute and is located at Cuttack.
48.tq: Use the institute’s former and present names to identify its location.

48.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indian Rice Research Institute — Hyderabad
2. Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research — Hyderabad
3. Indian Institute of Millets Research — Hyderabad

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
48.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. IIRR, IIOR and IIMR are located at Hyderabad.
48.tq: Check whether the common location is correctly applied to all the listed specialised institutes.

48.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Indian Institute of Maize Research — Ludhiana
Indian Institute of Millets Research — Ludhiana
Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research — New Delhi
48.x: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is located at Ludhiana. It should not be confused with the Indian Institute of Millets Research, which is located at Hyderabad; both use the acronym IIMR.
48.tq: Distinguish similar acronyms by expanding the institute names before matching the location.

48.s: Which of the following is classified as an input subsidy rather than public investment in agriculture?
o: Construction of a major irrigation project
Establishment of an agricultural research institute
48.x: Fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy and represents a current transfer. Irrigation projects, agricultural research and rural infrastructure are forms of public investment and capital formation.
48.tq: Classify the item by asking whether it is a current transfer to inputs or capital formation.

48.s:
Consider the following statements regarding agricultural support:
1. Power subsidy is an input subsidy.
2. Interest subvention on agricultural credit is an input subsidy.
3. Irrigation projects are classified as input subsidies.
4. Rural infrastructure represents public investment.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Power subsidy and interest subvention are input subsidies, while rural infrastructure is public investment. Irrigation projects are public investment, not input subsidies.
48.tq: Find the wrongly classified item by separating recurring input support from capital formation.

48.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Minimum Support Price from an input subsidy?
o: MSP is a price support measure, whereas fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy.
MSP is an input subsidy, whereas seed subsidy is a price support measure.
Both MSP and fertiliser subsidy are forms of public investment.
Both MSP and fertiliser subsidy are capital-formation measures.
48.x: MSP is a price support measure. Fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed and credit support are input subsidies.
48.tq: Separate price support for output from subsidised inputs used in production.

48.s: Which of the following is a criticism of agricultural subsidies mentioned in the context of their distributional effects?
o: They are directed exclusively towards agricultural research.
They mainly benefit prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry.
They have completely eliminated regional disparities.
They benefit only farmers in rain-fed regions.
48.x: Although subsidies helped small farmers adopt high-yielding varieties, they are criticised for disproportionately benefiting prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry.
48.tq: Identify the balanced criticism rather than an absolute claim about subsidy outcomes.

48.s: The urea-centred subsidy regime is criticised primarily because it
o: converts MSP into a capital investment
prevents the use of all chemical fertilisers
48.x: A urea-centred subsidy regime is criticised for distorting the balance among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, expressed as the NPK ratio.
48.tq: Link the policy focus on one fertiliser to its stated effect on nutrient balance.

48.s: An acre-based support system has been suggested as an alternative to the existing
48.x: An acre-based support system has been suggested as an alternative to the urea-centred subsidy approach.
48.tq: Match the proposed policy alternative with the regime it is intended to address.

48.s: Which of the following statements regarding the West Asia crisis and agricultural subsidies is correct?
o: Urea prices doubled between April 2025 and December 2026, while the subsidy bill was withdrawn.
The subsidy bill was fixed at ₹2.41 crore because urea prices remained unchanged.
Urea prices doubled between December 2025 and April 2026, and the subsidy bill may reach ₹2.41 lakh crore.
Urea prices were halved between December 2025 and April 2026, reducing the subsidy burden.
48.x: The West Asia crisis doubled urea prices between December 2025 and April 2026, and the subsidy bill may reach ₹2.41 lakh crore.
48.tq: Check both the time interval and the quantitative estimate instead of accepting a partially altered figure.

48.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh agricultural support arrangement?
o: APCNF is a central irrigation project, while RSKs conduct only agricultural exports.
APCNF is a fertiliser-pricing authority, while RSKs regulate international trade.
APCNF is a rural infrastructure fund, while RSKs determine MSP.
APCNF is a global natural-farming model, while RSKs deliver inputs at the village level.
48.x: APCNF is recognised as a global natural-farming model, and RSKs deliver agricultural inputs at the village level in Andhra Pradesh.
48.tq: Match each institution or initiative with its distinctive function rather than its general agricultural association.

48.s:
With reference to recent agricultural capacity-building measures, consider the following statements:
1. The KVK upgrade plan includes entrepreneurship centres in all KVKs by December 2028.
2. Andhra Pradesh has sought Central help for drones and mechanisation.
3. The KVK upgrade plan is limited to establishing research institutes at Hyderabad.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: The plan envisages entrepreneurship centres in all KVKs by December 2028, and Andhra Pradesh has sought Central assistance for drones and mechanisation. The third statement is incorrect.
48.tq: Reject the over-specific statement that changes the scope of a genuine capacity-building measure.

48.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: IIMR (Indian Institute of Maize Research) — Hyderabad
Regional Agricultural Research Station — Maruteru, rice
48.x: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is located at Ludhiana, not Hyderabad. The Indian Institute of Millets Research is the IIMR located at Hyderabad.
48.tq: Find the location error created by confusing two institutes sharing the acronym IIMR.

49.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
49.x: The Yellow Revolution is associated with oilseeds and edible oils. Blue is associated with fisheries, Silver with eggs and poultry, and Golden Fibre with jute.
49.tq: Start from the sure product-revolution pair and eliminate reversed commodities.

49.s:
With reference to agricultural revolutions in India, consider the following pairs:

a. Blue Revolution — Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan
b. Pink Revolution — Durgesh Patel
c. Red Revolution — Vishal Tewari
d. Golden Revolution — Nirpakh Tutej

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
49.x: All four pairs are correctly matched in the stated classification. The Blue Revolution is linked with fisheries and aquaculture, Pink with meat processing, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals, Red with meat and tomato, and Golden with horticulture and honey.
49.tq: Use the person-product association in each pair rather than relying on the colour alone.

49.s: The term ‘Golden Fibre Revolution’ is associated with which commodity?
49.x: The Golden Fibre Revolution refers to jute. Cotton is associated with the Silver Fibre Revolution.
49.tq: Tests a confusable colour-commodity pair using a nearby commodity as the distractor.

49.s: The Technology Mission on Cotton is associated with which revolution?
49.x: The Silver Fibre Revolution is associated with cotton through the Technology Mission on Cotton.
49.tq: Identify the exact official term instead of choosing the better-known Golden Fibre association.

49.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
49.x: The Round Revolution is associated with potato, not oilseeds. Oilseeds are associated with the Yellow Revolution.
49.tq: Find the single commodity that belongs to another colour revolution.

49.s: The expression ‘Rainbow Revolution’ refers to:
o: A programme limited to horticulture and honey production
Only the simultaneous growth of foodgrain and dairy production
The sequence of phases of the Green Revolution
The umbrella of colour revolutions covering crops, livestock and fisheries
49.x: Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for the different colour revolutions and represents holistic agricultural growth across crops, livestock and fisheries.
49.tq: Distinguish an umbrella concept from one of its component revolutions.

49.s: The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-1960s in the backdrop of which development?
o: The abolition of the Annual Plans in 1960
The completion of the Third Five-Year Plan with record foodgrain output
A decline in irrigation accompanied by a rise in foodgrain output
A sharp fall in foodgrain output after the droughts of 1965-66 and 1966-67
49.x: The Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s after droughts in 1965-66 and 1966-67 caused foodgrain output to fall sharply.
49.tq: Link the policy shift to its immediate economic trigger.

49.s: Foodgrain output in India fell to approximately what levels after the droughts of 1965-66 and 1966-67, respectively?
49.x: Foodgrain output fell to 72.3 million tonnes in 1965-66 and 74.2 million tonnes in 1966-67.
49.tq: Read the paired figures in the stated chronological order.

49.s: High-yielding variety seeds were adopted as a full programme during which period?
49.x: HYV seeds were adopted as a full programme from 1966 during the Annual Plans of 1966-69.
49.tq: Use the plan-period distinction to separate Annual Plans from Five-Year Plans.

49.s: Agricultural growth during the Annual Plans of 1966-69, when HYV seeds were adopted as a full programme, was approximately:
49.x: Agricultural growth during the Annual Plans of 1966-69 was 4.16%.
49.tq: Distinguish the exact percentage from nearby numerical distractors.

49.s: Which of the following correctly represents the phases of the Green Revolution given in the classification?
o: Pre-Green Revolution: 1951-68; Early phase: 1968-81; Later phase: 1987-92
Pre-Green Revolution: 1951-66; Early phase: 1966-80; Later phase: 1981-92
Pre-Green Revolution: 1956-68; Early phase: 1968-87; Later phase: 1987-95
Pre-Green Revolution: 1951-60; Early phase: 1960-75; Later phase: 1975-92
49.x: The stated classification identifies 1951-68 as the pre-Green Revolution period, 1968-81 as the early phase and 1987-92 as the later phase.
49.tq: Match each phase with its complete date range rather than only its starting year.

49.s: Who among the following was the Union Agriculture Minister associated with driving the policy shift towards the Green Revolution in India?
49.x: C. Subramaniam, as Union Agriculture Minister, drove the policy shift towards the Green Revolution. Norman Borlaug and M.S. Swaminathan had scientific roles, while Verghese Kurien was associated with the White Revolution.
49.tq: Separate the ministerial policy role from the scientific and dairy roles.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the contribution of Norman Borlaug?
o: He founded the National Dairy Development Board.
He developed semi-dwarf wheat and is regarded as the father of the global Green Revolution.
He developed the first semi-dwarf rice variety in India.
He developed the three-tier dairy cooperative model at Anand.
49.x: Norman Borlaug developed semi-dwarf wheat and is regarded as the father of the global Green Revolution.
49.tq: Use the contribution-based distinction among scientists, administrators and dairy pioneers.

49.s: Punjab is called the ‘Granary of India’ primarily because it was:
o: The pioneer state of the Green Revolution
The first state to introduce Operation Flood
The first state to establish the NDDB
The exclusive producer of Indian dwarf rice
49.x: Punjab was the pioneer state of the Green Revolution and is consequently called the ‘Granary of India’.
49.tq: Connect the title with the specific historical agricultural role stated for the state.

49.s: In 1966, approximately how much Mexican wheat was imported and crossed with local varieties in Punjab?
49.x: In 1966, 18,000 tonnes of Mexican wheat was imported and crossed with local varieties in Punjab.
49.tq: Test the exact quantity while keeping the unit and year fixed.

49.s: The rise in wheat production associated with the introduction of Mexican wheat varieties in Punjab was from approximately:
49.x: Wheat production rose from about 5 million tonnes to 17 million tonnes after the introduction and crossing of Mexican varieties.
49.tq: Compare the before-and-after production figures without reversing their order.

49.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a high-yielding variety or wheat selection?
o: Taichung Native-1 — First semi-dwarf rice introduced in India
Kalyan Sona — Mexican dwarf wheat developed by Borlaug
Lerma Rojo 64-A — Dwarf rice from the Philippines
49.x: Taichung Native-1, or TN-1, was the first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India in 1965. IR-8 was dwarf rice from IRRI, while Kalyan Sona was an Indian dwarf wheat selection and Lerma Rojo 64-A was Mexican dwarf wheat.
49.tq: Separate rice varieties from Mexican wheat and Indian wheat selections.

49.s: IR-8, often called ‘miracle rice’, was:
o: A dwarf rice variety from IRRI in the Philippines, associated with 1966
An Indian wheat selection resistant to lodging
The first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India in 1965 from Mexico
A variety of cotton developed under the Technology Mission on Cotton
49.x: IR-8 was a dwarf rice variety from the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines and is associated with 1966.
49.tq: Discriminate IR-8 from TN-1 and from the wheat varieties listed alongside it.

49.s: Which of the following pairs consists entirely of Mexican dwarf wheat varieties associated with Borlaug?
49.x: Lerma Rojo 64-A and Sonora 64 were Mexican dwarf wheat varieties associated with Borlaug. Kalyan Sona and Sonalika were Indian dwarf wheat selections.
49.tq: Group the varieties by crop origin and distinguish Mexican wheat from Indian selections.

49.s:
Which of the following statements regarding HYV crops is correct?
1. Their short stature helps them resist lodging.
2. They respond to fertiliser and water.
3. Their quicker maturity can permit double cropping.
49.x: All three statements are correct. HYVs are short-statured, respond to fertiliser and water, mature faster and can therefore support double cropping.
49.tq: Recognise a complete set of linked agronomic characteristics rather than isolating one feature.

49.s: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by which organisation?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
49.x: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).
49.tq: Apply the ‘who launched the programme?’ institutional trap.

49.s: The three-tier cooperative model adopted by Operation Flood was based on the model developed at:
49.x: Operation Flood copied the Amul three-tier cooperative model developed at Anand in Gujarat.
49.tq: Distinguish the starting location of the cooperative model from the Green Revolution state.

49.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three tiers of the Operation Flood cooperative model?
o: Village society → district union → state federation
Village society → state federation → district union
District union → village society → state federation
State federation → village society → district union
49.x: The three tiers proceed from the village society to the district union and then to the state federation.
49.tq: Arrange the institutional levels from the grassroots unit to the apex federation.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about Phase I of Operation Flood:
1. It covered the period 1970-80.
2. It was financed by the World Food Programme.
3. Milk sheds in 18 states were linked to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements correctly describe Phase I of Operation Flood: 1970-80, World Food Programme financing and linkage of milk sheds in 18 states to four major cities.
49.tq: Check the period, funding agency and achievement as three separate components.

49.s: During Phase II of Operation Flood, milk sheds increased from 18 to 136 and urban markets increased up to:
49.x: Phase II, covering 1981-85, increased milk sheds from 18 to 136 and expanded urban markets up to 200.
49.tq: Pair the phase-specific expansion figures rather than confusing them with Phase I or III.

49.s: What was the principal achievement attributed to Phase III of Operation Flood?
o: Establishing the first semi-dwarf rice research centre
Linking 18 milk sheds to four metropolitan cities
49.x: Phase III, covering 1985-96, added 30,000 new dairy cooperatives.
49.tq: Match the achievement with the correct phase and reject achievements belonging to earlier phases.

49.s: Operation Flood was associated with the dairy cooperative leadership of Verghese Kurien and:
49.x: Verghese Kurien worked with Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand in the development of the dairy cooperative movement.
49.tq: Use the associated-person trap by separating dairy pioneers from Green Revolution figures.

49.s: White Revolution 2.0 was launched in September 2024 by the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying alone
49.x: White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Cooperation in September 2024.
49.tq: Apply the ministry-swap trap to a recently launched programme.

49.s: White Revolution 2.0 plans to create how many new dairy cooperative societies?
49.x: White Revolution 2.0 plans to establish 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies.
49.tq: Test the programme target against nearby rounded figures.

49.s: The procurement target under White Revolution 2.0 by 2028-29 is:
49.x: The target is procurement of 1,007 lakh kilograms of milk per day by 2028-29.
49.tq: Identify the exact target and retain the lakh kg/day unit.

49.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding India’s milk production?
o: India produced about 148 MMT in 2023-24 and is the world’s largest producer.
India produced 239.3 MMT in 2023-24 and is the world’s largest milk producer.
India’s annual output is below 200 MT and is declining steadily.
India produced 239.3 MMT in 2023-24 but ranks second in the world.
49.x: Milk output was 239.3 million metric tonnes in 2023-24, and India is the world’s largest milk producer.
49.tq: Combine the numerical figure with the comparative world-ranking fact.

49.s:
The focus of the Second Green Revolution includes which of the following?
1. Pulses, oilseeds and millets
2. Precision farming using drones and artificial intelligence
3. Micro-irrigation and integrated nutrient and pest management
4. Climate-resilient varieties
49.x: The Second Green Revolution focuses on all the listed areas, including Shree Anna, precision technologies, resource-efficient irrigation, integrated management and climate resilience.
49.tq: Recognise the comprehensive objective list and use the all-inclusive option only when every item fits.

49.s: The principal objective associated with the Evergreen Revolution is to:
o: Raise productivity without causing ecological harm
Replace all foodgrains with commercial crops
Restrict agricultural growth to irrigated regions
Increase production exclusively through chemical fertilisers
49.x: The Evergreen Revolution seeks to raise agricultural productivity while avoiding ecological harm.
49.tq: Apply the sustainability principle to distinguish Evergreen Revolution from a purely output-oriented approach.

49.s: Which Prime Minister called for a Second Green Revolution?
49.x: Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution.
49.tq: Distinguish the political call for the Second Green Revolution from the scientific idea of Evergreen Revolution.

49.s: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) is a sub-scheme of:
49.x: BGREI is a sub-scheme of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY).
49.tq: Use the parent-scheme identification method and reject programmes from adjacent agricultural sectors.

49.s: BGREI has been implemented since:
49.x: BGREI has been implemented since 2010-11.
49.tq: Test the exact implementation year against adjacent agricultural programme years.

49.s: Which of the following states is NOT included in the listed geographical coverage of BGREI?
49.x: The listed BGREI states are Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. Tamil Nadu is not included in that list.
49.tq: Find the outsider in a region-based state list.

49.s: Which of the following correctly states the aim of BGREI?
o: To shift all cotton production from western India to eastern India
To promote petroleum production through eastern industrial corridors
To establish dairy cooperatives in every eastern district
To raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through HYVs, irrigation, balanced nutrients and IPM
49.x: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, balanced nutrient use and integrated pest management.
49.tq: Match the scheme with its crop, region and intervention package.

49.s: The later Purvodaya idea of shifting the rice bowl eastward follows the same broad logic as:
o: Expanding rice-based productivity in eastern India
Replacing HYV seeds with traditional varieties throughout India
Concentrating agriculture only in Punjab and Haryana
49.x: Purvodaya follows the logic of improving rice-based productivity and shifting the rice bowl towards eastern India, as envisaged by BGREI.
49.tq: Recognise the continuity between a later policy idea and the earlier regional productivity strategy.

49.s: Which crop gained the most during the initial phase of the Green Revolution in India?
49.x: Wheat recorded the greatest gains during the initial phase of the Green Revolution. Rice expanded significantly in a wider and later phase.
49.tq: Direct crop-wise recall using closely related agricultural crops as distractors.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional spread of the Green Revolution in India:
1. Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh recorded the biggest gains.
2. Rice registered important gains in the deltas of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
3. Eastern states such as Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam led the first phase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh recorded the biggest gains, while rice gains were notable in the deltas of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. The listed eastern states lagged during the first phase, making statement 3 false.
49.tq: Find the wrong regional statement by distinguishing the leading north-western belt from the lagging eastern states.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a major food-security outcome of the Green Revolution in India?
o: India became self-sufficient only in pulses and oilseeds
India replaced foodgrain production with commercial crops
India continued to depend on PL-480 imports despite rising foodgrain production
India became self-sufficient in foodgrains and stopped relying on PL-480 imports
49.x: The Green Revolution enabled India to become self-sufficient in foodgrains and discontinue dependence on PL-480 imports.
49.tq: Direct outcome recall with a policy-era import dependence trap.

49.s: India's foodgrain output increased from approximately what level in the mid-1960s to 357.73 million tonnes in 2024-25?
49.x: Foodgrain output rose from about 70–75 million tonnes in the mid-1960s to a record 357.73 million tonnes in 2024-25.
49.tq: Numerical range recall using ascending production figures.

49.s: Which category of farmers benefited the most from the Green Revolution?
49.x: The benefits were unevenly distributed, with farmers owning more than 10 hectares benefiting the most.
49.tq: Direct recall of the landholding-based distributional disparity.

49.s: The Green Revolution in India was criticised for neglecting which group of crops?
49.x: The Green Revolution focused strongly on wheat and rice and contributed to the neglect of pulses, oilseeds and millets.
49.tq: Direct crop-group discrimination between foodgrain priorities and neglected crops.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the ecological consequences of the Green Revolution:
1. Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is estimated to be 35–57 per cent more than recharge.
2. Salinity and loss of biodiversity are among its environmental costs.
3. The predominant fertiliser nutrient ratio was balanced at 1:1:1 for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is 35–57 per cent above recharge, and salinity and biodiversity loss are recognised costs. The reported N:P:K ratio was skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, not 1:1:1.
49.tq: Split the options by checking the ecological figures and the reversed fertiliser-ratio trap.

49.s: The reported N:P:K ratio associated with the fertiliser imbalance under the Green Revolution is:
49.x: The reported nutrient ratio is 10.9:4.1:1 for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, indicating a skewed use of fertilisers.
49.tq: Order-sensitive numerical recall of the N:P:K ratio.

49.s:
Assertion (A): The Green Revolution increased agricultural output but also produced ecological costs.
Reason (R): Its package relied on HYV seeds along with chemical fertilisers and assured irrigation, which intensified input use.
Choose the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
49.x: Both statements are true. The intensive use of HYV seeds, fertilisers and assured irrigation explains both higher output and ecological pressures such as groundwater depletion and soil-related problems.
49.tq: Link the package of inputs to both its productivity gains and ecological consequences.

49.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Green Revolution package approach?
o: Assured irrigation through canals and tubewells
Withdrawal of price support and formal credit
49.x: The package included HYV seeds, assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement. Withdrawal of price support and formal credit was not a component.
49.tq: Find the option that reverses a core element of the package approach.

49.s: Which one of the following combinations most appropriately represents the Green Revolution package approach?
o: Millet monoculture, no irrigation, no fertiliser use and market deregulation
Export subsidies, plantation crops, import restrictions and withdrawal of rural credit
HYV seeds, assured irrigation, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP
Traditional seeds, rain-fed cultivation, organic manure and abolition of procurement
49.x: The package approach combined HYV seeds with assured irrigation, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement.
49.tq: Package-combination recall using omission and reversal traps.

49.s: The Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) was begun in:
49.x: IADP began in 1960 as a pilot programme.
49.tq: Direct year recall with the closely related IAAP period as a distractor.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP):
1. It began as a pilot programme in 1960.
2. It covered seven districts in seven states.
3. West Godavari was the IADP district in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: IADP began in 1960 as a pilot in seven districts of seven states, and West Godavari was Andhra Pradesh's IADP district.
49.tq: Combine the programme's year, scale and Andhra Pradesh location before selecting the coded option.

49.s: The Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP) was introduced during:
49.x: IAAP was introduced in 1964-65 as an extension of the intensive agricultural programme approach.
49.tq: Direct programme-period recall against the IADP start year.

49.s: Which of the following correctly describes the coverage of the Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP)?
o: It covered 117 districts and 114 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in Krishna district
It covered 7 districts and 7 states, with West Godavari as the only Andhra Pradesh unit
It was confined to the Punjab-Haryana region and excluded Andhra Pradesh
It extended to 114 districts and 117 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in West Godavari
49.x: IAAP extended to 114 districts and 117 blocks in Andhra Pradesh, beginning in West Godavari.
49.tq: Separate the programme's district and block figures and watch for their reversal.

49.s: Which irrigation infrastructure helped make coastal Andhra Pradesh a rice-surplus belt?
o: The Godavari and Krishna delta canals associated with Sir Arthur Cotton's Dowleswaram barrage
The Cauvery and Vaigai canals associated with the Polavaram barrage
The Tungabhadra and Pennar canals associated with the Bhakra-Nangal project
The Mahanadi and Brahmani canals associated with the Nagarjuna Sagar project
49.x: The Godavari and Krishna delta canals, associated with Sir Arthur Cotton's Dowleswaram barrage, helped make coastal Andhra Pradesh a rice-surplus belt.
49.tq: Match the irrigation system, engineer and regional agricultural outcome.

49.s: MTU rice varieties are associated with which research station?
o: Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari
49.x: MTU varieties come from the Regional Agricultural Research Station at Maruteru in West Godavari. BPT varieties are associated with Bapatla.
49.tq: Origin-place discrimination between the MTU and BPT varietal groups.

49.s: BPT rice varieties are associated with:
49.x: BPT varieties come from Bapatla, whereas MTU varieties are associated with the Regional Agricultural Research Station at Maruteru.
49.tq: Confusable-place discrimination between Maruteru and Bapatla.

49.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Variety)
 a. BPT 5204
 b. MTU 1010
 c. MTU 7029

List-II (Description)
 i. Popular mega-variety
 ii. Parent of genome-edited DRR Dhan 100 Kamala
 iii. Parent of genome-edited Pusa DST Rice 1

Codes:
 a. a–ii, b–iii, c–i
 b. a–iii, b–ii, c–i
 c. a–ii, b–i, c–iii
 d. a–i, b–iii, c–ii
49.x: BPT 5204 is the parent of DRR Dhan 100 Kamala; MTU 1010 is the parent of Pusa DST Rice 1; and MTU 7029 is the popular mega-variety Swarna.
49.tq: Start from the sure variety-parent pair and eliminate codes with a repeated mismatch.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes MTU 1010?
o: It is a popular mega-variety known as Swarna
It is the parent of DRR Dhan 100 Kamala and is associated with Bapatla
It is a Rabi rice variety of southern states and the parent of Pusa DST Rice 1
It is the first semi-dwarf rice variety introduced in India

50.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: BGREI — Rice-based systems in eastern States
50.x: BGREI is a sub-scheme of RKVY concerned with rice-based systems in the eastern States. INSIMP concerns millets, NMOOP concerns oilseeds and oil palm, and NFSM has a broader crop portfolio.
50.tq: Use the mission-target association to eliminate swapped crop objectives.

50.s: The Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) programme covers which of the following groups of States?
o: Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Goa
Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh בלבד
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka
50.x: BGREI covers rice-based systems in Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
50.tq: Test the complete geographical membership of a named programme.

50.s: INSIMP, a scheme under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana, was primarily associated with which crop group?
50.x: INSIMP was launched under RKVY for millets, with the objective of promoting nutritional security.
50.tq: Distinguish similar crop missions by their precise target crop.

50.s:
Arrange the following missions in chronological order of their launch:
A. NMOOP
B. Technology Mission on Oilseeds
C. INSIMP
D. NFSM
50.x: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds was launched in 1986, NFSM in 2007-08, INSIMP in 2011-12 and NMOOP in 2014.
50.tq: Place the missions by their launch years before comparing the options.

50.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the oilseed-related missions is correct?
1. NMOOP was launched in 2014 for oilseeds and oil palm.
2. NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in 2021.
3. NMEO-Oilseeds was launched in 2024 with an approximate target of 70 million tonnes by 2030-31.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: All three statements are correct: NMOOP dates from 2014, NMEO-Oil Palm from 2021, and NMEO-Oilseeds from 2024 with a target of about 70 MT by 2030-31.
50.tq: Verify each mission by its year, crop focus and quantitative target.

50.s: The ‘Tilhan Mission’, referred to in February 2020, relates primarily to which of the following?
50.x: The Tilhan Mission relates to oilseed production.
50.tq: Discriminate between similarly named crop initiatives by identifying the target crop.

50.s: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, covering 2025-2031, primarily targets which combination of pulses?
50.x: The mission targets tur, urad and masur and seeks to end pulse imports.
50.tq: Test the exact membership of a named crop group rather than its broad objective.

50.s: The first major regional concentration of the Green Revolution was observed mainly in which area?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and coastal Karnataka
Assam, Odisha and eastern West Bengal
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
50.x: The first phase was concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, while several eastern and rainfed regions lagged.
50.tq: Identify the initial regional core instead of the later expansion area.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about the regional spread of the Green Revolution:
1. Irrigated rice deltas of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu benefited through irrigation.
2. Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam lagged during the first phase.
3. During the second phase in the 1980s, the spread extended towards both eastern and western regions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements correctly describe the regional pattern: irrigated rice deltas benefited, the eastern belt initially lagged, and the second phase spread eastward and westward in the 1980s.
50.tq: Combine regional beneficiaries, lagging regions and the later phase of expansion.

50.s: The growth rate of agricultural output during the second phase of the Green Revolution was approximately how much, compared with 2.3% in the earlier phase?
50.x: Output growth rose to approximately 3.4% during the second phase, compared with 2.3% earlier.
50.tq: Use the comparative numerical value rather than the familiar earlier figure.

50.s: Which of the following groups was comparatively neglected by the Green Revolution?
o: Large farmers with more than 10 hectares in irrigated areas
Rice farmers in irrigated deltas of Andhra Pradesh
Wheat farmers in Punjab and Haryana
Pulses, oilseeds and millets in rainfed and hilly areas
50.x: The gains were captured disproportionately by farmers with more than 10 hectares, while rainfed and hilly areas and crops such as pulses, oilseeds and millets were neglected.
50.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented beneficiaries and neglected groups.

50.s: The N:P:K ratio in Indian agriculture has worsened to which of the following, compared with the ideal ratio of 4:2:1?
50.x: The prevailing N:P:K ratio is given as 10.9:4.1:1, whereas the ideal ratio is 4:2:1. This imbalance is associated with concerns such as groundwater depletion and salinity.
50.tq: Separate the actual input ratio from the ideal benchmark.

50.s: Which phase of agricultural development is marked by a price policy based on minimum support price and procurement?
50.x: The third phase of agricultural development is marked by a price policy based on MSP and procurement.
50.tq: Associate the policy characteristic with the correct phase of agricultural development.

50.s: The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in which year, and when did it submit its final report?
50.x: The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in 1970 and submitted its final report in 1976.
50.tq: Pair the establishment year with the report year instead of treating them as one date.

50.s: The committee constituted to examine the objective of doubling farmers’ income was chaired by whom?
50.x: The committee on doubling farmers’ income was chaired by Ashok Dalwai. It was set up in 2016 and submitted its report in 2018.
50.tq: Match the committee’s objective with its chairman rather than with another agricultural expert.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about the committee on doubling farmers’ income:
1. It was set up in 2016.
2. It submitted its report in 2018.
3. It was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: The Ashok Dalwai Committee was set up in 2016, submitted its report in 2018 and was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.
50.tq: Cross-check the committee through its year of constitution, report year and chairmanship.

50.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the recorded 2025-26 output figures?
o: Foodgrains: 354.70 million tonnes; horticulture: 377.78 million tonnes
Foodgrains: 376.56 million tonnes; horticulture: 377.78 million tonnes
Foodgrains: 377.78 million tonnes; horticulture: 376.56 million tonnes
Foodgrains: 376.56 million tonnes; horticulture: 354.70 million tonnes
50.x: The recorded 2025-26 figures are 376.56 million tonnes of foodgrains and 377.78 million tonnes of horticulture output.
50.tq: Read the paired figures carefully and avoid reversing the two sectors.

50.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the recent agricultural export position mentioned in relation to 2025-26?
o: Agricultural exports reached 45.70 billion dollars, alongside an oilseed crisis.
Agricultural exports reached 70.54 billion dollars, alongside a rice crisis.
Agricultural exports fell to 54.70 billion dollars because of a wheat crisis.
Agricultural exports reached 54.70 billion dollars, alongside a cotton crisis.
50.x: Agricultural exports reached 54.70 billion dollars, while the sector simultaneously faced a cotton crisis.
50.tq: Link the exact export value with the associated sectoral concern.

50.s: Which one of the following best describes the agricultural situation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Its paddy yield is about 10 tonnes per hectare and output remains constant each year.
Its paddy yield is below 2 tonnes per hectare and foodgrain output is independent of the monsoon.
Its paddy yield is about 6 tonnes per hectare, but foodgrain output fluctuates with the monsoon.
Its paddy cultivation is confined to rainfed uplands and has no major deltaic concentration.
50.x: Andhra Pradesh has a paddy yield of about 6 tonnes per hectare, among the best, but its foodgrain output fluctuates with monsoon conditions.
50.tq: Combine the State’s productivity strength with its monsoon-related vulnerability.

50.s: The foodgrain output of Andhra Pradesh moved through which sequence during 2023-26?
50.x: The reported sequence of Andhra Pradesh foodgrain output was 143 lakh tonnes, followed by 162 lakh tonnes and 190 lakh tonnes across 2023-26.
50.tq: Arrange the successive annual output figures in their stated order.

50.s: India’s rice yield, in comparison with China’s rice yield, is described as being:
50.x: India’s rice yield is described as less than half of China’s rice yield, highlighting a major yield gap.
50.tq: Focus on the direction and magnitude of the inter-country yield comparison.

50.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the criticism concerning the sources of agricultural growth in India?
o: Growth has come more from expansion of area than from improvement in yield.
Growth has eliminated the yield gap with world averages.
Growth has come exclusively from yield improvement, with cultivated area declining continuously.
Growth has been driven only by foodgrain crops and not by allied activities.
50.x: A major criticism is that agricultural growth has depended more on area expansion than on yield improvement.
50.tq: Identify the cautious structural criticism and reject extreme formulations such as ‘exclusively’.

50.s: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research released how many new climate-resilient or high-yield varieties, covering how many crops?
50.x: ICAR released 184 new climate-resilient or high-yield varieties covering 25 crops. Since 2014, 3,236 HYVs had been approved.
50.tq: Match the exact variety count with the number of crops covered.

50.s: How many high-yielding varieties had been approved since 2014, according to the stated agricultural technology data?
50.x: A total of 3,236 high-yielding varieties had been approved since 2014.
50.tq: Distinguish the cumulative figure from the separate recent release of 184 varieties.

50.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh’s agricultural conditions is correct?
o: Foodgrain production was 116.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif sowing reached 161% of normal.
Foodgrain production was 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif 2026 sowing was about 61% of normal by 19 August because of El Nino.
Foodgrain production was 186.16 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif sowing was about 91% of normal.
Foodgrain production was 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while Kharif sowing was unaffected by El Nino.
50.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 161.86 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in 2024-25. By 19 August 2026, Kharif sowing was only about 61% of normal, attributed to El Nino conditions.
50.tq: Combine a precise State-level output figure with a weather-related sowing constraint.

50.s: Which sectoral pattern is identified as a recent feature of Indian agricultural growth?
o: Crop production alone is leading growth, while livestock and fisheries are contracting.
Livestock and fisheries are leading growth, while crop growth is about 3.5% and yields lag world averages.
Only horticulture is growing, with no contribution from livestock or fisheries.
Crop growth is about 8.5% and Indian yields exceed world averages.
50.x: Recent growth is led more by livestock and fisheries, while crop growth is about 3.5% and yields remain below world averages.
50.tq: Compare the leading subsectors with the weaker crop-growth and yield performance.

51.s: The National Food Security Mission was renamed as which of the following in Financial Year 2024-25?
o: National Food Security and Nutrition Mission
51.x: NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in FY 2024-25.
51.tq: Distinguish the original mission name from its later official renaming.

51.s:
With reference to the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), consider the following statements:
1. It is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
2. It focuses on climate-resilient and rainfed farming.
3. It became a sub-mission of Krishonnati from 2018-19.
4. It has been brought under PM-RKVY from 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional position and focus of NMSA.
51.tq: Track the mission through its parent climate programme, later sub-mission status and recent umbrella scheme.

51.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture?
51.x: RAD, Soil Health Management and Per Drop More Crop are NMSA components. National Agricultural Market is not listed as an NMSA component.
51.tq: Find the one item belonging to agricultural marketing rather than the mission’s sustainability components.

51.s: Under Rainfed Area Development (RAD), assistance of ₹30,000 per family is provided for which of the following?
51.x: RAD provides ₹30,000 per family for Integrated Farming System models developed with ICAR support.
51.tq: Link the numerical assistance with the specific intervention rather than with a general farm subsidy.

51.s: Under NMSA, the maximum subsidy mentioned for micro-irrigation is up to:
51.x: The micro-irrigation subsidy under NMSA may be provided up to 55%.
51.tq: Use the exact percentage and reject nearby rounded subsidy figures.

51.s: Soil Health Cards under the NMSA-related provision are to be provided free of cost at what interval?
51.x: Soil Health Cards are to be provided free every two years, not annually.
51.tq: Discriminate between the stated biennial interval and the tempting annual alternative.

51.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NMSA — Agroforestry
2. RAD — ICAR Integrated Farming System models
3. NFSM — Oil palm as its exclusive crop
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
51.x: Agroforestry is an NMSA component and RAD uses ICAR Integrated Farming System models. NFSM is not exclusively an oil-palm mission.
51.tq: Test the mission-component relationship while identifying the overbroad word 'exclusive'.

51.s:
The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) covers which of the following?
1. Fruits, vegetables and spices
2. Flowers and mushrooms
3. Coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo
Select the correct answer using the code below.
51.x: MIDH covers all the listed horticultural crops and products, including fruits, vegetables, spices, flowers, mushrooms, coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo.
51.tq: Group the complete crop coverage of a horticulture mission before selecting the code.

51.s: Which of the following funding ratios is associated with the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, including its special-region pattern?
o: 60:40 generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for the North-Eastern States
90:10 generally and 60:40 for the Himalayan States
51.x: MIDH follows a 60:40 sharing ratio generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan regions.
51.tq: Compare the normal cost-sharing ratio with the special-region ratio.

51.s: The National Mission on Edible Oils—Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with a financial outlay of:
51.x: NMEO-Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 with an outlay of ₹11,040 crore and focuses particularly on the North-East and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
51.tq: Separate the oil-palm mission’s outlay from the later oilseeds mission’s outlay.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Mission on Edible Oils—Oilseeds announced on 3 October 2024?
o: It focuses on oilseeds, has an outlay of ₹10,103 crore and targets 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
It focuses on horticulture and follows the MIDH funding ratio.
It focuses on pulses and targets 100 MT by 2029-30.
It focuses on oil palm and has an outlay of ₹11,040 crore.
51.x: NMEO-Oilseeds was announced on 3 October 2024 with ₹10,103 crore and aims to raise oilseed production from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
51.tq: Separate similar mission names by launch date, crop group, financial outlay and production target.

51.s: The National Mission on Edible Oils—Oilseeds seeks to increase production from 39 million tonnes to approximately how much by 2030-31?
51.x: The target is to raise oilseed production from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
51.tq: Use the stated baseline and target figures rather than calculating an unstated growth rate.

51.s: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) primarily aims to:
o: Provide grants to increase State expenditure on agriculture through State-led agricultural plans
Provide only crop insurance to farmers
Replace all State agricultural plans with a centrally fixed crop plan
Finance only oil-palm plantations in the North-Eastern States
51.x: RKVY supports State-led agricultural plans by providing grants intended to raise State spending on agriculture. It now functions under the umbrella PM-RKVY framework.
51.tq: Identify the scheme’s decentralised State-plan design instead of confusing it with a crop-specific mission.

51.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Technology Mission on Oilseeds, Pulses and Maize
B. National Food Security Mission
C. National Mission on Edible Oils—Oil Palm
D. National Mission on Edible Oils—Oilseeds
51.x: The sequence is 1986, 2007, August 2021 and 3 October 2024 respectively.
51.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest 1986 mission and the latest 2024 mission.

51.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana announced for 2025-26 is proposed as a Central Sector scheme covering:
o: All agricultural districts for five years
100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years
51.x: The scheme is proposed as a Central Sector scheme for 100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years.
51.tq: Match the scheme with its coverage, duration and performance-based district selection.

51.s: Under the pulses mission associated with the 2025-26 agricultural initiatives, 100% procurement at MSP is proposed for which crops through NAFED and NCCF?
51.x: The proposed mission provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor for four years through NAFED and NCCF.
51.tq: Distinguish the specified pulse trio from other pulses and oilseeds.

51.s: After 1991, agriculture’s share in India’s GDP declined from approximately 29.02% to 17.9% by 2014. Which broader development accompanied this change?
o: Complete withdrawal of agriculture from international trade
51.x: The decline in agriculture’s GDP share was accompanied by rising rural indebtedness.
51.tq: Read the paired trend carefully: falling GDP share was associated with rising, not falling, rural indebtedness.

51.s: Which one of the following was an effect of liberalisation after 1991 on Indian agriculture?
o: Replacement of agricultural subsidies by foreign aid
Increase in government investment in agriculture in every period
A ban on all private participation in agriculture
Decline in government investment in agriculture
51.x: The stated policy impact of post-1991 liberalisation was a decline in government investment in agriculture.
51.tq: Identify the precise policy consequence instead of accepting the positive-sounding reversal.

51.s: India’s entry into the WTO in 1995 was associated with which combination in the agricultural sector?
o: Reduced import competition and increased subsidies as a share of farm income
Increased import competition and declining subsidies as a share of farm income
Abolition of all domestic agricultural support
Reduced international trade and unchanged farm incomes
51.x: WTO entry increased import competition, while subsidies declined as a share of farm income.
51.tq: Pair the two stated effects and reject options that exaggerate them into total abolition or withdrawal.

51.s: Who among the following supported globalisation in the debate over agricultural liberalisation?
51.x: Sharad Joshi supported globalisation, whereas Tikait of BKU and Nanjundaswamy of KRRS opposed the Dunkel Draft.
51.tq: Separate the supporter of globalisation from the organisations and leaders associated with opposition to the Dunkel Draft.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding WTO boxes:
1. Green Box measures include research, disease control, infrastructure and food security support.
2. Blue Box payments are tied to limiting production.
3. Amber Box includes MSP and input subsidies such as power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All three statements correctly identify the measures associated with the Green, Blue and Amber Boxes.
51.tq: Match each box with its policy character before choosing the combined code.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly states the WTO treatment of the Amber Box?
o: It consists only of decoupled income support.
It is not trade-distorting and is freely allowed without limits.
It carries reduction commitments, subject to de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
It consists of payments tied to limiting production and has no reduction commitment.
51.x: Amber Box support is subject to reduction commitments, with de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
51.tq: Distinguish Amber Box reduction commitments from Green Box permission and Blue Box production-limitation payments.

51.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 was announced in:
51.x: The National Agriculture Policy was announced in July 2000.
51.tq: Use the announcement date rather than confusing it with the NFSM or NMEO launch dates.

51.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 envisaged annual agricultural growth of:
51.x: The policy targeted agricultural growth in excess of 4% per annum.
51.tq: Recall the exact threshold and distinguish 'in excess of' from an exact growth rate.

51.s:
Which of the following were key thrusts of the National Agriculture Policy, 2000?
1. Private participation through contract farming and land leasing
2. Price protection and national agricultural insurance
3. A Rainbow Revolution covering all farm sub-sectors
Select the correct answer using the code below.
51.x: The policy emphasised private participation, price protection, agricultural insurance and a broad-based Rainbow Revolution across farm sub-sectors.
51.tq: Test the complete set of policy thrusts rather than isolating contract farming alone.

51.s: Which one of the following colour-crop pairs is NOT correctly matched?
51.x: Silver Revolution is associated with eggs. Fertilisers are associated with the Grey Revolution.
51.tq: Use the colour association and identify the swapped pair between Silver and Grey Revolutions.

51.s: Sustainable agriculture is best understood as the use of land in a manner that:
o: Excludes all modern inputs from farming
Maximises present output regardless of future soil quality
Maintains land quality while meeting present needs without compromising future generations
Uses land only for export-oriented crops
51.x: Sustainable agriculture maintains the quality of land while meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
51.tq: Apply the intergenerational and resource-conservation test to the definition.

51.s:
The ultimate goal of sustainable agriculture includes which of the following pillars?
1. Environmental health
2. Economic profitability
3. Social and economic equity
Select the correct answer using the code below.
51.x: Sustainable agriculture seeks to combine environmental health, economic profitability and social and economic equity.
51.tq: Recognise that sustainability is a three-pillar framework, not merely an environmental objective.

51.s: Which statement best distinguishes sustainable agriculture from organic farming?
o: There is no conceptual distinction between the two.
Sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously through approaches such as IPM, precision farming and conservation tillage.
Sustainable agriculture necessarily prohibits all synthetic inputs.
Organic farming permits unlimited synthetic inputs, whereas sustainable agriculture prohibits them.
51.x: Unlike a strict organic approach, sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously along with integrated pest management, precision farming and conservation tillage.
51.tq: Focus on the qualifying word 'judiciously' when distinguishing the two approaches.
