51.s: Rainfed farming accounts for approximately what share of India’s net sown area and food production, respectively?
51.x: Rainfed farming covers about 50–60% of net sown area and contributes approximately 40% of food production.
51.tq: Keep the area share and production share separate; they are not the same percentage.

51.s: The National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), set up in 2006, is primarily an expert body for:
o: Providing knowledge inputs and coordinating dryland and rainfed upgradation through a watershed approach
Administering MSP procurement in all States
51.x: NRAA provides expert knowledge and coordinates the upgrading of dryland and rainfed areas through a watershed approach.
51.tq: Match the authority with its dryland, rainfed and watershed functions.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the pre-Green Revolution phase of agricultural development in India?
o: 1968–81; HYV seeds, fertiliser and irrigation under the New Agricultural Strategy
1987–92; spread of the Green Revolution to rice and other regions
1951–68; exclusive dependence on oilseeds and horticulture
1951–68; land reforms, irrigation, Community Development, PL-480 imports and droughts of 1965–67
51.x: The pre-Green Revolution phase covered 1951–68 and included land reforms, irrigation, Community Development, PL-480 imports and the droughts of 1965–67.
51.tq: Match the period with its defining features rather than with the later HYV phase.

51.s: The Early Green Revolution phase in India is associated with:
o: 1987–92 and the spread of horticulture alone
1968–81, HYV seeds beginning with wheat, fertiliser, irrigation and the New Agricultural Strategy
51.x: The Early Green Revolution phase was 1968–81 and was marked by HYV seeds, initially in wheat, along with fertiliser, irrigation and the New Agricultural Strategy.
51.tq: Use the wheat-first HYV clue to identify the Early Green Revolution period.

51.s: The Later Green Revolution phase, covering 1987–92, was characterised by:
o: The spread of the Green Revolution to rice and other regions
Land reforms and Community Development programmes
51.x: The Later Green Revolution phase saw the spread of Green Revolution benefits to rice and other regions during 1987–92.
51.tq: Match the later period with geographical and crop-wise expansion.

51.s:
Arrange the following phases of agricultural development in India in chronological order:
A. Later Green Revolution
B. Pre-Green Revolution
C. Early Green Revolution
51.x: The phases occurred in the order Pre-Green Revolution (1951–68), Early Green Revolution (1968–81) and Later Green Revolution (1987–92).
51.tq: Arrange the phases by their stated periods, using the earliest period as the first anchor.

51.s: India’s foodgrain production fell to approximately what level in 1965-66?
51.x: Foodgrain production fell to 72.3 million tonnes in 1965-66.
51.tq: Recall the historical low-point figure and distinguish it from the later production records.

51.s: Which statement correctly compares India’s recent foodgrain and horticulture production?
o: Horticulture production was below 300 MT in 2024-25.
Foodgrain production was 357.73 MT in 2024-25, while horticulture production was 362.08 MT and therefore higher.
Foodgrain production was 362.08 MT, while horticulture production was 357.73 MT.
Both foodgrain and horticulture production were exactly 357.73 MT.
51.x: Foodgrain production was recorded at 357.73 MT in 2024-25, while horticulture production reached 362.08 MT, making horticulture larger.
51.tq: Compare the two close figures carefully and identify which production category is higher.

51.s: The National Commission on Agriculture, which submitted its report in 1976, was chaired by whom?
51.x: The National Commission on Agriculture functioned during 1970–76 and submitted its report in 1976 under the chairmanship of Nathu Ram Mirdha.
51.tq: Use the chairperson–commission association to eliminate names belonging to other agricultural bodies.

51.s: Which one of the following was a recommendation or contribution associated with the National Commission on Agriculture?
o: Recommending MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent
Introducing the National Agricultural Risk Fund
51.x: The National Commission on Agriculture recommended HYVs, irrigation and credit reforms, and is associated with coining the term “social forestry”.
51.tq: Match the institutional recommendation with the correct commission instead of a neighbouring agricultural committee.

51.s: The National Commission on Farmers was constituted on:
51.x: The National Commission on Farmers was constituted on 18 November 2004.
51.tq: Distinguish the constitution date of the commission from dates associated with later schemes.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission on Farmers:
1. It was chaired by M. S. Swaminathan.
2. It submitted five reports during 2004–06.
3. It recommended universal crop insurance and a National Agricultural Risk Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All three statements are correct. The commission was chaired by M. S. Swaminathan, submitted five reports between 2004 and 2006, and recommended universal crop insurance and a National Agricultural Risk Fund.
51.tq: Check each statement against the commission’s chair, report count and recommendations before selecting the coded combination.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the recommended MSP formula of the National Commission on Farmers from the present Government MSP policy described here?
o: The Commission recommended C2+50 per cent, whereas the Government uses 1.5 times A2+FL.
The Commission recommended MSP for 22 crops, whereas the Government has no crop coverage.
The Commission recommended 1.5 times A2+FL, whereas the Government uses C2+50 per cent.
Both recommend only A2+FL without any addition.
51.x: The National Commission on Farmers recommended MSP at C2 plus 50 per cent, while the Government MSP policy uses 1.5 times A2+FL. MSPs are stated to cover 22 mandated crops.
51.tq: Split the paired cost concepts first: C2+50 per cent belongs to the Commission recommendation, while 1.5 times A2+FL belongs to current policy.

51.s: Under PM-AASHA, which component involves procurement by NAFED and NCCF?
51.x: The Price Support Scheme (PSS) under PM-AASHA involves procurement through agencies such as NAFED and NCCF.
51.tq: Discriminate among similarly abbreviated PM-AASHA components by matching each one with its specific function.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-AASHA:
1. It was launched in 2018 to provide remunerative prices.
2. Under PDPS, the price-gap coverage was raised to 40 per cent of State oilseed output.
3. Under MIS, the coverage mentioned is 25 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: PM-AASHA was launched in 2018. Its components include PDPS, with coverage raised to 40 per cent of State oilseed output, and MIS with 25 per cent coverage as specified.
51.tq: Retain the numerical pair 40 per cent and 25 per cent while testing the scheme’s objective and components together.

51.s: The e-NAM platform was launched in April 2016 by which organisation?
51.x: e-NAM was launched in April 2016 by the Small Farmers’ Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC).
51.tq: Use the launching agency as the decisive clue in a scheme–institution question.

51.s: As of March 2026, the e-NAM network covered:
o: 1,656 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories
1,656 mandis in 22 States and 5 Union Territories
1,856 mandis in 24 States and 3 Union Territories
1,565 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories
51.x: The e-NAM network was stated to cover 1,656 mandis across 23 States and 4 Union Territories as of March 2026.
51.tq: Treat the mandi, State and Union Territory figures as a single numerical combination and reject altered digits or coverage.

51.s: Operation Greens was initially intended to stabilise the prices of which group of commodities?
51.x: Operation Greens initially focused on stabilising Tomato–Onion–Potato prices, on the lines of Operation Flood.
51.tq: Recall the distinctive TOP acronym and avoid substituting other agricultural commodity groups.

51.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Operation Greens?
o: It transports perishables by air under the Price Support Scheme.
It was limited permanently to tomato, onion and potato.
It was provided for in Budget 2018–19 and was widened to 22 perishables from 2021–22.
It was launched in April 2016 and initially covered all cereals.
51.x: Operation Greens was included in Budget 2018–19 and, from 2021–22, was widened from the original TOP commodities to 22 perishables.
51.tq: Find the option that preserves both the initial policy year and the later expansion instead of an absolute limitation.

51.s: The primary purpose of Krishi UDAN is to:
o: Transport perishables by air to raise value realisation
Create a unified electronic APMC platform
Provide crop insurance to tenant farmers
51.x: Krishi UDAN uses air transport for perishables with the objective of improving value realisation.
51.tq: Identify the scheme from its operational instrument—air transport—rather than from a general price-support objective.

51.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget for 2026–27, consider the following statements:
1. Its approximate outlay was ₹53,753 crore.
2. The Agriculture Department allocation was ₹12,153 crore.
3. Agriculture accounted for 33.20 per cent of GSDP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: The 2026–27 Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Budget had an approximate outlay of ₹53,753 crore, included ₹12,153 crore for the Agriculture Department, and represented 33.20 per cent of GSDP.
51.tq: Verify the three figures independently, since the distractors alter either the allocation, total outlay or GSDP share.

51.s: The 2026–27 separate Agriculture Budget of Andhra Pradesh was the third such budget and was presented by:
51.x: The 2026–27 Agriculture Budget was the third separate Agriculture Budget of Andhra Pradesh and was presented by Minister K. Atchannaidu.
51.tq: Link the State budget sequence with the responsible Minister, not with chairs of national commissions.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes PM-KISAN?
o: A Central Sector scheme providing ₹6,000 annually in three instalments of ₹2,000 to landholding families
A Central Sector scheme providing ₹20,000 annually in two instalments to all rural households
A State scheme providing ₹13,500 annually to tenant farmers only
A procurement scheme providing MSP compensation to oilseed producers
51.x: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme, operative from 1 December 2018, that provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000 to eligible landholding farmer families.
51.tq: Separate PM-KISAN’s amount, instalment pattern and beneficiary category from State farmer-support schemes.

51.s: The cut-off date for identifying landholding families under PM-KISAN was:
51.x: The cut-off date specified for identifying landholding families under PM-KISAN was 1 February 2019.
51.tq: Distinguish the scheme’s commencement date from its beneficiary-identification cut-off date.

51.s: The 23rd instalment of PM-KISAN reached approximately how many farmers, with total disbursement exceeding which amount?
51.x: The 23rd instalment reached 9.49 crore farmers, and cumulative transfers exceeded ₹4.47 lakh crore.
51.tq: Pair the beneficiary count with the cumulative financial figure and reject reversals of units or digits.

51.s: Under Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan in Andhra Pradesh, the total annual assistance per family is:
51.x: The combined annual assistance is ₹20,000 per family, consisting of ₹14,000 from Andhra Pradesh and ₹6,000 from the Centre.
51.tq: Add the State and Central components before choosing the combined annual assistance.

51.s: Which of the following correctly gives the instalment pattern under Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan?
51.x: The instalments are ₹7,000 for Kharif, ₹7,000 for Rabi and ₹6,000 for Summer; each includes ₹2,000 from the Central component.
51.tq: Use the seasonal sequence to distinguish the two equal instalments from the smaller summer instalment.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan:
1. It covers landholders and tenant farmers.
2. Tenant farmers are outside the coverage of PM-KISAN.
3. In 2025–26, it covered 46.86 lakh families with ₹6,309 crore released in two instalments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct for Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan. Statement 2 is also true only in relation to PM-KISAN itself, but it conflicts with the first statement when the combined Andhra Pradesh scheme is being described; the stated combined scheme covers tenant farmers, while tenants are outside PM-KISAN.
51.tq: Separate the beneficiary coverage of the combined State scheme from the narrower coverage of PM-KISAN.

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Operation Greens — ₹20,000 per family per year to landless labourers
YSR Rythu Bharosa — ₹13,500 per family per year, including tenant and RoFR farmers
PM-KISAN — ₹13,500 per family per year, including tenant farmers
Annadata Sukhibhava — ₹6,000 per family per year without a State component
51.x: Earlier YSR Rythu Bharosa provided ₹13,500 per family per year and included tenant and RoFR farmers. The other options wrongly attribute amounts or objectives to unrelated schemes.
51.tq: Use beneficiary coverage and annual amount together to identify the correctly matched State scheme.

51.s: The Ashok Dalwai Committee on Doubling Farmers’ Income functioned during:
51.x: The Ashok Dalwai Committee functioned during 2016–18 and produced 14 volumes. The target year for doubling farmers’ income was 2022, with 2015–16 as the base year.
51.tq: Keep the committee’s functioning period separate from its base year and target year.

51.s: The target year and base year associated with the Doubling Farmers’ Income strategy were, respectively:
51.x: The strategy set 2022 as the target year and used 2015–16 as the base year.
51.tq: Read the pair in the order asked—target year first and base year second—to avoid reversing them.

51.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the identified sources of growth in farmers’ income?
o: Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops
51.x: The seven sources include crop productivity, livestock productivity, resource-use efficiency, cropping intensity, diversification to high-value crops, better price realisation and movement to non-farm jobs. Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops is not one of them.
51.tq: Find the option that contradicts the diversification and productivity-based approach.

51.s: The Doubling Farmers’ Income approach represents a shift from production-oriented thinking towards:
o: Income enhancement through value addition, market reform and post-harvest infrastructure
Withdrawal of livestock and fisheries from farm planning
51.x: The approach shifts from “production” to “income” through value addition, clusters, e-NAM and APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure, livestock-fisheries integration and land-leasing laws.
51.tq: In an application question, identify the option that combines the stated income-enhancing interventions rather than a single production measure.

51.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven sources of growth in farmers’ income?
51.x: The strategy identifies a shift to non-farm jobs as a source of income growth; reduction of non-farm employment opportunities is therefore not included.
51.tq: Watch for the reversed meaning in the option: the strategy supports a shift to non-farm jobs, not its reduction.

51.s: According to the Union Budget 2026–27 figure cited for agriculture, the allocation was approximately:
51.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹1.3 lakh crore to agriculture, representing a 2.6 per cent increase.
51.tq: Distinguish the Union agriculture allocation from the separate Andhra Pradesh budget and scheme-specific figures.

51.s: Farm unions criticised the Union Budget 2026–27 primarily for the absence of:
o: Oil palm cultivation and fisheries integration
51.x: Farm unions criticised the absence of statutory MSP and debt relief in the Union Budget 2026–27.
51.tq: Identify the specific criticism rather than selecting general agricultural policy measures.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding oil palm cultivation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm area.
2. Its oil palm area was 2.49 lakh hectares, constituting 48 per cent of India’s area.
3. Production of fresh fruit bunches was 22.81 lakh metric tonnes in 2024–25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm cultivation, with 2.49 lakh hectares or 48 per cent of India’s area, and produced 22.81 lakh metric tonnes of fresh fruit bunches in 2024–25.
51.tq: Check the leadership claim, area share and production figure as separate components of the State’s oil-palm position.

51.s: Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s agricultural growth objective mentioned in the material?
o: 30 per cent growth in one year through 22 growth engines
48 per cent agricultural growth in five years through 17 growth engines
17 per cent growth in five years through 30 growth engines
30 per cent agricultural growth in five years through 17 growth engines
51.x: Andhra Pradesh has set a target of 30 per cent agricultural growth in five years through 17 growth engines.
51.tq: Keep the two figures attached to their correct units—30 per cent is the growth target and 17 is the number of growth engines.

52.s: According to the Agricultural Census 2015-16, what proportion of total operational holdings and operated area respectively was accounted for by small and marginal holdings below 2 hectares?
52.x: Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of all holdings but accounted for only 47.3% of the operated area in 2015-16.
52.tq: Read the table row-wise and distinguish the share of holdings from the share of operated area.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Agricultural Census 2015-16:
1. Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of the holdings.
2. Semi-medium and medium holdings accounted for 43.6% of the operated area.
3. Semi-medium and medium holdings constituted 43.6% of the total holdings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Semi-medium and medium holdings constituted 13.2% of holdings, not 43.6%; 43.6% was their share of operated area.
52.tq: Separate percentages referring to holdings from those referring to operated area.

52.s: With reference to the Agricultural Census 2010-11, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 58% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 58% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 44% of holdings and held about 85% of operated area.
52.x: In the 2010-11 Agricultural Census, small holdings were about 85% of holdings but accounted for only about 44% of the operated area.
52.tq: Match the two percentages with their correct dimensions instead of reversing the table.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural holdings in India:
1. There were about 146 million holdings in 2015-16.
2. The average size of a holding was about 1.08 hectares in 2015-16.
3. The 11th Agriculture Census 2021-22 has, so far, only provisional State results.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct: India had about 146 million holdings averaging 1.08 hectares in 2015-16, while only provisional State results of the 2021-22 Census were available as stated.
52.tq: Check each numerical and status statement independently before selecting the combined option.

52.s: With reference to the provisional 11th Agriculture Census data for Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Average holding size—0.86 hectares; number of holdings—96.90 lakh
Average holding size—0.94 hectares; number of holdings—96.90 lakh
Average holding size—0.86 hectares; number of holdings—85.24 lakh
Average holding size—1.08 hectares; number of holdings—146 million
52.x: The provisional Andhra Pradesh figures are an average holding size of 0.86 hectares and 96.90 lakh holdings, compared with 0.94 hectares and 85.24 lakh holdings in 2015-16.
52.tq: Use the sure numerical pair and reject options that mix figures from different years or geographical levels.

52.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the poor viability of small and marginal agricultural holdings?
52.x: Small and marginal holdings are associated with few surpluses, not abundant marketable surpluses. Uneconomical mechanisation, weak bargaining power and poor credit are identified viability constraints.
52.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated condition rather than merely naming a related problem.

52.s: Which of the following measures is most directly intended to improve the viability and bargaining position of small and marginal farmers by aggregating them into producer organisations?
o: Reduction of operated area per holding
Replacement of crop insurance by informal lending
52.x: Farmer Producer Organisations aggregate farmers and improve their collective bargaining and economic position. The other alternatives would weaken, rather than improve, viability.
52.tq: Identify the institutional remedy that addresses fragmentation and weak bargaining power.

52.s: The Central Sector scheme for formation and promotion of how many Farmer Producer Organisations was launched in 2020, with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore?
52.x: The 10,000 FPO scheme was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore.
52.tq: Use the scheme’s distinctive target number and expenditure together.

52.s: As reported up to January 2026, how many farmers had been registered under the 10,000 FPO scheme?
52.x: By January 2026, 56.32 lakh farmers had been registered under the 10,000 FPO scheme.
52.tq: Distinguish lakh-level registration data from the number of holdings and the scheme target.

52.s: Which of the following set of measures is associated with improving the viability of small and marginal holdings?
o: Reduction of irrigation and removal of collective institutions
Exclusive dependence on individual machinery ownership and informal credit
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
Abolition of producer organisations and cluster-based activities
52.x: Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.
52.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated institutional and operational remedies.

52.s: Which one of the following statements regarding cooperative joint farming in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: There are 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, while their federations are under liquidation.
There are 10,000 primary societies functioning under the FPO scheme.
There are 85.24 primary societies, while federations are being expanded.
There are 210 federations, while all primary societies have been dissolved.
52.x: Andhra Pradesh has 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, while the federations are under liquidation as reported for 2024-25.
52.tq: Match the correct institutional level with the correct status instead of swapping societies and federations.

52.s: The principal source for official data on farmer and agricultural labourer suicides in India is which of the following?
o: Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
52.x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
52.tq: Identify the exact official report title rather than a related agricultural publication.

52.s: According to the NCRB ADSI 2015 data, the biggest reported cause of farmer suicides was:
52.x: The biggest cause identified in the NCRB ADSI 2015 data was bankruptcy or indebtedness.
52.tq: Recall the principal causal category and avoid substituting a general agricultural problem for the recorded cause.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional pattern of farmer suicides:
1. A 28-year NCRB analysis covered the period 1995-2023.
2. The analysis found a sharp resurgence in suicides in 2023 after a decade of decline.
3. Suicides have been concentrated mainly in rain-fed belts.
4. Historically, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have been among the most severely affected areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements correctly describe the reported time span, recent resurgence, rain-fed concentration and historical concentration in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
52.tq: Combine temporal, geographical and state-level clues only after checking each statement.

52.s: According to NCRB ADSI 2024, the total number of suicides reported in India and the number attributed to the farm sector respectively were:
52.x: ADSI 2024 reported 1,70,746 suicides in total, of which 10,546 belonged to the farm sector.
52.tq: Distinguish the aggregate total from the farm-sector subset.

52.s: The farm-sector suicide figure of 10,546 in NCRB ADSI 2024 comprised:
o: 10,546 farmers or cultivators and no agricultural labourers
4,481 farmers or cultivators and 152 agricultural labourers
4,633 farmers or cultivators and 5,913 agricultural labourers
5,913 farmers or cultivators and 4,633 agricultural labourers
52.x: The farm-sector total consisted of 4,633 farmers or cultivators and 5,913 agricultural labourers.
52.tq: Break the aggregate into its two component categories before selecting the option.

52.s: What percentage of total suicides did the farm sector account for in NCRB ADSI 2024?
52.x: The farm sector accounted for 10,546 out of 1,70,746 suicides, reported as 6.2% of the total.
52.tq: Link the percentage to the stated total and subset rather than to one component alone.

52.s: With reference to the gender-wise distribution of farmer or cultivator suicides in NCRB ADSI 2024, which one of the following is correct?
52.x: Of the farmer or cultivator suicides, 4,481 were men and 152 were women.
52.tq: Keep the farmer or cultivator category separate from the broader farm-sector total.

52.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported position regarding farmer and tenant suicides in Andhra Pradesh under the coalition government?
o: The Tenant Farmers Association reported over 300 deaths, while 112 were officially recognised.
The Association reported 112 deaths, while over 300 were officially recognised.
No deaths were reported and no demand for an inquiry was made.
Both the Association and official records reported exactly 300 deaths.
52.x: The Tenant Farmers Association claimed that more than 300 farmers and tenants died by suicide, whereas only 112 were officially recognised. It demanded a truth-finding committee.
52.tq: Distinguish an association’s claim from the number officially recognised.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the work of the National Commission on Farmers?
o: It was set up exclusively for food procurement and submitted one report in 2015.
It was set up to regulate foreign trade and submitted five reports during 1991-1996.
It was set up to formulate industrial policy and submitted two reports during 2007-2010.
It was set up to address the calamity of farmer suicides and submitted five reports during 2004-2006.
52.x: The Commission was established to address the crisis of farmer suicides and submitted five reports between 2004 and 2006.
52.tq: Match the Commission’s purpose with its correct number and period of reports.

52.s:
C2, in the MSP formula recommended by the National Commission on Farmers, includes which of the following components?
1. A2 costs
2. Imputed value of family labour
3. Imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: C2 includes A2, family labour and imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital; hence all three statements are correct.
52.tq: Expand the cost acronym component by component before judging the statements.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Commission’s MSP recommendation from the formula applied by the Government?
o: The Commission recommended C2 plus 50%, while the Government applies 50% over A2+FL.
The Commission recommended A2+FL plus 50%, while the Government applies C2 plus 50%.
The Commission recommended C2 minus 50%, while the Government applies A2 alone.
Both the Commission and the Government apply only C2 without any margin.
52.x: The Commission recommended C2 plus 50%, whereas the Government applies 50% over A2+FL, which does not include the full C2 cost concept.
52.tq: Split the similar-looking formulas at the cost base—C2 versus A2+FL.

52.s: Which of the following was NOT among the recommendations associated with the National Commission on Farmers?
o: Secure rights for women and tenants
52.x: The Commission recommended affordable credit, not its abolition. It also recommended land reforms, rights for women and tenants, universal crop insurance and a National Agricultural Risk Fund.
52.tq: Identify the option that reverses a recommendation by using an institutional opposite.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations and vision of the National Commission on Farmers:
1. It supported land reforms and market reforms.
2. It recommended irrigation, cheaper institutional credit and crop insurance.
3. It envisaged farming as economically viable and ecologically sustainable.
4. It sought improvement in the quality of life of farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements reflect the Commission’s recommendations and core vision for economically viable, ecologically sustainable farming and improved farmer welfare.
52.tq: Group the policy recommendations with the Commission’s broader outcome-oriented vision.

52.s: The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew upon the reports of which body?
o: Agricultural Costs and Prices Commission alone
52.x: The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew upon the reports of the National Commission on Farmers chaired by M. S. Swaminathan.
52.tq: Identify the policy-report linkage by matching the policy with the body that prepared the relevant recommendations.

52.s: The crop holiday observed by paddy farmers in 2011 was associated with which region of Andhra Pradesh?
52.x: The 2011 crop holiday was observed by paddy farmers of Konaseema in East Godavari district.
52.tq: Use the location clue to identify the specific agrarian movement.

52.s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 primarily provided tenants with which instrument?
52.x: The AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 provided Loan Eligibility Cards (LECs) to tenant cultivators.
52.tq: Discriminate between closely related agricultural card-based instruments.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Loan Eligibility Cards under the Andhra Pradesh Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011:
1. They facilitate access to credit for tenant cultivators.
2. They enable access to crop insurance.
3. They transfer ownership rights in the land to the tenant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Loan Eligibility Cards facilitate credit and insurance for tenants without affecting the landowner's rights. They do not transfer ownership of the land.
52.tq: Find the statement that incorrectly converts a tenancy benefit into an ownership right.

52.s: The Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivators Rights Act was enacted in which year?
52.x: The Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivators Rights Act was enacted in 2019.
52.tq: Test the year associated with a specific state tenancy law.

52.s:
With reference to Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCR cards) in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. They were issued from 2 October 2019.
2. They are valid for 11 months.
3. They require an agreement between the landowner and the cultivator.
4. They permanently transfer land ownership to the cultivator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: CCR cards were issued from 2 October 2019, remain valid for 11 months and require mutual agreement between owner and cultivator. They do not transfer land ownership.
52.tq: Separate tenancy documentation from ownership rights by eliminating the absolute claim.

52.s: Which one of the following is NOT a benefit associated with Crop Cultivator Rights Cards in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Automatic ownership of the cultivated land
52.x: CCR cards provide access to bank credit, insurance, input subsidy and benefits such as Annadata Sukhibhava without affecting the owner's rights. They do not confer ownership.
52.tq: Identify the ownership-related overstatement among genuine tenancy benefits.

52.s: As reported for the relevant period, the number of active Crop Cultivator Rights Cards in Andhra Pradesh was approximately:
52.x: Andhra Pradesh had approximately 8.24 lakh active CCR cards, comprising 7.47 lakh new and 0.78 lakh renewed cards.
52.tq: Use the total figure rather than confusing it with one component or an earlier estimate.

52.s: The composition of 8.24 lakh active Crop Cultivator Rights Cards in Andhra Pradesh was approximately:
o: 4.12 lakh new and 4.12 lakh renewed cards
7.47 lakh renewed and 0.78 lakh new cards
8.24 lakh new cards with no renewals
7.47 lakh new and 0.78 lakh renewed cards
52.x: The active total consisted of 7.47 lakh new cards and 0.78 lakh renewed cards.
52.tq: Split the total into its reported components before selecting the option.

52.s: The active Crop Cultivator Rights Cards in Andhra Pradesh had enabled tenant loans of approximately:
52.x: The active CCR cards had enabled approximately ₹3,768 crore in loans to tenant cultivators.
52.tq: Match the card-status figure with its associated credit-outcome figure.

52.s: Which of the following has been identified as a major obstacle in extending formal benefits to tenant cultivators in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Prohibition on crop insurance for tenants
Absence of crop cultivation in the State
52.x: The requirement of the landowner's signature is a major obstacle for tenant cultivators seeking formal credit and other benefits.
52.tq: Apply the institutional requirement to a practical tenant-finance situation.

52.s: According to the cited tenants' association estimate, tenant cultivators constitute approximately what proportion of cultivators in Andhra Pradesh?
52.x: The Andhra Pradesh Tenants' Farmers' Association has estimated that tenants constitute about 70–80 percent of the State's cultivators.
52.tq: Test the reported range rather than a single-point estimate.

52.s: Which combination correctly represents the mechanisms through which Andhra Pradesh has been described as a pioneer in tenant finance?
52.x: Andhra Pradesh has been described as a pioneer in tenant finance through Rythu Mitra Groups, Joint Liability Groups and Crop Cultivator Rights Cards.
52.tq: Start from the sure pair of the three tenant-finance mechanisms.

52.s: During 2024–25, APCOB lent approximately ₹125.90 crore to how many tenant farmers?
52.x: APCOB lent ₹125.90 crore to 14,425 tenant farmers during 2024–25.
52.tq: Link the reported loan amount with its corresponding beneficiary count.

52.s: The proposed Andhra Pradesh New Tenancy Act, 2024 envisaged the issue of:
52.x: The proposed Andhra Pradesh New Tenancy Act, 2024 envisaged tenant entitlement cards.
52.tq: Identify the specific legal instrument associated with the proposed legislation.

52.s: The tenants' association demand relating to Kisan Credit Card finance for RMG and JLG members was for unsecured crop loans of:
52.x: The tenants' association sought ₹2 lakh unsecured crop loans through KCCs for RMG and JLG members.
52.tq: Distinguish the demanded loan ceiling from other plausible credit limits.

52.s: The NSSO 77th Round Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households was associated with which year?
52.x: The NSSO 77th Round Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households was conducted for 2019.
52.tq: Separate the 77th Round reference year from the 70th Round year.

52.s: According to the NSSO 77th Round, approximately what proportion of agricultural households in India were indebted?
52.x: Approximately 50 percent of agricultural households were indebted according to the NSSO 77th Round.
52.tq: Use the broad national proportion rather than the much higher Andhra Pradesh figure.

52.s: The average outstanding debt per agricultural household reported in the NSSO 77th Round was approximately:
52.x: The average debt was approximately ₹74,121 per agricultural household, or more than ₹74,000.
52.tq: Recognise the exact figure behind the rounded value used in summaries.

52.s: Which State recorded the highest proportion of indebted agricultural households among the major States in the cited survey?
52.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded the highest proportion among major States, with 93.2 percent of agricultural households indebted.
52.tq: Compare the State-specific indebtedness figures before selecting the maximum.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding indebtedness of agricultural households:
1. In Andhra Pradesh, 93.2 percent of agricultural households were indebted.
2. In Telangana, the corresponding proportion was 91.7 percent.
3. Andhra Pradesh recorded a lower proportion than Telangana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Andhra Pradesh's 93.2 percent was higher than Telangana's 91.7 percent.
52.tq: Check the direction of the comparison after verifying the two percentages.

52.s: The reliance of Andhra Pradesh farmers on non-institutional credit was approximately what proportion, compared with about 31 percent nationally?
52.x: Approximately 50 percent of Andhra Pradesh farmers relied on non-institutional credit, compared with about 31 percent nationally.
52.tq: Use the State–national contrast rather than treating the national figure as the State figure.

52.s:
Arrange the following survey rounds and their associated years in chronological order:
A. NSSO 70th Round Situation Assessment Survey
B. NSSO 77th Round Situation Assessment Survey
C. Proposed next Situation Assessment Survey with AIDIS
D. Fieldwork period for the proposed next survey
52.x: The 70th Round relates to 2013, the 77th Round to 2019, the next survey is scheduled for 2026–27, and its fieldwork is scheduled from July 2026 to June 2027.
52.tq: Arrange the items by their survey year and then by the fieldwork period.

52.s: The next Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households, along with the All-India Debt and Investment Survey, is scheduled for:
52.x: The next Situation Assessment Survey, to be conducted with AIDIS, is scheduled for 2026–27.
52.tq: Distinguish the scheduled survey year from the year of the preceding economic survey reference.

52.s: The fieldwork for the next Situation Assessment Survey is scheduled to be conducted by the NSO during:
52.x: The NSO fieldwork is scheduled from July 2026 to June 2027.
52.tq: Read the survey schedule as a precise month-to-month period.

52.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a cause of agrarian distress in the cited assessment?
52.x: Crop failure, high input costs, unstable prices and dependence on rainfed agriculture are identified causes. Guaranteed and stable returns would not constitute a distress factor.
52.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated cause.

52.s: Which of the following correctly explains the role of rainfed dependence in agrarian distress?
o: It increases vulnerability when borewells fail or rainfall is inadequate.
It guarantees uniform yields across holdings.
It ensures access to institutional credit.
It eliminates the need for irrigation investment.
52.x: Dependence on rainfed agriculture increases vulnerability to inadequate rainfall and failed borewells, thereby contributing to agrarian distress.
52.tq: Apply the cause–effect relationship to a farm-risk situation.

52.s: According to the 77th Round income composition, which sequence correctly represents the major sources of agricultural household income in descending order?
52.x: Wages formed the largest share of agricultural household income, followed by crop cultivation and then livestock.
52.tq: Arrange income sources by relative share rather than by their conventional sectoral order.

52.s: The average monthly income of an agricultural household reported in the NSSO 77th Round was approximately:
52.x: The average monthly income of an agricultural household was approximately ₹10,218.
52.tq: Identify the precise survey income figure among closely spaced numerical options.

52.s: The national share of non-institutional credit in 2021–22 was reported as approximately:
52.x: The national non-institutional credit share was reported as 23.4 percent in 2021–22.
52.tq: Distinguish the later national estimate from the older historical benchmark.

52.s: A separate estimate placed the share of informal lenders at nearly 28 percent. Which statement best explains its relation to the 23.4 percent estimate?
o: The 23.4 percent figure refers exclusively to Andhra Pradesh.
The 28 percent figure refers to institutional credit only.
The difference can reflect different surveys and source methodologies.
Both figures necessarily refer to the same survey and year.
52.x: The two estimates come from different surveys and sources; therefore, their difference need not indicate a contradiction. The 23.4 percent figure is a national 2021–22 estimate, while the nearly 28 percent figure is from a separate estimate.
52.tq: Avoid merging figures from different surveys without checking their source and scope.

52.s: According to the cited data, farm household income recorded what nominal change between FY13 and FY19?
52.x: Farm household income recorded a 59 percent nominal rise between FY13 and FY19.
52.tq: Distinguish the nominal increase from nearby alternative percentage changes.

52.s: Input costs in Indian agriculture have risen by more than what percentage since the early 2000s, while real farm incomes stagnated?
52.x: Fertiliser, seed and pesticide costs rose by more than 300% since the early 2000s, while real farm incomes stagnated.
52.tq: Use the distinctive numerical trend rather than the general statement about rising costs.

52.s: A farmer receiving only about 35% of the retail price of agricultural produce is primarily affected by which factor?
52.x: Intermediaries and price volatility result in farmers receiving only about 35% of the retail price.
52.tq: Identify the cause from the farmer’s position in the value chain.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rainfall dependence and irrigation in India:
1. About 50% of the net sown area is rain-fed.
2. About 64% of irrigation depends on groundwater.
3. About 17% of groundwater blocks are over-exploited.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct: rain-fed farming covers about half of the net sown area, groundwater supplies about 64% of irrigation, and 17% of groundwater blocks are over-exploited.
52.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the coded combination.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the average foodgrain yield and the corresponding world average mentioned in relation to small holdings?
52.x: The average foodgrain yield is 2,929 kg per hectare, compared with a world average of 4,000 kg per hectare.
52.tq: Preserve the direction of the comparison before checking the figures.

52.s: What proportion of agricultural holdings in India are classified as small and marginal, with holdings below two hectares?
52.x: Small and marginal holdings account for about 86% of all holdings and are defined here as holdings under two hectares.
52.tq: Distinguish the share of holdings from the separate figures relating to irrigation and rainfall.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about post-harvest losses:
1. The cold-chain deficit is about 30%.
2. Fruits and vegetables may suffer post-harvest losses of up to 40%.
3. Farmers receive about 40% of the retail price.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Farmers receive about 35%, not 40%, of the retail price, so statement 3 is false.
52.tq: Watch for a small numerical alteration in an otherwise familiar statement.

52.s: The N:P:K ratio in Indian soils, as reported in the Economic Survey 2025–26, is approximately:
52.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 gives the prevailing N:P:K ratio as 10.9:4.1:1, compared with the ideal ratio of 4:2:1.
52.tq: Separate the prevailing ratio from the recommended ideal ratio and from the alternative reported figure.

52.s: Which of the following is the recommended ideal N:P:K ratio for balanced soil nutrient application?
52.x: The recommended ideal N:P:K ratio is 4:2:1. The ratios beginning with 10.9 describe the reported imbalance in soil nutrient use.
52.tq: Discriminate between the existing input pattern and the recommended benchmark.

52.s: With every 1°C rise in temperature, agricultural yields are reported to fall by approximately:
52.x: Agricultural yields fall by about 8% for every 1°C of warming.
52.tq: Recall the quantified climate-impact relationship rather than the general effect of warming.

52.s: Which of the following was NOT identified by the Andhra Pradesh Commission on Farmers’ Welfare as a main driver of agrarian distress?
52.x: The Commission identified lack of institutional credit, not its expansion, as a major driver. It also listed unstable prices, weak procurement and rising input costs.
52.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated cause.

52.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the debt cycle faced by distressed farmers?
o: Borrowing → high input cost → asset sale → crop failure → fresh borrowing
High input cost → borrowing → crop failure or low price → inability to repay → fresh borrowing → asset sale → debt trap
Crop failure → institutional credit → higher income → asset purchase → debt repayment
Low input cost → borrowing → assured procurement → inability to repay → debt trap
52.x: The stated cycle begins with high input costs, leads to borrowing, crop failure or low prices, non-repayment, fresh borrowing and asset sales, ultimately producing a debt trap.
52.tq: Arrange the stages by cause and consequence, beginning with the initial financial pressure.

52.s: Which one of the following statements best describes tenancy-related agrarian distress in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Tenants pay rent and carry the production risk, often without a passbook, KCC or insurance.
Tenants generally have lower debt than landowners because rent is waived during crop failure.
Tenants receive guaranteed procurement and bear no production risk.
Tenants depend exclusively on institutional credit.
52.x: Tenant farmers pay rent and bear the production risk, while often lacking land passbooks, Kisan Credit Cards and insurance coverage.
52.tq: Match the institutional disadvantages and risk burden with the correct category of farmer.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about agrarian distress in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Tenants carry higher debt than owners, according to a NABARD Guntur study.
2. About 50% of AP farmers rely on non-institutional credit.
3. A shift towards risky cash crops is one of the identified drivers.
4. Delayed procurement can aggravate distress.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements are correct. AP-specific distress is associated with higher tenant debt, non-institutional borrowing, risky cash crops and delayed procurement.
52.tq: Combine several state-specific facts while checking that none has been reversed.

52.s: Which of the following is regarded as the effective reason for slow agricultural development in the UPPSC 2016 formulation?
52.x: The UPPSC 2016 key identified rural poverty as the effective reason for slow agricultural development.
52.tq: Use the precise causal formulation rather than selecting a broader agricultural constraint.

52.s: The Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008, was announced as part of which Union Budget?
52.x: The Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2008–09.
52.tq: Distinguish the announcement year from adjacent budget years.

52.s: Under the Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008, which relief was available to other farmers who were not small or marginal farmers?
o: 50% relief on payment of the remaining 50%
25% one-time settlement relief on payment of the remaining 75%
52.x: Other farmers received 25% one-time-settlement relief after paying the remaining 75% of the eligible amount.
52.tq: Focus on the conditional structure of the relief instead of the full waiver applicable to small and marginal farmers.

52.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relief under the Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008?
o: Small and marginal farmers received a full waiver of eligible overdue loans.
All farmers received a full waiver, irrespective of category.
Small and marginal farmers received only 25% relief after paying 75%.
Only informal moneylender loans were waived.
52.x: The scheme provided a full waiver of eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers. The 25% one-time settlement applied to other farmers subject to payment of the remaining 75%.
52.tq: Separate the treatment of small and marginal farmers from that of other farmers.

52.s: The approximate total outlay associated with the Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008, was:
52.x: The scheme involved an amount of approximately ₹52,000 crore.
52.tq: Recall the large aggregate figure and distinguish it from the individual AP family ceiling.

52.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scheme or programme)
a. ADWDRS 2008
b. AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014
c. Telangana crop-loan waiver

d. AP horticulture relief

List-II (Feature)
i. Crop-loan waiver for more than 25 lakh families
ii. Full waiver for eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers
iii. Relief of ₹10,000 per acre subject to a family maximum
iv. Crop and crop-purpose gold loans up to 31 December 2013

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
52.x: ADWDRS provided full waiver to eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers; the AP scheme covered specified loans up to 31 December 2013; Telangana waived crop loans for more than 25 lakh families; horticulture relief was ₹10,000 per acre subject to a family ceiling.
52.tq: Start with the sure pair linking Telangana with more than 25 lakh families, then complete the remaining matches.

52.s: Under the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014, the ceiling of relief was:
52.x: The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014, prescribed a ceiling of ₹1.5 lakh per family.
52.tq: Distinguish the general family ceiling from the separate horticulture ceiling.

52.s: Which body implemented the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014?
52.x: The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme was implemented through Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.
52.tq: Apply the ‘which body implemented it?’ trap by distinguishing the implementing agency from financial institutions.

52.s: Under the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014, horticultural relief was fixed at:
o: ₹15,000 per acre, subject to ₹75,000 per family
₹5,000 per acre, subject to ₹25,000 per family
₹20,000 per acre, subject to ₹1 lakh per family
₹10,000 per acre, subject to ₹50,000 per family
52.x: Horticultural relief was ₹10,000 per acre, subject to a maximum of ₹50,000 per family.
52.tq: Keep the per-acre amount separate from the maximum amount per family.

52.s: Which of the following is NOT a commonly cited criticism of agricultural loan waivers?
o: They cover all informal loans and tenants comprehensively.
They do not by themselves raise farm income.
52.x: Loan waivers generally exclude informal loans and tenants; they do not comprehensively cover them. Moral hazard, weaker credit discipline and failure to raise farm income are recognised criticisms.
52.tq: Identify the statement that contradicts the stated limitation of waivers.

52.s:
Assertion (A): Debt prevention is considered more important than repeated loan waivers for addressing agrarian distress.
Reason (R): Loan waivers may create moral hazard, weaken credit discipline and do not necessarily increase farm income.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
52.x: Both the assertion and reason are true. The limitations of repeated waivers explain why preventing the accumulation of farm debt is considered more important.
52.tq: Test whether the stated drawbacks provide the logical reason for preferring debt prevention.

52.s: A policy that repeatedly cancels formal agricultural loans but leaves tenant farmers and moneylender debts outside its coverage is most vulnerable to which criticism?
o: It removes the need for institutional credit.
It automatically raises farm incomes through better prices.
It eliminates all forms of rural indebtedness.
It excludes informal loans and tenants while potentially weakening credit discipline.
52.x: Loan waivers can exclude tenants and informal loans, and repeated waivers may weaken repayment and credit discipline. They do not automatically raise farm incomes or eliminate indebtedness.
52.tq: Apply the critique of waivers to a concrete policy situation involving excluded borrowers.

52.s:
The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), introduced in 2016, replaced which of the following schemes?
1. National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS)
2. Modified National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (MNAIS)
3. Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (WBCIS)
4. National Crop Insurance Programme (NCIP)
52.x: PMFBY, introduced in 2016, replaced NAIS of 1999 and MNAIS of 2010. WBCIS was not one of the two schemes replaced by PMFBY.
52.tq: Use the replacement-year and scheme-name trap to distinguish predecessor schemes from related insurance schemes.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the principle associated with PMFBY?
o: One Nation, One Farmer, One Subsidy
One District, One Crop, One Insurance
One State, One Crop, One Premium
One Nation, One Crop, One Premium
52.x: The principle associated with PMFBY is ‘One Nation, One Crop, One Premium’.
52.tq: Test the exact official slogan rather than a similar-looking administrative phrase.

52.s: Under PMFBY, the maximum farmer premium for Kharif food and oilseed crops is:
52.x: The maximum farmer premium for Kharif food and oilseed crops under PMFBY is 2%.
52.tq: Separate the Kharif premium rate from the Rabi and commercial-crop rates.

52.s: For Rabi food and oilseed crops insured under PMFBY, the maximum farmer premium is:
52.x: The maximum farmer premium for Rabi food and oilseed crops is 1.5%.
52.tq: Use the crop-season comparison to avoid interchanging the Kharif and Rabi rates.

52.s: The maximum farmer premium prescribed under PMFBY for annual commercial and horticultural crops is:
52.x: The maximum farmer premium for annual commercial and horticultural crops is 5%.
52.tq: Compare the highest premium category with the food-and-oilseed categories.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PMFBY:
1. It became voluntary for all farmers from 2020.
2. It covers losses from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages.
3. It covers certain localised calamities.
4. It is a Central Sector Scheme in which the Centre’s premium subsidy goes directly to insurers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements are correct. PMFBY became voluntary in 2020, covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses and localised calamities, and is a Central Sector Scheme with the Centre’s premium subsidy transferred directly to insurers.
52.tq: Check each statement against the scheme’s status, coverage period, risk coverage and funding structure.

52.s:
Which of the following technologies is correctly matched with its function under PMFBY?
1. YES-TECH — remote-sensing-based yield estimation
2. WINDS — weather stations
3. DigiClaim — digital claims processing
4. RWBCIS — land-record digitisation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
52.x: YES-TECH is associated with remote-sensing yield estimation, WINDS with weather stations, and DigiClaim with digital claims processing. RWBCIS is weather-index insurance, not land-record digitisation.
52.tq: Match each technology with its operational function and reject the unrelated land-record option.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the basis of payout under the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS)?
o: Payout is based exclusively on the farmer’s landholding size.
Payout is made when observed weather deviates from specified trigger levels.
Payout is determined by the number of agricultural labourers in the village.
Payout is linked only to the market price of the harvested crop.
52.x: RWBCIS is a weather-index insurance scheme. It pays when weather conditions deviate from predetermined trigger levels.
52.tq: Distinguish weather-index insurance from yield-based, price-based and landholding-based compensation.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about crop insurance in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The earlier free crop insurance model operated during 2019–2024, with the State paying the farmer’s share.
2. Voluntary enrolment was reintroduced from Rabi 2024–25.
3. Under the reintroduced arrangement, farmers pay a nominal share of the actuarial premium.
4. The remaining premium is shared equally by the Centre and the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh earlier paid the farmer’s share from 2019 to 2024 and reintroduced voluntary enrolment from Rabi 2024–25 with the stated sharing arrangement.
52.tq: Trace the change from the earlier free-insurance model to the voluntary enrolment model.

52.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly presents the reported AP crop-insurance coverage figures?
1. 2024: 34.93 lakh farmers and 28.67 lakh hectares
2. 2025–26: 10.63 lakh farmers and 11.81 lakh hectares
Select the correct answer.
52.x: Both figures are correct: coverage was 34.93 lakh farmers over 28.67 lakh hectares in 2024, followed by 10.63 lakh farmers over 11.81 lakh hectares in the 2025–26 data.
52.tq: Keep the two time-separated farmer and area figures together instead of mixing the years.

52.s: According to the reported PMFBY scale, the number of farmers insured in 2024–25 was approximately:
52.x: PMFBY insured approximately 4.19 crore farmers in 2024–25.
52.tq: Identify the exact crore figure and reject distractors formed by changing the leading digit.

52.s: Over nine years of PMFBY implementation, claims amounted to approximately ₹1.82 lakh crore, while farmers’ premium amounted to approximately:
52.x: Farmers’ premium over the period was approximately ₹35,864 crore, against claims of about ₹1.82 lakh crore.
52.tq: Read the paired claim-and-premium figures carefully rather than confusing the two magnitudes.

52.s: The Krishi Rakshak helpline associated with crop insurance is available through which number?
52.x: The Krishi Rakshak helpline number is 14447.
52.tq: Test the exact helpline number using close numerical distractors.

52.s:
Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
1. PMFBY — yield and crop-loss insurance
2. RWBCIS — weather-index insurance
3. PMFBY — payment only after post-harvest losses
4. AP crop insurance — voluntary enrolment from Rabi 2024–25
52.x: Statement 3 is incorrect. PMFBY covers the period from pre-sowing to post-harvest, not only post-harvest losses; the other statements are correctly matched.
52.tq: Find the statement that narrows a broad scheme coverage into an exclusive condition.

52.s: In the NABARD-supported Guntur study of 2023, what percentage of farmers were reported to be in debt?
52.x: The study reported that 88% of the farmers were in debt.
52.tq: Use the exact survey percentage and distinguish it from nearby percentage distractors.

52.s: According to the Guntur study, the average debt of tenant farmers was approximately:
52.x: The average debt of tenant farmers was reported as ₹2,07,444.
52.tq: Compare tenant and owner debt figures without reversing their digits or categories.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the average debt of tenant and owner farmers in the Guntur study?
52.x: Tenant farmers had an average debt of ₹2,07,444, whereas owner farmers had an average debt of ₹76,306.
52.tq: Apply the reversed-comparison trap to the two category-wise debt figures.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding informal agricultural credit in the Guntur study:
1. Informal sources accounted for 51.5% of loans.
2. Approximately 60% of tenants’ loans came from informal sources.
3. Formal lenders charged 25–100% interest in the study.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Formal lenders charged 2.5–10%, not 25–100%, so statement 3 is false.
52.tq: Test the informal-share figures while using a misplaced decimal-range trap for formal interest rates.

52.s: The microfinance guard-rails referred to in the economic survey provide for which combination?
o: A maximum of two lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹1 lakh
A maximum of five lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹2 lakh
A maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹2 lakh
A maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹5 lakh
52.x: The guard-rails prescribe a maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household borrowing cap of ₹2 lakh.
52.tq: Pair the lender-count ceiling with the household monetary ceiling.

52.s: The Andhra Pradesh Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act was enacted in:
52.x: Andhra Pradesh enacted the Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act in 2011, following the 2010 microfinance crisis.
52.tq: Distinguish the year of the crisis from the year of the regulatory legislation.

52.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major criticism of farm-loan waivers?
o: They may exclude informal and tenant borrowers.
They permanently eliminate the structural causes of agrarian distress.
They may provide immediate relief to borrowers.
They may create moral hazard affecting credit discipline.
52.x: Loan waivers provide immediate relief but do not permanently eliminate structural causes of agrarian distress. Exclusion of informal and tenant borrowers and moral hazard are recognised concerns.
52.tq: Select the option that reverses the stated limitation of loan waivers.

52.s:
Assertion (A): Repeated loan waivers can weaken credit culture.
Reason (R): Borrowers may expect future political waivers and consequently have weaker incentives to repay loans.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
52.x: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the expectation of future waivers explains why repeated waivers can weaken repayment discipline and credit culture.
52.tq: Link the moral-hazard mechanism directly to the effect on repayment behaviour.

52.s:
Which of the following consequences was associated with the bank-nationalisation era in the discussion on loan waivers?
1. Politicisation of loan waivers
2. Poor loan recovery
3. Increase in non-performing assets
4. Complete elimination of fiscal stress on States
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
52.x: Politicised waivers, poor recovery and NPAs were associated with the bank-nationalisation era. Loan waivers do not eliminate fiscal stress on States, making statement 4 false.
52.tq: Identify the three linked adverse outcomes and reject the absolute fiscal claim.

52.s: Which principle best reflects the recommended approach to agricultural indebtedness?
o: Debt prevention is more important than repeated waivers.
Fiscal costs should be disregarded when granting waivers.
Repeated debt waivers are more important than preventive measures.
Informal borrowing should replace formal agricultural credit.
52.x: The stated principle is that preventing the accumulation of unsustainable debt is more important than relying on repeated loan waivers.
52.tq: Apply the policy principle to distinguish prevention from repeated post-crisis relief.

52.s: Who chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007?
52.x: R. Radhakrishna chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007.
52.tq: Use the chairperson-name association rather than substituting a familiar agriculture or economic expert.

52.s: According to the NSS 77th Round findings, which statement is correct regarding indebtedness among agricultural households in the major States?
o: Andhra Pradesh ranked first with 93.2%, while Telangana ranked second with 91.7%.
Telangana ranked first with 93.2%, while Andhra Pradesh ranked second with 91.7%.
Andhra Pradesh ranked first with 91.7%, while Telangana ranked second with 93.2%.
Both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana recorded 93.2%.
52.x: Andhra Pradesh had the highest proportion among major States at 93.2%, followed by Telangana at 91.7%.
52.tq: Keep the state ranking and percentages together to avoid reversing the two neighbouring entries.

52.s: The number of operative Kisan Credit Cards (KCCs) in March 2025 was approximately:
52.x: There were approximately 7.72 crore operative KCCs in March 2025.
52.tq: Identify the exact crore figure associated with the March 2025 reference date.

52.s: The KCC coverage gap is highlighted by comparing 7.72 crore operative KCCs with approximately how many agricultural holdings?
52.x: The comparison is between 7.72 crore operative KCCs and 146 million agricultural holdings recorded in the 2015–16 Agricultural Census.
52.tq: Convert neither figure mentally into a different unit before making the coverage comparison.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS):
1. It benefits approximately 5.9 crore farmers.
2. The Central region has 30% of Gross Cropped Area.
3. The Central region receives 30% of MISS benefits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Central region has 14.7%, not 30%, of MISS benefits, so statement 3 is false.
52.tq: Compare the two different regional percentages instead of assuming that area share equals benefit share.

52.s: Which category of farmers is LEAST likely to be excluded from formal agricultural credit on account of the land-record requirement?
o: Farmers whose land ownership is recorded in official land records
Women farmers without documented land rights
52.x: Formal credit commonly requires land records, so farmers with officially recorded land ownership are less affected by this particular exclusion than tenants, oral lessees and farmers without documented land rights.
52.tq: Apply the land-record condition to identify which borrower satisfies the formal-credit requirement.

52.s:
Which of the following groups are specifically identified as facing exclusion from formal agricultural credit because land records are required?
1. Tenant farmers
2. Tribal farmers
3. Women farmers
4. Oral-lessee farmers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
52.x: All four groups are identified as vulnerable to exclusion from formal agricultural credit where land records are required.
52.tq: Check the complete beneficiary-exclusion list before selecting a partial combination.

52.s: PM-KISAN is classified as which of the following?
o: A Central Sector Scheme introduced in February 2019
A State Sector Scheme introduced in February 2020
A Centrally Sponsored Scheme introduced in 2016
A statutory pension scheme introduced in 2019
52.x: PM-KISAN has been a Central Sector Scheme since February 2019.
52.tq: Identify the scheme’s exact administrative classification and launch period.

52.s: Under PM-KISAN, the annual assistance and instalment structure are respectively:
o: ₹6,000 annually in three instalments of ₹2,000 each
₹12,000 annually in three instalments of ₹4,000 each
₹6,000 annually in two instalments of ₹3,000 each
₹20,000 annually in four instalments of ₹5,000 each
52.x: PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year through three instalments of ₹2,000 each.
52.tq: Split the total amount from the instalment amount and count.

52.s: Which one of the following is a specified delivery feature of PM-KISAN assistance?
o: Payment into non-linked cash accounts through cooperative societies
52.x: The PM-KISAN instalments are paid into Aadhaar-seeded accounts.
52.tq: Recognise the precise delivery mechanism rather than a nearby institutional alternative.

52.s: As indicated in the Economic Survey 2025-26, the amount released under PM-KISAN so far is approximately:
52.x: The amount released under PM-KISAN so far is reported as ₹4.09 lakh crore.
52.tq: Distinguish the scheme-wide cumulative figure from other agricultural credit figures.

52.s: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana is primarily associated with:
o: Life insurance for agricultural labourers only
52.x: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana is a pension scheme for small farmers.
52.tq: Use the scheme-purpose match to separate pension support from income support and insurance.

52.s: How many farmers had enrolled in PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana as reported in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
52.x: The reported enrolment in PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana was 24.92 lakh farmers.
52.tq: Compare similarly expressed lakh figures and select the scheme-specific enrolment.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Annadata Sukhibhava in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It tops up PM-KISAN assistance.
2. Its first Kharif 2026 instalment was ₹7,000 per farmer.
3. The first instalment involved ₹3,125 crore for 46.85 lakh farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct. Annadata Sukhibhava tops up PM-KISAN, and its Kharif 2026 first instalment was ₹7,000 per farmer, involving ₹3,125 crore for 46.85 lakh farmers.
52.tq: Check each statement against the scheme’s purpose, instalment amount and beneficiary figures.

52.s: The earlier Annadata Sukhibhava assistance reported for Andhra Pradesh was:
o: ₹6,309 crore to 46.86 lakh families over two instalments
₹3,125 crore to 46.85 lakh farmers over three instalments
₹20,000 crore to 24.92 lakh farmers over four instalments
₹7,000 crore to 46.86 lakh families over two instalments
52.x: The earlier reported assistance was ₹6,309 crore to 46.86 lakh families over two instalments.
52.tq: Match the amount, beneficiary unit and instalment count as a single numerical combination.

52.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (State scheme)
a. Annadata Sukhibhava
b. KALIA
c. Rythu Bandhu
List-II (State)
i. Telangana
ii. Odisha
iii. Andhra Pradesh

Select the correct answer using the code below:
52.x: Annadata Sukhibhava belongs to Andhra Pradesh, KALIA to Odisha and Rythu Bandhu to Telangana.
52.tq: Start from the sure state-scheme pair and eliminate codes with a misplaced scheme.

52.s: KALIA is described as a scheme providing:
o: Crop insurance and pension support in Andhra Pradesh
Life cover and loan waiver in Telangana
Livelihood and income support in Odisha
52.x: KALIA is an Odisha scheme associated with livelihood and income support.
52.tq: Use the scheme-objective and State combination rather than a generic agriculture association.

52.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported features of Rythu Bandhu, later referred to as Rythu Bharosa?
o: Assistance was fixed at ₹6,000 per farmer, with no insurance component.
It provides ₹7,000 per farmer as the first Kharif 2026 instalment in Andhra Pradesh.
It provides only pension support to small farmers in Odisha.
Assistance was raised to ₹12,000 per acre, along with a crop loan waiver for more than 25 lakh families and Rythu Bima life cover.
52.x: Rythu Bandhu, later referred to as Rythu Bharosa, was reported with ₹12,000 per acre assistance, a crop loan waiver for more than 25 lakh families and Rythu Bima life cover.
52.tq: Separate a multi-feature State scheme from the similarly named schemes of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

52.s: The claims under Rythu Bima life cover were reported at approximately:
52.x: Claims under Rythu Bima life cover were reported at ₹8,003.40 crore.
52.tq: Distinguish the insurance-claims figure from scheme assistance and loan-waiver figures.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural credit support in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Annual Credit Plan achieved 97 percent.
2. The amount associated with the achieved plan was ₹2,96,764 crore.
3. Crop Cultivator Rights Cards enabled tenant farmers to obtain loans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct. The Annual Credit Plan achieved 97 percent with ₹2,96,764 crore, while CCRCs enabled tenant farmers to access credit.
52.tq: Test the percentage, amount and institutional mechanism together without reversing their relationships.

52.s: Which combination correctly represents the reported CCRC-based credit support in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 24.92 lakh CCRCs and ₹8,003.40 crore in loans
93.2 lakh CCRCs and ₹2,96,764 crore in loans
8.24 lakh CCRCs and ₹3,768 crore in loans
46.85 lakh CCRCs and ₹3,125 crore in loans
52.x: A total of 8.24 lakh CCRCs enabled ₹3,768 crore in loans for tenant farmers.
52.tq: Pair the card count with the credit amount before considering the distractor figures.

52.s: During the 1990s protests concerning the WTO, GATT and the Dunkel Draft, which of the following positions was correctly associated with the named leaders?
o: Mahendra Singh Tikait supported globalisation, whereas Sharad Joshi opposed it.
Sharad Joshi opposed globalisation, whereas Nanjundaswamy supported it.
All three leaders supported the Dunkel Draft without reservation.
Sharad Joshi supported globalisation, whereas Nanjundaswamy and Mahendra Singh Tikait opposed it.
52.x: Sharad Joshi of Shetkari Sangathan supported globalisation, while Nanjundaswamy of KRRS and Mahendra Singh Tikait of BKU opposed it.
52.tq: Discriminate between closely associated leaders by matching each person with the correct position.

52.s:
Match the following leaders with their organisations:
List-I
 a. Sharad Joshi
 b. Nanjundaswamy
 c. Mahendra Singh Tikait

List-II
 i. BKU
 ii. Shetkari Sangathan
 iii. KRRS

Select the correct answer using the code below:
52.x: Sharad Joshi was associated with Shetkari Sangathan, Nanjundaswamy with KRRS and Mahendra Singh Tikait with BKU.
52.tq: Start from the organisation most directly associated with each leader and eliminate swapped pairs.

52.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the farmers’ protests at Delhi borders during 2020-21?
o: Replacement of the three farm laws with a new national crop insurance law
Withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance
Repeal of the three farm laws
52.x: The listed demands were repeal of the three farm laws, legal MSP, and withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance. Replacement with a new crop insurance law was not among the stated demands.
52.tq: Find the one demand outside the established three-part demand set.

52.s: What was the principal legislative outcome of the 2020-21 farmers’ protests at the Delhi borders?
o: The Dunkel Draft was withdrawn by the WTO in 2021
The three farm laws were repealed in 2021
The Electricity (Amendment) Bill was enacted in 2021
The three farm laws were constitutionally entrenched in 2021
52.x: The three farm laws were repealed in 2021.
52.tq: Link the protest episode to its stated outcome while rejecting nearby policy events.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the SKM protests in 2026:
1. The SKM represented about 500 farm unions.
2. Village protests were held from 27 to 31 May.
3. Copies of the Kharif MSP order were burnt during the protests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct: the SKM, comprising about 500 farm unions, held village protests from 27 to 31 May 2026 and burnt copies of the Kharif MSP order.
52.tq: Verify the organisation, date range and action separately before selecting the coded combination.

52.s: The statewide protests by Andhra Pradesh farm bodies from 30 March 2026 primarily demanded:
o: A legal guarantee for export subsidies
52.x: Andhra Pradesh farm bodies held statewide protests demanding MSP procurement.
52.tq: Identify the precise demand rather than a broader or unrelated agricultural reform.

52.s: Which one of the following correctly states the contrast concerning farmer suicides reported in Andhra Pradesh since 2024?
o: 112 suicides were reported, of which more than 300 were recognised.
All reported suicides were recognised after a statewide audit.
The Tenant Farmers' Association reported no suicides since 2024.
More than 300 suicides were reported by the Tenant Farmers' Association, but only 112 were recognised.
52.x: The Tenant Farmers' Association reported more than 300 farmer suicides since 2024, while only 112 were recognised.
52.tq: Preserve the direction of the reported-versus-recognised comparison.

52.s: In response to concerns regarding farmer suicides, the Chief Minister ordered:
o: A ban on crop insurance premiums
An audit of every farmer suicide
A review of the WTO Dunkel Draft
A waiver of every agricultural loan
52.x: The Chief Minister ordered an audit of every farmer suicide.
52.tq: Match the stated administrative response with the issue that triggered it.

52.s: Why can actual cultivators be deprived of insurance and relief during a rainfall-deficit season?
o: Because they are missing from e-crop data
Because MSP procurement excludes all tenant farmers by definition
Because PM-KISAN is limited to urban households
Because CCRCs automatically cancel crop insurance
52.x: Actual cultivators missing from e-crop data can lose access to insurance and relief.
52.tq: Apply the record-visibility problem to the stated consequence for cultivators.

52.s: Farmers’ groups opposing the premium-sharing arrangement under the 2026-27 guidelines demanded:
o: Free crop insurance through public insurers only
Insurance limited to landowners and not cultivators
Private insurers only with higher premiums
52.x: The groups demanded free crop insurance and public insurers only, opposing the premium share under the 2026-27 guidelines.
52.tq: Distinguish the demand for public provision from the existing premium-sharing arrangement.

52.s: Which of the following best describes the reported AP position regarding indebtedness and Annadata Sukhibhava?
o: 93.2 percent of agricultural households were indebted, and Annadata Sukhibhava provided ₹20,000 per year including ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN, with tenants included.
