63.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after checking each policy emphasis separately.

63.s: District Industries Centres (DICs), created under the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977, were intended primarily to:
o: Provide one-roof support to small and cottage industries in every district
Issue licences exclusively to public-sector undertakings
Regulate the expansion of large industrial houses
63.x: DICs were established in every district to provide integrated support to small and cottage industries under one roof.
63.tq: Ask which institution would perform the described decentralised support function.

63.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the support functions associated with District Industries Centres?
63.x: DICs supported credit, raw materials, machinery and marketing for small and cottage industries; monetary policy was not their function.
63.tq: Find the institutionally unrelated function among closely related support services.

63.s: The Industrial Policy Statement of 1977 sought to curb large industrial houses mainly through:
63.x: The policy used the MRTP and FERA frameworks to curb the influence of large industrial houses.
63.tq: Match the policy objective with the two relevant regulatory instruments.

63.s: Which pair of companies is associated with exiting India in the context of the restrictive measures under the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977?
63.x: IBM and Coca-Cola exited India in the context of the restrictions associated with MRTP and FERA.
63.tq: Use a name-pair recall question based on the policy consequence.

63.s:
The Industrial Policy Statement of 1973 is associated with which of the following developments?
1. Identification of a core-sector list
2. Tightening of the MRTP framework
3. Creation of District Industries Centres
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The 1973 Statement identified a core-sector list and tightened MRTP. District Industries Centres were created under the 1977 policy.
63.tq: Separate similar industrial-policy years before selecting the coded combination.

63.s:
Arrange the following developments concerning the industrial policy institution in chronological order:
A. Department of Industry was set up under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
B. Department of Industrial Development was renamed as DIPP.
C. DIPP was created as a separate department.
D. Department of Industrial Development was merged with DIPP.
Select the correct sequence.
63.x: The sequence is 1961 Department of Industry, 1967 Department of Industrial Development, 1995 creation of DIPP, and 2000 merger into DIPP.
63.tq: Use the first and last dates, then place the intermediate institutional changes.

63.s: The Department of Industrial Development was renamed as the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion in:
63.x: DIPP was created as a separate department in 1995 after the earlier Department of Industrial Development had been renamed in 1967.
63.tq: Distinguish the year of institutional creation from the years of renaming and merger.

63.s: In 2000, which institutional change took place?
o: The Department of Industry was created under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Logistics development was allotted to DPIIT.
The Department of Industrial Development was merged with DIPP.
63.x: In 2000, the Department of Industrial Development was merged with DIPP.
63.tq: Match a specific year with the exact administrative change.

63.s: DIPP was renamed as the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in:
63.x: In 2019, DIPP was renamed DPIIT and internal trade, traders’ welfare and Startups were added to its responsibilities.
63.tq: Use the exact year of renaming rather than the year of a later mandate change.

63.s: Which one of the following was added to the responsibilities of DPIIT after its renaming?
63.x: The renamed DPIIT received responsibilities relating to internal trade, traders’ welfare and Startups.
63.tq: Identify the new administrative function while rejecting functions of other policy domains.

63.s: In November 2021, which mandate was allotted to DPIIT?
63.x: Integrated development of logistics was allotted to DPIIT in November 2021.
63.tq: Link the latest dated institutional change with its precise mandate.

63.s:
Which of the following is included in the mandate of DPIIT?
1. Promotion of Startups
2. Formulation of FDI policy
3. Intellectual property rights relating to patents, trademarks, designs and geographical indications
4. Promotion of industrial corridors
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: DPIIT’s mandate includes Startups, FDI policy, industrial corridors and IPR matters relating to patents, trademarks, designs and geographical indications, along with Make in India, PLI, PM GatiShakti NMP and ease of doing business.
63.tq: Check whether each listed function belongs to the broad industrial-promotion mandate.

63.s: Which of the following was a major effect of the 1991 industrial reforms?
o: Replacement of private industry by exclusive state ownership
Continuation of all expansion limits and price controls
Removal of licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions
63.x: The 1991 reforms ended the licence-permit-quota raj by removing industrial licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions.
63.tq: Identify the option that correctly combines the reform measures without reversing their direction.

63.s: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 was issued through which Government Order and on what date?
63.x: AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 was issued as G.O. Ms. No. 68 on 26 October 2024.
63.tq: Combine the government-order number and date to discriminate between closely related policy documents.

63.s: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 is valid for:
o: Three years or till a new policy is issued
Four years irrespective of any successor policy
Five years or till a new policy is issued
63.x: The policy is valid for five years or until a new policy is issued, whichever occurs earlier.
63.tq: Test the validity period together with its stated exception.

63.s: The earlier Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 2020-23 was replaced by:
63.x: The AP Industrial Development Policy 2020-23 was replaced by the Policy 4.0 suite.
63.tq: Distinguish the successor AP policy suite from national industrial policies.

63.s: Which of the following is NOT a target of Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0?
63.x: The targets include ₹30 lakh crore investment, USD 10 billion FDI and five lakh manufacturing jobs; USD 100 billion FDI is not specified.
63.tq: Spot the altered magnitude in a set of policy targets.

63.s: Under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0, the export target is intended to increase from:
63.x: The policy target is to increase exports from USD 20 billion to USD 40 billion.
63.tq: Test both ends of a policy target range rather than only one figure.

63.s: The target relating to industrial parks under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 is:
63.x: The policy aims to establish more than 175 industrial parks.
63.tq: Use an ascending numerical option set to identify the stated threshold.

63.s: Which of the following is classified as a propelling sector under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0?
63.x: Semiconductors and electronics are included among the propelling sectors. Automobiles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and textiles are listed as sustenance sectors.
63.tq: Separate the two policy categories by identifying a member of the propelling group.

63.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Automobiles — Sustenance sector
2. Green energy — Propelling sector
3. Textiles — Propelling sector
4. Aerospace and defence — Propelling sector
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
63.x: Automobiles are a sustenance sector, while green energy and aerospace-defence are propelling sectors. Textiles are a sustenance sector, so pair 3 is incorrect.
63.tq: Use category reversal as the trap in a comparison-based matching question.

63.s: Under the bands mentioned for the 2025-26 sectoral framework, a Mega project involves investment of:
o: More than ₹125 crore but up to ₹500 crore
63.x: A Mega project is defined in the ₹1,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore band. Sub-Large, Large and Ultra Mega occupy the other stated bands.
63.tq: Distinguish adjacent investment bands by their lower and upper limits.

63.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Early Bird incentive under the Andhra Pradesh industrial policy framework?
o: 30% FCI subsidy for the first 200 projects with CFE in 18 months
40% FCI subsidy for the first 100 projects with CFE in 12 months
40% FCI subsidy for every project irrespective of its sector
30% FCI subsidy for all projects with CFE in 24 months
63.x: The Early Bird provision offers a 30% FCI subsidy for the first 200 projects, with CFE in 18 months. PLI-sector projects can receive 40% with a 24-month period.
63.tq: Check the project count, subsidy rate and time limit together.

63.s: For projects belonging to PLI sectors, the Early Bird subsidy and CFE period are respectively:
63.x: PLI-sector projects are eligible for a 40% FCI subsidy with CFE within 24 months.
63.tq: Discriminate the special PLI-sector incentive from the general Early Bird provision.

63.s: Which authority chairs the State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) in Andhra Pradesh?
63.x: The SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister, while the SIPC is associated with the Chief Secretary.
63.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the two approval bodies.

63.s:
The MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 includes which of the following provisions?
1. ‘One Family One Entrepreneur’ by 2030
2. 175 MSME parks
3. Capital subsidy of 25%, rising to 45% for special categories
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: All three provisions form part of the MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 for 2024-29.
63.tq: Verify the policy slogan, numerical target and differentiated subsidy before choosing the combined code.

63.s: The target of the Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 includes:
o: Plug-and-play clusters, five lakh jobs and USD 10 billion investment
Only waste-recycling facilities and green-energy parks
63.x: The Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 focuses on plug-and-play clusters and targets five lakh jobs and USD 10 billion investment.
63.tq: Match a sector policy with its specific infrastructure and numerical targets.

63.s: Which policy is concerned with developing a component ecosystem in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025-30
63.x: The Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy 2025 is intended to develop a component ecosystem.
63.tq: Match the policy name with its narrowly defined sectoral objective.

63.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the remaining policies in the Andhra Pradesh Policy 4.0 suite?
o: Food Processing, Private Parks and EV 4.0; Aerospace and Defence and Space 4.0
Food Security, Monetary Policy and Space 4.0
EV 4.0, Banking Policy and Logistics Policy
Private Parks, MRTP Policy and FERA Policy
63.x: The suite includes Food Processing, Private Parks and EV 4.0 for 2024-29, and Aerospace and Defence and Space 4.0 for 2025-30.
63.tq: Start from the sure policy-sector pair and reject combinations containing unrelated national instruments.

63.s: The Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025-30 is associated with which Government Order?
63.x: The guidelines for the Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025-30 were issued through G.O. Ms. No. 26 on 6 February 2026.
63.tq: Distinguish government orders by both number and date.

63.s: The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 was introduced by which government and was based on which earlier resolution?
o: United Front Government; New Industrial Policy 1991
63.x: The 1980 policy was introduced by the Congress Government and was based on the 1956 Resolution with modifications.
63.tq: Match the policy year with both its political authority and institutional base.

63.s: Which of the following was a major focus of the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980?
o: Reintroduction of import and export restrictions
Exclusive promotion of cottage industries without modernisation
Complete withdrawal of the state from industry
63.x: The 1980 policy emphasised technological upgradation, modernisation and export orientation, with export orientation receiving strong emphasis for the first time.
63.tq: Identify the positive policy objectives while rejecting reversals of the reform direction.

63.s: The concept of ‘economic federalism’ in the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 involved:
o: Centralisation of all industrial approvals in metropolitan cities
Incentives for backward districts, including tax holidays and cheap credit
Uniform industrial incentives for every district
Withdrawal of credit support from backward regions
63.x: Economic federalism meant providing incentives to backward districts, including tax holidays and cheap credit.
63.tq: Translate a policy phrase into its practical regional incentive measures.

63.s: The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 sought to remove the ‘artificial barrier’ between:
63.x: The 1980 policy sought to remove the artificial barrier between large and small industrial units.
63.tq: Test the exact pair of sectors linked by the policy phrase.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980:
1. MRTP firms were permitted to expand capacity up to 25% without fresh approval.
2. Investment limits for small-scale industries were raised.
3. Excess capacity was regularised.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The 1980 policy allowed MRTP firms to expand capacity up to 25% without fresh approval, raised SSI investment limits and regularised excess capacity.
63.tq: Check the three linked relaxation measures before selecting the comprehensive option.

63.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980?
o: MRTP relaxation — complete prohibition on capacity expansion
Economic federalism — incentives for backward districts
63.x: The policy relaxed MRTP restrictions by permitting expansion up to 25% without fresh approval; it did not prohibit capacity expansion.
63.tq: Find the reversed policy effect in a not-correctly-matched question.

63.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, how many industries were reserved for the public sector in Schedule A?
63.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 reserved 17 industries for the public sector under Schedule A.
63.tq: Use the distinctive policy-wise numerical figure and eliminate nearby values.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the industries reserved for the public sector:
1. Eight industries were reserved under the New Industrial Policy, 1991.
2. The number was subsequently reduced to three.
3. After May 2001, only atomic energy and railway operations remained reserved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three statements are correct. The number declined from eight in 1991 to three and ultimately to two after defence was opened to private participation in May 2001.
63.tq: Track the policy sequence from the initial number to the present position.

63.s: Which one of the following was opened to the private sector in May 2001, thereby reducing the industries reserved for the public sector?
63.x: Defence production, including arms and ammunition, was opened to the private sector in May 2001. Atomic energy and railway operations continued in the reserved category.
63.tq: Distinguish the industry removed from the reserved list from those retained.

63.s: Which of the following policy resolutions is associated with the expression ‘Economic Constitution of India’ and ‘Bible of State Capitalism’?
63.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is described as the Economic Constitution of India and the Bible of State Capitalism.
63.tq: Match the distinctive descriptive label with the correct policy resolution.

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1980 — District Industries Centres
Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 — Joint sector concept
Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 — District Industries Centres
63.x: The Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 is associated with the joint sector concept and the core sector list. District Industries Centres were associated with the 1977 policy, while economic federalism was linked with the 1980 policy.
63.tq: Use policy-label association and reject swapped years.

63.s: The beginning of the ‘licence-permit-quota raj’ in India is generally associated with which policy resolution?
63.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is associated with the beginning of the licence-permit-quota raj.
63.tq: Identify the policy linked with the historical label rather than the later reform policy.

63.s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969?
o: To control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
To promote foreign direct investment in high-priority industries
To provide automatic approval for technology agreements
63.x: The MRTP Act, 1969 aimed to control private monopolies and prevent concentration of economic power. Its enactment followed the recommendations associated with the Dutt Committee.
63.tq: Distinguish the objective of the MRTP Act from objectives of later liberalisation measures.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the MRTP framework:
1. The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 and came into force in 1970.
2. The asset threshold for MRTP firms was raised to Rs. 100 crore in 1985.
3. The market-share criterion was reduced from 33 per cent to 25 per cent in 1984.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three statements are correct. The Act was enacted in 1969 and brought into force in 1970; the market-share limit was reduced in 1984 and the asset limit was raised in 1985.
63.tq: Check each date and numerical change independently before selecting the coded combination.

63.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was replaced by which legislation?
63.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act. The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India.
63.tq: Use the enactment-year trap to distinguish the Competition Act from FEMA.

63.s: What was the effect of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 on the MRTP asset threshold of Rs. 100 crore?
o: It made the threshold applicable only to public sector firms
It reduced the threshold to Rs. 50 crore
It doubled the threshold to Rs. 200 crore
It scrapped the threshold for large firms
63.x: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 scrapped the MRTP asset threshold. Large firms no longer required prior approval for expansion, mergers or takeovers merely because of their asset size.
63.tq: Apply the reform measure to the specific regulatory restriction being removed.

63.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Sick Industrial Companies Act
B. MRTP Act
C. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act
D. FERA
63.x: The correct order is Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951; MRTP Act, 1969; FERA, 1973; and Sick Industrial Companies Act, 1985.
63.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest enactments, then place the middle years.

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
63.x: The Sick Industrial Companies Act was enacted in 1985, not 1984. The other three year-pairs are correctly matched.
63.tq: Find the single altered year in an otherwise familiar chronology.

63.s: The R. K. Hazari report of 1967 primarily examined which subject?
63.x: The R. K. Hazari report examined industrial licensing and reported that big business houses had cornered licences.
63.tq: Match the committee or report with its precise policy subject.

63.s: Who chaired the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee which submitted its report in 1969?
63.x: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee was chaired by Subimal Dutt. Its report was submitted in 1969 and contributed to the enactment of the MRTP Act.
63.tq: Separate the report author from the later legislation and its commonly used committee name.

63.s: Item reservation for small-scale industries in India began in which year?
63.x: Item reservation for small-scale industries began in 1967. It continued after 1991, while the last reserved items were dereserved in 2015.
63.tq: Distinguish the origin year from later policy changes affecting SSI reservation.

63.s: Which one of the following statements regarding small-scale industries is correct?
o: The last SSI items were dereserved in 1980.
The 1977 policy defined tiny units and the 1980 policy raised SSI investment limits.
SSI item reservation began only after the New Industrial Policy, 1991.
The 1977 policy abolished tiny units and the 1980 policy ended SSI reservation.
63.x: The 1977 policy introduced the definition of tiny units, while the 1980 policy raised investment limits for small-scale industries. SSI item reservation began in 1967 and the last items were dereserved in 2015.
63.tq: Keep the two closely related policy changes in their correct year-policy combination.

63.s: The New Industrial Policy was announced on which date?
63.x: The New Industrial Policy was announced on 24 July 1991.
63.tq: Discriminate between the exact day-month-year and nearby reform dates.

63.s: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 initially applied to which category?
o: High-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries on the specified list
63.x: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity applied to a specified list of high-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries. It was not available to all industries without restriction.
63.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘all’ and identify the specified sectoral category.

63.s:
Which of the following was permitted under the foreign investment and technology provisions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
1. Automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in high-priority industries
2. Use of foreign brand names and trademarks
3. Establishment of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board to speed approvals
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three measures formed part of the liberalised foreign investment and technology framework associated with the 1991 policy.
63.tq: Test several related liberalisation measures together and use the complete combination only when all are supported.

63.s: Which one of the following statements about the later foreign investment approval framework is correct?
o: FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and approvals are processed through the FIF portal.
FIPB continues to be the sole approval authority for all foreign investment.
The negative-list approach was replaced by a complete prohibition on foreign equity.
63.x: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board was abolished in June 2017, and approvals were shifted to the FIF portal. FDI up to 100 per cent under the automatic route is permitted in most sectors subject to the applicable negative list.
63.tq: Identify the institutional change while rejecting absolute statements about FDI.

63.s: The FIF portal was integrated with the National Single Window System in which month and year?
63.x: The FIF portal was integrated with the National Single Window System in August 2022.
63.tq: Retain the precise month-year associated with the administrative reform.

63.s: How many industries were subject to compulsory industrial licensing in July 1991?
63.x: In July 1991, 18 industries were under compulsory industrial licensing.
63.tq: Distinguish the initial licensing count from the later reduced counts.

63.s: Which group of industries was delicensed in 1993?
o: Electronic aerospace equipment, defence equipment and drugs
63.x: Automobiles, white goods and leather were delicensed in 1993.
63.tq: Match the year of delicensing with the correct group rather than a later residual category.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reduction of compulsory licensing:
1. Electronic goods were delicensed in December 1996.
2. Five more industries were delicensed in July 1997.
3. Coal and petroleum were delicensed under the Budget for 1998–99.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three statements are correct. These successive measures reduced the number of industries under compulsory licensing to six by the 1998–99 Budget stage.
63.tq: Follow the dated stages of deregulation in sequence.

63.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five industries presently identified as remaining under compulsory licensing?
63.x: Drugs and pharmaceuticals were later delicensed. The remaining categories include alcohol, tobacco, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives.
63.tq: Find the item removed from the older six-item list to obtain the current five.

63.s: The term ‘jobless growth’ in the criticism of the post-1991 industrial policy refers to:
o: A decline in capital formation accompanied by higher employment
Growth driven mainly by labour-intensive industries creating extensive employment
Growth driven mainly by capital-intensive industries without proportionate employment generation
Growth restricted exclusively to the public sector
63.x: Jobless growth denotes capital-intensive growth that does not generate employment in proportion to the increase in output.
63.tq: Identify the exact meaning of the distinctive criticism rather than choosing a related growth concept.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional impact of the post-1991 industrial policy:
1. Investment became concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
2. The policy eliminated regional disparities in industrial investment.
3. Regional imbalance was identified as a criticism of the policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Investment became concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, making regional imbalance a criticism. The policy did not eliminate regional disparities.
63.tq: Find the reversed claim in the statement that says the policy eliminated disparities.

63.s: Premature deindustrialisation of small units after 1991 was primarily associated with:
o: Exclusive dependence of small units on government procurement
The abolition of all small-scale industrial units by constitutional amendment
Cheap imports, particularly from China, forcing many small units to close
A complete ban on imports of manufactured goods
63.x: Cheap imports, particularly from China, increased competitive pressure and caused the closure of many small units.
63.tq: Link the criticism with its specific cause and avoid extreme alternatives.

63.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the post-1991 concerns relating to industrial development?
o: Rising import dependence and environmental degradation
Declining consumer choice and complete withdrawal of foreign investment
Falling import dependence and improvement in environmental quality
Reduction in electronics imports and expansion of domestic API production
63.x: Rising import dependence in electronics, solar panels and APIs, along with environmental degradation, were identified as concerns.
63.tq: Match the two related concerns instead of selecting an achievement of liberalisation.

63.s: Which one of the following was NOT a criticism of the 1991 industrial policy?
63.x: Increase in consumer choice was an achievement associated with the post-1991 reforms, not a criticism. The other three were criticisms.
63.tq: Separate achievements from criticisms by locating the positive outcome.

63.s: In 1991, the disinvestment policy provided for disinvestment of what proportion in selected public sector undertakings?
63.x: The 1991 policy provided for 20 per cent disinvestment in selected public sector undertakings.
63.tq: Use the exact percentage and distinguish it from nearby altered figures.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about chronically sick public sector undertakings in the context of the 1991 policy:
1. They were referred to the BIFR.
2. The BIFR was established under the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.
3. The purpose of referral was revival or closure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Chronically sick PSUs were referred to the BIFR, established under SICA, 1985, for possible revival or closure. All three statements are correct.
63.tq: Test the complete institutional chain: referral, law and purpose.

63.s: With reference to the institutional changes concerning BIFR, which of the following is correct?
o: BIFR was converted into a department of the WTO in 2016
SICA was repealed and BIFR was dissolved in 2016, with cases moving under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
SICA and BIFR were strengthened and retained without change after 2016
BIFR was dissolved in 1991 and replaced by SICA in 2016
63.x: SICA was repealed and BIFR was dissolved in 2016; pending cases moved under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
63.tq: Use the chronology and distinguish repeal and dissolution from continuation.

63.s: The rise in India’s GDP growth from the approximate ‘Hindu rate’ to around 7–8 per cent is associated with:
o: The return to a licence-based industrial regime
The complete abolition of foreign trade
The exclusive expansion of traditional agriculture
63.x: Post-1991 reforms are associated with the rise from the approximate 3.5 per cent ‘Hindu rate’ of growth to around 7–8 per cent.
63.tq: Connect the before-and-after growth figures with the reform period.

63.s:
Assertion (A): Mergers and acquisitions became easier after the 1991 reforms.
Reason (R): Prior approval under the MRTP framework for mergers and acquisitions was removed.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
63.x: Both statements are true, and removal of MRTP pre-approval directly made mergers and acquisitions easier.
63.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the liberalisation of mergers and acquisitions.

63.s: According to the stated November 2025 figure, India’s foreign exchange reserves reached an all-time high of:
63.x: The stated all-time high was USD 702.28 billion in November 2025.
63.tq: Distinguish the precise current figure from the earlier approximate USD 600 billion figure.

63.s: Gross inward equity FDI during 2022–23 to 2025–26 was stated to be:
63.x: Gross inward equity FDI during 2022–23 to 2025–26 was stated as USD 317.80 billion.
63.tq: Separate gross inward inflow from repatriation and reserve figures.

63.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent FDI position stated for India?
o: Gross inward equity FDI was USD 702.28 billion and repatriation was nil.
Gross inward equity FDI was USD 178.9 billion and repatriation was USD 317.80 billion.
Gross inward equity FDI was USD 317.80 billion, while repatriation or disinvestment by foreign investors was USD 178.9 billion, leading to falling net FDI.
Both gross inward equity FDI and repatriation were USD 317.80 billion, leaving no net FDI.
63.x: Gross inward equity FDI was USD 317.80 billion, while repatriation or disinvestment was USD 178.9 billion; consequently, net FDI was falling despite high gross inflows.
63.tq: Split the figures into gross inflow, outflow and net impact before choosing.

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding MSMEs after 1991:
1. Removal of protection exposed small units to import competition.
2. Import competition adversely affected many small units.
3. SSI reservation continued after 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Removal of protection and import competition hurt small units, while reservation for SSI continued after 1991. All three statements are correct.
63.tq: Combine the adverse impact with the institutional continuity that remained after reform.

63.s: At the CII Partnership Summit held at Visakhapatnam on 14–15 November 2025, the investment commitment and employment potential were stated as:
63.x: The summit involved commitments of ₹2,80,384 crore and an employment potential of 5,01,746 jobs.
63.tq: Keep the commitment figure and job figure paired with the correct event.

63.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the industrial profile of Andhra Pradesh stated for 2025–26?
o: 3,15,000 operational large and mega units with investment of ₹1,119 crore
1,119 operational large and mega units with investment of ₹3.15 lakh crore
5,01,746 operational large and mega units with investment of ₹2,80,384 crore
1,119 operational large and mega units with investment of ₹2,80,384 crore
63.x: Andhra Pradesh had 1,119 operational large and mega units involving ₹3.15 lakh crore, as stated for 2025–26.
63.tq: Match the count of units with the corresponding investment value.

63.s: The post-1991 concern that growth was capital-intensive and regionally concentrated is sought to be addressed in the current policy context through:
o: PLI and the National Manufacturing Mission
A return to universal industrial licensing
A ban on foreign direct investment
63.x: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and the National Manufacturing Mission are identified as corrective measures for these concerns.
63.tq: Apply the stated policy response to the identified structural criticism.

63.s: The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India was adopted in:
63.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 was the first industrial policy of independent India.
63.tq: Use the FIRST principle to identify the earliest policy resolution.

63.s: The Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion was renamed or designated as DPIIT in:
63.x: The Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion acquired the name Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in 2019.
63.tq: Use the LAST-date cue and distinguish the institutional renaming from policy-launch years.

63.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is significant because it:
o: Established the public-sector-led, licence-based industrial model that continued until 1991
Introduced complete deregulation of all industries
Ended the role of the public sector in basic industries
Restricted industrial development entirely to foreign companies
63.x: The 1956 Resolution shaped a public-sector-led and licence-based industrial model that continued until the 1991 reforms.
63.tq: Identify the defining institutional feature associated with the 1956 Resolution.

63.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the criticism of the licence raj?
o: Removal of all regulatory barriers and complete competition
Automatic entry, low compliance costs and excess scale
Rent-seeking, entry barriers and lack of scale
63.x: The licence raj was criticised for encouraging rent-seeking, creating entry barriers and preventing firms from achieving adequate scale.
63.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of linked criticisms.

63.s: A major significance of the post-1991 reforms was the shift in the role of government from:
63.x: The reforms shifted the government’s role from direct regulation towards facilitation, forming the basis for today’s FDI framework and competition law.
63.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison in the two roles of government.

63.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0:
1. It covers the period 2024–29.
2. It was notified through G.O. Ms. No. 68.
3. The Government Order is dated 26 October 2024.
4. It is among the five Andhra Pradesh policies identified in APSES 2024–25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 covers 2024–29, is associated with G.O. Ms. No. 68 dated 26 October 2024, and is among the five policies identified in APSES 2024–25.
63.tq: Verify each date, order number, period and classification before selecting the coded combination.

63.s: Which of the following correctly captures the relationship between high gross FDI inflows and current FDI concerns?
o: Net FDI may fall even when gross inflows are high if repatriation and disinvestment are substantial.
High gross inflows necessarily imply that net FDI is rising.
Repatriation is counted as additional inward equity FDI.
Net FDI is unaffected by foreign investor repatriation.
63.x: Substantial repatriation or disinvestment can offset gross inward inflows, resulting in falling net FDI despite high gross FDI.
63.tq: Apply the difference between gross inflows and net flows to a current economic situation.

64.s: The Tiwari Committee, which investigated industrial sickness and recommended special legislation, was associated with which period?
64.x: The Tiwari Committee investigated industrial sickness during 1984-85 and recommended special legislation, leading to the enactment of SICA, 1985.
64.tq: Use the date attached to the committee before linking it to the legislation.

64.s: The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act was enacted in:
64.x: The Tiwari Committee's recommendations led to the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.
64.tq: Distinguish the legislation year from the later year in which BIFR began functioning.

64.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was set up in:
64.x: BIFR was created under SICA and was set up in January 1987, functioning from 1987.
64.tq: Separate the enactment year of SICA from the establishment year of BIFR.

64.s: Appeals against the decisions of the BIFR lay before the:
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
64.x: The Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction, or AAIFR, heard appeals against BIFR decisions.
64.tq: Discriminate between the old appellate authority and the later NCLAT.

64.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the functions associated with BIFR?
o: Early detection of sickness, revival of viable units and closure of unviable units
Regulation of stock exchanges, revival of banks and promotion of exports
Recovery of all agricultural loans and supervision of public-sector recruitment
Promotion of small-scale industries, control of inflation and management of foreign exchange
64.x: BIFR was concerned with early detection of industrial sickness, revival of viable units and closure or winding-up of unviable units.
64.tq: Identify the option that combines the three functions rather than a neighbouring economic responsibility.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the coverage of SICA, 1985:
1. It covered companies with industrial undertakings.
2. It applied only to public-sector companies.
3. It covered private companies also.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: SICA covered companies with industrial undertakings in both the public and private sectors. Therefore, statements 1 and 3 are correct, while statement 2 is false.
64.tq: Watch for the extreme word 'only' in the statement about public-sector coverage.

64.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a reason for the failure of the BIFR-based regime?
o: Legal loopholes enabling promoters to stall debt recovery
Excessively rapid resolution of all sick units
64.x: The regime was criticised for procedural delays, legal loopholes and an ineffective revival mechanism; rapid resolution was not a reason for its failure.
64.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented criticism of the institution.

64.s: BIFR ceased to exist on:
64.x: BIFR ceased on 30 November 2016. BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved from 1 December 2016.
64.tq: Distinguish the cessation date from the following date of dissolution and transition.

64.s: With effect from 1 December 2016, pending cases before BIFR and AAIFR were referred to which institutions under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
64.x: After BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved, pending cases were referred to the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal under IBC, 2016.
64.tq: Match the old institutions with their correct successor forums, not with regulatory or banking bodies.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. SICA, 1985
 b. BIFR
 c. AAIFR
 d. Debtor-in-possession

List-II
 i. Creditor-in-control under the new regime
 ii. National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
 iii. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
 iv. National Company Law Tribunal

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
64.x: SICA corresponds to the earlier regime replaced by IBC, BIFR was succeeded by NCLT, AAIFR by NCLAT, and debtor-in-possession was replaced by creditor-in-control.
64.tq: Start with the sure institutional successor pairs and eliminate codes with a repeated mismatch.

64.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the present insolvency framework?
o: IBBI — appellate tribunal for BIFR cases
64.x: NCLT functions as the adjudicating authority under the present framework. IBBI is the regulator and insolvency professionals are licensed under the framework.
64.tq: Identify the correct authority-function pair while rejecting swapped institutional roles.

64.s: Under the original SICA, 1985 definition, an industrial company could be treated as sick only when it had been registered for at least:
64.x: The original SICA definition required the industrial company to have been registered for at least seven years.
64.tq: Do not substitute the amended five-year threshold for the original SICA threshold.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the original SICA, 1985 definition of a sick industrial company:
1. Accumulated losses had to equal or exceed net worth at the end of a financial year.
2. Cash losses in that financial year and the preceding financial year were relevant.
3. The company had to have been registered for at least seven years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The original definition included all three conditions: at least seven years of registration, accumulated losses equal to or exceeding net worth, and cash losses in the relevant and preceding years.
64.tq: Combine the threshold, loss and cash-loss conditions before selecting the coded option.

64.s: Which change was introduced by the 1993 amendment to the SICA definition of a sick company?
o: The registration requirement was increased to ten years and cash losses were retained.
The registration requirement was reduced to three years and net worth was excluded.
The registration requirement was abolished and accumulated losses were ignored.
The registration requirement was reduced to five years and the cash-loss test was dropped.
64.x: The 1993 amendment reduced the minimum registration period from seven to five years and dropped the cash-loss test.
64.tq: Compare the original and amended definitions by isolating both changed elements.

64.s: In the general economic sense, a unit is considered sick when it:
o: Records a temporary fall in sales but remains financially self-sustaining
Fails to generate a surplus on a continuing basis and depends on repeated infusion of funds
Has a high level of exports and foreign exchange earnings
Receives a government subsidy for modernisation
64.x: Industrial sickness generally refers to the inability to generate surplus continuously and dependence on repeated infusion of funds.
64.tq: Choose the definition based on continuing financial dependence rather than a temporary business fluctuation.

64.s: Under the RBI definition for micro and small units, which of the following could indicate sickness?
o: Any borrowal account remaining NPA for more than three months
A 10 per cent rise in net worth through retained earnings
A single month of delayed sales without an NPA
A temporary increase in working capital
64.x: Under the stated RBI definition, a borrowal account remaining NPA for more than three months was one indicator of sickness.
64.tq: Focus on the precise NPA duration rather than a general reference to financial difficulty.

64.s: A micro or small unit could also be treated as sick under the RBI definition when its net worth had eroded by at least:
64.x: The RBI definition included erosion of net worth by 50 per cent through accumulated losses in the previous year.
64.tq: Use the exact percentage threshold and distinguish it from nearby percentage distractors.

64.s: The RBI's Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of MSMEs, introduced in 2016, emphasised:
o: Early identification of incipient stress and Committees for Stressed MSMEs
Replacement of all bank loans by government grants
Automatic closure of every account classified as NPA
64.x: The 2016 framework replaced the earlier definition with early identification of incipient stress through SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 categories and Committees for Stressed MSMEs.
64.tq: Select the option expressing the preventive and early-warning approach of the framework.

64.s: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the National Renewal Fund?
o: To provide export subsidies exclusively to private companies
To regulate the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India
To compensate and retrain workers displaced during industrial restructuring and support modernisation
To finance only the acquisition of agricultural land
64.x: The fund provided VRS compensation, retraining and redeployment for displaced workers and supported industrial restructuring and modernisation.
64.tq: Apply the fund's social-safety-net purpose to a restructuring situation.

64.s: The principal beneficiaries of the National Renewal Fund were:
o: Employees of the Reserve Bank of India
Workers of sick or restructured units, mainly in public-sector enterprises
Only foreign investors in special economic zones
64.x: The fund primarily benefited workers of sick or restructured units, especially workers in public-sector enterprises.
64.tq: Separate the beneficiaries from the wider industrial objectives of the fund.

64.s: Which one of the following is an INTERNAL cause of industrial sickness?
64.x: Diversion of funds is an internal management-related cause. Demand contraction, power shortages and regulatory changes are external causes.
64.tq: Classify the cause by asking whether it originates within the firm's management.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I: Causes of industrial sickness
 a. Poor working-capital management
 b. Aggressive competition
 c. Obsolete technology
 d. Sudden changes in export-import policy

List-II: Classification
 i. Internal production cause
 ii. External demand cause
 iii. Internal finance cause
 iv. External policy cause

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
64.x: Poor working-capital management is an internal finance cause; aggressive competition is an external demand cause; obsolete technology is an internal production cause; and export-import policy changes are external policy causes.
64.tq: Start by pairing the clear internal finance and external policy examples, then complete the classification.

64.s: For MSMEs, delayed payments by which of the following are identified as a major trigger of industrial sickness?
64.x: Delayed payments by large buyers and government departments create serious cash-flow problems and are a major trigger of sickness among MSMEs.
64.tq: Identify the specific creditor relationship rather than treating all delayed payments as equivalent.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of industrial sickness:
1. Bank loans may turn into non-performing assets.
2. Plant, land and funds may remain idle in unviable units.
3. Industrial sickness can cause unemployment.
4. It necessarily increases revenue receipts of the exchequer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Sickness can create NPAs, unemployment and locked capital. Idle assets also result in revenue loss to the exchequer, so statement 4 is false.
64.tq: Reject the reversed fiscal consequence and retain the three direct consequences.

64.s: The State takeover of certain sick private units, particularly in textiles and engineering, was primarily intended to:
o: Transfer all industrial land to banks
64.x: The State took over certain sick private units, especially textile and engineering units, mainly to protect jobs and employment.
64.tq: Link the policy intervention to its stated employment objective rather than ownership alone.

64.s: Which institution, set up in 1971, was associated with the rehabilitation of sick industrial units?
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
64.x: The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India, established in 1971, was set up to rehabilitate sick industrial units.
64.tq: Match the institution with its rehabilitation role and distinguish it from later forums.

64.s: The Liberalized Margin Money Scheme, introduced in June 1987, was associated with:
o: Regulating delayed payments by government departments
Reducing sickness in the small-scale sector
Providing compensation only to retrenched public-sector workers
64.x: The Liberalized Margin Money Scheme, introduced in June 1987, helped reduce sickness in the small-scale sector.
64.tq: Use the scheme's date and sectoral objective together to avoid confusing it with later MSME measures.

64.s: Which statement correctly describes the one-time restructuring measure for stressed MSME loans?
o: It was introduced in 2016 and prohibited all forms of restructuring.
It was introduced in 2019 without downgrade and extended during 2020-21.
It was introduced in 1987 and applied only to large public-sector companies.
It was introduced in 1992 and permanently cancelled all MSME loans.
64.x: A one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without downgrade was permitted in 2019 and extended during 2020-21.
64.tq: Track the measure through both its introduction year and extension period.

64.s: Which of the following correctly represents the present institutional arrangement for dealing with industrial distress and delayed MSME payments?
o: National Renewal Fund for companies, and IRBI for delayed payments
SICA through BIFR for companies, and AAIFR for delayed payments
NCLAT for all delayed payments, and RBI for winding-up companies
IBC 2016 through NCLT for companies, and MSME Samadhaan for delayed payments
64.x: The present framework uses IBC, 2016 and NCLT for company insolvency matters, while MSME Samadhaan addresses delayed payments to MSMEs.
64.tq: Separate the insolvency forum from the mechanism dealing specifically with delayed MSME payments.

64.s: Industrial sickness has been particularly concentrated in which group of sectors?
64.x: The sectors especially associated with industrial sickness are textiles, including cotton mills, jute, sugar and engineering.
64.tq: Recall the sectoral cluster rather than selecting a group of generally important industries.

64.s: The absorption of sick private textile and engineering units by the public sector had which consequence?
o: It increased the net worth of every public-sector enterprise.
It eliminated all unemployment in the industrial sector.
It lowered the returns of public-sector enterprises.
It ended the need for industrial restructuring.
64.x: The public sector absorbed sick private textile and engineering units to protect jobs, but this lowered the returns of public-sector enterprises.
64.tq: Trace the stated trade-off between employment protection and public-sector returns.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Tiwari Committee
B. Omkar Goswami Committee
C. Kohli Working Group
D. Eradi Committee

List-II (Subject or outcome)
1. Insolvency and winding-up leading to NCLT/NCLAT
2. Industrial sickness leading to SICA, 1985 and BIFR
3. Rehabilitation of sick SSI units
4. Industrial sickness and corporate restructuring

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
64.x: The Tiwari Committee was associated with SICA, 1985 and BIFR; the Omkar Goswami Committee examined industrial sickness and corporate restructuring; the Kohli Working Group dealt with rehabilitation of sick SSI units; and the Eradi Committee examined insolvency and winding-up, leading to NCLT/NCLAT.
64.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with swapped committee outcomes.

64.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their constitution or report:
A. T.K. Viswanathan Committee (BLRC)
B. Omkar Goswami Committee
C. Tiwari Committee
D. Kohli Working Group

Select the correct sequence.
64.x: The Tiwari Committee belongs to 1984–85, the Omkar Goswami Committee to 1993, the Kohli Working Group to 1999–2000, and the T.K. Viswanathan-led BLRC to 2015.
64.tq: Use the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two committees from the 1990s.

64.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the recommendation or association of the T.K. Viswanathan Committee, also known as the BLRC?
o: It dealt with rehabilitation of sick SSI units during 1999–2000.
It examined industrial sickness and corporate restructuring in 1993.
It led to the enactment of SICA, 1985 and establishment of BIFR.
It was associated with bankruptcy law and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
64.x: The T.K. Viswanathan-led Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee (BLRC) of 2015 was associated with bankruptcy law and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
64.tq: Use the committee–law association rather than confusing committees with similar industrial-sickness themes.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
64.x: The Eradi Committee was constituted in 1999 and dealt with insolvency and winding-up. The 2015 committee in the list is the T.K. Viswanathan-led BLRC.
64.tq: Check the dates against the committee names and identify the swapped year.

64.s:
With reference to the transition from SICA to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. It shifted the balance of power from the debtor towards the creditor.
2. It contributed to better credit recovery.
3. It improved the ease of doing business.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The shift from SICA to the IBC moved power from the debtor to the creditor and was regarded as improving both credit recovery and the ease of doing business.
64.tq: Test the complete set of stated consequences; all three statements describe the significance of the reform.

64.s: The delayed settlement of invoices is a major cause of sickness among MSMEs. Which of the following was required by the MSME Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in August 2026 to address this problem?
o: State governments were required to route all industrial loans through BIFR.
MSMEs were required to submit insolvency cases directly to NCLAT.
Banks were required to waive all overdue payments owed by MSMEs.
Central Public Sector Enterprises were required to settle MSME invoices through TReDS.
64.x: The measure required Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to settle MSME invoices through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), addressing delayed payments, a major cause of MSME sickness.
64.tq: Identify the institution required to act and the specific payment platform involved.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SICA and BIFR:
1. SICA was criticised for protecting defaulting promoters.
2. References to BIFR often took several years to conclude.
3. BIFR was the final SICA-era forum and was dissolved on 1 December 2016.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All three statements are correct. SICA was criticised for protecting defaulting promoters, BIFR references were often prolonged, and BIFR was dissolved on 1 December 2016 as the last SICA-era forum.
64.tq: Combine criticism, procedural consequence and the terminal date without reversing the institutional sequence.

64.s: Which one of the following was the first dedicated rehabilitation bank in India?
64.x: The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India (IRBI), established in 1971, was the first dedicated rehabilitation bank.
64.tq: Distinguish the earliest rehabilitation institution from later forums, tribunals and payment platforms.

64.s:
Assertion (A): The shift from SICA to the IBC strengthened the position of creditors in insolvency resolution.

Reason (R): The earlier SICA framework was criticised for protecting defaulting promoters and allowing BIFR proceedings to remain pending for years.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
64.x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. The weaknesses associated with SICA and prolonged BIFR proceedings explain the movement towards an IBC framework that gave creditors a stronger role.
64.tq: Check whether the criticism of the old framework explains the institutional shift towards creditor control.

65.s: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Indian policy framework through which of the following?
65.x: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Interim Budget presented in July 1991.
65.tq: Use the exact year and policy document rather than associating the term with a later committee.

65.s:
With reference to the first round of disinvestment in India, consider the following statements:
1. It was undertaken during 1991–92.
2. Minority stakes in 31 public sector undertakings were offered.
3. A disinvestment limit of 20 per cent was announced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: The first round of disinvestment took place in 1991–92, involved minority stakes in 31 PSUs and announced a 20 per cent disinvestment limit.
65.tq: Combine the date, number of enterprises and percentage in one statement set.

65.s: The Rangarajan Committee, constituted in 1993, recommended which of the following regarding disinvestment?
o: Retention of at least 74 per cent government ownership in every PSU
Complete privatisation of all public sector undertakings
A ban on strategic sales of public enterprises
Disinvestment up to 49 per cent in PSUs reserved for the public sector
65.x: The Rangarajan Committee recommended disinvestment up to 49 per cent in PSUs reserved for the public sector. It also suggested up to 74 per cent disinvestment in other enterprises.
65.tq: Test the committee’s recommendation through the specific percentage associated with it.

65.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: V. Krishnamurthy Committee — 1991 — Early disinvestment approach
Disinvestment Commission — 1993 — Faster disinvestment and governance reforms
Vijay Kelkar Committee — 1984 — PSU autonomy and MoUs
65.x: The V. Krishnamurthy Committee of 1991 represented an early approach to disinvestment. The other pairs confuse the years or functions of different bodies.
65.tq: Match each committee with its year and distinctive policy contribution.

65.s: The Disinvestment Commission established in 1996 was headed initially by
65.x: G.V. Ramakrishna was the first Chairperson of the Disinvestment Commission, established in 1996.
65.tq: Distinguish the chairperson of the Commission from the chairpersons of the recommendation committees.

65.s: The principal recommendation associated with the Disinvestment Commission headed by G.V. Ramakrishna was
o: Replacement of MRTP by the Competition Act
Transfer of all PSUs to State Governments
Case-by-case advice on sale of public enterprises
65.x: The Disinvestment Commission provided case-by-case advice on the sale of public enterprises and recommended strategic sales.
65.tq: Identify the body from its distinctive recommendation rather than from its establishment year alone.

65.s: The Department of Disinvestment was later renamed as DIPAM in
65.x: The Department of Disinvestment was renamed the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) in 2016.
65.tq: Use the renaming year to separate the department’s creation from its later institutional transformation.

65.s: DIPAM functions under the Ministry of Finance and is concerned primarily with
o: Managing Central Government equity and disinvestment
Regulating foreign exchange markets and monetary policy
65.x: DIPAM, under the Ministry of Finance, manages Central Government equity and disinvestment in public assets.
65.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the responsible department.

65.s: Which of the following is NOT a method or instrument managed in the context of Central Government disinvestment by DIPAM?
65.x: Strategic sale, Offer for Sale, IPO/FPO and CPSE ETF are disinvestment-related instruments. Statutory liquidity ratio is a monetary and banking instrument, not a disinvestment method.
65.tq: Find the one item belonging to monetary policy rather than public-asset management.

65.s:
Arrange the following phases of disinvestment in chronological order:
A. First strategic sales
B. Minority sales
C. Period in which about 70 per cent of cumulative proceeds since 1991 were realised
65.x: Minority sales characterised 1991–98, first strategic sales occurred during 1999–2004, and the period from 2014 onwards accounted for about 70 per cent of cumulative proceeds since 1991.
65.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest phase and then place the later strategic-sale phase.

65.s: During the phase from 1991 to 1998, the approximate amount realised through minority disinvestment was
65.x: Minority disinvestment during 1991–98 realised approximately ₹17,557 crore.
65.tq: Test the exact phase-wise realisation using closely spaced numerical distractors.

65.s: Which one of the following was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding rather than with the disinvestment policy recommendations?
65.x: Arjun Sengupta’s 1984 work was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding, not with the later disinvestment recommendations.
65.tq: Separate a nearby but distinct reform theme from the committees directly concerned with disinvestment.

65.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was primarily enacted to
o: Control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
Promote unrestricted concentration of economic power
Provide financial assistance to public enterprises
65.x: The MRTP Act sought to control private monopolies and concentration of economic power and to curb monopolistic, restrictive and unfair trade practices.
65.tq: Use the purpose of the statute to distinguish it from laws dealing with public finance or foreign exchange.

65.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was recommended by the
65.x: The Dutt Committee, formally the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, recommended the MRTP legislation.
65.tq: Trap the closely associated Hazari and Dutt committees by asking which one made the recommendation.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the MRTP Act:
1. It was enacted in 1969.
2. It became effective in 1970.
3. It was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969, came into effect in 1970 and was subsequently replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
65.tq: Distinguish the enactment year from the effective year and the later replacement law.

65.s: The MRTP Commission was replaced by the
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
65.x: The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) under the competition-law framework.
65.tq: Match the abolished statutory body with its institutional successor.

65.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change in the MRTP firm threshold?
o: The asset limit fell from ₹100 crore to ₹20 crore in 1985, while the market-share threshold rose from 25 per cent to 33 per cent in 1984.
The asset limit rose from ₹20 crore to ₹100 crore in 1985, while the market-share threshold was reduced from 33 per cent to 25 per cent in 1984.
Both the asset limit and the market-share threshold were reduced in 1984.
Both the asset limit and the market-share threshold were raised in 1985.
65.x: An MRTP firm was initially associated with assets of ₹20 crore or more or a 33 per cent market share. The market-share threshold was reduced to 25 per cent in 1984, and the asset limit was raised to ₹100 crore in 1985.
65.tq: Track the direction and year of each threshold change separately.

65.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes disinvestment from privatisation?
o: Disinvestment removes licences and quotas, whereas privatisation integrates the economy with the world economy.
Disinvestment always transfers management control, whereas privatisation may retain government control.
Disinvestment means sale of all government assets, whereas privatisation means sale of only minority shares.
Disinvestment reduces government equity, while privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector.
65.x: Disinvestment is the sale or reduction of government equity, with the government possibly retaining majority ownership and control. Privatisation involves transfer of ownership and management control to the private sector.
65.tq: Separate the two look-alike terms by asking whether ownership and management control are transferred.

65.s: Removal of licences, quotas and controls, with the State acting mainly as a facilitator, is known as
65.x: Liberalisation refers to removing licences, quotas and controls and changing the State’s role from controller to facilitator.
65.tq: Identify the LPG term from its defining policy action rather than from ownership changes.

65.s: Integration of the Indian economy with the world economy through tariff cuts, FDI and the transition from FERA to FEMA is termed
65.x: Globalisation denotes integration with the world economy and includes measures such as tariff reduction, FDI and the shift from FERA to FEMA.
65.tq: Use the policy instruments listed in the description to identify the correct LPG concept.

65.s: A government retains more than 51 per cent equity and control in a public sector enterprise while selling a part of its holding. This is called
65.x: Under minority disinvestment, the government retains more than 51 per cent ownership and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control while retaining a minority stake.
65.tq: Apply the percentage and control test to distinguish minority and majority disinvestment.

65.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the corresponding government stake or control?
o: Minority disinvestment — government retains more than 51 per cent and control
Majority disinvestment — government retains more than 51 per cent and control
Complete privatisation — government retains a controlling stake
Strategic sale — no transfer of management control
65.x: Minority disinvestment leaves the government with more than 51 per cent and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control, while complete privatisation transfers 100 per cent ownership and control.
65.tq: Start from the sure ownership-and-control pair and eliminate the reversed descriptions.

65.s: A strategic sale generally involves
o: Transfer of all public assets to another government department
Sale of exactly 10 per cent of shares without any change in management
Sale of a block of shares, usually 50 per cent or more, along with transfer of management control
Removal of industrial licences without any sale of equity
65.x: A strategic sale normally involves a block of shares, usually 50 per cent or more, together with transfer of management control to a strategic partner.
65.tq: Test the defining combination of a substantial share block and management control.

65.s: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 primarily provided for
o: Transfer of management of all industries to foreign investors
Regulation of agricultural land ceilings alone
Licensing for starting or expanding industrial units and the creation of Development Councils
Abolition of all industrial licences and quotas
65.x: The IDRA, 1951 provided for licensing of industrial units when they were started or expanded and also provided for Development Councils. It was amended in 1953.
65.tq: Identify the Act from its two core functions instead of confusing it with later liberalisation measures.

65.s: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 was amended in
65.x: The IDRA, 1951 was amended in 1953.
65.tq: Test the amendment year separately from the year of enactment.

65.s: The Hazari Report of 1967 and the Dutt Committee of 1969 exposed the fact that industrial licensing
o: Was confined exclusively to public sector enterprises
Had eliminated concentration of economic power
65.x: The Hazari Report and Dutt Committee found that the licensing system tended to favour large business houses, contributing to the subsequent MRTP framework.
65.tq: Link the reports to their common finding rather than confusing their dates with the MRTP enactment year.

65.s: In the 1980s, the number of industrial groups that were delicensed was
65.x: During the 1980s, 32 industrial groups were delicensed.
65.tq: Distinguish the number of delicensed groups from the later number of industries in the negative list.

65.s: The negative list announced in 1988 contained how many industries?
65.x: The negative list of 1988 contained 26 industries.
65.tq: Use the year-number association and avoid swapping it with the 32 groups delicensed in the 1980s.

65.s:
Which of the following industries were among the three additional sectors delicensed in 1993?
1. Automobiles
2. White goods
3. Leather
4. Industrial explosives
65.x: Automobiles, white goods and leather were the three sectors delicensed in 1993. Industrial explosives remained among the industries subject to compulsory licensing.
65.tq: Separate the three-item 1993 delicensing group from the later retained licensing categories.

65.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the later sequence of delicensing measures?
o: Electronic goods in December 1996/July 1997, followed by coal and petroleum in Budget 1998–99
Coal and petroleum in December 1996/July 1997, followed by electronic goods in Budget 1998–99
Leather in Budget 1998–99, followed by automobiles in December 1996/July 1997
Industrial explosives in 1993, followed by hazardous chemicals in 1996
65.x: Electronic goods were delicensed in December 1996/July 1997, and coal and petroleum were delicensed in the 1998–99 Budget.
65.tq: Arrange the policy steps by using the dated milestones rather than the sector names alone.

65.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the five industries that continued under compulsory licensing?
65.x: The five remaining categories were alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives. Leather had been delicensed in 1993.
65.tq: Find the sector removed from the final compulsory-licensing list by recalling the earlier delicensing step.

65.s: The National Investment Fund (NIF) was set up on which date?
65.x: The National Investment Fund was set up on 3 November 2005.
65.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish the fund from later disinvestment institutions.

65.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the use of proceeds credited to the National Investment Fund?
o: Only the income generated from the fund is used.
The entire principal is distributed annually to CPSE employees.
The proceeds are transferred exclusively to State governments.
The fund is used only for purchasing foreign exchange.
65.x: The proceeds are credited to the National Investment Fund, but only the income generated from it is used.
65.tq: Test the distinction between principal proceeds and income generated from a fund.

65.s:
With reference to disinvestment targets, consider the following statements:
1. The target for 2020–21 from PSBs and financial institutions was ₹90,000 crore.
2. The target for 2025–26 was ₹47,000 crore.
3. The target for 2026–27 was ₹80,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: All three statements are correct: the respective targets were ₹90,000 crore, ₹47,000 crore and ₹80,000 crore.
65.tq: Compare closely placed budget years and figures.

65.s: Since which financial year has there been no separate disinvestment head in the Budget, with disinvestment receipts merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts?
65.x: Since FY24, there has been no separate disinvestment head; it has been merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts.
65.tq: Use the time marker to identify the change in budget classification.

65.s:
Consider the following statements regarding strategic disinvestment:
1. In-principle approval has been given since 2016 for strategic disinvestment of 36 CPSEs.
2. Of these, 13 strategic disinvestments had been completed.
3. Strategic disinvestment refers only to sale of minority shares through an exchange offer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Strategic disinvestment is not limited to sale of minority shares through an exchange offer.
65.tq: Find the false definition hidden among numerical statements.

65.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
65.x: Modern Food Industries was sold to Hindustan Lever. BALCO was sold to Sterlite, VSNL to the Tata group and Air India to Tata Group.
65.tq: Start from the sure buyer-company pair and eliminate swapped buyers.

65.s:
Arrange the following strategic sales in chronological order:
A. Air India
B. VSNL
C. Modern Food Industries
D. BALCO
65.x: The correct order is Modern Food Industries (2000), BALCO (2001), VSNL (2002) and Air India (2021).
65.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the intervening years.

65.s: The Bharat Bond ETF raised approximately what amount in 2019?
65.x: The Bharat Bond ETF raised approximately ₹32,400 crore in 2019.
65.tq: Distinguish the ETF mobilisation figure from individual CPSE sale proceeds.

65.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the disinvestment outcome stated?
o: LIC IPO — conducted in 2019 with about 32 lakh applications
NINL — sale proceeds credited to the exchequer from government equity
REC — acquired by PFC for ₹14,500 crore
BPCL — strategic sale completed in mid-2022
65.x: REC was acquired by PFC for ₹14,500 crore in 2018–19. NINL yielded no proceeds to the exchequer because the government held no equity; the BPCL sale was called off and the LIC IPO was in 2022 with about 73 lakh applications.
65.tq: Check the company, transaction and outcome together rather than recognising only the company name.

65.s: The disinvestment target and realisation for 2021–22 were, respectively:
65.x: For 2021–22, the target was ₹1.75 lakh crore, whereas the realisation was only about ₹13,534 crore.
65.tq: Separate target figures from actual realisations in the same financial year.

65.s: Which of the following statements about disinvestment transactions is correct?
o: HPCL was sold to ONGC in 2017–18 for ₹36,915 crore.
Pawan Hans and Central Electronics sales were completed without delay.
The 2022–23 realisation of ₹35,294 crore came only from the LIC IPO.
IDBI Bank strategic sale was abandoned after completion.
65.x: HPCL was sold to ONGC in 2017–18 for ₹36,915 crore. The 2022–23 realisation involved several entities, while Pawan Hans and Central Electronics sales stalled and IDBI Bank remained in the pipeline.
65.tq: Use the buyer, year and amount as a three-part identification test.

65.s: The Industrial (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 is primarily associated with:
65.x: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 is associated with industrial licensing.
65.tq: Link each Act with its distinctive regulatory purpose.

65.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
65.x: The Competition Act was enacted in 2002 and commenced on 31 March 2003. The other pairs are correctly matched.
65.tq: Find the wrong year among a set of familiar regulatory enactments.

65.s: Which Act was replaced by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 in relation to the earlier sick-industrial-company regime?
65.x: The IBC, 2016 replaced the SICA regime, which had been associated with the functioning of BIFR.
65.tq: Identify the predecessor regime rather than the more widely known foreign-exchange replacement.

65.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the enactment of FEMA, the Competition Act and the IBC?
65.x: FEMA was enacted in 1999, the Competition Act in 2002 and the IBC in 2016.
65.tq: Arrange the Acts by their enactment years, not their commencement dates.

65.s: The National Renewal Fund, established in 1992, was intended primarily to provide:
o: A safety net and voluntary retirement support for workers affected by restructuring
Foreign exchange support to export-oriented industries
Direct loans to State electricity regulators
65.x: The National Renewal Fund provided a safety net, including VRS support, for workers affected by industrial restructuring.
65.tq: Match the fund with its beneficiary and policy purpose.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about BIFR:
1. It was created under SICA, 1985.
2. It began functioning in 1987.
3. It was dissolved on 1 December 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: All three statements are correct. BIFR was created under SICA, began functioning in 1987 and was dissolved on 1 December 2016.
65.tq: Test an institutional timeline through three linked dates.

65.s: After the dissolution of BIFR, its cases were transferred to which institutions under the IBC framework?
65.x: Following BIFR's dissolution, cases were transferred to the NCLT and NCLAT under the IBC framework.
65.tq: Trace the institutional successor relationship after a statutory body is dissolved.

65.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
o: It provides a time-bound, creditor-in-control resolution process.
It restores the earlier debtor-in-control SICA process.
It regulates only foreign exchange transactions.
It abolished the NCLT appellate structure.
65.x: The IBC provides a time-bound resolution process based on creditor control. Its regulator is the IBBI.
65.tq: Identify the core operational features of the law rather than its year alone.

65.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 was enacted on 28 May 2016 following the recommendations of which body?
o: T.K. Viswanathan-led Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee
65.x: The IBC followed the recommendations of the T.K. Viswanathan-led Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, which reported in 2015.
65.tq: Discriminate between committees associated with insolvency, company law and competition policy.

65.s: The National Company Law Tribunal was established under which provision and from which date?
o: Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013; 1 December 2016
Section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013; 1 June 2016
Section 5 of the Competition Act; 14 October 2003
65.x: The NCLT was established under Section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013, on 1 June 2016, following the Eradi Committee's recommendations.
65.tq: Combine the statutory section, establishing law and date in one precise recall question.

65.s: Which statement regarding NCLAT is correct?
o: It was created under Section 408 and hears only tax appeals.
It began functioning before the NCLT was established.
It replaced the CCI in investigating anti-competitive agreements.
It is constituted under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013 and has heard CCI appeals since 26 May 2017.
