Stand-Up India: up to ₹10 lakh; MUDRA: above ₹1 crore
Stand-Up India: ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore; MUDRA: up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus
67.x: Stand-Up India covers loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore, while MUDRA covers micro units up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus.
67.tq: Split the options by scheme and verify both loan ranges together.

68.s: The Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Policy was announced in April 2000 through which policy framework?
68.x: The SEZ Policy was announced in April 2000 through the EXIM Policy 2000-01.
68.tq: Identify the policy framework associated with the announcement year.

68.s:
Consider the following events relating to Special Economic Zones:
1. SEZ Policy announced through the EXIM Policy
2. SEZ Act passed
3. SEZ Act received Presidential assent
4. SEZ Act and SEZ Rules came into force
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
68.x: The SEZ Policy was announced in 2000, the Act was passed in May 2005, assent was given in June 2005, and the Act and Rules came into force on 10 February 2006.
68.tq: Arrange the milestones by separating the policy announcement, legislation, assent and commencement.

68.s: On which date did the SEZ Act and the SEZ Rules come into force together?
68.x: The SEZ Act and the SEZ Rules came into force on 10 February 2006.
68.tq: Test the exact commencement date rather than merely the year of enactment.

68.s: A principal institutional feature introduced under the SEZ framework is:
o: Mandatory clearance only through the Reserve Bank of India
Single-window clearance for Central and State matters
Separate customs clearance for every unit
68.x: The SEZ framework provides single-window clearance for matters involving both the Central and State Governments.
68.tq: Match the institutional mechanism with its practical administrative purpose.

68.s: Which of the following correctly describes the treatment of a duty-free enclave in an SEZ?
o: It is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes.
It can import goods only after payment of the basic customs duty.
It is treated as domestic territory for all customs purposes.
It is exempt only from State taxes and not customs duties.
68.x: A duty-free enclave is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes, although it remains within India territorially.
68.tq: Apply the special customs-status rule to distinguish legal treatment from geographical location.

68.s:
An SEZ may be set up by which of the following combinations?
1. Central Government
2. State Government
3. Private persons
4. Joint-sector entities
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: SEZs may be established jointly or severally by the Central Government, State Government or any person, including public, private and joint-sector entities.
68.tq: Use an inclusive list and test whether the extreme restriction that excludes private or joint-sector entities is justified.

68.s: Proposals for setting up SEZs are routed through the State Government to which body for approval?
68.x: Proposals for SEZs are routed through the State Government to the Board of Approval.
68.tq: Identify the specific approving body rather than a neighbouring economic institution.

68.s: SEZs under the current framework are described as being predominantly established by which sector?
68.x: Although Central, State, public, private and joint-sector entities can establish SEZs, SEZs under the Act are mainly private.
68.tq: Distinguish legal eligibility to establish from the predominant ownership pattern.

68.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the SEZ framework?
o: FDI in manufacturing SEZs—prohibited under the automatic route
100% FDI under the automatic route—every activity without exception
FDI in SEZs—permitted only through a constitutional amendment
100% FDI under the automatic route—most manufacturing activities in SEZs
68.x: Most manufacturing activities in SEZs permit 100% FDI under the automatic route. The provision is not stated as applying to every activity without exception.
68.tq: Reject the absolute claim and retain the qualified investment rule.

68.s:
With reference to an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in an SEZ, consider the following statements:
1. Section 18 of the SEZ Act allows an IFSC in an SEZ.
2. More than one IFSC may be established in the same SEZ under the stated provision.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
68.x: Section 18 allows an IFSC in an SEZ, but only one IFSC is permitted per SEZ.
68.tq: Test the statutory permission together with its numerical limitation.

68.s: Under Section 10AA, the income-tax exemption pattern for an eligible SEZ unit is:
o: 100% for ten years followed by complete exemption thereafter
100% exemption for three years and 25% for the next five years
100% for five years, 50% for the next five years, and 50% of reinvested profit for five further years
50% for five years and 100% for the next ten years
68.x: Section 10AA provides 100% exemption for the first five years, 50% for the next five years, and 50% of reinvested profit for five additional years.
68.tq: Read the tax-benefit slabs in sequence and distinguish duration from percentage.

68.s: The sunset phase-out of SEZ tax holidays took place during which period?
68.x: The tax holidays were phased out during 2017–2020 under the sunset clause.
68.tq: Test the policy window using close, ascending year ranges.

68.s: Under the SEZ (Amendment) Rules, 2025, the minimum land requirement for a semiconductor or electronic-component SEZ was reduced from:
68.x: The minimum land requirement for a semiconductor or electronic-component SEZ was reduced from 50 hectares to 10 hectares.
68.tq: Compare the old and revised thresholds rather than selecting only the new figure.

68.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the SEZ Act, 2005?
o: Promotion of exports of goods and services
Restriction of domestic and foreign investment
68.x: The SEZ Act seeks to promote domestic and foreign investment, not restrict it. Its objectives also include economic activity, exports, employment and infrastructure development.
68.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated policy objective.

68.s:
Consider the following objectives of the SEZ Act, 2005:
1. Promotion of investment, both domestic and foreign
2. Development of infrastructure
3. Promotion of exports of goods and services
4. Creation of employment
Which of the objectives given above are correct?
68.x: All four listed objectives are included in the objectives of the SEZ Act. Generation of additional economic activity is another stated objective.
68.tq: Recognise the comprehensive policy-objective combination rather than treating employment or infrastructure as exclusions.

68.s: Which of the following is the correct description of a free trade zone?
o: An area reserved exclusively for agricultural exports
An area where goods may be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without customs duty
An area where imported goods must be consumed before re-export
An area where only domestically produced goods may be sold without State taxes
68.x: A free trade zone permits goods to be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without payment of customs duty.
68.tq: Apply the operational definition by checking all four permitted activities.

68.s: Kandla, which became India's first Free Trade Zone, was subsequently converted into a:
o: Coastal Economic Zone under the ADB
National Investment and Manufacturing Zone only
68.x: Kandla was India's first Free Trade Zone and was later converted into a Special Economic Zone.
68.tq: Separate the earlier institutional designation from the later SEZ status.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
68.x: Falta is an Export Processing Zone in West Bengal. SEEPZ is located in Santacruz, Mumbai, while MEPZ is associated with Chennai.
68.tq: Use location-based elimination among similar-sounding export-processing zones.

68.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the other Export Processing Zones listed with Noida, Chennai, Cochin and Visakhapatnam?
68.x: Noida, Chennai, Cochin and Visakhapatnam are listed Export Processing Zones; Bengaluru is not included in that list.
68.tq: Find the geographically plausible but unlisted location.

68.s: As on 31 March 2025, how many SEZs were notified and how many were operational?
68.x: As on 31 March 2025, India had 368 notified SEZs, of which 276 were operational.
68.tq: Distinguish the larger notified stock from the smaller operational stock.

68.s: As on 31 March 2025, the number of units operating in SEZs was approximately:
68.x: There were 6,695 units operating in SEZs as on 31 March 2025.
68.tq: Use place-value discrimination among closely related numerical options.

68.s: The investment in SEZs as on 31 March 2025 was approximately:
68.x: The reported investment in SEZs was ₹7,82,192 crore as on 31 March 2025.
68.tq: Test digit grouping and distinguish crore-scale values.

68.s: What was the approximate employment generated in SEZs as on 31 March 2025?
68.x: SEZs accounted for approximately 31,77,893 jobs as on 31 March 2025.
68.tq: Check the Indian-numbering format and reject misplaced zeroes.

68.s: SEZ exports in FY 2024–25 were approximately:
68.x: SEZ exports in FY 2024–25 were reported at approximately ₹14,63,669 crore, equivalent to about US$173 billion.
68.tq: Match the reported export figure with its correct crore magnitude.

68.s: Which one of the following was identified as a criticism of the performance of SEZs?
o: SEZs received more than half of total foreign direct investment.
Domestic tariff area sales were completely unrestricted.
SEZs received less than 3% of foreign direct investment.
No SEZ units were shut during the five-year period.
68.x: SEZs received less than 3% of FDI. Other criticisms included capped DTA sales and the closure of many units.
68.tq: Select the qualified performance criticism and reject reversed or absolute statements.

68.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the recent slowdown in SEZs is correct?
1. 466 units shut down in five years across seven SEZs.
2. 100 units shut down in FY 2024–25.
3. Export growth was below 4% in FY 2024–25.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: All three statements describe reported indicators of the SEZ slowdown: 466 closures across seven SEZs, including 100 in FY 2024–25, and export growth below 4%.
68.tq: Combine multiple performance indicators and watch for the complete-code option.

68.s: The Baba Kalyani Committee, constituted in 2018, recommended renaming SEZs as:
68.x: The committee recommended renaming SEZs as 3Es—Employment and Economic Enclaves.
68.tq: Discriminate among closely similar expansions of an official abbreviation.

68.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Baba Kalyani Committee?
o: Complete abolition of SEZs without replacement
Separate rules for manufacturing and services
68.x: The committee recommended separate rules, extension of the sunset clause and a unified IFSC regulator. Complete abolition of SEZs was not the stated recommendation.
68.tq: Identify the option that changes reform and restructuring into outright abolition.

68.s: The DESH Bill, announced in the Union Budget 2022–23, seeks to:
o: Create a new Export Processing Zone at Kandla
68.x: The Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs (DESH) Bill was announced in Budget 2022–23 to replace the SEZ Act, but it remains pending.
68.tq: Match the proposed legislation with the law it is intended to replace.

68.s:
Which of the following changes is associated with the proposed DESH Bill?
1. Removal of the positive Net Foreign Exchange condition
2. Permission for Domestic Tariff Area sales
3. Immediate replacement of the SEZ Act through an enacted law
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: The DESH proposal removes the positive NFE condition and allows DTA sales. It remains pending and has not immediately replaced the SEZ Act.
68.tq: Separate proposed provisions from the legal status of a Bill that is still pending.

68.s: The Nandigram protests of 2007 were associated with opposition to land acquisition for a:
o: Free Trade Warehousing Zone at Kandla
68.x: Nandigram in West Bengal witnessed violent protests in 2007 against land acquisition for a chemical-hub SEZ.
68.tq: Link the place and year to the specific project that triggered the conflict.

68.s: Which corridor is correctly matched with its States and partner country?
o: DMIC—Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra—Japan
DMIC—Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh—United Kingdom
CBIC—Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal—Japan
68.x: The Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor covers Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra, with Japan as partner.
68.tq: Start with the sure corridor-country pair and verify the State cluster.

68.s: The Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor is aligned with which dedicated freight corridor?
68.x: The DMIC runs along the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.
68.tq: Associate the corridor with its defining transport alignment.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. CBIC—Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
2. CBIC—Japan through JICA
3. CBIC node in Andhra Pradesh—Krishnapatnam
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
68.x: CBIC covers Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, is associated with Japan through JICA, and has Krishnapatnam as its Andhra Pradesh node.
68.tq: Check the corridor, partner institution and State-specific node together.

68.s: The Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor covers which group of States?
o: Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal
Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Delhi, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
68.x: The AKIC covers Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal.
68.tq: Identify the full contiguous State group rather than a partial corridor list.

68.s: The Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor is associated with which transport infrastructure?
o: Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and coastal shipping only
Southern Dedicated Freight Corridor and NW-5
Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor and inland waterways of NW-1
68.x: The AKIC is associated with the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor and inland waterways along National Waterway-1.
68.tq: Match the corridor’s geography with its supporting transport infrastructure.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
68.x: The Bengaluru–Mumbai Economic Corridor covers Karnataka and Maharashtra and has the United Kingdom as partner.
68.tq: Use the partner-country clue to distinguish similar corridor abbreviations.

68.s:
Which of the following statements about the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor is correct?
1. It is approximately 800 km long.
2. Andhra Pradesh is the State covered in the listed corridor description.
3. It is associated with the Asian Development Bank.
4. It is India's first coastal corridor.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: VCIC is approximately 800 km long, covers Andhra Pradesh in the stated description, is associated with ADB and is India's first coastal corridor.
68.tq: Use the complete-code option when all geographic, numerical and institutional features align.

68.s: The East Coast Economic Corridor extends from:
68.x: The East Coast Economic Corridor extends from Kolkata to Kanyakumari.
68.tq: Distinguish the endpoints of similarly named national corridors.

68.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between ECEC and VCIC?
o: VCIC is the first phase of ECEC.
VCIC and ECEC are both phases of DMIC.
ECEC is the first phase of VCIC.
ECEC is a partner country of VCIC.
68.x: The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor.
68.tq: Test the direction of the phase-to-parent-corridor relationship.

68.s: The Andhra Pradesh node of the Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor is located at:
68.x: Orvakal is the Andhra Pradesh node of the Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
68.tq: Separate State-specific nodes belonging to different industrial corridors.

68.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
68.x: The Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor covers Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
68.tq: Match the corridor abbreviation with its exact State coverage.

68.s: How many industrial corridors are included under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme?
68.x: The National Industrial Corridor Development Programme includes 11 industrial corridors.
68.tq: Test the programme-wide count using close numerical distractors.

68.s: The integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor, proposed in Budget 2026–27, includes a node at:
68.x: Budget 2026–27 proposed an integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor with a node at Durgapur.
68.tq: Distinguish the newly specified node from existing corridor nodes.

68.s: NICDC was formerly known as which of the following organisations?
68.x: NICDC was formerly known as the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (DMICDC).
68.tq: Direct recall of an institutional name change.

68.s: NICDC was incorporated in which month and year?
68.x: NICDC was incorporated in January 2008.
68.tq: Numerical and date recall using closely spaced institutional milestones.

68.s: Which department and ministry are associated with NICDC?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Steel
68.x: NICDC is associated with DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
68.tq: Identify the correct ministry and department rather than a neighbouring authority.

68.s:
With reference to the institutional structure of industrial corridor development, consider the following statements:
1. NICDIT functions as an apex trust for funding nodes.
2. The Budget Estimate for NICDIT funding in 2026–27 is ₹3,000 crore.
3. NICDIT is described as a department of the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: NICDIT is an apex trust for funding nodes, with ₹3,000 crore provided in the 2026–27 Budget Estimate. It is not described as a Department of the Ministry of Finance.
68.tq: Find the wrong institutional description and retain the correct structure and figure.

68.s: Which pair of operational greenfield industrial smart cities is correctly matched with its State?
68.x: The operational cities identified are Dholera in Gujarat and Shendra-Bidkin in Maharashtra.
68.tq: Start from the sure location pair in a location-based matching question.

68.s: The combined investment associated with the operational cities Dholera and Shendra-Bidkin is reported as approximately:
68.x: The investment associated with Dholera and Shendra-Bidkin is ₹2.02 lakh crore.
68.tq: Distinguish a lakh-crore investment figure from corridor and scheme outlays.

68.s: Which of the following was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on 28 August 2024?
o: New greenfield industrial smart cities including Orvakal, Kopparthy and Krishnapatnam
Only the Sri City dry-port proposal
The creation of 14 Coastal Economic Zones
The VCIC policy loan of US$125 million
68.x: On 28 August 2024, the CCEA approved new smart cities including Orvakal, Kopparthy and Krishnapatnam.
68.tq: Match the approving authority and date with the correct policy decision.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Industrial city)
 a. Orvakal
 b. Kopparthy
 c. Krishnapatnam

List-II (Corridor)
 i. VCIC
 ii. CBIC
 iii. HBIC

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: Orvakal is associated with HBIC, Kopparthy with VCIC and Krishnapatnam with CBIC.
68.tq: Start from the sure corridor-city pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.

68.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
68.x: Orvakal covers 2,621 acres with an outlay of ₹1,781 crore. The figures 2,596 acres and ₹1,264 crore belong to Kopparthy.
68.tq: Use the swapped-number trap in a not-correctly-matched question.

68.s: BHAVYA, announced for 2026, stands for:
o: Bharat High-value Advancement and Yuva Authority
Bharat Advanced Manufacturing and Value Addition Yojana
68.x: BHAVYA stands for Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana.
68.tq: Direct recall of an expansion of an official programme acronym.

68.s:
Consider the following statements about BHAVYA:
1. It has an allocation of ₹33,660 crore.
2. It covers FY27–FY32.
3. It aims to establish 100 plug-and-play industrial parks.
4. It is implemented by NICDC through an SPV of NICDIT and a State agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All four statements correctly describe BHAVYA: its ₹33,660 crore allocation, FY27–FY32 period, 100 parks and implementation structure.
68.tq: Test a complete scheme profile through an all-statements option.

68.s: Which State is described as having nodes on all three of the VCIC, CBIC and HBIC national corridors?
68.x: Andhra Pradesh is described as the only State with nodes on the VCIC, CBIC and HBIC national corridors.
68.tq: Direct recall of a unique comparative distinction.

68.s: The total ADB assistance for the VCIC is US$840 million. Which of the following correctly represents its components?
o: Policy loan US$840 million with no separate project loan or GoAP contribution
Policy loan US$500 million, project loan US$215 million and GoAP contribution US$125 million
Policy loan US$215 million, project loan US$125 million and GoAP contribution US$500 million
Policy loan US$125 million, project loan US$500 million and GoAP contribution US$215 million
68.x: VCIC financing comprises an ADB policy loan of US$125 million, an ADB project loan of US$500 million and a GoAP contribution of US$215 million.
68.tq: Split the total into its component figures instead of relying on the aggregate alone.

68.s: Which of the following is the correct set of VCIC nodes in Andhra Pradesh?
68.x: The VCIC nodes are Visakhapatnam, Chittoor through the Srikalahasti-Yerpedu area, and Kopparthy.
68.tq: Identify the correct node list while separating it from CBIC and HBIC nodes.

68.s: Which of the following correctly describes the sectoral orientation of the VCIC?
o: Northern Andhra Pradesh—metallurgy, pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals and IT; Southern Andhra Pradesh—food processing, leather and automobiles
Northern Andhra Pradesh—only information technology; Southern Andhra Pradesh—only port services
Northern Andhra Pradesh—textiles and tourism; Southern Andhra Pradesh—coal and steel
Northern Andhra Pradesh—food processing, leather and automobiles; Southern Andhra Pradesh—metallurgy and pharmaceuticals
68.x: The northern part is associated with metallurgy, pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals and IT, while the southern part focuses on food processing, leather and automobiles.
68.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish northern and southern sectoral profiles.

68.s: The VCIC covers approximately how much land?
68.x: The VCIC covers approximately 33,000 acres.
68.tq: Distinguish the corridor-wide land area from individual nodes and SEZs.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
68.x: Krishnapatnam in SPSR Nellore is the CBIC node, while Orvakal in Kurnool is the HBIC node.
68.tq: Separate the two easily confusable corridor-node associations.

68.s: The CBIC node at Krishnapatnam is located in which district and has the reported area of:
68.x: The Krishnapatnam CBIC node is in SPSR Nellore and covers 13,919.67 acres according to the cited 2025–26 figure.
68.tq: Combine location and area to defeat a district-and-figure swap.

68.s: Which institution is identified as the VCIC funding partner in the APSES and CDI references?
68.x: The APSES and CDI references identify the Asian Development Bank (ADB) as the VCIC partner; JICA is mentioned only in a conflicting January 2026 note.
68.tq: Resolve a confusable institutional attribution by selecting the consistently identified partner.

68.s: Which of the following statements about notified SEZs in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: There were 33 notified SEZs in 2023, of which 10 were developed by NICDC.
There were 47 or more notified SEZs in 2023, of which 10 were developed by APIIC.
There were 10 notified SEZs in 2023, all developed by APIIC.
There were 47 or more notified SEZs in 2023, all developed by APIIC.
68.x: Andhra Pradesh had 47 or more notified SEZs in 2023, and 10 of them were developed by APIIC.
68.tq: Check both the total and the institutional subset in a numerical statement.

68.s: APSEZ is correctly described as:
o: A development authority covering four States and one Union Territory
A greenfield port with 16 MTPA capacity at Kakinada
Located in Tirupati district, combining an SEZ, DTZ, FTWZ and EMC
Located at Atchutapuram-Rambilli in Anakapalli, notified on 12 April 2007, covering 3,213 acres
68.x: APSEZ is located at Atchutapuram-Rambilli in Anakapalli, was notified on 12 April 2007 and covers 3,213 acres.
68.tq: Use a location-date-area combination to identify the exact SEZ profile.

68.s: Sri City is associated with which combination of facilities or zones?
o: SEZ, export processing zone and petroleum reserve only
CBIC node, HBIC node, DTZ and dry port only
SEZ, PCPIR, greenfield port and MTPA terminal
68.x: Sri City comprises an SEZ, Domestic Tariff Zone, Free Trade and Warehousing Zone and Electronics Manufacturing Cluster. A dry-port proposal was under examination.
68.tq: Recall the complete facility combination rather than one isolated designation.

68.s: The proposed dry port under examination was associated with:
68.x: The dry-port proposal under examination was associated with Sri City in Tirupati district.
68.tq: Match the proposal with the correct SEZ location.

68.s: The Visakhapatnam SEZ Development Authority oversees SEZ-related areas in:
o: Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Karnataka and Puducherry
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Yanam
Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu and Goa
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra and Yanam
68.x: The Visakhapatnam SEZ Development Authority oversees Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Yanam.
68.tq: Test the exact membership and geographical coverage of an authority.

68.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Kakinada SEZ project?
o: A greenfield industrial city at Orvakal with 2,621 acres
A greenfield port developed by GMR Kakinada Gateway, with 16 MTPA capacity and a cost of ₹2,123 crore
A port-led SEZ under Sagarmala with a capacity of 33 MTPA and a cost of ₹840 million
A dry port at Sri City with 3,213 acres and a cost of ₹1,264 crore
68.x: The Kakinada SEZ includes a greenfield port by GMR Kakinada Gateway, designed for 16 MTPA and costing ₹2,123 crore.
68.tq: Combine developer, capacity and cost to avoid swapped project details.

68.s: The Sagarmala National Perspective Plan proposed Coastal Economic Zones under which pillar?
68.x: The Sagarmala National Perspective Plan, formulated in 2016, proposed Coastal Economic Zones under its port-led industrialisation pillar.
68.tq: Link a programme with its specific policy pillar.

68.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Coastal Economic Zones:
1. They involve industrial clusters and SEZs near ports.
2. Fourteen Coastal Economic Zones were identified.
3. Their concept is linked with port-led industrialisation under Sagarmala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct: CEZs involve port-proximate industrial clusters and SEZs, 14 were identified, and they were proposed under Sagarmala's port-led industrialisation pillar.
68.tq: Confirm the complete concept through three linked policy statements.

68.s: Integration of industrial corridors with Sagarmala is intended primarily to:
o: Replace all SEZs with free trade zones
Transfer industrial corridors to State governments
68.x: The integration of corridors with Sagarmala is intended to reduce logistics costs.
68.tq: Identify the stated policy objective rather than an exaggerated consequence.

68.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning SEZs and industrial policy?
o: Land acquisition, including the Nandigram controversy
Guaranteed expansion of employment in every notified SEZ
68.x: Land acquisition, revenue loss, under-used land and WTO-inconsistent export subsidies are identified criticisms. Guaranteed employment expansion in every SEZ is not listed as a criticism.
68.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated criticism set.

68.s: The criticism that SEZ incentives may be WTO-inconsistent relates primarily to:
68.x: One criticism is that export subsidies associated with SEZs may be inconsistent with WTO obligations.
68.tq: Match the international trade concern with its precise subject.

68.s: Which recent policy change concerns sales by SEZ units in the domestic market?
o: SEZ units are prohibited from selling any output in India
SEZ units may sell domestically only after conversion into CEZs
SEZ units must transfer all domestic sales to NICDIT
SEZ units may sell in India at concessional tax under the 2026 Budget
68.x: The 2026 Budget permitted SEZ units to sell in India at concessional tax.
68.tq: Distinguish a current policy relaxation from an absolute prohibition.

68.s: Which of the following correctly associates the current-relevance items with their reported dates?
o: BHAVYA parks portal—9 June 2026; Sri City dry port—July 2026; SEZ-to-DTA concessional sales—April 2026
BHAVYA parks portal—April 2026; Sri City dry port—9 June 2026; concessional sales—July 2026

69.tq: Test classification by counting and identifying all members of the list.

69.s: Orvakal/Kurnool airport is notable because it was:
o: The first international airport of Andhra Pradesh, in 2021
The first airport in India built under the PPP-DBFOT model, in 2022
The first airport built by GMR in coastal Andhra Pradesh, in 2020
The first airport in South India built entirely by a State, in 2021
69.x: Orvakal/Kurnool airport was the first airport in South India built entirely by a State, and it was completed in 2021.
69.tq: Identify a distinction based on both superlative and year.

69.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, ₹1 of infrastructure spending is associated with approximately how much GDP generation?
69.x: The estimated GDP impact is ₹2.5–₹3.5 for every ₹1 of infrastructure spending.
69.tq: Use a range-based multiplier question with ascending numerical options.

69.s: National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 became a current policy reference in:
69.x: National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 was reported in February 2026.
69.tq: Distinguish a recent policy update by its precise month and year.

69.s: The Ballari–Guntakal third and fourth railway lines, planned through PM GatiShakti, involve an estimated amount of:
69.x: The Ballari–Guntakal third and fourth lines are planned at a cost of ₹1,264 crore through PM GatiShakti.
69.tq: Separate a railway-project allocation from other infrastructure figures.

69.s: The use of PM GatiShakti data for preparing plans at the grassroots level is associated with:
69.x: Gram panchayats are reported to be using PM GatiShakti data for preparing plans.
69.tq: Apply the programme’s data-use feature to the correct level of local government.

69.s: Which of the following pairs of stalled PPP ports and associated issue is correctly matched?
o: Ramayapatnam and Mulapeta — falling disinvestment receipts
Kakinada Deep Water and Machilipatnam — CBI probe
69.x: Vodarevu and Nizampatnam are stalled PPP port projects associated with a CBI probe. Falling disinvestment receipts are a separate criticism concerning the wider monetisation and disinvestment debate.
69.tq: Match the criticism with the projects actually linked to it, avoiding a nearby-issue swap.

69.s: Which one of the following is identified as a criticism in the infrastructure and asset-monetisation debate?
o: The abolition of all PPP projects
The withdrawal of the National Logistics Policy
A sharp increase in disinvestment receipts
69.x: Falling disinvestment receipts are identified as a criticism in the current debate.
69.tq: Find the statement that reflects the reported criticism rather than an extreme or unsupported consequence.

69.s: Andhra Pradesh’s Blue Economy target is to reach approximately:
69.x: Andhra Pradesh has set a Blue Economy target of US$20 billion by 2035.
69.tq: Test the target through both amount and deadline.

69.s: By 2030, Andhra Pradesh aims to have which combination of infrastructure?
o: Four greenfield ports and eleven fishing harbours
Eleven greenfield ports and four fishing harbours
Three greenfield ports and seventeen fishing harbours
Four major ports and eleven airports
69.x: The target for 2030 is four greenfield ports and eleven fishing harbours.
69.tq: Preserve the order and category of paired numerical targets.

70.s: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission (JNNSM), one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change, originally envisaged a solar capacity target of how much in 2010?
70.x: The original JNNSM target announced in 2010 was 20 GW. It was subsequently raised to 100 GW in 2015.
70.tq: Use the chronology of a policy target and distinguish the original figure from the revised figure.

70.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the composition of the 100 GW solar target under the JNNSM?
o: 50 GW rooftop solar and 50 GW large and medium solar projects
60 GW rooftop solar and 40 GW large and medium solar projects
20 GW rooftop solar and 80 GW large and medium solar projects
40 GW rooftop solar and 60 GW large and medium solar projects
70.x: The 100 GW target comprised 40 GW of rooftop solar and 60 GW of large and medium solar projects.
70.tq: Split a composite numerical target into its two stated components.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s renewable-energy and climate commitments:
1. India’s overall renewable-energy target was 175 GW by 2022.
2. Under the First NDC, India committed to raising the share of non-fossil capacity to above 40 per cent by 2030.
3. The First NDC included a reduction of emissions intensity by 33–35 per cent from the 2005 level by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All three statements are correct. The 175 GW renewable-energy target related to 2022, while the First NDC targets applied to 2030.
70.tq: Separate targets by both subject and target year before selecting the coded combination.

70.s:
With reference to the Panchamrit commitments announced at COP26 in 2021, consider the following statements:
1. India announced a target of 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel capacity by 2030.
2. India announced that 50 per cent of its energy requirements would be met from renewable energy by 2030.
3. India declared a net-zero target for 2070.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: The Panchamrit commitments included 500 GW of non-fossil capacity, meeting 50 per cent of requirements from renewable energy by 2030, and net zero by 2070.
70.tq: Check each commitment independently, especially the different target years.

70.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission has set a target of producing how much green hydrogen annually by 2030?
70.x: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets production of 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen per year by 2030.
70.tq: Directly distinguish the mission’s annual production target from other capacity targets.

70.s: India reached 50 per cent non-fossil installed power capacity in which month and year, according to the stated recent assessment?
70.x: India reached 50 per cent non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of the relevant milestone mentioned in the assessment.
70.tq: Use the precise date rather than confusing an achievement date with a target year.

70.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant — Tamil Nadu — 2 × 1,000 MW
2. Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park — Andhra Pradesh — 1,000 MW
3. Bhadla Solar Park — Rajasthan — desert/wasteland development model
70.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu, Kurnool Solar Park is in Andhra Pradesh, and Bhadla illustrates the desert or wasteland model in Rajasthan.
70.tq: Verify the location, capacity and distinguishing feature of each project separately.

70.s: The Solar Park Scheme under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy primarily provides which combination of support to developers?
o: Coal supply and railway freight subsidy
70.x: The Solar Park Scheme facilitates solar development by making land and transmission infrastructure available to developers.
70.tq: Identify the institutional support that directly addresses the infrastructure barriers of solar parks.

70.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s approximate installed power-capacity position in the latest assessment stated?
o: About 552 GW, with non-fossil capacity above 54 per cent
About 416 GW, with non-fossil capacity below 40 per cent
About 510 GW, with non-fossil capacity about 51.5 per cent
About 485 GW, with non-fossil capacity exactly 50 per cent
70.x: The latest assessment places India’s total installed capacity at approximately 552 GW, with the non-fossil share above 54 per cent.
70.tq: Match the latest total with its corresponding non-fossil share instead of an earlier dated figure.

70.s:
As on 31 March 2026, which one of the following combinations is correct for India’s non-fossil installed capacity?
1. Solar — 150.26 GW
2. Wind — 56.09 GW
3. Large hydro — 51.41 GW
4. Nuclear — 8.78 GW
70.x: All four figures are part of the stated 31 March 2026 non-fossil capacity composition, totalling 283.46 GW.
70.tq: Check every component of a source-wise numerical table before choosing the complete combination.

70.s:
Arrange the following milestones of India’s installed power capacity in chronological order:
A. Total capacity of about 552 GW and non-fossil share above 54 per cent
B. Total capacity of 416.6 GW and non-fossil share of 43 per cent
C. Total capacity of 484.82 GW and non-fossil share of 50.08 per cent
D. Total capacity of 509.64 GW and non-fossil share of 51.55 per cent
70.x: The milestones correspond respectively to 30 April 2023, June 2025, 30 November 2025 and August 2026.
70.tq: Place the dated capacity milestones first, then compare the two 2025 entries by month.

70.s: Which of the following statements regarding India’s power generation and capacity mix is correct?
o: Coal contributes over 70 per cent of installed capacity but less than 42 per cent of generation.
Coal has ceased to be a significant source of electricity generation.
Coal contributes less than 20 per cent of India’s electricity generation.
Coal contributes over 70 per cent of India’s electricity generation, although its share of installed capacity is about 42 per cent.
70.x: Coal still accounts for over 70 per cent of electricity generation, while coal-based capacity is approximately 42 per cent of total installed capacity.
70.tq: Do not confuse a source’s share in installed capacity with its share in actual generation.

70.s: In Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy capacity of 10,639.75 MW, which source has the largest share?
70.x: Solar is the largest component of Andhra Pradesh’s renewable capacity at 5,614.52 MW, followed by wind at 4,397.67 MW.
70.tq: Compare the source-wise figures rather than relying on the general prominence of wind power.

70.s:
The CEA’s National Generation Adequacy Plan for 2026–27 to 2035–36 envisages which of the following?
1. Total capacity of 1,121 GW
2. Peak demand of 459 GW
3. Non-fossil share of 70 per cent
4. Storage capacity of 174 GW
70.x: The plan envisages 1,121 GW of capacity, 459 GW peak demand, 70 per cent non-fossil capacity and 174 GW of storage.
70.tq: Treat each planning parameter as a separate numerical statement and test the complete set.

70.s:
With reference to the National Policy on Biofuels, consider the following statements:
1. The policy was introduced in 2018.
2. The 2022 amendment advanced the target of E20 from 2030 to 2025–26.
3. Ethanol blending is intended, among other things, to reduce oil imports and benefit sugarcane farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: The National Policy on Biofuels was introduced in 2018; its 2022 amendment advanced E20 to 2025–26, and ethanol blending helps reduce oil imports while supporting sugarcane farmers.
70.tq: Combine the policy’s date, amendment and objectives without confusing a target with actual achievement.

70.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as an ethanol feedstock?
70.x: Cassava, damaged food grains and rotten potatoes are identified ethanol feedstocks. Iron ore is not a biofuel feedstock.
70.tq: Find the item that does not belong to the stated agricultural and food-based feedstock group.

70.s: The National Biofuel Coordination Committee is chaired by the:
o: Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare
Minister of New and Renewable Energy
70.x: The Petroleum Minister chairs the National Biofuel Coordination Committee, which approves the use of surplus food grains for ethanol.
70.tq: Use the ‘who heads the body?’ approach and distinguish the petroleum portfolio from neighbouring ministries.

70.s: A proposal is made to use surplus food grains for ethanol production. Which body is responsible for approving such use?
70.x: Approval for using surplus food grains for ethanol is given by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee.
70.tq: Identify the authority associated with the specific regulatory decision rather than the general sector.

70.s:
Which of the following is a feature of the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024?
1. It provides a single framework for renewable energy, pumped storage, green hydrogen, biofuels and EV charging.
2. It provides for capital subsidies and tax exemptions.
3. It targets more than 160 GW of renewable energy.
4. It aims at Net Zero by 2047.
70.x: All four are features or targets of the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.
70.tq: Recognise a policy by its integrated coverage, incentives and multiple quantified targets.

70.s: The Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 targets investment and employment of approximately:
70.x: The policy targets investment of ₹10 lakh crore and the creation of 7.5 lakh jobs.
70.tq: Link the two headline economic targets instead of selecting a single isolated figure.

70.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024, the target cost range for the Green Hydrogen Valley is:
70.x: The Green Hydrogen Valley cost target is ₹160–170 per kilogram.
70.tq: Distinguish a cost target from production-capacity and investment targets.

70.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with an Andhra Pradesh energy-related scheme or initiative?
o: NEDCAP — 50,000 acres of agricultural forest reserved for coal mining
Virtual Net Metering — restriction to large industries only
PM Surya Ghar — compulsory coal-fired rooftop generation
70.x: PM-KUSUM is associated with 2.93 lakh pumps. NEDCAP is associated with using 50,000 acres of barren land for solar, while PM Surya Ghar with Virtual Net Metering has an SC/ST focus.
70.tq: Match each scheme with its beneficiary, technology or numerical target and reject the swapped descriptions.

70.s: Which of the following correctly states the sequence of coal-sector nationalisation in India?
o: Non-coking coal in 1971–72 followed by coking coal in 1973
Coking coal in 1971–72 followed by non-coking coal in 1973
Both coking and non-coking coal in 1971–72
Coking coal in 1973 followed by non-coking coal in 1975
70.x: Coking coal was nationalised in 1971–72, followed by non-coking coal in 1973.
70.tq: Use the order of two closely related nationalisation events to eliminate reversed sequences.

70.s: The Supreme Court’s cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 was followed by which legislative measure for auction-based allocation?
o: Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, without amendment
70.x: The cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 led to the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, which enabled auction-based allocation.
70.tq: Match the judicial event with the specific corrective legislation that followed it.

70.s:
With reference to the revised SHAKTI mechanism notified in May 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Window-I involves notified prices for central and State power plants.
2. Window-II involves auction at a premium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Both statements are correct. Revised SHAKTI provides a notified-price Window-I and a premium-based auction Window-II.
70.tq: Contrast the two windows by the basis on which coal is allocated or priced.

70.s:
Which of the following functions is performed by the Coal Controller’s Organisation?
1. Compilation of coal statistics
2. Monitoring of captive coal blocks
3. Hearing objections relating to acquisition of coal-bearing land

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
70.x: The Coal Controller’s Organisation performs all three functions: maintaining coal statistics, monitoring captive blocks and hearing objections concerning acquisition of coal-bearing land.
70.tq: Group the body’s technical, monitoring and quasi-adjudicatory functions before choosing the code.

70.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the coal sector figures stated for FY 2025–26?
o: Coal output was 1,040.08 million tonnes and thermal-plant imports increased by 27.4 per cent.
Coal output was 104.008 million tonnes and thermal-plant imports increased by 27.4 per cent.
Coal output was 1,040.08 million tonnes and thermal-plant imports declined by 27.4 per cent.
Coal output was 104.008 billion tonnes and thermal-plant imports declined by 27.4 per cent.
70.x: Coal output was 1,040.08 million tonnes in FY 2025–26, while imports by thermal plants declined by 27.4 per cent.
70.tq: Check both the unit and the direction of change; both are common numerical traps.

70.s: The ownership pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is:
o: 51 per cent Telangana Government and 49 per cent Government of India
49 per cent Telangana Government and 51 per cent private companies
51 per cent Government of India and 49 per cent Telangana Government
70.x: Singareni Collieries Company Limited is owned 51 per cent by Telangana and 49 per cent by the Government of India.
70.tq: Watch for reversal of majority and minority ownership shares.

70.s: The publication titled ‘Energy Statistics’ is brought out by the:
o: Coal Controller’s Organisation under the Ministry of Coal
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power
National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
70.x: Energy Statistics is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
70.tq: Identify the publishing authority and avoid swapping it with a sectoral regulator or ministry.

70.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Central Electricity Authority — technical planning and generation adequacy plans
2. CERC — central and inter-State electricity tariffs
3. APERC — State electricity tariffs
4. APTEL — appeals against CERC and SERC orders
70.x: All four pairs are correct. CEA performs technical planning, CERC and APERC deal with central/inter-State and State tariffs respectively, and APTEL hears relevant appeals.
70.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and distinguish central, State and appellate functions.

70.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: PNGRB — downstream oil and gas regulation
70.x: APGENCO is responsible for State electricity generation, not distribution. Distribution is performed by the DISCOMs, while APTRANSCO handles transmission.
70.tq: Find the swapped function among closely related State electricity institutions.

70.s: Electricity is included as Entry 38 in which list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution?
70.x: Electricity is Entry 38 of the Concurrent List, enabling both the Union and the States to legislate on the subject.
70.tq: Discriminate between the three legislative lists using the exact entry reference.

70.s: The Ministry of Power became an independent ministry with effect from:
70.x: The Ministry of Power became independent from 2 July 1992.
70.tq: Use the exact date and reject nearby decade-based distractors.

70.s:
The Electricity Act, 2003 replaced which of the following enactments?
1. Indian Electricity Act, 1910
2. Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948
3. Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: The Electricity Act, 2003 replaced all three enactments: the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 and the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.
70.tq: Check the complete statutory replacement list rather than selecting only the most familiar enactment.

70.s: Which one of the following features is associated with the Electricity Act, 2003?
o: Tariff determination exclusively by State Governments
Allocation of all power projects through administrative nomination
Elimination of open access to electricity networks
Provision for open access and tariff regulation by Electricity Regulatory Commissions
70.x: The Electricity Act, 2003 introduced open access and provided for tariff regulation by Electricity Regulatory Commissions.
70.tq: Identify the institutional and structural features directly associated with the legislation.

70.s: Under which Section of the Electricity Act, 2003 are tariffs determined through competitive bidding?
70.x: Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides for adoption of tariff determined through a transparent process of bidding in accordance with guidelines issued by the Central Government.
70.tq: Use the article-or-section number directly, with nearby statutory provisions as distractors.

70.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (Scheme)
a. DDUGJY
b. UDAY
c. Saubhagya
d. RDSS

List-II (Objective)
i. Household electrification
ii. Reduction of AT&C losses and smart metering
iii. Rural feeder separation
iv. Turnaround of DISCOMs

Which of the following is the correct code?
70.x: DDUGJY is associated with rural feeder separation, UDAY with DISCOM turnaround, Saubhagya with household electrification, and RDSS with reducing AT&C losses and smart metering.
70.tq: Start from the sure scheme-objective pair and eliminate codes containing mismatched objectives.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding UDAY:
1. It was launched in 2015.
2. It aimed at the turnaround of DISCOMs.
3. States were to take over 75% of DISCOM debt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: UDAY was launched in 2015 for DISCOM turnaround, with States taking over 75% of the debt of DISCOMs.
70.tq: Verify the year, objective and distinctive numerical feature together.

70.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the primary objective of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), launched in 2021?
o: Takeover of 75% of DISCOM debt by States
Rural feeder separation and agricultural feeder creation
Reduction of AT&C losses along with smart metering
70.x: RDSS, launched in 2021, focuses on reducing aggregate technical and commercial losses and promoting smart metering.
70.tq: Discriminate between closely related electricity-distribution schemes by their distinctive objectives.

70.s: An amount of ₹15,083.14 crore under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme is associated with which State?
70.x: Andhra Pradesh is associated with ₹15,083.14 crore under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme.
70.tq: Link the exact financial allocation with the State named in the policy data.

70.s: The aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses changed from 22.62% in FY14 to which level in FY25?
70.x: AT&C losses declined from 22.62% in FY14 to 15.04% in FY25.
70.tq: Test the direction and exact end value of a reported time-series change.

70.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the change in India's electricity demand-supply gap mentioned for FY14 to November 2025?
70.x: The demand-supply gap declined from 4.2% to zero by November 2025. The figures 22.62% and 15.04% relate to AT&C losses.
70.tq: Separate two pairs of numerical indicators and identify the correct trend.

70.s: India imports approximately what proportion of its petroleum and natural gas requirements, respectively?
70.x: India imports about 80% of its petroleum and about 25% of its natural gas requirements.
70.tq: Avoid reversing the two percentages when testing a paired import dependence figure.

70.s: Which of the following is the correct set of locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs)?
70.x: The Strategic Petroleum Reserves mentioned are located at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.
70.tq: Test a named-location list as a complete set and reject location substitutions.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves:
1. They provide about 9.5 days of cover.
2. The International Energy Agency norm is 90 days of cover.
3. India's existing cover is substantially lower than the IEA norm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: India's SPRs provide about 9.5 days of cover, whereas the IEA norm is 90 days; therefore, India's cover is substantially lower than the norm.
70.tq: Combine exact figures with the comparison they establish.

70.s:
Arrange the following developments in the chronological order of petroleum-price decontrol in India:
A. Decontrol of diesel prices
B. Decontrol of petrol prices

Select the correct answer.
70.x: Petrol prices were decontrolled in 2010, followed by diesel prices in 2014.
70.tq: Identify the earlier year first and then place the later reform.

70.s: Which one of the following combinations is associated with efforts to boost domestic energy supply?
o: SPRs, IEA norm and petrol decontrol
RDSS, open access and tariff regulation
70.x: HELP, OALP and coal gasification are identified as measures to boost domestic energy supply.
70.tq: Distinguish supply-enhancing exploration and fuel measures from distribution reforms.

70.s: India recorded a peak power demand of 270.82 GW on which date?
70.x: The record peak power demand of 270.82 GW was recorded on 21 May 2026.
70.tq: Match the exact peak-demand figure with its date rather than the date of a related report.

70.s:
Assertion (A): El Nino poses a risk to India's wind and hydropower generation.
Reason (R): Wind and hydropower generation are among the energy sectors identified as vulnerable to El Nino conditions.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
70.x: Both statements are true, and the identified vulnerability of wind and hydropower generation explains why El Nino is considered a risk to them.
70.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the stated climate-related energy risk.

70.s: With reference to battery storage in the power sector, which one of the following is correct?
o: India had 500 GWh of battery storage in September 2025, whereas 336 MWh is needed by 2029-30.
India had no identified battery-storage requirement for 2029-30.
India had 336 GWh of battery storage in September 2025 against a requirement of 500 MWh by 2029-30.
India had only 500 MWh of battery storage in September 2025, whereas 336 GWh is needed by 2029-30.
70.x: The reported position was only 500 MWh of battery storage in September 2025 against an estimated requirement of 336 GWh by 2029-30.
70.tq: Keep the units and scale of present capacity and future requirement aligned.

70.s: Andhra Pradesh's electricity demand is projected to grow at what compound annual growth rate (CAGR)?
70.x: Andhra Pradesh's electricity demand is projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.90%.
70.tq: Select the exact projected rate while separating it from other energy-sector percentages.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's coal-power procurement:
1. APERC approved 1,600 MW of coal power.
2. The approval was through Section 63 DBFOO bidding.
3. It forms the first phase of a planned 5,588 MW capacity by 2035-36.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: APERC approved 1,600 MW through Section 63 DBFOO bidding, constituting the first phase of a 5,588 MW plan by 2035-36.
70.tq: Combine the approving authority, procurement route and capacity phases in one policy question.

71.s: Which one of the following combinations best describes the principal characteristics of India's balance of payments crisis in 1991?
o: Stable prices, rising gold reserves and a balanced budget
Low inflation, high foreign exchange reserves and a fiscal surplus
High exports, falling public debt and a current account surplus
High inflation, low foreign exchange reserves and a large fiscal deficit
71.x: The 1991 crisis was characterised by high inflation, critically low foreign exchange reserves and a large fiscal deficit.
71.tq: Identify the three-part crisis profile rather than focusing on one indicator.

71.s: The foreign exchange reserves of India in June 1991 were approximately
o: $975 million, sufficient for about two weeks of imports
$69.3 billion, sufficient for about one year of imports
$22.8 billion, sufficient for about three months of imports
$9.75 billion, sufficient for about six months of imports
71.x: India's foreign exchange reserves stood at approximately $975 million in June 1991, covering only about two weeks of imports.
71.tq: Match the crisis-year figure with its associated coverage period.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's macroeconomic position during 1990-91 and 1991:
1. Inflation was approximately 12 per cent.
2. The current account deficit was around 3.1–3.2 per cent of GDP.
3. The trade deficit was ₹10,644 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Inflation was about 12 per cent, the current account deficit was 3.1–3.2 per cent of GDP, and the trade deficit was ₹10,644 crore, equivalent to about 3.2 per cent of GDP.
71.tq: Check each numerical indicator independently before selecting the coded combination.

71.s: The gross fiscal deficit of the Centre in 1990-91 was approximately
71.x: The Centre's gross fiscal deficit was 8.4 per cent of GDP in 1990-91, compared with 6.1 per cent in 1980-81. The 9.4 per cent figure refers to the combined Centre and States figure.
71.tq: Distinguish the Centre-only figure from the combined Centre and States figure.

71.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the change in India's internal government debt between 1980-81 and 1990-91?
o: It increased from 35 per cent to 53 per cent of GDP.
It declined from 53 per cent to 35 per cent of GDP.
It increased from 22.8 per cent to 69.3 per cent of GDP.
It remained unchanged at 35 per cent of GDP.
71.x: Internal government debt rose from 35 per cent of GDP in 1980-81 to 53 per cent in 1990-91.
71.tq: Read the direction of change before comparing the two dates.

71.s: India's GDP growth during the crisis period was approximately
o: 1.1 per cent in 1990-91 and 7–8 per cent in 1991-92
1.1 per cent in 1990-91 and below 1 per cent in 1991-92
7–8 per cent in 1990-91 and 3.5 per cent in 1991-92
3.5 per cent in 1990-91 and 1.3 per cent in 1991-92
71.x: GDP growth was about 1.1 per cent in 1990-91 and fell below 1 per cent in 1991-92. Another estimate places 1991 growth at about 1.3 per cent.
71.tq: Use the crisis-period sequence and reject the normal-growth figures.

71.s:
Which of the following factors contributed to India's balance of payments crisis in 1991?
1. The Gulf War led to a doubling of oil prices.
2. Remittances from the Gulf region dried up.
3. Non-Resident Indians withdrew their deposits.
4. Current account deficits had been financed through foreign borrowing since the 1980s.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: All four factors contributed to the crisis: the Gulf War increased oil prices, Gulf remittances declined, NRIs withdrew deposits and earlier current account deficits had been financed by foreign borrowing.
71.tq: Recognise a cumulative crisis caused by several mutually reinforcing factors.

71.s: The political event that intensified the balance of payments crisis in 1991 was the
o: formation of the first coalition government in 1989
fall of the Chandra Shekhar government
71.x: Political instability, including the fall of the Chandra Shekhar government, aggravated the economic crisis.
71.tq: Link the political trigger with the economic event without confusing it with a policy reform.

71.s: In response to the 1991 foreign exchange crisis, India pledged approximately how much gold to the Bank of England and UBS?
71.x: India pledged 67 tonnes of gold to the Bank of England and UBS as an emergency measure to raise foreign exchange.
71.tq: Recall the distinctive emergency quantity associated with gold pledging.

71.s: The two-step devaluation of the Indian rupee in July 1991 took place on
71.x: The rupee was devalued in two steps on 1 July and 3 July 1991, by approximately 20 per cent in total.
71.tq: Test the close date pair rather than the broader year alone.

71.s: The IMF assistance obtained during the 1991 crisis was associated with
o: a ban on all imports for five years
unconditional cancellation of India's external debt
71.x: The IMF loan was accompanied by conditionalities. The bailout is placed at approximately $7 billion in the cited estimate.
71.tq: Apply the standard IMF-loan and conditionality relationship.

71.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship among liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation in the context of the 1991 reforms?
o: Liberalisation and privatisation were strategies, while globalisation was the outcome.
All three were merely fiscal instruments.
Globalisation was restricted to public-sector disinvestment.
Liberalisation and privatisation were outcomes, while globalisation was a strategy.
71.x: Liberalisation and privatisation were reform strategies, while globalisation represented the resulting integration of the Indian economy with the world economy.
71.tq: Separate the two reform strategies from the broader outcome.

71.s: Which one of the following was a measure of liberalisation under the 1991 reforms?
o: Compulsory licensing of all private industries
Abolition of industrial licensing except for a few industries
Reservation of all industries for the public sector
71.x: Industrial licensing was abolished for all but a few industries as part of liberalisation.
71.tq: Identify the reform measure by its removal of a prior control.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about liberalisation measures:
1. MRTP asset limits were scrapped.
2. Interest rates were deregulated.
3. Private banks such as HDFC and ICICI were allowed in the reform framework.
4. Tax rates were increased while the tax base was narrowed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: MRTP asset limits were scrapped, interest rates were deregulated, and private banks such as HDFC and ICICI were allowed. Tax rates were cut and the tax base was widened, so statement 4 is false.
71.tq: Find the reversed tax-reform statement among otherwise correct liberalisation measures.

71.s: The Narasimham Committee was associated with which of the following reform measures?
o: Permission for private banks and deregulation of interest rates
Introduction of gold pledging to the Bank of England
Creation of the National Single Window System
71.x: The Narasimham Committee was associated with banking-sector reforms, including interest-rate deregulation and the entry of private banks such as HDFC and ICICI.
71.tq: Match the committee with its sector-specific reform recommendation.

71.s: The Chelliah Committee was associated with
o: gold imports and foreign exchange reserves
tax-rate reduction and widening of the tax base
industrial licensing and MRTP asset limits
71.x: The Chelliah Committee was associated with tax reforms involving lower tax rates and a wider tax base.
71.tq: Use the committee-measure association to distinguish tax reform from banking reform.

71.s: The Securities and Exchange Board of India became a statutory body in
71.x: SEBI was given statutory status in 1992 as part of the financial-market reform process.
71.tq: Distinguish the statutory-status year from the nearby reform years.

71.s: Which of the following correctly describes privatisation under the 1991 reform programme?
o: Restriction of all public-sector enterprises to small-scale industries
Nationalisation of private companies and abolition of public enterprises
Disinvestment of public-sector equity and greater autonomy through Navratna and Maharatna status
Replacement of public enterprises by foreign governments
71.x: Privatisation involved disinvestment of PSU equity and later attempts to improve efficiency through greater autonomy, including Navratna and Maharatna status.
71.tq: Combine the ownership and autonomy dimensions of privatisation.

71.s: Initially, disinvestment of public-sector equity was undertaken primarily to
71.x: The initial purpose of disinvestment was to help bridge the fiscal deficit; efficiency became an increasingly important objective later.
71.tq: Distinguish the initial fiscal objective from the later efficiency objective.

71.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the globalisation pillar of the 1991 reforms?
o: Export promotion — expansion of quantitative restrictions
Fixed exchange rate — replacement of all tariffs by quotas
FERA — abolition of foreign exchange regulation in 1991
71.x: Globalisation involved a shift from import substitution towards export promotion. Quantitative restrictions and EXIM scrips were abolished, and FERA was replaced by FEMA in 1999.
71.tq: Identify the reform direction by spotting the shift from inward orientation to export promotion.

71.s: The market-determined exchange rate was introduced in India in
71.x: The exchange rate became market-determined in 1993 as part of the external-sector reforms.
71.tq: Separate the exchange-rate reform year from the year of FEMA enactment.

71.s: FERA was replaced by FEMA in
71.x: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, or FERA, was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act, or FEMA, in 1999.
71.tq: Discriminate between two similar foreign-exchange laws and their year of transition.

71.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the 1991 New Economic Policy?
71.x: Nationalisation was not a feature of the 1991 New Economic Policy. The policy instead promoted delicensing, disinvestment and greater foreign investment.
71.tq: Find the measure that reverses the reform direction.

71.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the 1991 New Economic Policy is correct?
1. Full capital-account convertibility was not adopted.
2. Demonetisation formed part of the 1991 reform package.
3. Foreign direct investment was liberalised through an automatic route in high-priority industries.
4. Devaluation, tariff cuts and removal of import quotas were included among the external-sector measures.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: Full capital-account convertibility and demonetisation were not part of the 1991 package. FDI liberalisation, devaluation, tariff cuts and removal of import quotas were reform measures.
71.tq: Reject the famous-word traps and retain the measures that match the 1991 reform direction.

71.s: Under the 1991 reform framework, FDI through the automatic route was permitted up to 100 per cent in
o: all activities without any sectoral distinction
71.x: The 1991 policy permitted up to 100 per cent FDI through the automatic route in high-priority industries, subject to the applicable policy framework.
71.tq: Avoid converting a sector-specific permission into an unrestricted one.

71.s: Which of the following statements about India's present FDI framework is correct?
o: The FIPB continues to grant all FDI approvals.
It follows a negative-list approach, with up to 100 per cent automatic-route FDI in most sectors subject to policy conditions.
It follows a positive-list approach and prohibits automatic-route investment.
The National Single Window System began in 2017.
71.x: The present framework follows a negative-list approach, permitting up to 100 per cent FDI through the automatic route in most sectors subject to conditions. FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and the National Single Window System has operated since August 2022.
71.tq: Test current institutional arrangements by checking the authority and dates.

71.s: The FIPB was abolished in
71.x: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board was abolished in June 2017, after which approvals were handled through the concerned ministries and departments.
71.tq: Distinguish the institutional-change year from the later single-window year.

71.s: The National Single Window System for FDI-related approvals has been in operation since
71.x: The National Single Window System has been in operation since August 2022 for facilitating approvals through the relevant ministries and departments.
71.tq: Use the precise month and year to separate sequential institutional reforms.

71.s: Which of the following best defines globalisation in the economic context?
o: Replacement of domestic savings by government borrowing alone
Expansion of state control over domestic production and foreign trade
Reduction of all foreign trade to protect domestic industries
Integration of the domestic economy with the world through flows of trade, capital, technology and labour
71.x: Globalisation involves integration with the world economy through trade, capital, technology and labour flows. Greater state control or reduced foreign trade is contrary to this meaning.
71.tq: Select the comprehensive definition and reject its opposite.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the impact of globalisation on India:
1. Trade in goods and services expanded.
2. Access to foreign technology increased.
3. Imports grew faster than exports.
4. Exports grew faster than imports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Globalisation expanded trade and access to foreign technology, but imports grew faster than exports. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
71.tq: Catch the reversed comparison between export and import growth.

71.s: India's share of world trade declined from approximately what level in 1950 to what level in 1995?
71.x: India's share of world trade declined from 1.78 per cent in 1950 to 0.6 per cent in 1995.
71.tq: Keep the indicator and the direction of movement separate from the export-share figures.

71.s: India's share in world exports declined from approximately 2.2 per cent in 1948 to
71.x: India's share in world exports declined from 2.2 per cent in 1948 to 0.5 per cent in 1983.
71.tq: Distinguish export-share figures from the broader world-trade-share figures.

71.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the movement of India's net FDI figures mentioned for the recent period?
o: $44.0 billion in 2020-21, below $1 billion in 2024-25 and $7.6 billion in 2025-26
Below $1 billion in 2020-21, $44.0 billion in 2024-25 and $7.6 billion in 2025-26
$7.6 billion in 2020-21, $44.0 billion in 2024-25 and below $1 billion in 2025-26
$44.0 billion in 2020-21, $7.6 billion in 2024-25 and below $1 billion in 2025-26
71.x: Net FDI fell from $44.0 billion in 2020-21 to below $1 billion in 2024-25, before recovering to $7.6 billion in 2025-26.
71.tq: Arrange the three dated figures in sequence before comparing the trend.

71.s: The gross FDI inflow figure reported for the recent period was approximately
71.x: The reported gross FDI inflow was $94.6 billion. This should not be confused with the net FDI figures of $44.0 billion, below $1 billion and $7.6 billion for the specified years.
71.tq: Distinguish gross inflow from net-flow figures appearing in the same context.

71.s: Which of the following explains the role of FDI in India's economy?
o: FDI eliminates the need for domestic savings altogether.
FDI necessarily reduces access to foreign technology.
Foreign savings can help fill the savings-investment gap when domestic savings are around 30 per cent of GDP.
FDI is unrelated to the savings-investment balance.
71.x: Foreign savings through FDI help fill the savings-investment gap; domestic savings are approximately 30 per cent of GDP. FDI also contributed to India's position as a major destination for investment.
71.tq: Apply the savings-investment relationship to the role of foreign capital.

71.s: The expansion of India's information-technology and outsourcing sector helped to
o: widen the current account deficit without any offsetting effect
71.x: The IT and outsourcing boom generated services exports and helped cushion India's current account deficit.
71.tq: Link the service-export boom with its balance of payments effect.

71.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the recent Global Capability Centre figures?
o: 1,800+ centres and $38.25 billion of services exports
1,800+ centres and $7.6 billion of services exports
100 centres and $94.6 billion of services exports
350 centres and $44.0 billion of services exports
71.x: More than 1,800 Global Capability Centres were associated with $38.25 billion of services exports in the cited 2026 figure.
71.tq: Start with the distinctive count and pair it with the corresponding export value.

71.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes India's growth and corporate internationalisation after the reforms?
o: Growth moved from the approximately 3.5 per cent 'Hindu rate' to around 7–8 per cent, while Indian MNCs expanded globally.
The reforms affected only agriculture and had no relation to corporate internationalisation.
Growth fell from 7–8 per cent to below 1 per cent as Indian MNCs disappeared.
Growth remained permanently at 3.5 per cent and Indian firms withdrew from international markets.
71.x: India's growth moved from the approximately 3.5 per cent 'Hindu rate' to around 7–8 per cent, and companies such as Tata, Reliance, Infosys and Sun Pharma became global.
71.tq: Combine the growth-rate transition with the concrete corporate examples.

71.s: Which of the following companies was NOT included among the examples of Indian multinational corporations that went global?
71.x: Tata, Reliance, Infosys and Sun Pharma were cited as Indian companies that went global. HDFC was mentioned in the context of private banking, not in this list.
71.tq: Use the list-membership test and distinguish a nearby but unrelated name.

71.s: Which adverse outcome was associated with the pattern of growth after economic reforms?
o: Growth became entirely dependent on public-sector employment.
Agriculture received all investment and labour-intensive sectors disappeared.
Capital-intensive sectors generated more jobs than the available labour force.
Agriculture was neglected and capital-intensive growth generated too few jobs.
71.x: The pattern of growth was criticised for neglecting agriculture and concentrating growth in capital-intensive sectors, which created too few employment opportunities.
71.tq: Identify the stated distributional and employment consequence rather than the aggregate growth benefit.

71.s: In July 1991, the Indian rupee was devalued in two stages by approximately what percentage?
71.x: The rupee was devalued in July 1991 in two steps by about 20 percent.
71.tq: Use the precise year, month and magnitude together to distinguish the reform measure.

71.s: The principal objectives of the July 1991 devaluation of the rupee were to
o: reduce agricultural employment and raise public expenditure
make imports cheaper and widen the trade deficit
make exports competitive and correct the balance of payments
71.x: The devaluation was intended to improve export competitiveness and correct the balance of payments position.
71.tq: Link the policy instrument with its stated economic objectives.

71.s:
With reference to the Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS), consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in March 1992.
2. Sixty percent of export earnings were converted at the market rate.
3. Forty percent of export earnings were converted at the official rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: LERMS was introduced in March 1992 with a dual exchange rate: 60 percent at the market rate and 40 percent at the official rate.
71.tq: Verify each numerical component of a policy arrangement before selecting the coded option.

71.s: India adopted a unified market-determined exchange rate under the exchange reforms from
71.x: The dual-rate LERMS arrangement was followed by a unified market-determined exchange rate from March 1993.
71.tq: Separate the dates of introduction, transition and unification in a reform sequence.

71.s: Which one of the following best describes the change in India's average import tariff from the late 1980s to the early 2000s?
o: It rose from about 30 percent to about 125 percent.
It fell from about 30 percent to about 10 percent.
It fell from about 125 percent to about 30 percent.
It remained unchanged at about 125 percent.
71.x: Average import tariffs declined from approximately 125 percent in the late 1980s to about 30 percent in the early 2000s.
71.tq: Read the direction and the two endpoint values together rather than reversing the comparison.

71.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the sequence concerning India's import regime after 1991?
1. Import licensing was dismantled.
2. Remaining quantitative restrictions were removed in April 2001.
3. General customs duty was later reduced to 10 percent.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: Import licensing was dismantled, the remaining quantitative restrictions were removed in April 2001, and general customs duty was later reduced to 10 percent.
71.tq: Combine related trade-policy changes while checking the date-specific statement separately.

71.s: The export-led growth strategy was introduced in India in 1991 as a shift from
71.x: The 1991 reforms introduced export-led growth, marking a movement from import substitution towards export promotion.
71.tq: Discriminate between the two commonly reversed development strategies.

71.s: Which one of the following statements regarding foreign investment and exchange reforms is correct?
o: FIIs were prohibited from investing in Indian stock markets.
Foreign investment was permitted only through a case-by-case official route.
NRIs and OCBs were permitted investment up to 100 percent under the stated arrangement.
71.x: The reform framework provided an automatic route for investment, allowed NRIs and OCBs up to 100 percent, and permitted FIIs to enter stock markets.
71.tq: Reject absolute statements and identify the precise investment-related permission.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The rupee became market-determined in 1993.
2. The current account became convertible in 1994.
3. The capital account became fully convertible at the same time.
