1. The SDR was created in 1969 under the IMF’s First Amendment.
2. The proposal for the SDR was agreed in 1967.
3. Originally, 35 SDRs were equivalent to one ounce of gold.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: All three statements are correct. The SDR was agreed in 1967, formally created in 1969 under the IMF’s First Amendment, and was originally valued at 35 SDRs per ounce of gold.
76.tq: Separate the agreement date from the formal creation date and retain the numerical conversion.

76.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the currencies in the SDR basket since 1 October 2016?
o: US dollar, euro, renminbi, yen and pound sterling
US dollar, euro, rupee, yen and Swiss franc
US dollar, pound sterling, rupee, franc and yen
Euro, renminbi, rupee, Australian dollar and yen
76.x: Since 1 October 2016, the SDR basket comprises the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling.
76.tq: Start with the sure currency pair and eliminate options containing currencies outside the stated basket.

76.s: The largest general allocation of SDRs, amounting to approximately SDR 456 billion or about US$650 billion, was made in:
76.x: The largest general SDR allocation was made in August 2021 and amounted to approximately SDR 456 billion, equivalent to about US$650 billion.
76.tq: Match the unusually large numerical allocation with its correct year.

76.s: The reserve tranche of an IMF member refers to:
o: The part of the member’s IMF quota paid in reserve assets and drawable without conditions
The portion of the IMF quota payable only in domestic currency
A compulsory gold loan extended by the member to other countries
The part of an SDR allocation that cannot be withdrawn
76.x: The reserve tranche is the portion of an IMF member’s quota paid in reserve assets, historically gold. It can be drawn at any time without conditions.
76.tq: Identify the correct IMF quota component by asking who can draw it and under what conditions.

76.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the transition from FERA to FEMA?
o: FERA 1969 was replaced by FEMA 2006, which came into force on 31 July 2006
FERA 1973 was replaced by FEMA 1997, which came into force on 1 April 1998
FERA 1999 was replaced by FEMA 1973, which came into force on 1 June 2000
FERA 1973 was replaced by FEMA 1999, which came into force on 1 June 2000
76.x: The restrictive Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, which came into force on 1 June 2000.
76.tq: Use the law-year and commencement-date pair together to avoid swapping the two statutes.

76.s: The proposal to replace FERA with a new foreign exchange management law was associated with which of the following?
76.x: The proposal for the new foreign exchange management framework was made in the 1997–98 Budget.
76.tq: Test the budget-year association directly, using nearby reform years as distractors.

76.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tarapore Committees:
1. The First Tarapore Committee was constituted in 1997.
2. The Second Tarapore Committee was set up in March 2006.
3. The Second Committee reported on 31 July 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: All three statements are correct. The Tarapore Committees of 1997 and 2006 prepared roadmaps towards full capital account convertibility; the second committee reported on 31 July 2006.
76.tq: Check both the committee year and the distinct constitution and reporting dates.

76.s: The Tarapore Committees were primarily associated with the roadmap towards:
76.x: The First and Second Tarapore Committees were associated with preparing a roadmap towards full capital account convertibility.
76.tq: Match the named committee with its specific policy objective rather than a broader exchange-policy term.

76.s: Which of the following correctly states India’s position regarding rupee convertibility?
o: The rupee has full current account convertibility but only partial capital account convertibility
The rupee has neither current account nor capital account convertibility
The rupee has full capital account convertibility but partial current account convertibility
The rupee has full convertibility on both current and capital accounts
76.x: India has full current account convertibility, whereas capital account convertibility remains partial.
76.tq: Keep current-account and capital-account convertibility separate; the comparison is the key discriminator.

76.s: The base year used for the Reserve Bank of India’s NEER index is:
76.x: The NEER index uses 2015–16 as its base year, represented as 100.
76.tq: Identify the exact base-year figure instead of confusing it with earlier economic-series base years.

76.s:
With reference to the Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER), consider the following statements:
1. It is a trade-weighted average of the rupee against partner currencies.
2. A rise in NEER indicates appreciation of the rupee.
3. A rise in NEER generally makes imports cheaper and exports less competitive.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: All three statements are correct. NEER is trade-weighted, and its rise indicates rupee appreciation, which tends to reduce import costs but makes Indian exports less competitive.
76.tq: Trace the direction of appreciation through both import prices and export competitiveness.

76.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes REER from NEER?
o: NEER measures inflation while REER measures the fiscal deficit
REER is NEER adjusted for relative inflation
REER is NEER adjusted only for gold holdings
NEER is REER adjusted for reserve-tranche drawings
76.x: REER is obtained by adjusting NEER for relative inflation. It is considered a better indicator of external competitiveness, while a high REER suggests an overvalued rupee.
76.tq: Discriminate between the nominal index and its inflation-adjusted counterpart.

76.s: A high REER is generally interpreted as indicating that the rupee is:
o: Convertible only on the capital account
Fixed permanently to the US dollar
76.x: A high REER generally indicates an overvalued rupee. Since REER incorporates relative inflation, it is a better indicator of competitiveness than NEER alone.
76.tq: Apply the index interpretation to the policy meaning of an overvalued currency.

76.s: The Reserve Bank of India publishes trade-weighted NEER and REER indices based on:
76.x: The RBI publishes trade-weighted indices based on 40-currency and 6-currency baskets.
76.tq: Retain both components of the paired numerical fact instead of selecting a familiar-looking single basket.

76.s: During the rupee movement described for 2026, the rupee remained around which range against the US dollar, in the context of the West Asia crude shock and FPI selling?
76.x: The rupee was reported around ₹95–96 per US dollar through 2026 amid the West Asia crude shock and foreign portfolio investor selling.
76.tq: Link the exchange-rate range with the stated contemporaneous causes rather than using a historical rupee level.

76.s: In response to the rupee slide in 2026, which combination of measures was associated with the Reserve Bank of India’s approach?
o: Repo-rate reduction, gold sales and abolition of FCNR(B) deposits
Swaps, FCNR(B) measures and retention of the repo rate at 5.25% for the fourth straight meeting
Capital controls, SDR cancellation and a fixed dollar peg
Complete capital account convertibility and withdrawal from the foreign exchange market
76.x: The RBI leaned on swaps and FCNR(B) measures while keeping the repo rate at 5.25% for the fourth straight meeting in August 2026.
76.tq: Combine the policy instrument, deposit measure and unchanged rate to identify the complete response.

76.s: The first INR drawdown under the SAARC framework was made by:
76.x: The first INR drawdown under the SAARC framework was made by the Maldives in April 2026.
76.tq: Use the first-event and country-date combination as a three-part recall test.

76.s: According to the stated September 2026 position, India’s foreign exchange reserves were approximately:
76.x: India’s reserves were reported at US$785.71 billion, making India the fourth-largest holder according to the stated September 2026 position.
76.tq: Match the exact reserve figure with its corresponding global rank.

76.s: Deliberate undervaluation of a currency, as alleged in the case of China, is criticised as:
76.x: Deliberate undervaluation of a currency to gain trade advantages is criticised as currency manipulation.
76.tq: Match the policy criticism with the precise international-exchange term.

76.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Introduction of full current account convertibility in India
B. First Tarapore Committee
C. FEMA coming into force
D. Introduction of the rupee symbol
76.x: The correct sequence is full current account convertibility in 1994, the First Tarapore Committee in 1997, FEMA coming into force in 2000, and the rupee symbol in 2010.
76.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate reform milestones.

77.s: The Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) rests on which of the following three pillars?
o: Domestic support, market access and export competition
Market access, investment protection and government procurement
Export competition, services and industrial subsidies
Domestic support, intellectual property and trade facilitation
77.x: The AoA has three pillars: domestic support, market access and export competition.
77.tq: Identify the standard three-part structure of the agreement.

77.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with Blue Box support under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Research expenditure with no production connection
Direct payments linked to unlimited expansion of production
All subsidies prohibited under the SCM Agreement
77.x: Blue Box support consists of direct payments connected with production-limiting programmes. Although trade-distorting, such support is exempt from reduction commitments.
77.tq: Distinguish the production-limiting feature of the Blue Box from Green and Amber categories.

77.s: With reference to Amber Box subsidies, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They are direct payments that limit production and are exempt from all reductions.
They include price- or quantity-linked support such as MSP and input subsidies, measured through AMS.
They are support measures unrelated to prices or quantities and therefore have no limits.
They refer only to export subsidies paid to least developed countries.
77.x: Amber Box support covers price- or quantity-linked measures, including MSP, power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation subsidies. Such support is trade-distorting and is measured as Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS).
77.tq: Use the examples of price and input support to identify the Amber Box.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT an official subsidy box under the Agreement on Agriculture?
77.x: Green, Blue and Amber are the subsidy boxes under the AoA. Red, Orange and Yellow are not AoA boxes; a prohibited-subsidy category described as a red-light category belongs to the SCM context.
77.tq: Find the odd term in a closely related list of official categories.

77.s: The de minimis limit for Amber Box support is generally what percentage of the value of agricultural output for developing countries?
77.x: Developing countries are allowed Amber support up to 10 per cent of the value of agricultural output under the de minimis provision.
77.tq: Recall the country-category distinction in a percentage-based provision.

77.s: The de minimis limit for Amber Box support applicable to developed countries is:
77.x: For developed countries, Amber support within 5 per cent of the value of agricultural output is allowed without penalty under the de minimis provision.
77.tq: Compare the two country-specific thresholds rather than reversing them.

77.s: Under the market-access commitments of the Agreement on Agriculture, developed countries were required to reduce tariffs by 36 per cent over six years, whereas developing countries were required to reduce them by:
77.x: The specified commitment for developing countries was a 24 per cent tariff reduction over ten years, compared with 36 per cent over six years for developed countries.
77.tq: Match both the percentage and time period instead of relying on one figure alone.

77.s: The conversion of non-tariff agricultural barriers into tariffs under the Agreement on Agriculture is known as:
77.x: Tariffication means converting non-tariff barriers into tariff equivalents as part of the market-access commitments.
77.tq: Identify the exact technical term for a policy process.

77.s: The highest decision-making body of the World Trade Organization is required to meet:
o: Only when requested by the Director-General
At least once every two years
77.x: The WTO Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body and meets at least once every two years under the Marrakesh Agreement.
77.tq: Recall the institutional hierarchy and minimum meeting frequency.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding WTO Ministerial Conferences:

List-I (Conference)
a. First Ministerial Conference
b. Second Ministerial Conference
c. Third Ministerial Conference
d. Fourth Ministerial Conference

List-II (Venue and year)
i. Seattle, 1999
ii. Singapore, 1996
iii. Doha, 2001
iv. Geneva, 1998

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
77.x: MC1 was held at Singapore in 1996, MC2 at Geneva in 1998, MC3 at Seattle in 1999 and MC4 at Doha in 2001.
77.tq: Start from the sure venue-year pair and eliminate codes.

77.s: Which of the following was associated with the First WTO Ministerial Conference held at Singapore in 1996?
o: The adoption of the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
The launch of the Doha Development Agenda
The Singapore issues and the Information Technology Agreement
The beginning of the e-commerce customs-duty moratorium
77.x: The Singapore Ministerial Conference introduced the Singapore issues—investment, competition, procurement transparency and trade facilitation—and was associated with the Information Technology Agreement.
77.tq: Link a conference with its distinctive outcome rather than its venue alone.

77.s: The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium was begun at which WTO Ministerial Conference?
77.x: The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium began at the Second Ministerial Conference in Geneva in 1998.
77.tq: Discriminate between successive early Ministerial Conferences using their outcomes.

77.s: The Third WTO Ministerial Conference at Seattle in 1999 is remembered chiefly because it:
77.x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 collapsed amid protests.
77.tq: Associate a highly distinctive event with the correct conference.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Fourth WTO Ministerial Conference held at Doha in 2001?
o: The Bali Package and interim Peace Clause were adopted.
The e-commerce moratorium was begun and the Singapore issues were introduced.
The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted.
The Doha Development Agenda was launched and a TRIPS-public health declaration was adopted.
77.x: The Doha Conference launched the Doha Development Agenda and adopted the declaration concerning TRIPS and public health.
77.tq: Use the conference’s signature agenda and declaration to identify the correct option.

77.s: The Fifth WTO Ministerial Conference at Cancun in 2003 ended with which of the following developments?
o: It collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues, and the G-33 was formed.
It adopted the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS-public health declaration.
It adopted the COVID-related TRIPS waiver.
77.x: The Cancun Ministerial Conference collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues, and the G-33 was formed in that context.
77.tq: Avoid confusing the Cancun outcome with the outcomes of Doha and Nairobi.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sixth WTO Ministerial Conference at Hong Kong in 2005:
1. It included a commitment to end farm export subsidies.
2. It addressed duty-free and quota-free access for least developed countries.
3. It adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The Hong Kong Ministerial Conference dealt with ending farm export subsidies and duty-free, quota-free access for LDCs. The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement was adopted much later at MC12 in 2022.
77.tq: Reject the later-outcome trap by placing each development in its conference year.

77.s: The WTO Ministerial Conferences held at Geneva in 2009 and 2011 were principally associated with:
o: The launch of the Doha Development Agenda
The first adoption of the Singapore issues
77.x: MC7 in 2009 and MC8 in 2011, both held at Geneva, were primarily stock-taking conferences.
77.tq: Identify the common outcome of a paired conference entry.

77.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MC9 — Bali — Trade Facilitation Agreement and interim Peace Clause on food stockholding
MC11 — Buenos Aires — Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
MC12 — Geneva — Elimination of agricultural export subsidies
77.x: The Bali Ministerial Conference of 2013 produced the Bali Package, including the Trade Facilitation Agreement and an interim Peace Clause on food stockholding.
77.tq: Match the conference with its characteristic package while rejecting swapped outcomes.

77.s: The elimination of agricultural export subsidies was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference held at:
77.x: The Nairobi Ministerial Conference of 2015 adopted the outcome concerning elimination of agricultural export subsidies.
77.tq: Use the distinctive agricultural outcome to identify the correct conference.

77.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Eleventh WTO Ministerial Conference held at Buenos Aires in 2017?
o: It adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and the COVID TRIPS waiver.
It extended the e-commerce moratorium to March 2026.
It produced no ministerial declaration and included a fisheries work programme.
It adopted a ministerial declaration and a permanent solution on public stockholding.
77.x: MC11 at Buenos Aires produced no ministerial declaration but included work on fisheries.
77.tq: Distinguish an absence of declaration from formal agreements at later conferences.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the Twelfth WTO Ministerial Conference held at Geneva in June 2022:
1. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted.
2. A COVID-related TRIPS waiver was adopted.
3. The e-commerce customs-duty moratorium was permanently abolished.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: MC12 adopted the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies and a COVID-related TRIPS waiver. The e-commerce moratorium was extended, not permanently abolished, so statement 3 is false.
77.tq: Find the false later-development statement by separating extension from abolition.

77.s: At the Thirteenth WTO Ministerial Conference in Abu Dhabi in 2024, which of the following was the relevant outcome concerning the e-commerce moratorium and public stockholding?
o: The moratorium was extended to 31 March 2026, while no solution was reached on public stockholding.
The moratorium lapsed immediately and a permanent public-stockholding solution was adopted.
The moratorium was extended to 2030 and fisheries negotiations were concluded.
Both the moratorium and public-stockholding issue were permanently settled.
77.x: MC13 extended the e-commerce moratorium to 31 March 2026 but did not produce a solution on public stockholding.
77.tq: Compare two simultaneous outcomes instead of treating the conference as wholly successful or unsuccessful.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fourteenth WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in March 2026:
1. It produced only a draft ‘Yaounde package’ and no ministerial declaration.
2. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026.
3. Sixty-six members signed a separate E-Commerce Agreement barring duties on digital trade.
4. A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: MC14 produced no ministerial declaration, the e-commerce moratorium lapsed, and 66 members signed a separate agreement barring duties on digital trade. The permanent public-stockholding solution remained deadlocked, so statement 4 is false.
77.tq: Check each conference outcome separately and reject the over-claim of a settlement.

77.s: Which one of the following developments was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in 2026?
o: India blocked the addition of the Investment Facilitation for Development plurilateral agreement to Annex 4.
India proposed making the e-commerce moratorium permanent without opposition.
The Doha Development Agenda was launched.
The fisheries Phase 2 negotiations were concluded.
77.x: At MC14, India blocked addition of the IFD plurilateral agreement to Annex 4, although it had the backing of 129 of 166 members. Fisheries Phase 2 was deferred.
77.tq: Identify the relevant negotiating position while rejecting outcomes belonging to earlier conferences.

77.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade is correct?
o: It was created by the Doha Ministerial Conference in 2001.
It ceased to have any relevance after the establishment of the WTO.
It was signed in 1947 and came into force in 1948 with 23 countries.
It was signed in 1948 and came into force in 1995 with 166 countries.
77.x: GATT was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948 with 23 countries. GATT continues as part of the WTO agreements even after 1995.
77.tq: Separate the founding history of GATT from the later establishment of WTO.

77.s: The Uruguay Round of multilateral trade negotiations is correctly described as the:
o: Sixth round, held from 1973 to 1979 with 23 contracting parties
Seventh round, held from 1980 to 1985 with 92 contracting parties
Eighth round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993 with 123 contracting parties
Ninth round, launched at Marrakesh in 1994 with 166 contracting parties
77.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993, with 123 contracting parties.
77.tq: Verify round number, dates, venue and participation together.

77.s: Which of the following was NOT among the stated aims or areas of the Uruguay Round?
o: Coverage of investment and intellectual property rights
Establishment of a worldwide common currency
77.x: The Uruguay Round aimed to reduce farm subsidies, open services and cover investment and intellectual property rights. Establishment of a common currency was not its aim.
77.tq: Eliminate the unrelated policy objective from a list of negotiation aims.

77.s: The Dunkel Draft consisted principally of:
o: A schedule of tariff concessions adopted at Nairobi in 2015
Proposals by Arthur Dunkel for the Uruguay Round multilateral trade agreements
A declaration on fisheries subsidies adopted at Geneva in 2022
A treaty establishing the International Monetary Fund
77.x: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals made by Arthur Dunkel, the GATT Director-General and Chair of the Trade Negotiations Committee, for the Uruguay Round agreements.
77.tq: Link a named document with its author and negotiation context.

77.s: The Marrakesh Agreement of April 1994 resulted in which of the following?
o: Launch of the Doha Development Agenda in 2001
Creation of the WTO on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT system while retaining GATT as part of the WTO agreements
Creation of GATT in 1947 with 23 founding countries
Adoption of the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in 2022
77.x: The Marrakesh Agreement created the WTO, which began functioning on 1 January 1995. GATT continued as part of the WTO agreements rather than disappearing entirely.
77.tq: Distinguish institutional replacement from complete legal disappearance.

77.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the World Trade Organization?
o: Headquarters — New York; Director-General — Arthur Dunkel
Headquarters — Washington, D.C.; Director-General — Pascal Lamy
77.x: The WTO headquarters is in Geneva and its Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.
77.tq: Match the institution with its headquarters and current head without swapping officials.

77.s: India’s status in relation to GATT and the WTO is correctly stated as follows:
o: India was a founding member of GATT but joined the WTO only after the Doha Round.
India was a founding member of GATT and became a founding member of the WTO.
India was not a member of GATT but became a founding member of the WTO.
India joined GATT after 1995 but was a founding member of the WTO.
77.x: India was a founding member of both GATT and the WTO.
77.tq: Test membership in both predecessor and successor institutions together.

77.s: The WTO is commonly described as the third pillar of the world economy along with:
o: The IMF and the World Bank
77.x: The WTO is described as the third pillar of the world economy, alongside the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
77.tq: Recall the standard institutional trio.

77.s: A country grants an advantage in customs treatment to one WTO trading partner. Under the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, it must generally:
o: Apply the advantage only to domestic producers
Extend the same advantage to other WTO trading partners
Extend the advantage only to countries with which it has a customs union
Withdraw the advantage from all trading partners
77.x: MFN requires non-discrimination among trading partners, so an advantage granted to one partner should generally be extended to other WTO trading partners, subject to permitted exceptions.
77.tq: Apply the non-discrimination principle to a trade-policy situation.

77.s: Which situation best illustrates the national-treatment principle under WTO rules?
o: A country gives an export subsidy to domestic firms.
A country grants the same tariff concession to every foreign trading partner.
An imported product, after entering the domestic market, is treated like a similar domestic product for internal taxation and regulation.
A country imposes a quantitative restriction on all imports.
77.x: National treatment requires imported goods to be treated like domestic goods once they have entered the market, particularly in internal taxation and regulation. Equal treatment among foreign trading partners is the MFN principle.
77.tq: Separate national treatment from MFN by focusing on the point after importation.

77.s: According to the WTO Global Trade Outlook of April 2025, India ranked what position in merchandise exports and had what share?
77.x: India was ranked 18th in merchandise exports with a 1.8 per cent share according to the cited WTO Global Trade Outlook data.
77.tq: Match the rank and percentage as a single statistical pair.

77.s:
With reference to public stockholding for food security in the WTO, consider the following statements:
1. The Bali Ministerial Conference of 2013 provided interim protection under a Peace Clause.
2. The Peace Clause prevents legal challenges even when food-security procurement exceeds the limits prescribed under the Agreement on Agriculture.
3. India is seeking a permanent solution to the issue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All three statements are correct. The Bali Peace Clause provides interim protection, while India seeks a permanent solution for its food-security procurement programmes.
77.tq: Combine three related features of a WTO arrangement and identify the option containing all correct statements.

77.s: Why does India's public stockholding issue under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture involve an outdated reference price?
o: Because the reference price is fixed by the World Bank every five years
Because MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is calculated using a historical reference price
Because the reference price excludes all procurement by government agencies
Because the reference price is based on the international price of food imports in 2013
77.x: India argues that MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is treated as an Amber Box subsidy using an outdated historical reference price.
77.tq: Test the precise technical detail behind a current policy controversy rather than its general description.

77.s: The negotiations on a permanent solution to the WTO public stockholding issue remained deadlocked at which Ministerial Conference?
77.x: The negotiations on a permanent solution to public stockholding remained deadlocked at the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference.
77.tq: Use the conference-number trap by distinguishing the latest ministerial meeting from earlier WTO conferences.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT prohibited under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: Subsidies for fishing on unregulated high seas
Subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
Subsidies for fishing in overfished stocks, unless rebuilding conditions apply
77.x: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. Aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.
77.tq: Find the excluded activity rather than selecting one of the prohibited forms of fishing support.

77.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies applies primarily to which category of activity?
o: Only fishing undertaken within territorial waters
Only inland aquaculture operated by developing countries
Marine wild capture fishing and support provided at sea
All agricultural production connected with fisheries
77.x: The agreement covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. It does not generally cover aquaculture or inland fishing.
77.tq: Distinguish the positive scope of an agreement from nearby excluded sectors.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding special treatment under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies:
1. Developing countries and least-developed countries receive a two-year exemption in their exclusive economic zones.
2. The agreement provides for a Fish Fund to assist poorer members.
3. The exemption applies without any limitation to fishing on the high seas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The two-year exemption relates to fishing in the exclusive economic zones of developing countries and LDCs; it is not an unlimited high-seas exemption.
77.tq: Separate a limited territorial exemption from an incorrectly expanded high-seas exemption.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly states the recent status of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: It was adopted in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
It was adopted in 2025 and entered into force in September 2026.
It was adopted in 2013 and entered into force in 2016.
It was adopted in 2020 but has not yet entered into force.
77.x: The agreement was adopted at MC12 in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
77.tq: Check both the adoption year and the later entry-into-force date.

77.s: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is significant in WTO history because it is the first WTO agreement with which of the following objectives?
77.x: The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.
77.tq: Identify the distinctive historical first associated with an agreement.

77.s: India became the 123rd WTO member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance for the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in:
77.x: India deposited its Instrument of Acceptance in July 2026, becoming the 123rd WTO member to do so.
77.tq: Combine a membership number with the exact month and year of a treaty action.

77.s: What was the immediate trade-related consequence of the lapse of the WTO e-commerce moratorium on 31 March 2026?
o: The moratorium was extended automatically for another decade.
All customs duties on physical goods were suspended.
The WTO prohibited digital imports by developing countries.
Developing countries lost tariff revenue on digital imports.
77.x: The lapse of the e-commerce moratorium exposed developing countries to the loss of tariff revenue on digital imports.
77.tq: Link the date of a policy change with its principal fiscal consequence.

77.s: The WTO e-commerce moratorium, which lapsed on 31 March 2026, had continued without such a lapse since:
77.x: The e-commerce moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998.
77.tq: Test the “first time since” date rather than the more prominent lapse date.

77.s: The principal reason for the paralysis of the WTO Appellate Body is that:
o: The WTO Agreement on Dispute Settlement Understanding has expired.
India has refused to nominate appellate judges.
The European Union has withdrawn from the WTO dispute settlement system.
The United States has blocked appointments to the Appellate Body.
77.x: The United States has blocked appointments, leaving the Appellate Body non-functional since December 2019.
77.tq: Use the “who exercises the blocking role?” approach in an institutional question.

77.s: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since:
77.x: The Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019 because appointments have been blocked.
77.tq: Distinguish the precise start date of an institutional crisis from nearby years.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA)?
o: It is an EU-led stop-gap arrangement for appeals, and India has not joined it.
It is a compulsory arrangement to which all WTO members belong.
It is a fisheries agreement adopted by the WTO in 2022.
It is a permanent replacement for the WTO and is led by India.
77.x: The MPIA is an EU-led, 2020 stop-gap arrangement for appellate review during the Appellate Body crisis. India has not joined it.
77.tq: Discriminate between a temporary institutional arrangement and a permanent WTO body.

77.s: Which pair of WTO agreements is identified as the only two new agreements concluded in the last 30 years?
o: TFA and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
77.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only two new WTO agreements concluded in the last 30 years.
77.tq: Start from the distinctive pair and eliminate agreements belonging to the original WTO package.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Agreement)
a. TRIPS
a. TRIMS
c. GATS
d. SPS/TBT
List-II (Subject)
i. Trade in services
ii. Minimum intellectual-property standards
iii. Investment measures affecting trade
iv. Food safety, plant and animal health, and technical standards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
77.x: TRIPS concerns minimum IPR standards, TRIMS concerns trade-related investment measures, GATS concerns services, and SPS/TBT concern health and technical standards.
77.tq: Start from the sure pair TRIPS–IPR and complete the agreement-subject mapping.

77.s: Which Indian law was enacted in 2005 to comply with the TRIPS requirement relating to product patents?
o: The Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999
The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001
77.x: India amended its Patents Act in 2005 to introduce product patents in accordance with TRIPS requirements.
77.tq: Match the legal enactment with the specific TRIPS-related compliance measure.

77.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 — GI protection
2. PPV&FR Act, 2001 — plant varieties and farmers’ rights
3. Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 — food safety and standards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
77.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. These Indian enactments are associated with the relevant WTO-related compliance areas.
77.tq: Verify each law against its subject before selecting the all-correct combination.

77.s: India's compliance with TRIMS involved the:
o: Adoption of zero duty on all agricultural products
Introduction of compulsory export subsidies for all industries
Phase-out of local-content conditions affecting trade
77.x: TRIMS concerns investment measures affecting trade, and India's compliance involved phasing out local-content conditions.
77.tq: Distinguish a trade-related investment obligation from tariff and export-subsidy measures.

77.s: India's commitments under GATS are primarily associated with:
77.x: GATS deals with trade in services, and India's compliance is reflected in its services-liberalisation commitments.
77.tq: Use the subject acronym to identify the corresponding area of WTO regulation.

77.s: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is associated with India's compliance in the area covered by:
77.x: SPS/TBT cover food safety, plant and animal health, and technical standards. India's Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is relevant to this area.
77.tq: Match an Indian statute with the WTO agreement category covering its subject.

77.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) is correct?
o: It concerns services liberalisation, and India has not signed it.
It concerns geographical indications, and India joined the Lisbon Agreement.
It concerns zero duty on IT products, and India is a signatory.
It concerns public stockholding, and India ratified it in 2016.
77.x: The ITA concerns zero duty on IT products, and India is a signatory to it.
77.tq: Separate the ITA from the similarly abbreviated trade agreements and identify its subject and Indian position.

77.s: Which statement best describes India's position regarding the Lisbon Agreement on appellations?
o: India is a founding member but has suspended its membership.
India is a member and prefers it to TRIPS for GI protection.
India applies the Lisbon Agreement only to agricultural exports.
India is not a member and prefers TRIPS for GI protection.
77.x: India is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement on appellations and prefers to use TRIPS for geographical-indication protection.
77.tq: Discriminate between two international frameworks dealing with geographical indications.

77.s: The Doha Round of WTO negotiations is also known as the:
77.x: The Doha Round, launched in 2001, is known as the Development Round and covers agriculture, NAMA and services.
77.tq: Recall the distinctive informal title associated with a negotiating round.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly states the status and principal areas of the Doha Round?
o: It began in 1995 and was completed on agriculture alone.
It began in 2001, covers agriculture, NAMA and services, and remains unfinished.
It began in 2013 and covers only trade facilitation.
It began in 2022 and covers only fisheries subsidies.
77.x: The Doha Round began in 2001, is concerned with agriculture, non-agricultural market access and services, and remains unfinished.
77.tq: Check the year, scope and completion status together to reject partially correct alternatives.

77.s: The G-33 was formed in 2003 during the Doha process primarily to address:
o: Food security, special safeguard mechanisms and special products
77.x: The G-33 is a group of more than 40 developing countries, including India, focusing on food security, the Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products.
77.tq: Identify the negotiating group's agenda rather than its membership alone.

77.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Doha Round — Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies only
G-33 — African Group, ACP and LDCs
G-90 — Food security and special products only
NAMA-11 — Developing countries negotiating on non-agricultural market access
77.x: NAMA-11 is a group of developing countries, including India, concerned with non-agricultural market access. The G-90 consists of the African Group, ACP countries and LDCs.
77.tq: Use group-purpose matching and reject the swapped descriptions of G-33, G-90 and NAMA-11.

77.s: The G-90 comprises which of the following groups?
o: The African Group, ACP countries and least-developed countries
The European Union, Japan and the United States
India, China, Brazil and other emerging economies only
77.x: The G-90 consists of the African Group, African, Caribbean and Pacific countries, and least-developed countries.
77.tq: Test the composition of a country group using the membership trap.

77.s: In the WTO dispute concerning India's National Solar Mission, the subject of contention was India's:
o: Ban on imports of agricultural products
77.x: The US challenged the domestic-content requirement under India's National Solar Mission in dispute DS456.
77.tq: Match the dispute name with the specific domestic policy measure challenged.

77.s: What was the outcome of the WTO dispute DS456 concerning India's National Solar Mission?
o: The United States withdrew the complaint before a panel report
The dispute was settled through the MPIA
77.x: India lost the solar-cells dispute, DS456, in 2016.
77.tq: Distinguish the dispute number and subject from the outcome and settlement mechanism.

77.s: The WTO dispute DS541 involving India concerned which set of measures?
o: Steel safeguards imposed by the United Kingdom
The National Food Security Act and MSP procurement
77.x: DS541 concerned India's export subsidies under the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme, SEZ and EOU schemes.
77.tq: Use the dispute number to identify the cluster of domestic schemes involved.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the WTO proceedings concerning India's export subsidies under DS541?
o: The panel ruled for India in 2019 and the United States appealed to the MPIA.
The panel ruled against India in 2019, after which the matter was appealed into the void.
The dispute was decided in India's favour in 2023 by the Appellate Body.
The dispute concerned only India's fisheries subsidies and was withdrawn in 2021.
77.x: The panel ruled against India in 2019 in DS541, and the appeal went into the void because of the Appellate Body crisis.
77.tq: Combine the panel year, adverse finding and distinctive phrase describing an ineffective appeal.

77.s: The WTO dispute brought by Brazil, Australia and Guatemala against India related to:
o: Steel safeguards imposed by the United Kingdom
Tariffs on ICT products under the ITA
77.x: The sugar dispute involved India's cane pricing and export subsidies. The panel ruled against India in 2021, after which the matter was appealed.
77.tq: Match the complainant countries with the commodity and policy issue in dispute.

77.s: Which countries were involved in the WTO dispute concerning India's duties on phones and other ICT goods in relation to the ITA?
o: The United States, Canada and Mexico
The European Union, Japan and Taiwan
77.x: The ICT-tariff dispute was brought by the European Union, Japan and Taiwan and concerned duties on phones and ICT goods vis-à-vis the ITA.
77.tq: Identify the complainants in a trade dispute from a group of plausible country combinations.

77.s: The WTO panel ruled against India in the dispute concerning ICT tariffs in:
77.x: The panel ruled against India in the ICT-tariff dispute in 2023.
77.tq: Separate the years of the solar, export-subsidy, sugar and ICT disputes.

77.s: In May 2026, India raised the United Kingdom's steel safeguard at the WTO body known as the:
77.x: India raised the UK's steel safeguard at the Council for Trade in Goods in May 2026.
77.tq: Apply the “which WTO body handles goods-trade measures?” approach.

77.s: India's steel exports to the United Kingdom in 2025–26 were valued at approximately:
77.x: India's steel exports to the United Kingdom were valued at $893.4 million in 2025–26.
77.tq: Use ascending numerical options and distinguish the reported trade value from nearby figures.

77.s: The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference held at Yaoundé in March 2026:
o: Adopted the Doha Development Round as completed
Issued a comprehensive declaration on all pending issues
Replaced the Appellate Body with the MPIA
77.x: MC14, held at Yaoundé in March 2026, failed to issue a declaration.
77.tq: Test the outcome of the latest conference rather than its venue alone.

77.s: Which one of the following best describes India's concern regarding plurilateral initiatives such as the Investment Facilitation for Development and the E-Commerce Agreement?
o: They apply exclusively to agricultural subsidies and food security.
They may fragment the WTO system by moving away from consensus-based negotiations.
They would make the Appellate Body fully functional without appointments.
They would automatically abolish all WTO agreements.
77.x: India fears that plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and E-Commerce Agreement may fragment the WTO by weakening the consensus-based multilateral approach.
77.tq: Apply the institutional principle of consensus to a contemporary negotiating debate.

77.s: Why are the WTO fisheries-subsidy rules of particular relevance to Andhra Pradesh?
o: They affect the interests of Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, who have sought a fisher-centric approach.
They prohibit all fishing activity along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
They concern only software exports from Visakhapatnam.
They directly regulate only inland irrigation projects in Andhra Pradesh.
77.x: The rules are relevant to Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, and Indian fisher bodies have sought a fisher-centric approach to their implementation.
77.tq: Connect an international policy issue with its concrete regional stakeholder impact.

77.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the first WTO agreement with an environmental objective.
2. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998.
3. India joined the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All three statements are correct. The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective, the moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998, and India joined the fisheries agreement in July 2026.
77.tq: Combine separate current-affairs facts and check whether the comprehensive option is supported by all three.

78.s: With reference to foreign direct investment in the defence sector of India, which of the following is correct?
o: 100% is permitted under the automatic route without sectoral conditions
20% is permitted only through the Government route
49% is permitted under the automatic route and up to 74% through the Government route
74% is permitted under the automatic route and up to 100% through the Government route
78.x: FDI up to 74% in defence is permitted through the automatic route, while investment up to 100% may be allowed through the Government route.
78.tq: Check the sectoral cap and distinguish the automatic route from the Government route.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding FDI in the banking sector:
1. Foreign investment in private-sector banks is permitted up to 74%.
2. In private-sector banks, investment up to 49% is permitted through the automatic route.
3. Foreign investment in public-sector banks is permitted up to 20% through the Government route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. The private-bank cap is 74%, with 49% under the automatic route, whereas public-sector banks have a 20% Government-route limit.
78.tq: Split the options by identifying the separate caps and routes for private and public-sector banks.

78.s: The foreign investment ceiling in private-sector banks was raised to 74% in:
78.x: The foreign investment ceiling in private-sector banks was raised to 74% in 2004.
78.tq: Test the year associated with a specific policy change rather than the present sectoral cap.

78.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes single-brand retail from multi-brand retail with respect to FDI policy?
o: Single-brand retail permits 100% FDI through the automatic route, whereas multi-brand retail permits 51% through the Government route.
Single-brand retail permits 51% through the Government route, whereas multi-brand retail permits 100% automatically.
Both permit 100% FDI through the automatic route.
78.x: Single-brand retail allows 100% FDI through the automatic route, while multi-brand retail has a 51% cap through the Government route.
78.tq: Use the contrast between similar-sounding retail categories to avoid reversing their caps and routes.

78.s:
With reference to FDI in civil aviation, consider the following statements:
1. Scheduled air transport services permit up to 100% foreign investment.
2. Investment up to 49% is permitted through the automatic route, with investment beyond that requiring the Government route.
3. For NRIs, 100% investment is permitted through the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct for scheduled air transport services. The 100% automatic treatment applies specifically to NRIs, while investment beyond 49% for other investors requires the Government route.
78.tq: Separate the general route from the special treatment applicable to NRIs.

78.s: Which of the following statements about FDI in e-commerce is correct?
o: The marketplace model permits 100% FDI through the automatic route, while the inventory model is generally barred.
The inventory model permits 100% FDI through the automatic route, while the marketplace model is barred.
Both models permit only 51% FDI through the Government route.
Neither model permits foreign investment in India.
78.x: The marketplace model permits 100% FDI through the automatic route. FDI in the inventory model is generally not allowed, subject to the later export-related relaxation.
78.tq: Discriminate between marketplace and inventory models instead of applying one cap to both.

78.s: In July 2026, FDI in inventory-based e-commerce was allowed in a specific situation when:
o: The inventory is used for exporting domestically manufactured goods.
The platform operates only as a marketplace.
The inventory is owned entirely by foreign companies for domestic resale.
The inventory is used to sell imported goods in the domestic market.
78.x: The July 2026 relaxation allowed inventory-based e-commerce FDI where the inventory is used to export domestically manufactured goods.
78.tq: Identify the precise condition attached to a policy relaxation rather than its broader sector label.

78.s: Which one of the following statements regarding FDI policy is NOT correct?
o: Caps were raised after 2014 in sectors including defence, insurance and pension.
The marketplace model in e-commerce permits 100% FDI through the automatic route.
All sectors are exclusively on the automatic route.
More than 90% of sectors are on the automatic route.
78.x: The statement that all sectors are exclusively on the automatic route is incorrect. Although more than 90% of sectors are on the automatic route, some sectors retain Government-route requirements.
78.tq: Find the absolute statement that goes beyond the stated proportion.

78.s: Which of the following pairs relating to pharmaceuticals and medical devices is correctly matched?
o: Greenfield pharma — 100% automatic; brownfield pharma — 74% automatic, beyond which approval is required
Greenfield pharma — 74% automatic; brownfield pharma — 100% automatic
Greenfield pharma — 20% Government route; brownfield pharma — 49% automatic
78.x: Greenfield pharmaceutical projects permit 100% FDI automatically. Brownfield projects permit 74% automatically, with approval required beyond that; medical devices permit 100% automatically.
78.tq: Match the project classification with its distinct cap and route.

78.s: FDI in trading, including e-commerce, of food products manufactured or produced in India is permitted up to:
78.x: Trading, including e-commerce, of food products made in India permits 100% FDI through the Government route.
78.tq: Test the difference between a 100% cap and the route through which it is permitted.

78.s: Which one of the following sectors permits up to 100% FDI subject to sectoral conditions rather than an unconditional automatic route?
78.x: The space sector permits up to 100% FDI subject to sectoral conditions. The other options have different specified caps or routes.
78.tq: Use the qualifying phrase ‘subject to sectoral conditions’ to identify the exact policy category.

78.s: Which of the following was the first major relaxation in nearly a decade in the inventory-based e-commerce FDI policy?
o: Allowing foreign investment for exports of domestically manufactured goods
Allowing foreign investment in all domestic inventory without conditions
Replacing the automatic route with a complete prohibition
78.x: The July 2026 relaxation permitted inventory-based e-commerce FDI when the inventory is used for exports of domestically manufactured goods.
78.tq: Distinguish a conditional relaxation from a complete liberalisation.

78.s: India's e-commerce exports were approximately how much, compared with China's approximately $300 billion, according to the cited comparison?
78.x: India's e-commerce exports were cited at only about $5 billion, compared with approximately $300 billion for China.
78.tq: Use the comparison figure and eliminate unrelated FDI totals.

78.s: During FY 2024-25, India's gross FDI was approximately:
78.x: Gross FDI in FY 2024-25 was $81 billion, representing a 14% increase. The other figures relate to different periods or measures.
78.tq: Separate the financial year and measure before selecting the amount.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's FY 2024-25 FDI position?
o: Gross FDI was $94.6 billion and net FDI was $44 billion.
Gross FDI was $81 billion and net FDI was only $353 million.
Gross FDI was $23.6 billion and net FDI was $7.6 billion.
Gross FDI was $353 million and net FDI was $81 billion.
78.x: India recorded gross FDI of $81 billion in FY 2024-25, while net FDI was only $353 million.
78.tq: Distinguish gross inflows from net inflows rather than treating them as interchangeable.

78.s: The three leading sources of FDI in India during FY 2024-25, in descending order, were:
o: Singapore, Mauritius and the United States
The United States, Japan and the Netherlands
Singapore, Japan and the United Arab Emirates
78.x: Singapore contributed 30%, Mauritius 17% and the United States 11% of FDI in FY 2024-25.
78.tq: Arrange the source countries by their stated shares, not by general economic size.

78.s: Which sector was the leading recipient of FDI in India during FY 2024-25?
78.x: The services sector was the leading recipient of FDI during FY 2024-25.
78.tq: Use direct sectoral ranking recall and avoid substituting manufacturing for services.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about FDI during FY 2025-26:
1. Gross FDI during April-February was $88.3 billion.
2. Gross FDI during April-February increased by 18.1%.
3. Manufacturing, computer, financial, business and communication services together received over two-thirds of equity inflows.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct for April-February of FY 2025-26: gross FDI was $88.3 billion, growth was 18.1%, and the listed sectors accounted for over two-thirds of equity inflows.
78.tq: Verify the amount, growth rate and sectoral composition separately before choosing the combined code.

78.s: Net FDI in India remained negative for five consecutive months during which period?
78.x: Net FDI was negative for five straight months from September 2025 to January 2026, mainly due to repatriation and outward direct investment.
78.tq: Test the exact time interval associated with a reported trend.

78.s: The principal reasons cited for negative net FDI during the five-month period in FY 2025-26 were:
o: Reduction in remittances and gold imports
Decline in exports and agricultural drought
Fall in tax revenue and public borrowing
78.x: Negative net FDI was attributed mainly to repatriation and outward direct investment by Indian entities.
78.tq: Link the observed net-flow result with the stated financial causes.

78.s: In April 2026, gross and net FDI were approximately:
78.x: Gross FDI in April 2026 was $15.3 billion and net FDI was $6.6 billion, the highest gross level in nearly five years according to the cited report.
78.tq: Keep gross and net figures in the correct order and period.

78.s: More than 75% of India's FDI in April 2026 came from which group of countries?
o: The United States, Netherlands and the UAE
Singapore, the United Kingdom and France
78.x: More than 75% of April 2026 FDI came from Japan, Singapore and Mauritius.
78.tq: Identify the reported source-country cluster rather than selecting individually prominent economies.

78.s: Which of the following correctly gives the order of the top three states by FDI during the first half of FY 2025-26?
78.x: Maharashtra ranked first, Karnataka second and Tamil Nadu third during the first half of FY 2025-26.
78.tq: Arrange the states by rank and avoid confusing current rankings with older percentage data.

78.s: During the first half of FY 2025-26, Karnataka received approximately how much FDI and Tamil Nadu approximately how much?
78.x: Karnataka received approximately $9.4 billion and Tamil Nadu approximately $3.6 billion during the first half of FY 2025-26.
78.tq: Match each numerical value to the correct state before considering the distractors.

78.s: Information technology-related FDI in the first half of FY 2025-26 was approximately:
78.x: FDI in computer software and hardware doubled to approximately $9 billion, accounting for 25% of total FDI.
78.tq: Pair the absolute amount with its stated share instead of using either figure alone.

78.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, services accounted for what share of FDI during FY 2023-FY 2025?
78.x: Services accounted for 80.2% of FDI during FY 2023-FY 2025. Information and communication alone accounted for 25.8%.
78.tq: Distinguish the aggregate services share from the narrower information-and-communication share.

78.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with India's outward FDI in FY 2025?
o: $23.6 billion — Singapore, the United States and the UAE among the leading destinations
$9.4 billion — Japan, Mauritius and the Netherlands among the leading destinations
$44 billion — China, Germany and France among the leading destinations
$81 billion — Singapore, Australia and Canada among the leading destinations
78.x: Outward FDI was $23.6 billion in FY 2025, with Singapore, the United States and the UAE among the leading destinations.
78.tq: Match the outward-flow amount with its leading destination countries.

78.s:
Arrange the following RBI regional offices in ascending order of cumulative FDI received during April 2000–March 2015:
A. Mumbai
B. New Delhi
C. Chennai
D. Bangalore
78.x: The ascending order was Bangalore, Chennai, New Delhi and Mumbai. Mumbai received the largest amount among these regions.
78.tq: Start with the largest endpoint and reverse-check the ascending sequence.

78.s: Which statement best explains why net FDI may remain weak even when gross FDI inflows are high?
o: Net FDI is always lower because services are excluded from it.
Profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and private-equity or venture-capital exits reduce the net figure.
Net FDI excludes all equity investment by foreign companies.
Gross FDI is calculated only after deducting imports.
78.x: Net FDI is reduced by profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and PE/VC exits through mechanisms such as IPOs.
78.tq: Apply the gross-versus-net distinction to the flow components that raise or reduce the net value.

78.s: Approximately how much of the reported 2014–2026 equity ‘inflows’ was attributed to accounting changes rather than fresh capital?
78.x: About $40 billion of the reported 2014–2026 equity inflows was attributed to accounting changes rather than fresh capital.
78.tq: Identify the specific figure associated with the quality of reported inflows.

78.s: Which of the following correctly describes the FDI targets and major investment announcement associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets at least $10 billion FDI, and Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre in Visakhapatnam.
Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets $1 billion FDI, and Google announced a $10 billion data centre in Vijayawada.
The policy targets $15 billion FDI, and Google announced a 1 GW centre in Amaravati without an investment figure.
The policy targets $94.6 billion FDI, and Google announced a $23.6 billion centre in Visakhapatnam.
78.x: Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets at least $10 billion in FDI. Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre in Visakhapatnam, described as its largest AI hub outside the United States.
78.tq: Match the State policy target with the separate company investment announcement and location.

78.s: Google's proposed AI data centre in Visakhapatnam was described as:
o: The world's largest e-commerce export hub
Its largest AI hub outside the United States
Its largest data centre in South Asia
78.x: The Visakhapatnam project was described as Google's largest AI hub outside the United States.
78.tq: Test the exact superlative and location attached to the investment announcement.

78.s: Which of the following correctly represents the FDI figures cited for FY 2025-26?
o: Gross FDI was $23.6 billion, while net FDI was $9.4 billion.
Gross FDI was $88.3 billion, while net FDI was $44 billion.
Gross FDI was $94.6 billion, while net FDI was $7.6 billion.
Gross FDI was $81 billion, while net FDI was $353 million.
78.x: The cited FY 2025-26 table gives record gross FDI of $94.6 billion and net FDI of $7.6 billion. Net FDI had fallen below $1 billion in FY 2024-25 after peaking at $44 billion in 2020-21.
78.tq: Separate the record gross figure from the distinct net-FDI series across financial years.

78.s: The peak net FDI recorded in the cited series was:
78.x: Net FDI peaked at $44.0 billion in 2020-21, before falling below $1 billion in 2024-25 and recovering to $7.6 billion in 2025-26.
78.tq: Distinguish the peak net-flow figure from gross-FDI records and later recovery values.

78.s: In February 2026, net FDI became positive after six months and stood at approximately:
78.x: Net FDI in February 2026 was positive at approximately $4.6 billion, marking the first positive figure after six months.
78.tq: Match the month-specific figure with the correct flow measure.

78.s: Which of the following statements about older state-wise FDI shares is correct?
o: Karnataka 29%, Maharashtra 24%, Gujarat 17%, Delhi 5%, Tamil Nadu 13%.
Maharashtra 29%, Karnataka 24%, Gujarat 17%, Delhi 13%, Tamil Nadu 5%.
Maharashtra 30%, Karnataka 9.4%, Gujarat 17%, Delhi 13%, Tamil Nadu 3.6%.
Maharashtra 25.8%, Karnataka 29%, Gujarat 24%, Delhi 17%, Tamil Nadu 13%.
78.x: The older FY 2023 data gives Maharashtra 29%, Karnataka 24%, Gujarat 17%, Delhi 13% and Tamil Nadu 5%.
78.tq: Read the percentage table carefully and avoid substituting newer state rankings for older shares.

78.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Global FDI fell by 11% in 2024.
2. India remained the largest recipient of FDI in South Asia.
3. Global FDI rose by 6% to $1.6 trillion in 2025 according to the World Investment Report 2026.
4. The United States was the largest recipient and source of FDI in 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All four statements are correct. Global FDI fell in 2024, India remained South Asia's largest recipient, and the 2026 report recorded a 6% rise to $1.6 trillion in 2025 with the United States leading as both recipient and source.
78.tq: Combine the India-specific and global FDI trends while checking each year separately.

78.s: Which of the following was the order of earlier FY 2023 source-country shares in India's FDI, based on the stated percentages?
78.x: In the earlier FY 2023 data, Mauritius accounted for 26% and Singapore for 23% of FDI.
78.tq: Distinguish the earlier source-country shares from the later FY 2024-25 percentages.

78.s: With reference to the automatic route for foreign direct investment in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Approval of SEBI is required before the investment is made
Only approval of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board is required
Prior approval of the concerned Ministry is mandatory before investment
No prior approval of the RBI or the Government is required, but post-facto reporting to the RBI is necessary
78.x: Under the automatic route, no prior approval of the RBI or the Government is required. The investment is subject to post-facto reporting to the RBI.
78.tq: Distinguish the approval stage from the reporting stage.

78.s: Under the government route for FDI, prior approval is obtained through the Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal from the:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India בלבד
78.x: The government route requires prior approval of the concerned Ministry or Department through the Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal.
78.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ approach for regulatory powers.

78.s:
Which of the following statements regarding India’s FDI policy is correct?
1. The Foreign Investment Promotion Board was abolished in June 2017.
2. DPIIT is the nodal department for FDI policy.
3. India follows a positive-list approach under which FDI is permitted only in specifically named sectors.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
78.x: The FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and DPIIT is the nodal department. India follows a negative-list approach, not a positive-list approach.
78.tq: Identify the reversed policy concept in statement 3.

78.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the three broad FDI categories based on approval and sectoral limits?
1. 100% automatic sectors
2. Government route up to 100%
3. Automatic route up to a cap, with approval required beyond the cap
4. Fixed-cap sectors only
Select the correct answer.
78.x: The FDI policy recognises all four categories: fully automatic sectors, government route sectors up to 100%, sectors with automatic investment up to a cap, and sectors subject to a fixed cap.
78.tq: Check whether the option includes the complete classification rather than a partial list.

78.s: Which of the following is NOT a sector prohibited for FDI in India?
78.x: Railway operations are prohibited except for permitted activities, but railway infrastructure is included among sectors permitting 100% automatic FDI. Lottery business, chit funds and atomic energy are prohibited sectors.
78.tq: Separate a prohibited activity from a permitted infrastructure activity.

78.s:
Consider the following activities:
1. Trading in transferable development rights
2. Manufacture of cigars and cigarettes containing tobacco
3. Railway operations, except permitted activities
4. Real-estate business and construction of farmhouses
Which of the above are prohibited sectors for FDI?
78.x: Trading in TDRs, manufacture of tobacco cigars or cigarettes, prohibited railway operations, and real-estate business or farmhouses are all included in the prohibited list.
78.tq: Test the complete prohibited-sector list by grouping related activities.

78.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Civil aviation MRO — 100% automatic route
2. Multi-brand retail — government route up to 100%
3. Satellites — government route up to 100%
4. Railway infrastructure — 100% automatic route
78.x: Civil aviation MRO and railway infrastructure are 100% automatic sectors, while multi-brand retail and satellites fall under the government route up to 100%.
78.tq: Match each sector with its route and limit before selecting the code.

78.s: Which one of the following sectoral FDI combinations is correctly stated?
o: Defence — 100% automatic route without any government route
78.x: Telecom permits 100% FDI through the automatic route. Multi-brand retail is limited to 51% under the government route, single-brand retail allows 100% automatic FDI, and defence has 74% automatic FDI with government approval possible beyond that up to 100%.
78.tq: Compare the sectoral cap and route together, not the percentage alone.

78.s:
With reference to FDI in banking and pharmaceuticals, consider the following statements:
1. Private sector banks permit 49% FDI under the automatic route within an overall cap of 74%.
2. Public sector banks permit 20% FDI through the government route.
3. Greenfield pharmaceutical projects permit 100% automatic FDI.
4. Brownfield pharmaceutical projects permit 74% automatic FDI, with approval required beyond 74%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All four statements correctly state the applicable limits and routes for private banks, public sector banks, and greenfield and brownfield pharmaceutical projects.
78.tq: Check each sector separately before accepting the all-inclusive option.

78.s:
Which of the following sectors permits 100% automatic FDI according to the stated policy?
1. Medical devices
2. NBFCs
3. Construction and real-estate broking
4. Single-brand retail
Select the correct answer using the code below.
78.x: Medical devices, NBFCs, construction and real-estate broking, and single-brand retail are all listed as permitting 100% automatic FDI.
78.tq: Use the sector-list completeness test for 100% automatic categories.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the evolution of the FDI limit in the insurance sector?
78.x: The insurance FDI limit progressed from 26% to 49% in 2015, 74% in 2021 and 100% in 2025. The 100% limit is subject to the stated regulatory condition.
78.tq: Arrange successive policy revisions by year and verify the increasing limits.

78.s: The 100% FDI limit in insurance was enabled by amending the:
78.x: The 100% insurance FDI limit was enabled through an amendment to the FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019.
78.tq: Identify the correct legal instrument rather than the sector regulator.

78.s: Insurance is listed as Entry 47 in the:
78.x: Insurance is Entry 47 of the Union List. The headquarters of IRDAI is located in Hyderabad.
78.tq: Use the constitutional-list classification to eliminate neighbouring lists.

78.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the nature of an FDI project?
o: Greenfield investment — establishment of a new facility, such as Hyundai at Sriperumbudur
Greenfield investment — acquisition of an existing company
Brownfield investment — establishment of a new facility
Brownfield investment — construction of a facility without acquiring an existing business
78.x: A greenfield investment creates a new facility; Hyundai’s facility at Sriperumbudur is an example. A brownfield investment involves acquisition of an existing business, as in Vodafone’s acquisition of Hutchison Essar.
78.tq: Discriminate between the two similar project classifications by asking whether an existing facility is acquired.

78.s: Vodafone’s acquisition of Hutchison Essar is an example of:
78.x: The acquisition of an existing enterprise is brownfield investment. Greenfield investment refers to establishing a new facility.
78.tq: Apply the acquisition-versus-new-facility distinction to a named example.

78.s: For a listed company, foreign investment is generally classified as FDI when the investor’s equity holding is:
78.x: Under the threshold associated with the Arvind Mayaram Committee classification, an equity holding of 10% or more in a listed company is treated as FDI. Holdings below 10% are classified as portfolio investment.
78.tq: Separate the threshold from the maximum sectoral cap.

78.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes FDI from FPI?
o: FDI is restricted to unlisted companies, whereas FPI is restricted to government securities
FDI is always debt, whereas FPI is always equity
FDI is regulated only by SEBI, whereas FPI is regulated only by the RBI
FDI is generally long-term and may involve management control, whereas FPI is generally liquid and short-term
78.x: FDI is generally long-term and may bring management control and technology. FPI is portfolio investment, usually more liquid and potentially short-term or ‘hot money’.
78.tq: Compare investments across nature, control and liquidity rather than ownership alone.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about FDI and FPI:
1. FDI may enter through the automatic or government route and is associated with DPIIT and RBI oversight.
2. FPI investors must be registered with SEBI and are subject to SEBI and RBI oversight.
3. FII and FPI are essentially different categories with no substantive relationship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. FII and FPI are essentially the same category in the classification described, so statement 3 is false.
78.tq: Use the confusable-pair trap involving FII and FPI.

78.s: The legal and regulatory basis associated with the FDI–FPI threshold classification is correctly represented by:
o: Competition Act, 2002 and Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI Takeover Regulations, 2011
78.x: The classification is associated with FEMA, 1999 and the SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019. The 10% threshold is linked to the Arvind Mayaram Committee.
78.tq: Match the regulatory classification with its governing legal instruments.

78.s:
Foreign capital in India includes which of the following?
1. Foreign direct investment
2. Trade credit
3. Non-resident Indian deposits
4. External commercial borrowings
Select the correct answer using the code below.
78.x: Foreign capital includes FDI, trade credit, NRI deposits and external commercial borrowings. All four categories are included.
78.tq: Check the full enumeration rather than treating foreign capital as equity alone.

78.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as debt capital?
78.x: External commercial borrowing is debt capital. FDI and FPI are non-debt forms, while ADRs represent equity raised abroad through depository receipts.
78.tq: Separate debt instruments from non-debt equity instruments.

78.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. FDI — non-debt, long-term investment with possible management control
2. FPI/FII — non-debt, portfolio investment and relatively liquid
3. ECB and trade credit — debt
4. NRI deposits — banking capital and debt
Select the correct answer.
78.x: All four classifications are correct. FDI and FPI are non-debt forms, while ECB, trade credit and NRI deposits are debt or banking-capital forms.
78.tq: Classify each instrument by both its debt status and investment character.

78.s: Participatory notes issued by registered FPIs are best described as:
o: Debt instruments issued by the RBI to domestic investors
Offshore derivative instruments issued to overseas investors not registered with SEBI
Government securities issued under the external commercial borrowing route
Shares issued only by unlisted Indian companies
78.x: Participatory notes are offshore derivative instruments issued by registered FPIs to overseas investors who are not registered with SEBI. They provide a portfolio investment channel.
78.tq: Identify the issuer, recipient and registration status in the instrument’s definition.

78.s: In balance of payments data, ADRs and GDRs are counted as:
78.x: ADRs and GDRs represent equity raised abroad through depository receipts and are counted as portfolio investment in balance of payments data.
78.tq: Distinguish the form of fund-raising from its classification in BoP data.

78.s: Foreign currency convertible bonds are classified as:
78.x: FCCBs are debt instruments and are classified under external commercial borrowings, even though they may carry a conversion feature.
78.tq: Do not confuse convertibility into equity with the instrument’s initial debt classification.

78.s: Foreign Institutional Investment in India was opened in:
78.x: Foreign institutional investment was opened in India in 1992. FII and FPI are essentially the same category in the stated classification.
78.tq: Distinguish the opening year of portfolio investment from the year of FEMA enactment.

78.s: With reference to limits applicable to Foreign Portfolio Investors in government securities, which one of the following is correct?
o: 2% of outstanding Central Government securities and 6% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
10% of outstanding Central Government securities and 5% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 6% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
78.x: Under the General Route, the overall FPI limit is 6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of outstanding State Government securities. Security-wise and short-term limits have been removed.
78.tq: Use the paired percentages and avoid reversing the Central and State figures.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) for foreign investment in government securities:
1. FAR securities are not subject to investment limits.
2. New 15-year, 30-year and 40-year Government securities are covered under FAR.
3. Sovereign green bonds are covered under FAR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. FAR removes investment limits for specified securities, including new 15-year, 30-year and 40-year Government securities and sovereign green bonds.
78.tq: Check whether all listed categories fall within the stated no-limit route.

78.s: Which of the following best explains the distinction between FDI and FPI under the threshold prescribed for investment in a listed company?
o: An equity holding of 25% or more is treated as FDI, while a holding below 25% is treated as FPI
All equity investment in a listed company is treated as FDI, irrespective of the percentage held
An equity holding below 10% is treated as FDI, while a holding of 10% or more is treated as FPI
An equity holding of 10% or more is treated as FDI, while a holding below 10% is treated as FPI
78.x: Under the relevant FEMA threshold, an equity holding of 10% or more in a listed company is classified as FDI, while a holding below 10% is classified as FPI. Any stake in an unlisted company is treated as FDI.
78.tq: Separate the 10% listed-company threshold from the special rule for unlisted companies.

78.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Foreign Portfolio Investment in India is correct?
o: FPI was opened to India in 2000 and is regulated exclusively by the Ministry of Finance
FPI was opened to India in 1991 and is regulated exclusively by the RBI under FEMA
FPI was opened to India in 1992 and is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, along with the RBI
FPI was opened to India in 2019 and is regulated exclusively by SEBI without any role for the RBI
78.x: Foreign Portfolio Investment was opened to India in 1992. It is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, with the RBI also having a regulatory role.
78.tq: Combine the opening year with the two relevant regulators rather than selecting an exclusive regulator.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about recent FPI flows and their determinants:
1. FPI flows are influenced significantly by US Federal Reserve interest rates and global risk appetite.
