85.s: The leverage ratio was introduced as a Basel requirement under:
85.x: The leverage ratio came with Basel III as a non-risk-weighted backstop to prevent balance sheets from expanding on a thin capital base.
85.tq: Distinguish the later Basel III safeguard from the earlier capital frameworks.

85.s: A bank is required to maintain sufficient high-quality liquid assets to withstand a 30-day stress scenario. Which regulatory measure is being applied?
85.x: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) requires a stock of high-quality liquid assets sufficient to survive a 30-day stress period.
85.tq: Map the time horizon in the scenario to the corresponding liquidity ratio.

85.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: NSFR — survival during a 30-day stress period
LCR — stable funding over one year
LCR — high-quality liquid assets for a 30-day stress period
CCyB — high-quality liquid assets for a 30-day stress period
85.x: LCR concerns high-quality liquid assets adequate for a 30-day stress period. NSFR concerns stable funding over a one-year horizon.
85.tq: Use the time-period distinction to eliminate swapped definitions.

85.s: The Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) is concerned primarily with:
o: The credit-to-GDP gap during a boom
Capital adequacy during a 30-day stress period
Credit risk weights over five categories
Stable funding over a one-year horizon
85.x: NSFR promotes stable funding over a one-year horizon, whereas LCR addresses short-term liquidity over 30 days.
85.tq: Recall the longer liquidity horizon and contrast it with the short-term LCR.

85.s:
Which of the following are classified as Level 1 high-quality liquid assets for the purpose of LCR?
1. Cash
2. Government securities
3. Central-bank reserves
4. Highly rated corporate bonds
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: Cash, government securities and central-bank reserves are Level 1 HQLA. Highly rated corporate bonds are classified as Level 2 HQLA.
85.tq: Separate the core Level 1 assets from the corporate-bond example belonging to Level 2.

85.s: The minimum LCR and NSFR prescribed in the comparative Basel-RBI framework are:
o: LCR 100 per cent and NSFR 100 per cent
LCR 100 per cent and NSFR 90 per cent
LCR 110 per cent and NSFR 110 per cent
LCR 90 per cent and NSFR 100 per cent
85.x: The comparative framework lists both the LCR and NSFR minimums at 100 per cent for BCBS and RBI norms.
85.tq: Treat paired ratio figures independently and identify the matching value.

85.s: The RBI deferred the revised LCR norms up to:
85.x: The RBI deferred the revised Liquidity Coverage Ratio norms up to 31 March 2026.
85.tq: Distinguish the regulatory deferral date from the general LCR implementation period.

85.s: Which of the following correctly defines Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) or CRAR?
o: Total capital divided by risk-weighted assets
Total deposits divided by total advances
Tier 1 capital divided by total non-risk-weighted exposure
Liquid assets divided by short-term liabilities
85.x: CAR or CRAR is calculated as capital divided by risk-weighted assets. The leverage ratio, in contrast, uses total non-risk-weighted exposure.
85.tq: Distinguish risk-weighted capital adequacy from the non-risk-weighted leverage measure.

85.s: Which of the following statements regarding the components of regulatory capital is correct?
o: Tier 1 capital is composed exclusively of subordinated debt.
Tier 1 capital includes pure equity elements, while Tier 2 may include subordinated debt.
Tier 2 capital consists only of paid-up equity and reserves.
Both Tier 1 and Tier 2 consist entirely of government securities.
85.x: Tier 1 capital includes paid-up capital, reserves and undistributed profits as core equity. Tier 2 has a mixed equity-debt character and may include subordinated debt.
85.tq: Use the core-versus-supplementary capital distinction to identify the accurate composition.

85.s: Which of the following correctly presents the RBI norms for CET1, Tier 1 capital and total CRAR?
85.x: The RBI norms listed are CET1 5.5 per cent, Tier 1 capital 7 per cent and total CRAR 9 per cent.
85.tq: Read the three-column ratio comparison without substituting the BCBS minimums.

85.s: When the capital conservation buffer is included, the total CRAR requirement becomes:
o: 10.5 per cent under BCBS and 11.5 per cent under RBI
11.5 per cent under BCBS and 12.5 per cent under RBI
8 per cent under BCBS and 9 per cent under RBI
9 per cent under BCBS and 10 per cent under RBI
85.x: Adding the 2.5 per cent capital conservation buffer gives 10.5 per cent for the BCBS minimum and 11.5 per cent for the RBI norm.
85.tq: Add the buffer to the respective base ratio instead of confusing the two totals.

85.s: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower risk weights under Basel III for which of the following sectors?
85.x: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower Basel III risk weights for MSMEs and real estate.
85.tq: Use the sector-pair association while rejecting plausible but unlisted alternatives.

85.s: The regulatory CAR norm and the own CAR figure mentioned for HDFC Bank are, respectively:
85.x: HDFC Bank's regulatory CAR norm is 11.9 per cent, while its own reported CAR is 19.6 per cent.
85.tq: Read the order of the figures carefully: regulatory requirement first and bank's actual figure second.

85.s: Which one of the following was a key recommendation of the Committee on the Financial System chaired by M. Narasimham in 1991?
o: Creation of a single universal bank by merging all public sector banks
Introduction of prudential norms and capital adequacy requirements
Increase in statutory liquidity ratio and cash reserve ratio
Complete nationalisation of private sector banks
85.x: The Narasimham-I Committee recommended prudential norms, capital adequacy, reduction of SLR and CRR, and deregulation of interest rates.
85.tq: Identify the committee by its distinctive reform recommendations rather than by its name alone.

85.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Narasimham-I and Narasimham-II Committees:
1. Narasimham-I recommended reduction of SLR and CRR.
2. Narasimham-II recommended a three-tier banking structure.
3. Narasimham-II proposed that weak and unviable banks should be closed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All three statements are correct. Narasimham-I focused on foundational banking reforms, while Narasimham-II emphasised consolidation, a three-tier structure and resolution of weak banks.
85.tq: Test the different recommendations of two similarly named committees through statement combination.

85.s: The Committee on Banking Sector Reforms, generally referred to as Narasimham-II, was set up in:
85.x: Narasimham-II was set up in December 1997 and submitted its report in April 1998.
85.tq: Distinguish the constitution date from the report date in a close-date pair.

85.s: The report of the Narasimham-II Committee was submitted in:
85.x: The Committee on Banking Sector Reforms was constituted in December 1997 and submitted its report in April 1998.
85.tq: Use the report date rather than the committee’s constitution date.

85.s: The Committee on Banking Sector Reforms recommended that the Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) should be raised to:
85.x: Narasimham-II recommended raising CRAR to 10 per cent.
85.tq: Recall the precise numerical recommendation and distinguish it from nearby capital ratios.

85.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier banking structure suggested by the Narasimham-II Committee?
o: Two to three national banks, eight to ten international banks and no local banks
Two to three international banks, eight to ten national banks and many local banks
One international bank, five national banks and several regional banks
Only regional rural banks, cooperative banks and payment banks
85.x: The proposed structure consisted of two or three international banks, eight to ten national banks and many local banks.
85.tq: Match the committee’s structural proposal with its precise numerical tiers.

85.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nachiket Mor — Differentiated banking and financial inclusion
M.S. Verma — Restructuring of weak public sector banks
P.J. Nayak — Governance of bank boards
85.x: Goiporia was associated with customer service in banks. Insurance-sector reform was associated with the Malhotra Committee.
85.tq: Find the wrong committee-subject association by separating banking service reform from insurance reform.

85.s: The M.S. Verma Committee is associated with:
o: Financial inclusion and universal bank accounts
Harmonisation of the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions
85.x: The M.S. Verma Committee dealt with restructuring weak public sector banks and used seven parameters to identify weak banks.
85.tq: Use the committee’s subject as the direct identifier.

85.s: How many parameters were used for identifying weak banks by the M.S. Verma Committee?
85.x: The M.S. Verma Committee identified weak banks using seven parameters.
85.tq: Recall the exact count attached to a committee’s diagnostic framework.

85.s: The P.J. Nayak Committee is primarily associated with:
o: Governance of bank boards in India
Economic capital and transfer of RBI surplus
85.x: The P.J. Nayak Committee examined governance of bank boards, particularly in public sector banks, and its recommendations led to the Banks Board Bureau.
85.tq: Distinguish board governance from other banking and financial-sector committee subjects.

85.s: Which institution emerged from the recommendations associated with the P.J. Nayak Committee?
o: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
85.x: The recommendations on governance of bank boards led to the Banks Board Bureau.
85.tq: Link a committee recommendation to the institutional outcome it produced.

85.s: The Raghuram Rajan Committee on Financial Sector Reforms is associated with the report titled:
85.x: The Raghuram Rajan Committee’s report was titled “A Hundred Small Steps.”
85.tq: Identify a committee through its distinctive report title.

85.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Bimal Jalan — Economic Capital Framework of RBI
a. Nachiket Mor — Financial inclusion
c. S.H. Khan Working Group — Harmonisation of the roles of banks and DFIs
d. C. Rangarajan — Financial inclusion, 2006
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
85.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Bimal Jalan dealt with the RBI’s Economic Capital Framework, Nachiket Mor with financial inclusion, S.H. Khan with bank-DFI roles, and C. Rangarajan with financial inclusion in 2006.
85.tq: Check several committee-subject associations before selecting the complete combination.

85.s: The S.H. Khan Working Group of 1998 was concerned with:
o: Determining the contingent risk buffer of the RBI
Restructuring weak public sector banks through seven parameters
Setting up the Banks Board Bureau
Harmonising the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions
85.x: The S.H. Khan Working Group examined how the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions could be harmonised, leading towards universal banking.
85.tq: Separate the universal-banking recommendation from committee work on weak banks and RBI reserves.

85.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Committee on Financial Sector Assessment?
o: It was a joint Government of India–RBI self-assessment of financial-sector stability and standards.
It was a committee for fixing the CRAR of public sector banks at 10 per cent.
It was a committee for restructuring regional rural banks.
It was constituted exclusively to recommend bank mergers.
85.x: The Committee on Financial Sector Assessment, functioning during 2006–09, conducted a joint Government of India–RBI self-assessment of financial-sector stability and standards.
85.tq: Identify the institutional composition and purpose instead of relying only on the committee name.

85.s: The Economic Capital Framework of the RBI, associated with Bimal Jalan, dealt particularly with:
o: Merging strong banks and closing weak banks
Transfer of reserves and surplus to the Government
85.x: Bimal Jalan chaired the committee on the RBI’s Economic Capital Framework, including the issue of reserves and surplus transfer to the Government.
85.tq: Distinguish RBI balance-sheet and surplus issues from banking-structure reforms.

85.s: The contingent risk buffer recommended in the Economic Capital Framework of the RBI was in the range of:
85.x: The Economic Capital Framework specified a contingent risk buffer in the range of 5.5 to 6.5 per cent.
85.tq: Recall the numerical range attached to the RBI’s Economic Capital Framework.

85.s: Which committee laid the groundwork for universal bank accounts and the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana?
85.x: The Nachiket Mor Committee on differentiated banking and financial inclusion laid the groundwork for universal bank accounts and PMJDY.
85.tq: Connect the financial-inclusion objective with the correct committee.

85.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Committee)
a. Goiporia
b. Malhotra
c. C. Rangarajan
d. P.J. Nayak

List-II (Subject)
i. Insurance reform
ii. Governance of bank boards
iii. Customer service in banks
iv. Financial inclusion

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
85.x: Goiporia dealt with customer service, Malhotra with insurance reform, C. Rangarajan with financial inclusion, and P.J. Nayak with bank-board governance.
85.tq: Start from the sure committee-subject pairs and eliminate codes containing a wrong association.

85.s: Which of the following bank mergers became effective on 1 April 2019?
o: Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank into Bank of Baroda
Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India into Punjab National Bank
Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank into Union Bank of India
85.x: Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank were amalgamated with Bank of Baroda with effect from 1 April 2019.
85.tq: Distinguish the single 2019 merger from the group of mergers effective in 2020.

85.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank — Indian Bank
Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India — Punjab National Bank
Syndicate Bank — Union Bank of India
85.x: Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India were amalgamated with Punjab National Bank. Syndicate Bank merged with Canara Bank, Allahabad Bank with Indian Bank, and Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank with Union Bank of India.
85.tq: Use the anchor-bank mapping and reject swapped merger partners.

85.s: Andhra Bank was amalgamated with which anchor bank?
85.x: Andhra Bank, along with Corporation Bank, was amalgamated with Union Bank of India with effect from 1 April 2020.
85.tq: Test the fate of a specifically named bank against nearby anchor-bank distractors.

85.s: The merger of Syndicate Bank was with:
85.x: Syndicate Bank was amalgamated with Canara Bank with effect from 1 April 2020.
85.tq: Recall the anchor bank for a single-bank merger rather than a two-bank amalgamation.

85.s: The amalgamation of SBI’s associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank with SBI became effective on:
85.x: SBI’s associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank were amalgamated with SBI with effect from 1 April 2017.
85.tq: Place the earliest major merger in the correct chronological position.

85.s:
Arrange the following banking-sector amalgamations in chronological order:
A. Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank with Bank of Baroda
B. SBI associates and Bharatiya Mahila Bank with SBI
C. Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank with Union Bank of India
D. Allahabad Bank with Indian Bank
85.x: The mergers took effect in the order: SBI-related merger in 2017, Dena–Vijaya with Bank of Baroda in 2019, and Andhra–Corporation and Allahabad Bank mergers in 2020.
85.tq: Arrange events by their effective dates, giving priority to the distinct 2017 and 2019 milestones.

85.s: The number of public sector banks declined from 27 in 2017 to how many in 2020?
85.x: The number of public sector banks was reduced from 27 in 2017 to 12 in 2020 as a result of consolidation and mergers.
85.tq: Recall both endpoints of a structural numerical change.

85.s: Which of the following was NOT an expected gain from the consolidation of public sector banks?
o: Creation of lenders capable of competing globally
Economies of scale and lower costs
Permanent elimination of all non-performing assets
Better capital utilisation and risk management
85.x: The expected gains included scale, lower costs, global-size lenders, better capital use and improved risk management. Permanent elimination of all NPAs was not stated as an expected gain.
85.tq: Reject the extreme outcome that goes beyond the stated objectives of bank consolidation.

85.s: The idea of creating fewer and stronger banks through mergers was associated particularly with:
85.x: Narasimham-II recommended consolidation through mergers of strong banks and the creation of fewer, stronger banking institutions.
85.tq: Distinguish the consolidation agenda of Narasimham-II from the foundational reforms of Narasimham-I.

85.s:
Consider the following statements about the amalgamation of Regional Rural Banks:
1. The amalgamation was undertaken state by state.
2. The number of Regional Rural Banks is stated as 28.
3. The Viability Plan 2.0 tracks all 28 Regional Rural Banks on 30 parameters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All three statements are correct. RRBs were amalgamated state by state; 28 RRBs are covered, and Viability Plan 2.0 tracks them on 30 parameters.
85.tq: Combine the organisational process with the current numerical coverage of the reform plan.

85.s: Under Viability Plan 2.0, the Regional Rural Banks are tracked on parameters including:
o: Fiscal deficit, revenue deficit and primary deficit
Repo rate, reverse repo rate and bank rate
GDP, CPI and balance of payments
85.x: The 30 parameters under Viability Plan 2.0 include CRAR, credit-deposit ratio and NPAs.
85.tq: Select banking-performance indicators rather than macroeconomic or fiscal indicators.

85.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of Viability Plan 2.0 for Regional Rural Banks?
85.x: The four pillars are operational excellence, asset quality, profitability and growth. Monetary stability is not one of them.
85.tq: Find the unrelated policy objective among the four stated pillars.

85.s: The Viability Plan 2.0 for Regional Rural Banks covers which period?
85.x: Viability Plan 2.0 covers the period from 2025–26 to 2027–28.
85.tq: Recall the exact three-year implementation window of the plan.

85.s: The High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat was announced in:
85.x: The High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat was announced in Budget 2026–27 to review the banking sector as a whole.
85.tq: Use the budget-year association to identify the latest banking-sector committee.

85.s: Indradhanush, introduced in August 2015, was primarily associated with which of the following reforms?
o: A seven-point plan for capitalisation and governance reform of public sector banks
A fiscal-deficit reduction programme for the Union Government
A scheme for consolidation of Regional Rural Banks
A framework for regulating private insurance companies
85.x: Indradhanush was a seven-point plan introduced in August 2015 for capital infusion and governance reform in public sector banks.
85.tq: Identify the programme by its distinctive reform objective and date.

85.s: Which one of the following was NOT a component of the seven-point Indradhanush plan for public sector banks?
85.x: The seven components were Appointments, Banks Board Bureau, Capitalisation, De-stressing, Empowerment, Framework of accountability and Governance. Exchange-rate management was not a component.
85.tq: Find the option belonging to a neighbouring policy area rather than the named programme.

85.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indradhanush:
1. It provided for ₹70,000 crore of budgetary capital over four years.
2. It included the establishment of the Banks Board Bureau as one of its elements.
3. It was introduced in August 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: Indradhanush was introduced in August 2015, included the Banks Board Bureau, and provided ₹70,000 crore of budgetary capital over four years.
85.tq: Check the date, numerical provision and components together.

85.s: The Banks Board Bureau was established to perform which of the following functions in relation to public sector banks?
o: Determine the statutory liquidity ratio for all banks
Select chairpersons of public sector banks
Approve the Union Budget on behalf of Parliament
85.x: The Banks Board Bureau selects chairpersons of public sector banks. Its creation followed the recommendations of the P.J. Nayak Committee.
85.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish institutional functions.

85.s: In October 2017, the Union Government announced a recapitalisation package for public sector banks amounting to:
85.x: The October 2017 recapitalisation package for public sector banks amounted to ₹2.11 lakh crore.
85.tq: Distinguish the total package from the separate bond and bank-raised components.

85.s:
With reference to the October 2017 bank recapitalisation package, consider the following statements:
1. ₹1.35 lakh crore was provided through recapitalisation bonds.
2. Approximately ₹58,000 crore was raised by banks.
3. The recapitalisation bonds increased the Central Government’s debt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: The package included ₹1.35 lakh crore through recapitalisation bonds and approximately ₹58,000 crore raised by banks. The bonds pushed up Central Government debt.
85.tq: Separate the package total, its sources and its fiscal consequence.

85.s: How do recapitalisation bonds support public sector banks without requiring an equivalent immediate cash outgo from the Union budget?
o: The Government transfers its tax receipts directly to bank depositors
The Government writes off all outstanding bank loans through monetary creation
Banks issue equity directly to the Reserve Bank of India without Government involvement
The Government issues bonds to banks and invests the proceeds back into them as equity
85.x: Under the mechanism, the Government issues bonds to public sector banks and puts the money back into them as equity; therefore, no equivalent fresh cash leaves the budget immediately.
85.tq: Trace the transaction sequence rather than judging the policy only by its name.

85.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 4R strategy for public sector bank reform?
85.x: The 4R strategy consists of Recognise, Resolve, Recapitalise and Reform.
85.tq: Test the exact official expansion of a numbered reform strategy.

85.s:
Assertion (A): The EASE Index ranks participating public sector banks on reform performance.
Reason (R): The index benchmarks mid-size and large public sector banks against reform themes every quarter.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
85.x: Both statements are true. Quarterly benchmarking of mid-size and large public sector banks against reform themes provides the basis for ranking them in the EASE Index.
85.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the institutional function stated in the assertion.

85.s: EASE is the abbreviation for:
o: Enhanced Administration of Savings and Equity
85.x: EASE stands for Enhanced Access and Service Excellence.
85.tq: Discriminate between the exact official expansion and look-alike expansions.

85.s: EASE was conceived and launched in which of the following years respectively?
85.x: EASE was conceived in 2015 and launched in 2017.
85.tq: Keep the two close dates in their stated sequence rather than reversing them.

85.s: Which institution oversees EASE through its EASE Steering Committee?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
85.x: EASE is overseen by the EASE Steering Committee of the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA). It is not governed by a board of heads of premier financial institutions.
85.tq: Use the ‘which body performs the function?’ institutional trap.

85.s:
Consider the following statements about EASE reforms:
1. Public sector banks report quarterly against EASE benchmarks.
2. EASE 1.0 to 4.0 covered themes including digitisation, asset quality, governance and human resources.
3. EASE 5.0 to 7.0 formed part of EASENext after PSB Manthan 2.0 in April 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All three statements are correct. EASE uses quarterly reporting, its earlier versions covered the listed reform themes, and EASE 5.0–7.0 formed EASENext after PSB Manthan 2.0 in April 2022.
85.tq: Combine a reporting arrangement with version-wise reform themes and chronology.

85.s: The four focus areas of EASE 8.0, also called “EASE ₹ise”, for FY2026 are:
o: Risk and Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact, Excellence
85.x: EASE 8.0 or EASE ₹ise focuses on Risk and Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact and Excellence.
85.tq: Match the programme version with its exact four-part theme set.

85.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the stated aims of Enhanced Access and Service Excellence?
85.x: EASE aims include financial stability, credit growth, NPA management, risk mitigation, digital transformation, customer service and inclusion. Abolition of prudential regulation is not an aim.
85.tq: Reject the extreme option that contradicts the reform-oriented character of the programme.

85.s: Public sector banks recorded a combined net profit of ₹1.98 lakh crore in FY26. What policy implication was associated with this performance?
o: No budgetary recapitalisation is needed for the time being
All public sector banks must be privatised immediately
The Banks Board Bureau must be discontinued
The statutory liquidity ratio must be increased to 38.5 per cent
85.x: The record combined net profit of ₹1.98 lakh crore in FY26 was cited as meaning that budgetary recapitalisation is not currently needed.
85.tq: Link the numerical outcome with the stated policy consequence.

85.s: Which of the following correctly describes AT-1 bonds mentioned in the context of public sector bank capital raising?
o: They are short-term treasury bills without any redemption feature
They are compulsory deposits guaranteed by the Finance Commission
They are ordinary equity shares carrying voting rights
They are perpetual debt instruments with a call option
85.x: AT-1 bonds are perpetual debt instruments with a call option.
85.tq: Distinguish a perpetual debt instrument from equity and short-term debt.

85.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding recent capital raising by public sector banks?
o: SBI — ₹4,000 crore through AT-1 bonds in September 2026
Canara Bank — ₹2.11 lakh crore through recapitalisation bonds
SBI — ₹4,691 crore through its first Basel III AT-1 bonds of FY27
Canara Bank — ₹4,691 crore through Tier 2 bonds only
85.x: SBI raised ₹4,691 crore through its first Basel III AT-1 bonds of FY27. Canara Bank’s stated plans were up to ₹4,500 crore in AT-1 bonds and ₹4,000 crore in Tier 2 bonds.
85.tq: Match the bank with the correct instrument, amount and time reference.

85.s: Which one of the following was a component of financial-sector reforms undertaken after 1991?
o: Abolition of prudential norms for banks
Replacement of FEMA by FERA in 1999
85.x: Interest-rate deregulation was an important component of post-1991 financial-sector reforms.
85.tq: Select the reform measure and reject reversals of the reform direction.

85.s: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio stood at approximately what level in 1991–92 before being reduced as part of financial-sector reforms?
85.x: The SLR was 38.5 per cent in 1991–92 and was subsequently reduced along with reductions in reserve requirements.
85.tq: Use the distinctive historical percentage rather than a rounded or reversed figure.

85.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with the prudential reforms introduced after 1991?
o: Introduction of CRAR only after the GST regime began
Abolition of asset classification and provisioning requirements
Replacement of prudential norms by exchange controls
Income recognition, asset classification, provisioning and CRAR from 1992
85.x: Post-1991 reforms introduced prudential norms for income recognition, asset classification and provisioning, along with CRAR in 1992.
85.tq: Group the related prudential norms and avoid the reversal trap.

85.s: Which pair of banks exemplifies the entry of new private sector banks during the post-1991 reform period?
o: Regional Rural Bank and District Central Cooperative Bank
State Bank of India and Punjab National Bank
85.x: HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are examples of private banks that entered during the post-1991 reform period.
85.tq: Identify the private-bank entrants rather than established public or development institutions.

85.s:
Consider the following statements regarding post-1991 financial-sector reforms:
1. SEBI was made a statutory body in 1992.
2. The Banking Ombudsman was introduced in 1995.
3. Asset Reconstruction Companies and Debt Recovery Tribunals were associated with recovery of stressed assets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: SEBI received statutory status in 1992, the Banking Ombudsman was introduced in 1995, and ARCs and DRTs were associated with recovery mechanisms.
85.tq: Test dates and institutional functions together in a coded statement question.

85.s: A major change in the regulatory structure after financial-sector reforms was that:
o: SEBI assumed direct control over all public sector banks
The Finance Ministry’s Banking Division became the sole regulator of banks
The Banks Board Bureau replaced the RBI as the monetary authority
The RBI became the primary regulator and dual control with the Finance Ministry’s Banking Division ended
85.x: The RBI became the primary regulator, ending dual control with the Finance Ministry’s Banking Division. The reforms also promoted greater autonomy for public sector banks.
85.tq: Identify the correct authority and reject swapped institutional powers.

85.s: Which one of the following sets contains only measures belonging to the post-1991 financial-sector reform package?
o: Market-determined exchange rate, FEMA replacing FERA, and insurance opening under the IRDA Act
Bank nationalisation, FRBM Act and abolition of private banks
Replacement of FEMA by FERA, fixed exchange rate and closure of IRDA
Nationalisation of banks, universal interest controls and abolition of SEBI
85.x: The reform package included a market-determined exchange rate in 1993, replacement of FERA by FEMA in 1999, and opening of insurance under the IRDA Act, 1999.
85.tq: Screen the set for chronological and directional consistency of reforms.

85.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the financial-sector reforms initiated after 1991?
85.x: The FRBM Act, 2003 was a fiscal reform, not a financial-sector reform. The other three were components of post-1991 financial-sector reforms.
85.tq: Separate financial-sector reforms from a fiscal-policy measure.

85.s: The post-1991 change in the role of the Reserve Bank of India was described as a movement:
o: From monetary authority towards insurance regulator
From facilitator towards exclusive fiscal authority
From banking regulator towards legislative authority
85.x: The RBI’s role moved from regulator towards facilitator in the changing financial-sector framework.
85.tq: Test the precise direction of institutional change rather than a broad synonym.

85.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. FEMA replaced FERA
B. Market-determined exchange rate was introduced
C. Insurance was opened under the IRDA Act
D. SEBI was made a statutory body
85.x: SEBI became statutory in 1992, the market-determined exchange rate was introduced in 1993, FEMA replaced FERA in 1999, and insurance was opened under the IRDA Act in 1999. Thus the order is D, B, A, C.
85.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intermediate reforms by year.

85.s: How many Regional Rural Banks existed originally, and how many remained after the 2020–21 consolidation?
85.x: There were originally 196 RRBs, and their number came down to 43 after the 2020–21 consolidation.
85.tq: Keep the successive consolidation stages distinct instead of confusing the final figure with the intermediate figure.

85.s: Under the One State-One RRB arrangement, the number of Regional Rural Banks became:
85.x: Under the One State-One RRB arrangement, 15 RRBs were amalgamated and the number became 28, effective from 1 May 2025.
85.tq: Identify the final consolidation figure and distinguish it from the Centre’s shareholding percentage.

85.s:
Consider the following statements about the One State-One RRB arrangement:
1. Fifteen RRBs were amalgamated.
2. The arrangement became effective on 1 May 2025.
3. The Centre retains a 50 per cent share in RRBs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All three statements are correct: 15 RRBs were amalgamated, the arrangement took effect on 1 May 2025, and the Centre retains a 50 per cent share.
85.tq: Combine the consolidation count, effective date and ownership detail.

85.s: Which of the following correctly states the framework of Viability Plan 2.0?
o: It covers 15 RRBs, rests on four pillars and tracks 50 parameters.
It covers 43 RRBs, rests on three pillars and tracks 28 parameters.
It covers all 28 RRBs, rests on four pillars and tracks 30 parameters.
It covers all 28 RRBs, rests on five pillars and tracks 30 parameters.
85.x: Viability Plan 2.0 covers all 28 RRBs, rests on four pillars and tracks 30 parameters.
85.tq: Match the plan with its coverage, number of pillars and monitoring parameters.

85.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of Viability Plan 2.0?
85.x: The four pillars are operations, asset quality, profitability and growth. Exchange-rate determination is not a pillar of the plan.
85.tq: Find the unrelated macroeconomic term among the plan-specific pillars.

85.s: LIC acquired a majority stake in IDBI Bank in 2019. What was the consequence of this transaction for the regulatory classification of IDBI Bank?
o: It was reclassified by RBI as a private sector lender
It was classified as a foreign bank subsidiary
It was converted into a cooperative bank
It was classified by RBI as a regional rural bank
85.x: Following LIC’s acquisition of a majority stake in 2019, RBI reclassified IDBI Bank as a private sector lender.
85.tq: Link the transaction to its direct regulatory consequence.

85.s: The Government and LIC proposed to sell what proportion of their combined strategic stake in IDBI Bank?
85.x: The Government and LIC proposed the sale of a combined 60.72% strategic stake in IDBI Bank.
85.tq: Use the exact percentage rather than approximating the strategic stake.

85.s:
Minority stake sales were considered in which of the following public sector banks for meeting minimum public shareholding requirements?
1. UCO Bank
2. Bank of Maharashtra
3. Central Bank of India
4. Indian Overseas Bank
85.x: Minority stake sales were considered in UCO Bank, Bank of Maharashtra, Central Bank of India, Punjab & Sind Bank and Indian Overseas Bank. Thus, all four listed banks are included.
85.tq: Check the complete membership of the listed group before selecting the combination.

85.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. It came into force on 1 August 2025.
2. It made amendments across four principal banking-related enactments.
3. It made 19 amendments in all.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: The Act came into force on 1 August 2025 and made 19 amendments across the RBI Act, Banking Regulation Act, SBI Act, and the Banking Companies Acts of 1970 and 1980.
85.tq: Combine the date, count and legislative scope in a coded statement question.

85.s: Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, the threshold for ‘substantial interest’ was raised from ₹5 lakh to:
85.x: The threshold for substantial interest was raised from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore.
85.tq: Distinguish the revised threshold from the earlier amount.

85.s: The tenure of directors of cooperative banks was extended under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 from:
85.x: The Act increased the tenure of cooperative bank directors from 8 years to 10 years.
85.tq: Test both the original and revised limits in a close-number comparison.

85.s: Unclaimed shares of public sector banks may be transferred to which of the following under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025?
85.x: The Act permits unclaimed public sector bank shares to be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).
85.tq: Identify the statutory fund associated with unclaimed investor assets.

85.s: AITUC characterised the proposed High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat as:
o: A proposal to abolish priority sector lending
A clear call to nationalise private banks
A measure to merge all cooperative banks
A clear call to privatise public sector banks
85.x: AITUC described the committee as a clear call to privatisation of public sector banks.
85.tq: Match the stakeholder’s criticism with the policy debate it addressed.

85.s: Which of the following correctly describes the ownership status of DICGC?
o: It is owned by all scheduled commercial banks
It is an autonomous department of the Ministry of Finance
It is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India
It is a jointly owned subsidiary of RBI and SEBI
85.x: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.
85.tq: Apply the ‘who owns or supervises this body?’ test.

85.s: The present deposit insurance cover provided by DICGC is:
85.x: DICGC provides insurance cover of ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.
85.tq: Distinguish the present cover limit from the earlier limit.

85.s: The DICGC deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in the Budget for:
85.x: The deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in the 2020–21 Budget, following the PMC Bank crisis.
85.tq: Connect the revised figure with the budget year in which it was introduced.

85.s: Which of the following categories of deposits is NOT covered by DICGC insurance?
o: Deposits in branches of foreign banks operating in India
85.x: DICGC covers commercial banks, including foreign bank branches, regional rural banks and cooperative banks, but excludes deposits of foreign, Central and State governments.
85.tq: Find the excluded category rather than the widely covered banking categories.

85.s: Which one of the following is excluded from DICGC insurance coverage?
o: Savings deposits of individuals in commercial banks
85.x: Inter-bank deposits are excluded from DICGC insurance coverage. Individual deposits in the listed banking categories are generally covered subject to the limit.
85.tq: Use the exclusion list to separate institutional deposits from ordinary depositor accounts.

85.s: With regard to DICGC insurance, who bears the premium burden?
o: The insured bank, and not the depositor
RBI and the depositor in equal shares
85.x: Banks pay the DICGC insurance premium; the depositor does not pay it.
85.tq: Identify the party responsible for payment rather than the beneficiary of insurance.

85.s: Which of the following deposits is not covered under the DICGC scheme?
o: Deposits of a regional rural bank
Deposits of a foreign bank branch in India
85.x: Deposits accepted by NBFCs are not covered by DICGC, whereas the other listed banking institutions fall within the covered categories.
85.tq: Apply the banking-entity distinction to identify the excluded institution.

85.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Basel Accords — Bank capital, liquidity and risk
2. Basel Convention — Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
3. Basel Accords — UNEP-administered treaty
4. Basel Convention — BCBS/BIS framework
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
85.x: The Basel Accords concern bank capital, liquidity and risk and are associated with BCBS/BIS. The Basel Convention is a UNEP-administered treaty on hazardous wastes; therefore pairs 3 and 4 are reversed.
85.tq: Separate the similarly named financial framework from the environmental treaty.

85.s: The Basel Convention was adopted in 1989 and came into force in:
85.x: The Basel Convention on hazardous wastes was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992.
85.tq: Distinguish the adoption year from the year of entry into force.

85.s: Which one of the following bodies is associated with the Basel Accords?
o: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and BIS
85.x: The Basel Accords are associated with the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) and the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), based in Basel, Switzerland.
85.tq: Identify the institution by its subject area rather than by the shared name ‘Basel’.

85.s: The Basel Convention primarily deals with:
o: Cross-border movement and disposal of hazardous wastes
85.x: The Basel Convention is an environmental treaty dealing with the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal.
85.tq: Use the environmental subject to distinguish the convention from the banking accords.

85.s: The P.J. Nayak Committee, constituted in 2014, primarily identified weaknesses in the:
o: Governance of public sector bank boards
85.x: The P.J. Nayak Committee found that governance of public sector bank boards was weak and recommended structural changes.
85.tq: Match the committee with its central institutional diagnosis.

85.s:
Which of the following was proposed by the P.J. Nayak Committee?
1. Creation of a Bank Investment Company
2. Reduction of the Government’s stake below 50 percent
3. Professionalisation of public sector bank boards
85.x: The committee proposed a Bank Investment Company to hold the Government’s stake, reduction of that stake below 50 percent, and professional boards for public sector banks.
85.tq: Recognise the reform package rather than isolating one recommendation.

85.s: The Banks Board Bureau was established in 2016 as an idea associated with which initiative?
85.x: The Banks Board Bureau originated from the Indradhanush initiative and began functioning in 2016.
85.tq: Link the institutional reform body with the programme from which it emerged.

85.s: The Banks Board Bureau consisted of a chairman, how many ex-officio members and how many experts?
85.x: The Banks Board Bureau had one chairman, three ex-officio members and five experts.
85.tq: Recall the composition by separating ex-officio members from expert members.

85.s: In 2022, the Banks Board Bureau was replaced by the:
85.x: The Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) replaced the Banks Board Bureau in 2022.
85.tq: Use the successor institution to resolve a governance-body question.

85.s: The Union Budget 2021–22 announced the privatisation of:
o: Three public sector banks and one general insurance company
Two private banks and one public sector insurer
One public sector bank and two life insurance companies
Two public sector banks and one general insurance company
85.x: The Budget 2021–22 announced the privatisation of two public sector banks and one general insurance company.
85.tq: Keep the numerical composition of the privatisation announcement intact.

85.s: Which of the following correctly represents a major argument in the debate over privatisation of public sector banks?
o: Public ownership has no connection with financial inclusion
Privatisation may improve efficiency and governance, while public ownership supports social mandates
Privatisation necessarily eliminates rural branches and priority lending in every case
Privatisation is intended primarily to increase deposit insurance cover
85.x: The debate balances possible gains in efficiency and governance against the social mandate of public sector banks, including rural branches and priority lending.
85.tq: Compare the two sides of the policy debate without treating either as absolute.

85.s:
Which of the following was included in the banking-related measures announced in the Union Budget 2026–27?
1. High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat
2. Restructuring of PFC and REC
3. Activation of the countercyclical capital buffer by RBI
85.x: The Budget 2026–27 announced the High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat and restructuring of PFC and REC. RBI had kept the countercyclical capital buffer inactive, so statement 3 is false.
85.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the stated status of a policy instrument.

85.s: As of May 2026, the Reserve Bank of India had kept the countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB):
o: Activated only for public sector banks
85.x: RBI had kept the countercyclical capital buffer inactive, or unactivated, as of May 2026.
85.tq: Distinguish an inactive policy instrument from one that is selectively operational.

85.s: Who founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam?
85.x: Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
85.tq: Use the founder–institution association rather than the merger fact.

85.s: The merger of Andhra Bank into Union Bank of India became effective on:
85.x: Andhra Bank was merged into Union Bank of India with effect from 1 April 2020.
85.tq: Distinguish the effective date from other dates associated with the merger process.

85.s: The four regional rural banks operating in Andhra Pradesh were consolidated into:
o: Union Rural Bank of Andhra Pradesh
85.x: The four Andhra Pradesh RRBs were consolidated to form Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank.
85.tq: Identify the common successor from a consolidation question.

85.s: Which of the following is cited as a criticism of public sector bank privatisation by trade unions?
o: It would make recapitalisation unnecessary in every case
It would weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion
It would increase the number of rural branches automatically
It would eliminate all integration costs arising from mergers
85.x: Trade unions have argued that privatisation could weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion.
85.tq: Connect the policy proposal with its stated social-sector concern.

85.s: Which one of the following is identified as a possible cost of bank mergers?
o: Removal of the social mandate of all banks
85.x: Bank mergers can involve significant integration costs, including the task of combining systems, personnel and operations.
85.tq: Select the direct operational consequence rather than an absolute claim.

85.s: Following consolidation, recapitalisation and the 4Rs, the CRAR of scheduled commercial banks and public sector banks stood respectively at:
85.x: The CRAR reached 17.36% for scheduled commercial banks and 16.10% for public sector banks.
85.tq: Preserve the order of the two categories while comparing closely related percentages.

85.s: Scheduled commercial bank credit increased from ₹67 lakh crore in March 2015 to approximately what amount in March 2025?
85.x: Scheduled commercial bank credit increased from ₹67 lakh crore in March 2015 to ₹181 lakh crore in March 2025.
85.tq: Compare the initial and terminal values over the stated period.

85.s: The October 2025 draft on differentiated risk weights proposed lower risk weights for which categories?
o: Gold loans and foreign currency deposits
85.x: The draft proposed lower differentiated risk weights for MSMEs and real estate, which would reduce minimum capital needs.
85.tq: Match the proposed regulatory relief with the specified sectors.

85.s: A shift to the expected credit loss (ECL) framework was estimated to reduce Tier-1 capital ratios by approximately:
85.x: The expected credit loss shift was estimated to reduce Tier-1 ratios by about 100–150 basis points.
85.tq: Use the stated range and avoid confusing percentage points with basis points.

86.s: A loan or advance is generally classified as a Non-Performing Asset when the interest or principal instalment remains overdue for more than:
86.x: An asset becomes an NPA when interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
86.tq: Use the precise numerical threshold rather than a nearby overdue period.

86.s: In the case of farm loans, the overdue criterion for a short-duration crop is generally:
86.x: For short-duration crops, a farm loan is treated as overdue after two crop seasons.
86.tq: Distinguish crop-season rules from the general 90-day banking rule.

86.s: For a farm loan relating to a long-duration crop, the overdue criterion is:
86.x: For long-duration crops, the relevant overdue period is one crop season.
86.tq: Test the confusable pair of one crop season and two crop seasons.

86.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Standard asset — NPA for more than 12 months
Sub-standard asset — NPA for 12 months or less
Doubtful asset — regular account with no overdue
Loss asset — asset that has been fully recovered
86.x: A sub-standard asset is an NPA for 12 months or less. A doubtful asset is an NPA for more than 12 months, while a loss asset has been identified as a loss but may not yet have been written off.
86.tq: Match each classification with its exact time or recognition criterion.

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the new borrower-level NPA tagging system:
1. The system is to be effective from 1 April 2027.
2. If one loan of a borrower becomes an NPA, all loans of that borrower at the same bank become NPAs.
3. An account can be upgraded even if arrears on one facility remain unpaid.
4. Banks are required to identify NPAs through automated systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. An account is upgraded only after all arrears on every facility have been paid, so statement 3 is false.
86.tq: Find the single reversal in the condition for upgrading an account.

86.s: Special Mention Accounts are best described as accounts which are:
o: Stressed but still classified as standard
Loans overdue for more than 180 days
86.x: Special Mention Accounts are stressed accounts that remain standard, generally involving overdue periods of 1 to 90 days.
86.tq: Separate an early-warning category from the NPA categories.

86.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Special Mention Accounts.
List-I
 a. SMA-0
 b. SMA-1
 c. SMA-2
 d. NPA
List-II
 i. 61–90 days overdue
 ii. More than 90 days overdue
 iii. 0–30 days overdue
 iv. 31–60 days overdue
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
86.x: SMA-0 covers 0–30 days, SMA-1 covers 31–60 days, SMA-2 covers 61–90 days, and an NPA is generally beyond 90 days overdue.
86.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched day bands.

86.s: The usual progression of asset stress is:
o: NPA, SMA-2, SMA-1, SMA-0, standard asset
SMA-0, SMA-1, SMA-2, sub-standard, doubtful, loss
86.x: The sequence proceeds from SMA-0 to SMA-1 and SMA-2, followed by NPA classification as sub-standard, doubtful and loss.
86.tq: Arrange the stages from early stress to severe deterioration.

86.s: Stressed assets comprise:
o: NPAs, restructured loans and written-off assets
Only gross NPAs and net NPAs
86.x: Stressed assets include NPAs, restructured loans and written-off assets.
86.tq: Test the exact components of a composite banking term.

86.s: The Interest Coverage Ratio is calculated as:
o: Net profit divided by total assets
Interest due divided by operating earnings
Operating earnings divided by interest due
86.x: Interest Coverage Ratio equals operating earnings, or EBIT, divided by interest due.
86.tq: Recall the numerator-denominator order in the formula.

86.s: If the Interest Coverage Ratio of a borrower is below 1, it indicates that:
o: The borrower has no outstanding debt
The borrower's earnings exceed its interest obligation
The borrower's earnings do not cover the interest due
The loan has necessarily been written off
86.x: An Interest Coverage Ratio below 1 means that operating earnings are insufficient to cover interest due.
86.tq: Apply the formula to interpret a risk indicator rather than merely recalling its definition.

86.s: Net NPA is obtained by deducting which of the following from Gross NPA?
86.x: Net NPA is calculated as Gross NPA minus provisions.
86.tq: Distinguish the stock of bad loans from the amount remaining after provisioning.

86.s: The GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks reached an approximate peak of 11.2 per cent in:
86.x: SCB GNPA peaked at approximately 11.2 per cent in March 2018, after the Asset Quality Review.
86.tq: Use the peak-year clue to distinguish pre-AQR, post-AQR and recovery-period figures.

86.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the SCB GNPA position in March 2025?
86.x: In March 2025, SCB GNPA was approximately 2.2–2.3 per cent and NNPA was 0.5 per cent.
86.tq: Match the date with the correct ratio instead of relying on the direction of the trend alone.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about GNPA trends:
1. SCB GNPA was 4.28 per cent in March 2015.
2. SCB GNPA was approximately 11.2 per cent in March 2018.
3. SCB GNPA was 2.15 per cent in September 2025.
4. SCB GNPA was 1.93 per cent in March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All four statements correctly state the reported GNPA figures for the respective dates.
86.tq: Cross-check each date-value pair, especially the closely spaced 2025 and 2026 observations.

86.s: The GNPA of Scheduled Commercial Banks in March 2026, together with the corresponding NNPA, was:
86.x: In March 2026, GNPA was 1.93 per cent and NNPA was 0.39 per cent, described as a decadal low.
86.tq: Pair the two related ratios with the same reporting date.

86.s:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the banking-sector NPA trend?
1. GNPA has fallen for eight straight years.
2. Agriculture GNPA remains relatively high at about 6.0 per cent.
3. Agriculture GNPA is lower than 1 per cent.
4. September 2025 GNPA was reported at 2.15 per cent.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
86.x: Statement 3 is incorrect because agriculture GNPA was reported at about 6.0 per cent, with another estimate at 5.7 per cent. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
86.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the reported sectoral trend.

86.s: Between March 2015 and March 2025, the GNPA ratio of Public Sector Banks declined from:
86.x: PSB GNPA declined from 4.97 per cent in March 2015 to 2.58 per cent in March 2025.
86.tq: Read both endpoints and check the direction of change.

86.s: Which of the following private-bank GNPA figures for June 2026 is correctly matched?
86.x: The reported June 2026 GNPA figures were HDFC 1.17 per cent, ICICI 1.38 per cent and Axis 1.28 per cent.
86.tq: Use institution-figure pairing to avoid swapping closely related percentages.

86.s: Provisioning Coverage Ratio is defined as:
o: Provisions held divided by total deposits
Gross NPAs divided by provisions held
Net NPAs divided by Gross NPAs
Provisions held divided by Gross NPAs
86.x: PCR is the ratio of provisions held to Gross NPAs.
86.tq: Distinguish the coverage ratio from its reciprocal.

86.s: The PCR of Scheduled Commercial Banks reported for March 2025 was:
86.x: The reported SCB PCR for March 2025 was 76.3 per cent. A higher figure of 93.14 per cent was also cited in a context that included technical write-offs.
86.tq: Match the exact percentage with the correct institutional aggregate and date.

86.s: Under income-recognition norms, interest on an NPA is booked as income:
o: Only when it is actually received
After the asset is written off
When it is accrued, whether or not received
86.x: Interest on an NPA is not recognised as income until it is actually received. This forms part of the IRACP framework.
86.tq: Apply the recognition rule to distinguish accrual from actual receipt.

86.s: IRACP stands for:
o: Indian Regulation of Accounts and Credit Policy
86.x: IRACP means Income Recognition, Asset Classification, Provisioning.
86.tq: Test the exact expansion of a regulatory acronym.

86.s:
Match the stages of the Expected Credit Loss model with their provisioning treatment.
List-I
 a. Stage 1
 b. Stage 2
 c. Stage 3
 d. EIR method
List-II
 i. Lifetime expected loss
 ii. Effective interest rate method
 iii. 12-month expected loss
 iv. Full lifetime provision for credit-impaired assets
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
86.x: Stage 1 involves 12-month expected loss, Stage 2 lifetime loss, Stage 3 full lifetime provision, and loss allowances use the effective interest rate method.
86.tq: Start with the distinctive EIR pair and then match the three stages by severity.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the Expected Credit Loss model:
1. Stage 1 applies to low-risk exposures.
2. Stage 2 applies when there is a significant rise in risk.
3. Stage 3 applies to credit-impaired assets, including those overdue for more than 90 days.
4. ECL may reduce Tier-1 ratios by 100–150 basis points.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All four statements are correct descriptions of the proposed three-stage ECL framework and its possible effect on Tier-1 ratios.
86.tq: Check whether the final quantitative implication is also supported rather than stopping at the conceptual statements.

86.s: The twin balance sheet problem refers to the simultaneous existence of:
o: High exports and low public debt
Fiscal surplus and excess bank liquidity
High household savings and low inflation
Over-leveraged corporates and capital-starved, NPA-laden banks
86.x: The twin balance sheet problem describes over-leveraged firms alongside capital-starved banks burdened with NPAs.
86.tq: Identify the two linked balance-sheet weaknesses rather than one symptom alone.

86.s: The twin balance sheet problem was prominently framed in the Economic Survey:
86.x: The Economic Survey 2016–17, under Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, discussed the festering twin balance sheet problem.
86.tq: Use the year and institutional context together to avoid nearby Economic Survey years.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the mechanism of the twin balance sheet problem:
1. Loan losses erode bank capital.
2. Banks may freeze new lending rather than recall old loans.
3. Private investment can decline as a result.
4. Over-leveraged firms are able to undertake fresh investment without difficulty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Over-leveraged firms face difficulty investing, so statement 4 is false.
86.tq: Trace the cause-effect chain and reject the statement that reverses its final effect.

86.s: Aggressive lending during 2010–15 was especially associated with which sectors in the build-up of NPAs?
86.x: Aggressive lending to infrastructure, steel and power projects during 2010–15 contributed to the later NPA problem, particularly when projects stalled.
86.tq: Link the lending episode with the specific sectoral cluster.

86.s: Which of the following external developments weakened borrowers' cash flows and contributed to NPAs?
o: A fall in domestic savings alone
The 2008 global financial crisis and weak exports
A sharp rise in agricultural exports alone
The introduction of GST and higher tax compliance
86.x: The 2008 crisis and weak exports adversely affected borrowers' cash flows and contributed to stress in bank assets.
86.tq: Select the paired external shocks that explain the deterioration in repayment capacity.

86.s: A wilful defaulter is a borrower who:
o: Can pay but does not, or diverts borrowed funds
Cannot pay because of a temporary fall in income
Has an account overdue for less than 30 days
Has repaid the loan before its due date
86.x: A wilful defaulter has the capacity to repay but refuses to do so or diverts the borrowed funds.
86.tq: Distinguish deliberate non-payment from inability to repay.

86.s: Evergreening of loans means:
o: Writing off all old loans immediately
Converting all NPAs into equity automatically
Giving fresh loans to repay old loans and conceal default
86.x: Evergreening involves extending fresh loans to repay old loans, thereby keeping the underlying default hidden.
86.tq: Recognise the concealment mechanism rather than confuse it with write-off or restructuring.

86.s: Which one of the following was a direct effect of the Asset Quality Review on evergreening?
o: It strengthened the practice of concealing defaults
It reduced the need for provisioning
It ended the practice of evergreening by uncovering hidden stress
It converted all loans into standard assets
86.x: The Asset Quality Review exposed hidden stress and ended the practice of keeping defaults concealed through evergreening.
86.tq: Connect the regulatory intervention with its specific outcome.

86.s:
Which combination correctly identifies two structural causes of NPAs?
1. Weak credit appraisal
2. Slow recovery laws
3. Automatic repayment by promoters
4. Strict appraisal of every infrastructure project
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
86.x: Weak credit appraisal and slow recovery laws contributed to NPAs. Automatic repayment and strict appraisal are not causes identified in this context.
86.tq: Separate documented weaknesses from statements that describe their opposite.

86.s:
Arrange the following stages of the NPA vicious cycle in the correct sequence:
A. Provisioning and capital erosion
B. Aggressive lending and external shocks
C. Weak credit growth
D. Accumulation of NPAs
86.x: Aggressive lending and shocks lead to NPAs, which require provisioning and cause capital erosion, resulting in weak credit growth.
86.tq: Follow the causal sequence from initial shock to the final credit consequence.

86.s: The Asset Quality Review was carried out by the RBI in:
86.x: The RBI conducted the Asset Quality Review in 2015.
86.tq: Recall the intervention year and distinguish it from the later NPA peak.

86.s: The principal purpose of the Asset Quality Review was to:
o: Increase bank deposits through higher interest rates
Uncover hidden NPAs and make banks recognise them
Provide automatic loan waivers to infrastructure companies
86.x: The AQR was designed to uncover hidden NPAs and ensure that banks recognised the underlying asset quality problems.
86.tq: Identify the regulatory purpose rather than a general banking reform objective.

86.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Asset Quality Review?
1. Disclosed NPAs increased sharply.
2. NPA levels peaked in 2018.
3. The twin balance sheet problem was exposed.
4. Hidden defaults continued to be classified as standard in all cases.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
86.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The AQR was intended to end, not perpetuate, the concealment of defaults as standard assets.
86.tq: Reject the absolute reversal of the review's transparency objective.

86.s: The Government's 4R strategy in response to the banking-sector stress consisted of:
86.x: The four Rs were Recognise, Resolve, Recapitalise and Reform. The response included the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL.
86.tq: Recall the exact expansion of a policy framework acronym.

86.s:
Which of the following measures formed part of the Government's response to the NPA problem under the 4R strategy?
1. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
2. Bank recapitalisation
3. National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited
4. Abolition of provisioning norms
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
86.x: The response included the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL. Provisioning norms were not abolished.
86.tq: Identify the genuine policy instruments and eliminate the measure that contradicts banking prudence.

86.s: The new rules relating to Non-Performing Assets and Expected Credit Loss (ECL) are scheduled to come into force from:
86.x: The new NPA and ECL rules are scheduled to be implemented from 1 April 2027.
86.tq: Use the precise implementation date to distinguish the correct option from nearby dates.

86.s: The Gross Non-Performing Asset (GNPA) ratio of banks reached a record low of what level in September 2025?
86.x: The GNPA ratio stood at a record low of 2.15% in September 2025.
86.tq: Match the exact percentage with its stated reference period.

86.s: With the cleaning up of bank balance sheets, Scheduled Commercial Bank (SCB) credit nearly increased from:
o: ₹76 lakh crore in 2015 to ₹181 lakh crore in 2025
₹67 lakh crore in 2015 to ₹181 lakh crore in 2025
₹67 lakh crore in 2015 to ₹118 lakh crore in 2025
₹181 lakh crore in 2015 to ₹67 lakh crore in 2025
86.x: SCB credit nearly tripled from ₹67 lakh crore in 2015 to ₹181 lakh crore in 2025, alongside the cleaning up of bank balance sheets.
86.tq: Check both endpoints and the direction of change before selecting the comparison.

86.s: The Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) of Scheduled Commercial Banks is reported at:
86.x: The reported CRAR of Scheduled Commercial Banks is 17.3%.
86.tq: Distinguish the exact percentage from closely related figures by retaining the decimal value.

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank in FY26:
1. Its GNPA was reported at 0.91%.
2. Its NNPA was reported as nil.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: Both statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank reported GNPA of 0.91% and NNPA as nil in FY26.
86.tq: Verify each numerical statement independently before choosing the combined code.

86.s: Which one of the following is identified as a criticism or concern associated with the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) approach?
o: It prevents the recognition of all stressed assets.
It eliminates the need for capital adequacy requirements.
It raises the capital needs of banks.
86.x: A key criticism of the ECL approach is that it raises the capital needs of banks.
86.tq: Identify the practical consequence directly linked to the policy approach and reject absolute claims.

86.s: Approximately what proportion of written-off loans was recovered, highlighting that low NPAs are partly attributable to write-offs?
86.x: Only about 13% of written-off loans were recovered, indicating that low NPAs are partly explained by write-offs rather than complete recovery.
86.tq: Use the approximate recovery percentage to distinguish recovery from write-off-based reduction in NPAs.

87.s: In the context of banking supervision, PCA stands for:
87.x: PCA stands for Prompt Corrective Action, a framework used by the Reserve Bank of India to intervene in banks with weakening financial health.
87.tq: Test the exact expansion of a frequently confused institutional acronym.

87.s: The Prompt Corrective Action framework was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in:
87.x: The RBI introduced the Prompt Corrective Action framework in 2002 to monitor and restrict banks whose financial metrics deteriorate.
87.tq: Use the year-based direct-recall method for a regulatory framework.

87.s: Which of the following correctly represents the current trigger parameters under the revised Prompt Corrective Action framework?
o: Capital adequacy, branch expansion and dividends
87.x: The current PCA triggers are capital, measured through CRAR and CET1, asset quality measured through net NPA, and leverage measured through the Tier-1 leverage ratio.
87.tq: Identify the exact three-part regulatory classification rather than an associated restriction.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revised Prompt Corrective Action framework:
1. It was issued in November 2021.
2. It came into effect on 1 January 2022.
3. Profitability measured through Return on Assets remained a trigger under the revised framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: The revised framework was issued in November 2021 and took effect on 1 January 2022. The earlier Return on Assets profitability trigger was dropped.
87.tq: Split the statements by date and use the dropped-trigger distinction to eliminate the false statement.

87.s: Which one of the following is NOT a current trigger parameter under the revised PCA framework?
87.x: Return on Assets was an earlier profitability trigger but was dropped from the revised PCA framework. Net NPA, Tier-1 leverage and capital indicators remain relevant triggers.
87.tq: Find the omitted earlier parameter in an EXCEPT-style question.

87.s:
Match List-I with List-II in respect of PCA trigger parameters:
List-I (Trigger parameter)
a. Capital
b. Asset quality
c. Leverage

List-II (Indicator)
i. Net NPA ratio
ii. Tier-1 leverage ratio
iii. CRAR/Common Equity Tier 1

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
87.x: Capital is assessed through CRAR and Common Equity Tier 1, asset quality through the net NPA ratio, and leverage through the Tier-1 leverage ratio.
87.tq: Start from the sure indicator-parameter pair and eliminate codes containing mismatches.

87.s: Under the 2017 PCA framework, a CRAR between 7.75 per cent and 10.25 per cent corresponded to:
87.x: Under the 2017 framework, CRAR between 7.75 per cent and 10.25 per cent represented Threshold 1.
87.tq: Use the numerical range to distinguish adjacent PCA thresholds.

87.s: Which of the following correctly states the CRAR ranges associated with Threshold 2 under the 2017 PCA framework?
87.x: Threshold 2 was associated with a CRAR between 6.25 per cent and 7.75 per cent. A CET1 below 3.625 per cent represented Threshold 3.
87.tq: Compare neighbouring numerical thresholds rather than relying on the direction of the numbers alone.

87.s: A CET1 level below 3.625 per cent under the 2017 PCA framework indicated:
87.x: A CET1 level below 3.625 per cent was specified as Threshold 3 under the 2017 PCA framework.
87.tq: Test the exact cut-off associated with the most severe stated threshold.

87.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to net NPA and the 2017 PCA thresholds is correct?
o: Net NPA of 6–9 per cent — no threshold; net NPA of 12 per cent or more — Threshold 2
Net NPA of 6–9 per cent — Threshold 3; net NPA of 12 per cent or more — Threshold 1
Net NPA of 6–9 per cent — Threshold 1; net NPA of 12 per cent or more — Threshold 3
Net NPA of 6–9 per cent — Threshold 2; net NPA of 12 per cent or more — Threshold 1
87.x: A net NPA ratio of 6–9 per cent corresponded to Threshold 1, while a net NPA ratio of 12 per cent or more corresponded to Threshold 3.
87.tq: Check both ends of a numerical comparison and reject the reversed mapping.

87.s: Which of the following is generally associated with a bank being placed under the PCA framework?
o: Unrestricted branch expansion until profitability improves
Restrictions and monitoring until capital and asset quality recover
87.x: Banks with weak financial metrics are placed under watch and face restrictions until their capital and asset quality recover.
87.tq: Apply the purpose of the framework to a banking-supervision scenario.

87.s:
Under the PCA framework, restrictions may relate to:
1. Lending and risky exposures
2. Branch expansion
3. Dividend payments and management pay
4. Capital infusion, change of management or merger ordered by the RBI
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: PCA restrictions can cover lending, risky exposures, branch expansion, dividends and management pay. The RBI may also order capital infusion, a management change or a merger.
87.tq: Recognise that the framework includes both operational restrictions and structural corrective measures.

87.s:
Arrange the following earlier debt-resolution mechanisms in chronological order of their introduction:
A. Strategic Debt Restructuring
B. Corporate Debt Restructuring
C. S4A
D. 5/25 scheme
87.x: Corporate Debt Restructuring was introduced in 2001, followed by the 5/25 scheme in 2014, Strategic Debt Restructuring in 2015 and S4A in 2016.
87.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then arrange the intervening years.

87.s: Corporate Debt Restructuring, introduced in 2001, primarily provided for:
o: Conversion of all bank debt into government equity
Recovery of small loans through compromise
Joint restructuring of large multi-bank loans
Refinancing of infrastructure loans every five years
87.x: CDR involved joint restructuring of large loans owed to multiple banks, generally outside the court process.
87.tq: Match the mechanism with its defining institutional feature.

87.s: The 5/25 scheme introduced in 2014 related to:
o: Loans with a five-day repayment period and a 25 per cent interest subsidy
Conversion of 25 per cent of debt into equity after five years
Resolution of stressed assets within five months and 25 days
Infrastructure and core loans amortised over up to 25 years and refinanced every 5 years
87.x: The 5/25 scheme allowed infrastructure and core-sector loans to be amortised over up to 25 years, with refinancing at five-year intervals.
87.tq: Decode the numerical title by linking each number to the correct loan feature.

87.s: Under Strategic Debt Restructuring, lenders could:
o: Write off all debt without taking any control over the borrower
Recover dues exclusively through Lok Adalats
Convert debt into a majority equity stake of 51 per cent or more and change the management
Convert only 5 per cent of debt into preference shares
87.x: SDR, introduced in 2015, allowed lenders to convert debt into a majority equity stake of 51 per cent or more and change the management of the borrowing company.
87.tq: Use the lender-power and 51 per cent ownership clue to distinguish SDR from other mechanisms.

87.s: S4A is the acronym for:
o: Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets
Strategic Scheme for Secured Asset Allocation
System for Adjustment of Stressed Accounts
87.x: S4A stands for Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets, introduced by the RBI in 2016.
87.tq: Test the precise expansion of a similar-looking financial restructuring acronym.

87.s: The principal feature of the S4A scheme was to:
o: Replace the borrower’s debt entirely with deposits
Split the debt of stressed firms into sustainable and unsustainable portions
Permit refinancing of all loans once every 25 years
Transfer every stressed loan to the central government
87.x: S4A reworked the financial structure of stressed firms by dividing debt into sustainable and unsustainable parts.
87.tq: Identify the mechanism from the specific restructuring action it permits.

87.s: Project Sashakt was associated with which of the following?
o: A 2015 conversion of debt into 51 per cent equity
A 2014 refinancing scheme for infrastructure loans
A 2016 division of debt into sustainable and unsustainable portions
A 2018 Inter-Creditor Agreement for faster resolution of stressed consortium loans
87.x: Project Sashakt, introduced in 2018, provided an Inter-Creditor Agreement aimed at faster resolution of stressed consortium loans.
87.tq: Use the year-feature combination to separate Sashakt from SDR, S4A and 5/25.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Project Sashakt:
1. It was associated with the Sunil Mehta Committee.
2. The lead bank drives the resolution plan.
3. The plan binds all lenders once 66 per cent of lenders approve it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Project Sashakt was associated with the Sunil Mehta Committee. Its Inter-Creditor Agreement provides for the lead bank to drive the plan, which binds all lenders after approval by 66 per cent of lenders.
87.tq: Combine committee, procedural authority and approval-threshold facts in one coded question.

87.s: The Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets was issued on:
87.x: The Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets was issued on 7 June 2019.
87.tq: Distinguish a specific notification date from the effective date of a different framework.

87.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets?
o: A 30-day review after default, mandatory ICA and resolution within 180 days
A five-day review after default, mandatory auction and resolution within 66 days
A 90-day review after default, no ICA and resolution within 365 days
A 60-day notice, voluntary ICA and resolution within 25 years
87.x: The Prudential Framework requires a 30-day review after default, makes the Inter-Creditor Agreement mandatory and envisages resolution within 180 days.
87.tq: Match the resolution framework with its distinctive review period, ICA rule and deadline.

87.s: Which of the following mechanisms is specifically intended to settle small loans through compromise?
87.x: Lok Adalats provide a mechanism for settling small loans through compromise.
87.tq: Identify the institution from the scale and method of loan settlement.

87.s: Debt Recovery Tribunals are recovery tribunals established under the:
87.x: Debt Recovery Tribunals are recovery tribunals established under the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993, commonly referred to as the RDDBFI Act.
87.tq: Distinguish the statutory basis of DRTs from other debt-recovery laws.

87.s: Under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act, lenders holding what proportion of the dues may issue the relevant 60-day notice?
87.x: Under the stated SARFAESI provision, lenders holding 75 per cent of the dues issue a 60-day notice under Section 13(2).
87.tq: Separate the ownership threshold from the notice period and approval threshold used in other mechanisms.

87.s: Which of the following actions may be taken under Section 13(4) of the SARFAESI Act after the requisite notice?
o: Automatic conversion of debt into government equity
Compulsory settlement through a Lok Adalat
Taking possession, taking over management or selling the secured asset
87.x: Section 13(4) permits measures such as taking possession of the secured asset, taking over management and selling the asset for recovery.
87.tq: Match the statutory section with the powers it authorises.

87.s: A borrower’s right to redeem the secured asset under Section 13(8) of the SARFAESI Act is linked to:
o: Approval by 66 per cent of lenders
Payment of full dues before the auction notice
Payment of 25 per cent of dues after the auction
87.x: The borrower can redeem the secured asset by paying the full dues before publication of the auction notice, as associated with Section 13(8).
87.tq: Apply the redemption rule to the timing of payment in a recovery scenario.

87.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: ARCs — registered with RBI under SARFAESI
CDR — restructuring outside court for large multi-bank borrowers
Lok Adalats — conversion of lender debt into a 51 per cent equity stake
ARCs — purchase bad loans against security receipts
87.x: Conversion of lender debt into a 51 per cent or more equity stake is associated with Strategic Debt Restructuring, not Lok Adalats. ARCs, CDR and Lok Adalats have the other stated functions.
87.tq: Find the wrong mechanism-feature pairing by checking who performs the action.

87.s: Which body clarified the operation of Section 13(8) redemption and auction-stay rules in the stated Andhra Pradesh context?
o: A division bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
The Andhra Pradesh State Finance Commission
The Reserve Bank of India’s Central Board
A single judge of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
87.x: A division bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court clarified the Section 13(8) redemption and auction-stay rules in the stated May 2026 context.
87.tq: Use the judicial-composition clue to distinguish a division bench from other authorities.
