96.x: The concept of declared goods of special importance was dropped under the GST framework. Destination-based taxation, input tax credit and taxation of supply are GST features.
96.tq: Test the discontinued concept against continuing GST mechanisms.

96.s: Which one of the following is NOT retained outside GST?
96.x: Central Excise Duty was subsumed into GST. Basic Customs Duty, stamp duty and electricity duty are retained outside GST.
96.tq: Find the one item that does not belong among retained taxes.

96.s: A supplier pays tax on inputs and seeks to set it off against the tax payable on outward supplies. This facility is known as:
96.x: Input Tax Credit allows tax paid on inputs to be set off against output tax. It helps prevent cascading of taxes.
96.tq: Identify the mechanism from its practical business operation.

96.s: Under the Reverse Charge Mechanism in GST, the liability to pay tax is shifted from the:
96.x: Under reverse charge, the recipient, rather than the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.
96.tq: Distinguish the direction of liability by asking who actually remits the tax.

96.s: The anti-profiteering provision under Section 171 of the Central Goods and Services Tax framework is intended to ensure that:
o: The benefit of tax-rate reductions or input-tax credit reaches consumers
The supplier is exempt from GST when prices rise
All GST rates remain unchanged permanently
96.x: Section 171 requires the benefit of a rate reduction or input-tax credit to be passed on to consumers through commensurate reduction in prices.
96.tq: Link the statutory mechanism with its consumer-protection objective.

96.s: With effect from 1 October 2024, cases relating to anti-profiteering are handled by the:
o: Principal Bench of the GST Appellate Tribunal
96.x: From 1 October 2024, the Principal Bench of GSTAT handles anti-profiteering cases. The earlier institutional arrangements included the National Anti-Profiteering Authority and subsequently the CCI.
96.tq: Use the effective-date clue to identify the current adjudicatory body.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about the electronic way bill:
1. It is an electronic document used for movement of goods.
2. It is required for goods valued above ₹50,000.
3. Its validity is one day for every 200 kilometres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: An e-way bill is an electronic document for movement of goods valued above ₹50,000, with validity of one day per 200 kilometres.
96.tq: Verify the document, value threshold and validity-period statements together.

96.s: Under the destination principle of GST, tax revenue primarily accrues to the State:
o: Where the goods or services are consumed
96.x: The destination principle assigns revenue to the State of consumption rather than the State of production or registration.
96.tq: Distinguish destination-based taxation from origin-based taxation.

96.s: A registered person opts for the composition scheme. Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the scheme?
o: ₹50 lakh goods turnover, ₹1.5 crore services turnover, 1% goods, 6% services and no ITC
₹1.5 crore goods turnover, ₹50 lakh services turnover, 6% goods, 1% services and full ITC
₹1.5 crore goods turnover, ₹50 lakh services turnover, 1% goods, 6% services and no ITC
₹50 lakh goods turnover, ₹1.5 crore services turnover, 6% goods, 1% services and full ITC
96.x: The composition scheme applies up to ₹1.5 crore for goods and ₹50 lakh for services, with rates of 1% for goods and 6% for services and no input tax credit.
96.tq: Match the turnover limits, rates and ITC consequence as one complete package.

96.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the composition scheme is correct?
o: It does not allow input tax credit, although refunds may be allowed for an inverted duty structure.
It is available only to exporters making zero-rated supplies.
It replaces the destination principle with an origin principle.
It permits unrestricted input tax credit to the taxpayer.
96.x: A composition taxpayer cannot claim input tax credit. Refunds may nevertheless be permitted in relation to an inverted duty structure.
96.tq: Use the principal restriction to separate the composition scheme from the regular scheme.

96.s: Which of the following correctly describes GSTIN?
o: A 16-digit number issued by the RBI
A 12-digit number for e-way bills only
A 10-digit identification number for direct taxpayers
96.x: GSTIN is a 15-digit Goods and Services Tax Identification Number. It is not a PAN, RBI number or e-way bill number.
96.tq: Use the exact numerical length to distinguish GSTIN from other identifiers.

96.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with its GST compliance function?
o: E-invoicing — checking fake invoices; HSN/SAC — classification codes
E-invoicing — determining the State share of GST; HSN/SAC — fixing the repo rate
E-invoicing — replacing GSTIN; HSN/SAC — exempting all services
E-invoicing — collecting stamp duty; HSN/SAC — issuing passports
96.x: E-invoicing helps check fake invoices, while HSN and SAC are classification codes for goods and services respectively.
96.tq: Start from the sure compliance pair and reject unrelated administrative functions.

96.s: For low-risk applicants, automated GST registration is to be completed within:
96.x: Automated registration for low-risk applicants is completed within three working days.
96.tq: Recall the prescribed time limit and distinguish working days from calendar periods.

96.s: Revenue Neutral Rate (RNR) in the context of GST refers to a rate that:
o: Keeps revenue equal to the level prevailing before GST
Maximises tax revenue irrespective of the pre-GST position
96.x: RNR is the rate designed to keep revenue at the pre-GST level. The concept was associated with the Arvind Subramanian Committee in 2015.
96.tq: Match the technical term with its precise revenue objective.

96.s: The Revenue Neutral Rate in relation to GST was associated with the committee headed by:
96.x: The Revenue Neutral Rate was associated with the Arvind Subramanian Committee, constituted in 2015 for this purpose.
96.tq: Use the committee-chairperson association rather than confusing it with other fiscal committees.

96.s: Which of the following is constitutionally within the GST framework but is to be levied under GST only from a date recommended by the GST Council?
96.x: The Constitution permits petroleum products to be brought under GST from a date recommended by the GST Council. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is excluded by the Constitution itself.
96.tq: Separate constitutional inclusion with deferred levy from constitutional exclusion.

96.s: Which one of the following is constitutionally excluded from GST rather than merely awaiting a notified date for levy?
96.x: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from GST. The listed petroleum products are constitutionally within GST but have not been brought under it for levy.
96.tq: Compare the constitutional treatment of liquor with petroleum products.

96.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five petroleum products kept outside the current levy of GST?
96.x: The five petroleum products are crude oil, petrol or motor spirit, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel. Lubricating oil is not included in that specified list.
96.tq: Recall the complete five-item list and identify the outsider.

96.s:
Consider the following items:
1. Electricity supply
2. Real estate transactions subject to stamp duty
3. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption
4. Aviation turbine fuel
Which of the above are outside the current GST levy?
96.x: Electricity, real estate transactions subject to stamp duty, alcoholic liquor for human consumption and aviation turbine fuel are outside the current GST levy.
96.tq: Treat each item independently and select the complete set of excluded items.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes zero-rated supplies from nil-rated supplies under GST?
o: Nil-rated supplies are taxable at the standard rate, whereas zero-rated supplies are exempt by notification.
Zero-rated supplies include exports and SEZ supplies with full ITC refund; nil-rated supplies do not allow ITC.
Zero-rated supplies carry a 0% rate and nil-rated supplies allow full ITC refund.
Both categories are identical because neither permits ITC.
96.x: Exports and supplies to SEZs are zero-rated and permit full input tax credit refund. Nil-rated supplies attract a zero rate and do not permit ITC.
96.tq: Compare both the type of supply and the input-tax-credit consequence.

96.s: A supply is specifically exempted from GST by notification. Which one of the following follows from this classification?
o: It is automatically zero-rated and full ITC must be refunded.
It is taxed at the highest GST slab.
It is an exempt supply and input tax credit is unavailable.
It can be treated as an export irrespective of destination.
96.x: An exempt supply is notified as being outside tax and does not qualify for input tax credit. Exemption is distinct from zero-rating.
96.tq: Apply the ITC consequence to distinguish exempt from zero-rated supplies.

96.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Nil-rated — 0% rate; exempt — notified out of tax; zero-rated — exports and SEZ supplies
Nil-rated — full ITC refund; exempt — exports; zero-rated — no ITC
Nil-rated — only petroleum supplies; exempt — only liquor; zero-rated — only domestic supplies
Nil-rated — stamp duty; exempt — customs duty; zero-rated — electricity duty
96.x: Nil-rated supplies attract a zero rate, exempt supplies are notified out of tax, and zero-rated supplies include exports and SEZ supplies with full ITC refund.
96.tq: Match each term with its exact legal and ITC consequence.

96.s: Under the GST 2.0 changes referred to in the current tax structure, which of the following is exempted?
o: All motor vehicle insurance premiums without exception
Individual life and health insurance premiums
96.x: GST 2.0 provides exemption for individual life and health insurance premiums. The exemption is not stated as a blanket exemption for every insurance service.
96.tq: Avoid extending a specific exemption into an unsupported blanket exemption.

96.s: Under the GST 2.0 changes, rare-disease medicines are treated as:
o: Taxable at the highest GST rate
Outside GST but subject to stamp duty
96.x: Rare-disease medicines are fully exempt under the stated GST 2.0 changes.
96.tq: Identify the precise tax treatment rather than confusing exemption with zero-rating.

96.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between GST and input tax credit for non-taxable or exempt supplies?
o: ITC is compulsory even when no GST is charged.
ITC is available only on supplies subject to stamp duty.
ITC is available on every exempt and non-taxable supply.
ITC is not available on exempt or non-taxable supplies.
96.x: Input tax credit is not available on exempt or non-taxable supplies. Zero-rated supplies are different because they permit full ITC refund.
96.tq: Use the ITC rule to separate exempt and non-taxable supplies from zero-rated supplies.

96.s: Under the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017, the States were assured an annual revenue growth of:
96.x: The Act assured States 14% annual revenue growth over the base year 2015–16.
96.tq: Use the base year and percentage together to eliminate nearby figures.

96.s: The original period for compensation to States under the GST compensation mechanism extended up to:
96.x: The compensation period was for five years and ended in June 2022.
96.tq: Anchor the answer to the stated five-year compensation period.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding GST compensation cess:
1. Its levy was extended up to March 2026 to repay loans taken for paying compensation.
2. From 22 September 2025, it was scrapped for all goods without exception.
3. It continued on tobacco after the general withdrawal of the cess.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The cess was scrapped for all goods except tobacco, so statement 2 is false.
96.tq: Find the exception hidden in an otherwise broad statement.

96.s: Which of the following replaced the compensation-cess arrangement for tobacco and pan masala from 1 February 2026?
o: A special State GST on tobacco products
A customs duty collected by the GST Council
Higher excise on tobacco and Health Security se National Security Cess on pan masala units
A surcharge under the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act
96.x: Higher excise was imposed on tobacco under the Central Excise (Amendment) Act, 2025, while Health Security se National Security Cess was imposed on pan masala units.
96.tq: Match the replacement measures with the correct commodities.

96.s: The Health Security se National Security Cess on pan masala units is levied on the basis of:
96.x: The cess is levied on machine production capacity. Its proceeds are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India and are not shared with the States.
96.tq: Distinguish the production-capacity base from turnover-based taxation.

96.s: The compensation cess for States formally ended on:
96.x: Although the cess was withdrawn for most goods from 22 September 2025 and retained for tobacco, the compensation cess ended on 31 March 2026.
96.tq: Separate the rate-change date from the formal end date.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the GST rate structure from 22 September 2025?
o: 0%, 5% as merit rate, 18% as standard rate and 40% as demerit rate
96.x: GST 2.0 rationalised the principal slabs into 0%, 5%, 18% and 40%, with 5% as the merit rate, 18% as the standard rate and 40% as the demerit rate.
96.tq: Compare the post-rationalisation labels and rates as a complete structure.

96.s: The GST rate applicable to rough diamonds and gold, silver and jewellery under the special-rate structure is, respectively:
96.x: Rough diamonds attract a special rate of 0.25%, while gold, silver and jewellery attract 3%.
96.tq: Read paired numerical rates in the order in which the commodities are given.

96.s: Which of the following rate changes is correctly matched?
o: Small cars and bikes up to 350 cc — 28% to 5%
96.x: Air-conditioners were shifted from 28% to 18%. Tractors moved from 12% to 5%; small cars and bikes up to 350 cc moved from 28% to 18%; larger bikes and big cars moved to 40%.
96.tq: Check both the commodity and the direction of the rate change.

96.s: Under GST 2.0, which group was placed in the 40% demerit-rate category?
o: Ultra-luxury cars, tobacco, pan masala, online gaming and aerated drinks
Tractors, rough diamonds and agricultural implements
Small cars, bikes up to 350 cc and air-conditioners
96.x: The 40% rate applies to specified demerit goods and services, including ultra-luxury cars, tobacco, pan masala, online gaming and aerated drinks.
96.tq: Group the demerit items instead of confusing them with standard-rate goods.

96.s: Approximately what proportion of the items earlier taxed at 12% moved to the 5% slab under GST 2.0?
96.x: Approximately 99% of the items earlier in the 12% slab moved to 5%.
96.tq: Distinguish the 12% transition figure from the separate 28% transition figure.

96.s: Approximately what proportion of the items earlier taxed at 28% moved to the 18% slab under GST 2.0?
96.x: Approximately 90% of the items earlier taxed at 28% moved to 18%; the remaining demerit items moved to 40%.
96.tq: Keep the 90% figure linked to the old 28% slab.

96.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 described GST 2.0 as the:
96.x: GST 2.0 was described as the third pillar of tax reform, after the 2019 corporate tax cut and the 2025 personal income-tax reform.
96.tq: Use the sequence of reforms rather than identifying GST only by its tax rates.

96.s: Which of the following statements regarding the GST tax base and collections is correct?
o: The taxpayer base increased from 66.5 lakh in 2017 to 1.51 crore in 2025.
Gross GST revenue in FY 2024–25 was ₹8.43 lakh crore.
The taxpayer base declined from 1.51 crore in 2017 to 66.5 lakh in 2025.
The taxpayer base remained unchanged between 2017 and 2025.
96.x: The tax base increased from 66.5 lakh taxpayers in 2017 to 1.51 crore in 2025. Gross GST collections in FY 2024–25 were ₹22.08 lakh crore.
96.tq: Check the direction of change and distinguish taxpayer counts from revenue figures.

96.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
a. Kelkar Task Force
b. Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers
c. Revenue Neutral Rate Committee

List-II (Chair)
i. Arvind Subramanian
ii. Vijay Kelkar
iii. Asim Dasgupta

Select the correct answer using the code below.
96.x: The Kelkar Task Force was chaired by Vijay Kelkar, the Empowered Committee by Asim Dasgupta, and the Revenue Neutral Rate Committee by Arvind Subramanian.
96.tq: Start from the sure chairperson–committee pair and eliminate the codes.

96.s: The Kelkar Task Force first recommended a comprehensive national GST in connection with:
o: The implementation of the FRBM framework
The creation of the GST Appellate Tribunal
The introduction of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
96.x: The Kelkar Task Force was associated with FRBM implementation and first recommended a comprehensive national GST. The roadmap is also dated to 2002 in the cited chronology.
96.tq: Link the committee to its stated institutional context.

96.s: The Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers produced which of the following documents in April 2008?
o: A Model and Roadmap for GST
96.x: The Empowered Committee produced “A Model and Roadmap for GST” in April 2008 and issued the First Discussion Paper in November 2009.
96.tq: Distinguish the committee’s roadmap document from the later discussion paper.

96.s: The Revenue Neutral Rate Committee recommended an RNR of approximately:
96.x: The Revenue Neutral Rate Committee, chaired by Arvind Subramanian, recommended an RNR of about 15–15.5% and a standard rate of 17–18%.
96.tq: Keep the RNR range distinct from the proposed standard-rate range.

96.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First Discussion Paper on GST
B. GST rollout at a midnight session
C. Empowered Committee roadmap for GST
D. Union Finance Minister’s commitment to 1 April 2010 as the target date
96.x: The roadmap was issued in 2008, the commitment to 1 April 2010 was made in July 2009, the First Discussion Paper appeared in November 2009, and GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017.
96.tq: Fix the first and last events, then order the two intervening 2009 events.

96.s: Which of the following statements about the design and origin of GST is correct?
o: The GST idea was first proposed under the Vajpayee government, recommended by the Vijay Kelkar Task Force, and was based on the Canadian dual model.
The GST idea originated under the Manmohan Singh government and followed an exclusively French model.
The GST was first used in Canada and later proposed by the Kelkar Task Force.
The GST was designed as a single-level State tax without a dual structure.
96.x: The idea was first proposed under the Vajpayee government, recommended by the Vijay Kelkar Task Force, and followed the Canadian dual model. The concept was first used in France.
96.tq: Combine origin, recommending body and model while rejecting swapped-country traps.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the components of India’s dual GST system?
o: CGST is levied by States and SGST by the Centre on inter-State supplies.
UTGST is levied by States with legislatures on inter-State imports.
CGST and SGST are levied on intra-State supplies, while IGST is levied on inter-State supplies and imports.
IGST is levied by States and retained entirely by the exporting State.
96.x: CGST and SGST apply to intra-State supplies, while IGST is levied by the Centre on inter-State supplies and imports.
96.tq: Identify the taxing authority and type of supply together.

96.s: In an intra-State supply, the State component of GST is generally represented by:
o: UTGST, collected by the Centre in every State
SGST, collected by the State, alongside an equal CGST component
96.x: For an intra-State supply, CGST is levied by the Centre and SGST by the State in equal halves of the applicable GST rate.
96.tq: Apply the dual-tax principle to an intra-State transaction.

96.s: UTGST is applicable principally to:
o: Exports from Union Territories with legislatures
Inter-State supplies made by States with legislatures
Intra-Union Territory supplies in Union Territories without legislatures
96.x: UTGST is the Union Territory counterpart for intra-UT supplies in Union Territories without legislatures and is levied by the Centre.
96.tq: Match UTGST with both the territory and the nature of supply.

96.s: IGST revenue is ultimately apportioned to the:
o: Origin State from which the goods are dispatched
Union Territory in which the invoice is generated
Destination State where the goods or services are consumed
State having the largest tax base
96.x: IGST follows the destination principle; revenue is settled to the consuming or destination State.
96.tq: Apply the destination principle rather than the place-of-origin principle.

96.s: Which authority alone legislates on IGST?
o: The State Legislature of the exporting State
96.x: Parliament alone legislates on IGST, while the GST Council makes recommendations on GST matters.
96.tq: Distinguish the recommending body from the legislative authority.

96.s: GSTN primarily functions as the IT backbone for:
o: Customs valuation and foreign-exchange management only
96.x: GSTN supports GST registration, return filing and input-tax-credit matching; AI tools are also being used for scrutiny.
96.tq: Identify the core digital functions rather than unrelated financial functions.

96.s: The GSTN is using AI tools particularly for:
o: Determining the exchange rate of the rupee
Scrutiny of GST-related transactions and returns
96.x: AI tools are being used for scrutiny within the GSTN-supported tax administration system.
96.tq: Separate tax-administration applications of AI from RBI functions.

96.s:
Which of the following statements regarding compensation cess is correct?
1. It was imposed on specified luxury and sin goods.
2. It was intended to support compensation to States for five years at 14% annual growth over 2015–16.
3. Compensation to States continued indefinitely after June 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Compensation to States ended in June 2022, although cess collections continued for loan repayment.
96.tq: Reject the indefinite-continuation trap in statement 3.

96.s: Under the GST Acts, the ceiling for CGST is:
96.x: The CGST Act provides a ceiling of 20%. The corresponding IGST ceiling is 40%.
96.tq: Keep the CGST ceiling separate from the IGST ceiling.

96.s: Under the GST Acts, the ceiling for IGST is:
96.x: The IGST Act provides a ceiling of 40%, while the CGST ceiling is 20%.
96.tq: Use the paired statutory ceilings to avoid reversing them.

96.s: GST rates are normally changed by:
o: An order of the Reserve Bank of India
Amending the GST Acts through Parliament in every case
Government notification issued on the recommendation of the GST Council, subject to statutory ceilings
A resolution of the Finance Commission
96.x: Rates are normally changed through government notification on the recommendation of the GST Council, rather than by amending the Acts each time.
96.tq: Ask which authority performs the operational rate change and who recommends it.

96.s: An e-way bill is mandatory for the movement of goods when their value exceeds:
96.x: An e-way bill is mandatory for moving goods worth more than ₹50,000.
96.tq: Identify the statutory value threshold rather than the validity period.

96.s: The normal validity period of an e-way bill is:
96.x: The e-way bill is valid for one day for every 200 km of movement.
96.tq: Read the validity rule as a distance-to-day ratio.

96.s: The principal purpose of e-invoicing is to:
o: Replace all GST returns with paper invoices
Digitally report invoices, curb fake invoices and verify input-tax credit
Set the GST Council’s voting weights
Determine the annual borrowing limit of States
96.x: E-invoicing digitally reports invoices, helps curb fake invoices and supports verification of input-tax credit.
96.tq: Connect the digital mechanism with its compliance objectives.

96.s: Under Budget 2026–27, automated GST registration within three working days is intended for low-risk applicants whose monthly tax liability is up to:
96.x: Low-risk applicants with a monthly tax liability up to ₹2.5 lakh are eligible for the automated registration facility within three working days.
96.tq: Combine the applicant category, time limit and monetary threshold.

96.s:
Which of the following collection figures is correctly matched with its period?
1. January 2026 — ₹1.93 lakh crore
2. February 2026 — ₹1.83 lakh crore
3. April–July 2026 — ₹8.43 lakh crore
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: All three figures are correctly matched: ₹1.93 lakh crore in January 2026, ₹1.83 lakh crore in February 2026, and ₹8.43 lakh crore during April–July 2026.
96.tq: Verify each figure against its time period before selecting the coded option.

96.s: What was the gross Goods and Services Tax collection in India in April 2026?
96.x: India’s gross GST collection reached a record ₹2.43 lakh crore in April 2026.
96.tq: Use the exact record figure and distinguish it from other reported GST collections.

96.s:
With reference to GST collections in August 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Gross GST collection was ₹1,99,853 crore.
2. The collection recorded a year-on-year growth of 14.8%.
3. The collection was lower than the GST collection reported for December 2025 in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Gross GST collection in August 2026 was ₹1,99,853 crore, registering 14.8% growth. Statement 3 is incorrect because it compares India’s August gross collection with Andhra Pradesh’s December net GST collection, which is not a valid comparison of the same measure.
96.tq: Split the statements by figure, growth rate and an invalid comparison of unlike measures.

96.s: Goods and Services Tax is regarded as the biggest indirect tax reform in India since Independence primarily because it:
o: replaced the need for all direct taxes
abolished the divisible pool of taxes
created a unified framework for a large number of indirect taxes
transferred all taxation powers to the States
96.x: GST is considered the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence because it established a unified framework for indirect taxation by subsuming several indirect taxes.
96.tq: Identify the precise significance rather than choosing extreme claims about direct taxes or complete transfer of powers.

96.s: The increasing importance of monthly GST data as a macroeconomic indicator is mainly associated with its usefulness in assessing:
o: the constitutional composition of the GST Council
only the long-term population growth of India
short-term trends in economic activity and tax revenue
96.x: Monthly GST collections provide timely information on economic activity and government tax revenue, making them a useful macroeconomic indicator.
96.tq: Apply the function of a macro indicator to a short-term economic situation.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the impact of GST on States:
1. States surrendered some of their independent indirect-tax instruments after the introduction of GST.
2. Cesses are outside the divisible pool.
3. Tamil Nadu adopted a resolution relating to fair devolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: All three statements are correct. The GST framework led States to give up some independent indirect-tax powers, cesses remain outside the divisible pool, and Tamil Nadu raised the issue of fair devolution through a resolution.
96.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.

96.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the GST Council?
96.x: Arun Jaitley was the first Chairperson of the GST Council.
96.tq: Use the first-holder trap by distinguishing the inaugural chairperson from later office-holders and associated personalities.

96.s: Who was associated with GST as its brand ambassador?
96.x: Amitabh Bachchan was associated with GST as its brand ambassador.
96.tq: Discriminate between the office-holder and the public personality associated with the GST campaign.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the GST-related fiscal developments reported for July 2026 and the first quarter of 2026–27?
o: GST collection increased by 15.4%, while the Centre’s gross tax revenue increased by only 3.7%.
GST collection increased by 3.7%, while the Centre’s gross tax revenue increased by 15.4%.
Both GST collection and the Centre’s gross tax revenue increased by 15.4%.
Both GST collection and the Centre’s gross tax revenue increased by only 3.7%.
96.x: GST collection increased by 15.4% in July 2026, whereas the Centre’s gross tax revenue grew by only 3.7% in the first quarter of 2026–27, partly in the context of the GST 2.0 revenue cut.
96.tq: Match the correct percentage with the correct fiscal indicator instead of reversing the comparison.

96.s: Andhra Pradesh’s State GST was reported as its largest own-tax source in 2024–25 Revised Estimates. What were its approximate amount and share of the State’s own-tax revenue?
96.x: SGST was Andhra Pradesh’s largest own-tax source, amounting to ₹36,296 crore and constituting 38% of the State’s own-tax revenue in the 2024–25 Revised Estimates.
96.tq: Link the amount and percentage as a paired numerical fact.

96.s: In December 2025, Andhra Pradesh’s net GST collection was ₹2,652 crore. How did its growth compare with the national growth rate?
o: It grew by 14.8%, exceeding the national rate of 5.78%.
It grew by 5.61%, exactly equal to the national rate.
It grew by 5.78%, exceeding the national rate of 5.61%.
It grew by 5.61%, exceeding the national rate of 5.78%.
96.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded net GST of ₹2,652 crore in December 2025, with growth of 5.78%, which was higher than the national growth rate of 5.61%.
96.tq: Keep the State and national percentages in the correct order and distinguish them from other GST growth figures.

96.s: Which issue was highlighted by the Andhra Pradesh High Court regarding investigations by GST authorities?
o: GST investigations must be transferred to the GST Council.
The Centre and the State tax authorities must decide inter se which authority will investigate.
Only the State Government can investigate inter-State GST matters.
Only the Union Government can investigate every GST matter.
96.x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court held that the Centre and State tax authorities must decide inter se which authority is competent to investigate a particular matter.
96.tq: Identify the authority-responsibility issue by asking who must decide which body investigates.

97.s: What is identified as the biggest drawback of the multiple-rate structure under GST?
o: Delay in settlement of IGST between the Union and the States
Dependence of States on Finance Commission devolution
Misclassification of goods and services and classification disputes
Complete exclusion of petroleum products from taxation
97.x: The multiple-rate structure creates difficulties in classifying goods and services, resulting in frequent classification disputes.
97.tq: Directly identify the specific weakness associated with a tax structure.

97.s: The four-slab structure of GST was originally intended to be:
o: A permanent arrangement for all goods and services
A mechanism for distributing IGST among States
A structure applicable only to petroleum products
97.x: The four-slab GST structure was conceived as a transitional arrangement rather than a permanent structure.
97.tq: Test the intended character of a policy arrangement rather than its numerical details.

97.s: Under the GST 2.0 rate structure introduced on 22 September 2025, the principal slabs were reduced to:
97.x: GST 2.0, introduced on 22 September 2025, reduced the structure to 5%, 18% and 40% slabs.
97.tq: Recall the exact date and numerical slab combination.

97.s: Which of the following continue to remain outside the GST framework?
97.x: Petroleum and electricity remain outside the GST framework.
97.tq: Use confusable sector exclusions to distinguish items inside and outside a tax regime.

97.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT):
1. It was created through the Finance Act, 2024.
2. Its Principal Bench is located in New Delhi.
3. Its membership includes a President and Technical Members from the Centre and the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All three statements are correct. GSTAT was created through the Finance Act, 2024, has its Principal Bench at New Delhi, and includes a President and Centre- and State-level Technical Members.
97.tq: Combine legislative, locational and institutional-composition facts in a coded statement question.

97.s: The first President of the GST Appellate Tribunal was a former Chief Justice of the:
97.x: The first President of GSTAT was a former Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court.
97.tq: Apply the person-and-office trap by matching the office-holder with the correct institution.

97.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the operational timeline of GSTAT?
o: Formally launched in September 2025 and hearings commenced in December 2025
Formally launched in December 2025 and hearings commenced in September 2026
Formally launched in April 2024 and hearings commenced in September 2025
Formally launched in September 2026 and hearings commenced in December 2026
97.x: GSTAT was formally launched in September 2025, while hearings began in December 2025.
97.tq: Use the first-and-second event sequence to eliminate reversed timelines.

97.s: Appeals before the GST Appellate Tribunal are to be filed online within:
97.x: Appeals before GSTAT are to be filed online within three months.
97.tq: Recall the prescribed time limit using close numerical alternatives.

97.s: What was an important consequence of the earlier absence of GSTAT benches?
o: Appeals accumulated in the High Courts
Petroleum products were brought under GST
GST collections were transferred entirely to the States
The four GST slabs were abolished immediately
97.x: Before GSTAT benches became available, GST-related appeals accumulated in the High Courts.
97.tq: Link an institutional gap with its direct administrative consequence.

97.s: An inverted duty structure arises when:
o: Input tax is higher than output tax, resulting in blocked credit
Input and output taxes are equal but refunds are prohibited
Output tax is higher than input tax and exports are taxed fully
Output tax is collected by the State instead of the Centre
97.x: An inverted duty structure exists when the tax paid on inputs exceeds the tax charged on output, leading to blocked credit; refunds are allowed in such cases.
97.tq: Apply the definition to the relationship between input tax and output tax.

97.s: Domestic GST refunds surged by what percentage in August 2026 due to inverted duties?
97.x: Domestic refunds increased by 72.6% in August 2026, largely because of inverted-duty claims.
97.tq: Test a distinctive percentage with ascending numerical distractors.

97.s: Which practice is characteristic of the ITC fraud involving bogus entities?
o: Paying output tax twice on genuine transactions
Issuing invoices without actual supply of goods or services
Using only government invoices for exports
Claiming refunds on petroleum products outside GST
97.x: Bogus entities issue invoices without any corresponding supply in order to fraudulently claim input tax credit.
97.tq: Identify the fraudulent mechanism from a practical transaction scenario.

97.s: The fake-registration and scrap-bill network involved in ITC fraud operated across which group of States?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala
97.x: The reported network used fake registrations and scrap bills across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
97.tq: Discriminate among closely related geographical combinations.

97.s:
Which of the following measures are used to counter fraudulent input tax credit claims?
1. E-invoicing
2. UPI and Aadhaar tracking
3. Artificial Intelligence-based scrutiny
Select the correct answer using the code below.
97.x: E-invoicing, UPI/Aadhaar tracking and AI-based scrutiny are all measures used to counter ITC fraud.
97.tq: Use an all-inclusive option for a list of complementary enforcement measures.

97.s: Which of the following represents an unresolved demand associated with the future simplification of GST?
o: Replacement of GST by customs duty
Exclusion of all State taxes from GST
97.x: GST 3.0 simplification has been raised as an important demand, including by CII Andhra Pradesh.
97.tq: Identify the exact policy demand among nearby tax-policy alternatives.

97.s: Notebook manufacturers were reported to have raised sector-specific concerns following the GST rate revision of:
97.x: Notebook manufacturers raised concerns following the GST rate revision in September 2025.
97.tq: Match a sector-specific grievance with the correct policy-change date.

97.s: The average monthly gross GST collection during 2017-18 was approximately:
97.x: The average monthly gross GST collection in FY 2017-18 was about ₹82,000 crore.
97.tq: Recall an early benchmark and distinguish it from later collection levels.

97.s: In which month did monthly gross GST collections first exceed ₹2 lakh crore?
97.x: Monthly gross GST collections crossed ₹2 lakh crore for the first time in April 2024.
97.tq: Test a milestone date using close year alternatives.

97.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s gross GST collection during FY 2024-25?
o: ₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.04 lakh crore per month
₹24.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.04 lakh crore per month
₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.43 lakh crore per month
₹17.4 lakh crore, with an average of ₹1.82 lakh crore per month
97.x: Gross GST collection in FY 2024-25 was ₹22.08 lakh crore, averaging ₹2.04 lakh crore per month.
97.tq: Separate an annual total from its monthly average using precise numerical matching.

97.s: Gross GST collection during April–December 2025 was:
97.x: Gross GST collection during April–December 2025 amounted to ₹17.4 lakh crore, showing 6.7% growth.
97.tq: Match the period, total and growth rate in a quantitative data question.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about GST collections in April 2026:
1. Gross GST collection reached a record ₹2.43 lakh crore.
2. Gross collection grew by 8.7%.
3. Net GST collection was ₹2.11 lakh crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All three statements are correct for April 2026: gross collection was ₹2.43 lakh crore, growth was 8.7%, and net collection was ₹2.11 lakh crore.
97.tq: Test whether a complete set of related quantitative statements is internally consistent.

97.s: Which of the following correctly describes GST collections during April–July 2026?
o: Gross ₹8.43 lakh crore, growth 10.1%, and net ₹7.21 lakh crore with growth 9.2%
Gross ₹17.4 lakh crore, growth 6.7%, and net ₹8.43 lakh crore with growth 10.1%
Gross ₹7.21 lakh crore, growth 9.2%, and net ₹8.43 lakh crore with growth 10.1%
Gross ₹8.43 lakh crore, growth 8.7%, and net ₹7.21 lakh crore with growth 14.8%
97.x: During April–July 2026, gross GST collection was ₹8.43 lakh crore, up 10.1%; net collection was ₹7.21 lakh crore, up 9.2%.
97.tq: Compare gross and net figures while preserving their correct order and growth rates.

97.s:
Consider the following statements regarding GST collections in August 2026:
1. Gross GST collection grew by 14.8%.
2. Net GST collection grew by 8.3%.
3. Domestic GST grew by 9.3%.
4. Import-side GST grew faster than domestic GST.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All four statements are correct. August 2026 gross growth was 14.8%, net growth was 8.3%, domestic growth was 9.3%, and import-side GST grew faster than domestic GST.
97.tq: Combine headline growth, net growth and component-wise trends in a coded question.

97.s: The gross GST collection in April–December 2025 was what proportion of the FY 2024-25 annual gross collection, approximately?
o: More than the full annual collection
97.x: ₹17.4 lakh crore is approximately 79% of ₹22.08 lakh crore, which is about three-fourths and clearly more than one-half but less than the full annual amount.
97.tq: Use approximate ratio comparison rather than merely recalling an isolated figure.

97.s: Which statement best explains the reported weakness in GST buoyancy despite the August 2026 rate revision?
o: All States had recorded growth below the national average
Domestic GST had grown faster than import-side GST
Imports had stopped contributing to GST revenue
Revenue loss from the rate cut was still awaiting gains from higher volume
97.x: GST buoyancy remained weak because the revenue loss from the rate cut had not yet been fully offset by volume gains.
97.tq: Connect a policy rate change with its short-term revenue effect and delayed volume response.

97.s: Andhra Pradesh’s December 2025 net GST growth exceeded the national growth by approximately:
97.x: Andhra Pradesh grew by 5.78% against the national growth of 5.61%, a difference of 0.17 percentage point.
97.tq: Calculate the difference between two closely placed growth rates.

97.s: Which of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh’s commercial-tax and GST figures up to August 2026?
o: Commercial taxes ₹36,296 crore, up 38%; net GST ₹16,452.62 crore
Commercial taxes ₹16,452.62 crore, up 18.05%; net GST ₹25,449.80 crore
Commercial taxes ₹25,449.80 crore, up 18.05%; net GST ₹16,452.62 crore
Commercial taxes ₹13,282 crore, up 21%; net GST ₹25,449.80 crore
97.x: Up to August 2026, Andhra Pradesh’s commercial-tax collection was ₹25,449.80 crore, up 18.05%, while net GST was ₹16,452.62 crore.
97.tq: Avoid swapping the tax-head total and the net GST figure.

97.s: Andhra Pradesh’s GST collections increased by 21% to:
97.x: Andhra Pradesh GST collections increased by 21% to ₹13,282 crore.
97.tq: Match the growth rate with the correct resulting collection amount.

97.s:
Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s AI-powered GST model?
1. It uses a risk matrix.
2. Its Legal-AI assistant was trained on approximately 22,000 judgments.
3. It has dealt with more than 13,700 cases.
4. It is being studied by several other States.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
97.x: All four statements are correct. The model uses a risk matrix, a Legal-AI assistant trained on about 22,000 judgments, and has covered more than 13,700 cases; other States are studying it.
97.tq: Test a technology initiative through its components, scale and adoption by other States.

97.s: Which group of States is specifically mentioned as studying Andhra Pradesh’s AI-powered GST model?
o: Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Rajasthan, Kerala and Assam
Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Haryana, Assam and Madhya Pradesh
Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Kerala and Goa
Karnataka, Telangana, Odisha, Punjab and Gujarat
97.x: Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Rajasthan, Kerala, Assam and other States are studying Andhra Pradesh’s AI-powered GST model.
97.tq: Recall a multi-State institutional-adoption list without substituting neighbouring States.

97.s: One major fiscal consequence for States of surrendering independent indirect-tax powers under GST has been:
o: Greater dependence on transfers because of weak own revenues
Automatic equalisation of revenues among all States
Complete elimination of State taxation powers
97.x: The surrender of independent indirect-tax powers, combined with weak own revenues, has increased States’ dependence on transfers.
97.tq: Link the loss of fiscal autonomy with the resulting dependence on transfers.

97.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographical concentration of GST buoyancy:
1. Only 16 States and Union Territories recorded post-settlement GST growth above the national average.
2. Manufacturing States tend to gain from this pattern.
3. States with a large unorganised sector depend on Finance Commission devolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All three statements are correct. GST buoyancy was above the national average in only 16 States/UTs; manufacturing States gained, while unorganised-sector States relied more on Finance Commission devolution.
97.tq: Combine a numerical count with distributional consequences across State types.

97.s: The destination principle of GST generally favours:
o: States with the highest rates of State excise duty
Producing States because tax is collected at the point of manufacture
Consuming States because taxation follows the place of consumption
97.x: GST follows the destination principle, under which consuming States benefit because revenue is associated with the place of consumption.
97.tq: Distinguish destination-based taxation from origin-based taxation.

97.s: Andhra Pradesh, being a consuming State, benefits from GST primarily through:
o: State excise on petroleum under GST
Abolition of its own tax revenue
97.x: As a consuming State, Andhra Pradesh benefits from the destination principle through IGST settlement.
97.tq: Apply the destination principle to the fiscal position of a particular State.

97.s: Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s own tax revenue composition in 2024-25 (RE)?
97.x: In 2024-25 (RE), GST contributed 38% of Andhra Pradesh’s own tax revenue and State Excise contributed 22%.
97.tq: Compare the leading and second-largest tax contributors without reversing their shares.

97.s: Andhra Pradesh’s own tax revenue in 2024-25 (RE) was approximately what share of its revenue receipts?
97.x: Own tax revenue of ₹94,967 crore was approximately 48% of revenue receipts of ₹1,91,142 crore.
97.tq: Use the percentage relationship between a State’s own tax revenue and total revenue receipts.

97.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched for Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25 (RE)?
97.x: State Excise contributed ₹21,300 crore in 2024-25 (RE). GST was ₹36,296 crore, own tax revenue was ₹94,967 crore and revenue receipts were ₹1,91,142 crore.
97.tq: Find the correctly matched tax head and amount among swapped numerical pairs.

97.s: Andhra Pradesh’s GST contribution to own tax revenue changed from 36% in 2023-24 (RE) to:
97.x: GST’s share in Andhra Pradesh’s own tax revenue increased from 36% in 2023-24 (RE) to 38% in 2024-25 (RE).
97.tq: Track a year-on-year percentage change without confusing it with another tax share.

97.s: For Andhra Pradesh, “Net GST” is defined as:
o: Gross GST collections minus customs revenue
SGST plus the State’s share of IGST settlement
SGST minus the State’s share of IGST settlement
97.x: Andhra Pradesh’s Net GST consists of SGST plus its share received through IGST settlement.
97.tq: Discriminate between a State’s own GST component and its settled IGST share.

97.s: Which statement about Andhra Pradesh’s net GST collection in December 2025 is correct?
o: It was ₹2,652 crore, grew by 5.78%, was the highest December collection, and marked the ninth consecutive month above the previous year.
It was ₹2,652 crore, grew by 5.61%, and was the first month above the previous year.
It was ₹13,282 crore, grew by 21%, and marked the ninth consecutive month above the previous year.
It was ₹16,452.62 crore, grew by 18.05%, and was the highest-ever monthly collection.
97.x: December 2025 net GST was ₹2,652 crore, up 5.78%; it was Andhra Pradesh’s highest December collection and the ninth consecutive month above the corresponding previous-year level, despite GST 2.0 rate cuts.
97.tq: Use a long precise option and verify its figure, growth rate and sequential record together.

97.s: Which of the following is the most direct contribution of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to inter-State commerce?
o: Replacement of input tax credit by a turnover tax
Creation of a common national market through tax harmonisation
Exemption of all inter-State supplies from taxation
Retention of State border check-posts for all goods
97.x: GST created a common national market by harmonising indirect taxation across States. It also helped reduce the cascading effect through input tax credit.
97.tq: Identify the core objective rather than choosing an extreme or reversed consequence.

97.s: An electronic document is mandatory under GST for the movement of goods whose value exceeds:
97.x: An e-way bill is mandatory for the movement of goods valued at more than Rs 50,000.
97.tq: Recall the threshold figure directly and distinguish it from nearby numerical distractors.

97.s: For the movement of goods, an e-way bill is generally valid for:
97.x: The validity of an e-way bill is one day for every 200 kilometres of movement.
97.tq: Test a specific numerical rule using close range-based alternatives.

97.s:
Consider the following statements regarding e-way bills:
1. Their rollout helped replace physical checks at State borders.
2. Their use contributed to a reduction in truck waiting time.
3. Their volumes increased by 21 per cent year-on-year during April–December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All three statements are correct. E-way bills replaced physical border checks, reduced waiting time, and recorded 21 per cent year-on-year growth during April–December 2025.
97.tq: Combine operational effects with a current quantitative fact and test all statements together.

97.s: The removal of inter-State check-posts after the rollout of e-way bills primarily resulted in:
o: A shift from digital to manual tax reporting
Reduced transit time and logistics costs
The abolition of input tax credit
97.x: The replacement of physical checks and the dismantling of border check-posts reduced truck waiting time, transit time and logistics costs.
97.tq: Link the administrative reform to its practical logistics outcome.

97.s: Which of the following best indicates the expansion of formalisation under GST between 2017 and 2025?
o: The taxpayer base remained unchanged at 66.5 lakh
The taxpayer base increased from 1.51 crore to 66.5 lakh
The taxpayer base increased from 66.5 lakh to 1.51 crore
The taxpayer base declined from 1.51 crore to 66.5 lakh
97.x: The taxpayer base expanded from 66.5 lakh in 2017 to 1.51 crore in 2025, indicating greater formalisation.
97.tq: Compare the direction and magnitude of a two-point trend without reversing the figures.

97.s: Which of the following combinations most appropriately describes the benefits of GST formalisation for small firms?
o: Restriction of procurement to intra-State suppliers
Removal of digital records and greater dependence on intermediaries
Exemption from all registration requirements and cash-only transactions
97.x: Formalisation improved credit eligibility and procurement parity for small firms. Digitisation also reduced human interface.
97.tq: Select the paired benefits directly associated with formalisation.

97.s: The composition scheme is primarily intended to ease compliance for:
97.x: The composition scheme is designed to reduce the compliance burden for small taxpayers, including MSMEs.
97.tq: Match the simplified compliance mechanism with its intended beneficiary.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about the GST composition scheme:
1. The turnover limit is up to Rs 1.5 crore for goods.
2. The turnover limit is Rs 50 lakh for services.
3. A taxpayer under the scheme can claim input tax credit.
4. A taxpayer under the scheme can collect GST separately from the customer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: The composition scheme applies up to Rs 1.5 crore for goods and Rs 50 lakh for services. Its taxpayers cannot claim input tax credit or collect tax separately.
97.tq: Find the two correct eligibility statements and reject the reversed features of the scheme.

97.s: Under the composition scheme, the flat rate specified for goods and services respectively is:
o: 6 per cent for goods and 1 per cent for services
6 per cent for both goods and services
1 per cent for goods and 6 per cent for services
1 per cent for both goods and services
97.x: The specified flat rate is 1 per cent for goods and 6 per cent for services.
97.tq: Test a comparison-table row by preserving the order of the two categories.

97.s: Which of the following is a continuing compliance burden associated with GST?
o: Mandatory physical border verification for every consignment
Multiple returns and input tax credit matching
97.x: Multiple returns and input tax credit matching remain important compliance burdens under GST.
97.tq: Distinguish an identified unresolved burden from benefits and abolished procedures.

97.s: Which of the following forms part of the GST reform agenda for reducing compliance difficulties?
o: Pre-filled returns, time-bound digital registration and automated exporter refunds
Manual registration, physical returns and delayed refunds
Separate tax systems for every inter-State route
Abolition of e-invoicing and e-way bills
97.x: The reform agenda includes pre-filled returns, time-bound digital registration and automated refunds for exporters.
97.tq: Identify the complete reform package rather than a reversal of digitisation.

97.s: GST reduced the cascading effect of taxation mainly through:
o: A tax exemption for all intermediate goods
Taxation only at the point of manufacture
Input tax credit available at every stage
Abolition of all State taxes without replacement
97.x: Input tax credit at every stage reduces the tax-on-tax, or cascading, effect.
97.tq: Connect the stated mechanism with the economic effect instead of choosing a broad exemption.

97.s: The compensation period under GST for States formally ended in:
97.x: The GST compensation period ended in June 2022.
97.tq: Separate the end of the compensation period from the later continuation of the cess.

97.s: Why was the GST compensation cess continued after June 2022?
o: To replace input tax credit with a direct subsidy
To finance the creation of State border check-posts
To repay back-to-back loans raised for compensation purposes
97.x: The cess continued to service and repay back-to-back loans raised for GST compensation.
97.tq: Link the continuation of a levy to its stated debt-servicing purpose.

97.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the GST compensation cess:
1. It continued up to March 2026 for repayment of back-to-back loans.
2. It was scrapped on 22 September 2025 except in relation to tobacco.
3. It ended on 31 March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All three statements are correct. The cess continued for loan repayment, was scrapped on 22 September 2025 except for tobacco, and ended on 31 March 2026.
97.tq: Distinguish the announcement date, the exception and the final cessation date.

97.s: The tobacco excise and Health Security and National Security Cess introduced in place of the compensation cess are:
o: Shared with States through the GST Council
97.x: The replacement levies are not shared with the States.
97.tq: Test the important distinction between a divisible GST-related levy and a non-shared levy.

97.s: In Union of India v. Mohit Minerals, the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are:
o: Advisory only to the Union executive but binding on courts
Binding only on Parliament and not on States
Persuasive but not binding on Parliament and State legislatures
Binding on Parliament and State legislatures in every matter
97.x: The Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are persuasive and not binding on Parliament or State legislatures.
97.tq: Discriminate between persuasive and binding constitutional effects.

97.s: The judgment in Union of India v. Mohit Minerals was delivered in:
97.x: The Mohit Minerals judgment was delivered in May 2022.
97.tq: Recall the year and month of a landmark ruling using close chronological distractors.

97.s: The description of India as a “flexible federation” in the context of GST is associated with:
o: The exclusive legislative power of Parliament under Article 249
The simultaneous legislative power under Article 246A
The abolition of State legislative competence over taxation
The power of the GST Council to enact laws directly
97.x: The GST framework reflects simultaneous legislative power under Article 246A, contributing to the description of India as a flexible federation.
97.tq: Connect the constitutional concept with the specific provision and institutional arrangement.

97.s: Which of the following pairs consists of other landmark GST rulings cited along with Mohit Minerals?
97.x: Safari Retreats and VKC Footsteps are cited along with Mohit Minerals as landmark GST rulings.
97.tq: Group landmark cases from the same subject area and reject unrelated constitutional cases.

97.s: Under the GST Council voting arrangement, which of the following is correct?
o: The Centre has one-half weight and States together have one-half weight.
Each State has an equal weight and the Centre has no vote.
The Centre has one-third weight and the States together have two-thirds weight.
The Centre has two-thirds weight and States together have one-third weight.
97.x: The Centre has one-third of the weighted vote and the States together have two-thirds.
97.tq: Recall the composition of weighted voting without reversing the Centre-State shares.

97.s: Why does the Centre have an effective veto in the GST Council?
o: Because the Centre’s one-third vote can prevent a three-fourths majority
Because the Centre has two-thirds of the weighted vote
Because State representatives cannot vote on tax matters
Because the Centre alone nominates all State members
97.x: Since three-fourths weighted support is required and the Centre holds one-third of the vote, the Centre can block a proposal without its support.
97.tq: Infer institutional power from the voting weights and decision threshold.

97.s: Which of the following groups of petroleum products is covered by the GST law but remains outside GST taxation until a date recommended by the GST Council?
o: Crude oil, petrol, diesel, natural gas and ATF
Natural gas, electricity, alcohol, tobacco and ATF
Coal, electricity, iron ore, cement and steel
Gold, silver, diamonds, petrol and coal
97.x: Crude oil, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel are within the GST law but are taxed outside GST until the Council recommends a date under Article 279A(5).
97.tq: Test the complete list and distinguish legal inclusion from present tax treatment.

97.s: Article 279A(5) of the Constitution is relevant to the inclusion of which category within GST taxation?
97.x: Article 279A(5) concerns the date from which specified petroleum products may be brought within GST taxation on the GST Council’s recommendation.
97.tq: Match the constitutional provision with the specific unresolved GST issue.

97.s: Bogus input tax credit claims made through fictitious transactions are commonly associated with:
97.x: Fake invoicing involves bogus claims of input tax credit. E-invoicing, e-way bills and AI-based scrutiny are used to counter it.
97.tq: Distinguish an enforcement problem from genuine compliance and harmonisation measures.

97.s: Which combination is used to counter fake invoicing and bogus input tax credit claims?
o: State borrowing, compensation grants and tax amnesty
E-invoicing, e-way bills and AI-based scrutiny
Physical check-posts, cash payments and manual registers
Composition levy, customs duty and export subsidy
97.x: E-invoicing and e-way bills, supported by AI-based scrutiny, help detect and counter bogus input tax credit claims.
97.tq: Select the coordinated digital enforcement tools rather than an outdated physical-control method.

97.s: In May 2026, the Andhra Pradesh High Court held that where Central and State GST investigations overlap, the authorities must:
o: Abandon the investigation if the entity operates in more than one State
Decide inter se which authority will proceed
Transfer every case automatically to the Union Government
Both proceed simultaneously against the same entity
97.x: The Court held that Central and State GST authorities must decide inter se who will proceed against a common entity, thereby preventing dual action.
97.tq: Identify the precise institutional solution to overlapping jurisdiction.

97.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, a cut in GST rates may have what effect on revenue?
o: Volume effects may offset the initial revenue loss
It necessarily eliminates all future GST revenue
It reduces transaction volumes in every sector
It affects only customs revenue and not GST revenue
97.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 observed that increased volume of transactions following a rate cut may offset the associated revenue loss.
97.tq: Recognise the stated dynamic revenue effect instead of assuming a static tax-base response.

97.s: The gross GST collection during April–November 2019 was approximately:
97.x: Gross GST collection during April–November 2019 was Rs 8.05 lakh crore.
97.tq: Recall the reported aggregate using closely spaced lakh-crore alternatives.

97.s: According to the Economic Survey 2019–20, rationalisation shocks to GST rates generally raise collections for:
97.x: The Economic Survey 2019–20 noted that rationalisation shocks raise collections only for about one to three months.
97.tq: Test the limited duration of a revenue effect against exaggerated time periods.

97.s: The approximate Revenue Neutral Rate (RNR) proposed in the 2015 debate by the Arvind Subramanian Committee was:
97.x: The Arvind Subramanian Committee’s 2015 debate placed the approximate RNR at 15–15.5 per cent.
97.tq: Recall the range directly and distinguish it from lower standard-rate figures.

97.s: What is regarded as the biggest drawback of a multi-rate GST structure?
97.x: The biggest drawback of a multi-rate structure is misclassification. Near-identical products may fall under different slabs, leading to disputes and litigation.
97.tq: Identify the central drawback rather than a related consequence.

97.s:
Consider the following statements regarding classification disputes under a multi-rate GST structure:
1. Near-identical products may be placed in different tax slabs.
2. Such classification differences can invite litigation.
3. Standardising product classification has been identified as a pending reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: All three statements are correct. Differing classification of similar products creates disputes and litigation, while standardisation of product classification remains a reform issue.
97.tq: Check whether all statements describe linked consequences and reforms.

97.s: The term ‘Inverted Duty Structure’ in the GST system refers to a situation in which:
o: The output tax rate exceeds the input tax rate
The input tax rate exceeds the output tax rate
Input tax credit is unavailable despite payment of output tax
Both input and output are exempt from tax
97.x: An Inverted Duty Structure exists when the tax rate on inputs is higher than the tax rate on output. This causes accumulation of input tax credit.
97.tq: Discriminate between the rates on inputs and output.

97.s:
Assertion (A): An Inverted Duty Structure can block working capital of businesses.
Reason (R): Input tax credit accumulates when the tax paid on inputs is higher than the tax payable on output.

Choose the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
97.x: Both statements are true, and the accumulation of input tax credit caused by higher input taxation directly explains the blockage of working capital.
97.tq: Test the cause-and-effect relationship between the two statements.

97.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the law relating to an Inverted Duty Structure?
o: Refund of unutilised input tax credit is permitted in such cases
Output tax is permanently waived for affected businesses
Unutilised input tax credit is forfeited in every case
Input tax credit can be claimed only on exports
97.x: The law allows a refund of unutilised input tax credit in cases involving an Inverted Duty Structure.
97.tq: Look for the specific statutory remedy rather than the underlying problem.

97.s: Which of the following correctly represents the original GST rate structure introduced in 2017, apart from exempt goods and compensation cess?
97.x: The original GST structure contained slabs of 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, along with exempt goods and compensation cess over 28% for specified goods.
97.tq: Recall the complete original slab sequence.

97.s: Compensation cess over the 28% GST slab was originally imposed mainly on which category of goods?
97.x: Compensation cess over the 28% slab applied to luxury and sin goods, including luxury cars, aerated drinks, pan masala and tobacco.
97.tq: Match the tax instrument with its intended category.

97.s: The GST 2.0 reforms were approved at which GST Council meeting and became effective from which date?
97.x: The GST 2.0 reforms were approved at the 56th GST Council meeting held on 3–4 September 2025 and became effective on 22 September 2025.
97.tq: Pair the reform package with both its approving meeting and effective date.

97.s: Which of the following correctly compares the principal GST rate structure before and from 22 September 2025?
97.x: Before 22 September 2025, the principal slabs were 0%, 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, with cess. GST 2.0 uses 0%, 5% merit, 18% standard and 40% demerit slabs.
97.tq: Compare the complete old and new slab structures rather than one rate alone.

97.s: Under GST 2.0, approximately what proportion of items in the old 12% slab was shifted to the 5% slab?
97.x: Approximately 99% of the items in the old 12% slab were moved to the 5% slab under GST 2.0.
97.tq: Distinguish the specific percentage associated with the old 12% slab.

97.s: Under GST 2.0, approximately what proportion of items in the old 28% slab was shifted to the 18% slab?
97.x: Approximately 90% of the items in the old 28% slab were moved to the 18% slab; the remaining items moved to the 40% slab.
97.tq: Separate the 90% movement from the 99% movement under the two slab changes.

97.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 40% demerit goods under GST 2.0?
97.x: Ultra-luxury cars and SUVs, yachts, private aircraft, tobacco, pan masala and online gaming are included among the 40% demerit goods. Essential medicines are not listed in this category.
97.tq: Find the item that does not belong to the specified demerit category.

97.s: Which of the following taxes was NOT among the independent indirect-tax instruments surrendered by States to GST?
97.x: States surrendered instruments such as VAT, entry tax, luxury tax, entertainment tax and octroi to GST. Corporate income tax was not one of these State-level indirect taxes.
97.tq: Remove the tax belonging to a different level and category of taxation.

97.s: Under the GST compensation arrangement, States were guaranteed compensation for which period and at what annual growth rate over the 2015–16 base?
97.x: States were guaranteed compensation for five years, from July 2017 to June 2022, at an assured annual growth rate of 14% over the 2015–16 base.
97.tq: Link the compensation period with its guaranteed growth rate and base year.

97.s: The GST compensation cess was continued after the compensation period primarily to:
o: Repay loans taken to pay compensation during the COVID-19 period
97.x: After the compensation period, the cess was continued to repay loans taken for paying GST compensation during the COVID-19 period.
97.tq: Identify the stated purpose behind continuation of a fiscal instrument.

97.s: With effect from 22 September 2025, the GST compensation cess was scrapped for all goods except:
97.x: The compensation cess was scrapped on 22 September 2025 except for tobacco products, on which it continues until cess-account loan obligations are discharged.
97.tq: Test the exception to a general abolition of the cess.

97.s: GST is described as a destination-based consumption tax because its revenue principally accrues to:
o: The State where the supplier is incorporated
The Union Territory where the invoice is generated
The State where goods are produced
The State where goods or services are consumed
97.x: Under the destination-based principle, GST revenue goes to the State where goods or services are consumed, rather than where they are produced.
97.tq: Distinguish destination-based taxation from origin-based taxation.

97.s: With respect to an inter-State supply under GST, which of the following is correct?
o: IGST is levied by the Centre and apportioned, with the destination State receiving the State share
CGST and SGST are both collected exclusively by the producing State
IGST is levied by the destination State and transferred to the Centre
SGST is levied and retained entirely by the producing State
97.x: IGST on inter-State supplies is levied by the Centre and apportioned. The destination State receives the State share under the destination-based system.
97.tq: Identify the correct authority and destination for inter-State tax revenue.

97.s: Article 269A of the Constitution is primarily associated with:
o: Distribution of income tax between the Centre and States
GST on inter-State supplies and its apportionment
97.x: Article 269A deals with the levy and collection of GST on inter-State supplies and its apportionment between the Union and the States.
97.tq: Match the constitutional Article with its precise fiscal function.

97.s: Which group of States mainly represents manufacturing or producing States that feared revenue loss under the destination-based GST system?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
97.x: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka were identified as manufacturing States that feared losses because GST revenue follows consumption rather than production. This concern contributed to the five-year compensation guarantee.
97.tq: Match the policy effect with the group of affected producing States.

97.s:
Consider the following statements about the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT):
1. It is the second-appeal forum above the appellate authorities.
2. Its Principal Bench is located at New Delhi.
3. It has State benches.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
97.x: GSTAT is the second-appeal forum above appellate authorities, with its Principal Bench at New Delhi and State benches.
97.tq: Verify the tribunal’s level, principal location and bench structure together.

97.s: As of mid-2025, which problem was associated with the GST Appellate Tribunal?
o: State benches had exclusive jurisdiction over direct taxes
The tribunal had replaced the Supreme Court as the final court of appeal
Only the New Delhi Principal Bench had been abolished
Functional benches were absent in many States despite notification
97.x: Although GSTAT had been notified, functional benches were absent in many States as of mid-2025, causing appeals to accumulate in High Courts.
97.tq: Distinguish notification or legal creation from actual operationalisation.

97.s: Which of the following statements regarding the current operational status of GSTAT benches is appropriate?
o: No GSTAT bench has ever been notified
The Principal Bench is located in Mumbai
All bench-related developments after July 2025 are conclusively established here
The operational status of benches, including the Andhra Pradesh bench, after July 2025 remains outside the stated information
97.x: The operational status of GSTAT benches, including the Andhra Pradesh bench, after July 2025 is not specified. The established position is that many States lacked functional benches as of mid-2025.
97.tq: Avoid extending a known time-bound fact beyond its stated period.

97.s: The 57th GST Council meeting was scheduled for which date, with inverted-duty refunds flagged as an issue?
97.x: The 57th GST Council meeting was scheduled for 12 September 2026, and inverted-duty refunds were identified as an issue for consideration.
97.tq: Separate the meeting date from the dates of related reports.

97.s: Which of the following is a criticism of cesses in the GST framework?
o: They can be imposed only by State legislatures
They are always included in the divisible pool for distribution to States
They remain outside the divisible pool, contributing to concerns over State fiscal autonomy
97.x: Cesses outside the divisible pool reduce the share available for devolution and are therefore linked with concerns about States’ fiscal autonomy and vertical fiscal imbalance.
97.tq: Connect the fiscal instrument with its federal consequence.

97.s: Which development was associated with Andhra Pradesh in relation to GST collections after the GST 2.0 rate cuts?
o: Replacement of GST by entry tax
Abolition of all State own taxes
A complete suspension of GST registration
97.x: AI-based enforcement was reported to have lifted Andhra Pradesh’s GST collections despite the GST 2.0 rate cuts.
97.tq: Identify the State-specific administrative measure and its outcome.

97.s: GST was introduced in India with effect from 1 July 2017 through which constitutional framework?
o: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 and Articles 246A, 269A and 279A
The 86th Amendment Act and Articles 243G, 243H and 243I
The 73rd Amendment Act and Articles 280, 281 and 282
The 42nd Amendment Act and Articles 301, 302 and 303
97.x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, with Articles 246A, 269A and 279A forming its key constitutional basis.
97.tq: Match the reform with its effective date, amendment and constitutional Articles.

97.s: Which of the following best describes the significance attributed to GST in India?
o: It replaced all forms of taxation, including income tax
It is the first direct tax reform since Independence
It is a temporary surcharge applicable only to States
It is the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence
97.x: GST is regarded as the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence. It did not replace direct taxes such as income tax.
97.tq: Distinguish the reform’s scale and tax category from exaggerated alternatives.

97.s: The approximate gross GST revenue reported for August 2026 was:
97.x: Gross GST revenue for August 2026 was approximately Rs 2 lakh crore.
97.tq: Select the approximate magnitude rather than an exact unsupported figure.

97.s: In Andhra Pradesh, GST accounted for approximately what share of the State’s own tax revenue in 2024–25?
97.x: GST was Andhra Pradesh’s largest own-tax source, accounting for approximately 38% of its own tax revenue in 2024–25.
97.tq: Recall the State-specific percentage and identify the largest own-tax source.

98.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional arrangement under Article 268?
o: The Union levies and collects the tax, but distributes it exclusively to local bodies
The States levy, collect and appropriate the tax
The Union levies the tax and the States collect and appropriate it
The States levy the tax and the Union collects and appropriates it
98.x: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States. Stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques and promissory notes are examples.
98.tq: Match the constitutional article with the correct authority exercising levy and collection powers.

98.s: Which of the following is an example of a duty covered under Article 268?
o: Tax on inter-State supply under IGST
Stamp duty on bills of exchange and cheques
98.x: Stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques and promissory notes are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States under Article 268.
98.tq: Use the example attached to the article rather than relying only on the article number.

98.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 268A:
1. It was inserted by the 88th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
2. It dealt with service tax collected by both the Union and the States.
3. It was omitted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Article 268A was introduced by the 88th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, for service tax collected by the Union and the States, and was omitted after the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.
98.tq: Check the amendment sequence and the subject of the omitted constitutional provision.

98.s: Tax on inter-State sale or purchase and consignment of goods was constitutionally associated with which Article?
98.x: Article 269 dealt with taxes on inter-State sale or purchase and consignment of goods. These taxes were levied and collected by the Union and assigned to the States.
98.tq: Distinguish between Union taxes shared under Article 270 and taxes assigned to States under Article 269.

98.s: With reference to Article 269A, which one of the following is correct?
o: It deals with surcharge collected wholly by the Union
It deals with State excise duty on liquor
It deals with taxes on professions and callings
It deals with IGST on inter-State supply
98.x: Article 269A concerns IGST on inter-State supply. The proceeds are apportioned between the Centre and the States on the advice of the GST Council.
98.tq: Separate the similar-looking Articles 269 and 269A by identifying the specific GST subject.

98.s: The proceeds of IGST on inter-State supply are apportioned between the Centre and the States on the advice of the:
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
98.x: Article 269A provides for apportionment of IGST on inter-State supply between the Centre and the States on the advice of the GST Council.
98.tq: Identify the constitutional body associated with the specific tax-distribution mechanism.

98.s: Which of the following correctly describes the taxes covered by Article 270?
o: All Union List taxes without any exceptions
Union List taxes shared through the Finance Commission, excluding specified taxes, surcharges and cesses
Only customs duties and Union excise duties
All State List taxes collected by the Union
98.x: Article 270 covers Union List taxes shared as recommended by the Finance Commission, but excludes Articles 268, 269 and 269A taxes, Article 271 surcharges and cesses.
98.tq: Watch for the extreme word “all” and test the constitutional exclusions from the divisible pool.

98.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the authority that levies it?
98.x: Excise on liquor is a State tax. Customs duty is levied by the Union, agricultural income tax by the States, and entertainment tax is largely subsumed in GST except for local bodies.
98.tq: Use the “who levies the tax?” test to distinguish Union and State revenue sources.

98.s: Which of the following statements regarding the 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000, is correct?
o: It introduced an alternative scheme of devolution based on pooling and sharing all Union taxes
It transferred all customs revenue to the States
It introduced GST with effect from 1 April 1996
98.x: The 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000, effective from 1 April 1996, introduced an alternative scheme of devolution under which all Union taxes were pooled and shared, replacing the earlier arrangement involving 29% of certain taxes.
