Its completion was proposed after the 2028 Irrigation White Paper deadline, without any proposed water diversion.
It was proposed to divert about 200 TMC of Krishna water to the Vamsadhara ayacut before the 2027 Pushkaralu.
It was proposed to be completed before the 2026 Pushkaralu by diverting 68 TMC of Godavari water.
115.x: The proposal was to complete Polavaram before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu and to divert about 200 TMC of Godavari water to the Nagarjunasagar ayacut.
115.tq: Link the correct project, deadline, river, quantity and ayacut while rejecting swapped figures and locations.

115.s: The Vamsadhara-Nagavali link was reported to be due for completion by:
115.x: The Vamsadhara-Nagavali link was due by December 2026.
115.tq: Use the project-specific completion month and year rather than the broader White Paper deadline.

115.s:
Which of the following are components of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)?
1. Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme
2. Har Khet Ko Pani
3. Watershed
4. Per Drop More Crop
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: PMKSY includes AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Watershed and Per Drop More Crop.
115.tq: Verify every item in a named-scheme list before selecting the coded combination.

115.s:
With reference to PMKSY, consider the following statements:
1. M-CADWM was approved in 2025–26.
2. M-CADWM is a sub-scheme of PMKSY-AIBP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Both statements are correct. M-CADWM was approved in 2025–26 as a sub-scheme of PMKSY-AIBP.
115.tq: Match the special sub-scheme with its approval year and parent programme.

115.s: Under NABARD-RIDF, how many lift irrigation schemes in Andhra Pradesh are being modernised?
115.x: Sixty-eight lift irrigation schemes are being modernised under NABARD-RIDF.
115.tq: Distinguish the number of schemes from the financial allocation and area benefited.

115.s: The modernisation of 68 lift irrigation schemes in Andhra Pradesh under NABARD-RIDF involves which combination of allocation and area?
115.x: The modernisation involves Rs 74.22 crore and covers 1.03 lakh acres.
115.tq: Pair the correct financial figure with the correct beneficiary area instead of mixing figures from different irrigation programmes.

115.s: The National Hydrology Project helped Andhra Pradesh establish:
115.x: The National Hydrology Project set up Andhra Pradesh's real-time groundwater monitoring system.
115.tq: Identify the practical institutional outcome associated with the named national project.

116.s: Which of the following correctly describes the industrial loss suffered by the residual State of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
o: It lost the HITEC City and Financial District, which had been the engine of IT exports
It retained Hyderabad's IT clusters and lost only its agricultural-processing units
It retained HITEC City and the Financial District but lost its port-based industries
It lost all IT activity because no new IT park was established in the State
116.x: The residual State lost Hyderabad's HITEC City and Financial District, important centres of IT and IT-enabled services exports.
116.tq: Identify the precise sector-location combination rather than accepting an extreme statement.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IT sector after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. HITEC City and the Financial District remained in Hyderabad.
2. New IT parks had to be started at Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Vijayawada.
3. The loss affected the principal engine of IT exports available to the residual State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: All three statements are correct. The major Hyderabad IT clusters remained outside residual Andhra Pradesh, requiring new parks in Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Vijayawada.
116.tq: Test a table row through location, consequence and response statements.

116.s: The loss of which Hyderabad-region industrial complex particularly affected the pharmaceutical and bulk-drug base of residual Andhra Pradesh?
o: Genome Valley and the Hyderabad pharma belt
116.x: Genome Valley and the Hyderabad pharmaceutical belt, including their research and development facilities, remained outside residual Andhra Pradesh.
116.tq: Use the sector-specific location clue to distinguish industrial clusters.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Sector — Position after bifurcation

A. IT/ITeS — HITEC City became part of residual Andhra Pradesh
B. Pharma/bulk drugs — AP retained only a bulk-drug base at Visakhapatnam
C. MSMEs — Hyderabad-linked ancillary units remained fully integrated within AP
D. IT/ITeS — New parks were established only at Kakinada
116.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh retained a bulk-drug base at Visakhapatnam, while the major Hyderabad pharma and R&D belt remained outside it.
116.tq: Find the correctly matched row after eliminating reversed locations and exaggerated claims.

116.s: What was the principal industrial consequence for MSMEs linked to Hyderabad after bifurcation?
o: They shifted entirely to the ports of coastal Andhra Pradesh
Thousands of ancillary units ended up across the border, disrupting supply chains
They were absorbed into the new capital administration
They were converted into public sector undertakings
116.x: Many Hyderabad-linked ancillary MSMEs ended up across the border, breaking the supply chains on which they depended.
116.tq: Test the cause-and-effect link between ancillary units and supply chains.

116.s: Hyderabad, together with Rangareddy and Medak, contributed approximately what share of the revenue of the undivided State?
116.x: The Hyderabad region, including Rangareddy and Medak, generated nearly 50 percent of the revenue of the undivided State.
116.tq: Use the approximate percentage as the decisive numerical clue.

116.s:
With reference to the immediate fiscal position of residual Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation, consider the following statements:
1. It received 58 percent of the population of the undivided State.
2. It received 46 percent of the revenue.
3. It inherited 58 percent of the debt on a population basis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh received 58 percent of the population, 46 percent of the revenue and 58 percent of the debt on a population basis.
116.tq: Check all numerical components of a distribution rather than focusing on one figure.

116.s:
Just after bifurcation, the industrial structure of residual Andhra Pradesh was described as follows:
1. The State was approximately 60 percent agriculture-dependent.
2. Manufacturing accounted for around 10.5 percent of GSDP.
3. The figure of 10.5 percent represented the entire industry sector, including mining, construction and utilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh was about 60 percent agriculture-dependent, and manufacturing was put at around 10.5 percent of GSDP. The 10.5 percent figure did not represent the whole industry sector.
116.tq: Separate a precise sectoral figure from the broader aggregate to catch a scope error.

116.s: At current prices in 2025-26, what was the share of services in the Gross Value Added of Andhra Pradesh?
116.x: Services accounted for 43 percent of GVA at current prices in 2025-26.
116.tq: Distinguish the sector share asked for from the other nearby percentage values.

116.s: Which of the following correctly explains the distinction between the 10.5 percent and 24 percent figures associated with the industrial sector of Andhra Pradesh?
o: 10.5 percent refers to services in 2025-26, whereas 24 percent refers to agriculture just after bifurcation
10.5 percent refers to manufacturing just after bifurcation, whereas 24 percent refers to industry as a share of GVA in 2025-26
10.5 percent refers to the debt share, whereas 24 percent refers to the revenue share
Both figures refer exclusively to manufacturing in 2025-26
116.x: The approximately 10.5 percent figure related to manufacturing just after bifurcation, while 24 percent was the industry share of GVA in 2025-26.
116.tq: Resolve a confusable pair by comparing both the sectoral scope and the time period.

116.s: Why did the retention of corporate and bank regional headquarters in Hyderabad create a difficulty for residual Andhra Pradesh?
o: It deprived the State of all banking services
It prevented the formation of any district administration
It left the State without a commercial nerve centre
It transferred all ports to Telangana
116.x: Corporate and bank regional headquarters stayed in Hyderabad, leaving residual Andhra Pradesh without a commercial nerve centre.
116.tq: Infer the institutional consequence from the location of headquarters.

116.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding institutional division under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation framework.

List-I
 a. Schedule IX
 b. Schedule X
 c. Sheela Bhide Committee
 d. Section 53

List-II
 i. Division of 142 institutions, mostly in Hyderabad
 ii. Allocation of commercial undertakings by location and headquarters assets by population
 iii. Division of 91 companies and corporations
 iv. Committee associated with the division of institutions

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

116.s:
Which of the following institutions or facilities were specifically left out during the division-related arrangements?

2. Andhra Pradesh Police Academy (APPA)
3. Andhra Pradesh Finance Academy (APFA)

116.s: The headquarters of the APSWAN state network was shifted to which location in 2017?
116.x: The APSWAN state headquarters shifted to the Velagapudi Secretariat in 2017.
116.tq: Test the exact institution-location-year combination.

116.s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, Hyderabad was to function as the common capital for a period of up to:
116.x: Hyderabad was designated as the common capital for up to ten years, till 2024, under Section 5.

116.s: Which change was made by the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026?
o: Hyderabad was made the permanent capital of both States
Visakhapatnam was declared the common capital till 2036
Amaravati was made the sole capital through new Section 5(3)
The three-capitals arrangement was extended indefinitely
116.x: The 2026 Amendment Act inserted new Section 5(3) to make Amaravati the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.

116.s: Which of the following best describes the significance of the 2026 amendment concerning the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It ended the 2019-24 uncertainty over the three-capitals issue
It initiated the 2019-24 uncertainty over three capitals
It abolished the capital without designating a replacement
It restored Hyderabad as the sole capital after 2024

116.s: Which clause of Section 94 provides for fiscal measures, including tax incentives, for industrialisation and growth?
116.x: Section 94(1) provides for fiscal measures, including tax incentives, to promote industrialisation and growth.

116.s:
Match the following provisions of Section 94 with their respective purposes.

List-I
 a. Section 94(1)
 b. Section 94(2)
 c. Section 94(3)
 d. Section 94(4)

List-II
 i. Denotification of degraded forest land for the capital
 ii. Programmes for physical and social infrastructure in backward areas
 iii. Fiscal measures including tax incentives
 iv. Special support for the new capital

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
116.x: The four clauses respectively concern fiscal measures, backward-area infrastructure, special support for the new capital and denotification of degraded forest land.

116.s: Under Section 94(3), special support for the new capital included provision for which set of institutions and facilities?
o: Ports, airports, industrial parks and universities
District courts, municipalities and police stations only
Raj Bhavan, High Court, Secretariat, Assembly and Legislative Council

116.tq: Test the complete institutional list rather than a partial list.

116.s: What amount was released under Section 94(3) for special support for the new capital?
116.x: ₹2,500 crore was released for special support for the new capital under Section 94(3).
116.tq: Distinguish the capital-support release from other infrastructure and investment figures.

116.s: How many backward districts were covered by the backward-area funds associated with Section 94(2)?
o: Nine districts, comprising five Rayalaseema and four North Coastal districts
Five districts, comprising three Rayalaseema and two North Coastal districts
Seven districts, comprising four Rayalaseema and three North Coastal districts
Seven districts, comprising three Rayalaseema and four North Coastal districts
116.x: The funds covered seven backward districts: four in Rayalaseema and three in the North Coastal region.
116.tq: Check both the total and regional breakup to defeat a swapped-composition option.

116.s: Which statement regarding the backward-area funds and notified tax benefits is correct?
o: The funds were never allocated and the tax benefits applied only to existing units
Initial allocations were made but disbursement later stalled; new units received additional depreciation and investment allowance of 15 percent each in the notified districts
Disbursement was complete and the incentives consisted of a 15 percent export subsidy only
The incentives applied uniformly to all districts of India without any regional condition
116.x: Initial allocations for the seven backward districts were made, but disbursement stalled. Notified benefits for new units included additional depreciation and investment allowance of 15 percent each.
116.tq: Combine implementation status with the exact incentive figures and eligibility condition.

116.s: Which form of assistance was offered by the Centre in place of Special Category Status to Andhra Pradesh?
o: A Special Assistance Measure of ₹2,500 crore
A separate Finance Commission grant of ₹15,000 crore
A Special Assistance Measure of ₹24,350 crore
A permanent exemption from all central taxes
116.x: Special Category Status was refused with reference to the 14th Finance Commission, and the Centre offered a Special Assistance Measure of ₹24,350 crore instead.
116.tq: Use the substitute-policy and amount together to distinguish the central response.

116.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the industrial cluster at Sri City?
o: Tirupati district; automobile, electronics and EMC-related activities, with IIIT Sri City
YSR Kadapa district; integrated steel and petrochemicals
Kurnool district; aerospace and defence only
Anakapalli district; organic food processing only

o: Kakinada — Vizag-Kakinada PCPIR and Kakinada SEZ
Visakhapatnam — Pharma City, port-based industry and IT

116.tq: Find the wrong cluster-sector pairing by separating automobile, electronics and steel activities.

116.s: The Kia India car plant is located at which place-cluster combination?
o: Penukonda in Sri Sathya Sai district

116.tq: Test the exact industrial location rather than the district alone.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding major industrial nodes in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The JSW integrated steel plant is located in YSR Kadapa district.
2. Its Phase-I investment was ₹4,500 crore and the total investment was ₹16,350 crore.

116.s: Which of the following correctly represents the CBIC/HBIC industrial land figures and locations?
116.x: The CBIC/HBIC multi-sector nodes covered 10,834 acres at Krishnapatnam and 2,621 acres at Orvakal.

116.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a proposed BHAVYA industrial initiative in Andhra Pradesh?

116.s:
Which of the following was identified as a reason for the investment chill in Andhra Pradesh after 2014?
1. Uncertainty over the capital
2. Absence of a ready administrative set-up
3. Agitations
4. Lack of any coastline
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Capital uncertainty, the absence of a ready administrative set-up and agitations reduced FDI and private investment. Lack of a coastline was not a reason; Andhra Pradesh has a substantial coastline.
116.tq: Find the false cause by contrasting investment barriers with the State's geographical advantage.

116.s: Which of the following was NOT cited as a component of the high cost of doing business in post-bifurcation Andhra Pradesh?
o: Excessive concentration of mature industrial facilities outside Hyderabad
116.x: The high cost of doing business was linked to the lack of mature power grids, logistics parks and ready factories. The stated issue was not excessive concentration of mature facilities outside Hyderabad.
116.tq: Identify the exception by separating explicitly listed infrastructure gaps from an altered formulation.

116.s: What was the principal commercial consequence of the loss of Hyderabad-centred supply chains?
o: Trade was confined to the seven backward districts
Trade links with ports were permanently discontinued
Trade had to be re-routed away from those supply chains
All trade shifted automatically to Amaravati
116.x: With Hyderabad no longer serving as the commercial base, trade had to be re-routed away from Hyderabad-centred supply chains.
116.tq: Infer the operational consequence of losing a metropolitan supply-chain hub.

116.s: Which statement regarding the coastline of Andhra Pradesh and its commercial strategy is correct?
o: The coastline was used only for tourism and not for export-import activity
The coastline was reported as 974 km in the older figure and 1,053 km after remeasurement, supporting a port-led EXIM strategy
The remeasured coastline was shorter than the old figure and ports were transferred to Telangana
The State had no significant coastline and therefore adopted an inland-only strategy
116.x: The older coastline figure was 974 km and the remeasured figure was 1,053 km. The coastline and the State's ports supported a port-led export-import strategy.
116.tq: Compare old and remeasured figures while linking them to the stated policy advantage.

116.s: The Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) was first released for States in which year, with the collaboration of which institutions?
o: 2017, by the Ministry of Commerce and the World Bank

2016, by DPIIT in collaboration with the IMF

116.s:

119.tq: Apply the who-launched-what association without confusing the minister with other technology portfolios.

119.s: What is the telephone number associated with the Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance service?
119.x: The number associated with Mana Mitra is 9552300009.
119.tq: Test an exact service identifier through numerical recall.

119.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27, approximately how much was allocated to RTGS, with a target of providing 1,000 services?
119.x: Approximately ₹100 crore was provided for RTGS in the Budget 2026–27, with a target of 1,000 services.
119.tq: Link the allocation figure with the associated service-delivery target.

119.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an RTGS tool and its function?
119.x: AWARE is an RTGS tool used for disaster-related purposes. AP DigiVerify is associated with blockchain certificates, AI4PGRS with grievance redressal, and CCTV360° with surveillance.
119.tq: Start from the sure tool-function pair and reject swapped functions.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about RTGS in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is the nodal agency for real-time monitoring, data analytics, artificial intelligence and early warning.
2. It operates the State Data Lake, Data Lens and the Command and Control Centre.
3. It is confined to monitoring information technology exports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. RTGS has broad governance, analytics and early-warning functions; it is not confined to monitoring IT exports.
119.tq: Find the single over-narrow statement among the institutional functions.

119.s: The AI City Flood Alert system associated with RTGS was first started in which city?
119.x: The AI City Flood Alert system was first started in Vijayawada.
119.tq: Separate the pilot location from the partner institutions and other AP cities.

119.s:
The AI City Flood Alert system in Andhra Pradesh was developed with the participation of which institutions?
1. Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority
2. IIT Gandhinagar
3. NIELIT Tirupati
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The system was developed with APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar. NIELIT Tirupati was not identified as a partner in this system.
119.tq: Use the institutional-partner trap to reject an unrelated organisation.

119.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its RTGS-related application?
119.x: AI4PGRS uses artificial intelligence for grievance redressal. AWARE 2.0 concerns early warning, while AP DigiVerify is linked with blockchain records.
119.tq: Identify the correctly matched pair after checking for swapped functions.

119.s: AP DigiVerify is associated with approximately how many blockchain records?
119.x: AP DigiVerify had approximately 9.85 crore blockchain records.
119.tq: Distinguish crore and lakh figures in a data-technology statistic.

119.s: Which of the following statements regarding AWARE 2.0 is correct?
o: It is a blockchain system for land registration.
It is a platform for training MeeSeva agents through television.
It is an early-warning system used during cyclones Montha and Ditwa.
It is a portal for multi-product exports from Sri City.
119.x: AWARE 2.0 is an early-warning system that was used during cyclones Montha and Ditwa.
119.tq: Associate the named tool with its distinctive operational use.

119.s: Which platform was introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 1998 for computerised land and property registration?
119.x: CARD, or Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department, was introduced in 1998 for computerised land and property registration.
119.tq: Use the year-function association for a named e-governance platform.

119.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the principal Andhra Pradesh e-governance platforms?
A. MeeSeva
B. CARD
C. eSeva
119.x: CARD was introduced in 1998, eSeva in 2001 and MeeSeva in 2011. Therefore, the order is B, C, A.
119.tq: Arrange the platforms by their introduction years from earliest to latest.

119.s: Which one of the following was described as India's first integrated citizen service centre initiative?
119.x: eSeva, launched in 2001, was described as India's first integrated citizen service centre initiative.
119.tq: Test the distinctive first-in-India claim rather than the later single-window description.

119.s: eSeva was launched under the chief ministership of:
119.x: eSeva was launched under N. Chandrababu Naidu.
119.tq: Apply the chief-minister association to the correct historical initiative.

119.s: MeeSeva, introduced in 2011, is best described as a:
o: computerised system restricted to property registration
single-window citizen service delivery portal and centre network
119.x: MeeSeva is a single-window citizen service delivery portal and network of service centres.
119.tq: Match the platform with its defining service-delivery concept.

119.s: During its first year, MeeSeva training was delivered through television in partnership with:
119.x: MeeSeva training during its first year was delivered through television in partnership with MANA TV.
119.tq: Use the partner-organisation association and avoid confusing it with later technology institutions.

119.s: Which of the following statements regarding the digital records anchored on AP DigiVerify is correct?
o: 5.01 crore MeeSeva records and 5.70 crore AP Seva records are anchored on it.
5.70 crore MeeSeva records and 5.01 crore AP Seva records are anchored on it.
Only property-registration records are anchored on it.
Both MeeSeva and AP Seva have exactly 5.01 crore records on it.
119.x: AP DigiVerify anchors 5.01 crore MeeSeva records and 5.70 crore AP Seva records.
119.tq: Compare the two close numerical figures instead of reversing their platforms.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about electronic procurement in Andhra Pradesh:
1. e-Procurement has been operating since 2002.
2. The Konugolu e-auction portal came under G.O.Ms. No. 16 dated 27 September 2018.
3. The Konugolu portal was established under the AP IT Rules of 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Konugolu portal came under G.O.Ms. No. 16 of 27 September 2018, not under the AP IT Rules of 2011.
119.tq: Use the date-and-authority distinction to reject the swapped legal basis.

119.s:
Which of the following was a consequence of the Andhra Pradesh IT Rules (Electronic Service Delivery), 2011?
1. Digitally signed certificates received legal sanctity.
2. Electronic delivery of services was made mandatory for departments.
3. The Information Technology Act, 2000 was repealed in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The rules gave legal sanctity to digitally signed certificates and made electronic service delivery mandatory. They did not repeal the Information Technology Act, 2000.
119.tq: Reject the extreme legal-effect statement while retaining the two stated consequences.

119.s: The parent legislation for the Andhra Pradesh IT Rules (Electronic Service Delivery) is the:
119.x: The parent law is the Information Technology Act, 2000. The Act was last amended in 2008.
119.tq: Distinguish the parent Act from its later amendment year.

119.s: Which statement correctly describes the distribution of IT activity before the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014?
o: IT exports began only after the creation of RTGS.
Hyderabad's HITEC City and Cyberabad generated the state's IT exports.
Kopparthy was the principal source of the state's IT exports before 2014.
Residual Andhra Pradesh generated all the state's IT exports before bifurcation.
119.x: Before bifurcation, Hyderabad's HITEC City and Cyberabad, developed under N. Chandrababu Naidu, generated the state's IT exports.
119.tq: Separate the pre-bifurcation Hyderabad base from the post-bifurcation residual state.

119.s: The residual Andhra Pradesh IT sector was described as having started from zero after:
o: the bifurcation of the State in 2014
119.x: After bifurcation in 2014, residual Andhra Pradesh's IT sector was described as having started from zero.
119.tq: Link the sectoral trend to the relevant structural event.

119.s: In 2025, Andhra Pradesh's IT investment and employment figures were approximately:
119.x: The 2025 figures were IT investment of ₹1,48,956.49 crore and generation of 1,41,023 jobs.
119.tq: Keep the investment figure and employment figure in their correct units and order.

119.s: What was the value of the 54 IT-related Memoranda of Understanding brought by the CII Partnership Summit 2025?
119.x: The CII Partnership Summit 2025 brought 54 IT MoUs valued at ₹1,95,294 crore.
119.tq: Associate the number of MoUs with their aggregate investment value.

119.s: The proposed Google AI data centre in Andhra Pradesh, located in the Visakhapatnam–Anakapalle region, is valued at approximately:
119.x: The proposed Google AI data centre in the Visakhapatnam–Anakapalle region is valued at approximately ₹87,520 crore.
119.tq: Differentiate the data-centre investment from the state-wide and summit investment figures.

119.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Tirupati (Renigunta) — Tirupati district
2. Sri City — Tirupati district, formerly Chittoor
3. Kopparthy — YSR Kadapa district
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three pairs are correct. Tirupati (Renigunta) and Sri City are associated with Tirupati district, while Kopparthy is in YSR Kadapa district.
119.tq: Verify every location pair before selecting the complete combination.

119.s: Sri City is best described as a:
o: multi-product Special Economic Zone associated with Foxconn and Isuzu
state command centre for flood alerts
VCIC node in YSR Kadapa district
119.x: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ in the Tirupati region and is associated with Foxconn and Isuzu.
119.tq: Match the industrial cluster with its distinctive industrial and company profile.

119.s:
Which of the following statements about Kopparthy is correct?
1. It is a VCIC node.
2. It covers 2,596 acres.
3. It is planned as a smart industrial city with potential investment up to ₹8,860 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Kopparthy is a VCIC node covering 2,596 acres, planned as a smart industrial city with potential investment up to ₹8,860 crore.
119.tq: Use the complete set of location, area and investment details.

119.s: Which of the following institutions is located in Tirupati along with the Tirupati (Renigunta) Electronics Manufacturing Cluster?
119.x: IIDT and a NIELIT centre are also located in Tirupati in association with the Tirupati cluster area.
119.tq: Identify the institutions geographically associated with the cluster.

119.s:
The principal policy instruments mentioned for electronics manufacturing in Andhra Pradesh are:
1. Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 (2024–29)
2. Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy 2025
3. AP IT Rules (Electronic Service Delivery), 2011
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The two electronics-manufacturing policies are Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 (2024–29) and Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy 2025. The AP IT Rules concern electronic service delivery, not electronics manufacturing.
119.tq: Separate sector-specific manufacturing policies from an e-governance regulation.

119.s: NIELIT Tirupati, located at Sri Venkateswara University, was formally inaugurated on:
119.x: NIELIT Tirupati at Sri Venkateswara University was formally inaugurated on 2 October 2025.
119.tq: Use exact date recall for a recent institutional inauguration.

119.s: The Andhra Pradesh IT Policy 2021-24 was notified primarily with which objective?
o: To boost growth and employment generation
To establish only semiconductor fabrication units
To replace the State GST framework
119.x: The Andhra Pradesh IT Policy 2021-24 was notified to promote growth and generate employment in the information technology sector.
119.tq: Identify the stated policy objective rather than being distracted by unrelated sectoral functions.

119.s: The Andhra Pradesh IT & GCC Policy 4.0, 2024-29, came into force on:
119.x: The AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0, covering 2024-29, came into force on 12 December 2024.
119.tq: Use precise date discrimination among closely spaced policy years.

119.s: Which one of the following best describes the broad aim of the Andhra Pradesh IT & GCC Policy 4.0?
o: To restrict multinational companies to urban municipalities
To shift all IT activity outside the coastal region
To promote only government-owned software companies
To make Andhra Pradesh a global knowledge economy hub
119.x: The policy aims to position Andhra Pradesh as a global knowledge economy hub.
119.tq: Match the policy with its broad vision, avoiding extreme and restrictive distractors.

119.s: The co-working and neighbourhood workspaces proposed under the Andhra Pradesh IT & GCC Policy 4.0 include which set of cities?

119.tq: Test the exact membership of a location-based policy list.

119.s: A Global Capability Centre (GCC), in the context of Andhra Pradesh's IT policy, is best understood as:
o: A multinational company's own offshore unit
A public sector semiconductor testing laboratory
A third-party vendor supplying temporary clerical staff
119.x: A GCC is an offshore unit owned and operated by a multinational company for its own capabilities and operations, rather than a third-party vendor.
119.tq: Discriminate between a multinational's captive unit and an outsourced third-party service provider.

119.s: An IT Park for Phenom People is associated with which of the following locations and investment details?
o: 4.45 acres at Madhurawada, with an investment of ₹207.5 crore
18 acres at Tirupati, with an investment of ₹100 crore
50 acres at Gannavaram, with an investment of ₹1,205 crore
9 acres at Vijayawada, with an investment of ₹1,000 crore
119.x: The Phenom People IT Park is planned over 4.45 acres at Madhurawada in the Rushikonda non-SEZ area, involving ₹207.5 crore.

119.s: Madhurawada, where the Phenom People IT Park is located, is described as being in which category?
o: A notified Special Economic Zone at Amaravati
A semiconductor fabrication zone at Gannavaram
A quantum technology zone at Vijayawada

Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Acronym)
A. LIFT Policy 4.0

D. OSAT

119.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the two Quantum Test and Reference Facilities in Andhra Pradesh?

1S at IIT Hyderabad and 1Q at Amaravati Secretariat
1Q at SRM University-AP and 1S at Medha Towers, Gannavaram

Consider the following statements about the physical infrastructure of Quantum Valley Amaravati:

2. The project cost is ₹1,205 crore.
3. The towers are being built by Larsen & Toubro.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

o: The Valley has no announced launch timeline and no associated quantum computer proposal.
The Valley launched in April 2024 and the computer was promised for 2025.
The Valley was scheduled to launch in January, while the IBM-TCS quantum computer was promised for 2026.

119.s: Among the following, which was one of the outcomes or proposals associated with the seven MoUs signed in February 2026?

Construction of the Phenom People IT Park
Creation of a nine-gigawatt data-centre ecosystem

Which of the following combinations was associated with the seven MoUs signed in February 2026?
1. UNICC Centre of Excellence
2. IBM training one lakh youth
3. A NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
119.x: The seven MoUs included a UNICC Centre of Excellence, IBM's training initiative for one lakh youth and a NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university.
119.tq: Recognise a complete set of related MoU outcomes rather than selecting a partial combination.

119.x: The foundation for Google's 1 GW data centre was associated with April 2026.
119.tq: Use the exact month-year marker for a current infrastructure project.

119.x: The APCRDA call referred to a 9 GW data-centre ecosystem.

119.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of N. Chandrababu Naidu in Andhra Pradesh's technology development?
o: His 1990s IT push helped build HITEC City, while the post-2014 IT base was rebuilt around Visakhapatnam.
His IT push was confined to the establishment of APSFL after 2020.
He developed only the quantum test beds and had no role in earlier IT infrastructure.
His technology initiatives began only after 2014 and were centred exclusively on Tirupati.
119.x: Naidu's 1990s IT push contributed to HITEC City's development, and after 2014 Andhra Pradesh rebuilt its IT base around Visakhapatnam.
119.tq: Compare the pre- and post-2014 phases instead of treating them as one period.

119.s: Which of the following initiatives belonged to the Naidu era of 1995-2004 and helped lay the foundation of Andhra Pradesh's technology governance?
o: HITEC City, eSeva and the SMART governance model
Google's AI hub, APCRDA's 9 GW call and 1Q
The IBM-TCS quantum computer and NIELIT deemed university

119.s: APSFL is significant in the context of Andhra Pradesh because it was:
o: The first private GCC in Andhra Pradesh
The first state-owned Internet Service Provider
119.x: APSFL was the first state-owned Internet Service Provider.

119.s: Mana Mitra, included in the Andhra Pradesh Budget for 2026-27, was allocated:

119.tq: Match the scheme with its budget amount while avoiding figures from other projects.

119.tq: Recall the approximate share rather than substituting a round majority figure.

119.s: Which of the following correctly states a criticism associated with the expansion of data centres in Andhra Pradesh and India?
o: Data centres are criticised only because they reduce temple bookings.
India already has a universally binding sustainability policy for all data centres.
Data centres can strain power and water resources, and India lacks a binding data-centre sustainability policy.
Data centres eliminate the need for electricity and water management.
119.x: Data centres are criticised for their pressure on power and water resources, while India is noted as lacking a binding data-centre sustainability policy.
119.tq: Apply the environmental criticism to the infrastructure scenario without accepting absolute claims.

119.s: Which of the following concerns has been raised in relation to the Data Lake?
119.x: Privacy and algorithmic-bias concerns have been raised in relation to the Data Lake.
119.tq: Match the governance concern with the correct digital platform or data initiative.

119.s: Which statement best reflects the comparative position of Karnataka mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh's technology policies?
o: Karnataka has no GCC policy but has only a quantum policy.
Karnataka is the only Indian State with a data-centre policy.
Karnataka also operates GCC and data-centre policies.
Karnataka operates only agricultural technology policies.
119.x: Karnataka also runs policies relating to Global Capability Centres and data centres, making it a relevant comparator for Andhra Pradesh.
119.tq: Use comparative wording carefully and reject exclusive claims unsupported by the comparison.

119.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Google AI hub — 9 GW; APCRDA data-centre ecosystem call — 1 GW
Google AI hub — 1 GW; APCRDA data-centre ecosystem call — 9 GW
Google AI hub — 50 acres; APCRDA data-centre ecosystem call — 18 storeys
Google AI hub — ₹100 crore; APCRDA data-centre ecosystem call — ₹207.5 crore
119.x: Google's Vizag AI hub is associated with 1 GW, whereas the APCRDA call referred to a 9 GW data-centre ecosystem.
119.tq: Compare two related capacities to avoid reversing project-level and ecosystem-level figures.

119.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of selected initiatives from earliest to latest?
o: eSeva, Quantum Test and Reference Facilities, PanIIT Summit on deep tech
Quantum Test and Reference Facilities, eSeva, PanIIT Summit on deep tech
PanIIT Summit on deep tech, eSeva, Quantum Test and Reference Facilities
eSeva, PanIIT Summit on deep tech, Quantum Test and Reference Facilities
119.x: eSeva dates to 2001, the quantum facilities were launched in April 2026, and the PanIIT Summit is scheduled for October 2026.

119.s: Which of the following statements about the AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0 is INCORRECT?
o: It was approved by the State Cabinet.
It is restricted exclusively to third-party vendors and excludes GCCs.
It came into force on 12 December 2024.
119.x: The policy specifically includes GCCs; a GCC is a multinational's own offshore unit, not merely a third-party vendor.
119.tq: Find the statement that reverses the policy's central GCC focus.

119.s: The Quantum Valley project is associated with which national mission?
119.x: The Quantum Valley project has 50 acres under the National Quantum Mission.
119.tq: Match the specialised technology project with the correct national mission.

119.s: Which of the following correctly states the current relevance of quantum infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The quantum test beds are planned only after the 2030 data-centre ecosystem.
The quantum test beds were launched in January 2024 and the Valley launch was cancelled.
The quantum test beds and Valley were both launched in 2001.

119.tq: Combine two current milestones without confusing launch, foundation and projection dates.

120.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the administration of agricultural markets in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Rythu Bazars are run by Market Committees, whereas regulated yards are run by Estate Officers.
Rythu Bazars are run by Estate Officers, whereas regulated yards are run by Market Committees.

Equal to wholesale prices and above local retail prices
Equal to local retail prices and below wholesale prices
About 25% above wholesale prices and below local retail prices

120.s: Rythu Bharosa Kendras were established in Andhra Pradesh in 2020 with an initial network of:

120.x: The centres are now called Rythu Seva Kendras, and the rationalised number of functional RSKs is 8,489.

120.x: RSKs provide agricultural services such as soil testing, e-Panta, CCRC issuance, input subsidies, crop insurance, drone awareness and procurement. Issuing industrial licences is not among these services.

120.s: Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS) is best described as:
o: A not-for-profit company incorporated in October 2014
A statutory market committee established in 1999
A central government department established in 2020

o: Conducting the Agriculture Census and publishing the Economic Survey
Running the Debt Redemption Scheme 2014 and the Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming programme

120.x: Egg, meat and milk outputs all fell in 2023-24; milk recorded the largest decline, at 9.41%.
120.tq: Test the trend and the precise percentage together.

120.s: The tie-up between the Andhra Pradesh Dairy Development Cooperative Federation and Amul was made in:
120.x: The AP Dairy Development Cooperative Federation entered into the Amul-AP tie-up in 2020.
120.tq: Direct recall of the year associated with an institutional arrangement.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a breed associated with Andhra Pradesh?
120.x: Aseel is a poultry breed, not a buffalo breed. Ongole is cattle, Godavari is buffalo and Nellore is sheep.
120.tq: Find the wrong species association in a breed list.

120.s:
With reference to the 2019 livestock census in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Sheep population was 176.27 lakh and Andhra Pradesh ranked second.
2. Poultry population was 1,078.63 lakh and Andhra Pradesh ranked second.
3. Cattle population was 46.00 lakh and Andhra Pradesh ranked fourteenth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three statements correctly state the population, unit and national rank for 2019.
120.tq: Check population figures and ranks as separate components.

120.s: Which species had a population of 62.19 lakh in Andhra Pradesh in 2019 and ranked sixth nationally?
120.x: The buffalo population was 62.19 lakh and Andhra Pradesh ranked sixth nationally.
120.tq: Identify the species from its population-rank pair.

120.s: Which one of the following statements regarding livestock changes in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
120.x: Sheep population increased by 29.99% over 2012. Pigs declined by 41.40%, while cattle declined by 2.46%.
120.tq: Use the direction of change and percentage to reject reversed trends.

120.s: Milk production in Andhra Pradesh was sustained comparatively because of:
o: crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes
120.x: Milk production was supported by crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes.
120.tq: Link the stated production outcome with its identified cause.

120.s: India produced 239.30 MT of milk in 2023-24, with per capita availability of:
120.x: India's per capita milk availability was 471 grams per day in 2023-24.
120.tq: Associate a national production figure with its per capita measure.

120.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with India's 2023-24 allied-sector position in the world?
120.x: India ranked fourth in the world in meat production. It ranked second in eggs.
120.tq: Discriminate between closely placed international ranks.

120.s: The geographical area of Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
120.x: Andhra Pradesh has a geographical area of 162.97 lakh hectares according to APSES 2024-25.
120.tq: Distinguish the geographical base from component land-use areas.

120.s: In 2023-24, which category accounted for 49.55 lakh hectares, or 30.40% of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area?
o: Net area sown, including fish culture
120.x: Net area sown, including fish culture, was 49.55 lakh hectares, constituting 30.40% of the geographical area.
120.tq: Match the area figure with its land-use category and percentage.

120.s: Which of the following correctly represents the forest area of Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24?
o: 20.93 lakh hectares, or 12.84% of geographical area
24.29 lakh hectares, or 14.90% of geographical area
13.35 lakh hectares, or 8.19% of geographical area
36.88 lakh hectares, or 22.63% of geographical area
120.x: Forest area was 36.88 lakh hectares, accounting for 22.63% of the geographical area.
120.tq: Test the precise area-percentage pair rather than the category alone.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about land use in Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24:
1. Current fallows covered 24.29 lakh hectares.
2. Non-agricultural uses covered 20.93 lakh hectares.
3. Barren and unculturable land covered 13.35 lakh hectares.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three figures are correct for the respective land-use categories in 2023-24.
120.tq: Verify each area figure independently before choosing the combination.

120.s: Other fallows and culturable waste in Andhra Pradesh covered, respectively, how much area in 2023-24?
120.x: Other fallows covered 10.36 lakh hectares and culturable waste covered 4.04 lakh hectares.
120.tq: Compare adjacent land-use categories without reversing their order.

120.s: Net sown area in Andhra Pradesh declined from 67.26 lakh hectares in 2008-09 to which level in 2023-24?
120.x: Net sown area fell to 49.55 lakh hectares in 2023-24, a decline of about one-quarter from 2008-09.
120.tq: Track the end value in a two-year trend.

120.s: According to NITI Aayog, the cultivated area of Andhra Pradesh in 2020-21 was 10.1 million hectares, equivalent to approximately what share of its geographical area?
120.x: NITI Aayog reported 10.1 million hectares of cultivated area, equivalent to 37% of the geographical area.
120.tq: Connect the reported area with its stated percentage and year.

120.s:
Arrange the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order from earliest to latest:
A. 37.51 lakh hectares
B. 41.44 lakh hectares
C. 33.24 lakh hectares
120.x: Food-grain area was 41.44 lakh hectares in 2021-22, 33.24 lakh hectares in 2023-24 and 37.51 lakh hectares in 2024-25.
120.tq: Use the years attached to the figures to establish sequence.

120.s: The food-grain output of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25 was:
120.x: Food-grain output was 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024-25.
120.tq: Distinguish output from the corresponding cultivated-area figures.

120.s: The cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24, calculated as gross cropped area divided by net sown area, was:
120.x: The APSES 2024-25 recorded cropping intensity of 1.21 for 2023-24.
120.tq: Apply the stated ratio concept to the reported year-specific value.

120.s: An operational holding is best defined as:
o: Only irrigated land cultivated by a household
All land owned by a person, irrespective of whether it is cultivated
All land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit by one person, alone or with others, irrespective of title, size or location
Land recorded in the name of a single legal owner
120.x: An operational holding comprises land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit, regardless of title, size or location.
120.tq: Choose the definition that includes all qualifying conditions and the stated exception to title.

120.s: The Agriculture Census classifies operational holdings in Andhra Pradesh into how many size classes?
120.x: The five size classes are marginal, small, semi-medium, medium and large.
120.tq: Recall the number of categories in an official classification.

120.s: Which of the following is the correct order of operational holding size classes from smallest to largest?
120.x: The order is marginal, small, semi-medium, medium and large.
120.tq: Arrange classification categories by their area ranges.

120.s: A holding of 3 hectares belongs to which operational holding class?
120.x: Semi-medium holdings operate 2 to 4 hectares. A 3-hectare holding falls within this range.
120.tq: Apply the stated size boundaries to a practical case.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
120.x: Large holdings are 10 hectares and above, not below 10 hectares.
120.tq: Locate the reversed boundary in a classification table.

120.s: Besides five size classes, the Agriculture Census groups operational holdings into which three social groups?
120.x: The three social groups are Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Others.
120.tq: Separate social classification from area classification.

120.s: Sulakshana, associated with ICAR-CTRI, is a high-yielding variety of:
120.x: Sulakshana is a high-yielding tobacco variety developed in association with the Central Tobacco Research Institute.
120.tq: Direct recall of a variety-crop association.

120.s: The Central Tobacco Research Institute is located at:
120.x: The Central Tobacco Research Institute, an ICAR institute, is located at Rajahmundry.
120.tq: Recall the institute-location pair.

120.s: Why were Kakinada farmers advised in December 2019 to stop growing Bondalu paddy?
o: The variety was prohibited under the Agriculture Census.
Kerala, which had purchased the rice from Andhra Pradesh, began growing it itself.
The variety was declared unsuitable for black soils.
The variety required more irrigation than other paddy varieties.
120.x: Officials advised stopping Bondalu paddy cultivation because Kerala, its earlier buyer, had started producing the rice itself.
120.tq: Identify the market-related cause behind an agricultural advisory.

120.s: Which region is identified as Andhra Pradesh's main rice-growing area and aquaculture hub?
o: Godavari delta comprising East and West Godavari
120.x: The Godavari delta, covering East and West Godavari, is the main rice-growing area and an aquaculture hub.
120.tq: Match a region with its distinctive crop and allied activity.

120.s: Which crop combination is particularly associated with the Krishna zone comprising Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam?
120.x: The Krishna zone grows paddy, chillies and cotton.
120.tq: Recall a multi-crop regional association.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: Groundnut is the main crop of the scarce-rainfall district Anantapuramu. Guntur is associated with chillies, and Prakasam with FCV tobacco.
120.tq: Use the dominant crop-district pair and reject geographical swaps.

120.s: Guntur is especially known in Andhra Pradesh as the district associated with:
120.x: Guntur is identified as the chilli district of Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Direct recall of a crop-district identity.

120.s: Which districts are associated with onion production and the compensation payment of ₹128.33 crore to 37,752 onion farmers in 2025-26?
120.x: The onion-related compensation was paid to farmers in Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts.
120.tq: Link the compensation figure and beneficiary count to the correct districts.

120.s: The main FCV tobacco districts of Andhra Pradesh are:
120.x: Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.
120.tq: Distinguish the broader tobacco districts from the location of the Tobacco Board.

120.s: The Tobacco Board of India is located at:
120.x: The Tobacco Board is located at Guntur, although Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.
120.tq: Separate the institution's location from the crop's dominant districts.

120.s: With reference to the Economic Survey 2025-26, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Yields of major crops remained unchanged nationally and globally.
Yields of major crops declined nationally but exceeded global averages.
Yields of major crops rose globally but declined nationally.
Yields of major crops rose nationally but remained below global averages.
120.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that yields of major crops increased nationally, but they remained below global averages.
120.tq: Distinguish the direction of change from the comparison with the global average.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding food-grain and paddy area in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Kharif food-grain area increased from 18.13 lakh hectares in 2023-24 to 20.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25.
2. Rabi food-grain area increased from 15.11 lakh hectares to 17.15 lakh hectares during the same period.
3. Paddy area in Rabi 2024-25 was 6.93 lakh hectares.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three statements are correct. Kharif food-grain area was 20.36 lakh hectares, Rabi food-grain area was 17.15 lakh hectares and Rabi paddy area was 6.93 lakh hectares in 2024-25.
120.tq: Check each numerical row independently before selecting the coded combination.

120.s: The increase in food-grain area in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25 was associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: 16.5% increase in area and 11.7% rainfall deficit
12.85% increase in area and 11.7% rainfall surplus
11.7% increase in area and 12.85% rainfall surplus
12.85% decrease in area and 16.5% rainfall surplus
120.x: The 2024-25 rise in food-grain area was 12.85%, following an 11.7% rainfall surplus. The preceding year had recorded a 16.5% rainfall deficit.
120.tq: Separate the area percentage from the rainfall percentage and avoid reversing the two figures.

120.s: In the Kharif 2026 season, the sowing area recorded by 19 August was approximately what percentage of the normal area?
120.x: By 19 August, 18.9 lakh hectares had been sown against the normal 30.84 lakh hectares, or approximately 61%.
120.tq: Match the reported actual-to-normal area ratio with the percentage options.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Kharif 2026 crop-wise sowing position as a percentage of normal area?
120.x: The reported percentages were groundnut 34%, paddy 62%, maize 61%, pulses 70% and cotton 75% of normal area.
120.tq: Start with the sure crop-percentage pair and verify the remaining pairs before choosing the code.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kharif 2026 in Andhra Pradesh:
1. All 28 districts were in a rainfall-deficit condition.
2. Twenty-five districts were deficit and three were classified as large-deficit districts.
3. The sowing position was approximately 61% of the normal area by 19 August.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three statements are correct. Kharif 2026 was described as a drought season, with all 28 districts in deficit, 25 deficit and 3 large-deficit, and sowing at about 61% of normal by 19 August.
120.tq: Test the district count, its classification and the area figure as three separate statements.

120.s: The current shift in the cropping pattern of Andhra Pradesh is primarily towards:
o: Only paddy and other food grains
120.x: The cropping pattern is shifting towards fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices because of their profitability and export potential.
120.tq: Distinguish the emerging diversification pattern from the traditional crop groups.

120.s:
Which of the following factors are attributed to diversification of agriculture in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Market demand
2. Access to irrigation
3. Government policy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: Market demand, irrigation access and policy are all identified as factors driving agricultural diversification in Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: When all listed causal factors are directly relevant, test whether the complete combination is the key.

120.s: The conversion of paddy land into aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh has made which area the State's aquaculture hub?
120.x: Paddy land in the Godavari delta is being converted to aquaculture, making the delta the State's aquaculture hub.
120.tq: Apply the location-based trap by matching the activity with its specifically identified region.

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 11 crops targeted for productivity improvement under the 17 growth engines of Swarna Andhra @2047?
120.x: The 11 crops include paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, redgram, blackgram, bengalgram, groundnut, sunflower and sesamum. Sugarcane is not included in this specified list.
120.tq: Find the option outside the explicitly enumerated crop list.

120.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scheme)
a. YSR Jala Kala
b. YSR Rythu Bharosa
c. Rythu Bazars
 d. Jala Yagnam

List-II (Domain)
i. Investment support
 ii. Free borewells for farmers
 iii. Farmer-to-consumer sales
 iv. Irrigation through 52 major and medium projects

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: YSR Jala Kala provides free borewells; YSR Rythu Bharosa provides investment support; Rythu Bazars facilitate farmer-to-consumer sales; and Jala Yagnam concerns irrigation projects.
120.tq: Start from the sure scheme-domain pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining relationships.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jala Yagnam — Interest subvention on crop loans
120.x: Panta Sanjeevani refers to the construction of farm ponds. GAP Polambadi concerns farmer field schools and Ind.GAP certification, while Jala Yagnam concerns irrigation projects.
120.tq: Separate similarly agriculture-related schemes by identifying their precise domain rather than their broad sector.

120.s: Under Vaddi Leni Runalu or Pavala Vaddi, interest subvention on crop loans is provided as follows:
o: 1% up to ₹1 lakh and 4% for ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh
1% on all crop loans up to ₹3 lakh
4% up to ₹3 lakh and 1% above ₹3 lakh
4% up to ₹1 lakh and 1% for ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh
120.x: The scheme provides 4% interest subvention up to ₹1 lakh and 1% for the loan amount from ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh.
120.tq: Keep the two loan slabs and their respective rates in the correct order.

120.s: Panta Sanjeevani, in the context of Andhra Pradesh agriculture, refers to:
o: Distribution of free borewells to every farmer
Construction of farm ponds for rainwater harvesting and protective irrigation
Interest-free crop loans up to ₹3 lakh
Direct procurement of horticultural produce from farmers
120.x: Panta Sanjeevani means construction of farm ponds. It is a rainwater-harvesting measure for protective irrigation, with farm ponds dug through convergence with MGNREGS.
120.tq: Identify the practical component of the scheme from the agricultural problem it addresses.

120.s: Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with:
120.x: Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.
120.tq: Use the implementing-convergence relationship to distinguish the employment programme from insurance and certification schemes.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the free crop insurance arrangement in Andhra Pradesh during 2019-24?
o: The Centre paid the whole premium and only horticultural crops were covered.
The State and Centre shared the premium equally and enrolment was compulsory for all farmers.
The State paid the whole premium and CCRC holders were covered.
The farmer paid the entire actuarial premium and only loanee farmers were covered.
120.x: Under Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance during 2019-24, the State paid the entire premium and CCRC holders were covered.
120.tq: Distinguish the earlier free-insurance model from the subsequent voluntary premium-sharing model.

120.s: From Rabi 2024-25, Andhra Pradesh returned to which arrangement for crop insurance?
o: Voluntary enrolment under MNAIS with the Centre paying the full premium
Universal insurance under Ind.GAP with FPOs paying the premium
Compulsory enrolment under NAIS with the State paying the full premium
Voluntary enrolment under PMFBY/RWBCIS with the farmer paying a fixed share and the State and Centre sharing the balance equally
120.x: From Rabi 2024-25, enrolment became voluntary under PMFBY/RWBCIS. Farmers pay a small fixed share of the actuarial premium, while the State and Centre equally share the remainder.
120.tq: Compare the institutional arrangement, enrolment condition and premium-sharing formula in one option.

120.s:
Which of the following statements regarding PMFBY is/are correct?
1. PMFBY was introduced in 2016.
2. It replaced NAIS and MNAIS.
3. It became voluntary for all farmers from Kharif 2020.
4. It is a Central Sector scheme.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: PMFBY was introduced in 2016, replaced NAIS and MNAIS, became voluntary for all farmers from Kharif 2020, and is a Central Sector scheme.
120.tq: Test the scheme's year, predecessor schemes, enrolment rule and administrative classification separately.

120.s: Under PMFBY, the farmer's premium share is correctly stated as:
o: 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops
1.5% for Kharif, 2% for Rabi, and 5% for commercial crops
5% for Kharif, 2% for Rabi, and 1.5% for horticultural crops
2% for all crops in every season
120.x: The farmer premium under PMFBY is 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops.
120.tq: Avoid reversing the Kharif and Rabi rates and retain the separate commercial-crop rate.

120.s: The pilot project for direct benefit transfer of the agricultural power subsidy in Andhra Pradesh was undertaken in:
120.x: Srikakulam district was selected for the 2020 pilot involving smart meters on farm pump-sets and direct credit of subsidy to farmers' accounts.
120.tq: Use the district-specific location clue to distinguish the pilot site from other agricultural districts.

120.s: In the agricultural power subsidy DBT pilot in Andhra Pradesh, smart meters were installed on:
120.x: Smart meters were installed on farm pump-sets, and the subsidy was credited to farmers' accounts for payment to the distribution company.
120.tq: Identify the exact beneficiary asset rather than the broader electricity network.

120.s: Which one of the following is the stated long-term energy objective for agricultural pump-sets in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Restriction of agricultural power supply to Rabi season
Replacement of all pump-sets by diesel units
120.x: The State aims to achieve 100% renewable energy for agricultural pump-sets.
120.tq: Identify the precise policy target and reject options that reverse or narrow its objective.

120.s: GAP Polambadi is associated with:
o: Farmer Field Schools, Good Agricultural Practices and Ind.GAP certification
Crop insurance enrolment and premium collection
Construction of major and medium irrigation projects
120.x: Polambadi means Farmer Field Schools. GAP Polambadi teaches Good Agricultural Practices, aims to reduce chemical pesticide use and is linked to Ind.GAP certification for better prices for FPOs.
120.tq: Match the extension activity with its training, certification and pesticide-reduction functions.

120.s: The agricultural and allied-sector strategy under APSES 2024-25 targets what growth over five years?
120.x: The strategy targets 30% growth in agriculture and allied sectors over five years, delivered through 17 growth engines.
120.tq: Keep the target percentage and the number of delivery mechanisms together while rejecting swapped figures.

120.s: As per APSES 2025-26, the number of farmers practising natural farming in Andhra Pradesh is
120.x: APSES 2025-26 records 10.20 lakh farmers practising natural farming in Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from older and national farmer counts.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the area and number of Gram Panchayats covered under natural farming in Andhra Pradesh as per APSES 2025-26?
120.x: The reported coverage is 4.89 lakh hectares and 4,116 Gram Panchayats.
120.tq: Match two related numerical indicators without confusing area with kitchen-garden coverage.

120.s: The number of NF kitchen gardens reported under the natural farming programme is
120.x: The programme includes 3.68 lakh NF kitchen gardens.
120.tq: Use exact numerical recall for a smaller programme component.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the targets of natural farming in Andhra Pradesh:
1. All Gram Panchayats are targeted to be covered by 2026-27.
2. The target for 2028-29 is 41 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares.
3. The targets are associated with the Swarna Andhra@2047 initiative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three statements are correct: universal Gram Panchayat coverage is targeted for 2026-27, while 41 lakh farmers and 19 lakh hectares are targeted for 2028-29 under Swarna Andhra@2047.
120.tq: Test multiple target years and figures together through coded statements.

120.s: The natural farming programme works in clusters generally consisting of
120.x: The programme works in clusters of five villages covering approximately 1,500 to 2,500 acres.
120.tq: Recall a paired structural figure by linking the number of villages with the acreage range.

120.s: Under the 2024-25 plan, which one of the following correctly describes the proposed cluster arrangement per Parliamentary Constituency?
o: 10-15 village clusters, 5,000 acres per constituency and 50,000 acres in total
5-10 village clusters, 1,000 acres per constituency and 25,000 acres in total
2-5 village clusters, 2,500 acres per constituency and 10,000 acres in total
5-10 village clusters, 25,000 acres per constituency and 1,000 acres in total
120.x: The 2024-25 plan adopts 5-10 village clusters per Parliamentary Constituency, with 1,000 acres per constituency and 25,000 acres in total as stated in the programme design.
120.tq: Detect the reversed numerical relationship between per-constituency and total coverage figures.

120.s: The earlier count cited for farmers covered under the natural farming programme was
120.x: An earlier count cited in February 2026 referred to over 7 lakh farmers.
120.tq: Separate an earlier reported figure from the latest APSES coverage figure.

120.s: Rythu Sadhikara Samstha, commonly abbreviated as RySS, is
o: a private company established by farmer producer organisations
a not-for-profit company set up by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh
a statutory corporation under the Finance Department
a cooperative society under the Panchayat Raj Department
120.x: RySS stands for Rythu Sadhikara Samstha and is a not-for-profit company established by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Use the full-form and institutional-nature combination to avoid confusing a company with a statutory body or cooperative.

120.s: RySS was incorporated in
120.x: Rythu Sadhikara Samstha was incorporated in October 2014.
120.tq: Test the exact incorporation month and year against nearby programme dates.

120.s: In the context of Zero Budget Natural Farming, the expression “zero budget” primarily refers to
o: cultivation without purchased fertilisers or pesticides
120.x: “Zero budget” refers to avoiding purchased fertilisers and pesticides; it does not mean that every input or labour cost is absent.
120.tq: Interpret the exact meaning of a potentially misleading programme label.

120.s: Andhra Pradesh launched ZBNF in 2016 and subsequently renamed it as
120.x: The programme launched as ZBNF in 2016 was renamed APCNF, meaning Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming.
120.tq: Test the exact expansion of a renamed programme rather than a similar-sounding agricultural term.

120.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Jeevamrutham — seed treatment with cow dung, cow urine and lime
Mulching — sowing before rains on residual moisture
120.x: Ghanajeevamrutham is the solid form of Jeevamrutham. Beejamrutham is the seed treatment, while mulching is the use of crop residue or straw cover.
120.tq: Start from the sure practice-definition pair and reject swapped meanings.

120.s: Beejamrutham is used as
o: a solid bio-fertiliser made only from straw
a seed treatment prepared with cow dung, cow urine and lime
a trap crop consisting of marigold and castor
a crop-residue cover for suppressing weeds
120.x: Beejamrutham is a seed treatment involving cow dung, cow urine and lime.
120.tq: Distinguish a named preparation from other APCNF practices by its specific use.

120.s:
Which of the following ingredients are associated with Jeevamrutham?
1. Cow dung
2. Cow urine
3. Jaggery
4. Pulse flour
5. Soil
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: Jeevamrutham is prepared from cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, pulse flour and soil.
120.tq: Test a complete ingredient list through an all-inclusive coded option.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about APCNF practices:
1. Mulching uses crop-residue or straw cover to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
2. Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing involves sowing before the rains on residual moisture.
3. PMDS is associated with millets, pulses and oilseeds.
4. A 365-day green cover is maintained through cover cropping and polyculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements correctly describe mulching, PMDS and the 365-day green-cover approach.
120.tq: Combine closely related practice definitions while checking each statement independently.

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the APCNF practice package?
o: Exclusive dependence on purchased chemical fertilisers
Trap crops such as marigold and castor
120.x: APCNF promotes native seeds, minimal or no tillage, livestock integration and trap crops; exclusive dependence on purchased chemical fertilisers is contrary to the model.
120.tq: Find the one option that reverses the underlying principle of the programme.

120.s: Kurnool is promoting Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing on approximately how much area because of the El Nino-related rain deficit?
120.x: Kurnool is promoting PMDS on 92,000 acres in response to the El Nino-related rain deficit.
120.tq: Recall the exact area figure associated with a district-specific initiative.

120.s: The Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity associated with APCNF was awarded on
120.x: The Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity was awarded on 11 July 2024 in Lisbon and was shared with two others.
120.tq: Distinguish an exact award date from the dates of other natural-farming awards and initiatives.

120.s: The M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection was conferred on
o: the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh
120.x: The M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection was conferred on RySS.
120.tq: Use the award-recipient trap by distinguishing the implementing institution from an individual or foundation.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Food Planet Prize 2026:
1. APCNF was the first Indian finalist.
2. The prize amount was 1.5 million US dollars.
3. The award was associated with the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
4. It was held at Bastad in Sweden in June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All four statements are correct: APCNF was the first Indian finalist, and the June 2026 prize at Bastad, Sweden, carried an award of 1.5 million US dollars from the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
120.tq: Verify a named international award through its amount, sponsor, place and finalist status.

120.s:
Which of the following outcomes has been observed in the field in relation to APCNF?
1. Crop diversity
2. Better soil health

120.x: ₹315 lakh was paid to 63 families in 2024-25, with each family receiving ₹10 lakh.
120.tq: Use the aggregate-to-unit relationship to verify the beneficiary count.

120.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding national support measures for fishers?
o: Group Accident Insurance covers 33.15 lakh fishers annually, and KCC has been extended to fishers since 2018-19.
Group Accident Insurance covers 3.315 lakh fishers annually, and KCC began in 2024-25.
Group Accident Insurance covers 63 lakh fishers annually, and KCC is restricted to marine exporters.
Group Accident Insurance covers 1.17 lakh fishers annually, and KCC was extended from 2019-20.
120.x: National Group Accident Insurance covers 33.15 lakh fishers annually, and the Kisan Credit Card facility has been extended to fishers since 2018-19.
120.tq: Check both the coverage number and the year attached to the credit facility.

120.s: The fisheries cooperative structure in Andhra Pradesh comprises:
120.x: There are 2,356 fisheries cooperative societies with 3,09,018 members under the APCS Act, 1964.
120.tq: Retain the paired count of societies and members without reversing or altering the digits.

120.s: India’s first Mega Aqua Food Park was operationalised at:
120.x: The Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park at Tundurru in West Godavari was India’s first operational Mega Aqua Food Park.
120.tq: Link the project title, location and district to avoid confusing it with other aqua infrastructure.

120.s: The 10 fishing harbours in Andhra Pradesh, involving an outlay of ₹3,699.09 crore, are being implemented under:
120.x: The 10 fishing harbours are under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme component of PMMSY, not Sagarmala. The outlay is ₹3,699.09 crore.
120.tq: Identify the correct programme and reject the nearby infrastructure-scheme trap.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Upgrade of Kakinada fishing harbour — ₹178.51 crore
Modernisation of Visakhapatnam fishing harbour — ₹178.51 crore
120.x: Modernisation of Visakhapatnam fishing harbour has an outlay of ₹178.51 crore. Kakinada’s upgrade is ₹58.95 crore, the six Fish Landing Centres cost ₹126.91 crore, and the Integrated Aqua Park costs ₹88.08 crore.
120.tq: Match each project with its own outlay and eliminate swapped figures.

120.s: The number of Fish Landing Centres planned or supported in Andhra Pradesh under PMMSY, with an outlay of ₹126.91 crore, is:
120.x: Six Fish Landing Centres are supported with an outlay of ₹126.91 crore. The figures 10, 12 and 35 refer to other infrastructure or planning categories.
120.tq: Separate the number of landing centres from harbours, aquaparks and aqua laboratories.

120.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding aqua infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The RGCA brood centre at Visakhapatnam is meant for Vannamei shrimp only.
Thirty-five Integrated Aqua Parks are already operational in Andhra Pradesh.
The Integrated Aqua Park is located at Parasavaripalem in Bapatla and has an outlay of ₹88.08 crore.
The Integrated Aqua Park is located at Tundurru in West Godavari and has an outlay of ₹126.91 crore.
120.x: The Integrated Aqua Park is at Parasavaripalem in Bapatla and costs ₹88.08 crore. Thirty-five Integrated Aqua Labs are planned, of which 30 are working; the RGCA brood centre at Visakhapatnam is for black tiger shrimp.
120.tq: Use location, project type and amount together to detect swapped infrastructure details.

120.s: How many Integrated Aqua Labs are planned in Andhra Pradesh, and how many of them are working?
120.x: Thirty-five Integrated Aqua Labs are planned, of which 30 are working.
120.tq: Keep planned and operational counts in the correct order.

120.s: Which of the following is proposed in connection with aqua infrastructure and export support in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A cold chain at Tundurru and a salt laboratory at Tirupati
A fish auction centre at Amaravati and a marine museum at Kurnool
A hatchery at Vijayawada and a tuna port at Anantapur
A chilling plant at Bhogapuram airport and an Aquatic Quarantine Facility
120.x: A chilling plant at Bhogapuram airport and an Aquatic Quarantine Facility have been proposed. The Aquatic Quarantine Facility is associated with MPEDA.
120.tq: Identify the proposal by connecting the facility with its relevant logistics and quarantine function.

120.s: Under PMMSY, the total subsidy is what for the general category and women/SC/ST beneficiaries respectively?
120.x: The subsidy is 40% for the general category and 60% for women, SC and ST beneficiaries. The GoI-GoAP shares are 24%-16% and 36%-24% respectively.
120.tq: Read the categories in the same order as the question and do not reverse the percentage comparison.

120.s: The Government of India and Government of Andhra Pradesh components of the 40% general-category PMMSY subsidy are respectively:
120.x: For general-category beneficiaries, the 40% subsidy consists of 24% from the Government of India and 16% from the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Split the total subsidy into its two stated government components.

120.s: The implementation period and outlay of PM-MKSSY are:
120.x: PM-MKSSY covers FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 and has an outlay of ₹6,000 crore.
120.tq: Pair the scheme period with its own outlay rather than the larger PMMSY investment.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated feature of PM-MKSSY?
o: Compulsory replacement of all fishing boats with trawlers
Institutional credit for the fisheries sector
120.x: PM-MKSSY supports institutional credit, aquaculture insurance and supply-chain traceability. Compulsory replacement of all boats with trawlers is not a stated feature.
120.tq: Find the extreme and unsupported programme feature among the genuine objectives.

120.s: The National Fisheries Digital Platform under PM-MKSSY had registered approximately how many stakeholders?
120.x: The National Fisheries Digital Platform had registered 30.60 lakh stakeholders.
120.tq: Retain the decimal placement and distinguish lakh from crore-scale figures.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with PMMSY results?
120.x: The reported PMMSY results include 28 fishing harbours and 2,195 Fisheries Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs).
120.tq: Match the two scheme-result counts without interchanging the categories.

120.s: PMMSY results include how many Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages and Integrated Aquaparks respectively?
120.x: The reported results include 100 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages and 12 Integrated Aquaparks.
120.tq: Distinguish infrastructure counts from village and organisation counts.

120.s: The PMMSY allocation for 2026-27 and the FIDF corpus are respectively:
120.x: The PMMSY budget allocation for 2026-27 is ₹2,761.80 crore, while the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund corpus is ₹7,522 crore.
120.tq: Keep the annual allocation separate from the fund corpus and avoid reversing the pair.

120.s: Which of the following statements about fisheries initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: 2,195 boat transponders were allotted, and the project began for three years from 2025.
7,522 boat transponders were allotted, and the project began for five years from 2026.
4,484 boat transponders were allotted, and a GEF-FAO aquaculture project began for five years from 2025.
4,484 boat transponders were allotted, and the GEF-FAO project began for five years from 2020.
120.x: Andhra Pradesh allotted 4,484 boat transponders and has a GEF-FAO aquaculture project running for five years from 2025.
120.tq: Combine the correct quantity, project duration and starting year in one precise option.

120.s: According to the available information on production composition, which statement is correct?
o: Marine and inland fisheries contribute exactly equal shares in India.
Marine fisheries account for more than 75% of India’s fish output.
Andhra Pradesh’s marine and inland shares are stated as exactly 50:50.
Inland fisheries account for more than 75% of India’s fish output.
120.x: India-wide, inland fisheries contribute more than 75% of fish output. A specific marine-versus-inland percentage split for Andhra Pradesh is not provided.
120.tq: Do not transfer an India-wide comparison to the State level when the State-specific split is unavailable.
