125.tq: Use the conceptual contrast between the two policy groups rather than memorising isolated names.

125.s: Under the enterprise classification, the investment and turnover limits for a micro enterprise are respectively:
o: Up to ₹50 crore and up to ₹250 crore
Below ₹500 crore and up to ₹1,000 crore
Up to ₹1 crore and up to ₹5 crore
Up to ₹10 crore and up to ₹50 crore
125.x: A micro enterprise has investment up to ₹1 crore and turnover up to ₹5 crore under the stated classification.
125.tq: Pair the investment threshold with the corresponding turnover threshold.

125.s: Which of the following correctly represents the investment and turnover limits of a small enterprise?
125.x: The limits for a small enterprise are investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore.
125.tq: Distinguish successive enterprise thresholds without reversing investment and turnover.

125.s: An enterprise with investment up to ₹50 crore and turnover up to ₹250 crore falls under which category?
125.x: The stated limits of ₹50 crore investment and ₹250 crore turnover correspond to a medium enterprise.
125.tq: Apply the numerical classification thresholds to a hypothetical enterprise.

125.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Sub-Large — FCI below ₹500 crore
2. Large — ₹501–1,000 crore
3. Mega — ₹1,001–5,000 crore
4. Ultra-Mega — above ₹5,001 crore
125.x: All four category-threshold pairs are correctly stated. FCI means fixed capital investment in this classification.
125.tq: Check each adjacent investment band, where boundary figures are the main trap.

125.s: A project involving investment of ₹2,000 crore or generating 2,000 or more direct jobs is classified as:
125.x: A mega project involves ₹1,001–5,000 crore investment or 2,000 or more direct jobs.
125.tq: Apply the alternative investment-or-employment test for project classification.

125.s: Which statement regarding mega and ultra-mega projects is correct?
o: They receive identical benefits fixed uniformly by statute.
They are excluded from investment incentives.
They are eligible only if located in an industrial park.
They receive tailor-made packages decided on a case-by-case basis.
125.x: Mega and ultra-mega projects are eligible for tailor-made packages determined case by case.
125.tq: Identify the policy exception to uniform incentive rates.

125.s: The capital subsidy under MSME Policy 4.0 is stated as 25 per cent, subject to maximum limits of:
o: ₹25 lakh for micro, ₹1.5 crore for small and ₹7 crore for medium enterprises
₹50 lakh for micro, ₹1.5 crore for small and ₹7 crore for medium enterprises
₹10 lakh for micro, ₹50 lakh for small and ₹1 crore for medium enterprises
₹25 lakh for micro, ₹2 crore for small and ₹10 crore for medium enterprises
125.x: The capital subsidy is 25 per cent, capped at ₹25 lakh for micro, ₹1.5 crore for small, and ₹7 crore for medium enterprises.
125.tq: Match one common subsidy rate with three category-specific caps.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about industrial incentives:
1. The decarbonisation subsidy is capped at 6 per cent of FCI.
2. Women, BC, SC, ST and specially-abled entrepreneurs can receive an additional 5 per cent capital subsidy.
3. Food-processing projects with FCI above ₹100 crore may receive tailor-made benefits through SIPC/SIPB.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements correctly state the decarbonisation cap, the additional capital subsidy, and the special treatment for qualifying food-processing projects.
125.tq: Combine rate, beneficiary-category and sector-specific incentive provisions.

125.s: Under the incentive structure, the early-bird benefit for the first 200 CFEs within 18 months is:
125.x: The early-bird benefit is 30 per cent for the first 200 CFEs within 18 months.
125.tq: Separate the time-bound first tranche from the higher PLI-sector incentive.

125.s: For projects in PLI sectors with CFE within 24 months, the early-bird benefit is:
125.x: Projects in PLI sectors with CFE within 24 months are eligible for a 40 per cent early-bird benefit.
125.tq: Compare the sector-specific percentage with the general early-bird rate.

125.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Employment of Local Candidates in the Industries/Factories Act, 2019, the share of jobs reserved for local candidates is:
125.x: The 2019 Act provides for reservation of 75 per cent of jobs for local candidates.
125.tq: Recall the exact reservation percentage associated with the State employment law.

125.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Employment Creation Subsidy?
o: Up to 10 per cent of turnover for units with more than ten employees, paid over ten years
Up to 10 per cent of FCI for units with more than five employees and 8–9 per cent for units with five or fewer employees, paid over five years
A uniform 5 per cent of FCI for every unit, paid over three years
A subsidy of 1 per cent of export turnover for five years
125.x: The Employment Creation Subsidy is up to 10 per cent of FCI for units having more than five employees and 8–9 per cent for units having five or fewer employees, payable over five years.
125.tq: Compare employee-count slabs, the base for calculation and the payment period.

125.s: The Local Procurement Subsidy is calculated as:
o: 5 per cent of export turnover for three years
1 per cent of investment for five years
10 per cent of FCI for three years
1 per cent of export turnover for three years
125.x: The Local Procurement Subsidy is 1 per cent of export turnover for three years.
125.tq: Keep the subsidy base, rate and duration together rather than substituting a nearby incentive.

125.s: Which of the following is a stated function of the Single Desk system for investment proposals?
o: Providing one application point for every clearance required by an investment proposal
Providing only post-operation approvals to existing factories
Replacing all industrial licences with tax exemptions
125.x: The Single Desk system provides one application point for every clearance required by an investment proposal.
125.tq: Identify the core administrative purpose instead of confusing it with a substantive regulatory power.

125.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the online G2B services of the Single Desk system?
o: Physical submission as the exclusive mode of processing
125.x: The system provides online application, document upload, payment, status tracking and certificate download. Physical submission is not the exclusive mode of processing.
125.tq: Find the option that reverses the system’s online and transparency-oriented design.

125.s: A business applicant uses the Single Desk portal to upload documents, make payment, track the proposal and download the certificate. This illustrates which feature of the system?
125.x: The listed activities are integrated online Government-to-Business services under the Single Desk system.
125.tq: Recognise the underlying administrative concept from a practical sequence of services.

125.s: Under Industrial Development Policy 4.0, the dedicated Investment Facilitation Cell is intended primarily to provide:
o: Handholding, approval tracking and resolution of delays
Land acquisition through compulsory purchase alone
125.x: The Investment Facilitation Cell provides investor handholding, tracks approvals and helps resolve delays.
125.tq: Match the facilitation cell with its investor-support functions.

125.s: Which additional arrangement is associated with the Investment Facilitation Cell for foreign investors?
o: A compulsory public-sector joint venture desk
125.x: Country-specific desks are provided to support foreign investors.
125.tq: Identify the specialised support mechanism from among unrelated institutional functions.

125.s: The Tourism Policy 2024–29 established its own Investor Facilitation Cell at:
125.x: The Tourism Policy 2024–29 established its own Investor Facilitation Cell at Vijayawada.
125.tq: Test the location of a sector-specific facilitation institution.

125.s: Under the tourism incentive framework stated for March 2026, eligible projects may receive which combination of benefits?
o: 5–10 per cent FCI subsidy up to ₹40 crore and 100 per cent stamp duty benefit
A uniform 15 per cent FCI subsidy without any ceiling and 75 per cent stamp duty benefit
10–20 per cent turnover subsidy up to ₹20 crore and 50 per cent stamp duty benefit
1 per cent export-turnover subsidy for three years and no stamp duty benefit
125.x: The stated tourism incentive is a 5–10 per cent FCI subsidy capped at ₹40 crore, together with 100 per cent stamp duty benefit.
125.tq: Combine the rate range, monetary ceiling and accompanying concession.

125.s:
Which of the following States are cited for digitised, single-window clearances under BRAP in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
1. Andhra Pradesh
2. Kerala
3. Tamil Nadu
4. Odisha
Select the correct answer using the code below.
125.x: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are cited for digitised, single-window clearances. Odisha is not included in the stated group.
125.tq: Identify the exact membership of a named group and reject the nearby added State.

125.s:
BRAP 2024 covered which of the following areas?
1. Digital registration
2. Labour compliance
3. Construction permits
Select the correct answer using the code below.
125.x: BRAP 2024 covered digital registration, labour compliance and construction permits.
125.tq: When all listed policy components are supported, select the complete combination.

125.s: Preparation for which BRAP edition had begun as indicated in the India Year Book 2026?
125.x: Preparation for BRAP 2026 had begun.
125.tq: Distinguish the edition under preparation from the edition already implemented.

125.s:
Consider the following statements regarding national investment facilitation systems:
1. The FIF portal has been integrated with the National Single Window System since August 2022.
2. The new FDI SOP issued in May 2026 increased the approval period from 10 weeks to 12 weeks.
3. Presumed consent under the new FDI SOP arises after eight weeks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements are correct: FIF integration began in August 2022, the period became 12 weeks from 10 weeks, and presumed consent applies after eight weeks.
125.tq: Check dates and altered time limits separately before choosing the coded combination.

125.s: Which institution, together with the Industries Department, conducts investor outreach in Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: APEDB and the Industries Department conduct investor outreach under the stated CDI arrangement.
125.tq: Match the investor-facilitation function with the responsible institution.

125.s: Which organisation coordinates Single Desk clearances in Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: APIIC coordinates Single Desk clearances in Andhra Pradesh.
125.tq: Use the institutional-ownership trap by distinguishing APIIC from APEDB and financial bodies.

125.s: Large projects in Andhra Pradesh are tracked through which facility?
125.x: Large projects are tracked on the Investment Tracker.
125.tq: Identify the exact official name of the tracking mechanism.

125.s: Under IDP 4.0, which description correctly states the SGST reimbursement available to eligible industrial units?
o: 100% of customs duty for five years on imported machinery
100% of net SGST for five years from commercial production on final products made, sold and registered in Andhra Pradesh
50% of gross SGST for three years on all inputs purchased in India
25% of net SGST for ten years from the date of land allotment
125.x: IDP 4.0 provides 100% reimbursement of net SGST for five years from commercial production on final products made, sold and registered in Andhra Pradesh.
125.tq: Read the complete incentive condition, including base, duration, starting point and eligible products.

125.s:
Consider the following statements regarding stamp and transfer duty under IDP 4.0:
1. Reimbursement covers land purchase, lease of land, sheds or buildings.
2. Mortgages and hypothecations are covered.
3. The duty is paid once only on a given plot of land.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements are correct. The reimbursement covers the listed transactions and is paid only once for a given plot.
125.tq: Test coverage and the one-time limitation separately within the same incentive.

125.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 2020-23, SGST reimbursement for medium, large and mega units was linked to which condition?
125.x: For medium, large and mega units, SGST reimbursement was tied to employment creation for five years.
125.tq: Link the incentive to its qualifying performance condition rather than its duration.

125.s: What percentage of plots in APIIC parks was reserved for SC entrepreneurs under IDP 2020-23?
125.x: IDP 2020-23 reserved 16.2% of plots in APIIC parks for SC entrepreneurs.
125.tq: Use the exact percentage and reject rounded figures.

125.s: Under IDP 4.0, what proportion of the land-conversion fee is reimbursed?
125.x: IDP 4.0 provides 100% reimbursement of the land-conversion fee.
125.tq: Distinguish the current policy figure from the older concessional figure.

125.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the APIIC parks land-cost concession?
o: A 25% rebate up to ₹20 lakh per enterprise
A 50% rebate without any monetary ceiling
A 10% rebate up to ₹10 lakh per enterprise
A 20% rebate up to ₹15 lakh per enterprise
125.x: APIIC parks provide a 25% rebate on land cost, subject to a ceiling of ₹20 lakh per enterprise.
125.tq: Combine the percentage rebate with its monetary ceiling.

125.s: Under the power incentive described for Andhra Pradesh industrial units, fixed power cost is reimbursed at what rate and for what period?
o: ₹3 per unit for five years from registration
₹0.50 per unit for one year from allotment
₹1 per unit for two years from DCP
₹2 per unit for three years from commercial production
125.x: Fixed power cost is reimbursed at ₹1 per unit for two years from the date of commencement of production (DCP).
125.tq: Pair the unit rate with the exact starting point and duration.

125.s: Pavala vaddi enables a unit to pay interest effectively at which rate per ₹100 per month?
125.x: Under pavala vaddi, the State reimburses interest above 3% a year, so the unit effectively pays a quarter rupee, or 25 paise, per ₹100 per month.
125.tq: Convert the named fraction into its numerical amount.

125.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the interest-related support available under the stated schemes?
1. APSEZ units receive a 3% interest subsidy on term loans.
2. MSME Policy 4.0 offers collateral-free loans.
3. MSME Policy 4.0 provides interest subventions.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
125.x: APSEZ units receive a 3% subsidy on term loans, while MSME Policy 4.0 offers collateral-free loans and interest subventions.
125.tq: Separate the beneficiary-specific incentive from the broader MSME policy measures.

125.s: What mechanism was added in IDP 4.0 to ensure timely payment of promised subsidies?
125.x: IDP 4.0 introduced an Escrow Guarantee mechanism for timely payment of promised subsidies.
125.tq: Identify the exact institutional mechanism rather than a similarly named financial facility.

125.s: In July 2022, APIIC signed a memorandum of understanding with which institution to provide loans to MSMEs in 39 industrial parks?
125.x: APIIC signed the July 2022 MoU with Union Bank of India for loans to MSMEs in 39 industrial parks.
125.tq: Match the date, partner institution and beneficiary coverage in one combination.

125.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cooperative credit chain that reaches rural MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: The stated cooperative credit chain consists of 2,042 PACS, 13 DCCBs and APCOB, and it also reaches rural MSMEs.
125.tq: Check both the numerical composition and the apex institution.

125.s: Under the MSE-CDP of the Government of India, which organisation serves as the State Implementing Agency in Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: APIIC is the State Implementing Agency for the MSE Cluster Development Programme in Andhra Pradesh.
125.tq: Use the implementation-agency trap among closely related industrial institutions.

125.s:
Consider the following statements regarding MSE-CDP projects in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Twenty-nine projects were approved.
2. Eleven projects were completed.
3. Eighteen projects were at advanced stages.
4. Twenty-eight new proposals and three new industrial parks were included.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: The programme had 29 approved projects, of which 11 were completed and 18 were at advanced stages; it also recorded 28 new proposals and three new industrial parks.
125.tq: Retain the complete numerical profile instead of selecting only the headline total.

125.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cluster Development Programme (AP CDP) was notified through which Government Order and on what date?
125.x: AP CDP was notified through G.O. Ms. No. 17 dated 10 January 2026.
125.tq: Combine the order number with the exact date to avoid near-match distractors.

125.s: Which of the following correctly describes the approved AP Cluster Development Programme for 2026-30?
o: Outlay of ₹250 crore, 50 clusters and funding up to 75% of project cost
Outlay of ₹100 crore, 25 clusters and funding up to 50% of project cost
Outlay of ₹200 crore, 45 clusters with Common Facility Centres and funding up to 80% of project cost
Outlay of ₹200 crore, 30 clusters without Common Facility Centres and full funding of project cost
125.x: The AP CDP has an outlay of ₹200 crore, covers 45 clusters with Common Facility Centres and can fund up to 80% of project cost.
125.tq: Compare the programme's outlay, cluster count, facility component and funding ceiling together.

125.s: The revised AP CDP projections for 2026-30 indicate benefits for how many units and creation of how many jobs?
125.x: The revised projections are 1,688 units benefiting and 7,032 jobs being created. The earlier January 2026 announcement had mentioned 1,840 units and 7,500 jobs.
125.tq: Discriminate between revised figures and the earlier announcement.

125.s: The AP Cluster Development Programme is to operate across which three regions?
125.x: The three regions are Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati.
125.tq: Use the exact regional grouping rather than substituting other major Andhra Pradesh cities.

125.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Craft cluster)
 a. Etikoppaka lacquer toys
 b. Kondapalli toys
 c. Mangalagiri handloom

List-II (District)
 i. Guntur
 ii. NTR
 iii. Anakapalli

Select the correct answer using the code below.
125.x: Etikoppaka lacquer toys are associated with Anakapalli, Kondapalli toys with NTR, and Mangalagiri handloom with Guntur.
125.tq: Start with the sure craft-district pair and eliminate codes that break the remaining one-to-one matches.

125.s: Etikoppaka lacquer toys are particularly associated with which combination?
o: Kondapalli toys, teak wood and synthetic colours
Mangalagiri handloom, cotton yarn and block printing
GI status, bamboo wood and chemical dyes
GI status, Ankudu wood and natural dyes
125.x: Etikoppaka lacquer toys have GI status and are made using Ankudu wood and natural dyes.
125.tq: Test the distinctive material and GI descriptors of a craft cluster.

125.s: APMSMEDC, headquartered at Mangalagiri, implements which programme?
125.x: APMSMEDC, whose office is at Mangalagiri, implements the RAMP programme.
125.tq: Match the institution and location with its specific programme responsibility.

125.s:
Consider the following statements regarding RAMP:
1. It is a World Bank-backed central sector scheme.
2. It was launched in 2022.
3. Its stated period is 2022-23 to 2026-27.
4. States prepare Strategic Investment Plans under it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: RAMP is a World Bank-backed central sector scheme launched in 2022 for 2022-23 to 2026-27, with State Strategic Investment Plans.
125.tq: Verify the funding partner, launch year, duration and state-level planning feature independently.

125.s: Which organisation conducted a review of RAMP in April 2026?
125.x: A World Bank team reviewed RAMP in April 2026.
125.tq: Apply the organisation-scheme association without replacing the stated international partner.

125.s: The RAMP buyer-seller meet held from 19 to 21 August 2026 was run by APMSMEDC in association with which organisation?
125.x: APMSMEDC conducted the buyer-seller meet in association with FIEO.
125.tq: Match the event organiser with its collaborating organisation.

125.s: Which set of figures correctly describes the RAMP buyer-seller meet of August 2026?
o: 40+ buyers from 20 countries, 200 MSMEs and 88 MoUs
25+ buyers from 40 countries, 188 MSMEs and 80 MoUs
40+ buyers from 25 countries, 250+ MSMEs and 88 MoUs
50+ buyers from 25 countries, 250+ MSMEs and 68 MoUs
125.x: The event brought together more than 40 buyers from 25 countries, over 250 MSMEs and resulted in 88 MoUs.
125.tq: Retain the three-part event profile and reject options with one altered figure.

125.s: The NSIC Venture Capital Fund implements the SRI Fund, whose total size and GoI contribution are respectively:
125.x: The SRI Fund is ₹50,000 crore, consisting of ₹10,000 crore from the Government of India and ₹40,000 crore leveraged.
125.tq: Distinguish the total fund size from the government contribution and leveraged amount.

125.s: Which institution implements the MSMED Act at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: District Industries Centres implement the MSMED Act at the district level.
125.tq: Identify the level-specific implementing authority.

125.s: Which of the following is identified as a major credit-related problem faced by MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Compulsory foreign ownership of all MSMEs
Credit and collateral gaps, particularly for women entrepreneurs
Abolition of institutional lending to MSMEs
125.x: Credit and collateral gaps, especially among women entrepreneurs, are identified as a major problem faced by MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh.
125.tq: Identify the precise problem rather than being distracted by unrelated policy measures.

125.s:
With reference to delayed payments to MSMEs, consider the following statements:
1. MSME Samadhaan is associated with delayed-payment grievances.
2. The payment rule referred to for MSMEs prescribes a period of 45 days.
3. Delayed payment of incentives is unrelated to the MSME problem in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: MSME Samadhaan and the 45-day payment rule are associated with delayed payments. Delayed incentive payments are also a recognised MSME grievance, so statement 3 is false.
125.tq: Find the statement that reverses the documented grievance and eliminate it.

125.s: The escrow guarantee introduced under Industrial Development Policy 4.0 primarily seeks to address which issue concerning MSMEs?
125.x: The escrow guarantee mechanism under IDP 4.0 addresses the long-standing problem of arrears and delays in payment of industrial incentives to MSMEs.
125.tq: Match the institutional mechanism with the specific problem it is designed to solve.

125.s: ReSTART, launched by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in May 2020, was primarily intended as:
o: A COVID-19 relief package for MSMEs
A policy for foreign direct investment in defence
A programme for constructing industrial corridors
125.x: ReSTART was Andhra Pradesh’s COVID-19 relief package for MSMEs, launched in May 2020.
125.tq: Use the launch date and sector-purpose combination to distinguish the scheme from other industrial initiatives.

125.s: The approximate financial size of the ReSTART package for Andhra Pradesh MSMEs was:
125.x: The ReSTART package for MSMEs was valued at approximately ₹1,110 crore.
125.tq: Separate the scheme-specific amount from larger investment and project figures.

125.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal use of the ReSTART package?
o: Clearing pending incentive arrears of MSMEs
Providing only export subsidies to large enterprises
Financing only new steel plants in Rayalaseema
125.x: The ReSTART package mainly cleared pending incentive arrears and provided COVID-19 relief to MSMEs.
125.tq: Distinguish the principal objective of a scheme from unrelated sectoral initiatives.

125.s: Under the incentive provisions referred to for Andhra Pradesh, an additional capital subsidy of 5 per cent is available to entrepreneurs belonging to which groups?
o: Only large and mega industrial units
Only foreign investors and export houses
Women, SC, ST, BC and specially-abled entrepreneurs
125.x: A 5 per cent additional capital subsidy is available for women, SC, ST, BC and specially-abled entrepreneurs.
125.tq: Recall the complete beneficiary group instead of selecting a partial category.

125.s:
Consider the following statements regarding women, SC/ST, BC and specially-abled entrepreneurs in Andhra Pradesh:
1. They receive preferential access under the MSME policy.
2. They are eligible for an additional 5 per cent capital subsidy.
3. The additional capital subsidy is restricted exclusively to women entrepreneurs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: The MSME policy provides preferential access to these groups, and the additional subsidy is 5 per cent. It is not restricted exclusively to women entrepreneurs.
125.tq: Reject the exclusive-word trap in a statement that narrows a wider beneficiary group.

125.s: According to the cited national figure, women own what percentage of MSMEs?
125.x: Women own 20.37 per cent of MSMEs according to the cited national figure.
125.tq: Treat a percentage as a distinct factual value and distinguish it from rounded alternatives.

125.s: Which of the following combination correctly identifies the schemes mentioned as supporting women entrepreneurs nationally?
o: VCIC loan and RAMP export meet
125.x: Stand Up India and MUDRA (Tarun) are the schemes mentioned as supporting women entrepreneurs.
125.tq: Start with the sure pair linking the beneficiary group to the relevant schemes.

125.s: Andhra Pradesh has identified how many products under the One District One Product initiative?
125.x: Andhra Pradesh has identified 99 products under the One District One Product initiative.
125.tq: Distinguish the ODOP count from other figures relating to CFCs, proposals and units.

125.s: The One District One Product initiative is implemented by:
o: DPIIT in association with the States
The Reserve Bank of India independently of the States
The ADB through the VCIC loan only
125.x: ODOP is run by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) with the States.
125.tq: Apply the ‘who runs the programme?’ test to distinguish the implementing body.

125.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Product)
a. Udayagiri wooden cutlery
b. Paturu cotton silk sarees
c. Etikoppaka toys
d. Payakaraopeta silk sarees

List-II (District)
i. Anakapalli
ii. Nellore

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
125.x: Udayagiri wooden cutlery and Paturu cotton silk sarees are associated with Nellore, while Etikoppaka toys and Payakaraopeta silk sarees are associated with Anakapalli.
125.tq: Start from the repeated district pair and verify the remaining product associations.

125.s: The Chief Minister directed that all approved projects should:
o: Break ground by September 2026 and start operations by December 2028
Break ground by December 2028 and start operations by September 2026
Be completed by September 2025 and exported by December 2026
Receive approval by December 2026 and begin construction by 2030
125.x: The direction was that all approved projects should break ground by September 2026 and commence operations by December 2028.
125.tq: Keep the two deadlines in their correct sequence and do not reverse them.

125.s: During FY 2024-25, the SIPB approved projects in Andhra Pradesh involving investments of approximately:
125.x: SIPB approved projects involving approximately ₹2,45,275 crore in FY 2024-25.
125.tq: Separate the annual approved-investment figure from the cumulative investment figure for operational units.

125.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported position of large and mega industrial units in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 1,119 units operational, involving ₹2,45,275 crore and 50-acre land allotments
87 units operational, involving ₹34,000 crore and 45,000 jobs
99 units operational, involving ₹1,110 crore and 20.37 lakh jobs
1,119 units operational, involving ₹3.15 lakh crore and 5.85 lakh jobs
125.x: The reported position was 1,119 operational large and mega units, involving ₹3.15 lakh crore and generating 5.85 lakh jobs.
125.tq: Keep related counts, investment and employment figures together instead of mixing figures from separate reports.

125.s: The FDI drive mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh was aimed at strategic sectors ahead of the:
125.x: The FDI drive was linked to strategic sectors ahead of the Visakhapatnam CII Partnership Summit.
125.tq: Link the investment initiative with its stated event rather than with another industrial programme.

125.s: Rayalaseema is being developed as a hub for which combination of sectors?
o: Maritime administration, education, health and mining
125.x: Rayalaseema is being developed into an automobile, steel, defence and space hub.
125.tq: Recall the complete sectoral combination and avoid replacing one sector with a neighbouring economic activity.

125.s: Which statement best reflects the criticism concerning Andhra Pradesh’s industrial performance?
o: Manufacturing growth remains subdued despite strong investment momentum
Investment momentum has completely stopped despite rapid manufacturing growth
Manufacturing has expanded only because all projects are in Rayalaseema
Industrial growth has been unaffected by delays in incentive payments
125.x: The criticism is that manufacturing growth remains subdued even though investment momentum is strong.
125.tq: Identify the carefully worded criticism rather than choosing an extreme reversal.

125.s: The Cabinet ratified 87 SIPB proposals worth approximately ₹34,000 crore primarily with the objective of promoting:
o: Environmental clearances for all central projects
125.x: The 87 proposals, valued at approximately ₹34,000 crore, were aimed at promoting development in backward regions.
125.tq: Match the proposal package with its stated regional-development objective.

125.s: Which feature is specifically associated with the revamped Andhra Pradesh MSME Policy 2026?
o: Replacement of MSMEs by industrial nodes
Restriction of benefits to mega industries
Withdrawal of support from women-led units
125.x: The revamped MSME Policy 2026 is described as favouring women-led units.
125.tq: Use the policy’s beneficiary focus to distinguish it from broad industrial policies.

125.s: The ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ strategy is associated with which State?
125.x: Karnataka’s ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ strategy seeks to build district-specific industrial nodes.
125.tq: Test the State-policy association directly, a common location trap.

125.s: District-specific industrial nodes are a feature of Karnataka’s:
125.x: The ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ strategy builds district-specific industrial nodes.
125.tq: Distinguish a comparative State strategy from Andhra Pradesh’s own MSME and approval initiatives.

125.s: Time-bound and faceless approvals are considered significant in a single-window system mainly because they:
o: Transfer all approvals to foreign agencies
Eliminate the need for all industrial investment
Restrict applications to large and mega units
125.x: Time-bound, faceless approvals reduce discretionary interaction and are therefore regarded as an anti-corruption measure in a single-window system.
125.tq: Infer the governance significance of a procedural reform from its operational features.

125.s: The ADB’s policy-based loan connected with Andhra Pradesh supports:
o: The ODOP product list without State participation
Ease of Doing Business reforms under VCIC
125.x: The ADB’s VCIC policy-based loan supports Ease of Doing Business reforms.
125.tq: Match the lending institution and corridor initiative with the reform objective.

125.s: The APIIC initiative mentioned in the current industrial context involves direct allotment of:
125.x: The APIIC initiative provides for 50-acre direct allotment.
125.tq: Distinguish the land-allotment figure from counts of proposals, products and CFCs.

125.s: What is the significance of the CGD deemed-approval Government Order mentioned in the industrial context?
o: It provides deemed approval in the city gas distribution context
It abolishes all approvals for mega projects
It introduces deemed approval for ODOP products only
It transfers environmental clearances to the ADB
125.x: The cited G.O. concerns deemed approval in the city gas distribution (CGD) context.
125.tq: Read the sector abbreviation and connect the approval reform to its relevant field.

125.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: VCIC policy-based loan — Ease of Doing Business reforms
125.x: PARIVESH 3.0 is associated with environmental clearances, whereas E-Samudra is associated with maritime administration.
125.tq: Find the swapped function between two sector-specific single-window systems.

125.s: The Andhra Pradesh Comprehensive Development Plan mentioned in the current context includes how many Common Facility Centres (CFCs)?
125.x: The Andhra Pradesh Comprehensive Development Plan includes 45 Common Facility Centres.
125.tq: Separate the CFC count from the ODOP product count and SIPB proposal count.

125.s: The RAMP export meet mentioned in the industrial context is most directly associated with:
o: Construction of defence and space hubs only
125.x: The RAMP export meet is connected with MSME-related export support and activity.
125.tq: Use the programme’s export orientation to identify its likely sectoral purpose.

125.s: What is the flagship MSME goal of Andhra Pradesh described as ‘One Family, One Entrepreneur by 2030’?
o: To create one mega industry in every district by 2030
To provide one government job to every family by 2030
To encourage at least one entrepreneur in every family by 2030
To establish one export port in every district by 2030
125.x: ‘One Family, One Entrepreneur by 2030’ is Andhra Pradesh’s flagship MSME goal of promoting entrepreneurship at the family level.
125.tq: Translate the policy slogan into its precise programme objective without extending it to unrelated sectors.

126.s: Under Dr NTR Vaidya Seva, which of the following correctly describes the income eligibility and annual coverage?
o: Only BPL families, with coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year
All families irrespective of income, with coverage of ₹25 lakh per family per year
Families with income up to ₹2 lakh and coverage of ₹10 lakh per family
BPL families and families with income up to ₹5 lakh, with coverage of ₹25 lakh per family per year
126.x: Dr NTR Vaidya Seva covers BPL families and families with annual income up to ₹5 lakh, providing cover of ₹25 lakh per family per year.
126.tq: Split the options by checking both the income ceiling and the coverage amount.

126.s:
With reference to Dr NTR Vaidya Seva, consider the following statements:
1. There is no limit on the annual cover for cancer treatment.
2. The scheme covers 3,257 procedures.
3. It benefited 1.43 crore families according to APSES 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements are correct: cancer treatment has no cover limit, 3,257 procedures are covered, and 1.43 crore families benefited according to APSES 2024-25.
126.tq: Use the numerical cluster and verify each statement independently.

126.s: During June–December 2025, Dr NTR Vaidya Seva recorded which of the following figures?
o: 1.43 crore patients treated and ₹2,723 crore in claims
11.36 lakh patients treated and ₹2,723 crore in claims
9.22 lakh patients treated and ₹4,000 crore in claims
11.36 lakh patients treated and ₹9,668 crore in claims
126.x: During June–December 2025, 11.36 lakh patients were treated and claims amounted to ₹2,723 crore.
126.tq: Match the period with its treatment and claims figures.

126.s: In March 2026, which addition was made to Dr NTR Vaidya Seva?
126.x: Five cardiac procedures were added to Dr NTR Vaidya Seva in March 2026.
126.tq: Test the specific service addition rather than the broader scheme coverage.

126.s: The Universal Health Policy announced in 2026 provides free treatment up to which amount per citizen through insurers?
126.x: The Universal Health Policy provides free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh per citizen through insurers.
126.tq: Separate the individual limit under the Universal Health Policy from the higher Vaidya Seva limit.

126.s: Under the Universal Health Policy, which institution covers poor persons beyond the insurer-provided limit?
o: The Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust
126.x: The Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust covers poor persons beyond ₹2.5 lakh, up to ₹25 lakh.
126.tq: Use the ‘who covers the excess’ approach to distinguish institutions.

126.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the rural and urban Primary Health Centre network in Andhra Pradesh according to SES 2025-26?
126.x: The network comprised 1,293 rural PHCs and 559 urban PHCs.
126.tq: Check the rural–urban labels instead of merely recognising the numbers.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the health facility network in Andhra Pradesh:
1. There were 10,032 Village Health Clinics.
2. There were 11,086 sub-centres.
3. There were 173 Community Health Centres and 54 area hospitals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements correctly state the reported numbers of Village Health Clinics, sub-centres, CHCs and area hospitals.
126.tq: Group the facility figures and verify each category separately.

126.s: The Family Physician concept in Andhra Pradesh envisages that PHC doctors should:
o: Manage only private hospitals in villages
Visit village health clinics on fixed days
126.x: Under the Family Physician concept, PHC doctors visit village health clinics on fixed days.
126.tq: Identify the operational meaning of the service concept.

126.s:
Which of the following statements regarding emergency and mobile health services in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. The State had 768 ambulances under the 108 service.
2. These ambulances carried 9.22 lakh patients in 2024-25.
3. The State also had 104 Mobile Medical Units.
126.x: The 108 service had 768 ambulances, carried 9.22 lakh patients in 2024-25, and operated alongside 104 Mobile Medical Units.
126.tq: Combine service count, outcome count and facility count without swapping them.

126.s: Under Citizen Health Screening, the 104 Mobile Medical Units now conduct how many tests a year?
126.x: The 104 Mobile Medical Units conduct 47 tests a year under Citizen Health Screening.
126.tq: Distinguish the number of tests from the service number and facility counts.

126.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Dr YSR Kanti Velugu — Eye health
2. Nadu-Nedu — School education
3. YSR Nethanna Nestham — Handloom weavers
126.x: Dr YSR Kanti Velugu concerns eye health, Nadu-Nedu concerns school education, and YSR Nethanna Nestham benefits handloom weavers.
126.tq: Start from the sure pair and test whether the remaining pairings also belong to the same scheme list.

126.s: Telemedicine in Andhra Pradesh is associated with which of the following facilities?
126.x: Telemedicine is associated with Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres, or AB-HWCs.
126.tq: Identify the facility-based application rather than the implementing scheme’s general objective.

126.s: Talliki Vandanam, earlier known as Amma Vodi, provides which benefit?
o: ₹15,000 per student as a one-time scholarship
₹10,090 per child per year to the school
₹15,000 per child per year to the mother
126.x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per child per year to the mother of a child studying in a government or private school.
126.tq: Distinguish the beneficiary, periodicity and amount of the education benefit.

126.s: Talliki Vandanam was allocated ₹10,090 crore for how many students according to the reported January 2026 information?
126.x: An allocation of ₹10,090 crore was reported for 67.27 lakh students under Talliki Vandanam.
126.tq: Match the scheme allocation with its beneficiary count, not with figures from other education schemes.

126.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Mana Badi Mana Bhavishyathu (Nadu-Nedu)?
126.x: Mana Badi Mana Bhavishyathu, also called Nadu-Nedu, focuses on school infrastructure.
126.tq: Use objective-based discrimination among similarly named education schemes.

126.s:
Which of the following statements about Nadu-Nedu is correct?
1. ₹1,500 crore was provided for 2026-27.
2. Nadu-Nedu works worth ₹7,876 crore were left incomplete.
126.x: Both statements are correct: the 2026-27 provision was ₹1,500 crore and incomplete works were valued at ₹7,876 crore.
126.tq: Check whether the budget figure and implementation-status figure refer to the same scheme.

126.s:
Dokka Seethamma Madhyahna Bhojanam, formerly Jagananna Gorumudda, is characterised by which of the following?
1. It was extended to Intermediate students.
2. It covered 27.97 lakh students.
3. It provides five eggs and three chikkis a week.
126.x: The programme was extended to Intermediate, covered 27.97 lakh students, and provided five eggs and three chikkis per week.
126.tq: Test the programme’s extension, beneficiary number and nutrition entitlement together.

126.s: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan Vidyarthi Mitra, formerly Jagananna Vidya Kanuka, provides free:
o: Kits consisting of textbooks, uniforms, shoes and bags
Meals consisting of eggs and chikkis
126.x: The scheme provides free kits containing textbooks, uniforms, shoes and bags.
126.tq: Recognise the contents of the kit and distinguish them from meal and literacy programmes.

126.s: The objective of Akshara Andhra, implemented through the Adult Education Department, is:
126.x: Akshara Andhra aims at 100% literacy.
126.tq: Match the programme with its stated objective rather than its department alone.

126.s: How many adults passed the FLNAT 2026 test under Akshara Andhra?
126.x: A total of 24.7 lakh adults passed the FLNAT 2026 test under Akshara Andhra.
126.tq: Carefully retain the decimal placement in the lakh figure.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Samagra Shiksha in Andhra Pradesh:
1. There are 352 KGBVs.
2. Seats in KGBVs are allocated 75% to SC, ST, OBC and minority students and 25% to BPL students.
3. There are 679 Bhavitha centres for children with special needs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements are correct. Samagra Shiksha includes 352 KGBVs, the stated 75:25 seat distribution, and 679 Bhavitha centres.
126.tq: Check both composition percentages and facility counts before selecting the coded option.

126.s: Which programme provides one full meal to pregnant and lactating women at Anganwadis?
o: Poshana Plus exclusively for tribal children
126.x: Anna Amrutha Hastam provides one full meal to pregnant and lactating women at Anganwadis.
126.tq: Identify the target group and service together.

126.s: YSR Sampoorna Poshana and Poshana Plus target which group?
o: Only school-going children aged 6 to 14 years
Only adolescent girls in urban areas
Only elderly persons below the poverty line
Pregnant and lactating women and children aged 6 months to 6 years, with Plus operating in tribal areas
126.x: The programmes cover pregnant and lactating women and children aged 6 months to 6 years; the Plus version operates in tribal areas.
126.tq: Use the age band and the tribal-area distinction to eliminate partial matches.

126.s: Balasanjeevani SNP currently covers approximately:
o: 4.15 lakh adolescent girls and 19.13 lakh school children
19.13 lakh pregnant/lactating women and 4.15 lakh children under six
4.15 lakh pregnant/lactating women and 19.13 lakh children under six
1.31 crore women and 4.15 lakh children under six
126.x: Balasanjeevani SNP covers 4.15 lakh pregnant and lactating women and 19.13 lakh children under six.
126.tq: Do not reverse the two beneficiary categories while reading paired figures.

126.s: Anna Canteens are primarily intended for the:
126.x: Anna Canteens target the urban poor.
126.tq: Identify the programme by its principal target group.

126.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Anna Canteen network?
126.x: There were 204 Anna Canteens in 123 Urban Local Bodies.
126.tq: Keep the facility count and the local-body count in their proper order.

126.s:
Which of the following statements about ICDS in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. It has 55,746 Anganwadi Centres.
2. It has 257 ICDS projects.
3. Supplementary nutrition covers 98.54% of women and 95.62% of children.
126.x: All three statements are correct according to the reported ICDS figures.
126.tq: Check the institutional counts together with the two coverage percentages.

126.s:
The adolescent girls scheme in Andhra Pradesh operates in which districts?
1. Alluri Sitharama Raju
2. Parvathipuram Manyam
3. YSR Kadapa
126.x: The adolescent girls scheme operates in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa districts.
126.tq: Use the complete district list and avoid treating the tribal-area reference as a substitute for a district name.

126.s: According to SRS 2021-23, which indicator shows the following Andhra Pradesh and India values respectively: 30 and 88?
126.x: The maternal mortality ratio was 30 in Andhra Pradesh and 88 for India.
126.tq: Match the paired state–national values to the correct indicator.

126.s:
Arrange the following SRS 2021-23 indicators of Andhra Pradesh in descending order of their reported numerical values:
A. MMR
B. IMR
C. U5MR
D. TFR
126.x: The values are MMR 30, U5MR 21, IMR 19 and TFR 1.5; hence the descending order is A, C, B, D.
126.tq: Arrange by numerical magnitude, not by the order in which the indicators are commonly named.

126.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched for SRS 2021-23?
1. AP IMR — 19
2. India IMR — 25
3. AP U5MR — 21
4. India U5MR — 29
126.x: All four pairings are correct: AP and India recorded IMRs of 19 and 25, and U5MRs of 21 and 29 respectively.
126.tq: Verify each state–India pairing rather than relying on the indicator name alone.

126.s: According to SRS 2021-23, the total fertility rate was:
126.x: The total fertility rate was 1.5 in Andhra Pradesh and 1.9 in India.
126.tq: Watch for the reversed state–national comparison.

126.s: Which statement regarding life expectancy according to SRS 2021-23 is correct?
o: Female life expectancy was 68.5 years in AP and 72.5 years in India.
Male life expectancy was 73.3 years in both AP and India.
Female life expectancy was 72.5 years in AP and 73.3 years in India; male life expectancy was 68.5 years only in AP.
Female life expectancy was 73.3 years in AP and 72.5 years in India; male life expectancy was 68.5 years in both.
126.x: Female life expectancy was 73.3 years in AP and 72.5 years in India, while male life expectancy was 68.5 years in both.
126.tq: Separate sex-wise values before comparing AP with India.

126.s: The earlier reported values for Andhra Pradesh were which of the following?
126.x: The earlier reported values were an MMR of 45 and an IMR of 24.
126.tq: Distinguish earlier values from the latest SRS 2021-23 values.

126.s: What percentage of adolescent girls in Andhra Pradesh were anaemic according to NFHS-5?
126.x: NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 60.1% of adolescent girls in Andhra Pradesh.
126.tq: Separate the NFHS-5 estimate from the later state-screening percentage.

126.s: The state screening conducted in 2023-24 recorded anaemia among what percentage of adolescent girls in Andhra Pradesh?
126.x: The 2023-24 state screening recorded anaemia among 50.42% of adolescent girls.
126.tq: Compare the similarly worded NFHS-5 and state-screening percentages by year.

126.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change in child stunting reported by WDCW?
126.x: Child stunting declined from 21.21% to 11.15%.
126.tq: Read the direction of change as well as the two percentages.

126.s: Which of the following correctly states the WDCW-reported changes in underweight and wasting among children?
126.x: Underweight declined from 9.35% to 5.90%, while wasting declined from 5.21% to 3.98%.
126.tq: Avoid swapping the two nutrition indicators and preserve their respective before–after values.

126.s: NFHS-6 for 2023-24 was released on 1 June 2026 by which institution and was based on how many households?
126.x: NFHS-6 was released by IIPS Mumbai on 1 June 2026 and covered 6.79 lakh households.
126.tq: Link the release date with the issuing institution and survey size.

126.s: Sanjeevani, which became statewide from August 2026 after being piloted in Chittoor and Kuppam, provides every citizen with:
o: A ration card and Aadhaar number
A school identity card and FLNAT certificate
A health insurance card limited to ₹2.5 lakh
A digital health profile and ABHA ID
126.x: Sanjeevani provides every citizen with a digital health profile and an ABHA ID.
126.tq: Distinguish digital identity and health-record functions from insurance and welfare benefits.

126.s:
Which of the following facilities and services are linked through the Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App?
1. PHCs
2. Laboratories
3. e-Aushadhi
4. 108, 104 and telemedicine
126.x: The app links PHCs, laboratories, e-Aushadhi, 108, 104 and telemedicine.
126.tq: Treat the list as cumulative and select the option containing every stated linkage.

126.s: Which statement about the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is correct?
o: It was launched in 2021 by the Women Development and Child Welfare Department.
It was launched in 2026 by the Adult Education Department.
It was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
It was launched in 2014 by the Ministry of Rural Development.
126.x: ABDM was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
126.tq: Use the institution–year pairing and reject ministry swaps.

126.s: Universal NCD-CD screening in Andhra Pradesh has covered approximately:
126.x: Universal NCD-CD screening has covered 1.31 crore citizens.
126.tq: Pay attention to the lakh–crore scale in the coverage figure.

126.s: According to Census 2011, what was the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh?
126.x: The Census 2011 literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh was 67.35%. India’s corresponding literacy rate was 72.98%.
126.tq: Distinguish the exact official figure from a closely similar reported value.

126.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the literacy figures cited for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Census 2011 recorded 67.41%, while some compilations cite 67.35%.
Census 2011 recorded 83%, while some compilations cite 73%.
Census 2011 recorded 72.98%, while some compilations cite 67.35%.
Census 2011 recorded 67.35%, while some compilations cite 67.41%.
126.x: The Census 2011 figure given for Andhra Pradesh is 67.35%; some compilations cite 67.41%. The figures of 73% and 83% relate to the Minister’s statement on Akshara Andhra, not the Census 2011 figure.
126.tq: Discriminate between two closely resembling percentages associated with the same indicator.

126.s: The Minister stated that the Akshara Andhra initiative had raised literacy from approximately which level to which level?
126.x: The Minister stated that Akshara Andhra had raised literacy from 73% to 83%.
126.tq: Use the paired before-and-after figures rather than the Census literacy figures.

126.s: A door-to-door survey conducted in Andhra Pradesh from 12 June to 12 July 2025 identified how many out-of-school children, all of whom were reportedly mainstreamed?
126.x: The survey identified 1,60,196 out-of-school children, and all of them were mainstreamed.
126.tq: Read the Indian-style digit grouping carefully when identifying the exact survey figure.

126.s: Which statement best reflects the contrasting figures associated with school dropouts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The survey found 1,60,196 out-of-school children, while the Minister cited nearly one lakh dropouts.
The survey found nearly one lakh out-of-school children, while the Minister cited 1,60,196 dropouts.
The survey found no out-of-school children, while the Minister cited 1,60,196 dropouts.
Both the survey and the Minister cited exactly 1,60,196 dropouts.
126.x: The door-to-door survey found 1,60,196 out-of-school children, whereas the Minister separately cited nearly one lakh dropouts.
126.tq: Separate two similar but non-identical figures reported in different contexts.

126.s: The Andhra Model of Education aims at achieving:
126.x: The Andhra Model of Education aims at 100% enrolment.
126.tq: Identify the precise stated objective instead of substituting a related education goal.

126.s:
With reference to Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Language skills rose from 21% to 47%.
2. Mathematics skills rose from 20% to 50%.
3. Language skills rose from 20% to 50%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the language and mathematics figures.
126.tq: Match each intervention outcome with its correct subject-wise before-and-after figures.

126.s: The LEAP initiative in Andhra Pradesh primarily responds to:
o: Poor learning outcomes reported by ASER
The shortage of higher education institutions reported by the Census
The shortage of trained health workers under the Universal Health Policy
The decline in health expenditure reported by the SDG Index
126.x: LEAP responds to poor learning outcomes reported by ASER.
126.tq: Link the initiative to the problem it is designed to address.

126.s: What was the total expenditure provided in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27?
126.x: The total expenditure in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 was ₹3,32,205 crore.
126.tq: Distinguish the total budget size from the education-sector allocation.

126.s: Which department received the largest allocation in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27, and what was the allocation?
126.x: The School Education Department received ₹32,308 crore and was the largest department in the Budget 2026–27.
126.tq: Start from the sure department–allocation pair and reject swapped department names.

126.s: The allocation for Higher Education in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 was:
126.x: Higher Education received an allocation of ₹2,567 crore in the Budget 2026–27.
126.tq: Separate the higher education allocation from the much larger school education allocation.

126.s: The sector-wise total allocation for Health and Family Welfare in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 was:
126.x: The sector-wise total for Health and Family Welfare was ₹19,630 crore. This differs from the ₹19,306 crore allocation mentioned for the Health Department.
126.tq: Distinguish a department allocation from the broader sector-wise total.

126.s:
With reference to the education sector in the Andhra Pradesh Budget, consider the following statements:
1. The education sector as a whole received ₹35,673 crore.
2. It accounted for 11.7% of total spending.
3. The average share for all States was 14.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements are correct. The education sector received ₹35,673 crore, constituting 11.7% of spending, compared with the 14.5% average for all States.
126.tq: Compare the State’s sectoral share with the benchmark average while retaining the allocation figure.

126.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the expenditure shares mentioned for welfare and debt service in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Welfare 17 paise and debt service 18 paise per rupee
Welfare 18 paise and debt service 17 paise per rupee
Both welfare and debt service 17 paise per rupee
Both welfare and debt service 18 paise per rupee
126.x: Welfare accounted for 17 paise of every rupee, while debt service accounted for 18 paise. They were described as being broadly at the same level.
126.tq: Keep adjacent expenditure-share figures in their correct order.

126.s: In the 2024–25 Budget Estimates, the ten main social and economic heads together accounted for what share of total spending?
126.x: The ten main social and economic heads together accounted for 68% of spending in the 2024–25 Budget Estimates.
126.tq: Identify the aggregate share rather than confusing it with individual department percentages.

126.s: Andhra Pradesh secured which score and band in the SDG India Index 2023–24?
126.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 and was placed in the Front Runner band in the SDG India Index 2023–24.
126.tq: Pair the numerical score with its correct performance band.

126.s: The rollout of the Sanjeevani initiative in Andhra Pradesh was associated with which month and year?
126.x: The Sanjeevani rollout was associated with August 2026.
126.tq: Use the chronology of current initiatives to identify the correct rollout period.

126.s: The Universal Health Policy referred to for Andhra Pradesh provides coverage of:
126.x: The Universal Health Policy provides coverage of ₹2.5 lakh.
126.tq: Distinguish the policy coverage amount from nearby rounded figures.

126.s: The health outlay in Andhra Pradesh was reported to have increased by:
126.x: The health outlay was reported to have increased by 9.5%.
126.tq: Separate a year-on-year outlay increase from budget share percentages.

126.s: Which of the following correctly describes the controversy relating to Vaidya Seva in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹300 crore, and the opposition supported the insurance model.
Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹3,000 crore, and the opposition called the insurance model a dilution of Aarogyasri.
Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹30,000 crore, and the opposition called for replacing Aarogyasri with Vaidya Seva.
Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹3,000 crore, and the opposition described the model as strengthening Aarogyasri.
126.x: Hospitals halted services over ₹3,000 crore of unpaid Vaidya Seva dues. The opposition criticised the insurance model as a dilution of Aarogyasri.
126.tq: Check both the amount of unpaid dues and the direction of the political criticism.

126.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s demographic and health indicators is correct?
o: The TFR of Andhra Pradesh is 2.5, which is above replacement level.
Only the IMR of Andhra Pradesh is better than the national goal.
The TFR of Andhra Pradesh is 1.5, which is well below replacement level.
The MMR, IMR and TFR of Andhra Pradesh are all worse than the national goals.
126.x: Andhra Pradesh’s MMR, IMR and TFR are all better than the national goals. Its TFR is 1.5, well below replacement level.
126.tq: Reject the reversed comparison and focus on the exact fertility figure.

127.s:
Under the three-capital proposal of Andhra Pradesh, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Executive seat — Visakhapatnam
2. Legislative seat — Amaravati
3. Judicial seat — Kurnool
127.x: The proposal assigned Visakhapatnam as the executive seat, Amaravati as the legislative seat and Kurnool as the judicial seat.
127.tq: Start from the sure seat-city pair and eliminate codes with a swapped location.

127.s:
The three-capital proposal of Andhra Pradesh was based primarily on the recommendations or findings of which of the following?
1. G.N. Rao Committee
2. Boston Consulting Group study
3. Sarkaria Commission
127.x: The proposal was based on the G.N. Rao Committee and a Boston Consulting Group study. The Sarkaria Commission was not cited as its basis.
127.tq: Identify the bodies actually associated with the proposal and reject the unrelated constitutional body.

127.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the South African model cited in the context of Andhra Pradesh’s three-capital proposal?
127.x: The model cited assigned administrative functions to Pretoria, legislative functions to Cape Town and judicial functions to Bloemfontein.
127.tq: Discriminate between similar capital-function pairs rather than relying on the city names alone.

127.s: The Andhra Pradesh Government withdrew the three-capital and CRDA-repeal laws in:
127.x: Both the three-capital proposal and the CRDA-repeal laws were withdrawn in November 2021.
127.tq: Use the close-year trap by distinguishing withdrawal in 2021 from the later High Court decision.

127.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the later developments concerning Amaravati:
1. The Andhra Pradesh High Court upheld Amaravati as the capital in March 2022.
2. The Assembly resolved on 28 March 2026 to seek statutory status for Amaravati.
3. The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 made Amaravati the sole and permanent capital with retrospective effect from 2 June 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
127.x: All three statements are correct. The High Court decision was in March 2022, the Assembly resolution was on 28 March 2026, and the 2026 amendment provided for Amaravati’s sole and permanent-capital status retrospectively from 2 June 2024.

127.s: The capital city area of Amaravati comprises approximately:

127.x: The Prime Minister of India laid the foundation stone at Uddandarayunipalem in Guntur on 22 October 2015.

16,666 returnable plots were allotted in seven villages
37,921 returnable plots were allotted from 70,550 acres
70,550 acres were pooled and 37,921 plots were allotted

127.s:
Consider the following statements about rehabilitation and support under the Amaravati land-pooling process:

127.x: Farmers received ₹2,038.61 crore in annuity and 17,601 landless labourers received pensions. Statement 3 reverses the beneficiaries.

A desert-based industrial city on the Godavari
A coastal port city on the Bay of Bengal
A water-centric city on the Krishna

127.tq: Translate the planning concept into its geographical setting and reject reversed river-location options.

127.s:
Which of the following lender-amount pairs relating to Amaravati is correctly matched?

3. NaBFID — ₹7,500 crore

127.tq: Start with a sure lender-amount pair and check that no amount has been shifted to another institution.

127.s: The World Bank and ADB assistance for Phase I of Amaravati was described as:
127.x: The World Bank and ADB were associated with ₹15,000 crore of concessional assistance for Phase I.
127.tq: Distinguish the amount and character of finance from the facilities associated with other lenders.

127.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Amaravati works:
1. Ninety-six works worth ₹57,592.71 crore were sanctioned.

127.x: All three statements correctly state the sanctioned works, physical progress and Undavalli trunk-infrastructure sanction.
127.tq: Check the figures and dates independently instead of treating the large project amount as the only tested detail.

127.s: In Swachh Survekshan 2022, Visakhapatnam received the designation of:
o: Cleanest City in the small-town category
Top Impact Creator in the million-plus category
Safaimitra Suraksha Champion in the below-million category
127.x: Visakhapatnam was recognised as the Top Impact Creator in the million-plus city category in Swachh Survekshan 2022.
127.tq: Discriminate between the award title and the category instead of selecting a generic cleanliness label.

127.x: Tirupati Municipal Corporation ranked first in the Safaimitra Suraksha category.
127.tq: Separate the Safaimitra Suraksha result from Visakhapatnam’s different Top Impact Creator award.

127.x: The Swachh Survekshan 2024 rankings were used to choose 46 ULBs for sanitation PMUs.
127.tq: Distinguish the selected ULB count from the total number of ULBs and municipal categories in the State.

127.s: Which statement correctly compares the urbanisation level of Andhra Pradesh with that of India in 2011?
o: Andhra Pradesh had a lower urban share of 22.87%, while India had 29.47%.
Andhra Pradesh had a lower urban share, 29.47%, than India’s 31.16%.
Andhra Pradesh had a higher urban share, 40.81%, than India’s 31.16%.
Both had the same urban share of 29.47%.

4. Prakasam — 19.56%

127.x: The urban population was stated as 173.5 lakh, with a projection of 190.9 lakh by 2029.

127.s: Which of the following cities were selected as Andhra Pradesh’s four Smart Cities?

Area-based and pan-city projects through a 50:50 SPV

Integrated command centre and intelligent traffic system

12,370 houses with ₹4,451 crore aid, plus 61,084 flats in 30 layouts
