128.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
128.x: DAY-NRLM in rural areas is implemented through SERP. DAY-NULM is associated with MEPMA, while DDU-GKY is implemented through SEEDAP.
128.tq: Start from the rural mission pair and eliminate swapped implementing societies.

128.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Mission)
a. DAY-NRLM
b. DAY-NULM
c. DDU-GKY

List-II (Implementing society)
i. MEPMA
ii. SERP
iii. SEEDAP

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
128.x: DAY-NRLM is implemented by SERP, DAY-NULM by MEPMA and DDU-GKY by SEEDAP.
128.tq: Begin with the sure rural and urban pairs, then place the remaining society by elimination.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding livelihood missions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. SERP covers 84.47 lakh women under DAY-NRLM.
2. MEPMA covers 2.74 lakh Self-Help Groups under DAY-NULM.
3. SERP's SHG-bank linkage is first in India and accounts for 36% of national disbursements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. SERP covers 84.47 lakh women, MEPMA covers 2.74 lakh SHGs, and SERP's SHG-bank linkage is reported as first in India with 36% of national disbursements.
128.tq: Check coverage, group count and comparative performance as distinct statements.

128.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Streenidhi credit society?
128.x: Streenidhi lends up to ₹1 lakh at an interest rate of 11%.
128.tq: Pair the credit ceiling with the interest rate and reject altered figures.

128.s: The cumulative lending of Streenidhi credit society was reported as:
128.x: Streenidhi's cumulative lending was ₹26,540 crore.
128.tq: Identify the exact cumulative figure among closely spaced financial distractors.

128.s: Which of the following correctly states the number of Lakhpati Didis and the 2026-27 rural poverty-alleviation budget allocation?
128.x: There were 20.31 lakh Lakhpati Didis, and ₹1,877 crore was allocated for rural poverty alleviation in the 2026-27 budget; ₹818 crore was specifically allocated to NRLM.
128.tq: Separate the overall poverty-alleviation allocation from the NRLM sub-allocation.

128.s: OMCAP is the nodal agency for overseas recruitment in Andhra Pradesh under which law?
128.x: OMCAP, or Overseas Manpower Company AP Ltd, is the nodal agency for overseas recruitment under the Emigration Act, 1983.
128.tq: Match the agency with the specific governing law rather than a general migration statute.

128.s: Which of the following destinations are included among the places where OMCAP places workers?
o: Germany, Japan, the GCC and Europe
Germany, Russia, China and South Africa
Only the United States and Canada
Only the Gulf countries and Australia
128.x: OMCAP places workers in Germany, Japan, the GCC and Europe.
128.tq: Identify the complete destination group without adding unrelated regions.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about overseas employment through OMCAP:
1. OMCAP conducted a UAE taxi-driver recruitment drive in July 2026.
2. It was associated with recruitment for Saudi Arabia through L&T.
3. It is a private agent with no nodal role under the Emigration Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because OMCAP is the nodal agency for overseas recruitment under the Emigration Act, 1983, not merely a private agent.
128.tq: Find the institutional-role reversal in the false statement.

128.s: Gulf migration is reported to be particularly heavy among women from which area of Andhra Pradesh?
128.x: Gulf migration is particularly heavy among women from Konaseema.
128.tq: Test the precise regional association rather than select a broad geographical division.

128.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recruitment of housemaids for Gulf employment is correct?
o: Housemaids must be recruited through private agents because OMCAP handles only skilled workers.
Housemaids may be recruited only through OMCAP, not through private agents.
Housemaids may migrate without recruitment-channel regulation.
Housemaids must be recruited through local municipal bodies.
128.x: Housemaids are required to be recruited through OMCAP rather than private agents.
128.tq: Apply the stated recruitment rule to a specific category of overseas worker.

128.s: More than what proportion of abuse complaints among the concerned overseas workers came from workers not recruited through OMCAP?
128.x: More than 90% of abuse complaints came from workers who had not been recruited through OMCAP.
128.tq: Distinguish the reported threshold from lower rounded alternatives.

128.s: The Mega DSC-2025 in Andhra Pradesh recruited how many teachers and appointed how many police constables, respectively?
128.x: The Mega DSC-2025 recruited 15,941 teachers and 5,757 police constables were appointed.
128.tq: Split the paired figures carefully and match each number with its correct category.

128.s: The upper age limit for government jobs in Andhra Pradesh has been raised to which age, and up to which year does this provision apply?
128.x: The upper age limit for government jobs has been raised to 44 years till 2027.
128.tq: Pair the age limit with the corresponding validity year instead of treating them as separate facts.

128.s: Village and ward secretariats in Andhra Pradesh have been redesignated as which department?
o: Palle Pragathi and Ward Secretariat department
Grama Seva and Ward Development department
Swarna Andhra Village and Urban Services department
Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward department
128.x: Village and ward secretariats are now known as the Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward department.
128.tq: Test the exact official designation rather than a broad description of the institution.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the staff of village and ward secretariats in Andhra Pradesh:
1. They will act as Village Skill Officers.
2. They have mapped 1.68 crore households.
3. Their current staff strength has been officially specified as part of the available information.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Secretariat staff will act as Village Skill Officers and have mapped 1.68 crore households. The current staff strength is not specified.
128.tq: Find the unsupported statement; a precise numerical fact is combined with an unavailable detail.

128.s: VB-G RAM G commenced in Andhra Pradesh on:
128.x: VB-G RAM G began on 1 July 2026 and was launched in Andhra Pradesh.
128.tq: Use the exact commencement date and distinguish the year from nearby alternatives.

128.s: Which State has been reported as the top State on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, with more than one crore enrolments?
128.x: Andhra Pradesh is the top State on iGOT Karmayogi, with over one crore enrolments.
128.tq: Use the location clue and connect the platform ranking with the enrolment figure.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about employment-related issues in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The unemployment allowance has remained unpaid.
2. Disputes have arisen over the DSC merit list.
3. Youth unemployment in the State is reported at 17.5%, which is above the national rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct: the unemployment allowance is unpaid, disputes concern the DSC merit list, and youth unemployment is 17.5%, above the national rate.
128.tq: Check each separately stated criticism and use the all-inclusive option only when every statement is supported.

128.s: Which of the following is the target under the Super Six programme of Andhra Pradesh regarding employment?
128.x: The Super Six target is to create 20 lakh jobs in five years.
128.tq: Match the employment target with its stated time period.

129.s: As per the Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, the number of Fair Price Shops in Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
129.x: Andhra Pradesh had 29,796 Fair Price Shops according to the Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26.
129.tq: Use the exact numerical value rather than approximating the figure.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ration cards and beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh during 2025-26:
1. There were 1.48 crore ration cards.
2. The number of beneficiaries was 4.35 crore.
3. Aadhaar seeding covered 98% of the cards.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh had 1.48 crore ration cards, 4.35 crore beneficiaries and 98% Aadhaar seeding of cards.
129.tq: Combine closely related numerical indicators and test all three statements.

129.s: Which of the following correctly describes the coverage of Priority Household (PHH) and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) cards in Andhra Pradesh?
o: PHH: 139.40 lakh cards and 22.96 lakh people; AAY: 8.67 lakh cards and 411.91 lakh people
PHH: 8.67 lakh cards and 22.96 lakh people; AAY: 139.40 lakh cards and 411.91 lakh people
PHH: 411.91 lakh cards and 139.40 lakh people; AAY: 22.96 lakh cards and 8.67 lakh people
PHH: 139.40 lakh cards and 411.91 lakh people; AAY: 8.67 lakh cards and 22.96 lakh people
129.x: PHH cards numbered 139.40 lakh and covered 411.91 lakh people. AAY cards numbered 8.67 lakh and covered 22.96 lakh people.
129.tq: Match each category with both its card count and beneficiary count.

129.s: The monthly rice allocation under the public distribution system in Andhra Pradesh for 2025-26 was:
129.x: The monthly rice allocation was 2.36 lakh metric tonnes during 2025-26.
129.tq: Distinguish the exact allocation figure from close numerical alternatives.

129.s: Under the public distribution system in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correctly stated?
o: PHH households receive 5 kg per person and AAY households receive 35 kg per card.
PHH households receive 35 kg per person and AAY households receive 5 kg per card.
Both PHH and AAY households receive 5 kg per person.
Both PHH and AAY households receive 35 kg per card.
129.x: The entitlement is 5 kg per person for PHH beneficiaries and 35 kg per card for AAY beneficiaries.
129.tq: Test the reversed comparison between PHH and AAY entitlements.

129.s: Which of the following pairs relating to subsidised commodities in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ragi and jowar — ₹20 per kg up to 3 kg
129.x: Ragi and jowar up to 3 kg are provided free, not at ₹20 per kg. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
129.tq: Find the incorrectly stated price or entitlement among closely related commodities.

129.s: The fortified rice distributed through the public distribution system in Andhra Pradesh is fortified with:
o: Iron, Vitamin B12 and folic acid
129.x: The free Sortex fortified rice contains iron, Vitamin B12 and folic acid.
129.tq: Recall the exact composition of a welfare commodity.

129.s: Mana Biyyam, introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2013, provided BPL families with:
o: Fine rice at ₹5 per kg up to 35 kg per family
Fine rice at ₹1 per kg, subject to a ceiling of 20 kg per family
Wheat at ₹1 per kg without any family ceiling
129.x: Mana Biyyam provided fine rice at ₹1 per kg to BPL families, with a maximum of 20 kg per family.
129.tq: Link the scheme with its year, beneficiary group, price and quantity ceiling.

129.s: Door delivery of ration commodities to remote and tribal habitations in Andhra Pradesh used how many Mobile Dispensing Units according to APSES 2024-25?
129.x: Door delivery used 9,260 Mobile Dispensing Units for remote and tribal habitations according to APSES 2024-25.
129.tq: Recall the exact service-delivery infrastructure figure.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Deepam-2:
1. It provides three free LPG cylinders a year.
2. It had 1.84 crore beneficiaries.
3. An expenditure of ₹1,554.06 crore was recorded during April-December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Deepam-2 provides three free LPG cylinders annually, covers 1.84 crore beneficiaries and involved ₹1,554.06 crore during April-December 2025.
129.tq: Test the scheme through its benefit, coverage and expenditure figures.

129.s: DWCRA stands for:
o: Development of Women Cooperatives and Regional Associations
Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas
Department of Women and Community Rural Assistance
Development of Welfare Corporations in Rural Andhra
129.x: DWCRA means Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas. It was introduced in 1982-83 as a sub-scheme of IRDP.
129.tq: Test the exact expansion of a frequently confused programme acronym.

129.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between Velugu and DWCRA?
o: Velugu was merged with DWCRA as Indira Kranthi Patham and is run by SERP.
Velugu replaced DWCRA and is administered by the Reserve Bank of India.
DWCRA was converted into PMAY and is administered by APSHCL.
DWCRA was merged with Velugu as Stree Nidhi and is run by HUDCO.
129.x: Velugu, launched in 2000 for SHG-based poverty removal, was merged with DWCRA as Indira Kranthi Patham and is run by SERP.
129.tq: Use the scheme-merger and implementing-agency relationship to eliminate swapped authorities.

129.s: Stree Nidhi is primarily intended to provide SHG members with:
o: Full fee reimbursement for higher education
Timely and affordable credit, including loans up to ₹1 lakh at 11% interest
129.x: Stree Nidhi provides timely and affordable credit to SHG members, with loans up to ₹1 lakh at 11% interest.
129.tq: Match the programme with its core livelihood function rather than another welfare benefit.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pasupu Kumkuma — ₹10,000 grant per DWCRA woman
YSR Aasara — free bus travel for women
YSR Cheyutha — housing for poor families
Stree Nidhi — full fee reimbursement for students
129.x: Pasupu Kumkuma provided a ₹10,000 grant per DWCRA woman under the TDP government in 2019. The other programmes have different purposes.
129.tq: Discriminate among similar welfare schemes by their specific benefit.

129.s: YSR Aasara is associated with:
o: Provision of three free LPG cylinders annually
Construction of houses in Jagananna colonies
Reimbursement of SHG loan outstanding in instalments
129.x: YSR Aasara reimburses SHG loan outstanding in instalments.
129.tq: Identify the exact financial mechanism attached to the scheme.

129.s: YSR Cheyutha provides ₹18,750 per year to which group?
o: All SHG members irrespective of social group and age
SC, ST, BC and minority women aged 45-60 years
Only widows above 60 years of age
All women above 18 years of age
129.x: YSR Cheyutha provides ₹18,750 annually to SC, ST, BC and minority women in the 45-60 age group.
129.tq: Combine the beneficiary categories, age range and annual amount.

129.s: The AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project is correctly described by which of the following statements?
o: It is a World Bank-assisted project run by SERP and has five components.
It is an ADB-assisted project run by APSHCL and has three components.
It is a World Bank-assisted housing project run by HUDCO and has seven components.
It is a UNDP-assisted project run by the Department of Education and has five components.
129.x: The AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project is World Bank-assisted, implemented by SERP and comprises five components.
129.tq: Check the financing agency, implementing body and number of components together.

129.s: Which of the following statements about SERP and SHG-bank linkage in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: SERP mobilises 8.447 lakh rural women, and recovery is 99.09%.
SERP mobilises 84.47 lakh urban women, and recovery is 79.99%.
SERP mobilises 84.47 lakh rural women, and Andhra Pradesh has 99.99% recovery in SHG-bank linkage.
SERP mobilises 48.47 lakh rural women, and recovery is 89.99%.
129.x: SERP mobilises 84.47 lakh rural women, while Andhra Pradesh is reported to have 99.99% recovery in SHG-bank linkage.
129.tq: Distinguish exact lakh figures and percentage values from altered digits.

129.s: INDIRAMMA, the housing scheme for the poor, was launched in:
129.x: INDIRAMMA, expanded as Integrated Novel Development in Rural Areas and Model Municipal Areas, was launched in April 2006 for housing the poor.
129.tq: Link the scheme with its launch month and year.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: YSR Jagananna Housing — launched in April 2006
YSR Jagananna Housing — launched on 3 June 2021
129.x: YSR Jagananna Housing was launched on 3 June 2021. April 2006 is associated with INDIRAMMA, not YSR Jagananna Housing.
129.tq: Use the launch-date trap to separate two housing schemes.

129.s: YSR Jagananna Housing is implemented through APSHCL and provides houses in:
129.x: YSR Jagananna Housing is implemented by APSHCL and provides houses in Jagananna colonies.
129.tq: Match the scheme with its implementing agency and settlement name.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding housing initiatives in Andhra Pradesh:
1. APTIDCO is to complete 2.61 lakh PMAY-U 1.0 houses.
2. The APTIDCO project is supported by a ₹4,451 crore HUDCO loan.
3. APSHCL, EESL and APSEEDCO are to provide star-rated appliances to 5 lakh PMAY households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct. The appliance support is associated with 5 lakh PMAY households, while APTIDCO's target is 2.61 lakh houses backed by the HUDCO loan.
129.tq: Test institutional roles, project size and beneficiary coverage in one set.

129.s: Which of the following communities or groups is NOT included among the corporations grouped under the EWS Welfare Department?
129.x: The EWS Welfare Department groups the Reddy, Kamma, Kapu, Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vysya and EBC corporations. Scheduled Tribe corporations are separately identified under SC/ST/BC/minority welfare.
129.tq: Find the category that belongs to a separate welfare grouping.

129.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Andhra Pradesh welfare budget figures for 2026-27?
o: BC welfare ₹23,650.88 crore; SC welfare ₹6,090 crore; minorities ₹51,021 crore
BC welfare ₹51,021 crore; SC welfare ₹6,090 crore; minorities ₹20,644 crore
BC welfare ₹51,021 crore; SC welfare ₹20,644 crore; minorities ₹6,090 crore
BC welfare ₹20,644 crore; SC welfare ₹51,021 crore; minorities ₹3,133 crore
129.x: The 2026-27 figures were ₹51,021 crore for BC welfare, ₹20,644 crore for SC welfare and ₹6,090 crore for minorities. The BC department allocation within the total was ₹23,650.88 crore, while the minority sub-plan was ₹3,133 crore.
129.tq: Keep total welfare allocations separate from department and sub-plan allocations.

129.s: Jagananna Vidya Deevena and Vasathi De evena are respectively associated with:
o: Full fee reimbursement and hostel costs
129.x: Jagananna Vidya Deevena provides full fee reimbursement, while Vasathi Deevena supports hostel costs.
129.tq: Distinguish two related schemes by the specific educational expense they cover.

129.s: Post-matric Direct Benefit Transfer for minority students is available to students whose parental income is below:
129.x: The post-matric DBT for minority students covers those with parental income below ₹2.5 lakh.
129.tq: Recall the income ceiling without confusing it with other welfare thresholds.

129.s: The honorarium provided to Imams and Mouzams in Andhra Pradesh is in the range of:
129.x: Imams and Mouzams receive honoraria ranging from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000.
129.tq: Identify the correct range rather than a single amount.

129.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the social security pension amount in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Persons with 40% or more disability — ₹6,000 per month, with no age limit
Persons with 40% or more disability — ₹4,000 per month, subject to age above 60
Thalassaemia patients — ₹6,000 per month, subject to age above 60
Widows — ₹10,000 per month, without an age criterion
129.x: Persons with 40% or more disability receive ₹6,000 per month without an age limit. Thalassaemia and similar patients receive ₹10,000.
129.tq: Separate disability eligibility from age-based pensions and disease-specific support.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about social security pensions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The state had 63.12 lakh pensions in December 2025.
2. The monthly expenditure was ₹2,744 crore.
3. Payments are made through biometric, Aadhaar-based authentication.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct: there were 63.12 lakh pensions, monthly expenditure was ₹2,744 crore, and payments used biometric Aadhaar-based authentication.
129.tq: Combine beneficiary scale, expenditure and payment mechanism.

129.s: The AP Disha Bill, 2019 proposed which of the following timelines and penalty?
o: 14-day investigation, 7-day trial and life imprisonment only
129.x: The AP Disha Bill, 2019 proposed investigation within seven days, trial within fourteen days and the death penalty. It did not receive assent.
129.tq: Recall the exact sequence of timelines and the proposed punishment.

129.s: Which statement regarding the AP Disha Bill, 2019 is correct?
o: It never received assent and was withdrawn by the Cabinet in August 2026 on the Centre's advice after the BNS and BNSS came in.
It was withdrawn before the Hyderabad case because it conflicted with ICDS.
It was enacted as a Union law through the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
It received assent and came into force after the Hyderabad case.
129.x: The AP Disha Bill never received assent. The Cabinet withdrew it in August 2026 on the Centre's advice after the BNS and BNSS came into force.
129.tq: Distinguish a proposed state bill from an enacted law and track its final status.

129.s: Which of the following correctly describes ICDS infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
129.x: ICDS in Andhra Pradesh comprises 55,746 Anganwadis and 257 projects.
129.tq: Recall the paired infrastructure figures without transposing their digits.

129.s: Mission Shakti in Andhra Pradesh operates:
o: Fair Price Shops in all districts and the 1098 helpline
One Stop Centres in all districts and the 181 helpline
Anganwadis in all districts and the 112 helpline only
Women police stations in selected districts and the 104 helpline
129.x: Mission Shakti runs One Stop Centres in all districts and operates the 181 helpline.
129.tq: Match the programme with its institutional service and helpline number.

129.s: Stree Shakti, introduced on 15 August 2025, provides free bus travel to:
o: Women and persons with disabilities only
All residents of rural Andhra Pradesh
129.x: Stree Shakti provides free bus travel to women and transgender persons from 15 August 2025.
129.tq: Identify the exact beneficiary group and avoid adding later extensions to the original scheme.

129.s: Which of the following statements about Stree Shakti is correct?
o: It recorded 7.1 crore journeys by June 2026, with no change in the women's share.
It recorded more than 71 crore journeys by June 2026, and the women's share of bus passengers rose from 40% to 65%.
It recorded more than 71 lakh journeys by June 2026, and the women's share rose from 30% to 45%.
It recorded 17 crore journeys by June 2026, and the women's share fell from 65% to 40%.
129.x: Stree Shakti recorded more than 71 crore journeys by June 2026, while women's share of bus passengers increased from 40% to 65%.
129.tq: Check both the scale of usage and the direction of the percentage change.

129.s: Divyang Shakti, introduced in March 2026, extends the benefit of free bus travel to:
129.x: Divyang Shakti extends the free bus travel benefit to persons with disabilities.
129.tq: Link the programme name with its additional beneficiary category.

129.s: Kalyanamasthu and Shaadi Tohfa are respectively associated with:
o: Marriage assistance for poor brides and minority brides
Housing assistance for poor families and minority families
Education assistance for poor girls and minority students
Pension assistance for widows and transgender persons
129.x: Kalyanamasthu provides marriage assistance for poor brides, while Shaadi Tohfa provides marriage assistance for minority brides.
129.tq: Distinguish two similarly themed schemes by their beneficiary group.

129.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the scale of village and ward secretariats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: More than 15,000 secretariats offering more than 1,000 services
More than 20,000 secretariats offering more than 500 services
More than 10,000 secretariats offering more than 500 services
More than 5,000 secretariats offering more than 200 services
129.x: The village and ward secretariat system comprises more than 10,000 secretariats and offers more than 500 services.
129.tq: Match both quantitative dimensions rather than identifying only one correct figure.

129.s: The volunteer-based delivery model associated with Andhra Pradesh village and ward secretariats provides approximately one volunteer for every
129.x: The stated volunteer norm is one volunteer for every 50 households.
129.tq: Focus on the ratio and reject nearby numerical distractors.

129.s: How many households have been mapped under the Andhra Pradesh family-oriented welfare delivery exercise?
129.x: The family mapping exercise covered 1.68 crore households.
129.tq: Use exact-figure recall while distinguishing transposed digits and nearby values.

129.s: Navaratnalu, announced by the YSRCP in 2019, refers to
o: nine categories of local government institutions
129.x: Navaratnalu was the YSRCP's programme of nine welfare promises announced in 2019.
129.tq: Identify the programme's defining classification rather than an associated sector.

129.s:
Which of the following schemes were included among the promises associated with Navaratnalu?
1. Amma Vodi
2. Aasara
3. Pedalandariki Illu
4. Pension Kanuka
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Amma Vodi, Aasara, Pedalandariki Illu and Pension Kanuka were among the schemes included in Navaratnalu.
129.tq: Test a named-list cluster by checking whether every item belongs to the programme.

129.s: The Super Six welfare programme in Andhra Pradesh is associated with the
129.x: Super Six is associated with the NDA's 2024 programme.
129.tq: Separate the programme by political grouping and year.

129.s: Under the Talliki Vandanam promise, the proposed assistance is
129.x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per child.
129.tq: Recall the scheme-specific amount and reject amounts belonging to other Super Six promises.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Annadata Sukhibhava:
1. The total assistance is ₹20,000.
2. The State contribution is ₹14,000.
3. The PM-KISAN contribution is ₹6,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Annadata Sukhibhava provides ₹20,000 in total, comprising ₹14,000 from the State and ₹6,000 through PM-KISAN.
129.tq: Split the total into its component contributions before choosing the coded answer.

129.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a Super Six promise?
129.x: Deepam provides three free cylinders. Stree Shakti concerns free bus travel, Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per child, and Aadabidda Nidhi provides a monthly amount to women.
129.tq: Start with the sure scheme-benefit pair and use elimination for the swapped associations.

129.s: The Stree Shakti promise under the Super Six programme relates to
129.x: Stree Shakti provides free bus travel.
129.tq: Discriminate among closely related women-focused and household-focused benefits.

129.s: The employment-related promise under the Super Six programme consists of
129.x: The promise is for 20 lakh jobs or an unemployment allowance of ₹3,000.
129.tq: Compare the paired job target and allowance amount as one combined promise.

129.s: Aadabidda Nidhi under the Super Six programme provides women with
129.x: Aadabidda Nidhi provides ₹1,500 per month to women.
129.tq: Use exact monthly-amount recall and distinguish it from the unemployment allowance.

129.s: The proposed family-centred approach to welfare delivery in Andhra Pradesh treats the ______ as the unit and provides 5 kg of rice for every member.
129.x: The family is proposed as the unit of welfare, with 5 kg of rice for every family member.
129.tq: Apply the stated delivery principle to identify the relevant administrative unit.

129.s: Which one of the following statements regarding recent welfare and governance developments in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The Disha Bill was withdrawn in September 2025.
The Disha Bill was enacted in August 2026.
The Disha Bill was transferred to local governments in August 2026.
The Disha Bill was withdrawn in August 2026.
129.x: The Disha Bill was withdrawn in August 2026.
129.tq: Use precise date-and-event matching and avoid reversing enactment with withdrawal.

129.s: Before new pensions are issued in Andhra Pradesh, which of the following is expected to take place?
129.x: Family mapping is due before the issue of new pensions.
129.tq: Identify the prerequisite action in a policy-delivery sequence.

129.s: Welfare expenditure in Andhra Pradesh has been criticised on the ground that it accounts for approximately
129.x: Welfare expenditure has been described as accounting for 17 paise per rupee, raising concerns about fiscal strain.
129.tq: Recall the exact expenditure share and distinguish it from nearby proportions.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Welfare expenditure — 17 paise per rupee; poverty headcount in AP — 6.06%
Welfare expenditure — 6.06 paise per rupee; poverty headcount in AP — 17%
Welfare expenditure — 14.96 paise per rupee; poverty headcount in AP — 0.025%

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding own non-tax revenue of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Interest receipts are a component of non-tax revenue.
2. Royalties and user charges are included in non-tax revenue.
3. Non-tax revenue is raised exclusively through taxes on the public.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Interest receipts, royalties and user charges are forms of non-tax revenue. Statement 3 is false because non-tax revenue consists of receipts not raised by taxing the public.
130.tq: Find the statement that reverses the definition of non-tax revenue.

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II with reference to selected heads of Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue in 2024-25 RE:
List-I (Head)
 a. Mines and Minerals
 b. Police
 c. Medical and Health
 d. Education
List-II (Amount in ₹ crore)
 i. 55
 ii. 313
 iii. 389
 iv. 3,518
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: In 2024-25 RE, Mines and Minerals was ₹3,518 crore, Police ₹389 crore, Medical and Health ₹313 crore and Education ₹55 crore.
130.tq: Start from the distinctive high-value pair and verify the remaining pairs.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the trend in the share of Mines and Minerals in Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue?
o: 50 per cent in 2023-24 and 41 per cent in 2024-25 RE
34 per cent in 2023-24 and 37 per cent in 2024-25 RE
37 per cent in 2023-24 and 34 per cent in 2024-25 RE
41 per cent in 2023-24 and 50 per cent in 2024-25 RE
130.x: The share of Mines and Minerals increased from 41 per cent in 2023-24 to 50 per cent in 2024-25 RE.
130.tq: Check the direction of change before selecting the percentage pair.

130.s: In the revised estimates for 2024-25, which sequence correctly ranks the major components of Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts from highest to lowest share?
o: Own Tax, Central Transfers, Own Non-Tax
Own Non-Tax, Own Tax, Central Transfers
Central Transfers, Own Tax, Own Non-Tax
Own Tax, Own Non-Tax, Central Transfers
130.x: The ranking in 2024-25 RE was Own Tax, Central Transfers and Own Non-Tax. Own Non-Tax was the smallest of the three components.
130.tq: Arrange the components by relative share rather than by absolute revenue alone.

130.s: Which one of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's own revenue in 2024-25 is correct?
o: Own non-tax revenue exceeded its budget estimate.
Central transfers formed the smallest component of revenue receipts.
Own non-tax revenue fell from the budget estimate of ₹10,576 crore to the revised estimate of ₹7,018 crore.
Own tax revenue was lower than own non-tax revenue.
130.x: Own non-tax revenue was revised downward from the budget estimate of ₹10,576 crore to ₹7,018 crore.
130.tq: Test the direction of revision and reject reversed budget-revised figures.

130.s: Before the introduction of GST, which item accounted for approximately 73 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's total tax revenue in 2016-17 RE?
130.x: Before GST, Sales Tax/VAT accounted for approximately 73 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's total tax revenue in 2016-17 RE.
130.tq: Use the pre-GST and post-GST distinction to identify the relevant tax source.

130.s:
With reference to the post-GST tax structure in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. SGST accounted for about 40 per cent in 2025-26 RE.
2. Sales tax continues mainly on petroleum products and liquor.
3. Sales tax was completely abolished for every commodity after GST.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: SGST accounted for about 40 per cent in 2025-26 RE, while sales tax continues mainly on petroleum products and liquor. Statement 3 is false because these items remain outside GST.
130.tq: Identify the exception to the general post-GST position.

130.s: The Goods and Services Tax in India was introduced on 1 July 2017 under which Constitutional Amendment Act?
130.x: GST commenced on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
130.tq: Match the implementation date with the correct constitutional amendment.

130.s:
Match the following constitutional provisions with their GST-related subjects:
List-I (Article)
 a. Article 246A
 b. Article 269A
 c. Article 279A
List-II (Subject)
 i. GST Council
 ii. Levy and collection of IGST in the course of inter-State trade
 iii. Concurrent power to make laws relating to GST
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Article 246A provides concurrent GST legislative power, Article 269A concerns IGST, and Article 279A establishes the GST Council.
130.tq: Start with the familiar GST Council provision and eliminate mismatched articles.

130.s: In the GST Council, the voting weight is divided between the Centre and the States in which manner?
130.x: The Centre has one-third of the voting weight and all the States together have two-thirds.
130.tq: Distinguish voting weight from the separate majority required for decisions.

130.s: Across all States during 2014-15 to 2023-24, own tax revenue constituted approximately what share of revenue receipts?
130.x: Own tax revenue formed approximately 47 per cent of revenue receipts across all States during the stated period.
130.tq: Select the stated approximate share without confusing it with Andhra Pradesh's individual-year share.

130.s: Which of the following is NOT a usual component of non-tax revenue?
o: Dividends and profits of public sector undertakings
Compulsory tax collected from the public
130.x: Non-tax revenue includes dividends, profits, fees, fines, penalties, user charges, royalties and departmental receipts. A compulsory tax is tax revenue, not non-tax revenue.
130.tq: Find the option that contradicts the definition of non-tax revenue.

130.s: In February 2021, Andhra Pradesh became eligible for additional borrowing after completing power-sector reforms prescribed by which authority?
o: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
130.x: The power-sector reforms were prescribed by the Department of Expenditure under the Ministry of Finance and were linked to eligibility for additional borrowing.
130.tq: Identify the authority connected with reform-linked borrowing permission.

130.s: For 2026-27, interest payments of Andhra Pradesh were estimated at ₹37,281 crore. This represented approximately what share of revenue receipts?
130.x: Interest payments of ₹37,281 crore were estimated to account for 16 per cent of revenue receipts in 2026-27.
130.tq: Link the absolute amount with its stated percentage share.

130.s: For 2026-27, the pension expenditure of Andhra Pradesh was estimated at:
130.x: Pension expenditure was estimated at ₹23,713 crore in 2026-27, equivalent to about 10 per cent of revenue receipts.
130.tq: Distinguish the pension figure from the larger interest-payment figure.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the movement in Andhra Pradesh's interest payments?
o: ₹32,944 crore in 2023-24 and ₹29,481 crore in 2024-25 RE
₹29,481 crore in 2024-25 RE and ₹32,944 crore in 2025-26 RE
₹29,481 crore in 2023-24 and ₹32,944 crore in 2024-25 RE
₹37,233 crore in 2023-24 and ₹29,481 crore in 2024-25 RE
130.x: Interest paid increased from ₹29,481 crore in 2023-24 to ₹32,944 crore in 2024-25 RE.
130.tq: Check both the year and the direction of change in the paired figures.

130.s: Interest payments of Andhra Pradesh rose from ₹32,967 crore in 2024-25 to ₹37,233 crore in 2025-26 RE. The increase was:
130.x: The increase was ₹37,233 crore minus ₹32,967 crore, equal to ₹4,266 crore.
130.tq: Subtract the earlier year's expenditure from the revised estimate.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's fiscal position:
1. The State continued to run a primary deficit.
2. Interest payments and principal repayment together accounted for 18 paise of every rupee in 2026-27.
3. Interest payments and principal repayment were lower than welfare expenditure in the same comparison.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The State continued to run a primary deficit, and interest plus principal repayment accounted for 18 paise of every rupee. Statement 3 is false because this was described as level with welfare expenditure, which accounted for 17 paise.
130.tq: Compare the stated expenditure shares and reject the reversed comparison.

130.s: According to the reported CAG monthly data, revenue expenditure of Andhra Pradesh crossed what proportion of its annual estimate by November in each of the last three years?
130.x: Revenue expenditure crossed 60 per cent of the annual estimate by November in each of the last three years.
130.tq: Identify the precise threshold rather than selecting a nearby rounded figure.

130.s: In 2023-24, committed expenditure together with subsidies accounted for what share of revenue expenditure across all States?
130.x: Committed expenditure plus subsidies accounted for 51.76 per cent of revenue expenditure across all States in 2023-24.
130.tq: Distinguish the combined share from the individual expenditure components.

130.s: High interest payments, administrative costs and welfare commitments are associated with which of the following consequences in Andhra Pradesh's finances?
o: Fiscal rigidity and crowding out of capital outlay
Automatic elimination of the revenue deficit
Complete replacement of revenue expenditure by capital expenditure
130.x: High interest payments, administrative costs and welfare commitments create fiscal rigidity and crowd out capital outlay.
130.tq: Trace the stated cause-effect relationship from committed costs to capital expenditure.

130.s: According to the 2026–27 projections, the combined share of central taxes and grants in Andhra Pradesh’s revenue receipts is approximately
130.x: In 2026–27, Andhra Pradesh is projected to receive ₹64,362 crore as its share in central taxes and ₹32,458 crore as grants. Together, these constitute 41% of the State’s revenue receipts.
130.tq: Use the combined figure before matching it with the percentage.

130.s: For 2026–27, the amount projected for Andhra Pradesh as its share in central taxes is
130.x: Andhra Pradesh’s projected share in central taxes for 2026–27 is ₹64,362 crore. Grants are projected separately at ₹32,458 crore.
130.tq: Separate the tax-share figure from the grants figure.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s share in the divisible pool of Central taxes:
1. Its share under the 14th Finance Commission was 4.31%.
2. Its share under the 15th Finance Commission was 4.05%.
3. Its share under the 16th Finance Commission for 2026–31 is 4.22%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three statements are correct: the respective shares are 4.31%, 4.05% and 4.22%.
130.tq: Check each Finance Commission figure independently before selecting the coded combination.

130.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the 16th Finance Commission award to Andhra Pradesh for 2026–31?
o: Wastewater systems — ₹6,125 crore for each city
130.x: The 16th Finance Commission awarded ₹6,125 crore for disaster management. Rural and urban local body grants are ₹16,627 crore and ₹12,158 crore respectively.
130.tq: Match each grant head with its exact amount and reject reversed pairs.

130.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission awards, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam may each receive up to what amount for wastewater systems?
130.x: Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam can each receive special urban-infrastructure grants of up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater systems.
130.tq: Identify the per-city ceiling rather than the combined possible amount.

130.s: Which significant change is associated with the 16th Finance Commission’s recommendations for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It ended revenue-deficit grants to Andhra Pradesh.
It increased revenue-deficit grants to Andhra Pradesh.
It transferred disaster grants entirely to urban local bodies.
It abolished local-body grants to Andhra Pradesh.
130.x: The 16th Finance Commission ended revenue-deficit grants for Andhra Pradesh while providing grants for local bodies and disaster management.
130.tq: Focus on the policy change rather than the individual grant amounts.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission’s national grants:
1. Grants-in-aid amount to ₹9.47 lakh crore.
2. Their share in Finance Commission transfers fell from 19.4% to 8.3%.
3. Local bodies receive ₹7.91 lakh crore, divided into basic and performance grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three statements are correct. Grants-in-aid are ₹9.47 lakh crore, their share declined from 19.4% to 8.3%, and local bodies receive ₹7.91 lakh crore through basic and performance grants.
130.tq: Treat the percentages, totals and grant classification as separate checks.

130.s: The corpus recommended for the State Disaster Response Fund and State Disaster Mitigation Fund under the 16th Finance Commission is
130.x: The recommended SDRF/SDMF corpus is ₹2,04,401 crore. It is shared between the Centre and States in the prescribed ratio.
130.tq: Distinguish the disaster-fund corpus from local-body and grants-in-aid totals.

130.s: The SDRF/SDMF corpus is shared between the Centre and the States in which ratio for general States?
130.x: For general States, the Centre:State sharing ratio is 75:25. The ratio is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
130.tq: Separate the general-State ratio from the special ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

130.s: Heatwaves and lightning were recommended as
o: new categories of disasters under the disaster-finance framework
new sources of central tax revenue
130.x: The 16th Finance Commission recommended heatwaves and lightning as new disasters eligible for consideration under the disaster-finance framework.
130.tq: Identify the institutional context in which the newly listed items appear.

130.s: The 14th Finance Commission’s local-body grants amounted to ₹2,87,436 crore. Their distribution was based on
o: area weighted at 90% and 2011 population weighted at 10%
2011 population weighted at 90% and area weighted at 10%
130.x: The 14th Finance Commission distributed local-body grants using 2011 population with a 90% weight and area with a 10% weight.
130.tq: Check both the total and the two distribution weights.

130.s: Off-budget borrowing by Andhra Pradesh is best described as
o: grants received from the Finance Commission and repaid by local bodies
borrowings raised exclusively from foreign governments and not guaranteed by the State
loans raised by State PSUs or corporations and serviced from the State budget, but excluded from reported debt
direct borrowing by the State Government included in reported public debt
130.x: Off-budget borrowings are raised by State public-sector entities or corporations but serviced from the State budget. They are kept outside the State’s reported debt figures.
130.tq: Apply the definition by identifying both the borrower and the repayment responsibility.

130.s: According to the CAG, Andhra Pradesh’s off-budget borrowings stood at approximately what amount in March 2023?
130.x: The CAG reported Andhra Pradesh’s off-budget borrowings at ₹1.28 lakh crore in March 2023, equivalent to 9.7% of GSDP.
130.tq: Match the year-specific figure with the correct source and percentage.

130.s: In March 2023, Andhra Pradesh’s off-budget borrowings were equivalent to approximately
130.x: The CAG assessed the ₹1.28 lakh crore off-budget borrowing burden in March 2023 at 9.7% of GSDP.
130.tq: Use the percentage associated with the specified year, not a later guarantee ratio.

130.s:
Arrange the following amounts of Andhra Pradesh’s outstanding off-budget borrowings in chronological order:
A. ₹1,40,470 crore as on 31 March 2024
B. ₹1,18,394 crore as on 31 March 2022
C. ₹1.28 lakh crore in March 2023
130.x: The chronological order is ₹1,18,394 crore in March 2022, ₹1.28 lakh crore in March 2023 and ₹1,40,470 crore in March 2024.
130.tq: First arrange the dates, then attach the corresponding amounts.

130.s: As on 31 December 2025, the sanctioned exposure under Andhra Pradesh government guarantees was approximately
130.x: The sanctioned guarantee exposure as on 31 December 2025 was ₹3,11,182.28 crore, or approximately ₹3.11 lakh crore.
130.tq: Do not confuse sanctioned exposure with outstanding principal.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the guarantee position as on 31 December 2025?
o: Sanctioned guarantees ₹1,77,033.88 crore; outstanding principal ₹3,11,182.28 crore
Sanctioned guarantees ₹3,11,182.28 crore; outstanding principal ₹1,77,033.88 crore
Sanctioned guarantees ₹27,000 crore; outstanding principal ₹15,222 crore
Sanctioned guarantees ₹1,54,797 crore; outstanding principal ₹1,77,328 crore
130.x: The sanctioned guarantee exposure was ₹3,11,182.28 crore, while outstanding principal was ₹1,77,033.88 crore.
130.tq: Start with the sure distinction between total sanctioned exposure and the amount actually outstanding.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s guarantees:
1. Guarantees are contingent liabilities.
2. They are included in outstanding debt even before they are invoked.
3. They crystallise as liabilities if invoked.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Guarantees are contingent liabilities and crystallise if invoked. They are not included in outstanding debt before invocation, making statement 2 incorrect.
130.tq: Test the distinction between a contingent liability and an existing debt liability.

130.s: The amount of conditional guarantees included in Andhra Pradesh’s Budget 2026–27 is
130.x: Conditional guarantees not yet in force amounted to ₹27,000 crore in Budget 2026–27.
130.tq: Separate the total conditional guarantees from the portion relating to APSDC.

130.s: The ₹2,000 crore portion of Andhra Pradesh’s conditional guarantees is associated with
130.x: Conditional guarantees comprise ₹25,000 crore for APSDC and ₹2,000 crore for APRDC.
130.tq: Discriminate between the two corporations named in the guarantee breakup.

130.s: Which corporation owed ₹15,222 crore according to the information reported on 15 February 2026?
130.x: APSBCL was reported to owe ₹15,222 crore as on the specified reporting date.
130.tq: Match the corporation with its reported liability rather than with the guarantee amount.

130.s: The Guarantee Redemption Fund maintained by States is administered by
o: the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
130.x: The Guarantee Redemption Fund is an RBI-administered fund built by States to meet guarantees that are invoked.
130.tq: Use the ‘who administers the fund?’ approach to identify the responsible institution.

130.s: In Budget 2026–27, Andhra Pradesh’s outstanding guarantees were shown as approximately
130.x: Budget 2026–27 showed outstanding guarantees of ₹1,77,328 crore, equivalent to 10% of GSDP. The earlier figure was ₹1,54,797 crore, or 11% of GSDP, in 2023–24.
130.tq: Compare the current budget figure with the earlier benchmark without reversing the percentage and amount.

130.s: The trend in Andhra Pradesh’s stamp and registration revenue from 2022–23 to 2025–26 is correctly represented by
130.x: The reported sequence is ₹8,023 crore in 2022–23, ₹9,542 crore in 2023–24, ₹9,200 crore in 2024–25 revised estimates and ₹11,047 crore in 2025–26.
130.tq: Preserve the year order and distinguish the revised estimate from the actual trend values.

130.s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh’s stamp and registration revenue reach ₹11,047 crore according to the reported figures?
130.x: Stamp and registration revenue was reported at ₹11,047 crore for 2025–26.
130.tq: Match the highest stated amount with its corresponding financial year.

130.s: According to the stated policy view, settling disputes relating to Section 22A land would help Andhra Pradesh by
o: increasing its share in the divisible pool
130.x: The Chief Minister stated that resolving Section 22A land disputes would increase registration revenue by facilitating transactions and registrations.
130.tq: Link the administrative action with its direct revenue effect.

130.s: Andhra Pradesh’s commercial tax collection in June 2026 was reported as
130.x: Commercial tax collection was ₹4,829 crore in June 2026, representing 16% year-on-year growth.
130.tq: Match the monthly figure with its own growth rate, not the quarterly or GST figure.

130.s: Andhra Pradesh’s commercial tax collection for the first quarter of 2026–27 was
130.x: Commercial tax collection for the first quarter of 2026–27 was reported at ₹15,323 crore.
130.tq: Distinguish the quarterly aggregate from the June monthly collection.

130.s: When Central and State GST authorities investigate the same entity, the Andhra Pradesh High Court held that they must
o: decide between themselves which authority will proceed
transfer the investigation to the Finance Commission
allow only the Central authority to proceed
130.x: The High Court held that the Central and State GST authorities must decide between themselves which authority will proceed when both investigate the same entity.
130.tq: Identify the required coordination mechanism instead of assuming exclusive jurisdiction.

130.s: Excise revenue, mainly from liquor, is described as Andhra Pradesh’s
130.x: Excise, principally liquor-related revenue, is the second-largest own-tax source of Andhra Pradesh.
130.tq: Distinguish own-tax revenue from non-tax revenue and central transfers.

130.s: Which sequence correctly shows the reported amounts of Andhra Pradesh’s excise revenue?
130.x: The reported sequence of excise revenue is ₹14,799 crore, ₹15,998 crore and ₹21,300 crore, with ₹21,300 crore being the 2024–25 revised-estimate figure.
130.tq: Arrange the successive revenue figures without confusing them with their percentages.

130.s: Which statement regarding Andhra Pradesh’s excise revenue is correct?
o: It accounted for 5% of own-tax revenue in 2024–25 revised estimates.
It was classified as a central grant rather than own-tax revenue.
It was the slowest-growing own-tax head, increasing by 5%.
It was the fastest-growing revenue head in the 2024–25 Budget, increasing by 60%.
130.x: Excise was the fastest-growing head in the 2024–25 Budget, with growth of 60%. It accounted for about 22% of own-tax revenue in the revised estimates.
130.tq: Use the growth-rate clue while rejecting statements that reverse the revenue classification.

130.s: The share of excise revenue in Andhra Pradesh’s own-tax revenue was projected at what percentage in the 2025–26 revised estimates?
130.x: Excise revenue was projected to constitute 24% of Andhra Pradesh’s own-tax revenue in the 2025–26 revised estimates.
130.tq: Distinguish the later-year percentage from the 2024–25 revised-estimate percentage.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s motor vehicle tax and fuel VAT:
1. Motor vehicle tax was reported at ₹4,320 crore, ₹4,557 crore and ₹4,655 crore in the successive figures stated.
2. Motor vehicle tax constituted about 5% of own-tax revenue.
3. Fuel VAT is counted under Sales Tax.
4. Fuel VAT under Sales Tax was ₹18,505 crore in the 2024–25 revised estimates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All four statements are correct. The stated motor vehicle tax figures are ₹4,320 crore, ₹4,557 crore and ₹4,655 crore, while fuel VAT is included under Sales Tax and amounted to ₹18,505 crore in the 2024–25 revised estimates.
130.tq: Verify each revenue head, amount and classification separately before selecting the complete combination.

130.s:
With reference to the share of States in the divisible pool of Union taxes, consider the following pairs:

Finance Commission — States' share
1. 14th Finance Commission — 42%
2. 15th Finance Commission — 41%
3. 16th Finance Commission — 41%

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
130.x: The 14th Finance Commission fixed the States' share at 42%, while both the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions fixed it at 41%.
130.tq: Match each percentage with the correct Finance Commission before eliminating the codes.

130.s: The share of Andhra Pradesh in the divisible pool of Union taxes recommended by the 14th Finance Commission was approximately
130.x: The 14th Finance Commission assigned Andhra Pradesh a share of 4.305% in the divisible pool.
130.tq: Distinguish the close horizontal-devolution percentages by associating each with its Finance Commission period.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Andhra Pradesh's share in the divisible pool under the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions respectively?
130.x: Andhra Pradesh's share was 4.05% approximately under the 15th Finance Commission and 4.217% under the 16th Finance Commission.
130.tq: Use the chronological order of the Finance Commissions to avoid swapping similar percentages.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission:
1. It was chaired by Arvind Panagariya.
2. It retained the States' share in the divisible pool at 41%.
3. Eighteen States had asked for a 50% share for the States.
4. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar recorded higher shares than Andhra Pradesh under its recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All four statements are correct. The 16th Finance Commission was chaired by Arvind Panagariya, retained 41%, faced a demand for 50% from 18 States, and assigned higher shares to Uttar Pradesh and Bihar than to Andhra Pradesh.
130.tq: Check the chairperson, retained percentage, demand and comparative shares as separate factual units.

130.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under the 16th Finance Commission's share in the divisible pool?
130.x: Telangana's share was 2.174%, whereas Kerala's share was 2.382%. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu had shares of 4.131% and 4.097% respectively.
130.tq: Find the single altered figure in a set of closely related State percentages.

130.s: Revenue deficit grants to Andhra Pradesh after devolution were provided under which Article of the Constitution?
130.x: Revenue deficit grants are provided under Article 275. Article 270 concerns distribution of taxes, while Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
130.tq: Use the constitutional-Article discrimination method for grants, tax sharing and the Finance Commission.

130.s: Which statement best describes the post-devolution revenue deficit grants received by Andhra Pradesh?
o: They were discontinued immediately after bifurcation in 2014.
They were received under both the 14th and 15th Finance Commissions.
They were received only under the 16th Finance Commission.
They are a form of State tax revenue.
130.x: Andhra Pradesh, a chronic revenue-deficit State after 2014, received post-devolution revenue deficit grants under the 14th and 15th Finance Commissions.
130.tq: Distinguish the Finance Commissions that granted support from the one that discontinued it.

130.s: The post-devolution revenue deficit grants to Andhra Pradesh declined from ₹13,174 crore in 2022-23 to which amount in the 2024-25 Revised Estimates?
130.x: The grants declined from ₹13,174 crore in 2022-23 to ₹4,922 crore in the 2024-25 Revised Estimates.
130.tq: Compare the beginning and ending figures in the stated time sequence.

130.s: Which one of the following was discontinued by the 16th Finance Commission in relation to Andhra Pradesh?
o: The divisible pool of Union taxes
Revenue deficit grants and sector-specific and State-specific grants
130.x: The 16th Finance Commission discontinued revenue deficit grants as well as sector-specific and State-specific grants. Tax devolution and the Finance Commission continue constitutionally.
130.tq: Identify the institutional change without confusing it with the continuing constitutional arrangements.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's dependence on central transfers:
1. About 40% of Andhra Pradesh's revenues came from the Centre in the 2024-25 Budget Estimates.
2. The proportion was approximately 47% in the 2024-25 Revised Estimates when EAP loans were included.
3. Andhra Pradesh depended less on grants than the average State.
4. Centrally Sponsored Schemes constitute about 40% of all central transfers to Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Andhra Pradesh relies more on grants than the average State, so statement 3 is false.
130.tq: Locate the reversed comparison in the statement about dependence on grants.

130.s: According to the all-States average for 2014-15 to 2023-24, the largest share of State revenues among the following came from
130.x: The all-States average consisted of 47% own tax revenue, 28% share in Union taxes and 17% grants. Thus, own tax revenue was the largest component.
130.tq: Compare the three percentages directly and select the largest source.

130.s: Which feature of Centrally Sponsored Schemes contributes to Andhra Pradesh's dependence on central transfers but also limits fiscal flexibility?
o: They are excluded from central transfers.
They permit unrestricted reallocation by the State.
They are entirely financed from State tax revenue.
130.x: Centrally Sponsored Schemes constitute about 40% of central transfers and carry rigid co-financing conditions, limiting the State's flexibility.
130.tq: Connect the institutional feature of a scheme with its practical fiscal consequence.

130.s: Which criterion received the highest weight under the 15th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula?
130.x: Income distance had the highest weight under the 15th Finance Commission at 45%.
130.tq: Identify the maximum weight before considering the other criteria.

130.s: Which of the following changes between the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions is correctly matched?
130.x: Income distance declined from 45% under the 15th Finance Commission to 42.5% under the 16th. Population rose to 17.5%, area fell to 10%, and tax and fiscal effort was removed.
130.tq: Compare each criterion's old and new weight to detect the correctly paired change.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the horizontal devolution criteria of the 16th Finance Commission:
1. Population received a weight of 17.5%.
2. Demographic performance received a weight of 10%.
3. Area received a weight of 10%.
4. Contribution to GDP was introduced with a weight of 10%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All four statements are correct under the 16th Finance Commission's formula.
130.tq: Verify each numerical weight independently before selecting the complete combination.

130.s: Income distance for the purpose of horizontal devolution is measured with reference to a State's per capita GSDP and
o: the per capita GDP of the Union Territory of Delhi alone
the average of the top three large States
130.x: Income distance is measured by comparing a State's per capita GSDP with the average of the top three large States. A lower GSDP produces a higher share under this criterion.
130.tq: Discriminate the exact benchmark used in the income-distance formula.

130.s: Why does Andhra Pradesh face a 'prosperity paradox' under the income-distance criterion?
o: Its forest area is excluded from the formula.
Its above-average per capita income works against it in income-distance allocation.
Its tax effort is automatically assigned zero weight under every Finance Commission.
Its low population prevents it from receiving any tax devolution.
130.x: Andhra Pradesh's above-average per capita income works against it because the income-distance criterion gives greater weight to States with lower per capita GSDP.
130.tq: Apply the direction of the income-distance formula to Andhra Pradesh's relative prosperity.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the demographic-performance criterion under the 16th Finance Commission?
o: It was abolished and replaced by tax and fiscal effort.
It is measured by population growth from 1971 to 2011 and replaced the 15th Finance Commission's TFR metric.
It is measured only by the 2011 population and replaced the area criterion.
It uses only the change in population after 2011.
130.x: The 16th Finance Commission measures demographic performance through population growth from 1971 to 2011, replacing the 15th Finance Commission's total fertility rate metric.
130.tq: Separate the population base, time period and metric used by the 15th and 16th Commissions.

130.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the forest criterion under the 16th Finance Commission?
o: It retained a 10% weight and now includes open forests.
It was merged entirely with population.
It was reduced to zero weight.
It was replaced by tax and fiscal effort.
130.x: The forest criterion retained a 10% weight under the 16th Finance Commission and was expanded to include open forests.
130.tq: Check both the retained percentage and the changed scope of the criterion.

130.s: The introduction of the contribution-to-GDP criterion under the 16th Finance Commission helped Andhra Pradesh's share because it
o: recognised the State's contribution to economic output
increased the weight of tax and fiscal effort to 10%
excluded all States with above-average per capita income
removed the divisible pool from the devolution formula
130.x: The new contribution-to-GDP criterion carried a 10% weight and helped Andhra Pradesh's share rise by recognising its economic contribution.
130.tq: Link the newly introduced criterion with its stated effect on Andhra Pradesh's share.

130.s: Andhra Pradesh's tax devolution was estimated at ₹50,475 crore in 2024-25 Budget Estimates and ₹52,080 crore in Revised Estimates. The amount provided in the 2026-27 Budget Estimates was
130.x: The 2026-27 Budget Estimates provided ₹64,362 crore as Andhra Pradesh's tax devolution.
130.tq: Track the figures across Budget Estimates and Revised Estimates without interchanging years.

130.s: For all States taken together, tax devolution in 2024-25 was approximately
o: ₹12.87 lakh crore against a Budget Estimate of ₹12.47 lakh crore
₹10.87 lakh crore against a Budget Estimate of ₹12.47 lakh crore
₹12.47 lakh crore against a Budget Estimate of ₹10.87 lakh crore
₹12.47 lakh crore against a Budget Estimate of ₹12.87 lakh crore
130.x: Actual tax devolution for all States was ₹12.87 lakh crore against a Budget Estimate of ₹12.47 lakh crore.
130.tq: Read the actual and budget figures in the correct direction rather than reversing them.

130.s: In the first quarter of 2026-27, devolution to States contracted by approximately
130.x: Tax devolution to States contracted by 19.5% in the first quarter of 2026-27.
130.tq: Distinguish the precise contraction percentage from nearby altered figures.

130.s: Taxes are shared between the Union and the States under Article 270, whereas the Finance Commission is constituted under
130.x: Article 270 deals with the distribution of taxes, while Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
130.tq: Pair each constitutional Article with its distinct fiscal function.

130.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the major minerals of Andhra Pradesh?
130.x: Barytes, dolomite and uranium are listed among Andhra Pradesh's minerals. Platinum is not included in the specified list.
130.tq: Identify the outsider from the State-specific mineral list rather than relying on general mineral knowledge.

130.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of minerals listed among the major minerals of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Crude oil, natural gas, barytes and heavy mineral beach sands
130.x: Crude oil, natural gas, barytes and heavy mineral beach sands are all included in the specified list of Andhra Pradesh minerals.
130.tq: Start with a sure mineral pair and eliminate sets containing an unlisted mineral.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about important mineral locations in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Mangampet in YSR Kadapa is a major barytes deposit.
2. Mica is associated with the Nellore belt.
3. Limestone occurs in the Kadapa-Kurnool basins.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Mangampet is the country's major barytes deposit, mica occurs in the Nellore belt, and limestone is found in the Kadapa-Kurnool basins.
130.tq: Associate each mineral with its stated Andhra Pradesh location before selecting the combination.

130.s: Royalty on minerals in Andhra Pradesh is levied ad valorem on the
130.x: Under the MMDR Act, 1957, royalty is levied ad valorem on the Average Sale Price. The 2016 Mineral Concession Rules provide that ASP includes royalty, DMF and NMET payments.
130.tq: Distinguish the valuation base for royalty from land, machinery and macroeconomic measures.

130.s: Which statement correctly reflects the legal position affirmed by the Supreme Court regarding mineral royalty?
o: Royalty is not a tax, and States may tax mineral-bearing land.
Royalty is collected only by local bodies and cannot be imposed by the Union.
Royalty is a tax and States cannot tax mineral-bearing land.
States cannot receive auction revenue from mineral blocks.
130.x: The Supreme Court reaffirmed that royalty is not a tax and that States may tax mineral-bearing land. Auction revenue from mineral blocks accrues to State governments.
130.tq: Use the legal-status distinction between royalty and tax to reject the reversed statement.

130.s: The Supreme Court's upholding of the Union's royalty-calculation framework was stated to avert an estimated fall in States' mining revenue of
130.x: The judgment was stated to avert an estimated 15–17% fall in States' mining revenue.
130.tq: Retain the stated range and reject options that alter both its lower and upper limits.

130.s: Revenue from the auction of mineral blocks, including critical minerals, accrues to
130.x: Auction revenue from mineral blocks, including critical minerals, accrues to State governments.
130.tq: Ask which level of government receives the revenue rather than which body regulates mining.

130.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding non-tax revenue of State Public Sector Undertakings in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Profits and dividends — non-tax revenue retained by the State
Profits and dividends — tax revenue transferred to the Union
CPSE dividends — revenue retained by Andhra Pradesh
130.x: Profits and dividends of State PSUs are non-tax revenue retained by the State. In Andhra Pradesh's 2024-25 Revised Estimates, dividends were included under 'Others', while interest receipts were only ₹27 crore.
130.tq: Separate State PSU dividends from CPSE dividends and distinguish them from interest receipts.

130.s: In Andhra Pradesh's 2024-25 Revised Estimates, dividends from State PSUs were included under which head, since they were not shown separately?
130.x: The annexure did not show dividends separately; they were included under 'Others', amounting to ₹2,680 crore. Interest receipts were ₹27 crore.
130.tq: Use the reporting-head distinction to avoid confusing dividends with interest receipts.

130.s: The ₹2.68 lakh crore transfer referred to in the comparison of central non-tax revenue was a surplus transfer from
o: the Andhra Pradesh State Public Sector Undertakings
130.x: The Centre's non-tax revenue grew by 20.9% during April-November 2025, supported by a ₹2.68 lakh crore surplus transfer from the Reserve Bank of India.
130.tq: Identify the institution associated with the surplus transfer rather than the recipient revenue head.

130.s:
Which of the following statements regarding mining-sector revenue is correct?
1. Mining lease or auction premium and royalty accrue to the States.
2. Approximately 90% of mining-sector revenue accrues to the States.
3. The entire mining-sector revenue accrues to the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Mining lease or auction premium and royalty go to the States, and approximately 90% of mining-sector revenue accrues to the States. Statement 3 is incorrect because the entire revenue does not accrue to the Centre.
130.tq: Split the options by identifying the statement that reverses the Centre-State distribution.

130.s: Section 9D, introduced through an amendment to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) framework, relates to:
o: A scheme for providing free sand to rural households
A ban on auctioning mineral-bearing areas by the States
A Centre-controlled framework determining future State levies on minerals
A statutory trust for distributing mining royalties among districts
130.x: Section 9D makes future State levies on minerals dependent on a Centre-controlled framework. This provision has been criticised as unfair to mineral-rich States.
130.tq: Identify the authority controlling the framework rather than confusing it with a mining welfare institution.

130.s: The District Mineral Foundation (DMF) is best described as:
o: A profit-making company constituted under Section 9D of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015
A Central tax authority established under the Finance Act, 2015
A non-profit trust constituted under Section 9B of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015
A State department responsible for fixing irrigation water rates
130.x: The DMF is a non-profit trust established under Section 9B of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015.
130.tq: Use the section-number and institutional-form clues to distinguish DMF from other mining provisions.

130.s: User charges and fees collected for public services are classified under:
130.x: Licence fees, regulatory charges and user charges are forms of non-tax revenue.
130.tq: Discriminate between tax revenue and non-tax revenue by focusing on the nature of the receipt.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding departmental receipts of Andhra Pradesh for 2024-25 (Revised Estimates):
1. Medical and Health receipts were Rs. 313 crore.
2. Education receipts were Rs. 55 crore.
3. Police receipts were Rs. 389 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The departmental receipts were Rs. 313 crore for Medical and Health, Rs. 55 crore for Education and Rs. 389 crore for Police. All three statements are correct.
130.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the combined option.

130.s: Irrigation receipts, including receipts from water rates, are classified under which category of receipts?
130.x: Irrigation receipts fall under General/Economic Services receipts. The specific Andhra Pradesh figure for water-rate receipts is not specified here.
130.tq: Match the service with its budget classification instead of its broad social purpose.

130.s: Raising user charges for public services is generally used as a measure of:
130.x: Increasing user charges is a standard fiscal-consolidation tool because it can augment non-tax revenue and reduce the gap between receipts and expenditure.
130.tq: Apply the fiscal meaning of higher service charges to the stated policy objective.

130.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the nature of expenditure?
o: Capital expenditure — Interest payments and subsidies
Revenue expenditure — Creation of physical and financial assets
Revenue expenditure — Running the government and recurring expenditure
130.x: Revenue expenditure is recurring expenditure used for running the government, including salaries, pensions, interest, subsidies and maintenance. Capital expenditure mainly creates physical or financial assets.
130.tq: Separate recurring government operations from expenditure that creates assets.

130.s:
Which of the following items is generally classified as capital expenditure in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Roads
2. Irrigation projects
3. Buildings
4. Loans and advances
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Roads, irrigation projects, buildings, and loans and advances are included among capital expenditure items. They either create assets or represent financial asset creation.
130.tq: Use the asset-creation test to identify the capital-expenditure group.

130.s: The mnemonic “Revenue = Running the Government; Capital = Creating Assets” is intended to distinguish expenditure on the basis of:
o: Whether expenditure is recurring or asset-creating
Whether expenditure is financed through taxes or borrowings only
Whether expenditure is related to welfare or defence
Whether expenditure is incurred by the Centre or the State
130.x: Revenue expenditure is associated with recurring government operations, while capital expenditure is associated mainly with the creation of physical or financial assets.
130.tq: Translate the mnemonic into the underlying budget-classification principle.

130.s:
Arrange the following components of Andhra Pradesh expenditure in descending order according to their stated position:
A. Loans and Advances
B. Revenue Expenditure
C. Capital Outlay
130.x: The stated order is Revenue Expenditure greater than Capital Outlay, which is greater than Loans and Advances.
130.tq: Use the first comparison and then place the remaining smaller component.

130.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget Estimates for 2026-27, revenue expenditure constituted approximately what share of total expenditure?
130.x: Revenue expenditure constituted approximately 83% of Andhra Pradesh’s total expenditure in the 2026-27 Budget Estimates.
130.tq: Select the stated approximate share while rejecting nearby percentage distractors.

130.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of expenditure items funded through Andhra Pradesh revenue spending?
o: Polavaram, Amaravati, ports and metro rail only
Foreign exchange reserves, customs duties and public debt
Rice subsidy, power subsidy, welfare pensions and housing
Mining leases, auction premiums and royalties
130.x: Andhra Pradesh revenue spending funds rice subsidy, power subsidy, welfare pensions and housing. These are recurring expenditure commitments rather than primarily asset-creating projects.
130.tq: Identify the group containing recurring welfare and operating items.

130.s: Which scheme received the highest allocation among the following in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27?
130.x: NTR Bharosa Pension received Rs. 27,719 crore, exceeding Thalliki Vandanam at Rs. 8,456 crore, Annadata Sukhibhava at Rs. 6,600 crore and Amaravati capital at Rs. 6,000 crore.
130.tq: Compare the allocations directly and identify the largest value.

130.s: The allocation for NTR Bharosa Pension in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was:
130.x: The NTR Bharosa Pension allocation was Rs. 27,719 crore, approximately 11% of revenue expenditure.
130.tq: Distinguish the pension allocation from the nearby welfare and rural-development figures.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly describes welfare schemes such as pensions and recurring subsidies in budget classification?
o: They are non-tax revenue because they are transferred through DBT.
They are capital expenditure because they create financial assets.
They are public debt receipts because beneficiaries repay the expenditure.
They are revenue expenditure and may widen the revenue deficit because they create recurring liabilities.
130.x: Welfare schemes are revenue expenditure. Since they do not create assets and impose recurring liabilities, they can widen the revenue deficit.
130.tq: Apply the asset-creation and recurrence tests to welfare expenditure.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh Budget 2025-26:
1. Rural Development was allocated Rs. 18,140 crore.
2. Rural Development allocation increased by 50%.
3. Rs. 5,956 crore was provided for rural employment.
4. Social Welfare and Nutrition was allocated Rs. 9,071 crore, a decrease of 38%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All four statements are correct. Social Welfare and Nutrition also included Rs. 3,344 crore for rice subsidy and Rs. 900 crore for Bala Sanjeevani.
130.tq: Verify both allocation figures and percentage changes before choosing the complete combination.

130.s: The Public-Private-People Partnership (P4) model in Andhra Pradesh aims to:
o: Replace all welfare transfers with capital expenditure within one year
Provide only urban infrastructure through public-private financing
Achieve zero poverty in five years by treating the family as the unit and linking DBT beneficiaries with jobs and self-employment
Limit government support to agricultural subsidies alone
130.x: P4 aims at zero poverty in five years, treats the family as the unit, and links DBT beneficiaries to jobs and self-employment.
130.tq: Identify the option containing all the distinctive objectives of the P4 model.

130.s:
Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the trend in social-sector revenue spending across all States?
1. Its share in revenue expenditure has remained broadly stable since 2011-12.
2. Its share as a percentage of GDP has declined since 2020-21.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Across all States, social-sector revenue spending has remained stable as a share of revenue expenditure since 2011-12, while declining as a percentage of GDP since 2020-21.
130.tq: Compare the two different denominators: revenue expenditure and GDP.

130.s: All States together spent approximately how much on unconditional cash transfers, as reported by the 16th Finance Commission?
130.x: All States spent approximately Rs. 4.14 lakh crore on unconditional cash transfers. The Economic Survey 2025-26 urged conditional transfers or sunset clauses.
130.tq: Convert the lakh-crore figure carefully and reject the tenfold distractors.

130.s: Which of the following was urged by the Economic Survey 2025-26 in relation to unconditional cash transfers?
o: Their universal and permanent continuation without review
130.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 urged the use of conditional transfers or sunset clauses in relation to unconditional cash transfers.
130.tq: Distinguish the recommended policy safeguard from the nature of the expenditure.

130.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 allocation?
o: Polavaram — Rs. 6,105 crore; Amaravati capital — Rs. 6,000 crore
Polavaram — Rs. 6,000 crore; Amaravati capital — Rs. 6,105 crore
Polavaram — Rs. 6,705 crore; Amaravati capital — Rs. 3,447 crore
