The State where the employee last served
The State to which the employee is permanently allotted
136.x: Provident fund liability follows the State to which the employee is permanently allotted.
136.tq: Discriminate between the permanent-allotment basis and the population-ratio basis.

136.s: The salaries of judges in the common High Court were divided between the successor States on the basis of:
136.x: Under Section 30, judges' salaries in the common High Court were split according to the population ratio.
136.tq: Link the special expenditure item with its statutory apportionment basis.

136.s: Which of the following best explains the economic significance of salaries, pensions and interest in the post-bifurcation finances of Andhra Pradesh?
o: They are committed expenditure and may crowd out capital spending.
They are entirely discretionary expenditure and can be cancelled immediately.
They increase capital spending automatically through a multiplier effect.
They are treated only as receipts from the Union Government.
136.x: Salaries, pensions and interest are committed expenditure. Their large burden can reduce the funds available for capital spending.
136.tq: Apply the fiscal concept of committed expenditure to the stated cost issue.

136.s: How much did Andhra Pradesh pay in interest during 2024-25?
136.x: Andhra Pradesh paid Rs 32,944 crore in interest during 2024-25.
136.tq: Identify the exact expenditure figure rather than a nearby deficit estimate.

136.s: Which of the following disputes was stated to be pending before the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Tribunal?
o: Disputes over the appointment of the Finance Commission
Only disputes over the divisible pool percentage
136.x: Seniority and pension disputes continue to remain pending before the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Tribunal.
136.tq: Match the pending forum with the subject matter of the dispute.

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding power allocation after bifurcation:
1. Existing power purchase agreements with the DISCOMs continue under the Twelfth Schedule.
2. APGENCO plants are divided on the basis of their location.
3. Power from central stations is divided on the basis of consumption during the last five years.
4. Andhra Pradesh's share of central-station power is about 46 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All four statements are correct. The Twelfth Schedule continues existing PPAs, divides APGENCO plants by location and uses five-year consumption for central-station power, giving Andhra Pradesh about 46 per cent.
136.tq: Combine the legal continuity rule with the two different allocation bases.

136.s: Which statement correctly describes the dispute between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana concerning power dues?
o: Telangana accepted all APGENCO claims and the dispute was finally settled by the Central Government.
APGENCO was required to refund all payments received from Telangana after bifurcation.
APGENCO claimed that Telangana's DISCOMs owed thousands of crores for power supplied just after bifurcation, while Telangana raised counter-claims under other heads.
The dispute concerns only the division of central-station power and not unpaid dues.
136.x: APGENCO claimed unpaid dues from Telangana's DISCOMs for power supplied immediately after bifurcation. Telangana made counter-claims under other heads, and the dispute remains unresolved.
136.tq: Reject the options that wrongly convert an unresolved bilateral dispute into a settlement.

136.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the basis for division of tax arrears and refunds:

List-I
 a. Arrears of property tax or land revenue
 b. Arrears of other taxes
 c. Deferred taxes of industrial units
 d. Refund of other taxes collected in excess

List-II
 i. Population ratio
 ii. State where the industrial unit is located
 iii. State where the property lies
 iv. Place of assessment

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
136.x: Property-tax and land-revenue arrears follow the location of the property; other-tax arrears follow the place of assessment; deferred industrial-unit taxes follow the unit's location; and refunds of other taxes follow the population ratio.
136.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with a mismatched legal basis.

136.s: Under Section 50, arrears of taxes other than property tax or land revenue are assigned on the basis of:
o: State where the industrial unit is located
136.x: Section 50 assigns arrears of other taxes to the successor State containing the place of assessment.
136.tq: Discriminate between the place-of-assessment rule and the population-ratio refund rule.

136.s: Deferred taxes of industrial units in the form of loans and advances are assigned to the successor State in which:
o: The taxpayer's head office is situated
136.x: Under Section 51(1), deferred taxes of industrial units in the form of loans and advances follow the State where the industrial unit is located.
136.tq: Use the location of the industrial unit rather than the place of assessment as the deciding clue.

136.s: Which of the following correctly states the basis for refund of property tax collected in excess?
o: State where the industrial unit is located under Section 51(1)
State where the property lies under Section 55
136.x: Refund of property tax collected in excess follows the State where the property lies and is identified in the material with Section 55.
136.tq: Match the refund type with both its territorial basis and section number.

136.s: What anomaly arose from the different rules governing tax arrears and tax refunds after bifurcation?
o: Arrears followed the location of property, while all refunds followed the location of industrial units.
Arrears and refunds were both assigned to the Union Government.
Arrears generally followed the place of assessment, while refunds followed the population ratio.
Both arrears and refunds followed the population ratio, causing no dispute.
136.x: Arrears of other taxes generally followed the place of assessment, which was mostly Hyderabad, whereas refunds of other taxes followed the population ratio. This difference was considered disadvantageous to Andhra Pradesh.
136.tq: Compare the two rules side by side instead of treating all tax items alike.

136.s: According to the Fourteenth Finance Commission's estimate, the tax-arrears and refund anomaly cost Andhra Pradesh approximately:
136.x: The anomaly was estimated to have cost Andhra Pradesh about Rs 3,900 crore.
136.tq: Keep the crore figure and its zero count distinct from the larger resource-gap figures.

136.s: Which section is identified as the refund section for other taxes collected in excess?
136.x: Section 56 is identified as the refund section for other taxes collected in excess, although one cited source places the rule in Section 55 notes.
136.tq: Resolve the section-number conflict by identifying the specific refund category.

136.s: Under Section 46(1), the Thirteenth Finance Commission award to undivided Andhra Pradesh is to be divided by the Centre on the basis of:
o: Equal shares between the successor States
Only the location of public assets
Only the place of tax assessment
136.x: Section 46(1) provides that the Thirteenth Finance Commission award to undivided Andhra Pradesh is divided using the population ratio and other parameters.
136.tq: Notice the combined basis rather than an exclusive single criterion.

136.s: Sections 46(2) and 46(3) require the Centre to provide appropriate grants and a special development package particularly for which areas?
o: Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra Pradesh
Only the newly created capital region
136.x: The provisions specifically emphasise backward areas, especially Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
136.tq: Identify the regions expressly named in the statutory assistance provision.

136.s: In practice, the special development package under Section 46 covered how many backward districts?
136.x: The package covered seven backward districts: four in Rayalaseema and three in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
136.tq: Use the total and then verify it against the regional breakup.

136.s: The seven districts covered by the special development package were distributed as:
o: 3 in Rayalaseema and 4 in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh
4 in Rayalaseema and 3 in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh
5 in Rayalaseema and 2 in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh
2 in Rayalaseema and 5 in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh
136.x: The package covered four backward districts in Rayalaseema and three in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
136.tq: Test the regional breakup rather than merely recalling the total.

136.s: Which statement best describes the implementation of the special development package for backward districts?
o: Initial allocations were made, but subsequent disbursements stalled.
All allocations were disbursed before bifurcation.
No allocations were made and the proposal was abandoned immediately.
The package was converted entirely into a revenue deficit grant.
136.x: Initial allocations were made for the seven districts, but subsequent disbursements stalled.
136.tq: Distinguish an announced or allocated package from actual continuing disbursement.

136.s: Under Section 54 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, public debt and Public Account liabilities of the successor States are generally apportioned on the basis of
o: the geographical area of the successor States
the location of the project financed by the liability
136.x: Section 54 provides for the division of public debt and Public Account liabilities according to the population ratio, subject to the specific treatment of loans re-lent for activities confined to one State.
136.tq: Identify the statutory basis of apportionment rather than the location-based exception.

136.s: A loan was re-lent exclusively for an activity confined to one successor State. How is this loan treated under Section 54 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: It is divided according to the population ratio.
It is divided equally between the two successor States.
It remains with the State in which the activity is confined.
It is transferred to the Union Government.
136.x: Although Section 54 generally uses the population ratio, a loan re-lent for an activity confined to one State remains with that State. Thus, the location of the project determines its treatment.
136.tq: Apply the location-based exception to the general population-ratio rule.

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding floating loans under Section 55 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. A floating loan raised for the purposes of one successor State remains with that State.
2. Every floating loan is divided according to the population ratio.
3. Floating loans not raised for the purposes of one particular State are divided according to the population ratio.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Section 55 retains a floating loan with the State for whose purposes it was raised, while other floating loans are apportioned according to population; therefore, statement 2 is incorrect.
136.tq: Separate the specific State-purpose rule from the general rule for other floating loans.

136.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the general rules under Sections 54 and 55 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Public debt and Public Account liabilities generally follow population, while floating loans for one State’s purposes remain with that State.
Public debt follows project location, while all floating loans follow geographical area.
Both public debt and all floating loans are apportioned exclusively according to project location.
Both public debt and floating loans are assigned entirely to Andhra Pradesh.
136.x: Section 54 generally uses the population ratio for public debt and Public Account liabilities, with a location-based exception for confined activities. Section 55 similarly retains State-specific floating loans with that State and apportions other floating loans by population.
136.tq: Compare the general population rule with the State-specific project exception.

136.s:
Assertion (A): A project loan re-lent for an activity confined to one successor State is not divided solely on the population ratio.
Reason (R): The location of the activity determines which successor State retains such a loan under the statutory exception.
Choose the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
136.x: Both the assertion and the reason are true. The location-based treatment of a project confined to one State explains why the loan is not apportioned solely by population.
136.tq: Test whether the stated location principle actually explains the statutory exception.

136.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of debt apportionment after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh?

1. Public debt and Public Account liabilities — Population ratio
2. Loan re-lent for an activity confined to one State — State where the activity is confined
3. Floating loan for one State’s purposes — The same State
4. Other floating loans — Population ratio
136.x: All four pairings are correct. Sections 54 and 55 combine the population-ratio rule with exceptions based on the State-specific purpose or location of the activity.
136.tq: Start with the sure statutory pairs and verify whether the general rule also covers the remaining pair.

136.s: The criticism of the debt and revenue-asset apportionment after bifurcation principally relates to which combination?
o: Debt was divided by area, while revenue assets were divided by population.
Andhra Pradesh took 58% of the debt, whereas revenue assets were allocated by location and Andhra Pradesh received 46%.
Debt and revenue assets were both divided according to the population ratio.
Andhra Pradesh received 58% of the debt and 46% of the revenue assets.
136.x: The criticism is that debt was divided by population, resulting in Andhra Pradesh taking 58%, while revenue assets were allocated by location, with Andhra Pradesh receiving 46% of the revenue assets.
136.tq: Catch the reversed basis of allocation by contrasting population with location.

136.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh took 58% of the debt under the criticised apportionment arrangement.
2. Andhra Pradesh received 46% of the revenue assets when allocation was made by location.
3. Debt and revenue assets were both allocated by location.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the criticism specifically contrasts population-based debt division with location-based allocation of revenue assets.
136.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the statement that applies the same basis to both categories.

136.s: According to the debt indicators for Andhra Pradesh, the total debt for 2024-25 was
136.x: The total debt of Andhra Pradesh for 2024-25 was reported as Rs 5,68,623 crore in the State Economic Survey 2025-26.
136.tq: Match the financial year with the corresponding debt figure rather than the revised estimate or deficit figure.

136.s: The Revised Estimate for Andhra Pradesh’s total debt in 2025-26 was reported as
136.x: The 2025-26 Revised Estimate placed Andhra Pradesh’s total debt at Rs 6,35,177 crore.
136.tq: Distinguish the revised estimate from the previous year’s actual debt and budget deficit figures.

136.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 indicators in ascending order according to their percentage of GSDP:
A. Fiscal deficit
B. Revenue deficit
C. Off-budget borrowings reported for March 2023

Choose the correct sequence.
136.x: The percentages are 1.1% for the revenue deficit, 3.8% for the fiscal deficit and 9.7% for off-budget borrowings. Therefore, the ascending order is B, A, C.
136.tq: Use the numerical order of the percentages to eliminate sequences without comparing the rupee amounts.

136.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent central assistance to Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: After the 16th Finance Commission ended revenue deficit grants, the Centre sanctioned Rs 15,000 crore for Amaravati and other assistance to help Andhra Pradesh tide over its difficulties.
The Centre sanctioned Rs 15,000 crore exclusively for repayment of off-budget borrowings.
Revenue deficit grants were increased by the 16th Finance Commission without any additional assistance for Amaravati.
The 16th Finance Commission permanently converted the revenue deficit grant into a loan of Rs 15,000 crore.
136.x: After the 16th Finance Commission ended revenue deficit grants, the Centre sanctioned Rs 15,000 crore for Amaravati and provided other assistance to help Andhra Pradesh manage its financial difficulties.
136.tq: Separate the end of a grant mechanism from the later central assistance announced for specific support.

136.s: Special Assistance for Capital Investment (SASCI) 50-year interest-free loans to Andhra Pradesh are treated as
o: part of the revenue deficit grant
outside the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap
off-budget borrowings reported by the CAG for March 2023
part of the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap
136.x: SASCI 50-year interest-free loans are treated as outside the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap.
136.tq: Distinguish interest-free capital-investment loans from the fiscal-deficit ceiling and revenue grants.

136.s: Which of the following best captures the principal fiscal disagreement between the Centre and Andhra Pradesh in the context of post-bifurcation assistance?
o: The Centre prefers loans and guarantees, while Andhra Pradesh seeks non-repayable grants.
Andhra Pradesh opposes all forms of central assistance, including grants and loans.
The Centre prefers non-repayable grants, while Andhra Pradesh prefers loans and guarantees.
Both the Centre and Andhra Pradesh prefer only non-repayable grants.
136.x: The controversy is that the Centre is viewed as preferring loans and guarantees, whereas Andhra Pradesh seeks non-repayable grants to address its financial needs.
136.tq: Test the direction of the preference by avoiding the reversed Centre–State pairing.

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the lapse of central funds under SNA/PFMS rules:
1. Central funds can lapse through the operation of SNA/PFMS rules.
2. Out of Rs 15,031 crore, Rs 5,051 crore went unsecured.
3. The entire amount of Rs 15,031 crore was secured and utilised without lapse.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Rs 5,051 crore out of Rs 15,031 crore went unsecured through the SNA/PFMS-related process, so statement 3 is false.
136.tq: Reject the absolute statement that contradicts the stated unsecured amount.

137.s: Which committee was constituted under Section 6 to identify suitable locations for the capital of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
137.x: The Expert Committee under Section 6 was chaired by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan and was asked to identify locations for the new capital.
137.tq: Use the committee-function association to distinguish similar capital-location bodies.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Expert Committee under Section 6:
1. It was constituted by the Central Government.
2. It was required to submit its report within six months.
3. It supported the creation of a single super capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: The committee was constituted by the Centre and had to report within six months. It opposed a super capital because of concerns about ecological damage.
137.tq: Find the statement that reverses the committee's recommendation.

137.s: The Expert Committee chaired by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan submitted its report in:
137.x: The Expert Committee submitted its report in August 2014.
137.tq: Separate the report date from later capital-project and litigation dates.

137.s: The State ministerial committee known as the Capital City Advisory Committee was chaired by:
137.x: The Capital City Advisory Committee of the Andhra Pradesh Government was chaired by P. Narayana, the Minister for Municipal Administration.
137.tq: Match the committee with its chairperson rather than with its recommendation.

137.s: Which region was backed by the Capital City Advisory Committee for locating the capital?
137.x: The State ministerial committee backed the Vijayawada-Guntur region.
137.tq: Use the location-recommendation pairing to avoid confusing committees.

137.s: Who took the final decision to choose Amaravati as the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
137.x: The capital was chosen by the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet. Amaravati was selected on the Krishna River between Vijayawada and Guntur.
137.tq: Identify the authority that actually exercised the decision-making power.

137.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the three-capitals proposal of 2020?
137.x: The 2020 proposal assigned Amaravati as the legislative capital, Visakhapatnam as the executive capital and Kurnool as the judicial capital.
137.tq: Split the options by matching each city with its proposed function.

137.s: The three-capitals proposal of 2020 was based principally on the:
o: Capital City Advisory Committee and World Bank study
Sivaramakrishnan Committee and APCRDA master plan
G.N. Rao Committee and BCG study
137.x: The three-capitals proposal was based on the G.N. Rao Committee and the BCG study.
137.tq: Distinguish the bodies connected with the original capital choice from those connected with the three-capitals proposal.

137.s: The Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the CRDA Repeal Act, 2020 on:
137.x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the CRDA Repeal Act on 3 March 2022 and upheld Amaravati.
137.tq: Distinguish the litigation date from the foundation and later policy dates.

137.s: Under which provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is special financial support provided for essential facilities in the new capital?
137.x: Section 94(3) provides for special financial support for essential facilities in the new capital. Section 95 relates to higher-education quota provisions.
137.tq: Use the exact section number and reject the nearby-section trap.

137.s:
Which of the following facilities are specifically covered by Section 94(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
1. Raj Bhavan
2. Government Secretariat
3. High Court
4. Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: Section 94(3) covers the Raj Bhavan, High Court, Government Secretariat, Legislative Assembly, Legislative Council and other essential infrastructure.
137.tq: Recognise that the complete facility list is the correct combination.

137.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Provision)
a. Section 5
a. Section 6
c. Section 94(3)
d. Section 94(4)

List-II (Subject)
i. Expert committee for identifying capital locations
ii. Common capital arrangement for ten years
iii. Financial support for essential capital facilities
iv. Denotification of degraded forest land, if needed

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: Section 5 concerned Hyderabad as the common capital for ten years; Section 6 created the expert committee; Section 94(3) concerns financial support; and Section 94(4) concerns degraded forest land.
137.tq: Start from the sure section-function pairs and eliminate the remaining codes.

137.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Section 94(4) deals with denotification of degraded forest land for the capital, if required.
2. Section 6 made Hyderabad the common capital for ten years.
3. Section 5 dealt with the constitution of the expert committee for identifying capital locations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x: Only Statement 1 is correct. Section 5 concerned the common capital arrangement, while Section 6 set up the expert committee.
137.tq: Check the exact section-function relationship instead of relying on neighbouring numbers.

137.s: What was the total amount of direct central grants released for Amaravati under Section 94(3)?
137.x: The total direct central grant was Rs 2,500 crore, comprising an initial Rs 1,500 crore and a later Rs 1,000 crore for essential infrastructure.
137.tq: Add the two stated components and distinguish grants from the larger commitment estimate.

137.s: The direct central assistance for Amaravati was described as comprising:
o: Rs 1,000 crore initially and Rs 1,500 crore later
Rs 27,000 crore initially and Rs 2,500 crore later
Rs 1,500 crore initially and Rs 1,000 crore later
Rs 2,500 crore initially and no later assistance
137.x: The assistance consisted of Rs 1,500 crore initially for capital construction and a special Rs 1,000 crore later for essential infrastructure.
137.tq: Discriminate between the total amount and the order of its two components.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the estimated cost and central commitment for the capital:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Government estimated the capital cost at about Rs 1.2 lakh crore.
2. The Centre's stated commitment was about Rs 27,000 crore.
3. The central commitment fully covered the State's estimated cost.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: The State estimated the cost at about Rs 1.2 lakh crore, whereas the Centre's commitment was about Rs 27,000 crore. The commitment was therefore far smaller and heavy borrowing followed.
137.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the comparison between estimated cost and commitment.

137.s: The World Bank and ADB assistance for Amaravati was described as:
o: Rs 7,387.70 crore as infrastructure finance from NaBFID
Rs 15,000 crore at concessional terms of 0.6% plus TONA
Rs 11,000 crore as a HUDCO term loan
137.x: The World Bank and ADB assistance amounted to Rs 15,000 crore on concessional terms of 0.6% plus TONA.
137.tq: Match the lender with both the amount and the distinctive loan terms.

137.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: World Bank and ADB — Rs 7,387.70 crore infrastructure finance
HUDCO — Rs 11,000 crore term loan for urban infrastructure
NaBFID — Rs 11,000 crore concessional loan at 0.6% plus TONA
137.x: HUDCO sanctioned Rs 11,000 crore as a term loan for urban infrastructure. The other options interchange the lenders and amounts.
137.tq: Check the lender-purpose-amount triad and eliminate swapped institutions.

137.s: What amount of Centre-facilitated multilateral support for Amaravati was promised in the Union Budget 2024-25?
137.x: The Union Budget 2024-25 promised Rs 15,000 crore of Centre-facilitated multilateral support for Amaravati.
137.tq: Distinguish the budget promise from the broader amount described as facilitated through several lenders.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding assistance for Amaravati:
1. The Rs 15,000 crore assistance promised in the Union Budget 2024-25 was fast-tracked in January 2026.
2. The Centre described about Rs 26,000 crore as being facilitated through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO.
3. The assistance was structured entirely as non-repayable grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: The Rs 15,000 crore assistance was fast-tracked in January 2026, and about Rs 26,000 crore was described as facilitated through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO. The assistance was routed through loans and guarantees rather than being entirely grants.
137.tq: Identify the false absolute statement about the form of assistance.

137.s: The principal dispute between Andhra Pradesh and the Centre regarding capital assistance concerns whether the assistance should be provided as:
o: tax devolution or Finance Commission grants
non-repayable grants or loans supported by sovereign guarantees
foreign direct investment or equity shares
municipal bonds or State development loans
137.x: Andhra Pradesh sought non-repayable grants, whereas the Centre routed assistance through loans and sovereign guarantees, requiring approvals under Article 293(2).
137.tq: Apply the central distinction between grants and repayable borrowing to the policy dispute.

137.s: Article 293(2) is relevant to the Amaravati financing issue because it concerns:
o: the tenure of the common capital
approval relating to State borrowing when specified conditions apply
allocation of seats in the Legislative Assembly
137.x: The financing arrangement involved sovereign guarantees and approvals under Article 293(2), which relates to borrowing by States under specified conditions.
137.tq: Use the constitutional-article association rather than confusing it with Reorganisation Act provisions.

137.s: The projected debt of Andhra Pradesh referred to in relation to the capital-financing issue was approximately:
o: Rs 7.11 lakh crore, or about 36% of GSDP
Rs 5.25 lakh crore, or 27% of GSDP
Rs 11.00 lakh crore, or about 50% of GSDP
Rs 2.50 lakh crore, or 15% of GSDP
137.x: The projected debt was Rs 7.11 lakh crore, amounting to about 36% of GSDP.
137.tq: Read the amount and percentage together to avoid a single-figure trap.

137.s: The ‘Restart Amaravati’ initiative began in:
137.x: The ‘Restart Amaravati’ initiative began in April 2025.
137.tq: Separate the restart initiative from the original foundation ceremony.

137.s: The capital region administered in connection with APCRDA covers approximately:
137.x: The capital region covers about 8,452 sq km and includes Guntur, Palnadu, Bapatla and other areas.
137.tq: Distinguish the large capital-region area from the smaller capital-city area.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about the capital city area of Amaravati:
1. It covers 217.23 sq km.
2. It comprises 29 villages.
3. It is identical in area to the entire capital region of 8,452 sq km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: The capital city area is 217.23 sq km and covers 29 villages. It is distinct from the much larger capital region of 8,452 sq km.
137.tq: Use the area comparison to reject the statement equating the city with the region.

137.s: In Phase-I of land pooling for Amaravati, what proportion of the 37,921 acres notified had been pooled?
137.x: Phase-I land pooling covered 93.1% of the 37,921 acres notified.
137.tq: Distinguish the percentage pooled from the separate returnable-plot figures.

137.s: Which of the following correctly describes the returnable plots under Amaravati land pooling?
137.x: A total of 70,550 returnable plots were allotted, of which 62,150 were registered.
137.tq: Check the order of allotted and registered figures rather than treating them as interchangeable.

137.s: The amount paid towards farmers’ annuities up to December 2025 was:
137.x: Farmers’ annuities amounting to Rs 2,038.61 crore had been paid up to December 2025.
137.tq: Distinguish the annuity amount from the separate pension and project-sanction figures.

137.s: Which of the following correctly represents the status of works in the Amaravati capital project?
o: 85 works worth Rs 57,592.71 crore sanctioned; 96 works worth Rs 56,288 crore contracted; physical progress 8.64%
96 works worth Rs 56,288 crore sanctioned; 85 works worth Rs 57,592.71 crore contracted; physical progress 68.4%
96 works worth Rs 57,592.71 crore sanctioned; 85 works worth Rs 56,288 crore contracted; physical progress 6.84%
85 works worth Rs 57,592.71 crore sanctioned; 96 works worth Rs 56,288 crore contracted; physical progress 6.84%
137.x: Ninety-six works worth Rs 57,592.71 crore were sanctioned, 85 works worth Rs 56,288 crore were contracted, and physical progress was 6.84%.
137.tq: Keep the sanctioned and contracted counts and amounts in their correct order.

137.s: For the Assembly, High Court and Secretariat towers in Amaravati, the Chief Minister ordered:
o: a monthly financial audit by the Centre
a quarterly review by the World Bank
137.x: A two-month review cycle was ordered for the Assembly, High Court and Secretariat towers.
137.tq: Identify the administrative monitoring interval rather than confusing it with a funding condition.

137.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved land pooling of 6,212.50 acres for the:
137.x: The Cabinet approved land pooling of 6,212.50 acres for the Inner Ring Road.
137.tq: Match the exact acreage with the infrastructure project.

137.s:
Amaravati Sangamam, approved at Sakhamuru at a cost of Rs 759 crore, comprises which of the following?
1. State Public Library
2. An auditorium
3. Global Institute of Good Governance
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: Amaravati Sangamam comprises the State Public Library, an auditorium and the Global Institute of Good Governance, with an approved cost of Rs 759 crore.
137.tq: Recognise the complete set of components and retain the distinctive project cost.

137.s: Before clearing bills relating to capital grants, central ministries generally:
o: require approval only from the State Legislature
audit the State's claims in detail
refer every claim directly to the Reserve Bank of India
137.x: Central ministries scrutinise and audit State claims in detail before clearing bills relating to capital grants.
137.tq: Identify the authority's actual procedural role and reject extreme alternatives such as accepting all claims without verification.

137.s: When bills relating to capital grants are rejected during scrutiny, what is required before they can be processed afresh?
o: A fresh agreement with the Singapore consortium
137.x: Rejected bills require fresh mother sanctions before they can be submitted and processed again.

137.s: The value of bills rejected during a year-end rush in the capital-grants process was approximately:

137.tq: Use the exact figure and distinguish it from nearby altered numerical values.

137.s: Which of the following demands was associated with the CPI(M) in the debate on the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Three separate capitals outside the original capital region
A joint capital arrangement with Telangana
A single-phase capital within the original 29 villages
A capital restricted exclusively to the coastal districts
137.x: The CPI(M) asked for a single-phase capital within the original 29 villages.
137.tq: Match the political demand with its specific geographical and implementation condition.

137.s: Why has reliance on loans instead of grants for capital development been criticised?
o: It prevents all private investment in the capital
It transfers the entire capital expenditure to local governments
It increases repayment burdens and may crowd out welfare and development spending
It eliminates the need for utilisation certificates and audits
137.x: Borrowing instead of receiving grants adds repayment obligations and can reduce the fiscal space available for welfare and development expenditure.
137.tq: Apply the fiscal-consequence chain: borrowing creates repayment obligations and can displace other spending.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the CII Partnership Summit held in November 2025:
1. It brought investment commitments of Rs 45,589 crore for Amaravati.
2. These commitments were associated with about 72,000 jobs.
3. Fifteen banks broke ground in the capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct: the summit brought commitments of Rs 45,589 crore, was associated with about 72,000 jobs, and saw 15 banks break ground in Amaravati.
137.tq: Verify each numerical and event detail before selecting the comprehensive combination.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project — JICA
AP Irrigation and Livelihood Project Phase-II — JICA
South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme — World Bank

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding externally aided projects in Andhra Pradesh:
1. APIIATP is funded by the World Bank.
2. SAPAP is supported by UNDP.
3. The Green Energy Corridor Phase-I is supported by KfW of Germany.

138.x: All three statements are correct. APIIATP is a World Bank project, SAPAP is supported by UNDP, and Green Energy Corridor Phase-I is funded by KfW.

138.s: AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project is associated with which of the following objectives and coverage?
o: Repair of 850 km of major district roads in 13 districts
Industrial development across three corridors covering 33,000 acres
Urban water supply in 123 urban local bodies
Climate resilience and productivity in 565 minor-tank villages across 22 districts
138.x: APIIATP focuses on climate resilience and productivity in 565 minor-tank villages spread across 22 districts.
138.tq: Match the project with its distinctive coverage figures and objective.

138.x: APIIATP concluded on 31 October 2025.
138.tq: Use the exact completion date rather than confusing it with other project timelines.

With reference to APILIP-II, consider the following statements:
1. It covers 21 districts.
2. It was extended by three years.
3. Its extended period is from 2026–27 to 2028–29.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: APILIP-II covers 21 districts and was extended for three years, covering 2026–27 to 2028–29.
138.tq: Combine coverage, duration and date-range facts in a coded statement question.

138.s: The AP Climate Resilient Zero Budget Natural Farming Project received which amount under externally aided heads in the Union Budget 2026–27?
138.x: The project received ₹155.32 crore under externally aided heads in the Union Budget 2026–27.
138.tq: Test the exact budget allocation using closely spaced numerical options.

138.s: How much special assistance was fast-tracked for Amaravati works?
138.x: Special assistance of ₹15,000 crore was fast-tracked for Amaravati works.
138.tq: Test a headline financial figure with ascending numerical options.

138.s: The Union Budget 2026–27 provided how much through IBRD for the Amaravati Integrated Urban Development Programme?
138.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹432.09 crore through IBRD for the Amaravati Integrated Urban Development Programme.
138.tq: Distinguish a specific budget allocation from the larger special-assistance amount.

138.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Amaravati capital works is correct?
o: A World Bank–KfW delegation reviewed the works on 11 April 2026.
An ADB–JICA delegation reviewed the works on 11 May 2026.
An AIIB–NDB delegation reviewed the works on 12 May 2026.
A World Bank–ADB delegation reviewed APCRDA’s capital works on 11 May 2026.
138.x: A World Bank–ADB delegation reviewed APCRDA’s capital works on 11 May 2026.
138.tq: Discriminate between similar agencies and closely related dates.

o: AP Irrigation and Livelihood Project Phase-II

138.tq: Find the one World Bank project among projects supported by different agencies.

138.s: The World Bank-funded AP Road Sector Project provides for:
o: Construction of 800 km of urban roads in 123 ULBs
Repair and strengthening of 850 km of major district roads and State highways
Development of 1,243 km of rural roads under NDB assistance
Construction of 539.45 km of State highways under JICA assistance
138.x: The AP Road Sector Project covers repair and strengthening of 850 km of major district roads and State highways and is climate-resilient.
138.tq: Separate road projects by agency, road category and exact length.

138.s: The AP Disaster Recovery Project was taken up after:
138.x: The AP Disaster Recovery Project was taken up after Cyclone Hudhud in 2014.
138.tq: Link the recovery project with the correct disaster and year.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC):
1. It extends for approximately 800 km.
2. It forms part of the East Coast Economic Corridor.
3. It is linked with Act East and Make in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: VCIC is approximately 800 km long, forms part of the East Coast Economic Corridor, and is linked with Act East and Make in India.
138.tq: Use a three-statement combination to test identity, regional linkage and policy linkage.

138.s: Which of the following sets consists of the nodes of the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor mentioned in the project description?
138.x: The three identified VCIC nodes are Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy.
138.tq: Test the exact membership of a named project list.

138.s: The planned investment in VCIC was backed by an ADB loan of approximately:
138.x: The planned ₹5,000 crore investment was backed by an ADB loan of ₹3,300 crore in two tranches.
138.tq: Distinguish the planned investment from the external loan amount.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (VCIC loan component)
 a. Policy-based loan
 b. Project loan
 c. Programme total
 d. GoAP share in project loan

List-II (Amount or share)
 i. $840 million
 ii. 30 per cent or $215 million
 iii. $125 million
 iv. 70 per cent ADB financing

Select the correct answer using the code below.
138.x: The policy-based loan is $125 million, the project loan has 70% ADB financing, the programme total is $840 million, and the GoAP share is 30% or $215 million.

138.s: Which one of the following statements about the VCIC loan structure is NOT correct?
o: The policy-based loan was fully financed by ADB.
The policy-based loan amounted to $125 million.
The project loan had 70 per cent ADB financing and 30 per cent GoAP financing.
The GoAP contribution to the project loan was $125 million.

138.tq: Use a swapped financial figure to identify the NOT correct statement.

With reference to VCIC power transmission, consider the following statements:

2. A sanction of ₹694.90 crore was made for two Tranche-I packages.

138.x: All three statements correctly describe the VCIC power transmission project: its 2018 start, sanction for two packages and expenditure status.

138.s: Which organisation runs the VCIC, CBIC and HBIC corridors with support from ADB and NICDIT?
138.x: APIIC runs the VCIC, CBIC and HBIC corridors with support from ADB and NICDIT.

138.x: The NDB-to-State financing ratio for the road projects is 70:30.

NDB — AP Roads and Bridges Reconstruction and rural connectivity roads
KfW — AP Rural Inclusive Growth Project

138.x: The Green Energy Corridor involved ₹1,379.75 crore and eight packages.

Completed only in its transmission component

B. Finance Commission grants

138.x: The criticism is that VCIC progress remains slow; the project nevertheless has ADB and NICDIT support and ongoing implementation structures.
138.tq: Choose the precise criticism without extending it into an unsupported conclusion.

139.s: Under the backward districts package for Andhra Pradesh, what amount was provided per district per year?
139.x: The package provided Rs 50 crore per district per year.
139.tq: Use the exact figure and reject nearby amount traps.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the backward districts package of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It covered seven districts.
2. Four districts were from Rayalaseema.
3. Three districts were from North Coastal Andhra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. The package covered seven districts—four in Rayalaseema and three in North Coastal Andhra.
139.tq: Split the total into its regional components before selecting the coded option.

139.s: Which one of the following sets contains only the Rayalaseema districts covered under the backward districts package?
o: YSR Kadapa, Srikakulam, Anantapur and Vizianagaram
Anantapur, Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Chittoor
139.x: The four Rayalaseema districts in the package were Anantapur, Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Chittoor.
139.tq: Identify the regional grouping rather than relying only on the total number.

139.s: The total annual allocation under the backward districts package for the seven districts was approximately:
139.x: At Rs 50 crore per district for seven districts, the annual allocation was Rs 350 crore.
139.tq: Apply the simple multiplication of the per-district amount by the number of districts.

139.s: The Centre decided to continue support for Andhra Pradesh's backward districts. This decision relates primarily to which of the following?
o: Replacement of tax incentives by a corporate tax holiday
Transfer of all irrigation powers to the districts
Abolition of the special development package
Continuation of the backward districts package
139.x: The Centre decided to continue its support for Andhra Pradesh's backward districts under the package.
139.tq: Match the policy decision with its immediate subject.

139.s: The special packages for backward districts in Andhra Pradesh were modelled on which of the following?
o: Green Revolution and Golden Quadrilateral packages
Coastal Regulation and Smart Cities packages
139.x: The backward-district package drew upon the KBK (Koraput-Bolangir-Kalahandi) package of Odisha and the Bundelkhand special package.
139.tq: Expand the abbreviation and identify the paired models.

139.s: Which of the following best describes the adequacy issue concerning the backward districts package?
o: Initial allocations were made, but disbursements stalled.
Only North Coastal districts received the allocation.
The entire amount was released in the first year.
No allocation was ever made for the districts.
139.x: Initial allocations were made, but stalled disbursements slowed regional development.
139.tq: Distinguish between sanction or allocation and actual release.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Sections 46(2) and 46(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. They provide for appropriate grants by the Centre.
2. They provide for a special development package.
3. They specify particular incentives for Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Sections 46(2) and 46(3) provide for appropriate grants and a special development package, with particular incentives for Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
139.tq: Check whether all three provisions belong to the same statutory subsection.

139.s: The resource-gap grant provided to Andhra Pradesh for 2014–15 was:
139.x: The resource-gap grant for 2014–15 was Rs 3,979.50 crore.
139.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced numerical options.

139.s: Which of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh's position regarding transfers after bifurcation?
o: The transfers exceeded all Finance Commission recommendations and the Prime Minister's assurances.
The transfers fell short of the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commission recommendations and the Prime Minister's assurances in the Rajya Sabha.
The transfers were limited only because the Thirteenth Finance Commission award was cancelled.
The State did not raise any issue concerning the adequacy of transfers.
139.x: Andhra Pradesh maintained that the transfers fell short of the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commission recommendations and the Prime Minister's assurances in the Rajya Sabha.
139.tq: Test the comparison between promised or recommended transfers and actual transfers.

139.s: Section 94(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 envisages fiscal measures, including tax incentives, primarily to:
o: Determine the population ratio for grants
139.x: Section 94(1) directs the Centre to take fiscal measures, including tax incentives, to promote industrialisation.
139.tq: Link the statutory provision with its stated economic objective.

139.s: Which combination correctly describes the tax incentives notified in 2015 for eligible new units?
139.x: The notified incentives were an additional depreciation of 35% and an investment allowance of 15%.
139.tq: Keep the two percentages attached to their correct incentive names.

139.s: The tax incentives notified in 2015 applied to units set up during which period?
139.x: The incentives applied to units established between 1 April 2015 and 31 March 2020.
139.tq: Read both endpoints of the eligibility period; the starting year alone is insufficient.

139.s: The tax incentives under Section 94(1) were applicable to eligible units established in:
o: Only the capital region of Andhra Pradesh
The notified backward districts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
All districts of India without regional restriction
Only the coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh
139.x: The incentives applied to units set up in the notified backward districts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
139.tq: Use the exact geographical coverage instead of the broader State name.

139.s: Which of the following was criticised as falling short of the comprehensive package sought by Andhra Pradesh?
o: The creation of the KBK package
The division of the Thirteenth Finance Commission award
139.x: The tax incentives were criticised as insufficient compared with the comprehensive package sought by Andhra Pradesh.
139.tq: Find the policy measure that was considered inadequate rather than the statutory provision itself.

139.s: Which statement is correct regarding the proposed corporate tax holiday and Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh?
o: The corporate tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed under GST, and SCS was denied.
The corporate tax holiday was replaced by a permanent 90% central share of CSS.
SCS was granted, but the tax incentives were withdrawn before 2015.
The promised 10-year corporate tax holiday was implemented immediately and SCS was granted.
139.x: The promised 10-year corporate tax holiday was delayed, diluted or subsumed under GST, while Special Category Status, including its 90% central share of CSS and tax exemptions, was denied.
139.tq: Separate the promised benefit from the benefit actually received.

139.s: How many districts presently constitute Rayalaseema in the classification stated for its development issues?
139.x: Rayalaseema comprises eight districts: Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Satya Sai, YSR, Annamayya, Tirupati and Chittoor.
139.tq: Count the complete district list rather than confusing it with the four package districts.

139.s: Rayalaseema has a low population density primarily because of:
o: Absence of Eastern Ghats hill tracts
139.x: Recurring droughts and famines are identified as major reasons for Rayalaseema's low population density.
139.tq: Match the regional demographic feature with its stated cause.

139.s: Which district has the highest groundwater withdrawal among the two districts specified?
139.x: Sri Sathya Sai has the higher specified groundwater withdrawal at 57.44%, compared with Chittoor at 55.16%.
139.tq: Compare both the district name and the associated percentage.

139.s: The Godavari–Penna link, Phase I, is intended to transfer:
o: 73 TMC of Godavari flood water to the Pennar through a five-stage lift
71.5 TMC of Krishna water through a three-stage lift
3.283 lakh acres of irrigation water from the Krishna to Gundlakamma
24.20 TMC of Pennar water to the Godavari through a two-stage lift
139.x: Phase I of the Godavari–Penna link proposes to carry 73 TMC of Godavari flood water to the Pennar through a five-stage lift.
139.tq: Keep the source river, destination river, quantity and lift stages together.

139.s: Which project has been proposed to carry surplus Godavari water to Rayalaseema?
139.x: The Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link has been proposed to carry surplus Godavari water to Rayalaseema.
139.tq: Identify the project by its stated source, destination and purpose.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the Veligonda project:
1. It involves transfer from Krishna to Gundlakamma.
2. It was stated to be 71.5% complete.
3. Rs 768 crore was paid to 6,206 displaced families.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct regarding the Veligonda project and its rehabilitation payments.
139.tq: Verify the project route, completion percentage and rehabilitation figure independently.

139.s: Phase II of the Veligonda project is intended to add irrigation potential of:
139.x: Phase II of Veligonda is intended to add 3.283 lakh acres.
139.tq: Distinguish the irrigation-area figure from the project's completion percentage.

139.s: Handri Neeva Sujala Sravanthi is associated with the seasonal use of:
139.x: Handri Neeva Sujala Sravanthi is associated with the seasonal use of 24.20 TMC.
139.tq: Match the project name with its specific water quantity.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Rayalaseema's horticulture and micro-irrigation position:
1. It accounts for 43% of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture area.
2. It accounts for 52% of the State's horticulture output.
3. It accounts for 71% of the State's micro-irrigation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Rayalaseema accounts for 43% of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture area, 52% of its output and 71% of its micro-irrigation.
139.tq: Treat each percentage as a separate statement and check all three shares.

139.s: Which of the following correctly describes the distribution of districts in India's top ten for micro-irrigation?
o: Six Andhra Pradesh districts, including five from Rayalaseema and Prakasam
Six Andhra Pradesh districts, including all four package districts and two coastal districts
Seven Andhra Pradesh districts, all from North Coastal Andhra
Five Andhra Pradesh districts, all from Rayalaseema
139.x: Six Andhra Pradesh districts are among India's top ten for micro-irrigation: five from Rayalaseema and Prakasam.
139.tq: Check both the total count and the regional composition.

139.s: Which of the following is identified as a consequence of industrial backwardness in Rayalaseema?
o: Rapid urbanisation and reduced drought frequency
Expansion of coastal manufacturing into every district
139.x: Rayalaseema lacks anchor industries, and this contributes to distress migration and an agrarian crisis.
139.tq: Trace the stated chain from industrial imbalance to social and agrarian outcomes.

139.s: The Sri Bagh Pact, which promised Rayalaseema priority in irrigation for ten years, was concluded on:
139.x: The Sri Bagh Pact was concluded on 16 November 1937 and promised Rayalaseema irrigation priority for ten years.
139.tq: Use the exact historical date attached to the regional development promise.

139.s: How many districts constitute Uttarandhra, also referred to as Kalinga Andhra, in the classification stated for its backwardness?
139.x: Uttarandhra or Kalinga Andhra comprises six districts.
139.tq: Count the named districts and distinguish the total from Rayalaseema's total.

139.s: Which of the following is the correct list of districts of Uttarandhra?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam
Alluri Sitharama Raju, Eluru, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Srikakulam
Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Prakasam, Nellore, Tirupati and Chittoor
Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Satya Sai, YSR and Chittoor
139.x: The six Uttarandhra districts are Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam.
139.tq: Use elimination by checking every district in the regional list.

139.s: Which of the following pairs of tribal communities and areas is correctly matched?
o: Kotia and Porja — coastal Krishna delta
Khond and Jatapu — Bhogapuram urban area
139.x: Savara and Jatapu communities are associated with the Srikakulam side. Gadaba, Bagata, Kotia, Porja and Khond are associated with the Araku/Visakhapatnam agency.
139.tq: Start with the sure geographical pair and reject misplaced tribal groups.

139.s: The tribal belt of Uttarandhra primarily comprises the:
139.x: The tribal belt of Uttarandhra lies in the Eastern Ghats hill tracts.
139.tq: Match the regional tribal belt with its physical setting.

139.s: Which district has the lowest literacy among the indicators specified for Uttarandhra?
139.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district has the lowest literacy among the specified indicators, at 44.67%.
139.tq: Link the lowest indicator with the correct district and percentage.

139.s: The new Polavaram district, with headquarters at Rampachodavaram, was reported to have which combination of indicators?
o: Lowest literacy of 44.67% and density of 54
Lowest urbanisation of 2.84% and density of 54
139.x: The new Polavaram district, headquartered at Rampachodavaram, was reported to have urbanisation of 2.84% and population density of 54, both the lowest among the specified indicators.
139.tq: Keep the two indicators attached to the correct district and distinguish density from percentage.

139.s: The lack of anchor industries in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram is associated with:
o: A decline in horticultural output across Rayalaseema
139.x: The absence of anchor industries in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram contributes to distress migration.
139.tq: Connect the industrial gap with its stated migration outcome.

139.s: Vamsadhara Phase-II was reported to be approximately:
139.x: Vamsadhara Phase-II was reported to be 93.5% complete.
139.tq: Distinguish this completion percentage from the separate Veligonda figure.

139.s: Which of the following is the planned link project associated with the Thotapalli barrage?
139.x: The planned project is the Nagavali–Suvarnamukhi–Vegavathi–Champavathi link via the Thotapalli barrage.
139.tq: Recall the full sequence of rivers in the named link project.

139.s: Bhogapuram airport is located in which district, with commercial operations targeted for June 2026?
139.x: Bhogapuram airport is located in Vizianagaram district, and commercial operations were targeted for June 2026.
139.tq: Match the infrastructure project with its district and stated timeline.

139.s: Which one of the following statements regarding revenue deficit grants is correct?
o: They are released continuously to all States by every Finance Commission.
They were discontinued immediately after the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
They were released for some years but were subsequently stopped.
They are released only to States having Special Category Status.
139.x: Revenue deficit grants were released for some years and were subsequently stopped. The discontinuation was not linked to the 101st Constitutional Amendment or restricted to Special Category States.
139.tq: Use the precise time sequence and reject extreme claims such as continuously and immediately.

139.s: The 16th Finance Commission has discontinued revenue deficit grants for:
o: States affected by GST implementation alone
139.x: The 16th Finance Commission has discontinued revenue deficit grants for all States.
139.tq: Who or what is covered? Split the options by their scope before choosing.

139.s: Andhra Pradesh has stated that its revenue loss after bifurcation was up to approximately:
139.x: Andhra Pradesh has claimed that it lost revenue of up to Rs 38,000 crore.
139.tq: Check the scale and number of zeroes carefully in numerical options.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh and the 15th Finance Commission grants:
1. Andhra Pradesh had drawn the grants for 2024-25 and 2025-26 in advance.
2. The advance drawal was related to the 15th Finance Commission grants.
3. The grants were drawn only for the financial year 2023-24.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Andhra Pradesh had drawn 15th Finance Commission grants for 2024-25 and 2025-26 in advance. Statement 3 is false because 2023-24 is not the period identified.
139.tq: Separate the correct grant authority and years from the deliberately shifted year.

139.s: With reference to the revised cost estimate of the Polavaram project, which of the following is correct?
o: Only the State caps its liability at old price levels.
The Centre accepts liability at all revised price levels without limitation.
The dispute concerns only GST compensation and not project costs.
The Centre caps its liability at old price levels, while rehabilitation and resettlement costs remain disputed.
139.x: The Centre caps its liability for the Polavaram revised cost estimate at old price levels, and rehabilitation and resettlement costs are also disputed.
139.tq: Identify the authority attached to the power or liability and watch for the reversed subject.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Polavaram revised cost estimate — dispute over Centre's liability and R&R costs
BRGF releases — permanently released without interruption
SNA matching rules — automatic transfer of all unspent central funds
GST compensation — introduced by the 16th Finance Commission
139.x: The Polavaram issue involves the Centre's liability at old price levels and disputed rehabilitation and resettlement costs. The other pairs misstate the status or origin of the relevant funds.
139.tq: Start from the sure project-dispute pair and eliminate swapped institutions or opposite meanings.

139.s: Central funds may lapse under which of the following circumstances?
o: When the Polavaram estimate is revised upward
When the State receives GST compensation
When the State does not meet SNA matching requirements
When the 16th Finance Commission submits its report
139.x: Central funds can lapse under State Nodal Account matching rules when the required matching conditions are not fulfilled.
139.tq: Apply the funding rule to the situation that directly triggers lapse of funds.

139.s: The constitutional amendment that provided compensation to States for GST revenue loss was the:
139.x: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 provided for compensation to States for revenue loss arising from GST implementation.
139.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its exact amendment number and year.

139.s: What was the principal objective of the Backward Region Grant Fund (BRGF)?
o: To replace all State industrial policies
To compensate States exclusively for GST revenue loss
139.x: BRGF was a Central scheme intended to redress regional imbalances.
139.tq: Identify the scheme objective and reject options that substitute a different funding purpose.

139.s: BRGF was launched in which financial year?
139.x: The Backward Region Grant Fund was launched in 2006-07.
139.tq: Use the exact launch year rather than the later year associated with delinking.

139.s: BRGF was delinked from central support from:
139.x: BRGF was delinked from central support from 2015-16.
139.tq: Distinguish the scheme's launch year from the year of delinking.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the Backward Region Grant Fund:
1. It was a Central scheme.
2. It was intended to address regional imbalances.
3. It is presently a functioning Central scheme with continuing releases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: BRGF was a Central scheme for redressing regional imbalances, but it is now defunct. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
139.tq: Find the one false statement by testing the present-status claim against the scheme's history.

139.s: Which of the following best describes the present approach after BRGF became defunct?
o: All regional development is funded through the discontinued BRGF.
States use their own incentive policies, including capital subsidies and power-tariff concessions.
Only GST compensation is used for regional development.
States have abandoned industrial incentives in backward areas.
139.x: After BRGF became defunct, States use their own incentive policies. Andhra Pradesh's industrial policy includes capital subsidies and power-tariff concessions.
139.tq: Apply the transition from a discontinued Central scheme to the State-level policy response.

139.s: The Aspirational Districts Programme is regarded as the successor approach to BRGF and was associated with:
139.x: The Aspirational Districts Programme, associated with NITI Aayog, was launched as the successor approach in January 2018.
139.tq: Pair the successor programme with the correct institution and date.

139.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the features associated with the Aspirational Districts Programme?
139.x: The three stated themes of the Aspirational Districts Programme are Convergence, Collaboration and Competition. Compensation is not one of them.
139.tq: Find the odd policy term among three closely associated themes.

139.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Visakhapatnam Economic Region and the Tirupati Economic Region?
o: Only the Tirupati Economic Region has a growth plan.
The Visakhapatnam Economic Region is a single-district plan, whereas Tirupati has no regional plan.
Both provide each region with its own growth plan.
Both are components of the discontinued BRGF.
139.x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region and the Tirupati Economic Region are intended to give their respective regions their own growth plans.
139.tq: Compare the common function of the two named regional economic arrangements.

139.s: The criticism that backward-district funds were inadequate was based, among other things, on which comparison?
o: Rs 50 crore per district was minor compared with the loss of Hyderabad's revenue.
Rs 50 crore per district exceeded the revenue lost from Hyderabad.
The funds were intended only for GST compensation.
The funds were larger than the total investment tracked for North Andhra and Rayalaseema.
139.x: The criticism held that Rs 50 crore per district was small when compared with the revenue lost from Hyderabad. Releases were also criticised as irregular.
139.tq: Compare the scale of the grant with the much larger benchmark used in the criticism.

139.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding the release of backward-district funds in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The releases were regular and unlimited.
The releases were made only through GST compensation.
139.x: The release of backward-district funds was criticised as irregular, in addition to the criticism that the amount was small.
139.tq: Reject absolute alternatives and identify the precise criticism of implementation.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the Karnataka regional-imbalance report of 2026:
1. It was prepared by a committee headed by M. Govinda Rao.
2. It classified 177 of 236 taluks as backward.
3. It serves as a benchmark for studying intra-state gaps in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: The 2026 Karnataka report associated with the M. Govinda Rao committee classified 177 out of 236 taluks as backward and is used as a benchmark for studying Andhra Pradesh's intra-state disparities.
139.tq: Combine authorship, numerical composition and comparative relevance in one coded question.

140.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, within what period were the Indian Railways required to examine establishing a new railway zone in the successor State of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Three months from the appointed day
Two years from the appointed day
One year from the appointed day
Six months from the appointed day
140.x: The Act required the Indian Railways to examine establishing a new railway zone in Andhra Pradesh within six months from the appointed day.
140.tq: Fix the exact statutory time limit instead of confusing examination with establishment.

140.s: Which one of the following most accurately describes the obligation relating to the proposed railway zone in Andhra Pradesh under the Thirteenth Schedule?
o: Railways was required to examine establishing the zone and take an expeditious decision
The State Government was authorised to establish the zone independently
The Union Cabinet was required to establish the zone through a constitutional amendment
Railways was required to establish the zone within six months
140.x: The statutory wording created a feasibility-oriented obligation to examine the establishment of a zone and take an expeditious decision; it did not itself establish the zone.
140.tq: Distinguish the legally precise word 'examine' from the stronger word 'establish'.

140.s: The wording relating to the proposed railway zone in Andhra Pradesh followed the same pattern as the provisions concerning which of the following?
o: Metro rail, shipyard and fertilizer plant
Power plant, textile park and industrial corridor
Rail Coach Factory, inland waterways and ports
140.x: The railway-zone provision, like the provisions for a steel plant, refinery and airport, required examination and an expeditious decision rather than directly mandating establishment.
140.tq: Use the associated-list recall method for provisions carrying the same wording pattern.

140.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Thirteenth Schedule also asks Railways to examine a Rail Coach Factory for Telangana.
2. The Rail Coach Factory provision is the same as the new railway-zone provision for Andhra Pradesh.
3. The railway-zone provision concerns the successor State of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Rail Coach Factory provision for Telangana must not be confused with the railway-zone provision for Andhra Pradesh.
140.tq: Separate two similar Thirteenth Schedule provisions by their State and subject.

140.s: Railways is a Union subject under which entry of the Union List?
140.x: Railways falls under Entry 22 of List I, the Union List.
140.tq: Recall the exact constitutional entry associated with the subject.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the creation of a railway zone is correct?
o: A railway zone is created by an executive decision and gazette notification of the Ministry of Railways
A railway zone is created by the Finance Commission through an annual budget resolution
A railway zone is created automatically when a State is reorganised
A railway zone can be created only by an Act of the State Legislature
140.x: Creation of a railway zone is an executive decision followed by a gazette notification of the Ministry of Railways.
140.tq: Ask which authority would perform the administrative act rather than the legislative one.

140.s: South Coast Railway was announced in which year and was proposed to be carved out of which two railway zones?
o: 2019; South Central Railway and East Coast Railway
2021; East Coast Railway and Central Railway
2020; South Central Railway and Southern Railway
2018; East Coast Railway and North Central Railway
140.x: South Coast Railway was announced in 2019 in the Rail Budget and was to be carved out of South Central Railway and East Coast Railway.
140.tq: Combine the announcement year with the two parent zones without swapping neighbouring railway zones.

140.s: The South Coast Railway zone was officially notified in the Gazette on:
140.x: The Gazette notification establishing South Coast Railway was issued on 4 May 2026.
140.tq: Distinguish the notification date from the later date of full operationalisation.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about South Coast Railway:
1. Its headquarters is at Visakhapatnam.
2. Its area includes Andhra Pradesh and parts of Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu.
3. Sandeep Mathur is its General Manager.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: All three statements are correct: the headquarters is Visakhapatnam, the zone covers the stated States and Sandeep Mathur is the General Manager.
140.tq: Test a compact cluster of administrative identity, territorial coverage and leadership facts.

140.s: With effect from 1 June 2026, the Indian Railways logo was revised to contain:
140.x: The Indian Railways logo was revised from 17 stars to 18 stars with effect from 1 June 2026.
140.tq: Use the before-and-after numerical comparison rather than the final figure alone.

140.s: After the creation of South Coast Railway, which statement about South Central Railway is correct?
o: It retained all six divisions and covered 3,584 km
It was left with two divisions—Secunderabad and Hyderabad—and covered 3,584 km
It was left with three divisions—Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Nanded—and still covered 3,584 km
It was left with four divisions—Secunderabad, Hyderabad, Nanded and Vijayawada—and covered 2,584 km
140.x: South Central Railway was reduced from six to three divisions—Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Nanded—but continued to cover 3,584 km.
140.tq: Check both the change in division count and the unchanged route-length figure.

140.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the number of railway zones in India and Konkan Railway?
o: Some lists show 19 by counting Konkan Railway as a separate zone
Konkan Railway has its headquarters at Visakhapatnam
Konkan Railway is a public sector undertaking and not a railway zone
The number of railway zones is 18
140.x: Konkan Railway is not a railway zone; it is KRCL, a PSU headquartered at Navi Mumbai—CBD Belapur. Therefore, its headquarters is not Visakhapatnam.
140.tq: Find the wrong location in an otherwise familiar comparison between zones and a railway PSU.

140.s: Konkan Railway Corporation Limited, which is not counted as a railway zone, was established on:
140.x: Konkan Railway Corporation Limited was established on 26 January 1998 and has its headquarters at Navi Mumbai—CBD Belapur.
140.tq: Recall the exact date attached to the non-zone railway organisation.

140.s: What was the principal administrative fate of the Waltair division after the formation of South Coast Railway?
o: Its Andhra part became Visakhapatnam division of South Coast Railway and the rest became Rayagada division of East Coast Railway
It was abolished without creating any successor division
It remained wholly under East Coast Railway
It was transferred wholly to South Central Railway as Guntakal division
140.x: Waltair was split: its Andhra portion became the truncated Visakhapatnam division of South Coast Railway, while the remaining portion went to East Coast Railway as the new Rayagada division.
140.tq: Track the split of one old division into two new administrative units.

140.s: The Kottavalasa–Kirandul line became a major point of dispute mainly because it was regarded as:
o: The principal suburban line of Vijayawada
The only passenger line of Guntakal division
The headquarters route of South Central Railway
The revenue lifeline of Waltair division
140.x: The Kottavalasa–Kirandul line was described as the revenue lifeline of Waltair division and therefore became the central flashpoint in the reorganisation dispute.
140.tq: Identify the functional significance of the disputed asset before considering competing claims.

140.s: Which of the following correctly states the positions concerning the Kottavalasa–Kirandul line?
o: Andhra Pradesh claimed the entire line, while the Centre favoured moving it to Vijayawada
Odisha claimed the entire line, while the Centre favoured moving the entire line to Rayagada
Odisha offered the entire line to South Coast Railway, while Andhra Pradesh opposed any transfer
Both Odisha and Andhra Pradesh agreed that the line should remain wholly with Waltair
140.x: Odisha claimed the entire K-K line, and the Centre favoured shifting the entire line to the Rayagada division.
140.tq: Separate the positions of the claimant State and the Union Government instead of treating them as identical.

140.s: Which of the following represents Andhra Pradesh's position regarding the Kottavalasa–Kirandul line?
o: It offered only the Odisha stretches—Koraput–Kirandul, Kuneru–Theruvali and Koraput–Rayagada
It offered only the Vijayawada–Guntakal stretch
It offered the entire line to Odisha without any reservation
It demanded that the entire line be transferred to Telangana
140.x: Andhra Pradesh leaders offered only the Odisha stretches of the line, namely Koraput–Kirandul, Kuneru–Theruvali and Koraput–Rayagada.
140.tq: Test the exact components of a limited offer rather than the broader claim over the whole line.

140.s: Andhra Pradesh leaders argued that Waltair division had earned more revenue than which combination of divisions?
140.x: The Andhra Pradesh position was that Waltair had earned more than Vijayawada, Guntur and Guntakal combined.
140.tq: Use the revenue comparison to distinguish the disputed division from the three divisions named alongside it.

140.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. South Coast Railway becomes fully operational
B. South Coast Railway is announced
C. Gazette notification of South Coast Railway
D. The Act requires Railways to examine a new zone
140.x: The correct sequence is 2014 statutory provision, 2019 announcement, 4 May 2026 Gazette notification and 1 June 2026 full operationalisation.
140.tq: Fix the earliest statutory event first, then place announcement, notification and operation.

140.s: Which one of the following statements about the status of South Coast Railway before its Gazette notification is correct?
o: The General Manager appointed in March 2026 had full statutory powers immediately
The General Manager appointed in March 2026 had no powers without the Gazette notification
The zone's headquarters had already been completed in February 2026
The zone was fully operational in March 2026 despite the absence of notification
140.x: Although a General Manager was appointed in March 2026, the office had no powers until the Gazette notification was issued.
140.tq: Apply the difference between an appointment and the legal operational authority created by notification.

140.s: Which of the following correctly describes the April 2026 administrative arrangements for South Coast Railway?
o: Land-handover disputes were resolved, a temporary office was functioning at Siripuram with about 100 staff, and more than 1,300 posts were being filled
Land disputes remained unresolved, and all staff were shifted to Rayagada
The permanent headquarters at Mudasarlova began functioning with 1,300 staff
The temporary office was established at Vijayawada with 526 staff
140.x: In April 2026, land-handover disputes for the Visakhapatnam headquarters were resolved; a temporary office at Siripuram had about 100 staff and over 1,300 posts were being filled.
140.tq: Combine location, staffing and administrative progress while rejecting the premature permanent-office claim.

140.s: The proposed zonal headquarters of South Coast Railway at Mudasarlova, Visakhapatnam, is estimated to cost:
140.x: The proposed zonal headquarters at Mudasarlova, Visakhapatnam, is a ₹184-crore project; meanwhile, the zone works from a VMRDA building.
140.tq: Recall the exact project cost and distinguish the proposed headquarters from the temporary office.

140.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the staffing position mentioned for South Coast Railway headquarters and Rayagada division?
o: 183 of 191 headquarters posts and 47 of 526 Rayagada posts were filled
All 526 headquarters posts and 191 Rayagada posts were filled
526 of 183 headquarters posts and 191 of 47 Rayagada posts were filled
183 of 526 headquarters posts and 47 of 191 Rayagada posts were filled
140.x: Only 183 of 526 headquarters posts and 47 of 191 Rayagada posts had been filled. A Railway Board note attributed the gap to poor cooperation from existing zones.
140.tq: Read numerator and sanctioned-post denominator carefully in both staffing figures.

140.s: The Railway Board note of 14 May 2026 attributed the staffing gap in the new railway zone mainly to:
o: The cancellation of the Gazette notification
Poor cooperation from existing railway zones
140.x: The Railway Board note blamed poor cooperation from existing zones for the staffing gap.
140.tq: Match the administrative problem with the stated institutional cause.

140.s: In the first four months, the approximate gross originating revenue of Vijayawada division was:
