140.x: Vijayawada division recorded approximately ₹4,894 crore in gross originating revenue during its first four months.
140.tq: Distinguish the reported revenue figure from nearby altered figures.

140.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with the approved remodelling of Visakhapatnam station yard?
o: ₹400 crore and eight new platforms, making a total of sixteen
₹300 crore and six new platforms, making a total of fourteen
₹100 crore and four new platforms, making a total of ten
₹200 crore and five new platforms, making a total of twelve
140.x: A ₹300-crore remodelling project was approved for Visakhapatnam station yard, involving six new platforms and taking the total to 14.
140.tq: Link the project cost with both platform additions and the final platform count.

140.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the impact of South Coast Railway on East Coast Railway and the Kottavalasa–Kirandul line?
o: East Coast Railway is dissolved after the creation of South Coast Railway
East Coast Railway loses both the Andhra part of Waltair and all K-K line revenue
East Coast Railway gains the Andhra part of Waltair and transfers Rayagada to South Central Railway
East Coast Railway loses the Andhra part of Waltair but retains the K-K line revenue through Rayagada division
140.x: East Coast Railway loses the Andhra part of Waltair, but it retains the K-K line revenue through the new Rayagada division.
140.tq: Track what is transferred and what revenue source is retained by the existing zone.

140.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the positions of the neighbouring States and railway zones:
1. Odisha claimed the entire Kottavalasa–Kirandul line.
2. Andhra Pradesh objected that backward Uttarandhra areas would go to Rayagada.
3. South Central Railway was reduced to three divisions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: All three statements are correct. Odisha claimed the entire K-K line, Andhra Pradesh raised concerns regarding backward Uttarandhra areas, and SCR shrank to three divisions.
140.tq: Combine the positions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh with the institutional impact on SCR.

140.s: The establishment of South Coast Railway was described as significant because it was:
o: A demand pressed for over four decades and a statutory promise made in 2014, but notified only after a decade
A constitutional obligation implemented within six months of bifurcation
A demand raised for the first time in 2019 and implemented immediately
A proposal made only after the 2026 Gazette notification
140.x: The demand had been pressed for over four decades, while the statutory promise dated from 2014; the zone was notified only after about a decade.
140.tq: Compare the duration of the demand with the delay between statutory promise and notification.

140.s: Who described the notification of South Coast Railway as a “promise kept”?
o: The General Manager of East Coast Railway
140.x: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu described the notification as a “promise kept”.
140.tq: Match the quoted political statement with the correct office-holder.

140.s: The proposed Amaravati rail link is associated with which of the following projects?
140.x: The proposed Amaravati rail link is the new Errupalem–Namburu broad-gauge line.
140.tq: Identify the project by matching its stated purpose with the correct railway line.

140.s: The approximate length of the proposed Errupalem–Namburu broad-gauge line is:
140.x: The Errupalem–Namburu line is approximately 57 km long.
140.tq: Distinguish the specific project length from nearby railway figures.

140.s: The proposed Amaravati rail link includes a bridge of approximately what length over the Krishna River?
140.x: The project includes an approximately 3 km bridge over the Krishna River.
140.tq: Use the project-specific numerical figure rather than the total line length.

140.s:
Consider the following statements regarding land arrangements for the Amaravati rail link:
1. Farmers of Tadikonda and Mothadaka opted for land pooling.
2. A 100-metre buffer for the railway line was incorporated into the Amaravati Inner Ring Road land pooling.
3. The railway line was planned without any provision in the Inner Ring Road land pooling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: Farmers of Tadikonda and Mothadaka opted for land pooling, and a 100-metre buffer was built into the Amaravati Inner Ring Road land pooling. Statement 3 is false because such a buffer was provided.
140.tq: Find the statement that reverses the stated land-pooling arrangement.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the high-speed rail proposals is correct?
o: The 2026–27 Budget named seven high-speed rail growth connectors, including Hyderabad–Bengaluru, Hyderabad–Chennai and Chennai–Bengaluru.
The 2026–27 Budget named five high-speed rail growth connectors, excluding all southern corridors.
Amaravati–Hyderabad was proposed as a seven-hour high-speed rail journey.
Only Amaravati–Hyderabad was identified as a high-speed rail growth connector.
140.x: The 2026–27 Budget identified seven high-speed rail growth connectors, including the three listed southern corridors. Amaravati–Hyderabad was proposed to be covered in 70 minutes, not seven hours.
140.tq: Separate the complete list-based statement from options that alter the count or travel time.

140.s: Amaravati–Hyderabad high-speed rail connectivity was proposed to cover the distance in approximately:
140.x: The proposed Amaravati–Hyderabad high-speed rail journey was stated as 70 minutes.
140.tq: Recall the exact travel-time figure associated with the proposal.

140.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Railway project)
a. Nadikudi–Srikalahasti
b. Kotipalli–Narsapur
c. Ramayapatnam–Kadapa

a List-II (Description)
i. Dedicated line for a steel plant
ii. Railway line associated with the backward districts of Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore and Chittoor
iii. Railway line referred to as another proposed line in Andhra Pradesh

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
140.x: Nadikudi–Srikalahasti is associated with the four backward districts; Kotipalli–Narsapur is another railway line; and Ramayapatnam–Kadapa has a dedicated line approved for a steel plant.
140.tq: Start from the sure association between the steel plant and the Ramayapatnam–Kadapa line.

140.s: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti railway line has an approximate length of:
140.x: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line is approximately 308 km long.
140.tq: Distinguish the exact route length from nearby numerical distractors.

140.s: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line is particularly associated with improving railway connectivity for which group of districts?
o: Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and East Godavari
Kadapa, Kurnool, Nellore and West Godavari
140.x: The line was intended for the backward districts of Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore and Chittoor.
140.tq: Test the complete district grouping rather than a single district name.

140.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the agency responsible for building the Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line?
140.x: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line was stated to be built by the State.
140.tq: Apply the ‘who is responsible?’ test to distinguish the implementing authority.

140.s:
With reference to railway investment in Andhra Pradesh during 2026–27, consider the following statements:
1. The railway outlay for Andhra Pradesh was ₹10,134 crore.
2. The average railway outlay during 2009–14 was ₹886 crore.
3. The 2026–27 outlay was lower than the average outlay during 2009–14.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: The 2026–27 outlay was ₹10,134 crore, compared with an average of ₹886 crore during 2009–14. Therefore, Statement 3 is false because the later outlay was substantially higher.
140.tq: Compare the two outlay figures and reject the reversed comparison.

140.s: As of 1 April 2026, which one of the following combinations relating to railway projects in Andhra Pradesh was correct?
o: 74 projects, 4,768 km, ₹77,855 crore sanctioned and 1,465 km commissioned
42 projects, 1,465 km, ₹10,134 crore sanctioned and 4,768 km commissioned
42 projects, 4,768 km, ₹77,855 crore sanctioned and 1,465 km commissioned
42 projects, 7,855 km, ₹77,855 crore sanctioned and 1,134 km commissioned
140.x: As of 1 April 2026, 42 projects covering 4,768 km had ₹77,855 crore sanctioned, while 1,465 km had been commissioned.
140.tq: Keep the project count, route length, sanctioned amount and commissioned length in their correct positions.

140.s: What was the status of electrification of the railway network in Andhra Pradesh as stated for 2026?
140.x: The railway network in Andhra Pradesh was stated to be 100% electrified.
140.tq: Test the completion status directly and avoid confusing it with the length commissioned.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Amrit Bharat Stations in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Seventy-four stations in Andhra Pradesh were selected under the programme.
2. Sullurupeta station is near Sriharikota.
3. Sullurupeta station was opened on 22 May 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: All three statements are correct: 74 stations were selected, Sullurupeta is near Sriharikota, and it was opened on 22 May 2025.
140.tq: Verify the count, location and date together before selecting the complete combination.

140.s: The South Coast Railway (SCoR) became India’s 18th railway zone on:
140.x: SCoR became India’s 18th railway zone on 1 June 2026.
140.tq: Distinguish the formation date from the dates associated with Metro Railway and Sullurupeta station.

140.s: Which one of the following was identified as the 17th railway zone before SCoR became the 18th zone?
140.x: Metro Railway, Kolkata, was the 17th zone and dates from 29 December 2010, before SCoR became the 18th zone.
140.tq: Use the first-and-last comparison to identify the immediately preceding zone.

140.s:
Which of the following has been cited as a criticism or issue associated with the creation of the new railway zone in Andhra Pradesh?
1. A decade of delay
2. Ceding of the K-K line and Waltair revenue to Odisha
3. Staff shortages

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: The criticisms included a decade of delay, the ceding of the K-K line and Waltair revenue to Odisha, and staff shortages.
140.tq: Check whether each listed issue belongs to the same criticism cluster before choosing the complete combination.

140.s: A dedicated railway zone in Andhra Pradesh is expected to support the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor primarily by:
o: Increasing passenger fares and reducing industrial traffic
Transferring all railway revenue to Odisha
Replacing electrified railway lines with road transport
Cutting freight costs and improving port connectivity
140.x: The dedicated zone is expected to cut freight costs for the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor and improve port connectivity.
140.tq: Link the institutional reform to its stated economic and logistics outcomes.

140.s: The proposed role of the new railway zone as a “multimodal logistics hub” is most closely connected with which objective?
o: Reducing the number of railway projects in Andhra Pradesh
Integrating freight movement and port connectivity
Shifting all railway administration to Metro Railway, Kolkata
Restricting railway services to passenger traffic
140.x: The multimodal logistics hub concept refers to integrated freight movement and improved connectivity with ports, particularly in relation to the industrial corridor.
140.tq: Interpret the functional meaning of a logistics-hub label from its stated economic context.

141.s:
Under the educational commitments associated with the Thirteenth Schedule, which of the following was NOT included as one of the institutions proposed for Andhra Pradesh?

1. Indian Institute of Technology
2. National Institute of Technology
3. Indian Institute of Management
4. National Institute of Fashion Technology

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: The educational commitments included one each of an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central University, Petroleum University, Agricultural University and IIIT, besides an AIIMS-type hospital, Tribal Universities and NIDM. National Institute of Fashion Technology was not listed.
141.tq: Find the institution outside the specified commitment list.

141.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to higher educational institutions in Andhra Pradesh:

1. IIT Tirupati — Yerpedu
2. IIM Visakhapatnam — Gambheeram
3. NIT Andhra Pradesh — Tadepalligudem
4. IISER Tirupati — Kurnool

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
141.x: IIT Tirupati is at Yerpedu, IIM Visakhapatnam is at Gambheeram and NIT Andhra Pradesh is at Tadepalligudem. IISER Tirupati is also at Yerpedu, not Kurnool.
141.tq: Use location discrimination among closely related institutions.

141.s: IIT Tirupati was established under which legal instrument?
141.x: IIT Tirupati, which started in 2015 at Yerpedu, is associated with the Institutes of Technology (Amendment) Act, 2016.
141.tq: Match the institution with its specific establishing law.

141.s: Which one of the following institutions is correctly matched with its location and acreage?
o: Central Tribal University of AP — Marrivalasa, 183 acres
141.x: IIT Tirupati is located at Yerpedu on 548 acres. IIM Visakhapatnam occupies 241 acres, AIIMS Mangalagiri 183 acres and the Central Tribal University 490 acres.
141.tq: Compare the acreage figures attached to neighbouring institutions.

141.s: IIM Visakhapatnam was started in September 2015 with which institution as its mentor?
141.x: IIM Visakhapatnam began in September 2015 at Gambheeram, with IIM Bangalore serving as its mentor institution.
141.tq: Recall the mentor institution associated with the date of commencement.

141.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
141.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is associated with the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), not the IIM Act, 2017. NIT Andhra Pradesh and IISER Tirupati are linked with the NITSER Act, while IIPE is linked with the IIPE Act, 2017.
141.tq: Spot the swapped legal basis among similar institutional entries.

141.s:
Which of the following statements regarding institutions established in Andhra Pradesh is/are correct?

1. AIIMS Mangalagiri started in 2018.
2. IIPE is located in Visakhapatnam and started in 2016.
3. The Central University of Andhra Pradesh is located at Janthaluru in Anantapuramu.
4. The Central University of Andhra Pradesh started in 2015.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri started in 2018, IIPE is at Visakhapatnam and started in 2016, and the Central University of AP is at Janthaluru and started in 2018. Statement 4 is false because it started in 2018, not 2015.
141.tq: Separate the correct start years from a deliberately shifted year.

141.s: The Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh is located at which place?
141.x: The Central Tribal University of AP is located at Marrivalasa/Chinamedapalli in Dattirajeru mandal of Vizianagaram district, on 490 acres.
141.tq: Distinguish the tribal university location from other institutional campuses.

141.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019 created both the Central University of AP and the Central Tribal University of AP.
2. The Central University of AP is located at Janthaluru.
3. The Central Tribal University of AP was first proposed near Visakhapatnam and later moved to Vizianagaram.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements are correct. The 2019 Amendment Act created both universities; CUAP is at Janthaluru, while the proposed location of CTUAP shifted from near Visakhapatnam to Vizianagaram.
141.tq: Combine the establishing law, present location and relocation history.

141.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: IIITDM, Kurnool — Ministry of Education, Institution of National Importance
NIDM Southern Campus, Kondapalli — Ministry of Education, Institution of National Importance
IIPE, Visakhapatnam — Ministry of Home Affairs
141.x: IIITDM at Kurnool is under the Ministry of Education and has the status of an Institution of National Importance. The NIDM Southern Campus is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs, while PMSSY is associated with AIIMS Mangalagiri.
141.tq: Match each institution with the responsible ministry or legal status.

141.s: The NIDM Southern Campus associated with Andhra Pradesh is located at:
141.x: The Southern Campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management is located at Kondapalli, near Vijayawada, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
141.tq: Recall the location of the specialised institution rather than its ministry.

141.s: The number of premier institutions in Andhra Pradesh described as functional by the CDI is:
141.x: The CDI count places the number of functional premier institutions in Andhra Pradesh at 11.
141.tq: Recall the exact institutional count.

141.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, the Steel Authority of India Limited was required to examine, within six months, the feasibility of an integrated steel plant in:
141.x: The Act required SAIL to examine within six months the feasibility of integrated steel plants in YSR district of Andhra Pradesh and Khammam district of Telangana.
141.tq: Recall both locations attached to the statutory feasibility requirement.

141.s:
Consider the following events relating to the Kadapa steel plant:

A. Land was allotted to Brahmani Steels.
B. Foundation stone was laid at M. Kambala Dinne.
C. Stones were laid again by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
D. Construction of the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant was launched.

Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
141.x: Land was allotted during the YSR era of 2004–09, the foundation stone was laid in December 2018, stones were laid again in 2019 and 2023, and JSW construction was launched on 3 July 2026.
141.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the intermediate milestones by year.

141.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the institutional response to the Kadapa steel plant proposal is/are correct?

1. The Centre and SAIL did not build the plant.
2. The State formed AP High Grade Steels Limited in 2018.
3. The plant was constructed directly by SAIL after its feasibility examination.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: The Centre and SAIL did not build the plant; instead, the State formed its own special-purpose vehicle, AP High Grade Steels Limited, in 2018. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
141.tq: Identify the wrong authority and the State-created special-purpose vehicle.

141.s: On 3 July 2026, construction was launched for the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant at:
141.x: Construction was launched at Sunnapurallapalli and Peddandluru villages in the Jammalamadugu constituency of Kadapa on 3 July 2026.
141.tq: Recall the two construction-site villages as a pair.

141.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant?
o: Developer — AP High Grade Steels Ltd
Developer — JSW Andhra Pradesh Steel Ltd
Estimated investment — ₹16,350 crore in two phases
141.x: The developer is JSW Andhra Pradesh Steel Ltd. AP High Grade Steels Ltd was the State-created SPV formed in 2018, not the developer named for the JSW plant.
141.tq: Catch the swapped developer name in a project description.

141.s: The investment pattern for the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant is:
o: ₹16,350 crore in Phase I and no second phase
₹11,850 crore in Phase I and ₹4,500 crore in Phase II
₹5,640 crore in Phase I and ₹10,710 crore in Phase II
₹4,500 crore in Phase I and ₹11,850 crore in Phase II
141.x: The total investment is ₹16,350 crore, divided into ₹4,500 crore for Phase I and ₹11,850 crore for Phase II.
141.tq: Split the total project investment into its two stated phases.

141.s:
Which of the following statements about the JSW Rayalaseema Integrated Steel Plant are correct?

1. It is planned as a scrap-based Electric Arc Furnace green-steel project.
2. It is to receive 2 tmc ft of water per year from Gandikota.
3. The water is to be conveyed through a 15-kilometre pipeline.
4. Commercial production is targeted for 2028.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: All four statements are correct. The project uses a scrap-based Electric Arc Furnace, has a planned Gandikota water supply of 2 tmc ft per year through a 15-kilometre pipeline, and targets commercial production in 2028.
141.tq: Check all technical specifications before selecting the comprehensive option.

141.s: The first phase of the proposed two-phase investment in the JSW steel project amounts to:
141.x: Phase I of the JSW project involves an investment of ₹4,500 crore; Phase II involves ₹11,850 crore.
141.tq: Distinguish a phase-specific figure from the total project cost.

141.s: Which of the following Thirteenth Schedule commitments was dropped as non-feasible?
o: Examination of a new railway zone
New major port at Duggirajupatnam with Phase I by the end of 2018
Expansion of Visakhapatnam airport to international standards
141.x: The proposed new major port at Duggirajupatnam, for which Phase I was envisaged by the end of 2018, was dropped as non-feasible.
141.tq: Identify the commitment whose status is cancellation rather than delay or completion.

141.s: The present port-related development associated with the site of the dropped Duggirajupatnam proposal is described as:
o: A BPCL refinery and petrochemical complex
A VPA–APMB greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster
A new railway zone under SCoR
141.x: The present development is described as a VPA–APMB greenfield port together with a shipbuilding cluster.
141.tq: Distinguish the current substitute project from other infrastructure commitments.

141.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Greenfield refinery-petrochemical complex — BPCL refinery near Ramayapatnam
2. VCIC — ADB-funded project with slow progress
3. New railway zone — SCoR operational from 1 June 2026
4. Metro rail in Visakhapatnam — Already operational throughout the city

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
141.x: The first three pairs are correct. The Visakhapatnam metro project was still before the Centre in 2026 and was not operational throughout the city.
141.tq: Reject the completed-status trap attached to an ongoing project.

141.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule commitment relating to a refinery and petrochemical complex, which organisation was to examine the project?
141.x: The Act provided for IOC or HPCL to examine a greenfield refinery-petrochemical complex. The later status mentioned is a BPCL refinery near Ramayapatnam, with final clearances pending in September 2026.
141.tq: Separate the originally designated organisations from the later project organisation.

141.s: The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) commitment was to examine it on the lines of the:
141.x: The Thirteenth Schedule provided for examination of VCIC on the lines of the Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor. The project is ADB-funded, but progress has been slow.
141.tq: Recall the model corridor used for comparison.

141.s: Which set of airports was specifically identified for expansion to international standards?
141.x: The commitment covered the airports at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati. All three are described as international airports in the stated status update.
141.tq: Recall the complete three-airport set rather than a partial list.

141.s: The new airport dedicated on 1 August 2026 is:
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram
141.x: The Bhogapuram airport was dedicated on 1 August 2026 as the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport.
141.tq: Match the new airport with its official name and location.

141.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Bhogapuram airport are correct?

1. It is being built by GMR through GVIAL on a public-private partnership basis.
2. Its cost is over ₹5,640 crore.
3. Its planned capacity is 6 million passengers per year.
4. It is the first greenfield airport in Andhra Pradesh since 2014.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: All four statements are correct. Bhogapuram airport is being developed by GMR through GVIAL on PPP, costs over ₹5,640 crore, is designed for 6 million passengers annually and is the first greenfield airport in AP since 2014.
141.tq: Verify the project developer, financing model, cost and capacity together.

141.s: The metro rail feasibility commitment under the Thirteenth Schedule covered which corridors or urban regions?
141.x: The commitment was to examine metro rail feasibility for Visakhapatnam and the Vijayawada–Guntur–Tenali region within one year. In 2026, the Vizag metro proposal was still before the Centre.
141.tq: Recall both components of a combined regional infrastructure commitment.

141.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the status of the proposed new railway zone?
o: The new railway zone was dropped as non-feasible.
The railway zone is still only under preliminary examination.
The South Coast Railway became operational on 1 June 2026.
The South Central Railway became operational on 1 June 2026.
141.x: The South Coast Railway (SCoR) is stated to have become operational on 1 June 2026. It represents the status of the new railway-zone commitment.
141.tq: Discriminate between the similar railway-zone abbreviations and names.

141.s:
Assertion (A): All three airports identified for expansion under the Thirteenth Schedule are described as international airports.

Reason (R): Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports were among the airports specified for expansion to international standards.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
141.x: Both statements are true, and the identification of Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati as the airports targeted for international standards explains the stated status of all three.
141.tq: Test whether the statutory airport list explains the reported status.

141.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which port was specified for development as a new major port by the Government of India?
141.x: The Act states that the Government of India shall develop a new major port at Duggirajupatnam. It was the only port named in the Schedule for this purpose.
141.tq: Directly identify the exact name appearing in a statutory commitment.

141.s: Dugarajapatnam port was dropped from the original implementation plan primarily because of which reason?
141.x: The proposed Dugarajapatnam port was dropped because it was found to be non-feasible. The specific grounds for non-feasibility are not specified here.
141.tq: Distinguish the stated reason from plausible but unsupported alternatives.

141.s: Which port was developed by the State of Andhra Pradesh as a substitute greenfield port after Dugarajapatnam was found non-feasible?
141.x: After Dugarajapatnam was dropped on feasibility grounds, the State developed Ramayapatnam as the substitute greenfield port.
141.tq: Test the replacement relationship between two closely associated projects.

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revival of Dugarajapatnam port:
1. The revival was enabled by a Government Order dated 2 January 2026.
2. The project includes a greenfield port and a mega shipbuilding cluster.
3. The project is to be implemented under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements are correct. The 2 January 2026 Government Order allowed the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board to establish the port and shipbuilding cluster under the Centre’s Shipbuilding Development Scheme.
141.tq: Verify several linked features of a revived project before selecting the coded combination.

141.s: The Special Purpose Vehicle formed for the Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding and heavy industries project is named:
o: Andhra Pradesh Maritime Industrial Corporation Limited
National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Andhra Pradesh Limited
141.x: The SPV is National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Andhra Pradesh Ltd. It was created through G.O. Ms. No. 7 dated 2 March 2026.
141.tq: Test the exact official name of the implementing vehicle.

141.s:
With reference to the proposed Dugarajapatnam greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster, consider the following statements:
1. The SPV is a 50:50 joint venture of the Visakhapatnam Port Authority and the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board.
2. About 3,500 acres have been identified for the project.
3. The cluster is estimated to be worth ₹30,000 crore.
4. Andhra Pradesh is the only State selected for a national shipbuilding cluster.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the project is one of five national cluster sites; the others are in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Odisha and Maharashtra.
141.tq: Find the incorrect membership statement in a list-based question.

141.s: Ramayapatnam Port is presently located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
141.x: Ramayapatnam Port is presently in Prakasam district. Earlier material placed it in SPS Nellore district before district boundaries were redrawn.
141.tq: Separate the current district from the earlier district classification.

141.s: Before the redrawing of district boundaries, Ramayapatnam Port was placed in:
141.x: The APSES 2024–25 material placed Ramayapatnam in SPS Nellore district, specifically in Ulavapadu mandal, before district boundaries were redrawn.
141.tq: Use the older administrative description to resolve a district-based confusable pair.

141.s: Which of the following correctly describes the location of Ramayapatnam Port?
o: 93 km south of Krishnapatnam and 5 km west of Thettu
93 km north of Machilipatnam and 5 km east of Kavali on NH-65
93 km east of Krishnapatnam and 5 km north of Thettu on NH-16
93 km north of Krishnapatnam and 5 km east of Thettu on NH-16
141.x: Ramayapatnam is 93 km north of Krishnapatnam and 5 km east of Thettu on NH-16. Thettu is the nearest railway station.
141.tq: Check direction, distance and transport-location details together.

141.s: The State Special Purpose Vehicle responsible for developing Ramayapatnam Port is:
o: Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd
141.x: Ramayapatnam Port is being developed by the State SPV Ramayapatnam Port Development Corporation Ltd, permitted in February 2020.
141.tq: Identify the project-specific developer rather than the supervising authority.

141.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Ramayapatnam Port Development Corporation Ltd is correct?
o: It was permitted in February 2020 and the contract was signed on 30 July 2021.
It was permitted in July 2021 and the contract was signed in February 2020.
It was established in January 2026 and the contract was signed in March 2026.
It was permitted in 2014 and the contract was signed on 2 January 2026.
141.x: The corporation was permitted in February 2020, and its contract was signed on 30 July 2021.
141.tq: Use the sequence of approval and contract dates to reject reversed timelines.

141.s: The Phase-I plan of Ramayapatnam Port includes which of the following combinations?
o: ₹3,549.23 crore, four berths and 34.04 MTPA capacity
₹4,293.39 crore, three berths and 30.04 MTPA capacity
₹4,929.39 crore, four berths and 34.04 MTPA capacity
₹4,929.39 crore, six berths and 30.04 MTPA capacity
141.x: Phase-I of Ramayapatnam Port is estimated at ₹4,929.39 crore and provides four berths with a capacity of 34.04 MTPA.
141.tq: Match the project with its exact cost, berth count and capacity figures.

141.s: How much core land was provided for Phase-I of Ramayapatnam Port?
141.x: Phase-I of Ramayapatnam Port requires 850 acres of core land.
141.tq: Distinguish the port’s core land requirement from land figures of other projects.

141.s:
Arrange the reported physical progress of Ramayapatnam Port in chronological order, beginning with the earliest:
A. 81 per cent
B. 30.09 per cent
C. 74.34 per cent
141.x: The reported progress was 30.09 per cent in November 2024, 74.34 per cent in October 2025 and 81 per cent in August 2026.
141.tq: Arrange dated progress figures by first identifying the dates.

141.s: In October 2025, Ramayapatnam Port recorded which physical progress and status among the four greenfield ports?
141.x: In October 2025, physical progress at Ramayapatnam Port was 74.34 per cent, the highest among the four greenfield ports at that time.
141.tq: Link the percentage with its date and comparative ranking.

141.s: As reported in August 2026, which combination correctly represents the status of Ramayapatnam Port?
o: 74.34 per cent physical progress and 81 per cent of 850 acres acquired
95 per cent physical progress and 81 per cent of 850 acres acquired
81 per cent physical progress and 74.34 per cent of 850 acres acquired
81 per cent physical progress and 95 per cent of 850 acres acquired
141.x: By August 2026, physical progress was reported at 81 per cent and 95 per cent of the 850 acres had been acquired.
141.tq: Avoid swapping two closely related percentage figures.

141.s: Which of the following combinations relating to later financial approvals for port projects is correct?
o: ₹354.32 crore for variation works and ₹1,683.52 crore for Phase-II
₹354.23 crore for Phase-II and ₹1,638.52 crore for variation works
₹354.23 crore for variation works and ₹1,638.52 crore for Phase-II of three ports
₹354.23 crore for land acquisition and ₹1,638.52 crore for the Dugarajapatnam cluster
141.x: The Cabinet cleared ₹354.23 crore for variation works. A further ₹1,638.52 crore was approved for Phase-II of Ramayapatnam, Mulapeta and Machilipatnam.
141.tq: Match each financial figure with the correct expenditure purpose.

141.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, IOC or HPCL was required to examine within six months the establishment of a:
o: Greenfield crude refinery and petrochemical complex
Gas-based power plant and LNG terminal
141.x: The Act required Indian Oil Corporation or Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited to examine, within six months, a greenfield crude refinery and petrochemical complex.
141.tq: Identify the precise statutory obligation and its implementing entities.

141.s: The BPCL greenfield refinery-cum-petrochemical complex is proposed near Ramayapatnam Port between which districts?
141.x: The BPCL complex is proposed near Ramayapatnam Port, between Prakasam and Nellore districts, in the villages of Chevuru and Ravuru.
141.tq: Test the location by pairing the project with its two neighbouring districts.

141.s: Which of the following correctly describes the proposed BPCL refinery-cum-petrochemical complex?
o: Cost of about ₹30,000 crore and capacity of 9 MTPA
Cost of about ₹1 lakh crore and capacity of 4 MTPA
Cost of about ₹1.45 lakh crore and capacity of 9 MTPA
Cost of about ₹1.45 lakh crore and capacity of 34.04 MTPA
141.x: The project cost is currently estimated at about ₹1.45 lakh crore and its refinery capacity is 9 MTPA. An earlier estimate had quoted approximately ₹1 lakh crore.
141.tq: Use the updated estimate rather than the earlier quoted figure.

141.s: The BPCL project is expected to produce approximately how much Euro-6 fuel?
141.x: The proposed BPCL refinery-cum-petrochemical complex is expected to produce approximately 5.4 MT of Euro-6 fuels.
141.tq: Distinguish the fuel-output figure from refinery and port capacities.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about the BPCL refinery project:
1. It is proposed near Ramayapatnam Port.
2. The villages identified include Chevuru and Ravuru.
3. Seventy-five per cent of the 6,000 acres required had been handed over.
4. Final environmental clearance was expected by the end of September 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All four statements are correct. The project is near Ramayapatnam, involves Chevuru and Ravuru, has received 75 per cent of the 6,000 acres, and was expected to receive final environmental clearance by the end of September 2026.
141.tq: Combine location, land-acquisition and approval-status facts in one coded question.

141.s: Which statement regarding the proposed Kakinada petrochemical facility is correct?
o: It lies outside the Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR and has received central viability-gap funding.
Its MoUs were cleared by the State pollution board, and Kakinada lies in the Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR.
It is the BPCL refinery located between Prakasam and Nellore districts.
It was established under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme.
141.x: MoUs for a greenfield petrochemical facility near Kakinada were cleared by the State pollution board. Kakinada is located in the Visakhapatnam-Kakinada PCPIR; the available information does not specify viability-gap-funding figures.
141.tq: Reject options that merge the Kakinada facility with the separate BPCL refinery project.

141.s: Which organisation is the implementing agency for the metro rail projects in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada?
o: Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Ltd
141.x: The implementing agency for the metro rail projects in both cities is Andhra Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.
141.tq: Identify the designated implementing agency rather than an earlier consulting or project arrangement.

141.s: The proposed Visakhapatnam Metro Rail project comprises how many corridors covering what total length?
141.x: The Visakhapatnam Metro proposal has four corridors with a total length of 76.70 km.
141.tq: Match the corridor count with the project-length figure.

141.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Visakhapatnam Metro project?
o: Private land within Phase-I requirement — 7.57 acres
141.x: The compensation sought for the private land component is ₹600 crore, not ₹60 crore. The other three figures are correctly matched.
141.tq: Find the altered zero in a set of closely related numerical figures.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about the Visakhapatnam Metro project:
1. A double-decker metro-cum-road corridor on NH-16 is being surveyed.
2. The Detailed Project Report has been submitted.
3. The Centre is weighing ridership and viability.
4. The earlier GoI-GoAP-IL&FS joint-venture arrangement with a DPR by UMTC remains the current project arrangement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the earlier IL&FS-related arrangement has been superseded.
141.tq: Identify the superseded arrangement while retaining the current feasibility details.

141.s: According to the Governor’s address in January 2026, what was the status of the Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada metro projects at the State level?
o: They were approved by the State.
They had received final approval from the Union Government.
They were rejected by the State Government.
They were transferred to the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board.
141.x: The Governor’s address stated that the Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada metro projects had been approved by the State. The central approval status of the Vijayawada project is not specified.
141.tq: Distinguish State approval from Union-level approval.

141.s: Which of the following projects were cited together in criticism that promises worth approximately ₹5 lakh crore remained unfulfilled?
o: Machilipatnam Port, Mulapeta Port and Vijayawada airport
Ramayapatnam Port, Kakinada PCPIR and Bhogapuram airport
Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro projects
BPCL refinery, Visakhapatnam Port and the shipbuilding cluster
141.x: The criticism referred to the Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro projects, with the unfulfilled promises valued at approximately ₹5 lakh crore.
141.tq: Match a criticism with the complete set of projects named in it.

141.s: Which of the following correctly expresses the industrial-cluster linkage in southern Andhra Pradesh?
o: Kadapa steel, Machilipatnam Port and Visakhapatnam Metro are linked by a new rail line.
Kadapa steel, Ramayapatnam Port and the BPCL refinery are linked by a new rail line.
Ramayapatnam Port, Mulapeta Port and Bhogapuram airport are linked by a new rail line.
Dugarajapatnam Port, Bhogapuram airport and Kakinada PCPIR are linked by a new rail line.
141.x: Kadapa steel, Ramayapatnam Port and the BPCL refinery are linked by a new rail line, forming a southern Andhra Pradesh industrial cluster.
141.tq: Recognise the infrastructure linkage that defines the regional industrial cluster.

141.s: Bhogapuram is significant in the context of Andhra Pradesh infrastructure because it is described as the State’s:
141.x: Bhogapuram is described as Andhra Pradesh’s first greenfield airport since 2014.
141.tq: Identify the significance attached to a named infrastructure project.

141.s: Which of the following developments was reported as having been launched on 3 July 2026?
141.x: Works at the JSW Kadapa plant were launched on 3 July 2026. The BPCL refinery clearance was expected by the end of September 2026.
141.tq: Use the date to distinguish a launched project from a pending approval.

142.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Government of India was required to examine the feasibility of which industrial corridor within six months?
142.x: The Thirteenth Schedule directed the Government of India to examine the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor within six months.
142.tq: Identify the specific statutory obligation and avoid confusing the proposed corridor with its model corridor.

142.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor was proposed to be developed on the lines of which corridor?
142.x: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor was to be examined on the lines of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Distinguish the parent corridor from the model on which the project is based.

142.s: Which institution is the funding partner of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
142.x: The Asian Development Bank is the funding partner of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Use the funding-agency association rather than the country association of other corridors.

142.s: The total programme size of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is approximately:
142.x: The total programme size of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is USD 840 million.
142.tq: Separate the total programme amount from the policy-based and project-loan components.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor:
1. It is approximately 800 km long.
2. It constitutes the first phase or segment of the East Coast Economic Corridor.
3. It is linked with the Act East and Make in India initiatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. The corridor is about 800 km long, forms the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor, and is linked with Act East and Make in India.
142.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.

142.s: The East Coast Economic Corridor, of which the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase, extends from:
142.x: The East Coast Economic Corridor is described as extending from Kolkata to Tuticorin; some descriptions refer to its southern end as Kanyakumari.
142.tq: Test the geographical endpoints directly and distinguish the parent corridor from its first phase.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the East Coast Economic Corridor?
o: A corridor confined to Andhra Pradesh
A corridor developed only for the automobile sector
India's first exclusively inland freight corridor
142.x: The East Coast Economic Corridor is described as India's first coastal economic corridor.
142.tq: Use the defining descriptor and reject options that narrow the corridor without support.

142.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is intended, among other purposes, to connect India with:
142.x: The corridor is linked to the Act East policy and is intended to connect India with ASEAN and East Asia.
142.tq: Link the corridor's international orientation with the Act East policy.

142.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the ADB-identified Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor nodes?
142.x: The ADB-identified nodes listed are Visakhapatnam, Machilipatnam, Donakonda and Srikalahasti-Chittoor. Orvakal is associated with the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Find the item belonging to another corridor by separating node lists.

142.s: Which pair of Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor nodes was identified for long-term phased development?
142.x: Donakonda and Machilipatnam were identified for long-term phased development.
142.tq: Match the special status of the nodes with the correct pair.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the nodes of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor:
1. The Visakhapatnam node includes the Rambilli and Nakkapalli clusters.
2. The Chittoor node includes Chittoor-South and Naidupeta.
3. Kopparthy covers 2,596 acres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. The Visakhapatnam node includes Rambilli and Nakkapalli, the Chittoor node includes Chittoor-South and Naidupeta, and Kopparthy covers 2,596 acres.
142.tq: Verify node-component pairs and the numerical area separately.

142.s: The Visakhapatnam node of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor accounts for approximately what share of the corridor's output?
142.x: The Visakhapatnam node accounts for approximately 49 percent of the corridor's output.
142.tq: Retain the node-specific share instead of confusing it with the overall start-up-area percentage.

142.s:
Which of the following correctly matches a node with its development details?
1. Visakhapatnam — Bulk Drug Park of 2,002 acres
2. Chittoor — Start-up area of 2,628 acres and ₹463 crore
3. Kopparthy — Phase-I area of 2,596 acres
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three matches are correct. Visakhapatnam has the 2,002-acre Bulk Drug Park, Chittoor has the stated start-up area and cost, and Kopparthy has a 2,596-acre Phase-I area.
142.tq: Cross-check each node against its distinctive area or cost figure.

142.s: The Steel Cluster Phase-I at the Visakhapatnam node covers approximately:
142.x: The Steel Cluster Phase-I covers 2,200 acres, with another 4,000 acres planned.
142.tq: Distinguish the present Phase-I area from the additional planned area.

142.s: The Bulk Drug Park at the Visakhapatnam node is associated with which department of the Government of India?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
142.x: The Bulk Drug Park is associated with the Government of India's Department of Pharmaceuticals.
142.tq: Use the department-function association and avoid neighbouring industrial ministries.

142.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Kopparthy node?
o: Start-up area of 2,628 acres and ₹463 crore
Phase-I area of 2,596 acres and trunk infrastructure of about ₹1,264 crore
Phase-I area of 2,621 acres and ₹1,781 crore
142.x: Kopparthy has a Phase-I area of 2,596 acres and trunk infrastructure costing approximately ₹1,264 crore.
142.tq: Separate similar area-cost combinations belonging to different nodes and corridors.

142.s: The CCEA approval associated with the Kopparthy node was given on:
142.x: The CCEA approval for the Kopparthy-related development was given on 28 August 2024.
142.tq: Match the approval date with the specific node rather than with the loan-signing date.

142.s:
Which of the following statements about the overall Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor project is correct?
1. Its three principal nodes cover more than 33,000 acres.
2. Thirty percent of the area is developed first as a start-up area.
3. Works of ₹5,000 crore are backed by an ADB loan of ₹3,300 crore in two tranches.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct: the three nodes cover over 33,000 acres, 30 percent is developed initially as start-up area, and ₹5,000 crore of works are supported by a ₹3,300 crore ADB loan in two tranches.
142.tq: Combine area, percentage and financing figures only after checking each independently.

142.s: Which sectoral pattern is associated with the northern and southern parts of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor respectively?
o: North: leather and automobiles; South: pharmaceuticals and IT
North: food processing and leather; South: metallurgy and IT
North: automobiles and food processing; South: petrochemicals and metallurgy
North: metallurgy, pharma, petrochemicals and IT; South: food processing, leather and automobiles
142.x: The northern part is associated with metallurgy, pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals and IT, while the southern part is associated with food processing, leather and automobiles.
142.tq: Compare the north-south sectoral pattern without reversing the two sides.

142.s: Which industrial node had its land acquisition completed by APIIC under the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
142.x: APIIC completed land acquisition for the Nakkapalli industrial node in the Anakapalli area.
142.tq: Identify the agency-action and location pair directly.

142.s: The policy-based loan component of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor financing is intended for:
o: Land acquisition and steel-cluster expansion only
Ease of doing business and institutional reform
Construction of the East Coast railway network
142.x: The USD 125 million policy-based loan, entirely from the ADB, funds ease of doing business and institutional reform.
142.tq: Link the loan type with its policy purpose rather than with physical infrastructure.

142.s: Which statement regarding the loan structure of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is correct?
o: The policy-based loan is divided in a 70:30 ratio between ADB and the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
The project loan is USD 125 million and is entirely funded by the ADB.
The project loan is USD 715 million and is divided in a 70:30 ratio between ADB and the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
The Government of Andhra Pradesh's total share is USD 840 million.
142.x: The USD 715 million project loan is shared in a 70:30 ratio between the ADB and the Government of Andhra Pradesh. The policy-based loan is USD 125 million and entirely ADB-funded.
142.tq: Separate the two loan components and apply the stated funding ratio.

142.s: The total share of the Government of Andhra Pradesh in the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor financing is approximately:
142.x: The Government of Andhra Pradesh's total share is USD 215 million, or approximately 25.6 percent of the programme.
142.tq: Distinguish the State's contribution from the total project-loan amount.

142.s: The loans for the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor were signed on:
142.x: The loans were signed on 23 February 2017.
142.tq: Use the exact date and distinguish loan signing from later approval dates.

142.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the institutional arrangement for the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
1. Executing agency — Department of Industries and Commerce
2. Project Management Unit — under the Commissioner of Industries
3. Project Implementation Units — four, including APIIC, APRDC and AP Transco
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements correctly describe the institutional arrangement: the Department of Industries and Commerce is the executing agency, the PMU is under the Commissioner of Industries, and there are four PIUs including APIIC, APRDC and AP Transco.
142.tq: Match each institutional level with its designated agency or unit.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the three major industrial corridors having nodes in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh is the only State with nodes on the Vizag-Chennai, Chennai-Bengaluru and Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridors.
2. Japan supports the Delhi-Mumbai and Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridors.
3. The Chennai-Bengaluru corridor has an AP node at Krishnapatnam North.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh has nodes on all three corridors, Japan supports DMIC and CBIC, and Krishnapatnam North is the AP node of CBIC.
142.tq: Test multiple corridor relationships together while keeping corridor names distinct.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Krishnapatnam North node?
o: 10,834.5 acres, with a start-up area of 2,500 acres and ₹2,139 crore of investment
2,596 acres, with approximately ₹1,264 crore for trunk infrastructure
142.x: The Krishnapatnam North node covers 10,834.5 acres, has a 2,500-acre start-up area and involves ₹2,139 crore of investment.
142.tq: Use the distinctive area-cost combination to separate nodes across corridors.

142.s: The Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor extends for approximately 560 km across:
o: Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu
Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
142.x: The Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor extends for about 560 km across Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
142.tq: Combine the corridor length with its three-State geographical spread.

142.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Orvakal node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor?
o: Phase-I area of 2,621 acres and ₹1,781 crore; CCEA approval on 28 August 2024
Area of 10,834.5 acres and ₹463 crore; CCEA approval on 2 February 2026
Phase-I area of 2,596 acres and ₹1,264 crore; CCEA approval on 23 February 2017
Start-up area of 2,500 acres and ₹2,139 crore; CCEA approval on 28 August 2014
142.x: Orvakal has a Phase-I area of 2,621 acres, involves ₹1,781 crore and received CCEA approval on 28 August 2024.
142.tq: Combine node, area, cost and approval date to identify the precise project profile.

142.s: The nodes funded through NICDIT include:
142.x: Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal are identified as nodes funded through NICDIT.
142.tq: Identify the funding-agency node set without mixing it with the broader corridor node list.

142.s: Which of the following correctly summarises the principal scale indicators of the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
o: About 560 km; 33,000 acres; 2,596-acre start-up area; ₹1,264 crore
About 800 km; 33,000 acres; 30 percent start-up area; ₹5,000 crore of works
About 560 km; 10,834.5 acres; 2,500-acre start-up area; ₹2,139 crore
About 800 km; 2,621 acres; 70 percent start-up area; ₹1,781 crore
142.x: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor is about 800 km long, covers over 33,000 acres across its three principal nodes, develops 30 percent initially as start-up area and involves ₹5,000 crore of works.
142.tq: Compare the corridor-level figures rather than the figures of individual nodes or other corridors.

142.s: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway, in Andhra Pradesh, enters or passes through which district?
142.x: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway crosses Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh.
142.tq: Use the route-and-location association to distinguish nearby districts.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway:
1. It is a greenfield expressway.
2. It is being developed under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I.
3. It starts at Hoskote in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: The expressway is a greenfield project under Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I and starts at Hoskote in Karnataka.
142.tq: Combine project type, scheme and starting point before selecting the inclusive option.

142.s: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway passes through the Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary elephant corridor. The animal underpasses cleared for this corridor have a total length of:
142.x: The Supreme Court’s National Board for Wildlife clearance covers 3,475 metres of animal underpasses, including a continuous stretch of 1,400 metres.
142.tq: Separate the total length from the continuous sub-stretch.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the status of the Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway mentioned for 2024–26?
o: The Karnataka stretch was open, while the Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu stretches remained under construction.
All three State stretches were opened in December 2024.
The Tamil Nadu stretch was open, while the Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh stretches remained under construction.
Only the Andhra Pradesh stretch was opened in December 2024.
142.x: The Karnataka stretch was reported open since December 2024, whereas the Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu stretches were still under construction.
142.tq: Compare the status of each State stretch instead of treating the project as uniformly operational.

142.s: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway is regarded as a priority link of which industrial corridor?
142.x: The Bengaluru–Chennai Expressway is a priority link of the Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
142.tq: Match the transport link with its associated industrial corridor.

142.s: The proposed Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is to pass through which combination of States?
142.x: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam Expressway is described as a greenfield route through Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
142.tq: Use the endpoint-to-State route sequence to eliminate neighbouring-State combinations.

142.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the expressway proposals or fast-tracked routes associated with Andhra Pradesh?
142.x: Kharagpur–Amaravati, Nagpur–Machilipatnam via Vijayawada and Raipur–Amaravati are listed proposals. Mumbai–Nagpur–Vijayawada is not listed.
142.tq: Find the route that does not belong to the stated proposal list.

142.s: The Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor is expected to be completed by:
142.x: The Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor is expected to be completed by 2027.
142.tq: Identify the specific completion year rather than the separate year associated with NH works.

142.s: National Highway works worth approximately what amount were stated to be undertaken in Andhra Pradesh by 2029?
142.x: National Highway works valued at ₹1.40 lakh crore were stated to be undertaken by 2029.
142.tq: Read the amount and target year together as a numerical pair.

142.s: Which pair was listed as greenfield expressways being fast-tracked by the Governor?
142.x: The Governor listed Nagpur–Vijayawada and Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati as greenfield expressways being fast-tracked.
142.tq: Match the exact paired proposals rather than selecting routes merely mentioned elsewhere.

142.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, the Government of India is required to take steps for rapid rail and road connectivity from the new capital of Andhra Pradesh to:
o: Delhi and other important cities of northern India
Visakhapatnam and all coastal cities only
Bengaluru and all cities of Karnataka only
Hyderabad and other important cities of Telangana
142.x: The Act provides for rapid rail and road connectivity from the new Andhra Pradesh capital to Hyderabad and other important cities of Telangana.
142.tq: Focus on the statutory destination and the additional regional connectivity specified.

142.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven high-speed rail corridors identified as “growth connectors” in the Union Budget 2026–27?
142.x: The seven corridors include Pune–Hyderabad, Hyderabad–Chennai and Delhi–Varanasi; Amaravati–Visakhapatnam is not included in that list.
142.tq: Check every listed corridor against the complete seven-corridor set.

142.s: The total estimated cost of the seven high-speed rail corridors announced as “growth connectors” in the Union Budget 2026–27 is:
142.x: The total estimated cost of the seven high-speed rail corridors is ₹16 lakh crore.
142.tq: Use the aggregate figure rather than confusing it with the number of corridors.

142.s: The proposed Hyderabad–Chennai high-speed rail service is expected to cover the journey in approximately:
142.x: The Hyderabad–Chennai high-speed rail corridor is specified with a travel time of 2 hours 55 minutes.
142.tq: Distinguish the precise travel time from nearby rounded alternatives.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed Amaravati–Hyderabad bullet train:
1. The journey is proposed to take 70 minutes.
2. Amaravati is proposed as a stop through the 57-kilometre Errupalem–Namburu line.
3. A DPR for the Hyderabad–Chennai high-speed rail corridor is to be prepared.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: The proposed Amaravati–Hyderabad bullet train journey is 70 minutes, Amaravati is linked through the 57-kilometre Errupalem–Namburu line, and a DPR for Hyderabad–Chennai HSR is to be prepared.
142.tq: Test the travel time, intermediate line and DPR details as a combined factual set.

142.s: NICDC is the abbreviation for:
o: National Industrial Construction and Development Commission
National Infrastructure and Connectivity Development Council
142.x: NICDC stands for National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation.
142.tq: Discriminate between closely similar institutional expansions.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes NICDC?
o: It is the State nodal agency for industrial-park land in Andhra Pradesh.
It funds only road projects and has no role in industrial parks.
It was established under the A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017.
It was incorporated in January 2008 and was formerly known as DMICDC.
142.x: NICDC was incorporated in January 2008, was formerly known as DMICDC, and functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry through DPIIT.
142.tq: Use the incorporation date and former name to identify the correct institution.

142.s: NICDC functions under which Ministry and Department?
o: Ministry of Heavy Industries and Department of Public Enterprises
Ministry of Finance and Department of Economic Affairs
Ministry of Commerce and Industry and DPIIT
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and NHAI
142.x: NICDC functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with DPIIT as the concerned department.
142.tq: Apply the ‘who administers this body?’ institutional-authority test.

142.s: Which institution is responsible for funding node trunk infrastructure at Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal?
142.x: NICDIT funds node trunk infrastructure at the Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal nodes.
142.tq: Match the institution with its specific funding function and nodes.

142.s: The AP Industrial Corridor Development Authority was constituted under which legislation?
o: A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017
142.x: The AP Industrial Corridor Development Authority was constituted under the A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017.
142.tq: Use the exact statute-name and year distinction.

142.s: Industrial parks under the AP Industrial Corridor Development Authority are notified under which section of the 2017 Act?
142.x: Industrial parks are notified under Section 3 of the A.P. Industrial Corridor Development Authority Act, 2017.
142.tq: Test the exact statutory provision rather than the authority’s general function.

142.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: NICDC — Municipal agency for GVMC infrastructure
APIIC — State nodal agency for industrial parks and corridor land
NICDIT — State agency for all industrial-park land acquisition
AP-ICDA — Implementing agency for every national industrial corridor
142.x: APIIC is the State nodal agency for industrial parks and corridor land. The other institutions have different national, statutory or project-specific roles.
142.tq: Find the correct institution-function pairing among similar corridor bodies.

142.s: The approval of 12 additional industrial corridor projects by the Centre in August 2024 took the total number of projects to:
142.x: The 12 projects approved in August 2024 increased the total number of projects to 20.
142.tq: Distinguish the added number from the resulting total.

142.s: In the implementation structure of the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor, which body functions as the executing agency?
o: Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
142.x: The Department of Industries and Commerce is the executing agency for the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor machinery.
142.tq: Identify the executing authority rather than the project-management or field units.

142.s: Which of the following correctly lists the four Project Implementation Units of the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor?
o: APRDC, NHAI, AP Transco and CRDA
APIIC, APRDC, AP Transco and GVMC
142.x: The four PIUs are APIIC, APRDC, AP Transco and GVMC.
142.tq: Recall the complete institutional composition and reject swapped agencies.

142.s: Which statement about the BHAVYA scheme is correct?
o: It provides 100 plug-and-play parks during 2026–27 to 2031–32 with an outlay of ₹33,660 crore.
It is limited to railway sidings and water supply in Kopparthy.
It is implemented exclusively by APIIC without State special purpose vehicles.
It provides 20 industrial corridors during 2024–25 to 2026–27 with an outlay of ₹3,000 crore.
142.x: BHAVYA covers 2026–27 to 2031–32, provides 100 plug-and-play parks and has an outlay of ₹33,660 crore.
142.tq: Combine scheme period, physical target and financial outlay.

142.s: The six new parks proposed in Andhra Pradesh under BHAVYA are to be developed through:
142.x: BHAVYA parks are to be developed through NICDIT–State SPVs, with six new parks proposed in Andhra Pradesh.
142.tq: Identify the implementation partnership rather than the financing institution alone.

142.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Kopparthy industrial smart city project?
o: It costs ₹3,000 crore and targets about ₹33,660 crore of investment.
It costs ₹1,264 crore and targets about ₹8,860 crore of investment.
It costs ₹8,860 crore and targets about ₹1,264 crore of investment.
It costs ₹202 crore and targets about ₹2,300 crore of investment.
142.x: Kopparthy costs ₹1,264 crore and targets approximately ₹8,860 crore of investment.
142.tq: Keep project cost and targeted investment separate to avoid reversing the figures.

142.s: Under the ADB funding structure for the industrial corridor, the Policy-Based Loan consisted of:
142.x: The Policy-Based Loan provided $125 million from ADB, with no GoAP contribution shown for that component.
142.tq: Separate the policy loan from the infrastructure project loan.

142.s: The Project Loan for infrastructure under the ADB funding arrangement was divided between ADB and GoAP in which proportion?
142.x: The infrastructure Project Loan followed a 70:30 contribution structure between ADB and GoAP.
142.tq: Identify the stated contribution ratio before considering the total amount.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the total ADB funding arrangement?
o: ADB $715 million, GoAP $125 million and total $840 million
ADB $500 million, GoAP $215 million and total $625 million
ADB $625 million, GoAP $215 million and total $840 million
ADB $840 million, GoAP $625 million and total $215 million
142.x: The total arrangement comprises $625 million from ADB and $215 million from GoAP, making $840 million.
142.tq: Add the component contributions and verify the total.

142.s: Tranche-I and the Policy-Based Loan agreements for the industrial corridor were signed on:
142.x: The Tranche-I and Policy-Based Loan agreements were signed on 23 February 2017 by the DEA, ADB and GoAP.
142.tq: Use the exact agreement date and distinguish it from later progress reports.

142.s: The approximate value of Tranche-I works, which were described as being at an advanced stage, is:
142.x: Tranche-I works were valued at approximately ₹2,300 crore and were described as being at an advanced stage.
142.tq: Match the progress description with the corresponding project value.

142.s: Under PM Gati Shakti–SASCI, Kopparthy received ₹202 crore for:
o: A 70-kilometre expressway and a freight terminal
Land acquisition and plug-and-play factory construction
A 100 MLD water supply and an airport link
A 46 MLD water supply and a railway siding
142.x: Kopparthy received ₹202 crore under PM Gati Shakti–SASCI for a 46 MLD water supply system and a railway siding.
142.tq: Match the allocation with its specific infrastructure purposes and capacity figure.

142.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the reported implementation status of the industrial corridor?
o: Development was described as rapid, with no further funding demand from industry.
Development was cancelled because ADB withdrew its entire loan.
Development was described as slow, and industry sought a special fund for VCIC and HBIC plug-and-play infrastructure.
Development was completed, and industry sought funds only for new expressways.
142.x: Implementation was described as slow, while CII sought a special fund for VCIC and HBIC plug-and-play infrastructure before the 2026–27 Budget.
142.tq: Combine the progress assessment with the industry’s funding demand.

142.s: Which one of the following is the nodal agency for industrial infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh, including IT, biotech and apparel parks and SEZs?
142.x: APIIC is the nodal agency for industrial infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh, including IT, biotech and apparel parks and SEZs.
142.tq: Identify the correct institutional authority by matching the body with its assigned function.

142.s: The industrial infrastructure projects of APIIC, including parks and SEZs, are developed using which model?
142.x: APIIC uses the public-private partnership (PPP) model for industrial infrastructure.
142.tq: Who would perform this function? Link the agency with the implementation model stated for it.

142.s: How many joint ventures (JVs) does APIIC have according to the 2024–25 figure?
142.x: APIIC has 22 joint ventures according to the 2024–25 figure.
142.tq: Distinguish the current institutional count from nearby park and investment figures.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding APIIC-managed industrial parks:
1. APIIC manages 571 industrial parks.
2. The component figures of 264 APIIC parks and 283 UDL parks add up to 547.
3. The component figures stated for APIIC and UDL parks exactly account for all 571 parks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: The stated total is 571, while 264 plus 283 equals 547. Therefore, statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is false.
142.tq: Split the total from its component figures and check whether the arithmetic is consistent.

142.s: In 2024, APIIC allotted how many acres to industrial units?
142.x: APIIC allotted 5,862 acres in 2024.
142.tq: Read the exact land-allotment figure without confusing it with investment or employment data.

142.s: In 2024, the 816 units to which APIIC allotted land involved a proposed investment of approximately:
142.x: The proposed investment associated with the 816 units was ₹81,062 crore.
142.tq: Separate the investment figure from the number of units and jobs mentioned in the same context.

142.s: The 816 units covered by the 2024 APIIC allotments were expected to generate how many jobs?
142.x: The proposed employment associated with the allotments was 79,261 jobs.
142.tq: Use the employment figure as the distinguishing quantitative clue.

142.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sri City — Tirupati district on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border
142.x: Sri City, a multi-product SEZ, is located in Tirupati district on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border. Mallavalli is associated with the Mega Food Park, while Kopparthi is in Kadapa.
142.tq: Eliminate location swaps by checking the district and border description together.

142.s: Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City is located at:
142.x: Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City is located at Parawada in Visakhapatnam.
142.tq: Distinguish the named industrial city from the separate APIIC cluster locations in the same region.

142.s:
Which of the following locations are associated with APIIC clusters?
1. Gandrajupalle
2. Kopparthi
3. Makavarapalem
4. Machilipatnam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
142.x: The listed APIIC cluster locations are Gandrajupalle in Chittoor, Kopparthi in Kadapa, Makavarapalem in Visakhapatnam and Machilipatnam.
142.tq: Check every location in the list rather than relying on one familiar district.

142.s: The allocation of ₹40,000 crore for electronics components in Budget 2026–27 is expected to help which industrial location in Andhra Pradesh?
142.x: The ₹40,000 crore electronics components allocation is expected to help Sri City.
142.tq: Link the budget allocation to the specific industrial location, not to a general APIIC park.

142.s: Which one of the following is NOT an incentive listed for SEZs in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 15% capital subsidy for micro and small units
Reimbursement of VAT/CST on export inputs
25% capital subsidy for all large units
142.x: The listed incentives are 100% stamp duty exemption, VAT/CST reimbursement on export inputs, a 15% capital subsidy for micro and small units and a 3% interest subsidy. A 25% capital subsidy for all large units is not listed.
142.tq: Find the option that changes both the beneficiary category and the percentage of the stated incentive.

142.s: The capital subsidy available for micro and small units in Andhra Pradesh SEZs is:
142.x: Micro and small units are eligible for a 15% capital subsidy.
142.tq: Separate the capital-subsidy percentage from the different interest-subsidy percentage.

142.s: The interest subsidy listed for SEZs in Andhra Pradesh is:
142.x: The listed interest subsidy is 3%.
142.tq: Avoid reversing the small interest-subsidy figure with the larger capital-subsidy figure.

142.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Sri City and Visakhapatnam SEZ?
o: Sri City is a central government SEZ, whereas Visakhapatnam SEZ is a multi-product SEZ.
Sri City is a multi-product SEZ, whereas Visakhapatnam SEZ at Duvvada is a central government SEZ.
Both are sector-specific SEZs located in Krishna district.
142.x: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ. Visakhapatnam SEZ, located at Duvvada, is a central government SEZ.
142.tq: Use the contrast in classification and location rather than treating both SEZs as identical.

142.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh industrial-corridor and logistics focus is correct?
1. Budget-era focus includes the Visakhapatnam–Kakinada port corridor.
2. Port-led growth is associated with this focus.
3. PM Gati Shakti discussions include multimodal logistics parks and freight corridors.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
142.x: The stated focus includes the Visakhapatnam–Kakinada port corridor and port-led growth, while PM Gati Shakti-related planning includes multimodal logistics parks and freight corridors.
142.tq: Recognise the common logistics theme linking the port corridor, multimodal parks and freight corridors.

142.s: APIIC can directly allot industrial land up to which maximum area?
142.x: APIIC can directly allot land up to 50 acres.
142.tq: Distinguish the direct-allotment ceiling from larger project-area figures.

142.s: Which one of the following is identified as a criticism or controversy relating to the VCIC?
o: The corridor has been criticised only for excessive dependence on Japanese aid.
The corridor has been criticised as slow, with the Opposition alleging that corridor and metro promises remain unfulfilled.
The corridor has already completed all its promised projects ahead of schedule.
The corridor has been opposed because it is entirely inland and has no port linkage.
142.x: The VCIC has been criticised for slow progress, and the Opposition has alleged that corridor and metro promises remain unfulfilled.
142.tq: Select the option that captures both parts of the stated criticism without adding an unsupported cause.

142.s: Which of the following is identified as contributing to the logistics chain of the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)?
o: Only SEZs located in Krishna district
Only inland waterways and hill stations
Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and Japanese aid
SCoR zone, greenfield ports and Bhogapuram airport
142.x: The SCoR zone, greenfield ports and Bhogapuram airport are identified as feeding the VCIC logistics chain.
142.tq: Trace the practical logistics inputs associated with the corridor rather than confusing them with another corridor's features.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about DMIC and VCIC:
1. DMIC runs on the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.
2. Japanese aid is associated with DMIC.
3. VCIC is ADB-funded and port-led.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. DMIC is associated with the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and Japanese aid, whereas VCIC is ADB-funded and port-led.
142.tq: Keep the two corridors separate by comparing their funding, freight-corridor and development characteristics.

143.s: Special Category Status (SCS) was first introduced in India in 1969 on the recommendation of which body?
143.x: Special Category Status was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the Fifth Finance Commission. The National Development Council later endorsed the Gadgil Formula for Plan fund distribution.
143.tq: Identify the recommending body rather than the institution that later endorsed the related formula.

143.s: The Gadgil Formula, under which Special Category States received preferential Central assistance, was endorsed by the National Development Council during:
143.x: The National Development Council endorsed the Gadgil Formula during 1968-69. The formula was used for distributing Plan funds, with preferential assistance for Special Category States.
143.tq: Distinguish the year of the formula’s endorsement from the year in which SCS was introduced.

143.s: Which one of the following sets correctly represents the first three States to be granted Special Category Status?
143.x: The first three States granted Special Category Status were Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland.
143.tq: Start with the known first recipients and reject later additions to the category.

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Special Category Status:
1. It is expressly provided for in the Constitution of India.
2. It was an executive and Planning Commission-era classification.
3. It was associated with preferential Central assistance under Plan fund distribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Special Category Status is not a constitutional category; it emerged as an executive and Planning Commission-era classification linked to preferential Plan assistance.
143.tq: Test whether the classification is constitutional or executive before considering its financial consequence.

143.s: On which date did Prime Minister Manmohan Singh assure the Rajya Sabha that Andhra Pradesh would receive Special Category Status?
143.x: The assurance was given in the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014.
143.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish the parliamentary assurance from later Finance Commission developments.

143.s: Who gave the assurance in the Rajya Sabha regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh in February 2014?
